name: Number of innovations (technologies, practices and tools) co-developed by CIMMYT together with partners
resultsLevel: Output, per CIMMYT's MEAL Framework, which defines an output as a delivered result: a co-developed innovation is a product, and the CGIAR quality-assurance guidance lists new varieties, research methods and institutional innovations among its own output examples. CGIAR's control-and-externality test gives the same level.
primaryObjective: PO1 Defined by transdisciplinarity, CIMMYT is an efficient, innovative, and inclusive partner contributing to agrifood systems transformation. Contributing: PO2, PO3, PO4 (food and nutrition security; smallholder livelihoods; inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate-resilient agrifood systems).
cgiarImpactArea: Recorded per innovation. No single area fits an indicator counting innovations of any kind: a drought-tolerant variety, a biofortified variety and a soil-management advisory map to Climate Adaptation & Mitigation, Nutrition, Health & Food Security and Environmental Health & Biodiversity respectively. Each innovation carries its own tag and the annual total is never reported against one area. Per the pathway convention, set per strand rather than per indicator group, as the Introduction sets out, since two of the three groups run more than one strand.
sdgTarget: None. No SDG indicator counts innovations developed by a research organization; the nearest neighbors measure money and people instead (SDG 2.a.1, agriculture orientation of government expenditure; SDG 9.5.1, research and development expenditure as a share of gross domestic product).
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Results Framework: Innovation Development output category, standard indicator "Number of innovations profiled". A close variant, adapted rather than adopted: CGIAR counts profiled innovations whether or not a partner co-developed them, and its own review notes that "profiled" is undefined (Claus et al., 2023). The category carries into 2025-30 unchanged (CGIAR System Organization, 2025). ICARDA: OP-05, Number of innovations developed (co-developed), the closest cross-center analog (same level, unit and counting method). Not adopted: CGIAR's Innovation Packages and Scaling Readiness self-assessment (CGIAR System Organization, 2025); CIMMYT reports it into CGIAR systems where required but does not use it as a KPI construct, because it is self-assessed rather than evidence-based.
definition: Counts the technologies, practices and tools CIMMYT develops jointly with one or more partners in the reporting year, counted once per distinct innovation at the co-development milestone: a dated, jointly authored innovation description naming the partner's technical role, entered in the project innovation register. That description is also the test of co-development, applied as Eligibility criteria and missing data sets it out. "Innovation" is CGIAR's Innovation Development construct (Claus et al., 2023), narrowed here to technologies, practices and tools: practices are in, policies are out and counted under the policy indicators. The count records existence at the milestone; validation, release and adoption are measured by later indicators in the pathway.
rationale: Answers how much new or improved technology, practice and tooling CIMMYT produces with partners each year, rather than alone. Joint production is the first observable step of the innovation pathway: nothing can later be validated, released or adopted that was not first developed. It evidences the Primary Objective 1 sub-objective that "effective and efficient environments for co-creating and scaling relevant, accessible technologies, including disruptive solutions, are built through strategic partnerships".
projectSpecificApplication: State which innovations the project co-develops, with which named partners, in which crops or systems and countries, and the milestone applied (see Calculation method). Do not alter the institutional definition, unit or counting rule; if the milestone cannot be applied in this project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State which donor results line or workplan milestone this count evidences, and what project decision it informs (for example, reviewing a country workplan where joint development stalls while partner costs continue).
projectTypesNotApplicable: none. Any project type can co-develop an innovation, and the exclusions in Eligibility turn on what was produced
not on the type of project that produced it
projectTypesRaw:
Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: none. Any project type can co-develop an innovation, and the exclusions in Eligibility turn on what was produced, not on the type of project that produced it.
unit: Number of innovations (distinct technologies, practices or tools)
directionOfChange: Increase, with a caveat. A rising value means more distinct innovations were co-developed with partners. The count rewards volume and carries no quality test, so it is read with the pathway's validation, release and adoption indicators (KPI-O02, KPI-OC02, KPI-OC01).
disaggregationRequired: Required: none. Recommended: innovation type (technology / practice / tool, the register's own split), innovation status (new / significantly improved / adapted, matching Eligibility's admitted categories), targeted CGIAR Impact Area, partner type, country and crop. ICARDA disaggregates its equivalent innovation count the same way, by five type categories (production systems, genetic innovation, social science innovation, innovative biophysical research, innovative methods and tools) plus new-or-improved status. ICARDA's type split is a discipline axis mapped to its own team structure; CIMMYT's is an object axis taken from the indicator title, so the two are not interchangeable and the status disaggregation is adopted while the type list stays CIMMYT's. This indicator is not disaggregated by stage of development: the pathway carries stage as separate indicators (validation at KPI-O02, release at KPI-OC02, adoption at scale at KPI-OC01), so a stage cut here would repeat them or run a second staging scheme beside them.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register mandates no cut for any project type, and the recommended cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country and sub-national location; crop or system; partner type; targeted CGIAR Impact Area; whether women's or youth organizations were among the co-developing partners.
unitOfObservation: The innovation (one distinct technology, practice or tool). Result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct innovations that in the reporting year meet the definition above, have a named partner technical role in the innovation description, and reached the defined milestone. The milestone is the dated, jointly authored innovation description naming the partner's technical role, entered in the project innovation register, as set out in the Definition. The significant-improvement test, and every inclusion, exclusion and missing-data rule, is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; it is not restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: the project's own innovation register and management records, evidenced per counted innovation by a dated innovation description, the partnership agreement or contract naming the partner, and the milestone record (signed protocol, trial or development report, or prototype handover note). Co-development is documented as a by-product of the work (ICARDA likewise names routine recording). Not applicable DS1: co-development is established from project documentation, not by surveying a population. Not applicable DS3: an innovation is not an observable land or surface feature. Not applicable DS4: CGIAR institutional records (CGSpace and CGIAR results-reporting entries) cannot evidence the milestone, which is an entry in the project innovation register, and usually lack partner-role evidence. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced data cannot evidence a documented milestone or partner role.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Name the project innovation register the count was taken from.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, secondary source. Verification is documentary review of the description, agreement and milestone record against the inclusion criteria.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as innovations reach the milestone; compiled once per reporting year
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the innovation reached the milestone: a within-year count, not a cumulative stock. The institutional reporting year is January to December, on CIMMYT's own institutional convention; a project following a donor year states which one.
baselineRequired: No. The baseline is zero by construction: the indicator counts within the reporting year, so each year starts from zero. This is CIMMYT's own counting convention and needs no external source, being a statement about how this register counts. Prior-year values remain useful for trends; a project starting mid-year reports its partial first year in that year's value, labeled partial, and its first full year is the first point for trend comparison.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One reporting year, one innovation register scope. Distinct innovations pool across projects, countries and crops: the object counted is the innovation itself, and it does not change when the project counting it does. Values from different reporting years are never pooled into one figure. Weight: one each per distinct innovation, whatever its type or expected benefit.

B: Combination method: sum. Institutional total = Σ distinct innovations across projects, after the de-duplication in Block E. Never average project counts: a mean over projects answers how productive a typical project was, not how many innovations exist.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying innovations. At institutional level, the de-duplicated sum of those counts. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the number of innovations excluded for missing partner role, milestone record or register entry, and the number of duplicates removed.

D: Never pooled. Counts across results levels: the same innovation appears again at validation (KPI-O02), release (KPI-OC02) and adoption (KPI-OC01), so summing across them counts one object several times; the levels connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative, not by arithmetic. A progression ratio, the share of a cohort later validated, requires cohort tracking and is never one indicator's same-year value divided by another's. Counts from different reporting years.

E: Deduplication and coverage. A record is one distinct innovation. The same innovation is often co-developed by several CIMMYT projects or with another CGIAR center, and innovations carry no institutional identifier, so de-duplicate on the innovation, its title reconciled against the jointly authored description; crop, system, country and partner are recorded as disaggregations, never as parts of the key. Count each innovation once, and label the pooled figure an upper estimate until an identifier exists. Report the number of projects contributing and the number of duplicates removed. A genomic, phenotyping or bioinformatics platform or tool co-developed with a partner is counted here at its co-development milestone and by KPI-O11 at release; the two count the same object at different milestones, so they are never summed, and reporting states which platforms and tools appear in both.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
A partner that funded the work, hosted a trial or disseminated the result, without a named technical role in the innovation description, is not a co-developer. Include new, significantly improved and adapted technologies, practices and tools that reached the milestone in the reporting year with a named partner technical role. Significantly improved means the innovation serves a new purpose or a new class of users. That test is CIMMYT's own convention, applied by the MEAL unit to keep an incremental revision from being counted as a second innovation; it is stated on CIMMYT's authority rather than taken from a donor handbook. Adapted means an innovation not first developed under this indicator, whether another organization's or CIMMYT's own from before the project innovation register, modified with the partner for a context it was not designed for (a different agroecology, farming system or crop), where the jointly authored description records what was changed in the innovation itself; a translation, a relabeling, or use in a new location with nothing changed is not an adaptation. That test is also CIMMYT's own convention. An adaptation of an innovation already counted here is not a new adapted innovation and counts only under the significant-improvement test (Repeated observations); for such an innovation, a new country, agroecology, farming system or crop alone is not a new class of users under that test. Exclude innovations CIMMYT developed alone; publications, datasets and training materials, which are knowledge products counted elsewhere; diagnostic or root-cause research that produced no technology, practice or tool; and anything counted in an earlier year.

Missing data. An innovation with no documented partner role, no dated milestone record, or no entry in the project innovation register is excluded, never estimated, and the number excluded is reported with the value so weak record-keeping is visible rather than absorbed.

Repeated observations. Each innovation is counted once, in the first year it reaches the milestone. A later adaptation counts as new only where it meets the significant-improvement test, with the justification recorded against it.
limitations: Supports no claim about benefit: the count says what CIMMYT and partners produced, not that anything was tested, released, adopted, or improved yield, income or diets; it should never be quoted alone as a result.

The count is only as good as the milestone definition and record-keeping behind it: a loose milestone lets projects count early ideas, a strict one favors well-documented projects, so counts are not reliably comparable until one milestone is fixed everywhere.
Innovations developed before the project innovation register enter as adaptations when modified, so the register's first years carry a one-time wave of them.

The counted objects are not equivalent: a new maize variety representing years of breeding and a modified planting calendar each count as one; the total measures neither effort nor expected benefit, and no weighting is applied.

A pooled figure without matched innovation identifiers is an upper estimate (none exist at CIMMYT), and the figure is not interchangeable with the CGIAR "innovations profiled" count, which does not require partner co-development.
A rise means CIMMYT and partners produced more innovations that year, nothing more: not that the innovations work, that anyone can obtain them, or that anyone uses them.
subMetrics: None. Innovation type, partner type, country, crop and status are disaggregations of one count, not sub-metrics. One derived count is flagged rather than adopted: ICARDA derives a climate-adaptation sub-count (OP-05.1) from its equivalent indicator; a CIMMYT equivalent would be a derived sub-count with a stated assessment rule. Related sheets: KPI-O02, KPI-OC02, KPI-OC01, KPI-I01.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E officer with the responsible scientist for each register entry. Validation: project MEAL officer, against the inclusion criteria and milestone evidence. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (counting rule and cross-project de-duplication). Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit, which publishes the pooled figure.
sourceRef: Volume 1 · Innovation development & scaling — Reference sheet KPI-O01

name: Number of innovations validated through participatory engagement with farmers and partners in CIMMYT intervention areas
resultsLevel: Output, per CIMMYT's MEAL Framework, which defines an output as a delivered result: the validated innovation is a product of the research process, and validation delivers it rather than changing anyone's behavior. The change sits further along, at KPI-OC01 and KPI-OC16. CGIAR's control-and-externality test gives the same level.
primaryObjective: PO1 Defined by transdisciplinarity, CIMMYT is an efficient, innovative, and inclusive partner contributing to agrifood systems transformation. Contributing only: PO2, PO3, PO4.
cgiarImpactArea: Recorded per innovation. No single area fits an indicator counting innovations of any kind: a drought-tolerant variety, a biofortified variety and a soil-management advisory map to Climate Adaptation & Mitigation, Nutrition, Health & Food Security and Environmental Health & Biodiversity respectively. Each innovation carries its own tag and the annual total is never reported against one area. Per the pathway convention, set per strand rather than per indicator group, as the Introduction sets out, since two of the three groups run more than one strand.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator counts innovations validated with farmers. The nearest targets, 2.a and 9.5, are measured by investment flows, expenditure shares and researcher numbers, so a mapping would be a stretch rather than a correspondence.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR counts innovations profiled under its Innovation Development output category but has no standard indicator for validated innovations; it handles intermediate stages through Innovation Packages and Scaling Readiness, which CIMMYT has decided not to adopt, so validation here is not a readiness score.
definition: Counts the co-developed innovations tested and validated with farmers and partners in CIMMYT intervention areas in the reporting year. An innovation is a technology, practice or tool developed jointly by CIMMYT and at least one partner, the same object counted at co-development stage by KPI-O01. Validation means participatory field testing confirmed the innovation performs as intended, in four parts: testing in a CIMMYT intervention area under conditions resembling those intended users face, not only on station; farmers and partners taking part in assessing the test, whether or not they also ran it: hosting a trial without judging its result does not qualify; a performance criterion written into the protocol before testing and met; and a dated trial or evaluation record.
rationale: Answers whether the innovations CIMMYT develops with partners work in farmers' fields, and were judged to work by those farmers and partners, before anything is put forward for release. It is the evidence gate of the innovation pathway: co-development (KPI-O01) shows what was created, this indicator what was proven, release (KPI-OC02) what moved on, adoption (KPI-OC01, KPI-OC16) what was taken up, and it is the first evidence-backed step behind CIMMYT's claim to be an effective and inclusive innovation partner.
projectSpecificApplication: State the innovations covered and their type, the testing network used (for example a regional on-farm testing network, a mother and baby trial network, a hub site), the countries and seasons, and the form participation takes. Do not alter the institutional definition, validation conditions, unit or counting rule; if validation as defined is not feasible here, raise it with the MEAL focal point.
projectSpecificRationale: State which donor milestone or results-framework line the count evidences, which project decision it informs (which innovations go forward, which return for redesign, which are dropped), and what a shortfall triggers, for example a review of trial siting or of farmer involvement.
projectTypesNotApplicable: none. Any project type can validate a co-developed innovation, and the exclusions in Eligibility turn on the testing and its documentation
projectTypesRaw:
Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: none. Any project type can validate a co-developed innovation, and the exclusions in Eligibility turn on the testing and its documentation, not on the project type.
unit: Number of innovations (distinct innovations, not trials, sites, seasons or participating farmers). An innovation KPI-O01 counts as distinct, whether new, significantly improved under its new-purpose or new-class-of-users test, or adapted, is a distinct innovation here.
directionOfChange: Increase, read alongside KPI-O01 and KPI-OC02. A rising value means more co-developed innovations completed participatory field testing. A rising validation count that never converts into releases signals a pipeline that proves things and then stops.
disaggregationRequired: Required: none institutionally required (the register sets none here). The counted unit is an innovation, not a person, so CIMMYT's standard sex and age disaggregations do not apply to the count; who took part belongs in the participation record under Collection instrument. Recommended: innovation type (technology / practice / tool), innovation status (new / significantly improved / adapted) and targeted CGIAR Impact Area, per KPI-O01. None is promoted to required.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Innovation type, on the register's own split (technology / practice / tool), the same axis KPI-O01 uses, so the two counts in one pipeline are cut the same way; crop and trait class, aligned to KPI-OC02; country and agroecology; partner type; form of farmer participation; whether women's or youth organizations took part.
unitOfObservation: The innovation, rolled up to one record per innovation. Result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct innovations that during the reporting year met all four validation conditions in the Definition. Performance criterion: the protocol must state before testing what "performs as intended" means. For varietal and germplasm innovations the criterion is CIMMYT's own convention: the entry is new and superior to the standard check for a specific trait, evidenced by field performance data collected under end-user conditions. For practices and tools, an equivalent statement of superiority or acceptability against current farmer practice. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1 (censuses and surveys, which here includes on-farm trials and objective field measurement): the participatory trial or evaluation itself, the field performance measurements on the plots plus the participants' assessment, recorded against the protocol. Fallback DS5, scoped to participants' assessment data from a farmer-managed crowdsourced trial, where a project runs one; a validation whose farmer assessment comes from such a trial rests on this route, not on DS1, whatever plot measurements accompany it. Fallback DS2 (administrative and registry data): the partner's own validation record where CIMMYT does not hold the trial data, evidenced by the dated record and the protocol it was judged against; flag such innovations as fallback-sourced, since the criterion and the depth of farmer involvement may differ. Not applicable DS3 (geospatial and Earth observation) and DS4 (secondary and international databases): neither can establish that a specific innovation was tested with farmers against a stated criterion.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role was used. For Recommended, give the trial design, the number of sites and the participating farmers behind each validated innovation. For Fallback, name the innovations validated on it and the route: for DS2, say why the primary data were unavailable, name the partner, and give the criterion it applied; for DS5, name the crowdsourced trial whose assessment data were used.
collectionInstrument: The trial or evaluation protocol carrying the performance criterion, paired with a participatory assessment instrument, for example a structured evaluation or preference-scoring form completed with participating farmers at trial evaluation. Respondent: the farmer hosting or managing the trial, or the farmer group, with the partner staff running it. Mode: field measurement plus face-to-face evaluation at or after harvest. Whatever system holds it, the validation record carries at minimum the performance criterion as written before testing, who assessed and in what role, the result against the criterion including a negative result, the country and agroecology of the validation, the date, and the sign-off.
collectionFrequency: Continuous: trial and evaluation records are produced at the end of each testing cycle, then consolidated once per reporting year.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Annual values must not be added into a cumulative figure without first removing innovations already counted.
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the validation result was documented, January to December at institutional level; projects on a donor year state which they use, and a cropping season is assigned to its harvest year. Where validation spans seasons, the value belongs to the year the result was confirmed. A within-year count, not a cumulative stock.
baselineRequired: No. An annual count of validation events starts from zero each year, so there is no prior-period reference value to establish. The zero baseline is CIMMYT's own counting convention, being a statement about how this register counts rather than a borrowed rule. A project wanting to show pipeline progression uses its own co-development count (KPI-O01) for the same cohort as the reference point.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. Weight: one each per distinct innovation, whatever the number of sites, seasons or participating farmers behind it. (2) Across projects: sum distinct innovations with a validation evidenced wholly by the Recommended source; an innovation whose only qualifying validations draw on a Fallback (DS5 assessment data or a DS2 partner record) is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note naming it and its route, not blended into it.

B: Combination method. The institutional figure is the sum of distinct innovations across projects after de-duplication; never average project counts.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying validated innovations for the reporting year. At institutional level, the de-duplicated sum of those counts, computed from the records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since the same innovation is often validated in more than one project, country or season. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the number of candidate innovations excluded under Eligibility and why, the tested-but-not-validated figure (Sub-metrics), and the number of innovations reported alongside as Fallback-sourced, by route.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: no. This count does not combine arithmetically with KPI-O01 (co-developed), KPI-OC02 (released for scaling), KPI-OC01 (share adopted at scale) or KPI-I01 (partner-of-choice standing): the same innovation passes through several of those milestones, so adding across levels would count one object twice. Overlap with KPI-O01 and KPI-OC02 is structural and the three must never be summed; the levels connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative. The one legitimate cross-level use is a cohort progression ratio, how many innovations co-developed in a cohort were later validated, which needs an identifier.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: the same innovation is often validated in more than one project, country or season, and jointly developed innovations may be reported by more than one CGIAR center. CIMMYT has confirmed that no identifier or institute-level registry exists for innovations, so the pooled figure is labeled an upper estimate. De-duplicate before pooling on the innovation, its title reconciled against the jointly authored description KPI-O01 records; crop, system, country and partner are recorded as disaggregations, never as parts of the key. Repeat the step before adding annual totals.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Repeated observations: one innovation counts once, in the year it is validated, whatever the number of sites, seasons or projects were involved, and is not re-reported in later years. Validation of the same innovation, one not distinct under the Unit of measure's test, for a materially new context (a new country or agroecology) is recorded, with the country and agroecology its validation record carries, as a disaggregation of the same innovation, not as a second count.
limitations: Validated is not adopted and is not benefit: the count says an innovation was proven to work with farmers, not that farmers use it or gain from it. Use KPI-OC01 and KPI-OC16 for use and adoption.

A count treats unlike things alike: one validated innovation may be a hybrid, another a planting practice, another a digital advisory tool, each worth one and none weighted, so read it with the innovation-type split.

The quality of participation varies within what still qualifies. The Definition sets assessing the result as the floor, but "assessing" still spans a single yes/no judgment and co-designing the trial and scoring every entry, so counts above that floor are not finely comparable across projects or years.

Counting boundaries move the number as much as the science does, and the count is sensitive to the rules this sheet settles: an innovation validated in three countries counts once, re-validation does not add to the count, and a failed test of an innovation not yet validated is recorded as tested but not validated rather than counted. With no identifier, the pooled figure is an upper estimate.

A rise means more co-developed options were confirmed to work that year; a fall may reflect trial cycles, season quality or project timing rather than weaker science. The result is jointly produced, so it supports contribution claims only.
subMetrics: One required companion figure: tested but not validated, the count of innovations not validated in the reporting year or an earlier one that have either a field-testing result under this indicator's conditions documented in the reporting year that does not meet the performance criterion, or field testing that concluded in the previous reporting year with no result documented by the end of this one, the number counted on the second ground being reported with the figure; testing still running at year end enters neither figure, a result documented later belongs to the year it is documented, as Reference period sets out, and an innovation counted on the second ground is not counted here again when that test's result is documented. Reported alongside the validated count, never subtracted from KPI-O01's co-developed count or folded into it. A validation gate whose rejections are invisible is not a gate: a program that validates everything looks identical to one testing rigorously and turning things down. Otherwise none: innovation type, crop, trait class, country and targeted Impact Area are disaggregations of one count, not separately calculated metrics. The neighboring pathway milestones each have their own sheet: KPI-O01, KPI-OC02, KPI-OC01, KPI-OC16, KPI-I01.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the program science lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project research and agronomy team with partner staff and participating farmers. Validation: the responsible scientist confirms the evidence meets the protocol criterion and the project MEAL officer confirms the record is complete. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 1 · Innovation development & scaling — Reference sheet KPI-O02

name: Number of formal partnership agreements (MoUs, consortia, licensing deals) established for innovation, for co-creating and scaling relevant and accessible technologies including disruptive solutions, and for institutional capacity strengthening
resultsLevel: Output, per CIMMYT's MEAL Framework, which defines an output as a delivered result: a signed agreement is an instrument CIMMYT has produced. The behavioral change among partners is the change, and it sits one level up, at KPI-OC03 and KPI-OC05.
indicatorScope: Mission, although CIMMYT's own partnering practice sits on the Institutional branch (KPI-O57, KPI-OC60): partner-of-choice standing is part of the innovation narrative rather than a measure of institutional operations. The indicator group spans both branches by design.
primaryObjective: PO1: Defined by transdisciplinarity, CIMMYT is an efficient, innovative, and inclusive partner contributing to agrifood systems transformation. The mapping is direct: strategic objective 1.4, "Effective and efficient environments for co-creating and scaling relevant, accessible technologies, including disruptive solutions, are built through strategic partnerships", is the wording this indicator follows. Contributing: PO3, anchored in strategic objective 3.3 on strengthening institutions that provide novel technologies and services. PO5 is not a contributing objective: the Strategy commits CIMMYT to advocating for partnerships as a global agenda, but a count of CIMMYT's own agreements does not evidence the global community taking coordinated measures, and where partnering does advance that it is already read in the Policy, finance & market systems pathway.
cgiarImpactArea: Recorded per agreement. Agreements are counted whatever their thematic content, so each is tagged with the area or areas it serves and reported in total and by area; area counts overlap and are never summed. Per the pathway convention, set per strand rather than per indicator group, as the Introduction sets out, since two of the three groups run more than one strand.
sdgTarget: None. The thematically closest target is SDG 17.17 (effective public, public-private and civil society partnerships), but its official indicator 17.17.1 measures United States dollars committed to public-private partnerships for infrastructure, not a count of agreements.
otherFrameworks: ICARDA's OP-12 (Number of partnerships established, Output level) is the closest external equivalent, and its derived indicator OP-12.1 (Number of partnership agreements signed or renewed) the nearest match to what O03 counts; ICARDA also counts informal partnerships, so its values are not comparable with this formal-instruments-only count. CGIAR has no standard partnership-agreement indicator: the 32 standard indicators contain none, and the Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 instead adds a partner engagement/partnership building result category and foresees possible new engagement indicators. Hence the register records a CIMMYT-own definition.
definition: Counts the formal partnership agreements between CIMMYT and external institutions that are in force at any point in the reporting year, from their year of signature, for co-creating and scaling relevant and accessible technologies and for strengthening the institutional capacity of partners. The annual value is a stock, reported with a required new/continuing split; the new subtotal is the year's flow. A formal partnership agreement is a signed, dated written instrument setting out shared objectives and each party's obligations; any instrument meeting the four criteria in Calculation method counts, for example a memorandum of understanding, consortium agreement, licensing deal or sub-grant. Working relationships with no signed instrument are outside this indicator.
rationale: Answers how many formal commitments CIMMYT holds to build and scale technology with others and to strengthen the institutions it works through, and, through the new subtotal, how many it entered in the year: the countable output step behind the 2030 Strategy objective on building partnership environments for co-creating and scaling technologies. It measures commitments made, not what they produced; results are read from KPI-OC03 (repeat partnering) and KPI-OC05 (partnership quality).
projectSpecificApplication: State which agreements the project counts: partner institutions and types, instrument type, purpose, countries covered, and the signature and end dates placing each agreement in force in the reporting year and classifying it as new or continuing; state which instruments are excluded as held centrally by CIMMYT, so nothing is reported twice. Do not change the definition or the counting rule; if the project's partnering does not run through signed instruments, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining the indicator here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision, donor commitment or workplan milestone this count serves (for example a consortium-formation or licensing milestone), and what a shortfall triggers, such as a review of missing partners or contracting delays.
projectTypesNotApplicable: none. Any project type can establish a formal partnership agreement
projectTypesRaw:
Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: none. Any project type can establish a formal partnership agreement.
unit: Number of formal partnership agreements (distinct signed instruments, not partner organizations, projects or countries)
directionOfChange: Increase, read together with KPI-OC03 and KPI-OC05. A rising value means more formal partnership agreements were in force during the year, from more signings, fewer expiries or both; the new subtotal shows which. The count is of signed instruments and carries no quality claim about the partnerships behind them.
disaggregationRequired: Required: agreement status (new / continuing), classified by signing year; partner/institution type. The confirmed category list is: CGIAR center; national agricultural research and extension system (NARES); university or higher education institution; government ministry or public agency; international research organization, non-CGIAR; multilateral or UN agency; regional or sub-regional organization; private company; financial institution; non-governmental or civil society organization; farmer organization or cooperative; foundation; other. If more than 10 percent of records fall to "other" in a year, the list is revised rather than the partners reclassified. Partners are classified at the signing legal entity, so a ministry and its national research institute are two partners in two categories. An agreement binding partners of several types is classified once, on its lead partner, otherwise the first partner named, so the type counts add to the total. CGIAR Impact Area is also required, as that field sets out. Sex and age do not apply: the counted unit is an agreement, not a person.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Instrument type; purpose (technology co-creation and scaling, capacity strengthening, both); country or region; new versus existing partner (the cut that connects to KPI-OC03); Global South partner marker (read against KPI-OC60 without duplicating it); whether the agreement carries a financial transfer to the partner, which separates sub-grant instruments from other instrument classes.
unitOfObservation: Result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation: the partnership agreement, meaning one distinct signed instrument, which can bind several organizations.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct formal partnership agreements meeting all four criteria: (a) written and signed by CIMMYT and at least one external institution; (b) in force at any point during the reporting year, from its year of signature; (c) states shared objectives and each party's obligations; (d) purpose covers co-creating or scaling technologies, strengthening partner institutional capacity, or both. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (administrative and registry data): CIMMYT's contracts and agreements records, where signed instruments are filed by the responsible legal, partnerships or contracts function, plus project and country office agreement files; the signed instrument is the evidence, no separate measurement is required. CIMMYT's Legal team holds these instruments and each carries a unique number, so the record set is de-duplicable. Fallback DS1 (surveys): a structured annual return in which project leaders and country representatives enumerate the agreements signed in the year, used only for an agreement a project or country office reports whose signed instrument neither the contracts and agreements records nor the project and country office agreement files hold; flag such agreements as fallback-sourced, since self-reported enumeration is more exposed to omission. Not applicable DS3: geospatial data cannot establish that an instrument was signed. Not applicable DS4: no third-party database independently records CIMMYT's agreements, CGIAR systems holding only downstream copies of CIMMYT's own submissions. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced data cannot establish the existence or content of a signed instrument.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which route each agreement rests on, Recommended or Fallback. For agreements on the Recommended route, state the records system and each instrument's reference; for any on the Fallback, state why the records did not hold its signed instrument, who completed the return, and how double reporting was checked.
collectionInstrument: For the DS1 fallback only: a structured annual return, one row per agreement, listing instrument reference, each partner with its partner type, in the order the instrument names them, with the lead partner marked, signature date, instrument type, purpose, countries, and CIMMYT signatory. Respondent: the project leader or country representative accountable for the agreement. Mode: electronic return with the instrument or its reference attached. For the Recommended DS2 route: not applicable, the filed instrument is the record itself.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as agreements are filed; consolidated once per year.
reportingFrequency: Annually. The annual value is a stock, agreements in force during the year, so it must never be summed across years: a continuing agreement appears in every year it remains in force. The new subtotal is the year's flow and is the figure to use for year-on-year growth.
referencePeriod: The reporting year, January to December at institutional level. An agreement belongs to every reporting year from its year of signature in which it is in force for at least one day, and its signature year classifies it as new or continuing. Projects following a donor reporting year state so.
baselineRequired: No. Each year's value is a self-standing stock; change is read from the year-on-year series, and the first reported year serves as the reference point. A one-point-in-time baseline is not commensurable with a period stock: comparing a start-of-period count against an in-force-at-any-point count manufactures apparent change that is not there. The new subtotal needs no baseline either, since it starts from zero each year.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. Weight: one each per distinct signed agreement, whatever its scope or the number of parties to it. (2) Across projects: sum the agreements the Recommended contracts records hold; agreements known only through the Fallback annual return are reported alongside the pooled figure with their count and a note naming them, never blended in.

B: Combination method. Sum distinct agreements after de-duplication.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying partnership agreements for the reporting year. At institutional level, the de-duplicated sum of those counts, computed from the records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one agreement can be reported by every party to it. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the number of partnership agreements excluded under Eligibility and why, the number of agreements known only through the Fallback return, the number of this sheet's agreements also counted by KPI-O57, and the number of agreements first on file after the value for their signature year was compiled, which enter no new subtotal.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: no. This count does not combine arithmetically with KPI-OC03 (a percentage over a multi-year partner set), KPI-OC05 (a quality score) or KPI-I01; they connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative, not arithmetic. (2) With KPI-O57: never. An instrument meeting both definitions is counted on both sheets, so the two values overlap by construction and adding them double-counts every shared instrument. No figure combines them, at any level. Each sheet publishes the number of instruments it shares with the other, which is what makes the overlap visible rather than hidden.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: a multi-party consortium agreement counts once, not once per partner; an agreement covering several projects or countries counts once, attributed to one reporting unit agreed in advance; an agreement signed centrally and also logged by a project is one agreement. Every filed instrument carries a unique number issued by CIMMYT's Legal team, so de-duplication is by instrument reference and the institutional total is a true count, not an upper estimate. This count and KPI-O57 are never summed. An instrument meeting both definitions is carried by both, by design, and each sheet publishes how many of its instruments the other also counts.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusions: agreements signed centrally, by a project, or by a country office, each counted once.

Exclusions: relationships with no signed instrument; procurement, employment and consultancy contracts; confidentiality and material-transfer instruments; funding agreements whose substance is CIMMYT receiving money (resource mobilization pathway). A sub-grant instrument that meets all four criteria is counted: it establishes a formal partnership, which is what this indicator measures, and the fact that KPI-O57 also counts it is not a reason to leave it out.

Missing data: an agreement with no retrievable signed instrument when a year's value is compiled is not counted in that value and not imputed; once filed it counts in every later compiled year in which it is in force, classified as new or continuing by its signature year, and values already published are not revised. An agreement known only through the Fallback annual return is reported alongside the pooled figure as Aggregation rule Block A sets out, not among the exclusions.

Repeated observations: one agreement counts once per reporting year, classified by its year of signature; two distinct agreements with the same partner count as two; amendments, extensions and no-cost variations do not create a second count. Counting basis, confirmed by CIMMYT: the annual value counts agreements new and continuing, with signing year as the classifier. An agreement signed in the reporting year is new; one signed earlier and still in force is continuing; a renewal without a new instrument stays continuing. The two subtotals are reported separately and the new subtotal is the year's flow.
limitations: A signed agreement is a commitment, not a result: agreements that lapse without activity count the same as agreements that deliver. Read only alongside KPI-OC03 and KPI-OC05; a rising count with flat quality and repeat-partnering values is a warning sign.

The count treats unlike instruments alike: a licensing deal, a multi-year consortium agreement and a statement-of-intent memorandum each count as one, so totals are only interpretable with the instrument-type and partner-type splits attached.

Formal-only counting under-records partnering where institutions collaborate without signed instruments, and makes the value non-comparable with counts including informal partnerships (such as ICARDA's OP-12) unless the difference is stated.

Counting boundaries move the total as much as partnering practice does: the multi-party rule and the new-versus-continuing split each change what the headline says, so totals are comparable only where those rules are applied identically. Read the stock and the new subtotal together: a flat stock can hide both a strong intake and a matching wave of expiries.
subMetrics: None. Partner type, instrument type and purpose are disaggregations of one count, not sub-metrics. Related sheets: KPI-OC03 and KPI-OC05, which this output feeds per the register; KPI-O57 and KPI-OC60 (Institutional branch); KPI-I01 (the pathway impact).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: the CIMMYT function that files signed agreements, being the legal, contracts or partnerships office as each project's own governance assigns it, for the Recommended route; project leaders or country representatives for the Fallback return. Validation: the responsible contracts or partnerships officer confirms each instrument is signed, dated and in scope; the project MEAL officer checks no instrument is reported twice. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, applying the rules above. Approval: project team lead for project-reported values; the responsible partnerships function for centrally held agreements. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 1 · Innovation development & scaling — Reference sheet KPI-O03

name: Number of farmers in CIMMYT intervention areas trained in improved production practices
resultsLevel: Output
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Contributing: PO1 (Defined by transdisciplinarity, CIMMYT is an efficient, innovative, and inclusive partner contributing to agrifood systems transformation), PO2 (Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries), PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs, following the primary objective PO3. Stable for this indicator because it counts people rather than result objects. Per the pathway convention, set per strand rather than per indicator group, as the Introduction sets out, since two of the three groups run more than one strand.
sdgTarget: None. No SDG indicator counts program training participation; the closest theme, SDG indicator 4.3.1, measures population-level participation rates in formal and non-formal education and training, not the delivery reach of a specific program, so there is no direct correspondence.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Technical Reporting: number of people trained (gender disaggregated), with length of training and delivery method, is the capacity-development element of CGIAR's minimum data standard for project outputs.
definition: Counts unique farmers in CIMMYT intervention areas trained in improved production practices during the reporting year, counted once per farmer regardless of number of trainings (project totals de-duplicate, not sum). "Trained" means completing structured instruction with a planned curriculum intended to change knowledge and behavior, delivered in person or digitally; brief sensitization contact does not count. The indicator is adapted from the CGIAR standard indicator "Number of people trained" (Capacity Sharing for Development result category: people trained by CGIAR with the aim of leading to changes in knowledge and behavior), narrowed in two ways: only farmers are counted, and only training on improved production practices qualifies.
rationale: Answers how many farmers CIMMYT's projects reached with structured training on improved production practices in the year: the delivery step of the innovation-scaling pathway on which the adoption outcome (KPI-OC16) is built. A gender-disaggregated people-trained count is part of CGIAR's minimum data standard for capacity-development outputs, so this value feeds CGIAR technical reporting directly as well as donor reach reporting.
projectSpecificApplication: State the project's intervention area, the improved production practices its training covers, and who delivers the training (CIMMYT staff, implementing partners, or CIMMYT-trained lead farmers under a deliberate cascade strategy). Qualifying items are those on the project's promoted-item list, approved with its MEAL plan and frozen for the reporting year; the CIMMYT MEAL unit holds the lists. Do not alter the unique-farmer counting rule, the structured-training threshold, or the reporting-year window. If individually recorded attendance is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining the indicator here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count informs: for example, a donor-required participation or reach indicator, or an internal delivery target that triggers a review of the extension strategy if training reach falls behind plan.
projectTypesNotApplicable: none. Any project type can train farmers
projectTypesRaw:
Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: none. Any project type can train farmers.
unit: Number of farmers (unique individuals per reporting year)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more farmers completed training in improved production practices; it establishes reach, not learning, use or benefit. A farmer trained several times is counted once, so the value counts farmers rather than training events, and a structured training event is counted here and not by KPI-O20.
disaggregationRequired: Required: sex (female/male at minimum, per CGIAR's sex-disaggregated data standards); age (youth/non-youth, with youth defined as 15 to 30, stated once in Core Section 4.1; projects record date of birth or exact age, not a band, so other donors' cuts, for example a donor band of 15 to 29, can be derived without recollecting data); delivery route (direct, by CIMMYT staff or implementing partners / cascade, by CIMMYT-trained lead farmers; a farmer completing training on both routes in one reporting year is reported under direct), since cascade-trained farmers count as trained but the training quality differs and must stay visible rather than blended into the direct-delivery total.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Smallholder / non-smallholder status, as Annex B defines it; practice or crop covered; training length and delivery method (in person / digital); country or sub-national region.
unitOfObservation: Individual
calculationSummary: Value = the count of unique farmers, matched by farmer identifier in the project's beneficiary registry, who completed at least one qualifying training during the reporting year. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: training attendance registers from every qualifying event, linked to the project's beneficiary registry through the standard registration template (CIMMYT maintains per-project farmer and household identifiers built from traditional plus biometric references), which is what makes the unique-farmer count reliable within a project. Fallback DS2: partner-reported training counts without registry linkage, used only where a partner delivers training but cannot share personal identifiers; such counts cannot be de-duplicated against the project registry, so they are flagged and reported separately as an upper estimate, never blended into the registry-based total. Not applicable DS1: a sample survey estimates a population share, it cannot produce the de-duplicated census count of named participants this indicator requires. Not applicable DS3: training participation is not observable from satellite or geospatial data. Not applicable DS4: no third-party database records participation in CIMMYT project training. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or self-reported claims of having been trained cannot be verified against event attendance.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether Recommended or Fallback was used. If Fallback (unlinked partner counts), state which partner, why registry linkage was not feasible, and report the unlinked count separately from the registry-based count.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). The operative recording tools, the event attendance register and the standard beneficiary registration template, are described under Data source.
collectionFrequency: Continuous: attendance is recorded at every training event as it happens.
referencePeriod: The reporting year, January to December at institutional level. Projects may follow a donor fiscal year (for example USDA October to September, FCDO April to March) and must state which year basis the value covers.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual delivery count and each reporting year stands alone; prior-year values provide trend context but no baseline is needed to report the indicator.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. Weight: one each per unique farmer, whatever the number or length of trainings attended. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool registry-linked (Recommended) records across projects and count distinct farmers as Block B sets out. A partner's unlinked (Fallback) count is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note naming the partner, never blended in; the same project's registry-linked records are pooled.

B: Combination method: sum of distinct persons. Within a project, unique farmers on the registry identifier. Across projects, the union of the registries where they share an identifier; otherwise the sum of project counts, labeled an upper estimate, with the share of the total that comes from reconciled registries stated.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of unique farmers on that project's training registry for the reporting year, de-duplicated on the project's registry farmer identifier. At institutional level, the count of unique farmers across projects, de-duplicated again across registries where they share an identifier, since one farmer trained by two projects is one farmer and summing project counts would report them twice. Where identifiers cannot be reconciled across registries, the institutional figure is the sum of project counts and is labeled an upper estimate rather than presented as a count. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the reconciliation basis, the number of records dropped for want of an identifier, the number of attendance records dropped for want of a session date, and the partial-attendance count.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no arithmetic aggregation. This output enters the adoption outcome (KPI-OC16) as a population dependency: farmers who completed a qualifying training and meet KPI-OC16's season test form part of the population from which KPI-OC16's denominator and sampling frame are drawn. The output count is never added to any outcome or impact value.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: within a project the beneficiary registry de-duplicates reliably. Across projects there is no institute-level registry, so a farmer participating in two projects can be counted twice, and the institutional total carries the label Block C sets out. Named overlaps with other register indicators: a farmer on the direct delivery route (trained by CIMMYT staff, or by an implementing partner under a project agreement) also meets the definition of KPI-O04 (individuals trained by CIMMYT), so the two counts overlap and must never be summed; a farmer on the cascade route, trained by a CIMMYT-trained lead farmer, is counted here only, since KPI-O04 admits only training delivered by CIMMYT or on its behalf under a project agreement; farmers reached through innovation-package access (KPI-O20) are a separate assisted-person channel, and a farmer both trained and receiving a package is one assisted person, not two, in KPI-OC16's denominator. Values are not summable across reporting years: a farmer trained in two years is counted in each, so a multi-year total requires de-duplication across years by identifier.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion: farmers (crop or livestock producers) located in the project's intervention area who complete structured, curriculum-based training on one or more improved production practices, delivered by CIMMYT, an implementing partner under a project agreement, or CIMMYT-trained lead farmers under a deliberate cascade strategy, with attendance individually recorded. Each attendance is recorded with its session date, and each training event with its length and delivery method (in person / digital). Qualifying items are those on the project's promoted-item list, approved with its MEAL plan and frozen for the reporting year; the CIMMYT MEAL unit holds the lists. Completion is the attendance the curriculum sets as its completion condition, recorded in the training record; a single-session event is completed by attending it. Farmers who attended without completing are held out of the count and reported as a separate partial-attendance count; a farmer counted as trained is not also in the partial-attendance count.
limitations: Measures delivery reach, not learning or behavior change: a rise means more farmers were reached with training, not that knowledge or practice improved. Read it alongside the adoption outcome (KPI-OC16) for the change narrative.

"Training" spans very different intensities, from a half-day session to a season-long course. Counts are comparable across projects only if the length and delivery method of each training are recorded alongside attendance, as CGIAR's minimum data standard requires.

De-duplication is reliable within a project (registry identifiers exist for farmers and households) but not across projects (there is no institute-level registry), so institutional totals are upper estimates wherever identifiers cannot be reconciled across projects.

Partner-delivered and cascade training depend on partner attendance records of variable quality; unlinked partner counts can inflate reach and must stay visibly separate from the registry-based total.
subMetrics: None. Sex and age are disaggregations of the same count, not sub-metrics. Related indicators with their own sheets: KPI-O04 (number of individuals trained annually by CIMMYT, the institution-wide count that overlaps this one for training delivered by CIMMYT or under a project agreement), KPI-O20 (farmers reached through innovation-package access, the sibling delivery channel), and KPI-OC16 (percentage of assisted persons reporting adoption of new or improved inputs, technologies or practices, the outcome this output feeds per the register roll-up).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project field and training teams and implementing partners, via event attendance registers. Validation: project MEAL officer (registry matching and de-duplication). Calculation: project M&E, per Calculation method. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 1 · Innovation development & scaling — Reference sheet KPI-O18

name: Number of farmers in CIMMYT intervention areas accessing improved technological packages
resultsLevel: Output
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Contributing: PO1 (Defined by transdisciplinarity, CIMMYT is an efficient, innovative, and inclusive partner contributing to agrifood systems transformation), PO2 (Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries), PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs, following the primary objective PO3. Stable for this indicator because it counts people rather than result objects. Per the pathway convention, set per strand rather than per indicator group, as the Introduction sets out, since two of the three groups run more than one strand.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest correspondence is SDG target 2.3, whose text names secure and equal access to productive resources, inputs and knowledge for small-scale food producers, but its indicators measure results rather than access: 2.3.1 is volume of production per labor unit and 2.3.2 is average income of small-scale food producers. Neither counts people reached with access, so no direct SDG indicator mapping exists.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Results Framework (Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30): no output-level people-reach category exists (outputs are innovation development, capacity sharing and knowledge products); the nearest CGIAR measure is the outcome-level innovation-use count (number of people using the innovation, disaggregated by gender and youth), which sits downstream of this indicator at KPI-OC16's level.
definition: Counts the unique farmers in CIMMYT intervention areas who accessed improved technological packages (seed, inputs, agronomic advisories, mechanization) in the reporting year, counted once per farmer regardless of the number of packages. A farmer "accesses" a package when they come into direct contact with at least one package component delivered or facilitated by CIMMYT or its implementing partners: receiving or purchasing improved seed or inputs through a project-linked channel, receiving an agronomic advisory service, or using a mechanization service. The contact must be a significant intervention, the threshold set in Eligibility criteria and missing data. Access is the opportunity to use an innovation, not its use (KPI-OC16).
rationale: Answers how many farmers CIMMYT's innovation pathway reached with something they could use: the count of people given a real opportunity to take up an improved technology. It is the reach base of the innovation results chain: together with farmers trained (KPI-O18) it defines the population of assisted persons from which the adoption rate (KPI-OC16) is read, and it evidences the delivery effort behind innovations adopted at scale (KPI-OC01). Used by project management to track delivery breadth and by institutional and donor reporting on the reach of CIMMYT's work.
projectSpecificApplication: State the package components the project offers (seed, inputs, advisories, mechanization, or a subset), the delivery channels used (direct distribution, partner agrodealers or service providers, digital advisory platforms), and the geographic intervention area covered. Qualifying items are those on the project's promoted-item list, approved with its MEAL plan and frozen for the reporting year; the CIMMYT MEAL unit holds the lists. Do not alter the unique-farmer counting rule or the access threshold. If applying the indicator as defined is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this reach count informs: for example a donor-required beneficiary-reach indicator, or an internal delivery milestone that triggers corrective action if access numbers fall behind the seasonal plan.
projectTypesNotApplicable: none. Any project type can put an improved technology or package within farmers' reach
projectTypesRaw:
Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: none. Any project type can put an improved technology or package within farmers' reach.
unit: Number of farmers (unique individuals)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more farmers obtained access to an improved technological package; it establishes reach, not learning, use or benefit. Agronomic advisories count here only where delivered as a service outside a training event, which is what separates this indicator from KPI-O18.
disaggregationRequired: Required: Sex (female/male at minimum); Age (youth/non-youth, youth defined as 15 to 30, stated once in Core Section 4.1). Projects record date of birth or exact age, not an age band, so any donor's cut, for example a donor band of 15 to 29, can be derived without recollecting data.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Package component (seed, other inputs, agronomic advisories, mechanization): a farmer accessing several components appears under each, so component counts sum to more than the unique-farmer total and must never be added together. Smallholder / non-smallholder, as Annex B defines it; ownership of the land or livestock is not required. Access channel (direct delivery vs partner-facilitated). Geography or agroecological zone.
unitOfObservation: Individual (farmer)
calculationSummary: Value = the count of unique farmers with at least one qualifying access event, or a qualifying service period, in the reporting year (Eligibility, Repeated observations), de-duplicated by farmer identifier. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: the project beneficiary registry and delivery records (distribution lists, service records, digital advisory platform logs, partner reporting from assisted agrodealers and service providers), built on CIMMYT's standard registration template with unique farmer identifiers (traditional plus biometric references). Fallback DS1: a farmer survey module estimating access in the reporting year, used only where a delivery channel produces no usable records (for example open-market sales by partner-supported input suppliers); flag any survey-based figure as fallback-sourced. Not applicable DS3: an access event is a transaction between a farmer and a delivery channel; it cannot be observed from satellite or GIS data. Not applicable DS4: national or international statistics do not resolve CIMMYT intervention areas and cannot attribute access to CIMMYT-supported channels. Not applicable DS5: unverified crowdsourced claims of access cannot be de-duplicated against the registry; logs from a CIMMYT-run digital advisory platform are administrative records (DS2), not citizen-generated data.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether Recommended or Fallback was used per channel. If Fallback, state which channels lacked records, the survey design used to estimate access, the population the survey sample was drawn from and its size, with the source of that size where it is itself an estimate, and why record-based counting was not feasible.
collectionInstrument: For the Fallback DS1 only: a short access module in the project farmer survey asking whether the respondent obtained each package component through the project or its partner channels during the reporting year. Respondent: the farmer. Mode: face-to-face or phone interview. Where the Recommended DS2 source is used, no instrument applies: the record system itself is the source.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as access events are recorded in delivery and partner records; consolidated at least annually. Fallback survey measurement: annually.
referencePeriod: The reporting year: January to December at institutional level. Projects following a donor fiscal year (for example USDA October to September, FCDO April to March) may report on that year and must state which year basis applies.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual delivery count: before the intervention the value is zero by construction, so a pre-intervention baseline carries no information. The first reporting year serves as the reference point for reach trajectories.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. Weight: one each per unique farmer, whatever the number of packages or components accessed. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool registry-based (Recommended) records across projects and count distinct farmers as Block B sets out; a channel reported through a survey-based Fallback estimate is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, never blended in, because a survey estimate and a registry count have different error structures; the same project's registry-recorded channels are pooled.

B: Combination method: sum of distinct persons. Within a project, unique farmers on the registry identifier. Across projects, the union of the registries where they share an identifier; otherwise the sum of project counts, labeled an upper estimate, with the share of the total that comes from reconciled registries stated.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of unique farmers recorded as having gained access in the reporting year, de-duplicated on the project's registry farmer identifier. At institutional level, the count of unique farmers across projects, de-duplicated again across registries where they share an identifier: a farmer who gained access to two packages, or through two projects, is one farmer. Where identifiers cannot be reconciled, the institutional figure is the sum of project counts and is labeled an upper estimate. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the reconciliation basis, the number of records dropped for want of an identifier, and the number of access records dropped for want of an event date.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count does not add arithmetically to KPI-OC16 or KPI-OC01; note however that the registry-matched persons in this indicator's access records since project start, dated or not, together with those trained (KPI-O18), form the de-duplicated union from which KPI-OC16's denominator is drawn, a population dependency rather than arithmetic, so the three sheets must use consistent identifiers.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: within a project, unique farmer identifiers from the beneficiary registry make the count exact for registry-matched records, no upper-estimate caveat is needed on that total. Across projects, farmer identifiers are reconciled where the registries share one; where they cannot be reconciled, the cross-project total carries the label Block C sets out. Overlap with other register indicators: a farmer counted here may also be counted under KPI-O18 (trained) and KPI-O19 (linked to financial services); these indicators must never be summed into a combined "farmers reached" figure without de-duplication across them. Values are also not summable across reporting years, because new and continuing farmers are not separated; a multi-year total requires de-duplication across years by identifier. The registry count is a census of registry-matched records and has no sampling error to report. A Fallback survey estimate of a channel's access is a sample estimate, the weighted share of sampled farmers reporting access through that channel multiplied by the size of the population the sample was drawn from, reported beside the registry count with its coverage and precision on the coefficient-of-variation bands: 16.5 percent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 percent released flagged, above 33.3 percent not released as an estimate. The coefficient-of-variation bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records; below 30 the estimate is not released. A record is one completed survey interview with a sampled farmer in the reporting year. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: farmers located in the project's intervention area whose access event was delivered or facilitated by CIMMYT or its implementing partners, including purchases from partner-supported channels (for example an assisted agrodealer). A qualifying access event, on CIMMYT's own convention, is one in which the named farmer individually receives a package component: seed or input transferred to or bought by them and recorded against their identifier; an advisory delivered to them or to a group of individually registered members; or a mechanization service on their plot. Each access event is recorded with its date and, for a service with a duration (a digital advisory subscription, scheduled extension visits), the end date of its service period.

Exclusion: contacts with an unregistered audience, below the significance threshold set by Inclusion (mass events, broadcasts); attendance at a field day, demonstration or sensitization meeting, whether or not attendees are registered; participation in a structured training event, which is counted by KPI-O18 and not by this indicator, so the advisory component covers only advice delivered as a service outside a training event (a digital advisory subscription, a scheduled extension visit, a service-provider recommendation attached to an input); indirect beneficiaries with no access event of their own (neighbors copying a practice, household members of the accessing farmer).
limitations: Measures opportunity, not use: a rising access count says nothing about whether farmers adopted anything. Read it only alongside the adoption outcome (KPI-OC16); reach is an output, not an outcome, and reach without adoption is delivery with no behavior change to show for it.
