Insensitive to intensity: a farmer receiving one seed packet counts the same as a farmer receiving the full package all season. The significance threshold sets a floor, but the count cannot distinguish light from deep engagement.

Channel-dependent accuracy: direct-delivery counts come from CIMMYT's own registry and are exact for registry-matched records. Partner-facilitated channels (for example agrodealer sales) count only records carrying the farmer identifier; unmatched records are excluded from the unique count and reported separately, per Eligibility; a channel with no usable identifier-matched records is estimated by the Fallback survey and reported apart from the registry-based total.

Comparability across projects is limited because each project's promoted-item list is its own: two projects can set different standards for what qualifies as an improved package, so a pooled figure mixes those standards rather than applying one throughout.
Annual values are not a cumulative reach series: the same farmer reappears each year they access a package, so summing years overstates unique reach.
subMetrics: None. Package components (seed, inputs, advisories, mechanization) are disaggregations of the same count, not separately calculated metrics. Related indicators in the results chain have their own sheets: KPI-O18 (farmers trained, the parallel reach output), KPI-OC16 (share of assisted persons reporting adoption, whose denominator this indicator co-defines), and KPI-OC01 (share of released innovations adopted at scale).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project field team and implementing partners maintaining the beneficiary registry and delivery records. Validation: project MEAL officer (identifier de-duplication and channel record checks). Calculation: project M&E, per the calculation method above. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 1 · Innovation development & scaling — Reference sheet KPI-O20

name: Number of research priorities formally co-defined with smallholder farmers
resultsLevel: Output, per CIMMYT's MEAL Framework, which defines an output as a delivered result: a priority-setting exercise and an agenda entry are both delivered products, not changes in anyone's behavior or practice. Whether the portfolio responds is the change, and it is measured at KPI-OC23. CGIAR's control-and-externality test gives the same level.
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved, whose sub-objective 3.1 is the closest sentence in the Strategy to this indicator's subject. Contributing only: PO1, grounded in the Strategy's partnership commitment to active listening and co-defining objectives with partners. PO3 is primary because sub-objective 3.1 describes this indicator's subject verbatim, while PO1 describes the way of working and is contributing.
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs, following the primary objective PO3. Stable for this indicator: the unit counted is a research priority stated by smallholder farmers, so what is measured is farmer influence over the research agenda rather than the thematic content of any one priority, and that influence sits in this area whatever the priority is about. Per the pathway convention, set per strand rather than per indicator group, as the Introduction sets out, since two of the three groups run more than one strand.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest target, SDG 2.a (increase investment in agricultural research and extension), is measured by indicator 2.a.1, the agriculture orientation index for government expenditures, a spending ratio that says nothing about who sets research priorities.
otherFrameworks: None identified. CGIAR's standard output categories (Knowledge Product, Innovation Development, Capacity Sharing for Development) do not cover participatory agenda-setting, and the CGIAR Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 handles prioritization through innovation portfolio management, not an indicator of farmer co-definition. The definition is CIMMYT's own; no donor framework with a close variant has been identified.
definition: Counts the distinct research priorities, formally co-defined with smallholder farmers through documented participatory priority-setting, that were first entered into CIMMYT's research agenda in the reporting year. A research priority is a problem, need, trait or research question that farmers themselves state and rank, written specifically enough for a research team to act on ("reduce grain loss to stem borer in late-planted maize", not "improve maize"). Two conditions must both hold, formally co-defined and entered into CIMMYT's research agenda, and both are specified in Eligibility criteria and missing data. Counts distinct priorities, not exercises, not farmers, not the research that follows.
rationale: Answers whether the people the research is for are setting what it works on. The 2030 Strategy commits, under Primary Objective 3, that "The aspirations and needs of smallholder farmers drive and consistently inform the agrifood research agenda"; this count is the most directly attributable evidence of that commitment, since co-defining and entering a priority are acts CIMMYT controls and can document. It is the input step to KPI-OC23 and serves donors requiring evidence of demand-driven design.
projectSpecificApplication: State the farmer groups engaged, countries and sites, crops or systems covered, and the reporting-year boundary. The counting unit, qualifying conditions and calculation method stay unchanged; if the indicator cannot be applied as defined, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision, donor requirement or reporting need the count serves: for example adaptive management comparing the priorities farmers ranked highest against the activities budgeted.
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, which sets its research agenda ahead of and independently of a farmer co-definition exercise.
unit: Number of distinct research priorities (not exercises, farmers, or resulting research activities)
directionOfChange: Increase, read with the granularity caution in section 6 (Limitations and interpretation). A rising value means more research priorities co-defined with smallholder farmers through documented participatory priority-setting were first entered into CIMMYT's research agenda that year. Finely written priorities inflate the count without any change in substance.
disaggregationRequired: Required: sex composition of the farmers taking part in the priority-setting exercise behind each priority (female / male at minimum), reported as the number of counted priorities ranked in at least one session with female participants, and the female share of all participants across the sessions behind the counted priorities. The counted object is a priority rather than a person, so this is not a breakdown of the count itself but an attribute of how each priority was produced. The session records already list who attended, so the data exists, and why it is required is stated in Limitations and interpretation.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country and site or agroecology; crop or farming system; priority theme (variety and trait, agronomy, pest and disease, mechanization, post-harvest, market, climate risk); the rank farmers gave the priority; type of farmer group; planning-document type; new priority versus restatement.
unitOfObservation: Result object (the research priority itself), one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation. The farmer group that articulated the priority is recorded in the exercise record under Eligibility criteria and missing data, not here.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct research priorities that met both qualifying conditions and were first entered into CIMMYT's research agenda during the reporting year, after de-duplication. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (administrative and registry data): the documentation pack of each exercise (session report, participant list with sex composition, method note, agreed ranked priorities) with the dated planning document carrying the entry. Both halves of the definition are CIMMYT-controlled activities whose records already exist, so the value is a census auditable to a dated document. Each project maintains its own priority list, carrying a local identifier, entry date and source route (Recommended, Fallback DS1 or Fallback DS5) per priority; this project-held list, not an institute-level registry, is what KPI-OC23 maps its numerator against. Fallback DS1 (censuses and surveys): where priorities were elicited from individual farmers through a structured instrument (trait-preference ranking, choice experiment, structured scoring) rather than agreed in a group session, the instrument's aggregated ranking supplies the priority statements, with agenda-entry evidence still from the planning document; flag such priorities as fallback-sourced, since a survey-elicited ranking and a negotiated group list are not interchangeable evidence of co-definition. A group session that agrees its ranking through structured scoring is the Recommended route. Fallback DS5, scoped to a documented ranking exercise on structured digital channels, where a project runs one; a crowdsourced feedback stream with no identifiable participant group or agreed ranked output does not qualify and DS5 stays Not applicable to it. Not applicable: DS3 (geospatial and Earth observation), a negotiated statement cannot be observed remotely. Not applicable: DS4 (secondary and international databases), no third party records which priorities farmers defined with CIMMYT.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role was used. For Recommended, give the number of exercises, groups and sites and the planning document entered into. For Fallback, name the priorities that entered through it and the instrument used, and state why group priority-setting was not used for them.
collectionInstrument: Applies to the DS1 fallback route: a structured priority or trait-preference elicitation module with an explicit ranking or scoring method and a documented option set including an open "other" category; the option set is drawn from a prior documented farmer session or left open, since an option set fixed by researchers alone does not meet the Definition's farmer-stated test, and only farmer-added "other" entries qualify from such a set. Respondent: the sampled smallholder farmer, no proxy ranking. Mode: face-to-face or facilitated tablet-assisted session. The Recommended DS2 route is a documentation standard, not an instrument; its minimum record fields are in Eligibility criteria and missing data.
collectionFrequency: Continuous: exercises and entries are documented as they happen, then compiled and de-duplicated once per reporting year.
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the priority was entered into the research agenda: January to December at institutional level; projects on a donor year state which they use. Where exercise and entry fall in different years, the entry date governs. A within-year count, not a cumulative stock.
baselineRequired: No. An annual count starts from zero each year and is interpretable without a prior-period value. For a trend, the reference year is the first year the documentation standard was applied; earlier undocumented years are not comparable. A farmer-responsiveness change claim belongs to KPI-OC23, which is a share.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One reporting year and one research agenda: priorities entered in the same reporting year may enter one figure, and priorities from different years are reported side by side and never summed. Weight: one each, since the counted object is the priority and no priority counts for more than another. (2) Across projects: pool Recommended-sourced priorities by taking the union of de-duplicated priority lists; a priority that entered through a Fallback route is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note naming it and its route, never blended in; the same project's Recommended-sourced priorities are pooled.

B: Combination method: sum. The institutional figure is the count of distinct priorities across projects, taken after de-duplication; never add project totals without de-duplicating first.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying co-defined research priorities for the reporting year. At institutional level, the de-duplicated sum of those counts, computed from the records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one priority is often co-defined in more than one community or project. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the number of candidate priorities excluded under Eligibility and why, the articulated-but-not-entered figure (Sub-metrics), the documentation residual (Eligibility, Missing data), and the number of priorities reported alongside as Fallback-sourced, by route.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: no. The count does not combine arithmetically with KPI-OC23 or KPI-I01; levels connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative. One non-arithmetic dependency: this indicator's priority list is the reference list for OC23's numerator, a lookup, not a sum; changing what counts as a priority here changes what OC23 measures, so the two sheets are revised together.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: the same priority raised in several sessions or projects counts once. Priority statements carry a project-level identifier and entry date (Data source), but no institute-level registry or cross-project identifier scheme exists, so cross-project de-duplication still needs a documented matching step (same crop, constraint and target environment) with a named arbiter for near-matches; where that cannot be performed, publish the pooled figure as a labeled upper estimate. Across years, never sum: a priority counts only in its entry year.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: "formally co-defined" means the priority came out of a documented participatory exercise in which smallholder farmers took part in identifying and ranking priorities, so informing farmers of decisions already taken or interviewing them for background only does not qualify; "entered into CIMMYT's research agenda" means the priority appears in a dated planning document (workplan, concept note, product profile, proposal, or program priority list).

Smallholder farmers took an active part in identifying and ranking the priority (participants are the smallholder farmers the exercise was convened for, as the session record identifies them; "smallholder" here qualifies the priority, so no per-farm threshold is applied, and ownership of the land or livestock is not required); the exercise has a dated record naming facilitator, location, participant numbers and composition, method, and the agreed ranked priorities (for the Fallback DS1 route, the aggregated ranking the instrument produced); and the priority is recorded in a dated planning document.
limitations: Measures agenda-setting, not research and not influence: a priority can be co-defined, entered in a workplan, and never worked on. Whether the portfolio responds is KPI-OC23's question.

The count is highly sensitive to how finely a priority is written. The actionable-specificity test sets a floor on vagueness but no ceiling on splitting: one project's single priority is another's six, so comparisons are weak and the number can be inflated by writing finely.

Whose priorities were counted matters more than how many: participatory exercises over-represent male, better-resourced, better-connected farmers unless deliberately structured otherwise, and the headline number cannot show the difference. This is why the sex-composition cut is required: if only men attend the sessions, a "farmer-defined" agenda is a men's agenda and the count would report success regardless.

The value reflects what was documented, not what happened: well-documented projects appear more farmer-responsive than equally participatory ones whose sessions were never written up. Read a low value as a possible documentation gap first.

A rise means more farmer-defined priorities were formally entered that year; not that the agenda changed in substance, that the highest-ranked priorities were taken, or that farmers gained influence. Read it with KPI-OC23 and the articulated-but-not-entered residual.
subMetrics: One required companion figure: articulated but not entered, the count of priorities farmers stated in a qualifying session that were not written into a planning document within the reporting year, each counted once, in the year first articulated. Reported alongside the main count, never subtracted from it. Otherwise none: theme, crop, rank, group type and document type are disaggregations of one count. KPI-OC23 (outcome) takes this priority list as the reference for its numerator, never combined arithmetically; KPI-O01 (same level) counts things made with partners, not questions set with farmers; the two are never summed.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the program or research-unit leader as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: the project research and social-science team, or the partner organization, facilitating the exercise and producing the documentation pack. Validation: project MEAL officer checks inclusion criteria, confirms the agenda-entry reference, and de-duplicates within the project and year. Calculation: project MEAL officer produces the project value; the CIMMYT MEAL unit performs cross-project de-duplication and pooling. Approval: project leader, with the program or research-unit leader confirming the agenda entry. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 1 · Innovation development & scaling — Reference sheet KPI-O25

name: Number of active partnership and sub-grant agreements with local and Global South partners
resultsLevel: Output, per CIMMYT's MEAL Framework, which defines an output as a delivered result: an agreement in force is an instrument CIMMYT has produced, and the CGIAR quality-assurance guidance lists partnerships arising from a signed memorandum of understanding among its own output examples. Whether the sub-grant portfolio is equitable is the change, and it reads one level up, at KPI-OC60.
primaryObjective: Partnership (institutional component). The mapping is direct: the component's stated "Why we partner" objectives include institutionalizing CIMMYT's interventions and building the capacity of local organizations to innovate, collaborate and scale, and its ways of working commit to enhancing grant management systems and "streamlining sub-granting and project oversight" as part of remaining a partner of choice. Sub-grants also appear under Excellence in Operations as delivery logistics; this indicator sits under Partnership because it measures the relationship the instrument creates, not its administrative processing.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. This indicator measures CIMMYT's own partnering practice, not a result delivered to an external population, so it does not map to any of the five CGIAR Impact Areas.
sdgTarget: None. The thematically closest target is SDG 17.17 (effective public, public-private and civil society partnerships), but its official indicator 17.17.1 measures United States dollars committed to public-private partnerships for infrastructure, not a count of agreements or the devolution of roles to local organizations.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR has no standard indicator counting partnership or sub-grant agreements: the 32 standard indicators contain none, and the Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 instead adds a partner engagement/partnership building result category and foresees possible new engagement indicators (Intensity of Partnerships, due diligence). ICARDA's OP-12 (Number of partnerships established) and its derived OP-12.1 (agreements signed or renewed) are the nearest external counts, but neither restricts to local and Global South partners nor isolates sub-grants, so values are not comparable. Hence a CIMMYT-own definition.
definition: Counts the partnership and sub-grant agreements between CIMMYT and local or Global South partner organizations active in the reporting year, meaning in force at any point between January and December, from their year of signature. A sub-grant agreement is an instrument under which CIMMYT passes funds and defined implementation roles to a partner organization under an award CIMMYT holds: the vehicle through which CIMMYT devolves resources and responsibilities to partners. Distinct from KPI-O03 in scope, not in instrument class: KPI-O03 counts formal partnership agreements with any partner, and this indicator is restricted to local and Global South partners. An instrument meeting both definitions is counted on both sheets; the aggregation rule sets out why and forbids adding the two.
rationale: The 2030 Strategy's Partnership component commits CIMMYT to build the capacity of local organizations to innovate, collaborate and scale, with streamlined sub-granting among its ways of working. This indicator answers, for leadership and the partnerships function, whether that commitment shows up in practice: how many live agreements place local and Global South organizations in resourced, responsible roles. It is drawn from the same grants and contracts records as KPI-OC60 and feeds the partner-of-choice narrative read at KPI-I01.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator: computed once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate grants and contracts records, no project instance to adapt it to).
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it counts CIMMYT's own active agreements and is computed once at institutional level.
unit: Number of agreements (distinct signed instruments, not partner organizations or countries)
directionOfChange: Increase, read together with KPI-OC60. A rising value means more active partnership and sub-grant agreements are held with local and Global South partners. The count shows the breadth of devolved partnering, not its equity or the value of the resources devolved.
disaggregationRequired: Required: partner/institution type (per the register; uses the confirmed 13-category list shared with KPI-O03, KPI-OC03, KPI-OC05 and KPI-OC60); instrument class (partnership agreement / sub-grant agreement), added by this sheet; partner origin (local to the country where the work takes place / other Global South); agreement status (new in the year / continuing), classified by signing year as on KPI-O03, since a stock cannot be read for the year's flow without it. An instrument with several qualifying partners is classified once for these cuts, as Calculation method sets out, so the cuts stay additive. Sex and age do not apply: the counted unit is an agreement, not a person.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country or region; CIMMYT program or project; agreement value band, for sub-grants the funds devolved (USD).
unitOfObservation: Result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation: the agreement, meaning one distinct signed instrument of either class, partnership or sub-grant, which can bind several organizations.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct agreements meeting all three criteria: (a) a written instrument signed by CIMMYT and at least one partner organization that is local to the country where the work takes place or based in the Global South; (b) instrument class is a formal partnership agreement as KPI-O03 defines it (a signed instrument setting out shared objectives and each party's obligations) or a sub-grant agreement (funds and defined implementation roles passed to the partner under an award CIMMYT holds); (c) active in the reporting year: in force at any point between 1 January and 31 December, from its year of signature. Boundary definitions, confirmed: local partner, an organization legally registered and headquartered in the country where the work takes place; Global South, countries on the OECD DAC List of ODA Recipients, the edition effective for reporting on 2025 flows, stated with the value. A partner is based in the Global South where its signing legal entity is registered in a country on that list, and for an instrument covering several countries it is local where it is local to any one of them. An instrument with several qualifying partners is classified once for the required cuts, on one Global South partner: its lead recipient where that recipient is in the Global South; otherwise the Global South partner with the largest stated allocation; otherwise the first Global South partner named in the instrument. Where no qualifying partner is in the Global South, the same order applies to the qualifying local partners. For a partnership agreement, which names no recipient or allocation, the lead recipient in this order is the partner the instrument names as lead, and the allocation step does not apply. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (administrative and registry data): CIMMYT's grant-management and contracts records, where sub-grant and partnership instruments are filed with their signature and end dates, covering centrally held, project and country-office instruments; the filed instrument is the evidence, no separate measurement is required. CIMMYT's Legal team holds these instruments and each carries a unique number, so the record set is de-duplicable. Fallback DS1 (surveys): a structured annual return in which project leaders and country representatives enumerate the agreements active in the year, used only for an agreement a project or country office reports whose signed instrument the corporate records do not hold; flag such agreements as fallback-sourced, since self-reported enumeration is more exposed to omission and status errors. Not applicable DS3: geospatial data cannot establish that a legal instrument exists or is in force. Not applicable DS4: no third-party database independently records CIMMYT's agreements, CGIAR systems holding only downstream copies of CIMMYT's own submissions. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced data cannot establish the existence or status of a signed instrument.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: For the DS1 fallback only: a structured annual return, one row per agreement, listing instrument reference, each partner with its partner type, country of registration and headquarters country, the lead partner or recipient and any allocation by partner the instrument states, partner origin, instrument class, signature and end dates, countries covered, and the CIMMYT unit holding the instrument. Respondent: the project leader or country representative accountable for the agreement. Mode: electronic return with the instrument or its reference attached. For the Recommended DS2 route: not applicable, the filed instrument is the record itself.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as instruments are filed and closed in grants and contracts records; consolidated once a year at year-end.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Each annual value is a stock; values are never summed across years.
referencePeriod: The reporting year, January to December at institutional level. The value describes agreements in force at any point in that window, from their year of signature: a stock, not the year's new signings.
baselineRequired: No. Each year's value is a self-standing stock; change is read from the year-on-year series, and the first reported year serves as the reference point.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. Weight: one each per distinct signed agreement, whatever its value or the number of parties to it. (2) Across CIMMYT units: sum the agreements the Recommended corporate records hold; agreements known only through the Fallback annual return are reported alongside the pooled figure with their count and a note naming them, never blended in.

B: Combination method. Sum distinct active agreements after de-duplication, always reporting the instrument-class split alongside the total.

C: Levels and operations. Computed once at CIMMYT-wide level, as the de-duplicated count taken from the agreements records themselves rather than by adding unit figures, since one agreement can be reported by every CIMMYT unit party to it. There is no Project area figure: this indicator has no project instance, as Project types that apply states. Also report: the number of active partnership and sub-grant agreements excluded under Eligibility and why, the number of agreements known only through the Fallback return, the number of this sheet's agreements also counted by KPI-O03, and the number of agreements first on file after the value for their signature year was compiled, which enter no new subtotal.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: no, values at different levels are never added. The count connects to KPI-OC60 (outcome) and KPI-I01 (impact) through the Theory of Change; OC60 is derived from the same record set, not from this reported value. (2) With KPI-O03: never. An instrument meeting both definitions is counted on both sheets, so the two values overlap by construction and adding them double-counts every shared instrument. No figure combines them, at any level. Each sheet publishes the number of instruments it shares with the other, which is what makes the overlap visible rather than hidden.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: a multi-party agreement counts once, not once per partner; an agreement covering several projects or countries counts once, attributed to one reporting unit agreed in advance; an instrument held centrally and also logged by a project is one agreement. Every filed instrument carries a unique number issued by CIMMYT's Legal team, so de-duplication is by instrument reference and both instrument classes resolve to a true count, not an upper estimate. This count and KPI-O03 are never summed. An instrument meeting both definitions, for example a capacity-strengthening sub-grant to a Global South partner, is carried by both, by design, and each sheet publishes how many of its instruments the other also counts.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Missing data: an agreement with no retrievable signed instrument, or whose start and end dates cannot be established, when a year's value is compiled is not counted in that value and not imputed; once its instrument and dates are on file it counts in every later compiled year in which it is in force, and values already published are not revised. An agreement known only through the Fallback annual return is reported alongside the pooled figure as Aggregation rule Block A sets out, not among the exclusions.

Repeated observations: one agreement counts once per reporting year whatever the number of amendments or no-cost extensions it carries; an agreement in force across several years counts in each of those years; two distinct agreements with the same partner count as two.
limitations: An active agreement is standing infrastructure, not performance: a dormant sub-grant with no disbursement in the year counts the same as a heavily used one, so pair the count with disbursement or activity data before claiming devolution is working.

The count weights all instruments equally (a single-season sub-grant and a multi-country partnership agreement each count one) and says nothing about the value of resources devolved: the count can rise while the funding passed to partners falls. Totals are only interpretable with the instrument-class and partner-type splits attached. The instrument-class cut is added by this sheet, and not by KPI-O03, because this indicator exists to isolate the sub-granting vehicle, and its sub-grant subset is what KPI-OC60's numerator relates to.

The classification boundaries do the work: what counts as local, as Global South and as a sub-grant each move the total. Global South is the OECD DAC List of ODA Recipients, which is revised on a published cycle, so a value is comparable across years only where the same edition is applied and the edition applied travels with the value.
As a stock, the series is insensitive to churn: expiries offset by new signings leave the value flat. Read the new subtotal, here and on KPI-O03, for the year's flow of new partnering.

A rising count shows CIMMYT holds more such agreements; it does not show that partnership quality improved or that partners gained capacity or standing. Those read at KPI-OC05 and the pathway's outcome level.
subMetrics: None. Instrument class, partner type and partner origin are disaggregations of one count, not sub-metrics. Related sheets: KPI-OC60, which derives its Global South share from the same records; KPI-O03, formal partnership agreements with any partner, a qualifying sub-grant counting on both sheets by design; KPI-I01, the pathway impact.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: the CIMMYT grants-management or contracts function that files sub-grant and partnership instruments for the Recommended route; project leaders or country representatives for the Fallback return. Validation: the partnerships function confirms partner origin and instrument class; grants management confirms signature and end dates. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, applying the rules above. Approval: the partnerships function, which owns the partnering practice this figure describes; grants management compiles it from the instrument records. Reporting: CIMMYT MEAL unit into institutional reporting.
sourceRef: Volume 1 · Innovation development & scaling — Reference sheet KPI-O57

name: Percentage of released co-created innovations adopted at scale by partners or farmers
resultsLevel: Outcome, per CIMMYT's MEAL Framework, which defines outcomes as changes in behaviors, systems, practice, capacity, policy or performance. Uptake at scale is exactly that change: an actor other than CIMMYT carries the innovation to farmers on its own account. CGIAR's control-and-externality test gives the same level.
primaryObjective: PO1 Defined by transdisciplinarity, CIMMYT is an efficient, innovative, and inclusive partner contributing to agrifood systems transformation. Contributing only: PO2, PO3, PO4.
cgiarImpactArea: Recorded per innovation. No single area fits an indicator counting innovations of any kind: a drought-tolerant variety, a biofortified variety and a soil-management advisory map to Climate Adaptation & Mitigation, Nutrition, Health & Food Security and Environmental Health & Biodiversity respectively. Each innovation carries its own tag and the annual total is never reported against one area. Per the pathway convention, set per strand rather than per indicator group, as the Introduction sets out, since two of the three groups run more than one strand.
sdgTarget: None. No SDG indicator measures the share of a research organization's innovations that reach scale. The nearest neighbors measure something else: 2.4.1 is a share of agricultural land area under productive and sustainable agriculture, not of innovations, and 9.5.1 is research and development expenditure as a share of gross domestic product, a spending input not an uptake outcome.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Results Framework: the Innovation use outcome category, standard indicator "number of innovations being used (disaggregated by stage)", carried into 2025-30 unchanged. Adapted rather than adopted: CGIAR counts innovations in use, this indicator expresses uptake as a share of a release cohort. ICARDA: OC-08, innovations being used by next users, the closest cross-center analog, a count rather than a share. Not adopted as the threshold: CGIAR's Innovation Packages and Scaling Readiness self-assessment (readiness levels 0 to 9), because a self-assessed score is not a basis for a KPI; CIMMYT still reports into CGIAR systems where required.
definition: Of the innovations CIMMYT and its partners released for scaling (counted by KPI-OC02), the share that subsequently reach a defined scaling threshold: a public or private actor, farmer organizations included, has institutionalized or funded the innovation's dissemination and that dissemination is not sustained only by continuing CIMMYT project funding or by donor funding channeled through a CIMMYT project; continued CIMMYT technical support does not by itself prevent a crossing. Farmer use enters this indicator only through the actor that carries the innovation to farmers; use by individual farmers is read at KPI-OC16. Both the numerator and the denominator count innovation-and-country pairs from the same release cohort, observed after a defined lag (Reference period).
rationale: Answers the question this pathway exists for: of what CIMMYT and its partners released, how much is carried forward by someone other than CIMMYT on its own account. It separates delivery from activity, and evidences the 2030 Strategy sub-objective that effective and efficient environments for co-creating and scaling relevant, accessible technologies are built through strategic partnerships. Used by institutional and donor reporting as the central evidence of CIMMYT's partner-of-choice standing, and by project management to test a release strategy.
projectSpecificApplication: State which release cohort the value describes (which innovations, released in which years), the observation lag, the partners and countries involved, and the evidence used per innovation-and-country pair. Do not alter the definition, unit, threshold or cohort rule; if the cohort cannot be tracked here, raise it with the MEAL focal point.
projectSpecificRationale: State which donor results line or workplan commitment this share evidences, and what project decision it informs (for example, redirecting scaling investment away from a release channel where nothing crosses the threshold).
projectTypesNotApplicable: none. Any project type can release an innovation that is later adopted
projectTypesRaw:
Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: none. Any project type can release an innovation that is later adopted.
unit: Percentage of released innovation-and-country pairs in the cohort
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of the released innovation-and-country pairs reached the defined scaling threshold. A share is easy to inflate on a small cohort, so the numerator and denominator are published with it.
disaggregationRequired: Required: innovation type (seed or variety / decision-support tool / extension or advisory package / license or other agreement, matching KPI-OC02's release type and classified as KPI-OC02 classifies it, so numerator and denominator can be compared by type); scaling actor type (public sector / private company / non-governmental organization / farmer organization or cooperative / other); release cohort year. Why each is required is stated in Limitations and interpretation.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country and sub-national location; crop or system; partner type; intended CGIAR Impact Area; whether women's or youth organizations are among the scaling partners.
unitOfObservation: Result object: the innovation-and-country pair, meaning one released innovation in one country, matching the object KPI-OC02 counts. The denominator is imported from that indicator, so the two must be in the same unit.
calculationSummary: Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100, computed on a single release cohort. Numerator: innovation-and-country pairs in the cohort with documented evidence that the threshold was reached by the observation date; reach and user numbers are not part of the test. Denominator: all innovation-and-country pairs in that cohort, as KPI-OC02 counts them, including those that never cross; across projects, a pair KPI-OC02 reports alongside as Fallback-sourced is outside both terms (Aggregation rule, Block A). Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: documentary evidence from project, partner and national records, one dated record per counted innovation-and-country pair (dissemination or licensing agreement, partner seed production or sales records, national variety registration and seed certification, extension deployment records, partner reports). Documentation is recommended over expert judgment because CGIAR's quality-assurance guidance requires an innovation-use figure to rest on substantiated actual data, not an estimate. Fallback DS1: a structured partner key-informant instrument, where no documentary trail exists; a pair whose threshold evidence comes only from it is treated as Aggregation rule Block A sets out, since a reported claim of scale is weaker than a record of it. Fallback DS4: CGIAR results-reporting and CGSpace innovation-use entries, only where a project kept no records of its own; these rarely resolve to a cohort. Not applicable DS3: Earth observation can corroborate area under a practice, a different indicator, but cannot establish that a named innovation crossed a threshold. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or mobile data cannot substantiate a documented threshold crossing for a named innovation.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether Recommended or Fallback was used, per innovation-and-country pair if the cohort mixes both; if Fallback, explain why no documentary trail existed.
collectionInstrument: Applicable only where the DS1 fallback is used. Partner key-informant instrument: one interview per scaling partner per innovation-and-country pair; respondent is the manager accountable for the dissemination decision, not a project liaison; mode face-to-face or phone; records what was disseminated, to how many users or over what area, when, and under whose funding. No farmer-side module is fielded for this indicator: use by individual farmers is KPI-OC16's and is never reported as this indicator.
collectionFrequency: Annually, re-observing every open cohort until its observation window closes
reportingFrequency: Annually, always with the cohort year and lag stated; a value is never carried forward unlabeled
referencePeriod: A rolling three-year release cohort observed at a five-year lag: the 2026 value reads the innovation-and-country pairs released in 2019 to 2021, each pair entering the cohort of its own country's release year. The lag runs from the cohort's last release year, so the pairs in one cohort are observed five, six and seven years after their release, and one reported share pools those three follow-up windows. Three-year cohorts are used because a single release year gives a noisy share when annual release counts are small; a five-year lag because varietal seed systems are the slowest and most numerous case, with multiplication alone running two to three seasons before uptake can begin. The lag is set by seed-system timelines and is applied on this sheet's authority; no institutional lag is prescribed. Until five years of release data exist, the value is reported on the earliest available cohort with the actual lag stated, never presented as the full window. The observation date is 31 December of the reporting year. The institutional reporting year is January to December; a project on a donor year states which one.
baselineRequired: No prospective baseline: the denominator is a release cohort, so the indicator cannot be reported until a cohort exists and its lag has elapsed. The first cohort measured becomes the reference point, labeled with its cohort year and lag. A project inheriting earlier releases may build a retrospective cohort from release records, and must say so.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One release cohort read at its lag: innovation-and-country pairs from the same cohort pool across projects, crops and countries, country being part of the counted pair rather than a separate domain. Weight: one each per innovation-and-country pair, whatever the reach of its uptake. (2) Across projects: pool the cohort's pairs. A pair KPI-OC02 reports alongside as Fallback-sourced is outside both terms; a pair whose threshold evidence came only through a Fallback route (DS1 or DS4) stays in the denominator and out of the numerator of the pooled figure. The number of each, with the number the Fallback evidence shows as crossing, is reported beside the pooled figure with a note naming the pairs and their route, never blended in.

B: Combination method. Pool numerators and denominators separately across projects and divide once at institutional level; never average project percentages.

C: Levels and operations. A share is recomputed at every level from its own numerator and denominator, never averaged from the levels beneath it: a mean of project percentages weights a project of thirty equally with one of three thousand. At project level, adopted innovation-and-country pairs in the cohort over all innovation-and-country pairs in that cohort for that project. At institutional level, the summed numerator over the summed denominator, within the pooling domain of Block A. Both sums are taken over the de-duplicated cohort records Block E describes, never over project figures added together. The denominator is a cohort, so the share is recomputed against that cohort's own size at every level and never against the current year's releases. Also report: the numerator and the denominator itself, the cohort years and lag, the threshold in force, the number of units excluded under Eligibility, and the number of pairs with no traceable evidence either way, since a share without its denominator cannot be read.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: no. The same innovation appears at co-development (KPI-O01), validation (KPI-O02) and release (KPI-OC02), so summing across levels counts the same objects repeatedly; levels connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative, not arithmetic. The one legitimate arithmetic link is internal: the denominator comes from a past KPI-OC02 cohort, never from the current year's release count.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: a live risk, since innovations carry no institutional identifier and one released or scaled through several CIMMYT projects, or jointly with another CGIAR center, can enter the pooled cohort twice. The cohort is the release records KPI-OC02 pools for the cohort years, de-duplicated and keyed as KPI-OC02 keys them; it is not re-de-duplicated here, and threshold evidence attaches to those records. Where KPI-OC02 could not reconcile a pair across projects, the share is labeled not de-duplicated, with the number of pairs reported by more than one project stated where known; the bias can run either way, since an undetected duplicate enters the denominator always and the numerator only if it qualifies. Two overlaps are named rather than assumed away: KPI-OC16 measures the same uptake from the person's side, so the two are never added; and market or business-model innovations counted under the market systems indicators also satisfy this definition and are inside the cohort, necessarily, since this indicator's denominator is KPI-OC02's release cohort, so the two are never summed.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: innovation-and-country pairs, one per country of release, whose innovation was formally released or packaged for scaling as KPI-OC02 counts it, whether or not CIMMYT was the sole releasing entity; the partner test is applied once, at co-development (KPI-O01), and KPI-OC02 admits only co-developed innovations.

Exclusion: pairs whose innovation is still under development or validation (not yet in a cohort); uptake sustained only by continuing CIMMYT project funding or by donor funding channeled through a CIMMYT project, which is not evidence that anyone else adopted it and puts no pair in the numerator.

Missing data: a pair with no traceable evidence either way stays in the denominator and out of the numerator, with the number of such cases reported alongside the value, so weak follow-up depresses the rate instead of disappearing.

Repeated observations: each innovation-and-country pair counts once per cohort, at its first threshold crossing in that country; an innovation released in several countries is one pair per country and can cross in one country and not another, so it may enter the numerator more than once, exactly as KPI-OC02 counts it in the denominator. Every reported value is labeled with its cohort and lag.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only: whether an innovation scales depends on partner capacity, seed and input systems, policy, prices and demand, so the share alone is never evidence of CIMMYT's effect.
The threshold is institutional independence, not observed use: a documented partner commitment can satisfy it before any farmer receives the innovation.
A ratio hides both the size of the cohort and the size of the uptake: a pair reaching a few hundred thousand users and one reaching tens of millions each count as one crossing, unweighted.

Values are comparable across projects and years only where the same uptake threshold was applied, so the threshold in force travels with every value; every framework that stages uptake this way carries the same requirement.

The value is sensitive to two choices that are not properties of the world, the cohort window and the observation lag: a short lag understates adoption, and changing either breaks the time series. Within one cohort the follow-up window runs from five to seven years (Reference period), so the pooled share mixes pairs that had two more years to cross the threshold with pairs that had less; this is why the cohort-year cut is required. The five-year lag is calibrated to varietal seed-system timelines; for decision-support tools, advisory packages and licenses, whose scaling can complete faster, it does not understate their share but reports it later than those types need.

Innovation type and scaling actor type are required cuts because, without innovation type, the share cannot be read against its own cohort, and the scaling actor must already be identified to apply the threshold test, so recording its type needs no further collection.

A rise means a larger share of that cohort crossed the threshold, nothing more: not that farmers gained yield, income or better diets, which other pathways measure, and not that the uptake will persist.
subMetrics: None. Innovation type, scaling actor type, cohort year, country and crop are disaggregations of one rate, not separate metrics. Related sheets: KPI-OC02 (releases, supplying the denominator), KPI-O01 and KPI-O02 (upstream), KPI-OC16 (adoption from the person's side), KPI-I01 (the partner-of-choice impact statement this indicator feeds).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E officer with the responsible scientist and the scaling or partnership lead, assembling threshold evidence per innovation-and-country pair. Validation: project MEAL officer, against the threshold criteria and evidence rule. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (cohort assembly, pooled numerator and denominator, de-duplication). Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit, which publishes pooled and fallback figures separately.
sourceRef: Volume 1 · Innovation development & scaling — Reference sheet KPI-OC01

name: Number of co-developed innovation releases for scaling, counted per innovation and country of release (seed, decision tools, extension packages, licenses)
resultsLevel: Outcome, per CIMMYT's MEAL Framework, which defines outcomes as changes in behaviors, systems, practice, capacity, policy or performance. A release changes what is available to actors outside CIMMYT, so the value stands. CGIAR's control-and-externality test would read this stage as an output; Core Section 5.4 (CGIAR standard crosswalk) records the divergence once, not indicator by indicator.
indicatorScope: Mission. What is measured is an innovation becoming available to actors outside CIMMYT (seed producers, extension services, licensees, national systems) through project implementation, so the sheet carries the project-specific layer below.
primaryObjective: PO1 Defined by transdisciplinarity, CIMMYT is an efficient, innovative, and inclusive partner contributing to agrifood systems transformation. Its sub-objective is that "effective and efficient environments for co-creating and scaling relevant, accessible technologies, including disruptive solutions, are built through strategic partnerships", and a documented release is where co-creation becomes something a partner can scale. Contributing objectives, contribution only: PO2 (food and nutrition security within planetary boundaries), PO3 (resilient and improved smallholder livelihoods), PO4 (more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient agrifood systems). One primary objective per indicator.
cgiarImpactArea: Recorded per innovation. No single area fits an indicator counting innovations of any kind: a drought-tolerant variety, a biofortified variety and a soil-management advisory map to Climate Adaptation & Mitigation, Nutrition, Health & Food Security and Environmental Health & Biodiversity respectively. Each innovation carries its own tag and the annual total is never reported against one area. Per the pathway convention, set per strand rather than per indicator group, as the Introduction sets out, since two of the three groups run more than one strand.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator counts innovations released or made available for uptake. The nearest, indicator 17.7.1 under target 17.7 (promote the development, transfer, dissemination and diffusion of environmentally sound technologies to developing countries), measures the amount of funding for that transfer, which is money rather than innovations.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR results framework: a partial correspondence to the CGIAR outcome indicator "number of innovation packages designed" under innovation use. Partial, not equivalent, because CIMMYT counts released innovations rather than packages and does not adopt the CGIAR constructs "innovation packages" or "scaling readiness". The definition of record here is CIMMYT's own.
definition: Counts innovation-and-country pairs: each validated innovation formally released, or packaged and made available, for scaling in a country during the reporting year, one count per country of release, marking the transition from a tested innovation to a product available for uptake in that country. Release is a documented event, not a judgment: a variety registered for multiplication, a decision-support tool published for use, an advisory package issued for delivery, or a license letting a partner produce or distribute the innovation. "Innovation" is the CGIAR construct CIMMYT reports against (Claus et al., 2023). Only innovations co-developed with partners (KPI-O01) and validated with farmers and partners (KPI-O02) are eligible.
rationale: Answers whether the innovations CIMMYT builds with its partners leave the research pipeline and become available for others to use, the step where research effort turns into something that can reach farmers at scale. Project teams see whether their release pathway is moving or stuck; CIMMYT and its donors use it as the bridge between what was validated and what is later adopted, and it is the denominator of the adoption share at KPI-OC01.
projectSpecificApplication: State which of the project's innovations are in scope, in which countries release is pursued, and over which project years; the institutional definition, evidence requirement and counting rule are unchanged. Where release runs through a national authority (a variety release committee, a seed regulator), the project names that authority in its MEAL plan so the evidence trail is agreed at the start. A release pathway that does not fit the evidence categories below goes to the CIMMYT MEAL focal point, not into a local redefinition.
projectSpecificRationale: State why this project tracks releases: a donor deliverable expressed as technologies made available for uptake, a milestone tied to national variety release, or the project's need to know whether the regulatory, licensing and packaging steps after validation are on schedule.
projectTypesNotApplicable: none. Any project type can carry an innovation to release
projectTypesRaw:
Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: none. Any project type can carry an innovation to release.
unit: Number of innovation-and-country pairs: one count for each distinct innovation in each country where it was released in the reporting year. An innovation released in three countries counts three.
directionOfChange: Increase, with one caution. A rising value means more innovation-and-country pairs reached availability, through new innovations being released or existing ones reaching further countries; the release-type and country cuts show which. It is a throughput measure and not a quality measure, so the count is meaningful only where the release standard and the counting rule are held constant.
disaggregationRequired: Required for all releases: release type (seed or variety / decision-support tool / extension or advisory package / license or other agreement; type classifies what the innovation is, not how it was released: a licensed variety is seed or variety, and license or other agreement is kept for an innovation whose only released form is the agreement itself); country of release, which is part of the counted object, so the country subtotals add up to the headline. Required for the seed and variety subset only: crop and trait class, since a tool, package or license has no trait class and often no single crop. Trait class takes the toolbox's eight-class controlled vocabulary, the same list KPI-O12 applies: yield and yield potential; abiotic stress tolerance (drought, heat, waterlogging); biotic stress resistance (disease, pest); nutritional quality (including biofortification); end-use and processing quality; agronomic and adaptation traits; and not trait-targeted (genome-wide characterization, identity confirmation, diversity assessment). Not yet characterized does not apply to a release: it is the class for uncharacterized genebank holdings (KPI-O14). Named traits are recorded at a second level within a class rather than instead of it. A release carrying several traits is assigned to the class that justified it and listed under the others in a secondary field, so primary-class subtotals, with the not-available category, add to the seed and variety total, and secondary-field subtotals may exceed it and are never summed. A release whose trait class is blank in the release record, or whose record states that characterization is outstanding, stays in the total and is reported under the not-available category, which records a missing cut rather than a ninth class.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Type of receiving partner (national research system, seed company, extension service, non-governmental organization, other); release route (registration, publication or deposit, license); CGIAR Impact Area served; explicit gender or social-inclusion design feature; validated in the country of release (yes / no), read from the country of validation that the KPI-O02 validation record carries, so computable for every pair.
unitOfObservation: The individual innovation release, meaning one innovation in one country. Result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation.
calculationSummary:
Release evidence, at least one per counted pair, from the country of release: (a) an official variety release, registration or approval certificate from the competent national authority; (b) a dated launch, publication or repository deposit record for a tool, model or advisory package; (c) an executed license, material transfer or commercialization agreement naming the innovation and the receiving partner.

Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended, DS2 (administrative and registry data): the project's innovation and release log holding the release evidence above, with CIMMYT's variety release records, the license and partnership agreement records KPI-O03 and KPI-O57 hold, and CIMMYT's own repository deposit records for tools and knowledge products. A release is an administrative event with a document attached, and the closest donor framework uses the same source class (activity records, reports or surveys).
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role the project used, Recommended (its own release log with evidence attached) or Fallback (national catalogs or repository records other than CIMMYT's own), and if Fallback, name the pairs it evidenced and why the project's own records could not supply the evidence.
collectionInstrument: No survey instrument; the Recommended source is the release log. Projects should still use one standard release-log format (innovation name, release type, crop and trait class where applicable, country, release route, release date, evidence reference, contributing projects) so records are comparable and can be de-duplicated centrally.
collectionFrequency: Continuous. Releases are logged as they occur with the supporting document filed at the same time; the annual figure is compiled at year end.
reportingFrequency: Annually. The value is a within-year count, not a cumulative total; where a cumulative figure is also shown, the start year is stated next to it.
referencePeriod: The reporting year: releases whose documented release date falls inside that 12-month window. The institutional reporting year is January to December; a project on a donor year (for example October to September) reports on that basis and says so.
baselineRequired: No. For a within-year count of new releases the baseline is zero, the convention the closest donor framework also applies. Reporting requires instead the prior-year series as the comparison and, where a cumulative total is presented, an explicit start year.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One reporting year: innovation-and-country pairs released in the same year pool across projects, crops and countries, country being part of the counted pair rather than a separate domain. Weight: one each per innovation-and-country pair, whatever its release type or potential reach. (2) Across projects: count distinct innovation-and-country pairs after de-duplication, never sum project counts, since several projects often contribute to one release. Pool the pairs the Recommended source evidences; a pair evidenced only through a Fallback catalog or repository record is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note naming it, not blended into it, since a catalog record may not confirm CIMMYT's role.

B: Combination method: sum of distinct releases. Institutional total = Σ distinct innovation-and-country pairs after the de-duplication in Block E; project counts are never summed, because several projects often contribute to one release.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying innovation releases, one innovation in one country for the reporting year. At institutional level, the de-duplicated sum of those counts, computed from the records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since several projects often contribute to one release. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the number of innovation releases (one innovation in one country) excluded under Eligibility and why, and the number of pairs reported alongside as Fallback-sourced.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: no. This value never adds to KPI-O01 or KPI-O02, which count the same innovations at earlier steps, and not to KPI-OC01 either, since it is OC01's denominator, a defined arithmetic relationship rather than an aggregation. The levels connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative (co-developed, validated, released, adopted), not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: de-duplicate every release on the innovation and its country of release, whatever the route; for a license-route release the Legal team's unique instrument number, the same number that identifies the instruments KPI-O03 and KPI-O57 count, reconciles license records to that pair, one instrument able to evidence several pairs and several instruments one pair; for any other route, differing internal names are reconciled against the release evidence. CIMMYT holds no institute-level registry or identifier for innovations, so any cross-project pooled figure is an upper estimate until one exists. Two named overlap risks: an innovation released in a previous year does not re-enter the count unless availability extends to a new country; and this indicator is never added to KPI-O12 (varieties released), because a released variety legitimately appears in both and summing them double-counts one event.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: each country in which a co-developed, validated innovation was released inside the reporting year, whether or not CIMMYT is the sole releasing entity. One innovation released in several countries contributes one count per country.

Exclusion: innovations still under validation (KPI-O02); innovations developed without CIMMYT; internal milestones (a completed trial, material passed to another researcher, an internal readiness assessment), none of which make an innovation available to a user; re-issues or minor updates of an innovation already counted in that same country. The last two are CIMMYT's own convention: an internal milestone does not make an innovation available to a user, and a re-issue in a country that already has the innovation reaches no new user. A first release in a further country is not a re-issue: it reaches users who did not have it.
limitations: The counted object is the innovation-and-country pair, and country is therefore load-bearing for the headline rather than only a cut. One innovation released in three countries counts three. Any figure computed on this sheet is larger than one computed on distinct innovations, and a series that spans the change from counting distinct innovations to counting pairs will show a step that is definitional and not a change in CIMMYT's output. State the basis with any comparison across that boundary, and never read a jump at it as growth.

Availability, not use. A release means an innovation can now be taken up, not that anyone did, how many farmers it reached, or how it performed. Uptake sits at KPI-OC01 and KPI-OC16, and reading a release count as impact is the most common misreading of this indicator.

Counts carry no weight. A nationally released staple crop variety and a single advisory leaflet each add one, although their potential reach differs by orders of magnitude. Read the breakdown, not the headline number.

The value is partly outside CIMMYT's control and lumpy in time. Release committees, regulators and partner legal processes set the pace, so a low year may reflect a queue at a national authority and a high year several long-pending approvals clearing at once.

Validation is counted once, not per country. KPI-O02 validates an innovation once and records validation in a further context as a disaggregation, so a pair can enter this count in a country where the innovation was never tested, on validation evidence from another. A release count is therefore not a count of innovations proven for their country of release; the optional validated-in-country cut shows how many pairs rest on evidence from elsewhere.
Record-keeping drives comparability. Projects with well-kept release logs look more productive than projects doing the same work with weaker records.

A movement means the flow of innovations reaching availability changed in CIMMYT's records, not that research quality or farmer benefit changed. Read it with the validation count before it and the adoption share after it.
subMetrics: None. Release type, crop and trait class are disaggregations of one count, not separately calculated metrics. Read the sheet with KPI-O02 (the eligibility gate), KPI-OC01 (which uses this value as its denominator) and KPI-O12 (which overlaps the seed and variety portion).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Project-level roles. Collection: the research or breeding lead for the innovation, who logs the release and attaches the evidence. Validation: project MEAL officer, checking that each counted release carries a qualifying dated document and is not counted twice inside the project. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, which de-duplicates across projects. Approval: project team lead, and the MEAL unit lead for the institutional figure. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 1 · Innovation development & scaling — Reference sheet KPI-OC02

name: Percentage of partners returning to CIMMYT for follow-on work (repeat-partnership rate)
resultsLevel: Outcome. A partner's return is a change in the behavior of an external actor: the partner organization, not CIMMYT, decides to re-engage. Signing the agreement is the controllable act, and it sits below this at KPI-O03.
indicatorScope: Mission, although CIMMYT's own partnering practice sits on the Institutional branch (KPI-O57, KPI-OC60) and this rate is computed once at institutional level: partner-of-choice standing is part of the innovation narrative. The indicator group spans both branches by design.
primaryObjective: PO1: Defined by transdisciplinarity, CIMMYT is an efficient, innovative, and inclusive partner contributing to agrifood systems transformation. The mapping is direct: the strategy names PO1 "The way we work: eager to learn, lead, and be a partner of choice" and commits CIMMYT "to continuing to be a partner of choice"; strategic objectives 1.1 (active engagement with partners around common goals) and 1.4 (co-creation and scaling environments built through strategic partnerships) are the anchors this rate tests behaviorally. Contributing: PO3, through strategic objective 3.3 on strengthening institutions that provide novel technologies and services. PO5 is not a contributing objective: partners returning for follow-on work carries no evidence about the global community taking coordinated measures.
cgiarImpactArea: Recorded per engagement and read per partner organization, the counted unit here being a returning partner: a partner's own engagements are tagged with the area or areas they serve and the repeat-partnership rate is reported both in total and within each area. An area subtotal is a rate over that area's own partner set, not a share of the headline denominator, so area subtotals are not additive to the total. Within an area, the denominator is partners with at least one engagement tagged to that area in the window, and the numerator those with two or more distinct engagements tagged to that area in the window. Per the pathway convention, set per strand rather than per indicator group, as the Introduction sets out, since two of the three groups run more than one strand.
sdgTarget: None. The thematically closest target is SDG 17.17 (effective public, public-private and civil society partnerships), but its official indicator 17.17.1 measures United States dollars committed to public-private partnerships for infrastructure, not partner retention.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR's Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 foresees a possible future "Intensity of Partnerships" indicator (depth and quality of interactions, collaboration frequency, resource-sharing): the nearest CGIAR construct, not yet defined. ICARDA's derived indicator OP-12.1 counts partnership agreements "signed or renewed" at output level; renewal is the nearest external analog to a return. No held framework defines a repeat-partnership rate and the 32 CGIAR standard indicators contain no partnership indicator, so the definition is CIMMYT's own.
definition: Measures the share of CIMMYT's external partners that returned for follow-on work within a defined multi-year window; a proxy for CIMMYT's standing as a partner of choice. A partner that chooses to work with CIMMYT again shows, by its own decision, that the earlier collaboration was worth repeating: the indicator reads partnering effectiveness from partner behavior, not CIMMYT's self-assessment. Numerator: distinct partner organizations with more than one engagement in the window; denominator: all distinct partner organizations engaged in the window. An engagement is a formal partnership agreement as counted under KPI-O03.
rationale: Answers whether the institutions CIMMYT works with come back for more: the behavioral test of the 2030 Strategy's commitment to being a partner of choice. KPI-O03 counts the agreements CIMMYT signs, KPI-OC05 asks partners to rate quality; this indicator observes what partners do next. Serves institutional reporting on partnership performance.
projectSpecificApplication: The rate is computed once, institution-wide: a partner returning through a different project or country office is exactly the signal measured, and a single project cannot see it. The project's role is to feed the computation by reporting every agreement with partner names, types and signature dates under KPI-O03. A project-level repeat rate is meaningful only for long or multi-phase programs and must state its own window; raise departures with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining the indicator here.
projectSpecificRationale: State what the project draws from this indicator, typically a follow-on commitment from named partners as a workplan milestone, and what a non-return triggers, such as an exit conversation feeding the KPI-OC05 partner survey.
projectTypesNotApplicable: none. Any project type can hold a repeat partnership
projectTypesRaw:
Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: none. Any project type can hold a repeat partnership.
unit: Percentage of distinct partner organizations
directionOfChange: Increase, read together with KPI-O03's new-agreement subtotal. A rising value means a larger share of partners returned to CIMMYT for follow-on work. A high return rate over a shrinking or closed partner set is not strength.
disaggregationRequired: Required: partner/institution type. The confirmed category list is: CGIAR center; national agricultural research and extension system (NARES); university or higher education institution; government ministry or public agency; international research organization, non-CGIAR; multilateral or UN agency; regional or sub-regional organization; private company; financial institution; non-governmental or civil society organization; farmer organization or cooperative; foundation; other. If more than 10 percent of records fall to "other" in a year, the list is revised rather than the partners reclassified. Partners are classified at the signing legal entity, so a ministry and its national research institute are two partners in two categories. CGIAR Impact Area is also required, as that field sets out. Sex and age do not apply: the unit is an organization, not a person.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country or region; purpose (co-creation and scaling, capacity strengthening, both); number of engagements per partner (two, three or more); time between first and follow-on engagement; Global South partner marker (read against KPI-OC60).
unitOfObservation: Organization (the partner organization)
calculationSummary: Numerator: distinct partner organizations that are party to two or more distinct engagements whose signature dates fall within the window. Denominator: distinct partner organizations party to at least one engagement in the window. Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (administrative and registry data): the contracts and agreements records that feed KPI-O03, read across the full window, with partner names resolved to distinct organizations; the signed instruments are the evidence. CIMMYT holds no partner master list and no stable partner identifier, so none is named as the matching key: partners are resolved at the signing legal entity, by registered name and country of registration, and the resolution basis travels with the value.
