Fallback DS1 (surveys): a structured annual return in which project leaders and country representatives enumerate their partners and each partner's prior engagements, used only where the records do not resolve partners or do not reach back the full window; engagements known only through the return are reported beside the headline, flagged fallback-sourced and never blended into it, since recalled histories are exposed to omission. Not applicable DS3: partnering cannot be observed from geospatial data. Not applicable DS4: no third-party database records who partners with CIMMYT. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced data cannot establish a signed instrument or a partner's identity.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State how many of the project's engagements rest on the Recommended contracts records and how many are known only through the Fallback return; for the latter, state whether the records did not resolve the partner or did not reach back the full window, and who completed the return.
collectionInstrument: For the DS1 fallback only: a structured annual return, one row per partner, listing partner name and type and each engagement's instrument reference and signature date. Respondent: the project leader or country representative accountable for the partnership. Mode: electronic return with instrument references attached. For the Recommended DS2 route: not applicable, the filed instruments are the record.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as agreements are filed (inherited from KPI-O03); partner identity resolution and the rate computation once per year.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Every reported value states the window it covers.
referencePeriod: A rolling five-year window ending with the reporting year, with engagements assigned to the window by signature date. The reporting year runs January to December at institutional level; projects following a donor year state so.
baselineRequired: No. Each window value stands alone and change is read from the year-on-year series of same-length windows. What is required is an agreements record reaching back the full window: where records fall short, compute over the years available and label the shortened window, since a truncated window mechanically lowers the rate; no change claims across windows of different lengths.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. Weight: one each per distinct partner organization, whatever its number of engagements. (2) Across projects: engagement records from the Recommended contracts records pool before the rate is computed; project-level rates are never averaged into the institutional value. Engagements known only through the Fallback return are not blended into the headline: the rate is computed on the Recommended records, and the Fallback-sourced engagements are reported beside it with their count, so a reader can see how much of the partner history the headline does not reach. A partner identity that links engagements only through the Fallback return is not applied in the headline; the number of such links is reported beside it.

B: Combination method. Computed once at institutional level over the pooled agreements record (pooling is the construct itself; see project-specific application).

C: Levels and operations. Computed once, at institutional level, from the pooled and de-duplicated agreements record: each partner's engagements are counted across every project and office before the partner is classified as returning, so a partner engaged once in each of two projects is a returner. Project numerators are never summed, since a partner's return across projects is invisible to each of them. A project-level rate, where a long or multi-phase program reports one, uses that project's engagements only, states its own window, is labeled as a project view, and never enters the institutional value. Also report: the denominator itself, the number of units excluded under Eligibility, the number of engagements known only through the Fallback return, the number of partner links made only through the Fallback return, and the partner-resolution basis, since a share without its denominator cannot be read.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: no. The rate does not combine arithmetically with KPI-O03 (an agreement count), KPI-OC05 (a quality score) or KPI-I01; they connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative, not arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: the exposure runs both ways. Duplicated engagement records (one agreement filed centrally and by a project) must collapse to one engagement before counting; unmatched identities for one partner (name variants, subsidiaries, mergers) split it into apparent one-time partners and deflate the rate. CIMMYT's confirmed identifier systems cover people, plots, enterprises and facilities, not partner organizations, so until a partner identifier exists, values are published as lower estimates with the resolution method stated. This rate and KPI-OC60 are computed over overlapping but differently scoped instrument sets and never combined.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusions: every external partner organization party to at least one formal partnership agreement in KPI-O03's scope whose signature date falls inside the window, resolved at the signing legal entity, so a ministry and its national research institute are two partners. Engagement rule: an engagement is a formal partnership agreement meeting KPI-O03's criteria (a), (c) and (d), with signature inside the window in place of its criterion (b), so a completed agreement followed by a return still counts; a renewal signed as a new instrument is a new engagement, and an amendment, extension or no-cost variation is not. Partner rule: a partner is the external legal entity that signed; each multi-party agreement contributes one engagement to each external signatory; engagements with different CIMMYT projects or offices belong to one partner.
limitations: Return is a proxy for preference, not proof of it: partners also return because a donor routes funds through CIMMYT or alternatives are scarce, and non-return often means a completed mandate or a deliberately one-off engagement, not dissatisfaction. It supports a contribution claim only; read together with KPI-OC05.

The value is mechanically sensitive to the window and to growth of the partner base: a short window or a fast inflow of first-time partners lowers the rate with no change in partnering quality. Compare only same-length windows, alongside KPI-O03's new-agreement subtotal.

Identity resolution is the main measurement error: name variants, mergers and subsidiary-level signing split one partner into several apparent one-time partners, so reported values understate the rate until a stable partner identifier exists.

The formal-agreements basis under-reads continuity: follow-on collaboration without a new signed instrument, such as work under an extended workplan, never registers as a return, penalizing long-standing relationships.

A rising rate means a larger share of engaged partners re-engaged; it says nothing about the size, value or results of those engagements, and a very high rate with few new partners can signal a closed partner circle rather than strength.
subMetrics: None. Partner type, country and engagement-count splits are disaggregations of one rate, not sub-metrics. Related sheets: KPI-O03 (the agreements that define engagements), KPI-OC05 (partner-rated quality), KPI-O57 and KPI-OC60 (sub-grant instruments, Institutional branch), KPI-I01 (pathway impact).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: the CIMMYT function that files signed agreements, being the legal, contracts or partnerships office as each project's own governance assigns it, for the Recommended route; project leaders or country representatives for the Fallback return. Validation: the responsible partnerships officer resolves partner identities and collapses duplicate engagement records. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, once per year at institutional level. Approval: the responsible partnerships function. Reporting: CIMMYT MEAL unit into institutional reporting.
sourceRef: Volume 1 · Innovation development & scaling — Reference sheet KPI-OC03

name: Annual partnership quality score: partners' rating of CIMMYT partnerships on trust, equity and effectiveness
resultsLevel: Outcome. The score is the partners' own judgment of the relationship: an attitude held by external actors, not a fact about CIMMYT's own action. Establishing the partnership is the controllable act, and it sits below this at KPI-O03.
indicatorScope: Mission, although CIMMYT's own partnering practice sits on the Institutional branch (KPI-O57, KPI-OC60) and this score is measured once at institutional level: partner-of-choice standing is part of the innovation narrative. The indicator group spans both branches by design.
primaryObjective: PO1: Defined by transdisciplinarity, CIMMYT is an efficient, innovative, and inclusive partner contributing to agrifood systems transformation. The strategy names PO1 "The way we work: eager to learn, lead, and be a partner of choice"; strategic objectives 1.1 (active engagement with partners around common goals) and 1.4 (co-creation and scaling environments built through strategic partnerships) name the relationships this score rates. Contributing: PO3, via strategic objective 3.3 (strengthening institutions that provide novel technologies and services). PO5 is not a contributing objective, consistently across the indicator group: although CIMMYT's rapid-response partnerships with UN agencies and governments are the strongest version of the claim, a partner-rated quality score measures the relationship rather than coordinated global action, which is read in the Policy, finance & market systems pathway.
cgiarImpactArea: Read as spanning all areas, with no single value recorded. The indicator summarizes work spanning every area and counts no object that can be tagged with an area, so no area tag is recorded and no distribution across areas is computed. KPI-OC05 and KPI-I01 are the two exceptions to the pathway convention, which sets the area per strand rather than per indicator group, as the Introduction sets out.
sdgTarget: None. SDG 17.16.1 counts countries reporting progress in multi-stakeholder development-effectiveness monitoring frameworks; SDG 17.17.1 measures United States dollars committed to public-private infrastructure partnerships. Neither measures organization-level partner experience.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR's Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 foresees a possible future "Intensity of Partnerships" indicator (depth and quality of interactions): the nearest CGIAR construct, not yet defined. The 32 CGIAR standard indicators contain no partnership indicator, so the definition is CIMMYT's own. The Keystone Partner Survey (Keystone Accountability) is the nearest off-the-shelf instrument for the construct, and it was considered and not adopted because its five question areas do not map onto trust, equity and effectiveness, the three dimensions the register defines (see Collection instrument). The item set is therefore CIMMYT's own, so the score carries no external benchmark and is an internal trend series, not a value comparable with any other organization's partnership score.
definition: An annual composite score of how CIMMYT's partner organizations rate the quality of working with CIMMYT, from a confidential partner survey, on three dimensions: trust (CIMMYT does what it agreed and communicates openly about strengths and limitations), equity (objectives, roles, resources and decision rights are shared) and effectiveness (the partnership delivered and its contracting, payment and day-to-day processes worked). Higher is stronger. Partnership quality is a judgment held by the partner, so only the partner can report it.
rationale: Answers whether partners experience CIMMYT as the collaborator its 2030 Strategy commits it to be: "beyond transactional partnerships", "a partner of choice", "an equitable voice for all involved parties". Each commitment is visible only from the partner's side. KPI-O03 counts the agreements CIMMYT signs, KPI-OC03 observes whether partners return; this indicator asks partners directly, giving management an early, specific warning (a falling equity score) that agreement counts never produce.
projectSpecificApplication: The score comes from one institution-wide partner survey per year, never from parallel project surveys (non-comparable, duplicate burden). A project applies the indicator by keeping its partner records and relationship contacts current in the agreements register, the survey frame's source for partnership and sub-grant agreements. A project view is the institutional score among the project's partner organizations, who rate CIMMYT as a whole; it is labeled so and never reported as a rating of the project. Raise departures with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining the indicator.
projectSpecificRationale: State what the project draws from this indicator: typically its partners' filtered scores as feedback on whether its contracting, payment and decision-making practices work for the organizations doing the work, and any donor requirement for evidence of equitable partnering.
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: the partnership survey is fielded once for CIMMYT and reported at institutional level.
unit: Favorable share per dimension: the percentage of responding organizations' partner sets whose dimension score is 4.0 or above. The composite is the unweighted mean of the three dimension shares, a summary index in percentage points and not the share of any set of organizations; it is never reported without the three dimensions. The raw five-point mean, respondent count and response rate are reported alongside. The favorable share is the headline because it is directly interpretable and moves less than a mean with how strongly an agreeing respondent agrees, which is one way scale use differs across a partner base spanning many countries. It gives no protection against acquiescence, to which a fixed cutpoint is if anything more exposed than a mean (Limitations and interpretation).
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising dimension value means a larger percentage of responding organizations' partner sets score 4.0 or above on that dimension; a rising composite means the mean of the three dimension shares rose. A numeric target is not advised, since it invites managing the survey rather than the partnerships.
disaggregationRequired: Required: partner/institution type, per the register; a global average conceals exactly the equity question the indicator exists to ask. The confirmed category list is: CGIAR center; national agricultural research and extension system (NARES); university or higher education institution; government ministry or public agency; international research organization, non-CGIAR; multilateral or UN agency; regional or sub-regional organization; private company; financial institution; non-governmental or civil society organization; farmer organization or cooperative; foundation; other. If more than 10 percent of records fall to "other" in a year, the list is revised rather than the partners reclassified. Partners are classified at the signing legal entity, so a ministry and its national research institute are two partners in two categories. Sex and age do not apply: the unit is an organization, not a person.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Global South / Global North location, read against KPI-OC60; country or region; relationship length and status; partner role; sub-grant marker (KPI-O57); CIMMYT program or project. Cells below the minimum respondent count are suppressed.
unitOfObservation: Organization (the partner organization)
calculationSummary: A composite survey index. Structure: a fixed item set grouped into the three register dimensions, each item on a five-point agreement scale (1 strongly disagree to 5 strongly agree) with an unscored "cannot say" option. Step 1: responses from the same organization are averaged at item level within each role, partner relationships and funding-agreement relationships forming separate sets, so an organization contributes one partner set, one funder set, or one of each where it holds both roles; one organization, one vote per role, whatever the number of agreements it holds. A qualifying set is a partner set: only partner sets enter the dimension shares and the composite, and funder sets are reported as their own favorable shares per dimension (Aggregation rule, Block C). Step 2: per set, each dimension score is the mean of the items answered with a scored response. Step 3: the reported dimension value is the favorable share, the percentage of responding organizations' partner sets whose Step 2 dimension mean is 4.0 or above. Numerator: responding organizations' partner sets with a dimension mean of 4.0 or above on that dimension; denominator: responding organizations' partner sets answering that dimension under the missing-data rule (Eligibility). The raw five-point mean of the same partner sets is reported alongside it, unrescaled, with the respondent count and response rate. Step 4: the composite is the unweighted mean of the three dimension favorable shares, with the unweighted mean of the three dimension five-point means alongside it. No score is rescaled to a 0 to 100 range: a rescaled mean reads as a percentage and is not one. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1 (censuses and surveys): a confidential survey of CIMMYT's partner organizations, run as a census of the frame. This is the only source that can produce the value: the construct is a judgment held by the partner and nothing else observes it. Frame DS2 (administrative and registry data): the agreements register and, for funding-agreement holders, the resource-mobilization records supply the frame (Eligibility), the partner-type coding and the respondent contacts (Collection instrument), each for the agreements it holds; they support but never source, since no record contains a partner's opinion. Fallback: none exists. In a year the survey is not fielded no new value is reported, the latest value being carried forward with its year of measurement (Reporting frequency); behavioral context (KPI-OC03) may be shown alongside, labeled as context. Not applicable DS3: geospatial data cannot observe whether a partner trusts CIMMYT. Not applicable DS4: no third-party database publishes partner ratings of CIMMYT. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or social-media sentiment is a reputation signal from a different population, not the defined construct.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether the project drew a filtered view of the institutional results; a project never fields its own instrument.
collectionInstrument: Built on the three register dimensions, administered by a contracted third party. The register defines this indicator as partners' rating on trust, equity and effectiveness, so an off-the-shelf survey reporting its own dimensions cannot produce it; the item set is therefore CIMMYT's, worded from the Strategy's own partnership commitments. Administration is contracted out because a partner asked by its own CIMMYT contact will answer politely. The instrument specifies: a fixed item set on the three register dimensions, at least three items per dimension, worded from the Strategy's own partnership commitments rather than invented; a five-point agreement scale with "cannot say"; one respondent per CIMMYT relationship the organization holds, the partner organization's day-to-day relationship holder for that relationship, identified from the respondent contact the agreements register carries for it (Data source), or for a funding agreement the funder-side focal point named on the agreement in the resource-mobilization records, rather than nominated by the partner itself, with an organization's relationships averaged at item level within each role per Step 1; an online questionnaire in the partner base's working languages; and confidential administration by a party that is not the CIMMYT staff member managing the relationship. The off-the-shelf alternative was considered and not adopted: the Keystone Partner Survey (Keystone Accountability) offers anonymous third-party collection with a benchmarked item subset, but its five question areas do not map one to one onto trust, equity and effectiveness, so it cannot produce the register's indicator.
collectionFrequency: Annually, per the register. Partnership quality moves slowly and annual surveying of the same base risks response fatigue, so if the response rate falls below the 50 percent threshold in two consecutive rounds, moving to a biennial cycle should be reconsidered as a register change rather than absorbed silently.
reportingFrequency: Annually. In a year the survey is not fielded, including after a move beyond annual collection, no new value is reported and the latest value is carried forward with its year of measurement stated.
referencePeriod: The reporting year, January to December. The survey is fielded after the year closes, at a date fixed across rounds and stated with the value, and asks respondents to rate that calendar year, not the whole relationship.
baselineRequired: Yes: a single index value has no interpretation alone. The first survey round is the baseline, reported as a level with no change claim. The only additional reference point is cross-partner-type comparison within the same round. No external benchmark exists, so the value is read against CIMMYT's own earlier rounds and against nothing else. Recall-based reconstruction of past partnership quality is not acceptable: recall error would be larger than the change it is meant to detect.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. Weight: one each per responding organization in each dimension's favorable share, an organization holding several partner relationships contributing one averaged partner set (Calculation method, Step 1); the composite weights the three dimensions equally. (2) Across projects: project figures are filtered views of the one institutional result, never independently collected or averaged back together.

B: Combination method. Computed once at institutional level; there is nothing to aggregate upward.

C: Levels and operations. The favorable share is recomputed from the item responses at every level, never averaged from the levels beneath it, and the composite is recomputed from its three dimensions rather than from other composites: a mean of composite scores is not a composite, because the dimension shares of different subsets rest on different numbers of responding organizations. The survey is fielded and reported at institutional level; where a regional or program view is wanted it is recomputed from that subset's own responses. Also report: the raw five-point mean, the respondent count and the response rate with every share, the survey's fielding date, the indicative label where the response rate is below 50 percent, the year of measurement where the value is carried forward, each dimension alongside the composite, the funder sets' favorable share per dimension with their respondent count and the funder response rate, over the organizations holding a funding agreement in the period, an organization responding for this rate where a funding-agreement relationship holder completes, the funder shares being labeled indicative where that rate is below 50 percent, the "cannot say" share for each item, and any dimension whose item set was incomplete.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: no; the score never combines arithmetically with KPI-O03, KPI-OC03 or KPI-I01, which connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: the frame is de-duplicated to the legal entity, so an organization partnered with three projects counts once. This score, KPI-O03 and KPI-OC03 read overlapping portfolios at different levels; the overlap is by design; they are never summed.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusions: every organization holding a partnership or sub-grant agreement at any point in the reference period, from the agreements register, whatever the partner's origin, plus every organization holding a funding agreement with CIMMYT in the period, from resource-mobilization records, de-duplicated to the legal entity; partners whose agreement ended or lapsed are included: they are the most likely to report a poor experience.

Exclusions: individuals not acting for a partner organization; CIMMYT staff; pure suppliers with no research or delivery content. A funder is flagged by that role, not counted as a fourteenth partner/institution type; the 13-category list stands, and the CIMMYT MEAL unit codes a funder's institutional type on it from the resource-mobilization records, at the signing legal entity, and flags it funder. Funders' scores are reported outside the composite as funder sets (Calculation method, Step 1), never blended into it: a funder assesses stewardship, a delivery partner assesses collaboration, and they are different constructs.

Missing data: a set (Calculation method, Step 1) giving a scored response to fewer than half of a dimension's items is excluded from that dimension's denominator for its role, "cannot say" not counting as an answer for this rule, and since the instrument carries at least three items per dimension (Collection instrument), no set is classed on a dimension from a single answer; "cannot say" is excluded from the item mean, never scored as neutral; non-response is never imputed, and the response rate accompanies every partner-set score, computed over the organizations holding a partnership or sub-grant agreement in the period, an organization responding where at least one of its partner-relationship holders completes, with a 50 percent minimum below which the value is labeled indicative, and any figure or disaggregation cell with fewer than five responding organizations is suppressed, both to protect confidentiality and to stop a "score" being reported off two respondents.

Repeated observations: one response set per organization per role per round; after initial non-response, only the completed response counts. Annual values never sum or average across years.
limitations: Courtesy bias is the structural risk: most respondents depend on CIMMYT for funding, so scores skew positive even with confidential third-party administration. Trends and gaps between dimensions and partner types carry more information than the level.

Acquiescence bias is a separate risk from courtesy bias: every item is worded in the agreement direction with no reverse-scored item to catch a respondent who agrees regardless of content, and this risk is sharper across a partner base spanning many countries and languages, where agreement-direction response styles vary. A respondent pushed from 3 to 4 by agreeing regardless of content crosses the favorable cutpoint, so the favorable share is more exposed to this than the five-point mean reported beside it.

The respondent-selection rule is its own bias source, distinct from courtesy bias in how the selected respondent answers: the one partner-side respondent surveyed per relationship is the contact CIMMYT's agreements register, or for a funder its resource-mobilization records, names for that relationship (Collection instrument), not one the partner organization nominates, so a relationship the register misidentifies, or a contact CIMMYT's own staff prefer to ask, is never checked against another voice at the same partner.

The frame is bounded to formally contracted partners: the same structural gap KPI-O03 discloses for its own count ("Formal-only counting under-records partnering where institutions collaborate without signed instruments"), carried here because this score's frame is drawn from the same agreements register, with funding-agreement holders added from resource-mobilization records, which are equally bounded to signed instruments.
Non-response bias compounds it: the least satisfied partners are the least likely to answer, so the score is best read as an upper estimate of partner experience.
The composite conceals movement: trust can fall while effectiveness rises with no net change in the headline number. Never read the composite without its three dimension scores.

Comparability over time is fragile: any change to the instrument, scale, frame rule or partner mix moves the score without any change in partner experience. Read trends only across identically constructed rounds.

The item set is CIMMYT's own, built on the register's three dimensions, so no external benchmark exists for the level. The score is comparable with CIMMYT's own earlier rounds and with nothing else, and it is never read as a standing against other organizations.

A rising score means responding partners reported a better experience; it does not mean the partnerships produced more results (KPI-OC01 and KPI-OC16 speak to that), and it supports a contribution claim to partner-of-choice standing only, read with KPI-OC03.
subMetrics: Three dimension values, trust, equity and effectiveness, each produced by steps 1 to 3 of the Calculation method as the favorable share, the percentage of responding organizations' partner sets with a dimension mean of 4.0 or above, with the raw five-point mean reported alongside it unrescaled: components of the composite, not disaggregations, each reportable in its own right. Related sheets: KPI-O03 (agreements frame), KPI-OC03 (repeat-partnership rate), KPI-O57 and KPI-OC60 (sub-grants), KPI-I01 (pathway impact, which this score feeds).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: a contracted third party. Validation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (frame de-duplication, duplicate responses, minimum-cell and missing-data rules). Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: the CIMMYT MEAL unit, on the institutional reporting line rather than any single project's, because the score is a statement about CIMMYT as an institution. Reporting: CIMMYT MEAL unit into institutional reporting, with results fed back to responding partners.
sourceRef: Volume 1 · Innovation development & scaling — Reference sheet KPI-OC05

name: Percentage of assisted persons in CIMMYT intervention areas reporting adoption of new or improved inputs, technologies, or practices relative to a baseline
resultsLevel: Outcome. Whether an assisted farmer keeps using an input, technology or practice after support ends is a behavior change among the farmers and partners CIMMYT assists, CGIAR's own textbook example of an outcome (farmers using a new seed variety).
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Contributing: PO1 (Defined by transdisciplinarity, CIMMYT is an efficient, innovative, and inclusive partner contributing to agrifood systems transformation), PO2 (Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries), PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs, following the primary objective PO3. Stable for this indicator because it counts people rather than result objects. Per the pathway convention, set per strand rather than per indicator group, as the Introduction sets out, since two of the three groups run more than one strand.
sdgTarget: None. The closest theme is SDG indicator 2.4.1 (proportion of agricultural area under productive and sustainable agriculture), but it measures land area meeting sustainability criteria at national scale, not the share of assisted persons adopting promoted innovations, so there is no direct correspondence.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Technical Reporting: the minimum data standard for Innovation Use outcomes requires user type and the number of people using, disaggregated by gender and youth; this indicator's numerator supplies that count and disaggregation directly. No donor reporting framework carries an equivalent share: the nearest donor constructs count individuals who applied a promoted practice at least once in the reporting year, where this indicator requires continued use beyond the intervention and reads as a share of assisted persons.
definition: Among assisted persons in CIMMYT intervention areas whose direct support ended before the start of the most recent completed cropping season of their intervention area's declared calendar (Data source, Frame DS2), the share reporting adoption of new or improved inputs, technologies or practices relative to a baseline. "Assisted persons" are the unique individuals reached through KPI-O18 training, as completers, or KPI-O20 package access, matched in the project's beneficiary registry and counted once across both channels. "Adoption" is self-reported continued use after direct project support ended, not having tried the item while supported, and "relative to a baseline" means new or improved for that person against their own pre-intervention practice.
rationale: Answers whether the people CIMMYT's projects reached go on to use the promoted innovations once direct support ends: the first behavioral test of the innovation-scaling pathway. It serves project management (a low rate triggers a rethink of what is promoted or how), institutional reporting under Primary Objective 3, and CGIAR technical reporting, where innovation use is a named outcome result category.
projectSpecificApplication: State the project's intervention area, its cropping-season calendar per intervention area (Data source, Frame DS2), the promoted items its adoption survey covers (the project's own promoted list, not any improved practice in general), the field-observation subsample size (Collection instrument), and when the survey rounds run relative to the end of intervention support. Where the registry does not date each person's last delivery event, state the support-end date per cohort or intervention area declared in the project's MEAL plan (Data source, Frame DS2). Do not alter the numerator, denominator, continued-use threshold, or baseline-relative rule; if measuring adoption after support ends is not feasible, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining adoption here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this rate informs: for example, a donor-required adoption indicator, or an internal rule that a promoted item with persistently low adoption is redesigned or dropped at the next season's planning.
projectTypesNotApplicable: none. Any project type can reach farmers with training or an improved package
projectTypesRaw:
Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: none. Any project type can reach farmers with training or an improved package.
unit: Percentage of assisted persons
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of assisted persons report continued adoption of new or improved inputs, technologies or practices.
disaggregationRequired: Required: sex (female/male at minimum, per CGIAR's sex-disaggregated data standards); age (youth/non-youth, with youth defined as 15 to 30, stated once in Core Section 4.1; projects record date of birth or exact age, not a band, so other donors' cuts can be derived without recollecting data); assistance channel (trained (completer) only / package access only / both), matching KPI-O18 and KPI-O20's different intervention types. The register lists sex and age; the channel cut is added by this sheet, and why it is required is stated in Limitations and interpretation.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Type of input, technology or practice adopted (from the promoted list, so a no-cost practice change and a costly technology purchase are visible separately); smallholder / non-smallholder status, as Annex B defines it, set from the household's landholding at baseline where the adoption module records it (Collection instrument); country or sub-national region.
unitOfObservation: Individual
calculationSummary: Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100, estimated from a representative sample of assisted persons and applied with survey weights. Numerator: assisted persons in the denominator reporting continued use, beyond the intervention, of at least one promoted input, technology or practice they were not using at baseline. Denominator: assisted persons eligible under Eligibility criteria and missing data, drawn from the project registry's cumulative KPI-O18 attendance and KPI-O20 access records, from project start to the round's first interview date, not from any reporting year's count, and de-duplicated by registry identifier; how the frame is built, how the end of direct support is dated, how the season test is applied and how a sampled person found at interview to fail it is treated are set out under Data source (Frame DS2). The sample is drawn from that eligible registry subset, so each round's denominator is the eligible registry population at that round, estimated from the frame count by the weighted in-scope share. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1: an adoption survey on a representative random sample of assisted persons, drawn from the registry persons eligible for the denominator. Frame DS2 (registry: denominator and sampling frame): the registry records of the persons eligible for the denominator are also the sampling frame the DS1 survey draws from. The frame is built from the project registry's cumulative KPI-O18 attendance and KPI-O20 access records, from project start to the round's first interview date; a record that cannot be matched to a registry identifier does not enter it, and a matched record with no date does, its person dated as set out below. End of direct support is dated per person at the latest qualifying delivery event recorded against that person in either channel: for KPI-O18, the last qualifying training session (KPI-O18 Eligibility) attended by a person who completed a qualifying training, from the individually recorded attendance; for KPI-O20, the last qualifying access event (KPI-O20 Eligibility) or, for a service with a duration such as a subscription or scheduled visits, the end of the service period, both dated in the KPI-O20 access record; a person in both channels takes the later date. Non-qualifying contacts, such as field days and sensitization meetings, do not extend support. The frame reads these dates from the registry; where the registry does not hold them at person level, the support-end date the project declares per cohort or intervention area in its MEAL plan applies, and a person whose latest delivery event cannot be dated from the registry, including a service with no recorded end date, takes the later of that declared date and their latest dated delivery event. The basis used, registry dates or declared date, is reported with the rate, with the number of persons dated on each where both are used. The season test: the project declares its cropping-season calendar per intervention area in its MEAL plan, and a person is eligible where direct support ended before the start of the most recent completed cropping season of that calendar, the season the adoption questions refer to; the frame applies the test at the round's first interview date. Registry or declared dates govern membership of the frame; the survey answer governs the frame-error test only, and persons the frame excludes are not re-tested. The survey records the season in which each sampled person's direct support ended (Collection instrument), and a sampled person whose support, at the interview date, did not end before the start of the most recent completed cropping season, or has not ended, is a frame error: out of scope, excluded from both terms and never imputed. The weighted in-scope share is computed over interviewed sampled persons with the design weights, which carry no separate non-response adjustment, non-respondents being assumed in scope at that share; the eligible population is estimated as the frame count multiplied by that share; the estimated adopters are that eligible population multiplied by the weighted adoption share, the design-weighted count of adopters over the design-weighted count of in-scope persons among interviewed sampled persons, so the project rate is that weighted share. Follow-up monitoring records kept by field staff or partners are not a route to the value: staff observe the farmers they still visit, so the records overstate adoption, and they carry no sampling design the release rule (Aggregation rule, Block E) can apply to; where no post-support survey round was fielded, no rate is reported. Not applicable DS3: continued use by named individuals is not observable from satellite data; area under a practice is a different quantity from the share of persons adopting. Not applicable DS4: no third-party database records adoption among CIMMYT-assisted persons at intervention-area resolution. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced use reports cannot be matched to the registry denominator, so they cannot produce a rate among assisted persons.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State the survey round used, the sampling design and the achieved sample.
collectionInstrument: Adoption module listing the project's promoted items one by one, asking for each: use before the project (baseline reference), use in the most recent completed cropping season of the intervention area's declared calendar, and the season of the last project training session, package delivery or purchase through a project partner channel, advisory or mechanization service, or end of a service period for it, field days, sensitization meetings and other one-off informational contacts not counting, or that project support for it has not ended, or that the person received no project support for it. The person's direct support has not ended where any item's has not, and otherwise ended in the latest season recorded, which is kept for the frame-error test (Data source, Frame DS2); where no item records a season, the registry or declared date stands and the person is not a frame error. Wherever KPI-OC19 is reported, the module also records the household's landholding at baseline, in the land concept and unit of the threshold declared under Annex B, from which KPI-OC19 sets smallholder status. Respondent: the assisted person themselves, identified by their registry record, not a household proxy. Mode: face-to-face or phone interview. Field-observation verification is required wherever the promoted item is identifiable on inspection, such as a machine or a residue-retention practice, and does not apply where it is not, such as a storage or timing decision: the project declares the subsample size in its MEAL plan and draws the subsample at random from interviewed in-scope persons holding an item identifiable on inspection; the share of the subsample where observation contradicts self-report is reported beside the rate (Aggregation rule, Block C), and the rate is not corrected. A variety is a third case: the crop stand is visible but the variety is not identifiable by looking at it, so field observation cannot verify which variety is grown and the variety component rests on the farmer-reported name. Genotyping a leaf or grain sample against the crop's genetic reference library is the method that does identify a variety, and it is what KPI-OC12 uses for varietal age. It is conditional, not absolute: it depends on a complete genetic reference library, and widely grown varieties missing from that library return unidentified samples that are dropped.
collectionFrequency: At least one survey round after direct support ends, typically midline and endline for multi-year projects; each round covers only persons meeting the season test (Data source, Frame DS2), so the value measures unsupported use.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Between survey rounds the latest measured value is carried forward with its year of measurement noted.
referencePeriod: Use in the most recent completed cropping season before the interview, on the intervention area's declared calendar (Data source, Frame DS2), a season being assigned to its harvest year, referenced to the person's pre-intervention baseline.
baselineRequired: Yes, by construction: adoption is defined relative to the person's pre-intervention practice. The baseline is recorded by recall in the first adoption survey (whether the person used each promoted item before the project, Collection instrument), standard adoption-survey practice but subject to recall error and stated as recall-based wherever reported. If no baseline reference can be established, the project may report current-use levels among assisted persons but cannot report adoption claims against this indicator.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One measurement round per project and one reporting year for the pooled figure. Weight: each assisted person counts once in a project's denominator, so within a project the survey weights carry the in-scope sample to the eligible registry population and across projects the pooled rate weights each project by the size of its denominator. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool by summing numerators and denominators across Recommended-sourced projects and recomputing the rate, never by averaging project percentages.

B: Combination method: ratio of sums. Within a project, the denominator is the eligible subset of the de-duplicated union of the project registry's cumulative KPI-O18 and KPI-O20 records (Calculation method), net of frame errors found at interview (Data source, Frame DS2), and the numerator the estimated adopters among them: one weighted adoption rate per project per measurement round, with numerator and denominator counts retained alongside the percentage. Across projects, the sum of estimated adopters over the sum of project denominators; no cross-project union is computed, since project sample estimates cannot be merged into one list, and the pooled rate carries the label Block C sets out. A project active in the reporting year whose latest measurement round predates it enters both sums with its last measured numerator and denominator, on the same footing as a project measured that year and carrying its round year; a round's year is the year of its last interview date; the pooled rate is labeled with the range of round years it combines, and the share of the pooled denominator measured in each round year is reported with it.

C: Levels and operations. A share is recomputed at every level from its own numerator and denominator, never averaged from the levels beneath it: a mean of project percentages weights a project of thirty equally with one of three thousand. At project level, assisted persons reporting continued use over the eligible assisted persons of that project's denominator. At institutional level, the summed numerator over the summed denominator, within the pooling domain of Block A. Within a project the denominator is drawn from the de-duplicated union of the KPI-O18 and KPI-O20 records, never from their sum; across projects the project denominators are added, as Block B sets out, and a pooled rate combining more than one project is labeled not de-duplicated across projects, since a person can appear in two project denominators. Also report, since a share without its denominator cannot be read: the denominator itself; the frame errors, sampled persons excluded under Eligibility for failing the season test at interview, as a count and as a share of interviewed sampled persons; the number of registry persons whose direct support does not meet the season test (Data source, Frame DS2), as a count beside the rate and never entered into it; the project's KPI-O18 and KPI-O20 counts for the round's reporting year; the basis on which the end of direct support was dated (registry dates or declared date, with the number of persons on each where both are used); the non-response share; the pre-existing-use share, eligible persons using at least one promoted item at baseline over the denominator, overall and per item; and, where field-observation verification applies, the share of the subsample where observation contradicts self-report.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. KPI-O18 and KPI-O20 records form the population this indicator's denominator is drawn from (the eligible subset of the registry union of the two channels), a population dependency, but their reported counts are never combined with this rate; and this outcome feeds the pathway impact KPI-I01 (partner-of-choice standing, a composite judgment) as evidence, not as an addend. Levels connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative, not arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: within a project the beneficiary registry de-duplicates across the two channels reliably; across projects there is no institute-level registry, so a person can appear in two project denominators, and the pooled institutional rate carries the label Block C sets out. Named overlaps: KPI-OC01 counts adopted innovations while this indicator counts adopting people, never combined into one figure; KPI-O18 and KPI-O20 are reach counts, never summed with this rate. Each project rate is a survey estimate of its eligible registry population, so coverage and precision are reported with every figure at project level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands: 16.5 percent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 percent released flagged, above 33.3 percent not released as an estimate. The coefficient-of-variation bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records; below 30 the estimate is not released. A record is one completed interview with a sampled in-scope assisted person in the measurement round. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place, and the pooled rate's coefficient of variation is computed from the project estimates' own sampling variances, the project samples being drawn independently.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: registry persons who completed a qualifying training (KPI-O18 Eligibility) or had a qualifying access event (KPI-O20 Eligibility), and whose direct support ended before the start of the most recent completed cropping season of their intervention area's declared calendar, the season test (Data source, Frame DS2), whatever their assistance channel; adoption of any item on the promoted list qualifies. Qualifying items are those on the project's promoted-item list, approved with its MEAL plan and frozen for the reporting year; the CIMMYT MEAL unit holds the lists.

Exclusion: persons outside the registry (spillover adopters appear in neither numerator nor denominator); registry persons reached through KPI-O18 alone who did not complete a qualifying training; registry persons whose direct support does not meet the season test; a sampled person found at interview to fail the season test, a frame error excluded from both terms (Data source, Frame DS2); use of practices not on the promoted list. A person whose continued use is only of items they already used at baseline stays in the denominator and out of the numerator, and the pre-existing-use share is reported (Aggregation rule, Block C).
limitations: Adoption is self-reported, and people interviewed by the project that assisted them tend to over-report use out of courtesy; a rise can reflect reporting behavior rather than field practice. The required field-observation subsample is the protection, and the survey is run by enumerators not involved in delivering the assistance.

Where the promoted item is a variety, the rate is variety-name-based and self-reported, and the field-observation subsample does not protect it: farmers frequently misidentify or cannot name what they grow, and a crop stand does not show which variety it is. Read the variety component as adoption of a variety the farmer names, not of a variety identified. Genotyping against the crop's genetic reference library is the stronger route and is what would make it an identified-variety rate, subject to the same condition KPI-OC12 states: a variety missing from the reference library returns an unidentified sample that is dropped, and the varieties most likely to be missing are widely grown ones, which is where an adoption rate carries most of its weight.

The measure is a binary snapshot per person: it does not capture intensity, area, or partial adoption, and continued use in the reference season does not preclude later dis-adoption. The denominator is the eligible registry population at each round, so it can move between rounds for reasons unrelated to adoption: registry records are closed or merged, such as a duplicate record merged on cleaning or a person who withdraws consent or dies, and persons leave the eligible population, such as a person whose direct support resumes before the round. Where the persons removed were disproportionately non-adopters the rate rises with no change in adoption, so read each round's rate with its denominator, the count of registry persons whose direct support does not meet the season test and the KPI-O18 and KPI-O20 counts beside it (Aggregation rule, Block C).

Where the declared support-end date is used, a person whose support in fact ended before the start of the season the adoption questions refer to, but whose declared date falls on or after that start, is left out of the frame and is not re-tested at interview, so errors of exclusion in the declared date go uncorrected, while errors of inclusion are caught by the frame-error test.

The denominator is restricted to assisted persons, so the indicator measures conversion of project reach into use, not diffusion: farmers who adopt through neighbors or markets are invisible to it, and it understates total innovation spread by design. Persons whose only reach is recorded through KPI-O18's unlinked partner counts or through a channel KPI-O20 reports by a survey-based Fallback estimate hold no attendance or access record in the registry, so they are outside the frame as well.
Supports a contribution claim only: continued use also responds to input prices, market demand, weather and partner activity, so the rate alone never proves CIMMYT caused the adoption.

Training (KPI-O18) and package access (KPI-O20) are mechanistically different interventions, which is why the assistance-channel cut is required: without it, a pooled adoption rate cannot be read against the intervention that produced it.

Pooled rates conflate very different behaviors, because promoted lists differ across projects (a no-cost agronomic practice and a purchased mechanization service are both "adoption"); report the practice-type disaggregation alongside any pooled figure.
subMetrics: None. Sex, age, and the type of item adopted are disaggregations of the same rate, not sub-metrics. Related sheets: KPI-O18 (farmers trained) and KPI-O20 (farmers accessing improved technological packages), the two delivery channels from which the denominator is drawn; KPI-OC19 (the gap between male and female adoption rates), which uses this indicator's survey, eligibility rule, adoption test and weights, applied per named practice to the smallholders in this indicator's eligible population, so its two rates reconcile with this indicator's smallholder cut for that practice, not with this indicator's rate; KPI-OC01 (share of released innovations adopted at scale, the innovation-counting sibling outcome); KPI-I01 (partner-of-choice standing, the pathway impact this outcome feeds per the register roll-up).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E team and trained enumerators (adoption survey), independent of the delivery teams. Validation: project MEAL officer (registry match, non-response check, verification subsample). Calculation: project M&E, per Calculation method; the CIMMYT MEAL unit pools across projects. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 1 · Innovation development & scaling — Reference sheet KPI-OC16

name: Percentage of CIMMYT's smallholder-facing research portfolio responding to farmer-articulated priorities
resultsLevel: Outcome, per CIMMYT's MEAL Framework, which defines outcomes as changes in behaviors, systems, practice, capacity, policy or performance. What changes is the composition of CIMMYT's research portfolio, and the change is achieved through convening farmers, consolidating and prioritizing what they said, and carrying it into planning decisions. CGIAR's control-and-externality test would read this as an output, since the portfolio is CIMMYT's own; Core Section 5.4 (CGIAR standard crosswalk) records the divergence.
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. The indicator measures PO3's first sub-objective almost word for word: "The aspirations and needs of smallholder farmers drive and consistently inform the agrifood research agenda", a claim about the composition of the agenda over time, which is what a portfolio share reports. Contributing only: PO1 Defined by transdisciplinarity, CIMMYT is an efficient, innovative, and inclusive partner contributing to agrifood systems transformation.
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs, following the primary objective PO3. Stable for this indicator: the unit counted is a research activity, and what the share measures is whose priorities the portfolio answers, so the area follows the population whose priorities are at issue rather than the thematic content of the activities. Per the pathway convention, set per strand rather than per indicator group, as the Introduction sets out, since two of the three groups run more than one strand.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator measures whether a research portfolio reflects the priorities of the farmers it serves. The nearest target, SDG 2.a (increase investment in agricultural research and extension), is measured by indicator 2.a.1, the agriculture orientation index for government expenditures: a spending ratio, silent on whose priorities the spending serves.
otherFrameworks: None. The definition is CIMMYT's own. The closest CGIAR construct is "Demand-Supply Alignment" within CGIAR's Innovation Packages and Scaling Readiness approach: a portfolio-management practice, not a reported indicator, and one working from the innovation side. The CIMMYT to CGIAR crosswalk records no CGIAR Results Framework counterpart.
definition: The share of CIMMYT's smallholder-facing research work in a reporting year, documented as addressing priorities smallholder farmers themselves stated. The smallholder-facing research portfolio is CIMMYT research activities that year whose intended users are smallholder producers in CIMMYT's target geographies ("smallholder" qualifies the portfolio, not a per-farm threshold). The counted unit is a research activity: the work package, or the workplan activity line where a project has none (see Eligibility criteria). Responding to a farmer-articulated priority means a dated planning record names a specific priority from the project's own priority list under KPI-O25 (identifier and entry date attached); general language about serving farmers does not qualify.
rationale: Answers the question KPI-O25 leaves open: CIMMYT recorded what farmers asked for, but did the research follow? Priorities on a list show listening; the share of the portfolio acting on them shows whether listening changed anything. It serves research management, institutional reporting on Primary Objective 3, and donors funding CIMMYT on the premise that its research is demand-driven.
projectSpecificApplication: State which of the project's activities fall inside the smallholder-facing portfolio, at which level the project counts them (work package, or workplan activity line where it uses no work packages), and the reporting-year boundary; activities are mapped against the project's own KPI-O25 priority list. The counting unit, qualifying condition and calculation method stay unchanged.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision, donor requirement or reporting need the share serves, for example an annual review comparing the ranked farmer priority list against the activities budgeted.
projectTypesNotApplicable: none. Any project type can hold smallholder-facing research activities
projectTypesRaw:
Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: none. Any project type can hold smallholder-facing research activities.
unit: Percentage of smallholder-facing research activities (a share of activity counts, not of budget, staff time or publications).
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of the smallholder-facing research portfolio addresses farmer-articulated priorities.
disaggregationRequired: Required: sex composition of the farmer groups behind the priorities each mapped activity responds to, carried through from KPI-O25, reported as the number of responsive activities mapped to at least one priority ranked in a session with female participants. The counted object is a research activity rather than a person, so this is an attribute of the priority being answered, not a breakdown of the share itself, and why it is required is stated in Limitations and interpretation.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Crop or farming system; country and region; research theme (breeding, agronomy, mechanization, post-harvest, socio-economics); theme and farmer-given rank of the priority addressed, separating a portfolio answering farmers' top priorities from one answering their marginal ones; funder; research unit; mapping made at design or retrospectively.
unitOfObservation: Result object: the research activity, as carried on the portfolio record.
calculationSummary: Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100, unweighted, reported alongside a budget-weighted companion value computed on the same numerator and denominator over the activities with an allocated budget, each weighted by that budget, with the number and share of denominator activities without one (staff time only) reported beside it; the companion value is computable unless no activity in the denominator has an allocated budget. Numerator: smallholder-facing research activities active in the reporting year that a dated planning record documents as addressing at least one farmer-articulated priority recorded under KPI-O25. An activity addressing several priorities counts once, never once per priority. Denominator: all smallholder-facing research activities active in the year. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (administrative and registry data): the annual research workplan or activity register that defines the denominator, the KPI-O25 priority lists held by projects, which supply the reference list, and the dated mapping record linking an activity to a named priority. The activity register exists as a CIMMYT-controlled record, so the denominator is available without new collection; the dated mapping record is a documentation standard introduced with this indicator, so every counted activity traces to a dated document from the point the standard was applied, per Baseline required. Fallback DS1 (censuses and surveys): where an activity has no dated mapping record, its mapping may be collected through a structured census of activity leaders against the closed KPI-O25 priority list; flagged as fallback-sourced, since it is self-reported by the people whose work is classified. Not applicable: DS3 (geospatial and Earth observation), portfolio composition cannot be observed remotely. Not applicable: DS4 (secondary and international databases), no third party publishes CIMMYT's activity list mapped to farmer priorities. Not applicable: DS5 (citizen-generated data), crowdsourced or mobile data cannot enumerate research activities.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role was used. For Recommended, name the activity register, the priority list mapped against, and who validated the mapping. For Fallback, name the activities mapped through the census and state why no dated mapping record exists for them.
collectionInstrument: Applies to the DS1 fallback route: a structured portfolio-mapping form, one response per activity, presenting the closed KPI-O25 priority list and asking the respondent to select the priorities addressed, cite the text evidencing each link, and state whether the priority was known at design or matched afterwards. Respondent: the named activity leader, for that activity only. Mode: online form with MEAL follow-up on non-response. The Recommended DS2 route is a documentation standard, not an instrument; each activity record carries its identifier, workplan reference, active dates, smallholder-facing status, priorities addressed or none with an evidence reference, and validator and date.
collectionFrequency: Annually: at approval of the year's activity register, and again at year end for activities added or closed during the year.
referencePeriod: The reporting year, describing the portfolio as it stood that year: January to December at institutional level, with projects on a donor year stating which they use.
baselineRequired: Yes. The value is comparative: no external benchmark exists for what share of a research portfolio should answer stated farmer priorities. Fallbacks: retrospective coding of an earlier year's approved workplan against the KPI-O25 priority lists, preferred because it applies the same rules; failing that, the first year the mapping standard was applied becomes the reference year. Where neither fallback is available, the indicator is reported for monitoring without a reference year.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One reporting year and one smallholder-facing research portfolio: activities active in the same reporting year may enter one figure, and different years are reported side by side and never summed. Weight: one activity each for the headline value, with the counting level (work package or workplan activity line) recorded with each project value, since pooled projects may count at different levels; the budget-weighted companion figure weights each activity by its allocated budget, and the two are reported together and never mixed. (2) Across projects: pool by summing numerators and denominators. An activity whose mapping comes only from the Fallback census, or all of whose mapped priorities KPI-O25 records as Fallback-sourced, stays in the denominator and counts as not responding in the pooled figure, as Eligibility sets out for an unmapped activity; the number of such activities, and how many of them the census or the Fallback-sourced priorities would count as responding, are reported beside the pooled figure with a note naming them, never blended in.

B: Combination method: ratio of sums. Sum the responsive activities and the smallholder-facing activities separately over the domain of Block A, then divide, after de-duplicating activities within each project, each project's activities assessed on the January to December year. Never average project percentages.

C: Levels and operations. A share is recomputed at every level from its own numerator and denominator, never averaged from the levels beneath it: a mean of project percentages weights a project of thirty equally with one of three thousand. At project level, smallholder-facing research activities meeting the test over all smallholder-facing research activities active in the year for that project. At institutional level, the summed numerator over the summed denominator, within the pooling domain of Block A. Also report: the denominator itself, the number of units excluded under Eligibility, the number of unmapped activities and the number of activities whose mapping is not yet validated, since a share without its denominator cannot be read.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: no. This share does not combine arithmetically with KPI-O25 or KPI-I01; levels connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative. The one dependency is a lookup, not arithmetic: the KPI-O25 priority lists define this numerator, so any change to what counts as a priority changes what this share measures, and the two sheets are revised together.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: an activity funded by two projects, or reported by both a project and a program, must count once on each side, which needs a stable activity identifier. None exists portfolio-wide: CIMMYT's confirmed identifier set covers farmers, plots, enterprises, facilities and datasets, with no institute-level registry, so activity identification is project-based. Publish any value pooled over more than one project with both counts shown, labeled not de-duplicated, with the number of activities reported by more than one project stated where known; the bias can run either way, since an undetected duplicate enters the denominator always and the numerator only if it qualifies. Overlap to name explicitly: this denominator and the priority count in KPI-O25 are different objects and must never be combined into one ratio.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Repeated observations: a multi-year activity counts once in each year it is active, on both sides; annual values are never summed. Counting unit: the work package, or the workplan activity line where a project does not use work packages. That is the level at which CIMMYT plans and budgets, so it is where responding to a priority is decided and where records exist; a project is too coarse, since one project holds responsive and unresponsive activities alike, and a product line is a breeding construct that does not generalize. The mapping requires only that the activity addresses the priority; the priority need not have informed the activity's design.
limitations: Measures the composition of CIMMYT's own research agenda, not any benefit to farmers. A portfolio can answer precisely what farmers asked for and still produce research that fails or is never taken up.

The denominator can be managed. The work-package rule fixes the counting level, but what a project classes as smallholder-facing and how it partitions its work into work packages or activity lines still set both halves of the ratio, so the share can be raised without changing any research.

The numerator rests on a mapping usually proposed by those whose work is classified. Independent validation limits the upward pull but cannot remove it, since the validator chooses among mappings the activity leader proposed rather than searching independently for one; retrospective mapping is the sharper form of the problem, since almost any agronomy activity can be matched to some priority on a long enough list after the fact. A value near 100 percent is therefore checked for loose mapping or a narrowed denominator before it is read as responsiveness: some legitimate smallholder-facing research is anticipatory, addressing risks farmers cannot yet state, and is counted as not responding.

Whose priorities were answered matters as much as how many. The share inherits the representativeness weaknesses of the exercises behind KPI-O25, and cannot distinguish a portfolio answering better-connected male farmers from one answering a representative set. This is why the sex-composition cut is required: a portfolio can respond faithfully to priorities that only men set, so a rising share would report success regardless of whose priorities were served.

A rise means a larger share of the portfolio is documented as addressing stated priorities. It does not mean farmers set the agenda, that the priorities addressed were those ranked highest, that budget followed, or that the research succeeded.
subMetrics:
Two required companion figures. Unmapped activities, the count of smallholder-facing activities in the denominator with no mapping decision recorded either way, reported alongside the share; Eligibility criteria and missing data already excludes these from the numerator rather than dropping them from the denominator, so this figure makes that exclusion visible rather than silent. The budget-weighted share, as Calculation method defines it. Otherwise none: the breakdowns listed under Measurement basics are disaggregations of one share, not separately calculated metrics.

On neighboring sheets: KPI-O25 supplies the priority lists this numerator is mapped against, and KPI-I01 receives this indicator as one constituent of a composite judgment, not an arithmetic input. The budget-weighted share is reported alongside the headline and never mixed with it.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the research-unit leader as technical reviewer for the portfolio scope
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project or program planning focal point, maintaining the activity register and priority mapping. Validation: project MEAL officer, checking the denominator criteria, checking each numerator mapping resolves to a named priority on the project's KPI-O25 priority list, and removing duplicates; never the leader of the activity classified. Calculation: project MEAL officer for the project value, CIMMYT MEAL unit for the portfolio census and pooling. Approval: project leader, with the research-unit leader confirming the smallholder-facing classification. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the MEAL unit.

name: Share of sub-grants involving Global South partner organizations
resultsLevel: Outcome, per CIMMYT's MEAL Framework, which defines outcomes as changes in behaviors, systems, practice, capacity, policy or performance and lists "shifts in investment decisions" among its own examples. A shift in which partners receive sub-grants is exactly that. CGIAR's control-and-externality test would read this as an output, since the composition of the portfolio is a property of CIMMYT's own decisions; Core Section 5.4 (CGIAR standard crosswalk) records the divergence. Within the pathway chain the value reads one level above KPI-O57: that indicator counts the agreements CIMMYT holds, this indicator reads whether the partnering practice those agreements add up to is equitable.
primaryObjective: Partnership (institutional component). The mapping is direct: the component's ways of working commit CIMMYT to streamlined sub-granting, transparent partnership expectations, and "an equitable voice for all involved parties", and its stated "Why we partner" objectives include building the capacity of local organizations to innovate, collaborate and scale. This indicator tests whether those commitments show up in the composition of the devolved-funding portfolio. Partnership is the component for this indicator, as for KPI-O57.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. The indicator measures CIMMYT's own partnering practice, not a result delivered to an external population, so it does not map to any of the five CGIAR Impact Areas.
sdgTarget: None. The thematically closest target is SDG 17.17 (effective public, public-private and civil society partnerships), but its official indicator 17.17.1 measures United States dollars committed to public-private partnerships for infrastructure, not the composition of an organization's sub-grant portfolio.
otherFrameworks: None with a comparable measure. CGIAR's 32 standard indicators contain no measure of partnership composition or sub-granting, and the Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 instead adds a partner engagement/partnership building result category and foresees possible future engagement indicators (Intensity of Partnerships, due diligence), none yet defined. The definition is therefore CIMMYT's own. Localization-share metrics used by some donors (for example targets for the share of funding to local organizations) are policy targets, not published indicator standards, and are not cited as a methodology here.
definition: The percentage of sub-grants signed by CIMMYT in the reporting year in which at least one recipient partner organization is based in the Global South. A sub-grant is an instrument under which CIMMYT passes funds and defined implementation roles to a partner organization under an award CIMMYT holds: the vehicle through which CIMMYT devolves resources and responsibility. The indicator measures the equity of CIMMYT's partnering practice: whether devolved funding reaches organizations in the regions where CIMMYT's mission is delivered, rather than circulating among Global North intermediaries.
rationale: The 2030 Strategy's Partnership component commits CIMMYT to incorporate social justice considerations, ensure "an equitable voice for all involved parties", and build the capacity of local organizations to innovate, collaborate and scale. This indicator answers, for leadership and the partnerships function, whether that commitment is visible in the funding: what share of the sub-grants CIMMYT issues places Global South organizations in funded, responsible roles. It turns the partner-of-choice narrative read at KPI-I01 into a verifiable annual proportion.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator: computed once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate grants and contracts records, no project instance to adapt it to).
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT's own sub-granting and is computed once at institutional level.
unit: Percentage of sub-grants
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of CIMMYT sub-grants involve at least one Global South partner organization.
