The share reads the composition of partnering practice and not the value of resources devolved, so it is read with the underlying counts and with the value-weighted share (Sub-metrics) where that is computable.
disaggregationRequired: Required: partner origin within the numerator (local to the country where the work takes place / other Global South); recipient role (Global South organization is the lead recipient / a non-lead recipient); partner/institution type. The confirmed category list is: CGIAR center; national agricultural research and extension system (NARES); university or higher education institution; government ministry or public agency; international research organization, non-CGIAR; multilateral or UN agency; regional or sub-regional organization; private company; financial institution; non-governmental or civil society organization; farmer organization or cooperative; foundation; other. If more than 10 percent of records fall to "other" in a year, the list is revised rather than the partners reclassified. Partners are classified at the signing legal entity, so a ministry and its national research institute are two partners in two categories. A sub-grant with several recipients is classified once for these cuts, on one recipient, as Calculation method sets out, so the cuts stay additive. Sex and age do not apply: the counted unit is an agreement, not a person.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country or region; CIMMYT program or business line; sub-grant value band (USD); funder of the prime award under which the sub-grant is issued.
unitOfObservation: Result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation: the sub-grant agreement, meaning one distinct signed instrument, which can bind several organizations.
calculationSummary: Numerator: sub-grants signed in the reporting year in which at least one recipient partner organization is based in the Global South, meaning its signing legal entity is registered in a country on the OECD DAC List of ODA Recipients (OECD, 2025), edition effective for reporting on 2025 flows, as KPI-O57. A sub-grant with several recipients is classified once for the required cuts, on one Global South recipient: its lead recipient where that recipient is in the Global South; otherwise the Global South recipient with the largest stated allocation; otherwise the first Global South recipient named in the instrument. For the partner-origin cut, that recipient is local where it is an organization legally registered and headquartered in the country where the work takes place, or for an instrument covering several countries in any one of them, KPI-O57's boundary, and other Global South otherwise. Denominator: all sub-grants signed in the reporting year. Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100. Both terms are counts of distinct signed instruments taken from the same grants and contracts records that feed KPI-O57. KPI-O57 is a stock of agreements in force, restricted to local and Global South partners, so it cannot supply an unfiltered flow of all sub-grants signed; its sub-grant subset relates to this indicator's numerator instead. Because CIMMYT issues a unique number for every sub-grant, both terms de-duplicate cleanly and this share is a true figure rather than an upper estimate. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (administrative and registry data): CIMMYT's grant-management and contracts records, where sub-grant instruments are filed with their signature dates and partner details; partner origin (local / other Global South) is classified from those details on the boundary definitions in Calculation method, which are KPI-O57's, so the two sheets classify the same partner the same way. For the value-weighted companion figure the record also carries each instrument's value and, where the instrument's budget states one, its allocation by recipient organization. Where corporate records do not reach every instrument, the fallback below applies. Fallback DS1 (surveys): a structured annual return in which project leaders and country representatives enumerate the sub-grants signed in the year, used only where corporate records do not reach project-level instruments; instruments known only through the return are reported beside the headline and its value-weighted share, flagged fallback-sourced and never blended into either, since self-reported enumeration is more exposed to omission. Not applicable DS3: geospatial data cannot establish that a legal instrument exists or who its parties are. Not applicable DS4: no third-party database independently records CIMMYT's sub-grants. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced data cannot establish the existence or parties of a signed instrument.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: For the DS1 fallback only: a structured annual return, one row per sub-grant, listing instrument reference, partner organization(s) with the lead recipient marked, each partner's country of registration and headquarters country, the country or countries where the work takes place, signature date, value (USD) and its allocation by recipient organization where the instrument states one, and the CIMMYT unit holding the instrument. Respondent: the project leader or country representative accountable for the agreement. Mode: electronic return with the instrument or its reference attached. For the Recommended DS2 route: not applicable, the filed instrument is the record itself.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as instruments are filed in grants and contracts records; consolidated once a year at year-end.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Each annual value is a self-standing proportion; values are never averaged or summed across years.
referencePeriod: The reporting year, January to December at institutional level. The value describes the flow of sub-grants newly signed in that window, unlike KPI-O57, which describes the stock of agreements in force.
baselineRequired: No. Each year's value is a self-standing proportion; change is read from the year-on-year series, and the first reported year serves as the reference point.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. Weight: one each per distinct signed sub-grant for the headline share, whatever its value; the value-weighted companion figure (Sub-metrics) weights each sub-grant by value, and the two are reported together and never mixed. (2) Aggregation across CIMMYT units: instruments from units covered by the Recommended corporate records are pooled directly and the headline and the value-weighted share are computed on them alone; instruments a unit could supply only through the Fallback annual return are reported beside both, with their count, share and total value, and never blended into either.

B: Combination method. Computed once at institutional level: pool every sub-grant the Recommended records hold for the year into one numerator and one denominator, then divide. Never average shares computed per project, program or country office, because units issue very different numbers of sub-grants.

C: Levels and operations. Computed once at CIMMYT-wide level, as the summed numerator over the summed denominator within the pooling domain of Block A. There is no Project area figure: this is a property of CIMMYT's own granting, and this indicator has no project instance, as Project types that apply states. Also report: the denominator itself, the number of sub-grants excluded under Eligibility, the number excluded for want of a signature date, the percentage of sub-grants with no recipient established as registered in a Global South country and at least one whose country of registration cannot be established, and the number of numerator sub-grants not classified by partner origin, since a share without its denominator cannot be read.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no, values at different levels are never combined arithmetically. This share is derived from the same record set as KPI-O57 (output) and feeds the partner-of-choice narrative at KPI-I01 (impact) through the Theory of Change, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: one instrument counts once in both terms, identified by instrument reference; a multi-party sub-grant counts once, not once per partner; an instrument held centrally and also logged by a project is one instrument. Every sub-grant carries a unique instrument number, so de-duplication by instrument reference is complete in both terms and the share is a true figure, not an approximation.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Missing data: a sub-grant with no recipient established as registered in a Global South country and at least one recipient whose country of registration cannot be established stays in the denominator and out of the numerator, so unclassified records lower the share rather than inflate it; the percentage of such sub-grants is reported alongside the value. A numerator sub-grant whose classified recipient's headquarters country or country of work cannot be established stays in the numerator and is reported under partner origin as not classified. A sub-grant with no signature date cannot be placed in a reporting year: it is excluded from both terms and the number of such sub-grants is reported alongside the value.

Repeated observations: each sub-grant counts once, in its year of signature, whatever the number of amendments it later carries; a sub-grant binding several partner organizations counts once; several sub-grants to the same partner in one year count separately.
limitations: The share weights every sub-grant equally regardless of value: it can rise while the funding passed to Global South partners falls. The value-weighted share under Sub-metrics is the required companion figure for exactly this, and a claim that devolution deepened rests on both. Where unallocated sub-grants make the value-weighted share a range, the count-based share is read with that range; only where an instrument's total value is missing is the value-weighted share not computable, and the count-based share then read alone and labeled as silent on value.

"At least one Global South partner" is a low bar: a sub-grant led by a Global North organization with a minor Global South sub-partner counts the same as one held outright by a Global South NARES. The indicator reads presence, not leadership, role or budget share. That is why the recipient-role cut is required, an organization named behind a Global North lead being a weaker claim to equitable partnering than one leading the work; the partner-origin cut is required because a portfolio can be Global South-heavy while bypassing the countries where the work happens.

The classification boundaries do the work: what counts as a sub-grant and which countries count as Global South each move the value. Global South is the OECD DAC List of ODA Recipients, which is revised on a published cycle, so a value is comparable across years only where the same edition is applied and the edition applied travels with the value.
In a year when few sub-grants are signed, single instruments swing the percentage. Always report the numerator and denominator counts alongside the share.

A rising share shows the composition of newly signed sub-grants changed; it does not show that partner organizations gained capacity, standing or satisfaction. Those read at the pathway's partnership-quality indicators and at KPI-I01.
subMetrics: One required companion figure: the value-weighted share, the percentage of sub-granted funds committed to Global South recipients, alongside the count-based share. Numerator: the value apportioned to the Global South recipient organization(s) in each qualifying sub-grant, not the instrument's full value, so a Global South sub-partner holding a minor share of a Global North-led instrument contributes only that share. A sub-grant with a single recipient organization allocates its full value to that recipient. A sub-grant whose recipients are all inside the Global South allocates its full value to them, and one whose recipients are all outside it allocates none. Where a qualifying sub-grant has recipients both inside and outside the Global South, or recipients whose country of registration cannot be established, and its budget does not allocate value by recipient, the value-weighted share is reported as a range and no split is imputed: the lower bound assigns none of that sub-grant's value to Global South recipients and the upper bound all of it, and the number and total value of such unallocated sub-grants are stated with the range. The value-weighted share is computable unless an instrument's total value is missing. A sub-grant with no recipient established as registered in a Global South country and at least one recipient whose country of registration cannot be established keeps its value in the denominator and out of the numerator. Values stated in another currency are converted to USD at the exchange rate at the sub-grant's signature date, with the rate and its source recorded against the instrument. A sub-grant's value is the value as stated in the instrument at signature, excluding later amendments. Denominator: the total value of the sub-grants in the headline's denominator. Apportioning the numerator this way is what keeps the companion figure a correction on the count-based headline's presence bias (Limitations) rather than a second figure carrying the same bias forward. Otherwise none: the numerator and denominator are working terms of one proportion, not sub-metrics, and are reported alongside the share; both are drawn from the record set documented at KPI-O57. Related sheets: KPI-O57, the count of active partnership and sub-grant agreements with local and Global South partners; KPI-O03, partnership agreements in force; KPI-I01, the pathway impact this share feeds.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: the CIMMYT grants-management or contracts function that files sub-grant instruments, the same function KPI-O57 names, for the Recommended route; project leaders or country representatives for the Fallback return. Validation: the partnerships function confirms partner origin classification; grants management confirms signature dates and instrument class. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, applying the rules above. Approval: the partnerships function, as KPI-O57 names. Reporting: CIMMYT MEAL unit into institutional reporting.
sourceRef: Volume 1 · Innovation development & scaling — Reference sheet KPI-OC60

name: CIMMYT's effectiveness as a partner of choice, demonstrated by the extent to which its co-developed innovations are taken up and scaled by partners and farmers
resultsLevel: Impact, as recorded in the register: sustained uptake and scaling of innovations beyond CIMMYT's control is the long-term systemic change this pathway drives toward. Read with care: CGIAR's control-and-externality test is written for single results, and the object judged here, CIMMYT's own standing, is a property of the institution evidenced through external behavior. What is measured is two bodies of evidence, uptake of co-developed innovations and partnership standing; the partner-of-choice standing is the reading of both.
primaryObjective: PO1 Defined by transdisciplinarity, CIMMYT is an efficient, innovative, and inclusive partner contributing to agrifood systems transformation. Sub-objectives 1.1 (active engagement with partners around common goals) and 1.4 (environments for co-creating and scaling technologies, built through strategic partnerships) are the closest Strategy sentences to this indicator's subject. Contributing only: PO2, PO3, PO4, through the adoption feeders whose benefits those objectives claim.
cgiarImpactArea: Read as spanning all areas, with no single value recorded. The indicator summarizes work spanning every area and counts no object that can be tagged with an area, so no area tag is recorded and no distribution across areas is computed. KPI-OC05 and KPI-I01 are the two exceptions to the pathway convention, which sets the area per strand rather than per indicator group, as the Introduction sets out.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest candidate, SDG indicator 17.16.1, counts countries reporting in multi-stakeholder development effectiveness monitoring frameworks; no SDG indicator measures one organization's partnership standing or the uptake of its innovations.
otherFrameworks: None adopted. The One CGIAR Standard Indicators report notes the emphasis on partnerships as a means of change but finds no partnership indicator in the standard set. The CGIAR Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 adds a partner engagement and partnership building result category, described as a bridge between outputs and outcomes, not an impact measure. CGIAR's innovation-use standard indicators correspond to feeders KPI-OC01 and KPI-OC16 and are mapped on those sheets. The composite is CIMMYT's own construct.
definition: A composite judgment of CIMMYT's standing as a partner of choice, evidenced by the extent to which its co-developed innovations are taken up and scaled by partners and farmers. Not a single measured value: a written, evidence-referenced conclusion compiled once a year at institutional level from seven outcome indicators, six in this pathway and KPI-OC04 in Capacity, data & institutions, read as two groups, adoption and partnership standing. "Partner of choice" is the standing the 2030 Strategy commits to: the organization that partners and farmers keep choosing to co-develop with, scale with, and return to. The judgment states whether the seven indicators, read together, show that standing strengthening, holding or weakening, or whether the reading is mixed or not assessable.
rationale: Answers the summative question this pathway exists to answer: is CIMMYT the partner that others choose, and does that standing show up as innovations taken up and scaled beyond CIMMYT's own control? The 2030 Strategy frames Primary Objective 1 as "the way we work: eager to learn, lead, and be a partner of choice", and this indicator is the register's direct evidence line for that commitment. Used in institutional reporting to the Board and to donors as the top of the innovation-and-scaling results narrative.
projectSpecificApplication: Projects do not report this indicator; no project-level value of it exists. A project contributes through the seven feeders, whose pipelines pool its results before they reach this judgment. A project asked by a donor for partner-of-choice evidence presents its own feeder values and cases, not a project-level version of this composite.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable: the judgment is institutional. Projects state their rationale on the feeder sheets they report against.
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a judgment about CIMMYT as a whole, formed once at institutional level.
unit: Composite qualitative judgment: a written, evidence-referenced statement, not a number, with one five-value summary category: strengthening / holding / weakening / mixed / not assessable, mixed being used where the adoption and partnership groups read differently and not assessable where either group is not read (Calculation method).
directionOfChange: Not directional at the composite level, the reported object being a narrative judgment. Each feeder carries an unambiguous direction of its own: six are increases, and KPI-OC04, which reports the change in a skills gap, is a decrease. Favorable movement therefore means each place moving in its own favorable direction, as Calculation method defines movement, which is what supports a strengthening conclusion.
disaggregationRequired: Required: none (the register records none, and the judged object is CIMMYT's institution-wide standing, which does not disaggregate). The evidence pack must preserve the feeders' own required disaggregations, notably sex and age from KPI-OC16 and partner type from KPI-OC03 and KPI-OC05, so the judgment can say for whom the standing holds.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Not applicable at project level. The judgment may present feeder evidence by region, crop or system, and partner type, where the feeders carry those splits.
unitOfObservation: Organization: CIMMYT as a whole. The underlying observations belong to the feeders and keep their own units there.
calculationSummary: The value is a structured synthesis, compiled annually. Inputs: the latest validated institutional value of each feeder, which is its pooled value and excludes what its own sheet reports alongside as Fallback-sourced, carried with its vintage, its variance where its sheet reports one, and any estimate label from its own sheet. A place is filled and moved only by that value; what a feeder reports alongside as Fallback-sourced is cited in the evidence pack and never fills or moves a place. The seven feeders are read as two groups, named under Sub-metrics. Within a group, each feeder fills one place, except that KPI-OC01 and KPI-OC16 fill one place together, since they read one uptake from two sides: that place moves in whichever direction either of them moved, and reads unchanged, with the disagreement recorded, where they moved in opposite directions. A feeder value is fresh in the year it is first entered in a judgment and carried forward in any later year, having already been entered in an earlier year's judgment (Eligibility, Repeated observations). A group's current places are those with a reportable value that year, fresh or carried forward; a place with no reportable value is left out of them and named as missing. A feeder value not released under its own sheet is not reportable. The joint KPI-OC01 and KPI-OC16 place is fresh where either member is fresh, carried forward where neither is fresh and at least one is carried forward, and missing only where both are missing. Movement: a place moved where its feeder's fresh value differs from the value entered for that feeder in the last judgment; for a record-based feeder any change counts, a census of a frame, such as KPI-OC05's partner survey, being read as record-based, and for a feeder its own sheet estimates from a sample only a difference statistically significant at 95 percent on a two-sided test of the difference using the variances each value's own sheet reports, the two values treated as independent, counts, a place for which either value lacks a variance from its own sheet being not moved, with that recorded. KPI-OC05 is read on its composite. A place is able to move where a feeder filling it has a value entered in an earlier judgment. The group reads strengthening where at least half its current places moved in their favorable direction and more moved favorably than unfavorably; weakening symmetrically; otherwise holding. A group with no current places is not read and is reported as without evidence. A group with current places none of which is able to move is not read either; in the first judgment no place is able to move, so the composite is not assessable and the judgment is labeled the reference judgment. A carried-forward feeder counts as unchanged and stays among the current places, so it cannot on its own move a group's reading in either direction. Within partnership standing, where KPI-OC03 and KPI-OC05 move in opposite directions, the judgment records the divergence, naming which moved which way, whatever the group reads. Between groups: the composite reads strengthening where both groups read strengthening, holding where both read holding, and weakening where both read weakening; every other combination of two read groups is recorded as mixed, naming what each group reads and why; where either group is not read the composite is not assessable, naming that group and why it was not read. Independent external reviews are admissible in the evidence pack as corroboration, cited and read alongside the feeders, but are never scored into the judgment. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (administrative and registry data): CIMMYT's institutional M&E results record, that is, the validated annual values and evidence packs of the seven feeder indicators, each collected under its own reference sheet. Fallback: none; there is no alternative route to a composite of CIMMYT's own outcomes, and a year with missing feeders yields a partial judgment under the missing-data rule, or a not-assessable one where a group is not read, not a value from another source. Not applicable: DS1 (censuses and surveys), the composite fields no instrument of its own; primary collection, including the partner survey, happens inside the feeders. Not applicable: DS3 (geospatial and Earth observation), an institutional standing cannot be observed remotely. Not applicable: DS4 (secondary and international databases), no third party publishes a measure of CIMMYT's partnership standing. Not applicable: DS5 (citizen-generated and other non-traditional data), unsolicited commentary is excluded by the calculation method.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable: compiled once at institutional level; projects report into the feeder indicators, not into this one.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, derived from the feeders' validated values; no DS1 or DS5 source is listed.
collectionFrequency: Annual compilation, after the feeder indicators' institutional values close for the year.
referencePeriod: The January to December reporting year of compilation. Each feeder is read at its latest available vintage, stated per feeder in the evidence pack: some feeders describe multi-year windows by design (KPI-OC01 observes release cohorts after a lag; KPI-OC03 uses a multi-year engagement window), so the judgment describes standing as evidenced by the data available that year, not a single measurement window.
baselineRequired: No. The first compiled judgment is the reference judgment, labeled with its year, feeder set and rubric: no place is able to move, so its composite is not assessable (Calculation method). A claim that standing changed over time requires the same rubric and feeder set in both years; if either changes, the comparison is re-based and says so.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. Weight: none; the seven feeders are not weighted against each other and are read by the rubric under Calculation method. (2) Across projects: handled inside each feeder per its own sheet before values reach this judgment; what a feeder reports alongside its pooled value as Fallback-sourced is cited in the evidence pack, as Calculation method sets out.

B: Combination method. Compiled once at institutional level; nothing further aggregates at this level.

C: Levels and operations. The judgment is formed once, at institutional level, because that is the level its question is asked at: whether CIMMYT is a partner of choice is not a property any single project holds. It is never averaged across projects or feeders, and no project-level version of it is produced. Each feeder is aggregated on its own sheet before its value arrives here. Also report: the feeder values the judgment rests on, each group's reading with its count of fresh and carried-forward places, which feeders were unavailable and how their absence was treated, and the evidence date, since a composite with a silent missing component is not comparable with one that has all of them.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: this is the register's one designed cross-level read: outcome-level values serve as evidence for an impact-level judgment. No arithmetic combines them, and none could: a cohort share, a survey score and several percentages have no common unit. The levels connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: the composite adds none of its own, but two risks carry through and must be named in the judgment text. Feeder values labeled as upper estimates or as not de-duplicated across projects (innovations carry no institutional identifier; cross-project person counts cannot always be de-duplicated) keep that label. And KPI-OC01 and KPI-OC16 view the same uptake from two sides, innovation's and person's, so favorable movement in both is one signal read twice, not two independent confirmations, and the two fill one place in the group reading (Calculation method).
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Missing data: a feeder with no reportable value that year, fresh or carried forward, is named as missing, never silently skipped, and the judgment proceeds on the remaining feeders with its reduced evidence base stated. A value once entered is carried forward in later years, so a feeder is missing only where no validated value of it has ever been entered. A group left with no current places, or with no place able to move, is not read, and the summary category is then not assessable (Calculation method).

Repeated observations: one judgment per reporting year; a feeder value already entered in an earlier year's judgment may reappear only labeled as carried forward, not as new evidence, and a value first entered this year is fresh. The synthesis rubric applying that rule is set out under Calculation method and Sub-metrics.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only, twice over: each feeder already stops at contribution (adoption and partnership behavior depend on partner capacity, markets and policy), and the composite adds an interpretive step on top. It is also largely a self-assessment: KPI-OC05 is the only feeder carrying the partner's own voice, and it is itself skewed upward by courtesy bias, so it corroborates rather than corrects; where KPI-OC05 and KPI-OC03 diverge, the judgment records the divergence rather than resolving it toward either.

Inherits every feeder's measurement error and labels: KPI-OC01's threshold and lag sensitivity, self-reported adoption in KPI-OC16, upper-estimate labels where de-duplication was not possible, and KPI-OC04's two moving parts, where the gap index can fall because required competencies were defined downward, so a favorable movement can mean the standard dropped rather than capability rose. A confident-sounding conclusion cannot be more precise than its weakest feeder.

Without a fixed rubric, values are not comparable across years and the composite invites narrative inflation: seven indicators can be read selectively to support a preferred conclusion. The rubric's test is reproducibility: two compilers reaching the same conclusion from the same evidence pack, which is why movement is read against the value entered in the last judgment under a stated significance rule (Calculation method).
KPI-OC01 and KPI-OC16 measure the same uptake from two sides; agreement between them is expected, not corroborating, which is why the rubric counts them as one place.

A "strengthening" judgment means the feeder evidence moved favorably, nothing more: not that farmer incomes, food security or environmental outcomes improved (other pathways measure those), and not a claim that any given partner would endorse CIMMYT.
subMetrics:
The register's one genuinely composite indicator: each component is a separately calculated metric with its own reference sheet, cross-referenced rather than reproduced here.

— KPI-OC01: Percentage of released co-created innovations adopted at scale (adoption, innovation side).

— KPI-OC16: Percentage of assisted persons reporting adoption of new or improved inputs, technologies or practices (adoption, person side; sex- and age-disaggregated).

— KPI-OC23: Percentage of the smallholder-facing research portfolio responding to farmer-articulated priorities.

— KPI-OC03: Percentage of partners returning for follow-on work (repeat partnership).

— KPI-OC05: Partner-survey score of partnership quality across trust, equity and effectiveness (the one feeder carrying the partner's own voice).

— KPI-OC04: Percentage change in the digital-skills gap index among CIMMYT staff and partners (capability built in partner organizations; the one feeder from another pathway, Capacity, data & institutions).

— KPI-OC60: Percentage of sub-grants involving Global South partners (equity of partnering practice).

The seven are not weighted against each other; they are read as two groups: adoption (KPI-OC01, KPI-OC16, KPI-OC23) and partnership standing (KPI-OC03, KPI-OC04, KPI-OC05, KPI-OC60). The within-group and between-group reading rules are set out under Calculation method.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: none of its own; feeder values arrive through their own sheets' pipelines. Validation: CIMMYT MEAL unit confirms each feeder value is final and carried with its vintage and any estimate label. Calculation (compilation): CIMMYT MEAL unit assembles the evidence pack and drafts the judgment per the rubric. Approval: the office that approves CIMMYT's institutional results reporting. Reporting: CIMMYT MEAL unit into institutional and Board reporting.
sourceRef: Volume 1 · Innovation development & scaling — Reference sheet KPI-I01

name: Number of individuals trained annually by CIMMYT
resultsLevel: Output. What the count reports is a delivered result: a person who completed structured training, which is the capacity CIMMYT delivered. Whether trainees' knowledge or behaviour then changed is a change rather than a delivery, measured at outcome level for the digital-capability slice by KPI-OC04; the rest of the count has no single outcome indicator above it. CGIAR reporting carries people trained at output level under Capacity Development; this sheet follows that convention (see Limitations for the boundary caveat).
primaryObjective: PO1 Defined by transdisciplinarity, CIMMYT is an efficient, innovative, and inclusive partner contributing to agrifood systems transformation. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved).
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs: training builds the skills base through which livelihood and job improvements travel. CGIAR itself does not assign capacity sharing results to a single Impact Area; each reported training carries its own Impact Area scores. The register carries no Impact Area column; the value follows the pathway-wide rule, which decides the area by what the indicator measures.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest indicator is SDG 4.3.1 (participation rate of youth and adults in formal and non-formal education and training in the previous 12 months, by sex), but it measures population-level participation from national labour force surveys, not one organization's training delivery count.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR: this is the CGIAR standard output indicator "Number of people trained" under Capacity Sharing for Development; the Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 requires it gender disaggregated, with length of training and delivery method. No other external framework supplies the method for this count; the structured-learning boundary and the unique-count rule are CIMMYT's own, applied on CGIAR's definition.
definition: Counts unique individuals trained by CIMMYT in the reporting year, disaggregated by age and sex, counted once per individual regardless of the number of trainings attended. It uses the CGIAR definition of people trained: individuals trained with the aim of leading to changes in knowledge and behaviour. Training means a structured learning activity with defined learning objectives, short-term (less than 3 months) or long-term (3 months or more, including supervised MSc and PhD students), delivered in person, virtually or blended. Attendance at meetings, field days or events without a structured learning objective is not training.
rationale: Answers how many people CIMMYT equipped with new knowledge and skills each year: the delivery step of the capacity development pathway, and, for its digital-capability slice, the base against which capacity change (KPI-OC04) is read. It adopts the CGIAR standard "number of people trained" definition unchanged, so project values feed CGIAR technical reporting directly and are comparable across CGIAR centers.
projectSpecificApplication: State which training activities the project delivers (courses, workshops, e-learning, degree supervision), the trainee groups targeted, the geographic scope, and which attendance registers feed the count. Do not alter the unique-count rule, the completed-training rule, or the structured-learning boundary; if the indicator as defined is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count informs: for example a donor-required capacity development indicator, a training coverage target, or a trigger to adjust recruitment or delivery mode if participation among women or youth stays low.
projectTypesNotApplicable: none. Any project type can deliver structured training, and the exclusions in Eligibility turn on what the activity was
not on the type of project that ran it
projectTypesRaw:
Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: none. Any project type can deliver structured training, and the exclusions in Eligibility turn on what the activity was, not on the type of project that ran it.
unit: Number of individuals (unique persons)
directionOfChange: Increase, read against the delivery plan. A rising value means more individuals were trained by CIMMYT. The count says nothing about training quality or depth, so it is read alongside the length-of-training breakdown.
disaggregationRequired: Required: sex (collected as female, male, and prefer not to say; reported as female and male per the register, with the third category reported as a labelled residual rather than dropped or redistributed, because a redistributed count cannot be recovered afterwards and a dropped one shrinks the total without saying so); age (youth/non-youth, 15 to 30, stated once in Core Section 4.1; projects record date of birth or exact age so other bands, for example a donor band of 15 to 29, can be derived without recollecting data); length of training (short-term, under 3 months / long-term, 3 months or more, including MSc and PhD students) and delivery method (in-person / virtual / blended), which CGIAR's Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 requires with sex; the register does not list them, and they are required here on that ground. A person may appear in more than one length or delivery subtotal, so subtotals are never summed to the headline.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Trainee group (farmer, extension agent, researcher, student, partner staff); attending on behalf of an organization; country or region.
unitOfObservation: Individual
calculationSummary: Value = the count of unique individuals who completed at least one qualifying CIMMYT training in the reporting year. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: the training programmes' own administrative records: attendance registers, registration databases, learning-management-system completion records, and university enrolment and graduation records for supervised degree students, each carrying a unique identifier, sex, age and organization. Fallback DS1: a follow-up survey of participants to reconstruct completion and identity fields where registers are incomplete or lack the fields needed for de-duplication; values from this route are flagged as fallback-sourced. Not applicable DS3: receipt of training is not observable from satellite data. Not applicable DS4: secondary databases hold no record of who CIMMYT trained. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced data cannot verify that an identified individual completed a CIMMYT training.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether Recommended or Fallback was used, which registers or platforms supplied records, and how de-duplication across trainings and partners was done. If Fallback, state why the training registers were not usable.
collectionInstrument: For the recommended DS2 route: a standard registration and attendance template capturing name or ID, sex, age, organization represented, and course metadata (title, dates, length category, delivery method). For the DS1 fallback: a short participant survey module capturing the same fields plus completion status, administered in person or by phone.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as attendance registers and learning platforms log participation; compiled and de-duplicated annually.
referencePeriod: The reporting year; a long-term trainee is counted in the year the training is completed. Each annual value stands alone (see Limitations on why annual values are never summed).
baselineRequired: No. As an annual output count the value starts from zero each reporting year; the first reported year serves as the reference point for trend context. No change or impact claim rests on this indicator alone.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool counts from projects that used the Recommended source; a project that used the Fallback survey route is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, not blended in, because survey-reconstructed counts carry recall and identification error.

B: Combination method. Sum unique individuals across trainings and projects after de-duplication by identifier, so a person trained twice by CIMMYT counts once in the institutional figure.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of unique individuals on that project's training registers who completed a qualifying training in the reporting year, de-duplicated on the identifier Block E names. At institutional level, the count of unique individuals across projects, de-duplicated again across registers, since one person trained by two projects is one person and summing project counts would report them twice. Where identifiers cannot be reconciled across registers, the institutional figure is labelled an upper estimate rather than presented as a count. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the reconciliation basis, and the number of records dropped for want of an identifier.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count does not add to KPI-OC04 or any outcome value; the levels connect through the theory of change, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: de-duplicate by identifier across trainings and projects; where matching is not possible, label the pooled figure an upper estimate. The identifier is the register's unique person ID where one exists, otherwise an exact match on full name, sex and organization, with date of birth where recorded. A person appearing in both a Recommended register and a Fallback survey figure is one person: the survey figure is reduced by the matched records before it is reported beside the pooled count, and where the two cannot be matched the note beside the Fallback figure says so rather than the two being added. Across indicators, overlap is named, never summed: this count is the institutional umbrella and includes the farmers Vol. 1 · KPI-O18 counts on its direct delivery route (both descend from the same CGIAR people-trained standard), so the two are never summed and the institutional report states that overlap alongside the umbrella total; KPI-O18's cascade-trained farmers are not in this count; CIMMYT staff completing internal capacity development are excluded here; structured development through the Learning and Training academy is counted under Vol. 12 · KPI-O53, and internal training outside the academy is counted by no indicator in the register.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion: individuals completing a structured training activity with defined learning objectives, delivered by CIMMYT or on its behalf under a project agreement; short-term and long-term training both count, and supervised MSc and PhD students count as long-term trainees. Only completed trainings are reported (the CGIAR rule), which prevents the same trainee being counted across several years of a multi-year programme.
limitations: Counts delivery, not learning: completing a training says nothing about whether knowledge or behaviour changed. CGIAR's own review of its standard indicators judged people trained mismatched to its result level, a better proxy of capacity change than of capacity sharing; this sheet keeps it at output level, as current CGIAR reporting does, and reads it only as the delivery step of the pathway, alongside KPI-OC04 for the digital-capability slice.

A headcount carries no intensity: a one-day workshop participant and a completed PhD each count as one individual, so the headline can rise while training depth falls. Always read it with the short-term/long-term and delivery-method breakdowns.

De-duplication quality drives the number: registers with inconsistent or missing identifiers hide repeat trainees (overcount) or merge distinct people (undercount); the identification standard applied must travel with the value.

The structured-learning boundary is a judgement at the margin: extended field days or coaching series can resemble training, so where the line is drawn affects comparability across projects and years; state the rule applied.

Annual values are not cumulative: the same person can count in successive years, so summing years overstates unique people trained. The completed-training rule also delays long-term trainees to their completion year, so a year with many ongoing degree students can look artificially low.
subMetrics: None. Length of training, delivery method and trainee group are disaggregations of the same unique count, not separately calculated metrics. Related indicators have their own sheets: KPI-O18 (farmers trained, a sibling count from the same CGIAR standard), KPI-O53 (staff completing structured capacity or career development, the institutional counterpart) and KPI-OC04 (digital-skills gap index among CIMMYT staff and partners, the outcome for this count's digital-capability slice only).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the capacity development / academic programmes lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: training organizers and project teams maintaining attendance registers, learning platforms and student records. Validation: project MEAL officer (identity fields complete, completion verified, structured-learning boundary applied). Calculation: project M&E, applying the unique-count rule; cross-project de-duplication by the CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit, which reports the institutional figure through CGIAR technical reporting.
sourceRef: Volume 2 · Capacity, data & institutions — Reference sheet KPI-O04

name: Proportion of CIMMYT research datasets that are disaggregated by sex
resultsLevel: Output. What the share reports is a delivered result: whether the datasets CIMMYT registered in the period carry a populated sex variable. It is a property of the deliverable itself and not a change in behaviour, systems or practice, which is what would put it at outcome level.
indicatorScope: Mission. It measures a property of the research CIMMYT produces rather than of CIMMYT as an organization, which is what keeps it on the Mission branch even though the outcome it contributes to (KPI-OC41) is Institutional; the reasoning is in the settled note below.
primaryObjective: PO1 Defined by transdisciplinarity, CIMMYT is an efficient, innovative, and inclusive partner contributing to agrifood systems transformation. It serves objective 1.5, capacity to handle data and reduce gaps in data and knowledge management to support evidence-based decision making within CIMMYT and among partners. Contributing objectives: none; the register records PO1 alone.
cgiarImpactArea: Gender Equality, Youth & Social Inclusion. Sex-disaggregated data is the evidentiary basis on which any gender-equality claim in CIMMYT's portfolio rests. The register carries no Impact Area column; the value follows the pathway-wide rule, which decides the area by what the indicator measures.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest target is SDG 17.18 (increase significantly the availability of high-quality, timely and reliable data disaggregated by income, gender, age and other characteristics), but its indicators measure national statistical systems, not a research organization's own datasets: 17.18.1 scores national statistical office websites through the Open Data Inventory coverage index, and 17.18.2 and 17.18.3 concern national statistical legislation and funded national statistical plans.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR: the Performance and Results Management Framework 2022-30 requires results data to be disaggregated by gender for capacity development, empowerment, inclusion and smallholder-benefit results, and the Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 instructs that indicators be disaggregated by gender and youth where possible. CGIAR evaluation practice treats the presence of sex-disaggregated data as one of the features determining whether gender, equality, youth and social inclusion questions can be evaluated at all. No donor framework known to this handbook carries this indicator as a named metric.
definition: Measures the share of CIMMYT research datasets registered in the reporting period that carry a sex variable, so their data can be analysed separately for women and men. The share is taken over the eligible subset, datasets describing people or households, with the share over all registered datasets reported alongside it. A dataset qualifies when the sex of the person each record describes is recorded as a variable in the dataset itself, using female and male as the minimum categories, and populated for at least 90 percent of the records it applies to. Recording sex only in a report, or only for the person interviewed while the observations describe others, does not qualify. It measures readiness for gender analysis, not whether such analysis was carried out.
rationale: Answers whether the evidence CIMMYT produces can be read separately for women and men, the precondition for every gender-differentiated finding the institution later reports. A sex variable missing from the data cannot be recovered afterwards, so this indicator tracks a choice made at instrument-design stage, for research management, CGIAR technical reporting, and donors requiring gender-responsive evidence.
projectSpecificApplication: State which of the project's datasets fall inside the reporting period, where they are deposited, and which person-level or household-level units they describe. Do not change the qualifying rule, the denominator, or the calculation method above. If the project generates only datasets with no person-level unit of observation, say so rather than reporting a value of zero, and raise it with the MEAL focal point.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this share informs: for example a donor requirement for gender-disaggregated evidence, a data management plan commitment, or an internal trigger to revise survey instruments and data templates if the share stays low.
projectTypesNotApplicable: none. Every project type registers research datasets and so contributes to the denominator
where a project type produces no dataset with a person or household unit
so the type is not excluded here
projectTypesRaw:
Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: none. Every project type registers research datasets and so contributes to the denominator; where a project type produces no dataset with a person or household unit, the eligible-subset screen handles it, so the type is not excluded here.
unit: Percentage of datasets
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of CIMMYT research datasets carry sex disaggregation. The denominator is the eligible subset (datasets describing people or households); the share over all registered datasets is reported beside it.
disaggregationRequired: Required: eligibility for sex disaggregation (datasets whose unit of observation is a person or household, against those whose unit is a plot, genotype, environment or market series), reported as two subtotals, since the headline share is taken over the eligible subset and the share over all registered datasets is reported beside it. Sex categories inside a dataset use female and male at minimum, following the CGIAR standards for collecting sex-disaggregated data.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Research programme or unit; data type (survey, trial, laboratory, administrative); country or region; deposit status (open, embargoed, internal); funder.
unitOfObservation: Result object: one CIMMYT research dataset, the thing each record describes. A dataset CIMMYT produces is a delivered knowledge product, which is what the result-object value covers; "secondary dataset" is the value for a dataset CIMMYT reads rather than produces. KPI-O44 and KPI-OC41 name the same unit the same way.
calculationSummary: Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100. Numerator: CIMMYT research datasets registered in the reporting period carrying a populated sex variable that meets the qualifying rule in the Definition; for a dataset whose unit is the household, the variable qualifies when sex is recorded for each member the household roster lists, or for the individual respondent where the observations describe that respondent, and sex of the household head alone does not qualify; the base for the 90 percent completeness test is the records the variable applies to, excluding records for which sex is legitimately not applicable. Denominator: the eligible subset, that is CIMMYT research datasets registered in the reporting period whose unit of observation is a person or a household. The same numerator over all registered datasets is computed and reported alongside as the second figure, so a reader can see both the practice and the research mix behind it; the two are never combined into one number. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: CIMMYT's own research data management records, that is the deposit and curation records of the institutional system of record, the dataset registry KPI-O44 and KPI-OC41 also read, read for each dataset's unit of observation, variable list or variable-level metadata, and any flag recording whether a sex variable is present. Comparator DS4: CGIAR-level and other external repositories holding CIMMYT datasets, used to check the internal inventory's completeness: a CIMMYT dataset they hold that is not registered in the system of record is outside both shares and is reported beside them; never pooled. Not applicable DS1: whether a dataset carries a sex variable is a property of an existing file, established by inspecting it, not by surveying respondents or measuring in the field; researcher self-report would not verify the variable's presence. Not applicable DS3: a dataset's variable structure is not observable from satellite or geospatial data. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced and mobile data cannot establish what variables CIMMYT's datasets contain.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which system supplied the dataset list and how datasets deposited in more than one repository were de-duplicated.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source. The screening rule is set out under Calculation method and runs in two steps. Presence of the sex variable is read from the deposit record or, where the deposit form carries no sex-disaggregation field, from the dataset's variable list. Completeness is then computed against the deposited data itself, as the share of in-scope records carrying a value, since a variable list establishes that a column exists and never that it is filled. Where the deposited data cannot be read and only the variable list is available, completeness cannot be tested: the dataset stays in the denominator, counts as not disaggregated, and the share of such datasets is reported beside the value.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as datasets are deposited and their metadata recorded; compiled annually.
referencePeriod: The reporting year: datasets registered between 1 January and 31 December. Each annual value describes that year's data production, not accumulated repository holdings.
baselineRequired: Yes. The value is only interpretable as a trend. Where no baseline was set: recompute a past year's value from existing repository metadata, which is retrospective by nature; if earlier metadata holds no variable-level information, audit a random sample of that year's datasets. The sample estimates that year's share and its error, reported with the confidence interval; it does not replace the full count of datasets in the system of record, which every later year is computed on, so a change against a sampled baseline is claimed only where the later year's value lies outside that interval. If neither is feasible: monitoring only, no change claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool the datasets registered in the system of record, after the de-duplication Block E requires.

B: Combination method. Pool at dataset level: the institutional figure is qualifying datasets divided by the eligible datasets in scope, never the average of project-level percentages; the all-registered share is formed the same way, over its own wider denominator.

C: Levels and operations. A share is recomputed at every level from its own numerator and denominator, never averaged from the levels beneath it: a mean of project percentages weights a project depositing three datasets equally with one depositing three hundred. The denominator is a portfolio of datasets rather than a population measured in the field, so the measurement levels do not apply here and the levels are reporting levels. At project level, that project's qualifying datasets over its own eligible datasets registered in the period. At institutional level, the summed numerator over the summed denominator across projects, after the de-duplication Block E requires, since a dataset deposited by two projects is one dataset and not two. Both figures are built this way, the eligible-subset share and the all-registered share, at every level. Also report: the eligible denominator itself, the all-registered share beside it so the screen is visible, the number of datasets excluded under Eligibility, the share whose metadata could not be screened, the share that could not be tested for completeness because the deposited data could not be read, and the number of CIMMYT datasets held externally and not registered.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This share does not add to or average with KPI-OC41 (FAIR compliance), the outcome it contributes to; the two measure different properties of the same datasets and connect through the theory of change, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: de-duplicate by persistent identifier (DOI or handle) before pooling, so a dataset held in two repositories or produced jointly by two projects counts once; where identifiers are absent, match on title, unit of observation and period, and label the pooled denominator an upper estimate. Overlap across indicators must be named, never summed: KPI-O05, KPI-O44 and KPI-OC41 read the same dataset registry, so their numerators are overlapping subsets of one population and must not be added into a single data-quality total; their denominators are not the same quantity, KPI-O44 being a count with no denominator and KPI-OC41's being the cumulative registered stock.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: datasets registered in CIMMYT's system of record during the period, whether generated by CIMMYT staff or by partners under a CIMMYT project agreement. Each dataset's unit of observation is recorded at registration, since it is what places the dataset inside or outside the eligible subset; a dataset whose component tables have different units is in the eligible subset when any of them has a person or a household as its unit, and the qualifying rule and the 90 percent completeness test apply to those tables only; a dataset outside the eligible subset is not dropped, it is reported in the second figure.

Exclusion: corporate and administrative datasets that are not research outputs (human resources, finance, procurement); duplicate deposits; versions already counted in an earlier period, unless the new version adds the sex variable, in which case it counts in the period of the revision.

Missing data: a dataset whose metadata does not record whether a sex variable is present, or whose deposited data cannot be read to test completeness, stays in the denominator and counts as not disaggregated, with each share reported alongside the value, since the alternative overstates the result. A CIMMYT dataset held externally and not registered in the system of record is reported beside both shares as Data source sets out, not among the exclusions.

Repeated observations: one dataset counts once per period, whatever the number of files, tables or waves it contains; a multi-part deposit sharing one persistent identifier is one dataset.
limitations: Presence is not quality: a dataset can clear the qualifying rule and still not support gender analysis, for example when the ten percent the completeness floor allows is concentrated in the subgroup an analysis needs. The floor removes the emptiest cases; it does not make a variable analytically sufficient.

Which denominator is read matters as much as practice does: most CIMMYT research datasets have a plot, genotype, environment or market series as their unit of observation, where sex is not a meaningful attribute. The headline is therefore taken over the eligible subset; the all-registered share is reported beside it and moves with the annual mix of research types, so it reads as a statement about CIMMYT's research portfolio rather than about its disaggregation practice.

Only registered datasets are visible: datasets held on project drives and never deposited cannot be counted, so a rising value may reflect improved deposit compliance rather than improved disaggregation practice.

Comparability over time and across centers depends on a stable rule for what counts as a research dataset and what counts as disaggregated; if the screening rule changes, the series breaks and must be restated.

A rise means a larger share of the eligible datasets CIMMYT registered that year can be analysed by sex. It does not mean gender analysis was performed, published or used in a decision, and it says nothing about gender equality outcomes in the field.
subMetrics: None. The eligibility split and the research-unit breakdowns are disaggregations of the same ratio, not separately calculated metrics. Two indicators in this indicator group read the same dataset registry and have their own sheets: KPI-O44 (number of datasets produced or published following FAIR principles) and KPI-OC41 (percentage compliant with FAIR principles), the outcome this indicator contributes to.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with CIMMYT's research data and knowledge management function as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project data managers and principal investigators depositing datasets, with curators recording unit of observation and variable-level metadata. Validation: the research data management function, confirming consistent application of the screening rule and reporting both the share whose metadata could not be screened and the share that could not be tested for completeness. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: project leader for the project-level value; MEAL unit head for the institutional figure. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 2 · Capacity, data & institutions — Reference sheet KPI-O05

name: Number of farmers reached with digital advisory services
resultsLevel: Output. What the count reports is a delivered result: a farmer reached with a digital advisory service, which is the delivery itself. Whether farmers then act on the advice is a change rather than a delivery, measured at outcome level by Vol. 1 · KPI-OC16.
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Contributing: PO1 (Defined by transdisciplinarity, CIMMYT is an efficient, innovative, and inclusive partner contributing to agrifood systems transformation).
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs. Reaching farmers with advisory services is a delivery step of the livelihood pathway PO3 describes; the contribution to Gender Equality, Youth & Social Inclusion is carried by the required sex and age breakdowns. The register carries no Impact Area column; the value follows the pathway-wide rule, which decides the area by what the indicator measures.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest target is SDG 2.3 (double the productivity and incomes of small-scale food producers), but its official indicators (2.3.1, production per labour unit; 2.3.2, average income of small-scale food producers) measure results among producers, not how many are reached by services. SDG 17.8.1 (proportion of individuals using the Internet) measures population-level ICT use, not programme reach.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR: the One CGIAR standard indicator set carries "Number of people (m/f) reached by CGIAR innovations" under Innovation Use, and this count feeds it as supporting evidence. It does not feed the Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 minimum data standard's "number of people using" field, which records use, and a delivered advisory is not use. No external framework supplies the method for this count: the identification requirement, the unique-count rule and the exclusion of unidentifiable broadcast audiences are CIMMYT's own, applied on CIMMYT's authority.
definition: Counts unique farmers reached with digital advisory services by CIMMYT in the reporting year, once per farmer. Digital advisory services are agronomic, weather and climate, or market advice delivered digitally: mobile applications, SMS or voice messaging, interactive voice response, call centres, chatbots, or digitally supported extension. A farmer counts as reached when identifiable in the service's records by a registration ID or phone number and reached by at least one advisory in the year through a service CIMMYT runs or that runs for it. Audiences that cannot be identified individually, such as radio, are not counted. No farmer is excluded for farm size: smallholder status is recorded as an attribute per Annex B, with the declared threshold travelling with the value.
rationale: Answers how many individual farmers CIMMYT's digital advisory work reaches each year: the delivery step of the digital advisory and service delivery pathway, extending advice beyond what face-to-face extension can cover. It establishes the reach base against which adoption (Vol. 1 · KPI-OC16) can be read and supplies the sex- and age-disaggregated reach reporting donors and CGIAR technical reporting expect. It connects to service-reach expansion (KPI-OC24) through handover, when a platform CIMMYT ran passes to a strengthened provider.
projectSpecificApplication: Where the project's own scope is smallholders, declare that scope here with the Annex B threshold it applies; the institutional figure counts all farmers reached, and a count over all farmers and a count over smallholders are reported side by side and never pooled. State which digital channels and platforms the project runs, the geographic scope, the advisory content covered, and which platform records feed the count. Do not change the unique-count rule or the identification requirement; if applying the indicator as defined is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count informs: for example a donor-required digital-reach indicator, a platform coverage target, or an internal trigger to adjust content, language or channel mix if reach among women or youth stays low.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work runs no advisory service and has no farmers to reach
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI; breeding and varietal development.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work runs no advisory service and has no farmers to reach.
unit: Number of farmers (unique individuals), with smallholder status recorded as a disaggregation per Annex B
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more farmers were reached with digital advisory services.
disaggregationRequired: Required: sex (female/male); age (youth/non-youth, 15 to 30, stated once in Core Section 4.1; projects record date of birth or exact age so that other bands, for example a donor band of 15 to 29, can be derived without recollecting data). Smallholder status is not required here, and the difference from Vol. 7 · KPI-O24 is deliberate: O24's smallholder attribute is required because the impact indicator it feeds cannot otherwise draw its population. KPI-O26 contributes to KPI-OC24, which is terminal to PO3 and feeds no impact indicator, so that ground is absent. Smallholder status is recorded as a disaggregation per Annex B, with the declared threshold travelling with the value; it is not a required institutional cut. The register lists smallholder status among this indicator's disaggregations, so recording it as an attribute rather than requiring it as a cut is a deliberate divergence from that row, for the reason above. Sex is reported only where the account holder is the advice recipient. On a shared or household device the registered identity and the person who receives the advice can differ, so a sex breakdown built on the account holder would attribute advice to the wrong person; where the platform cannot establish that the two are the same, the record stays in the total under the not-available category rather than being assigned a sex.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Delivery channel (app / SMS or voice / interactive voice response / call centre / digitally supported extension; a farmer using several channels appears in each channel subtotal, so subtotals may exceed the unique headline count and must never be summed); advisory content type; country or region; new versus continuing users.
unitOfObservation: Individual
calculationSummary: Value = the count of unique farmers with at least one qualifying digital advisory contact in the reporting year. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: the digital services' own administrative and registration records: registration databases, message delivery and call logs, call-centre records and app usage logs, each carrying a unique identifier (registration ID or phone number), sex, age, location and landholding as registered. Not applicable DS1: a farmer survey cannot place a farmer in the service's records, which is what makes a farmer reached. Not applicable DS3: receipt of an advisory message is not observable from satellite or geospatial data. Not applicable DS4: secondary and international databases hold no records of who CIMMYT's services reached. Not applicable DS5: telecom big data or crowdsourced claims can indicate connectivity but cannot verify that an identified individual received CIMMYT advisory content, nor establish smallholder status.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which platforms supplied records and how de-duplication across platforms and partners was done. State the event each platform logs as a delivery.
collectionInstrument: The recommended DS2 route uses a standard registration template that captures the identity fields Data source names at sign-up, applied by the platform operator under the project's guidance.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as the platforms log registrations and deliveries; compiled and de-duplicated annually.
referencePeriod: The reporting year; each annual value stands alone (see Limitations on why annual values are never summed).
baselineRequired: No. As an annual reach count the value starts from zero for each new service and each reporting year; the first reported year serves as the reference point for trend context. No change or impact claim rests on this indicator alone.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool unique farmers across projects after the de-duplication in Block B.

B: Combination method. Sum unique farmers across platforms and projects after de-duplication by identifier (phone number or registration ID), so a farmer registered on two CIMMYT services counts once in the institutional figure.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of unique farmers on that project's platform registers who received at least one qualifying advisory in the reporting year, de-duplicated on the identifier Block E names. At institutional level, the count of unique farmers across projects, de-duplicated again across platform registers, since one farmer reached by two projects is one farmer and summing project counts would report them twice. Where identifiers cannot be reconciled across registers, the institutional figure is labelled an upper estimate rather than presented as a count. Where a service run on CIMMYT's behalf by an ag-tech partner reports only an aggregated figure, the partner's figure is reported as supplied, with the supplying partner, the event it counts as a delivery and the population the figure represents recorded alongside it. Such a figure cannot be de-duplicated against CIMMYT-run platform registers, so it sits beside the pooled institutional count and is never blended into it. The smallholder-status breakdown is recomputed at each level from that level's own records, never carried forward from a lower one, and the unknown share travels with it. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the reconciliation basis, the number of records dropped for want of an identifier, the engaged share where the platform records engagement, and the share of the count whose smallholder status is unknown.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count does not add to KPI-OC24 or KPI-OC16; the levels connect through the theory of change, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: de-duplicate by identifier across channels, platforms and projects; where matching is not possible (different identifier systems), label the pooled figure an upper estimate. The identifier is the phone number or registration ID Block B names. Across indicators, overlap must be named, never summed: a farmer reached digitally may also appear in Vol. 1 · KPI-O18 (farmers trained) or Vol. 1 · KPI-O20 (farmers accessing technology packages). Users of a platform CIMMYT co-runs with a provider strengthened under KPI-O27 are counted here and excluded from KPI-OC24; users of a platform handed to such a provider leave this count once the provider runs it on its own account and enter KPI-OC24's reach (see Eligibility). Never add this indicator to any of those to produce a total-farmers-reached figure.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: farmers individually identifiable in the records of a CIMMYT-run digital advisory service (or one run on CIMMYT's behalf, or co-run by CIMMYT with a provider strengthened under KPI-O27) who received at least one advisory in the year, received meaning an advisory the platform logs as delivered to the recipient (for example an SMS delivery receipt, a connected call, an app session, a delivered push notification or a logged extension contact); a message logged only as sent does not count.

Exclusion: audiences that cannot be individually identified (radio, public social media); non-farmers registered on the platform (extension agents, agrodealers, students); farmers reached only by independent providers CIMMYT strengthened, which belong to KPI-OC24's reach; duplicate accounts. No farmer is excluded for farm size: smallholder status is recorded as an attribute per Annex B, not used to restrict the count.
limitations: Measures reach, not use or benefit: a delivered advisory says nothing about whether the farmer read, understood or applied it. Read this count only as the delivery step of the pathway, alongside KPI-OC24 and KPI-OC16.

Delivery is not engagement: a message confirmed as delivered to an unused phone still counts as reach. The event each platform logs as a delivery is stated with the value, and where a platform records engagement, the engaged share is reported beside it.

Identification error runs in both directions: shared phones and household devices hide farmers behind one identifier, while multiple SIMs and duplicate accounts inflate the count; de-duplication quality determines how close the figure is to unique people.
