Smallholder status is weakly evidenced at registration: landholding is self-reported and rarely verified on digital platforms, so the smallholder breakdown is approximate; report the unknown share alongside the value rather than assuming the balance either way.
Annual values are not cumulative: the same farmer can be a continuing user across years, so summing years overstates total reach; multi-year reach requires de-duplication across the whole period.
subMetrics: None. Delivery channels and advisory content types are disaggregations of the same unique count, not separately calculated metrics. Related indicators have their own sheets: KPI-O27 (public or private service providers strengthened, the sibling output in this indicator group) and KPI-OC24 (change in service-delivery reach of strengthened service providers, the outcome this count contributes to per the register).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the digital advisory / extension systems lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: platform operators and project field teams maintaining registration and delivery logs. Validation: project MEAL officer (identity fields complete, de-duplication run, smallholder screen applied). Calculation: project M&E, applying the unique-count rule; cross-platform and cross-project de-duplication by the CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 2 · Capacity, data & institutions — Reference sheet KPI-O26

name: Number of public or private service providers strengthened to deliver technologies/services to smallholders
resultsLevel: Output. What the count reports is a delivered result: a provider organization that received a defined and documented capacity increase, which is the delivery itself. Whether the provider then performs better or reaches more farmers is a change rather than a delivery, measured at outcome level (KPI-OC24). This indicator stops at delivery, which keeps it at output level.
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Contributing: PO1 (Defined by transdisciplinarity, CIMMYT is an efficient, innovative, and inclusive partner contributing to agrifood systems transformation).
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs. Strengthened providers are the delivery channel through which technologies and services reach smallholder livelihoods, the pathway PO3 describes. The register carries no Impact Area column; the value follows the pathway-wide rule, which decides the area by what the indicator measures.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest target is SDG 2.a (increase investment in rural infrastructure, agricultural research and extension services), but its official indicator 2.a.1 (agriculture orientation index for government expenditures) measures the orientation of government spending, not providers strengthened, so there is no direct correspondence.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR: the results framework carries Capacity Sharing for Development as an output category (people trained, not organizations) and a capacity-change outcome standard indicator covering individuals, organizations and networks; the CGIAR standard set has no organization-level output count, so this indicator feeds those fields as supporting evidence rather than mapping one-to-one. No external framework supplies the method: the documented-capacity-increase test and the once-per-provider rule are CIMMYT's own, applied on CIMMYT's authority.
definition: Counts public or private service providers strengthened by CIMMYT to deliver technologies or services to smallholders in the reporting year; strengthening means a defined capacity increase (training, tools, systems), counted once per provider. A service provider is an organization, not an individual: an extension service, agrodealer network, seed producer, cooperative, mechanization or financial service provider, or digital platform operator. A provider counts as strengthened when CIMMYT, or a partner acting for it, delivered a defined and documented capacity increase against needs identified with the organization: staff training, tools or equipment, or systems installed or upgraded. Incidental contact, such as staff attending an untailored open event, does not count.
rationale: Answers how many delivery-channel organizations CIMMYT equipped each year to serve smallholder farmers. CIMMYT cannot reach every smallholder directly, so strengthening the providers farmers already use is the multiplier step of the service-delivery pathway: this count establishes the population of strengthened providers whose expanded reach is measured at outcome level (KPI-OC24), and it contributes evidence toward the CGIAR results framework's capacity-change outcome category.
projectSpecificApplication: State which provider types the project works with, the geographic scope, the forms of strengthening delivered, and the records documenting each provider's capacity increase. Do not change the once-per-provider rule, the organization-level unit, or the requirement for a defined and documented capacity increase; if applying the indicator as defined is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count informs: a donor-required capacity-strengthening indicator, a scaling strategy working through local providers, or a trigger to rebalance support across provider types if public or private channels lag.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no delivery channel to strengthen
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no delivery channel to strengthen.
unit: Number of service providers (organizations)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more public or private service providers met the defined capacity-increase criterion.
disaggregationRequired: Required: provider type (public/private).
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cut above applies to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Provider category (extension service, agrodealer, seed producer, cooperative or producer organization, mechanization or financial service provider, digital platform operator); form of strengthening (training, tools, systems; a provider receiving several forms appears in each subtotal, so subtotals may exceed the unique count and must never be summed); country or region; newly versus previously strengthened.
unitOfObservation: Organization
calculationSummary: Value = the count of unique service providers that received a defined, documented capacity increase from CIMMYT in the reporting year. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: project administrative and M&E records: capacity development plans or agreements with each provider, training registries, and delivery or installation records, each carrying the provider's name, type (public/private), category, location and dates of support. Fallback DS1: a structured verification interview with provider organizations, used where project records are incomplete or strengthening ran through an intermediary partner whose records CIMMYT cannot access; values from this route are flagged as fallback-sourced. Not applicable DS3: organizational capacity strengthening is not observable from satellite or geospatial data. Not applicable DS4: secondary and international databases hold no records of which providers CIMMYT strengthened. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced data cannot verify that a specific organization received a defined capacity increase from CIMMYT.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role each provider rests on, which records supplied the provider list, and how de-duplication was done. If Fallback, state why project records were not usable.
collectionInstrument: For the DS1 fallback: a provider verification questionnaire capturing the strengthening received, its form, dates, and the provider's type and category; respondent is a manager or authorized representative of the provider, in person or by phone. The recommended DS2 route uses a standard capacity-strengthening record template capturing the same fields at the point of delivery.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as projects log strengthening activities and completion; compiled and de-duplicated annually.
referencePeriod: The reporting year; each annual value stands alone (see Limitations on why annual values are never summed).
baselineRequired: No. As an annual delivery count the value starts from zero each reporting year; the first reported year is the reference point for trend context. Change in provider performance is measured by KPI-OC24 against its own baseline.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool the providers for which project records document (a) to (c) under Eligibility (Recommended); a provider for which any of them rests only on the Fallback verification interview is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note naming it, never blended in; the same project's record-evidenced providers stay pooled.

B: Combination method. Sum unique providers across projects after de-duplication by provider identity (organization name, registration number where available, location), so a provider strengthened by two CIMMYT projects counts once in the institutional figure.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying providers for the reporting year. At institutional level, the de-duplicated sum of those counts, computed from the provider records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one provider is often strengthened by more than one project. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels: a provider organization has no plot and no household, so the levels here are reporting levels rather than measurement levels. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the counting unit applied (headquarters or operating branch), the number of providers excluded under Eligibility and why, the cumulative count of distinct providers strengthened to date, and the number of providers reported alongside because they rest on the Fallback.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count does not add to KPI-OC24; the output and outcome connect through the theory of change, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: de-duplicate by provider identity across projects and partners; the counting unit is the operating unit that received the capacity increase, at the level at which it delivers to farmers, so where two projects strengthened branches of the same national organization each strengthened branch counts once; where records cannot resolve which unit received the strengthening, label the pooled figure an upper estimate. Across indicators, overlap must be named, never summed: the providers counted here, pooled or reported alongside, are the base population for KPI-OC24, and provider staff trained under an organizational strengthening plan may also appear in KPI-O04 (individuals trained); the same activity may legitimately generate counts in both, but the two count different units and must never be combined.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion: organizations delivering technologies or services to smallholders, for which project records document (a) capacity needs identified with the provider, (b) the strengthening delivered (training, tools, systems), and (c) completion within the reporting year. Smallholder-serving qualifies the provider and is not a per-farm test, so no Annex B threshold is applied to its clients: a provider qualifies where its client records or the project's documented targeting show that it serves smallholders, and the basis is recorded with the provider; no provider is excluded because part of its clientele is larger.
limitations: Measures support delivered, not capacity used: capacity is potential, visible only in performance, so a strengthened provider is one that received defined support, not one that demonstrably improved. Read this count only alongside KPI-OC24, which measures whether strengthened providers reach more farmers.

One provider is not one scale of delivery: a national extension agency and a single agrodealer each count as one, so the count says nothing about how many farmers the strengthened providers can serve; use the provider-category breakdown when interpreting movements.

The documentation test is fixed across projects, but it sets no floor on the intensity of support, so providers receiving very different packages count alike; the form-of-strengthening breakdown, where reported, shows the mix.

Counting units can shift: branches, franchises and federated cooperatives can read as one organization or many. The rule is fixed, the operating unit that received the capacity increase at the level at which it delivers to farmers, and it must be held constant across years; borderline cases are ruled by the project MEAL focal point and recorded with the reason.

Annual values are not cumulative: the same provider can receive support across several years, so summing years overstates the number of distinct organizations strengthened; multi-year totals require de-duplication across the whole period.
subMetrics: None. Provider types, categories and forms of strengthening are disaggregations of the same unique count, not separately calculated metrics. Related indicators have their own sheets: KPI-O26 (farmers reached with digital advisory services), KPI-O04 (individuals trained), and KPI-OC24 (change in service-delivery reach of strengthened providers, the outcome this count contributes to).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the capacity development / partnerships lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project teams and implementing partners maintaining capacity-strengthening records per provider. Validation: project MEAL officer (documentation complete, documentation test applied, provider type classified). Calculation: project M&E, applying the unique-count rule; cross-project de-duplication by the CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 2 · Capacity, data & institutions — Reference sheet KPI-O27

name: Number of datasets produced or published following FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) principles
resultsLevel: Output. The Core's results-level test asks whether the indicator reports a delivered result or a change, and reads it from the indicator statement itself for Institutional-branch indicators, because there is no external actor. What this count reports is the delivery: the datasets published to the FAIR standard in the year. By design in this pathway, the count of FAIR datasets is the output and the institution-wide compliance share (KPI-OC41) is the outcome expressing adopted practice.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Excellence in Operations.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. The indicator measures a property of CIMMYT's own data-management operations, an internal enabler rather than a result delivered to an external population; FAIR datasets serve every Impact Area indirectly by making evidence reusable, which is not a direct link.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator counts an organization's FAIR-compliant datasets. SDG target 17.18 (data availability) concerns national statistical capacity, not institutional research data management, so it is thematically adjacent only, not a correspondence.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR's open and FAIR data policy, which supplies the "data asset" concept CGIAR's quality-assurance guidance uses and makes FAIR management a CGIAR-wide obligation; CGIAR Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30, under which CGIAR's quality assurance screens reported knowledge products against FAIR criteria using automated scoring; the FAIR Guiding Principles themselves (Wilkinson et al. 2016), the international reference the acronym comes from.
definition: Counts the CIMMYT research datasets produced or published in the reporting year that follow the FAIR principles: Findable (persistent identifier and rich metadata), Accessible (retrievable through a clear access protocol), Interoperable (standard formats and vocabularies), Reusable (documented provenance and an explicit licence). Each distinct dataset meeting the FAIR criteria counts once, whatever the number of repositories holding it or projects reporting it. FAIR concerns how a dataset is described, licensed, and made available, not whether it is open: a dataset holding sensitive or personal data can be fully FAIR under controlled access.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT is turning its research data into a findable, usable institutional asset. The 2030 Strategy's Excellence in Operations objectives commit CIMMYT to "promote information and data sharing to foster a collaborative culture" and to "make relevant data accessible to partners and beneficiaries outside the organization"; publishing datasets to the FAIR standard is the verifiable expression of those commitments. It is also a CGIAR system obligation: CGIAR's quality-assurance guidance defines reported data assets by reference to CGIAR's open and FAIR data policy and screens them against FAIR criteria. The annual count of FAIR datasets is the volume behind the outcome indicator KPI-OC41 (share of all CIMMYT research datasets that are FAIR-compliant): the count shows publication effort, the share shows whether FAIR practice is becoming the institutional norm.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator). Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate data-management systems; there is no project instance to adapt it to.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organization, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Number of datasets (count of distinct FAIR-compliant research datasets in the reporting year)
directionOfChange: Increase, read with the volume caveat in section 6 (Limitations and interpretation). A rising value means more datasets were produced or published meeting the FAIR criteria. The count also rises when CIMMYT produces more datasets, so it is paired with KPI-OC41, the compliance share, before it is read as improved data governance.
disaggregationRequired: None. The register specifies no required disaggregation for this indicator.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Research programme or unit; repository of deposit; crop or research theme; access status (open versus controlled access). The template's "optional (project-specific)" field does not apply to an Institutional indicator; these are optional institutional cuts the data-governance function may add for management use.
unitOfObservation: Result object: one CIMMYT research dataset, the thing each record describes. It is a delivered knowledge product, which is what the result-object value covers; "secondary dataset" is the value for a dataset CIMMYT reads rather than produces, and is not this unit.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct CIMMYT research datasets produced or published during the reporting year that meet the FAIR criteria. The assessment instrument is the RDA FAIR Data Maturity Model indicator set. The pass set is its 20 essential indicators plus four the toolbox raises to essential, because the model classes none of its Interoperable indicators as essential: RDA-I1-01M and RDA-I1-01D (metadata and data expressed in a standardised knowledge-representation format), RDA-I2-01M (metadata using FAIR-compliant vocabularies) and RDA-R1.2-01M (provenance recorded to a community standard). A dataset passes when every indicator in the pass set is met. The profile is this toolbox's convention, which the model provides for, and it is the same test KPI-OC41 applies to the same dataset population. Where CGIAR's automated screening has already assessed a dataset, its result is reused only for the indicators in the pass set that the screening tests, as recorded with the assessment; every other indicator in the pass set is assessed by curator review. The two sheets must not apply different FAIR tests, or the year's count and the compliance share would describe different populations. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): CIMMYT's institutional research data repositories and data-management records, exported as metadata listing each dataset, its persistent identifier, deposit date, and FAIR assessment result. Comparator DS4 (Secondary & international databases): CGIAR system-level records (CGSpace and the CGIAR results-reporting platform), used to check the registry's completeness: a CIMMYT dataset these records list and the institutional research-data registry does not is outside the count and is reported beside it; never pooled, and never reported as a KPI-O44 value. Reusing CGIAR's screening result for a dataset the registry lists, as Calculation method sets out, is part of the Recommended route. Not applicable DS1 (Censuses & surveys): FAIR compliance is an administrative fact evidenced in repository records, not a condition reported by respondents. Not applicable DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation): data-management practice cannot be observed remotely. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): not relevant to an internal data-governance record.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source. The indicator is compiled from existing DS2 repository records, not collected with a DS1 or DS5 instrument.
collectionFrequency: Continuous administrative logging: repository records capture each deposit and its FAIR assessment as it occurs; compiled once per year.
referencePeriod: The CIMMYT reporting year in which the counting event falls. The counting event is publication or deposit in the repository, whichever is later, so each dataset is attributed to exactly one year and the register's "produced or published" wording is not read as two occasions to count.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual institutional count; the previous year's value is the reference for trend. Where a multi-year trend is wanted, the first year with complete repository records and a stable FAIR assessment instrument serves as the reference year.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable. This is an Institutional indicator compiled once from corporate data-management systems; there are no project-level instances to pool.

B: Combination method. Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level: distinct FAIR-compliant datasets are summed across programmes, units, and repositories after de-duplication by persistent identifier; never averaged.

C: Levels and operations. Computed once, at institutional level, as the count of distinct FAIR-compliant datasets produced or published in the reporting year, de-duplicated on the persistent identifier Block E names: one dataset held in three repositories is one dataset. There is no level beneath it, because no project, programme or unit holds a share of an institutional count; a dataset enters CIMMYT's holdings rather than the project that generated it. Where a view by programme, unit or repository is wanted, it is recomputed from that subset's own records, never taken as a share of the institutional figure. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels: a dataset has no plot and no household. Also report: the number of datasets assessed against the number registered, the count excluded under Eligibility and why, and the number of CIMMYT datasets CGIAR records list and the registry does not.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no, the default for the whole register. This count is the volume behind the numerator of KPI-OC41 (share of datasets FAIR-compliant), but the two are not added or otherwise combined arithmetically; they connect through the data-governance results chain as a narrative (effort produces practice).

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: the same dataset deposited in several repositories or reported through several projects is matched on its DOI or handle and counted once; if identifiers cannot be matched across all sources, the figure is labelled an upper estimate. Two named overlap risks: a dataset co-produced with another CGIAR center can be counted twice in CGIAR-level aggregation, so a co-produced dataset registered by CIMMYT counts once for CIMMYT and is flagged, letting CGIAR-level aggregation remove the duplicate; and a published dataset may also appear in a knowledge-product count in CGIAR reporting, a different indicator, so the two counts are never summed.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion and exclusion: includes research datasets registered in CIMMYT's institutional research-data registry, whether generated by CIMMYT staff or by partners under a CIMMYT project agreement, and deposited in a repository with a persistent identifier and machine-readable metadata; excludes internal working files and drafts, datasets without a persistent identifier, and non-data knowledge products (papers, reports, briefs) even where they carry data annexes. A new version of an already-counted dataset is the same dataset, not a new one, unless it constitutes a substantially new data collection.
limitations: Output-level only: counting FAIR-compliant datasets evidences publication practice, not that anyone found, accessed, or reused the data. Reuse and uptake are outside this indicator, and institutional adoption of FAIR practice is measured separately by KPI-OC41.

The count is volume-sensitive: it rises when CIMMYT produces more datasets, even if the share published FAIR stays flat or falls. A rising count with a falling KPI-OC41 share can mean output growth, not better governance; always read the pair together.

FAIR compliance is graded in most assessment tools (a score across the four principles), while this indicator needs a yes/no per dataset. The count therefore depends on the chosen instrument and threshold; changing either breaks comparability across years and must be documented, with the series restated or footnoted.
Accessible does not mean open: FAIR permits controlled access with clear conditions, so the count does not certify open data and should not be reported as an open-data figure.

Year attribution depends on the counting event: a dataset produced late in one year and published early in the next shifts between years, and the "produced or published" wording could count it twice if applied loosely. Fixing the counting event at the later of deposit and publication removes both distortions.
subMetrics: None. The related measure KPI-OC41 (percentage of CIMMYT research datasets compliant with FAIR principles) is a separate outcome indicator with its own reference sheet, not a sub-metric of this count: it adds a denominator (all CIMMYT research datasets) that this indicator deliberately does not carry.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: Knowledge Management & IT, which holds the research-data repository and registry records (deposit logging and FAIR assessment). Validation: Knowledge Management & IT data curators (identifier and metadata checks). Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (de-duplication and the distinct-dataset count per the Calculation method). Approval: head of Knowledge Management & IT, as the corporate data owner for research-data records. Reporting: Knowledge Management & IT to the CIMMYT MEAL unit. The same roles carry KPI-OC41, which reads the same registry.
sourceRef: Volume 2 · Capacity, data & institutions — Reference sheet KPI-O44

name: Percentage change in the digital-skills gap index among CIMMYT staff and partners
resultsLevel: Outcome, as recorded in the register. Tracked as change against baseline, not as an activity count: it moves only when assessed people can do more, not when CIMMYT delivers more training (counted at output level by KPI-O04 for partner staff). CGIAR's quality-assurance definitions place changes in the skills of external actors at outcome level; the partner-staff portion fits directly, and the CIMMYT-staff portion is an internal capability change the strategy objective explicitly covers ("within CIMMYT and among partners").
primaryObjective: PO1 Defined by transdisciplinarity, CIMMYT is an efficient, innovative, and inclusive partner contributing to agrifood systems transformation. Grounded in two PO1 sub-objectives: "CIMMYT's human and infrastructural capacities are continuously improved", and the data sub-objective assuring capacity to handle data and reduce data and knowledge management gaps "within CIMMYT and among partners". Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved), because digitally capable partner staff are the channel through which digital advisory and data-driven services reach smallholders.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. None of the five official Impact Areas fits, because this indicator measures the capability of CIMMYT and its partners rather than a result delivered to a population, and the pathway rule is that the Impact Area follows what the indicator measures rather than which branch it sits on.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest official indicator, SDG 4.4.1 (proportion of youth and adults with ICT skills, by type of skill; custodian ITU), measures the share of a general population performing defined ICT activities in the last three months, not a required-versus-current gap in a defined cohort. Its five skill areas are the core of the index's competence taxonomy (see Calculation method).
otherFrameworks: CGIAR results taxonomy: the Capacity Change standard indicator, "Change in capacity of key (a) individuals (b) organizations, (c) networks" (One CGIAR Standard Indicators report), is the one this change evidences, at scale (a), individuals; an individual gap index does not by itself evidence organizational capacity change; the standard indicator set counts people trained but has no skills-gap index. GRI 404: Training and Education 2016 frames the staff side (Disclosure 404-2, programmes for upgrading employee skills) but defines no gap index. No external framework defines a digital-skills gap index; the construct is CIMMYT-defined.
definition: Measures the percentage change, relative to a baseline assessment, in a digital-skills gap index covering CIMMYT staff and the staff of its partner organizations. The index expresses the distance between the digital competencies people's roles require and the competencies they currently demonstrate: zero means no gap, larger values mean a wider gap. The indicator reports the change against baseline, not the index level; a negative value means the gap is closing.
rationale: Answers whether the people CIMMYT's work depends on, its own staff and its partners' staff, are becoming able to do what increasingly digital agrifood research and delivery require. It measures the 2030 Strategy's Primary Objective 1 commitments on human capacities and data-handling capacity, and reads whether the capability gap narrows in the assessed population. For partner staff the training behind it is counted by KPI-O04. CIMMYT's own staff are excluded there, and their structured development through the Learning and Training academy is counted by Vol. 12 · KPI-O53, a related indicator the register does not route here.
projectSpecificApplication: State which partner organizations and staff cohorts the project assesses, in which countries, and around which capacity-development activities. The index construction, competence taxonomy, instrument and calculation are unchanged; only population, geography and assessment timing are project-specific. If applying the indicator as defined is not feasible, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this measure informs: for example a donor-funded digital capacity-building component that must demonstrate skills change rather than attendance, or an internal trigger to redesign training if a cohort's gap is not closing.
projectTypesNotApplicable: none. Any project type may hold a capacity-development agreement with a partner whose staff are assessed. The CIMMYT-staff half of the population has no project instance at all: it is assessed centrally, and only the partner-staff half carries a project layer
projectTypesRaw:
Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: none. Any project type may hold a capacity-development agreement with a partner whose staff are assessed. The CIMMYT-staff half of the population has no project instance at all: it is assessed centrally, and only the partner-staff half carries a project layer.
unit: Percentage change in the index relative to baseline, or change in index points where the baseline falls below the floor declared with it (see Calculation method)
directionOfChange: Decrease. A falling value means the gap between required and current digital competencies narrowed, the desired result being a negative change against baseline. The index can also fall because required competencies were defined downward, so reporting states which side of the gap moved (see Calculation method).
disaggregationRequired: Required: respondent group (CIMMYT staff / partner staff), since pooling the two populations can hide a widening partner gap behind staff progress; and sex (female/male), per CGIAR's sex-disaggregated data standards. The register records no disaggregation for this indicator; these two are set on the sheet's own authority, because a single blended figure would conceal the two things the indicator exists to reveal.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every cohort assessed.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Competence area; staff category or role group; partner organization type; country or region; age (youth/non-youth, 15 to 30, stated once in Core Section 4.1; projects record date of birth or exact age so other bands, such as a donor band of 15 to 29, can be derived).
unitOfObservation: Individual
calculationSummary: Two steps. Step 1, the index per assessment round: for each assessed person, gap share = (role-required competencies not met at required proficiency) / (total role-required competencies), 0 to 100. The round's index is the mean gap share across assessed individuals. Step 2, the indicator: Value = ((Index_current - Index_baseline) / Index_baseline) x 100. Numerator: current index minus baseline index. Denominator: baseline index. Where the baseline index is zero the percentage change is undefined and is not reported: the value is reported as the change in index points, and a baseline of zero means no measured gap existed, which is itself the finding. Near-zero baselines behave the same way in a weaker form, so the floor below which points change is reported rather than percentage change is declared once with each baseline, which fixes the unit, points or percent, for every round measured against that baseline; the floor and the unit are stated with the value. Where required-competency profiles are revised between the baseline round and the current round, the current round is scored twice: against the profiles in force at baseline, which gives the reported change, and against the revised profiles, which becomes the baseline of a new series: from the next round the value is the change against that revised baseline, reported with the round it starts from, and it is not chained to or compared with values before the revision. The difference between the two scores, over the persons scored both ways, is the movement on the requirement side and is reported beside the value. A person whose role had no profile at baseline is scored against the revised profile only and does not enter the reported change. The competence taxonomy is the five SDG 4.4.1 skill areas (information and data literacy; communication and collaboration; digital content creation; problem solving; safety) plus CIMMYT-defined role-specific research and data competencies. The construction is CIMMYT's own, applied on CIMMYT's authority: no external framework defines a digital-skills gap index. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended, DS1 (Censuses & surveys): a structured digital-competency assessment combining self-assessment against role-based required-competency profiles with skills testing where feasible; the only source observing both sides of the gap. Fallback, DS2 (Administrative & registry data): human-resources and learning-management records mapping completed training and certifications to required-competency profiles, used only where an assessment round cannot be fielded for part of the population; flagged as fallback: completing a course evidences exposure, not competence, so a DS2-based index tends to understate the gap. Not applicable, DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation): skills are not observable from satellite or geographic data. Not applicable, DS4 (Secondary & international databases): national ICT-skills statistics (e.g. the SDG 4.4.1 series) describe general populations and cannot resolve CIMMYT's staff and partner cohort. Not applicable, DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): crowdsourced or self-published data cannot verify competencies against defined role requirements.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether the project's partner-staff cohorts used the Recommended assessment instrument or the DS2 fallback mapping, and if Fallback, why an assessment round was not feasible.
collectionInstrument: For DS1: the instrument of record is CIMMYT's existing third-party digital-skills audit, run by Knowledge Management and Information Technology (KMIT), not an instrument built for this indicator; its items are mapped to the competence taxonomy in Calculation method before gap shares are computed. In form it is a digital-competency assessment (questionnaire with optional practical test items) administered online; the respondent is each in-scope staff or partner staff member, with the role's required-competency profile assigned beforehand.
collectionFrequency: A full assessment round every two years, with the latest value carried forward in intervening years and labelled as carried forward. Competence does not move fast enough to justify annual reassessment of the same population, and annual re-testing costs respondents more than the extra data point is worth.
reportingFrequency: Annually; between rounds the latest measured value is carried forward with its assessment year stated.
referencePeriod: Competencies as demonstrated at the assessment round, compared against the baseline round. Each value describes cumulative change since the baseline round in force (see Calculation method), not change during the reporting year.
baselineRequired: Yes, by construction: without a baseline round there is no value at all. Fallback where none exists: the first completed assessment round becomes the baseline, reporting from the second round onward. Retrospective reconstruction from training records is not acceptable, since it measures exposure rather than competence. Until a second round exists: monitoring only, no change claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Across projects: pool individual records assessed with the Recommended instrument. A record from the DS2 fallback, in any cohort or in the centrally assessed CIMMYT-staff population, is kept out of the pooled index and its change and reported beside them as a separately labelled index level with its record count, because a DS2 record evidences exposure rather than competence and understates the gap.

B: Combination method. The institutional value is computed once from the pooled individual assessment records of each round, never by averaging project-level percentage changes: a mean of changes across cohorts of very different sizes is not the change of the mean.

C: Levels and operations. Two things are computed here and neither may be averaged upward. The index for a round is recomputed at every level from that level's own individual assessment records, never from the indices beneath it: a mean of cohort indices weights a cohort of twelve equally with one of twelve hundred, and the per-person gap shares beneath them rest on different numbers of required competencies. The change is recomputed the same way, as the difference between two indices each built at that level from its own records, never as a mean of cohort-level changes. There is no project level for the CIMMYT-staff population, which is assessed once centrally. For partner staff, a project-level value is the index over that project's own assessed partner staff, and the change against the same construction in that cohort's baseline round. At institutional level, the index is computed from the pooled individual records of the round within the pooling domain of Block A, and the change against the baseline round built identically. Also report: the number of individuals assessed and the response rate at each level, the respondent-group split, the share of competence ratings scored by skills test rather than self-assessment, whether the required-competency profiles were revised between the two rounds, and which side of the gap moved, since an index that fell because requirements were redefined is not the same result as one that fell because competence rose.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: no. This value does not combine arithmetically with KPI-O04 (individuals trained), even though training is the main pathway to closing the gap; they connect through the theory of change.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: de-duplicate by personnel or participant identifier before computing the index; a person appearing in two cohorts (staff and partner project, or two projects) counts once per round, in one respondent group. If identifiers cannot be matched, state that the assessed-population total is an upper estimate.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion: all CIMMYT staff whose role profile carries a digital competence requirement, and staff of partner organizations holding a current capacity-development agreement with CIMMYT whose role profile carries such a requirement. The role-profile test applies to both populations: a person with no role-required competencies has no denominator for a gap share and is out of scope, not a zero. Partners without such an agreement are out of scope: CIMMYT has no standing to assess them and no mandate to close their gaps.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only: the gap also closes through recruitment, turnover, partners' own investment and general digitalization, and can widen despite good training because required competencies rise as technology changes.

The index has two moving parts, requirement and competence, and either moves the value: redefining role requirements shifts the index without anyone learning anything. Hold the taxonomy and required-proficiency profiles constant between rounds; across a revision, values are compared only on the baseline profiles (see Calculation method).

Self-assessed competence diverges from demonstrated competence, unevenly across groups, and training itself shifts the standard against which people rate themselves, so a self-assessed gap can move between rounds without any change in competence. Neither a level difference between groups nor a trend is read without the share of ratings scored by skills test, which is reported beside the value.

The assessed population is not a fixed panel: turnover, partner cohort changes and response-rate shifts move the index without any individual's skills changing. Report response rate and cohort composition alongside the value.
A falling index means the measured gap narrowed in the assessed population; it does not mean research output, delivery or partner performance improved, which are measured by other indicators.
subMetrics: None. Competence-area scores and the staff and partner group indices are disaggregations of one index, not separately calculated metrics. Related sheet: KPI-O04 (individuals trained annually by CIMMYT), the output the register routes into this indicator. Vol. 12 · KPI-O53 (staff completing structured development through the Learning and Training academy) is related and not routed here.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: Knowledge Management and Information Technology (KMIT), which runs the digital-skills audit, for the staff cohort; project teams for the partner-staff cohorts. Validation: project MEAL officers for project cohorts; KMIT for the staff cohort. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, per this sheet. Approval: CIMMYT MEAL unit lead. Reporting: CIMMYT MEAL unit; project MEAL focal points submit assessment records, not computed changes.
sourceRef: Volume 2 · Capacity, data & institutions — Reference sheet KPI-OC04

name: Change in service-delivery reach of strengthened service providers
resultsLevel: Outcome. What the value reports is a change rather than a delivery: the movement in the number of farmers strengthened providers reach, measured against each provider's own baseline. A value expressed as change against a baseline is an outcome. The strengthening activity itself is the delivered result, counted at output level under KPI-O27.
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Contributing: PO1 (Defined by transdisciplinarity, CIMMYT is an efficient, innovative, and inclusive partner contributing to agrifood systems transformation).
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs. Expanding the delivery capacity of providers who serve smallholders widens the population whose livelihoods CIMMYT's work can improve. The register carries no Impact Area column; the value follows the pathway-wide rule, which decides the area by what the indicator measures.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest target is SDG 2.3 (double the productivity and incomes of small-scale food producers), but its official indicators (2.3.1, production per labour unit; 2.3.2, average income of small-scale producers) measure results among producers, not the delivery reach of the organizations serving them.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR: the One CGIAR standard indicator set carries "Change in capacity of key (a) individuals (b) organizations, (c) networks" under the Capacity Change outcome category; the farmer-reach figures here do not feed the Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 "number of people using" field, since reach is not use. No external framework supplies the method: reading expanded delivery as the performance evidence that strengthening worked, and the cohort and baseline rules that make it measurable, are CIMMYT's own, applied on CIMMYT's authority.
definition: Measures the change in the number of farmers reached with technologies or services by the public and private service providers CIMMYT has strengthened (the providers counted under KPI-O27), relative to each provider's baseline reach recorded at the time of strengthening. Capacity only becomes visible when used, so expanded delivery is read as the performance evidence that the strengthening worked: the value is the net expansion in farmers served, summed across the strengthened-provider cohort. It counts farmers reached by the providers themselves, not farmers reached directly by CIMMYT's own services (KPI-O26). Smallholder is defined in Annex B, and the declared threshold travels with the value; it classifies the farmers reached rather than restricting who is counted.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's investment in service-provider capacity translates into more farmers served: the outcome step of the service-delivery pathway, turning providers strengthened (KPI-O27) into expanded delivery on the ground. It is the register's evidence for the CGIAR Capacity Change outcome category and supports institutional and donor reporting on whether capacity work scales delivery beyond what CIMMYT could reach alone.
projectSpecificApplication: Where the project's own scope is smallholders, declare that scope here with the Annex B threshold it applies; the institutional figure counts all farmers reached, and a count over all farmers and a count over smallholders are reported side by side and never pooled. State which strengthened providers the project tracks, the geographic scope, the services they deliver, each provider's baseline year and baseline reach figure, and which provider records feed the annual count. Do not change the change-relative-to-baseline construct, the cohort rule, or the boundary with KPI-O26; if applying the indicator as defined is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this measure informs: a donor-required capacity-strengthening outcome, a sustainability case for exiting direct delivery, or a trigger to revisit the strengthening package if providers' reach stagnates after support ends.
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, which strengthens no delivery channel and so contributes no provider to the cohort this indicator measures.
unit: Number of farmers (net change in farmers reached, relative to baseline), with smallholder status recorded as a disaggregation per Annex B
directionOfChange: Increase. A higher value means the strengthened providers in the cohort reach more farmers, net of their own baselines. It is a net change, so growth at one provider can be offset by contraction at another.
disaggregationRequired: Required: partner/institution type (public / private, per the register), using the provider-type categories applied in KPI-O27 so the two indicators disaggregate consistently. Smallholder status is not required here, and the difference from Vol. 7 · KPI-O24 is deliberate: O24's smallholder attribute is required because the impact indicator it feeds cannot otherwise draw its population. KPI-OC24 is terminal to PO3 and feeds no impact indicator, so that ground is absent. Smallholder status is recorded as a disaggregation per Annex B, with the declared threshold travelling with the value, because the reach it describes is a smallholder-serving one; it is not a required institutional cut. The register lists smallholder status among this indicator's disaggregations, so recording it as an attribute rather than requiring it as a cut is a deliberate divergence from that row, for the reason above.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cut above applies to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Sex and age of farmers reached, where provider records carry them (many do not; report the coverage of this breakdown rather than forcing it); country or region; service or technology type; per-provider percent change relative to baseline as a complementary presentation.
unitOfObservation: Organization (the strengthened service provider); the reported value counts the farmers in the providers' delivery records.
calculationSummary: Value = the sum, across strengthened providers in the cohort, of (farmers reached by the provider in the reporting year minus the provider's baseline reach). This is a net-change count, not a proportion. Baseline reach is the number of farmers the provider reached in the 12 months before CIMMYT's strengthening began, documented when the provider is counted under KPI-O27, and restated on a handover as Baseline required sets out or on re-entry after cohort exit as Eligibility sets out. The value is reported with its sign as measured: a provider or a cohort whose reach contracts produces a negative value, which is reported as such and is never floored at zero, because a contraction is the finding the indicator exists to surface. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: the strengthened providers' own administrative and delivery records (client registers, sales and distribution records, extension visit logs, platform user records), supplied through partner reporting under data-sharing terms agreed as part of the strengthening package. Fallback DS1: a structured provider survey collecting reported client numbers with spot verification against a sample of underlying records, used where a provider's record system cannot produce a client count; values from this route are flagged as fallback-sourced. Not applicable DS3: a provider-farmer service transaction is not observable from satellite or geospatial data. Not applicable DS4: no secondary database records which providers CIMMYT strengthened or how many clients they serve. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or telecom data cannot attribute delivery to a specific provider or establish smallholder status.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role each provider rests on, which providers supplied records versus survey responses, how baselines were documented, and the service event each provider's reach is read from. If Fallback, state why provider records were not usable.
collectionInstrument: For the DS1 fallback: a provider survey module capturing clients served in the reporting year and the baseline period, service types, and provider type; respondent is the provider's manager or records officer, in person or by phone, with spot verification of a record sample. The recommended DS2 route uses a standard partner reporting template, agreed at strengthening, capturing the same fields annually.
collectionFrequency: Annually, from provider delivery records compiled at year end.
referencePeriod: The reporting year, compared against each provider's own baseline period (the 12 months before strengthening began). Providers enter the cohort in different years, so the value is a rolling comparison against provider-specific baselines, not a single institutional base year.
baselineRequired: Yes, definitionally: the indicator is a change against each provider's baseline reach, so a provider without a baseline cannot enter the value. Where a service CIMMYT ran is handed to a provider in the cohort, the provider's baseline is restated upward by the number of farmers transferred at handover, and the restatement and its date are named in the reporting note: the transferred users are reach CIMMYT already built, so leaving the baseline at its pre-strengthening level would score an inherited user base as expansion the strengthening produced. The boundary rule that moves those farmers from KPI-O26 to this indicator decides which indicator counts them; it does not decide the baseline they are counted against. Fallback: reconstruct the pre-strengthening year's client count retrospectively from the provider's own records, flagged as reconstructed; if records do not go back that far, the provider is monitored (current reach reported descriptively) but contributes no change value and no outcome claim.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool the per-provider differences evidenced in the providers' own records (Recommended); a provider whose reach comes only from the Fallback survey, or that KPI-O27 reports alongside its own pooled figure, is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note naming it, never blended in; the same project's other providers are pooled.

B: Combination method. Sum per-provider net changes across providers; never average per-provider percent changes into an institutional figure, because providers differ enormously in size.

C: Levels and operations. What adds here is the difference, not the reach: the value is a sum of per-provider differences, each provider's reporting-year reach minus its own documented baseline reach. At provider level, that difference, computed against the baseline recorded when the provider entered the KPI-O27 cohort, as restated on any handover or re-entry. At project level, the sum of the differences for the providers that project tracks. At institutional level, the sum of the per-provider differences for every provider within the pooling domain of Block A, after the provider-identity de-duplication Block E requires. Percent changes are never summed or averaged upward: a provider doubling from two hundred farmers and one adding fifty thousand are not comparable as rates, and a mean of their percentages is not a portfolio figure. Because providers enter in different years, the institutional value is a sum of differences against staggered baselines rather than a comparison of two portfolio totals, and it is labelled as such wherever it is reported. The smallholder-status breakdown is recomputed at each level from that level's own provider records, with its unknown share. Also report: the cohort coverage rate (providers reporting over providers strengthened), the number of providers entering and leaving the cohort in the year, the number of providers that ceased operating in their window and their combined baseline reach, the number of providers whose baseline is reconstructed, the number of providers reported alongside under Block A, and the two level sums behind the net value, each labelled an upper estimate of unique farmers.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This value does not add to KPI-O27 or KPI-O26; the levels connect through the theory of change, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: a provider strengthened by two CIMMYT projects counts once, matched by provider identity, with its change reported by the project that documented its baseline. At farmer level, clients cannot be matched across providers' record systems, so the level sums are upper estimates of unique farmers and the net change has no known direction of error. Overlap with other indicators must be named, never summed: users of a platform CIMMYT hands to a strengthened provider move from KPI-O26 into this indicator's reach, with the baseline restated as Baseline required sets out, and users of a platform CIMMYT co-runs with a provider stay in KPI-O26 (see Eligibility); a farmer in a provider's reach may also appear in Vol. 1 · KPI-O18 (farmers trained) or Vol. 1 · KPI-OC16 (farmers adopting). Never add this indicator to any farmer-reach count to produce a total-farmers-reached figure.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: providers counted under KPI-O27, pooled or reported alongside, with a documented baseline: a provider stays in the cohort for three years after strengthening ends, then leaves, and providers leaving the cohort are named in the reporting note so a fall in the total is not misread as declining reach. A provider strengthened a second time inside its window restarts the three-year clock from the end of the later strengthening and keeps its original documented baseline, so a second package cannot reset the comparison to a level CIMMYT's own earlier work produced. A provider strengthened again after it has left the cohort re-enters with a new baseline, its reach in the 12 months before the new strengthening began, because growth after its window closed is growth this indicator does not read against CIMMYT's contribution. A provider documented as having ceased operating inside its window stays in the cohort with a reach of zero until the window closes. A farmer is in a provider's reach for a period when the provider's records show a service delivered to that farmer within it; a registration or account opened in an earlier period is not reach. The service event is recorded with the provider's baseline and held constant, and a year reported on a different event is treated as missing for that provider. For a provider on the Fallback survey route, reach is the client number the survey reports for the service event recorded with its baseline; the provider is reported as Aggregation rule Block A sets out and counts as reporting in the cohort coverage rate. Reach and baseline are measured for the same operating unit counted under KPI-O27.

Exclusion: providers more than three years past the end of strengthening, whose growth can no longer be read against CIMMYT's contribution; providers without a documented baseline (monitoring only, no change value); farmers reached directly by CIMMYT-run services (KPI-O26), including farmers on a platform CIMMYT co-runs with the provider; no client is excluded for farm size: smallholder status is recorded as an attribute per Annex B, not used to restrict the count.

Missing data: an operating provider that fails to report is dropped from both sides of the calculation for that year, and the cohort coverage rate (providers reporting / providers strengthened) is reported alongside the value; do not impute or carry forward a provider's last value.

Repeated observations: a farmer served several times by the same provider in the year counts once in that provider's reach; farmers served by two strengthened providers usually cannot be matched across record systems, so each level sum, reporting-year reach and baseline reach, is an upper estimate of unique farmers; the net change equals the change in unique farmers only where overlap is constant, and its error has no known direction.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only: a provider's reach also responds to its own investment, market growth, other funders and policy conditions; a reach increase does not by itself prove CIMMYT's strengthening caused it. Pair with the KPI-O27 record of what strengthening each provider received.

Provider-reported records are the measurement base: quality varies widely, and a provider reporting to the organization that supported it has an incentive to over-state clients; spot verification and fallback flagging limit but do not remove this error.

Overlap has no known direction in the net figure: clients cannot be de-duplicated across providers' record systems, so both level sums overstate unique farmers where service areas overlap, and the net change is exact only if that overlap is the same in both periods.

The net figure can hide cohort attrition: an operating provider that stops reporting drops out of the calculation, while one that ceases operating stays in with a reach of zero until its window closes. Read the value with the cohort coverage rate beside it.
A rise in reach does not mean the farmers reached adopted or benefited from what was delivered. Adoption and livelihood change are carried by Vol. 1 · KPI-OC16 and by the income indicators of Vol. 5.
subMetrics: None. Baseline reach and reporting-year reach per provider are calculation inputs, not separately reported metrics, and per-provider percent change is a presentation of the same data. Related sheets: KPI-O27 (providers strengthened, the output defining this cohort), KPI-O26 (farmers reached by CIMMYT's own digital services, the boundary sibling), KPI-OC16 (adoption, the next pathway step).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the digital advisory / extension systems lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: strengthened providers via the agreed partner reporting template, compiled by project field teams. Validation: project MEAL officer (baseline documented, records spot-checked, provider-type categories applied). Calculation: project M&E, computing per-provider change; cross-project pooling and de-duplication by the CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
