name: Percentage of CIMMYT research datasets compliant with FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) principles
resultsLevel: Outcome. The Core's results-level test asks whether the indicator reports a delivered result or a change, and reads it from the indicator statement itself for Institutional-branch indicators, because there is no external actor. The count of datasets produced or published following FAIR principles in a year reports the delivery and is the output; this indicator reports how widely FAIR practice has been made operational across the whole registered holding, which is the organization operating differently, and is therefore the outcome. CGIAR's formal test (a change in the behaviour of external actors outside the research team) is written for research results and does not map cleanly onto internal operations indicators such as this one, which is why the Core states the institutional reading rather than borrowing it.
indicatorScope: Institutional. This indicator measures a property of CIMMYT as an organization (the governance of its own research data holdings), not an outcome delivered to an external population. It is reported once, at CIMMYT-institutional level, from corporate knowledge-management systems, so this sheet carries no project-specific layer.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Excellence in Operations. The indicator sits under the Excellence in Operations objectives on effective systems and tools, data sharing for a collaborative culture (objective 2.2), and making relevant data accessible to partners and beneficiaries outside the organization (objective 3.1). As an Institutional indicator it does not map to mission objectives PO1 to PO5..
institutionalComponent: Excellence in Operations. The indicator sits under the Excellence in Operations objectives on effective systems and tools, data sharing for a collaborative culture (objective 2.2), and making relevant data accessible to partners and beneficiaries outside the organization (objective 3.1). As an Institutional indicator it does not map to mission objectives PO1 to PO5.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. Institutional data-governance measure; it enables mission reporting across all Impact Areas but has no single direct Impact Area correspondence.
sdgTarget: None. No SDG indicator measures organizational research-data governance.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR results reporting: CGIAR's Performance and Results Management System (PRMS) screens reported knowledge products against FAIR criteria using automated tools, and the CGIAR Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 commits to extending that automated FAIR screening within quality assurance.
definition: The share of CIMMYT research datasets that comply with the FAIR principles: Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable. Numerator: datasets meeting all FAIR criteria; denominator: all CIMMYT research datasets. Under FAIR (Wilkinson et al., 2016), a dataset is Findable when it carries a persistent identifier (such as a DOI) and rich metadata, Accessible when it can be retrieved through a standard open protocol (which includes managed-access datasets, since FAIR does not require data to be open), Interoperable when it uses shared formats and vocabularies that let machines and other researchers combine it with other data, and Reusable when its licence, provenance and documentation allow someone else to use it with confidence.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's research data holdings are governed to the standard that CIMMYT's own strategy and CGIAR-level reporting expect: data that partners, funders and future researchers can find, access and reuse. It serves the Excellence in Operations commitments to promote information and data sharing across the organization and to make relevant data accessible to partners and beneficiaries outside it (CIMMYT 2030 Strategy, Excellence in Operations objectives 2.2 and 3.1), and it gives institutional reporting and donors a single verifiable measure of research-data governance.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional scope; there is no project instance to adapt).
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organization, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Percentage of research datasets.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of CIMMYT research datasets meet all the FAIR criteria. It is the compliance share that KPI-O44's count is read against.
disaggregationRequired: None. The indicator is reported as a single institutional share (register: no required disaggregation).
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Research programme or unit; data repository; year of dataset publication; individual FAIR dimension (F, A, I, R) where the assessment instrument scores them separately. These are internal management breakdowns, not reporting requirements. The template's "optional (project-specific)" field does not apply to an Institutional indicator; these are optional institutional cuts the data-governance function may add.
unitOfObservation: Result object: one CIMMYT research dataset, the thing each record describes. A dataset CIMMYT produces is a delivered knowledge product, which is what the result-object value covers; "secondary dataset" is the value for a dataset CIMMYT reads rather than produces. KPI-O05 and KPI-O44 name the same unit the same way.
calculationSummary:
Numerator: datasets meeting every indicator in the pass set: the 20 essential indicators of the RDA FAIR Data Maturity Model plus RDA-I1-01M, RDA-I1-01D, RDA-I2-01M and RDA-R1.2-01M, which the toolbox raises to essential because the model classes none of its Interoperable indicators as essential. The profile is this toolbox's convention and is the same test KPI-O44 applies. Where CGIAR's automated screening has already assessed a dataset, its result is reused only for the indicators in the pass set that the screening tests, as recorded with the assessment; every other indicator in the pass set is assessed by curator review.

Denominator: all CIMMYT research datasets registered in the institutional registry. The datasets registered in the reporting year are reported as a subtotal on the same basis.

Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (administrative and registry data): CIMMYT's institutional research-data repository and data-management registry records, with FAIR compliance assessed by automated screening of the metadata records plus curator review of ambiguous cases and of every pass-set indicator the screening does not test. Comparator DS4 (secondary and international databases): CGIAR-level reporting records (PRMS FAIR screening results for CIMMYT-reported data assets), used to estimate registry coverage (Block C, Block E): a CIMMYT dataset these records list and the registry does not enters neither term; never pooled, and never reported as a KPI-OC41 value. Reusing CGIAR's screening result for a dataset the registry lists, as Calculation method sets out, is part of the Recommended route. Not applicable: DS1 (censuses and surveys), DS3 (geospatial and Earth observation), DS5 (citizen-generated data). FAIR compliance is a property of dataset records and metadata; it cannot be measured by surveying people, by satellite, or by crowdsourcing.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative and secondary sources only (no DS1 or DS5 source listed).
collectionFrequency: Annual assessment of the registry.
referencePeriod: Status of the registered data holdings on 31 December of the reporting year. An earlier year's result stands for a dataset whose record has not changed, except that the automated checks are re-run on the whole registered stock each year, since identifiers and licence links can stop resolving.
baselineRequired: Yes. The first full annual assessment of the registry establishes the baseline share. If earlier years cannot be reconstructed from repository records, no retrospective baseline is built: the first assessed year is the baseline and change is claimed only from that year forward.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable, since datasets generated by projects enter the central registry and are assessed there, and projects do not report their own values. One domain only: the datasets held in CIMMYT's institutional research-data registry, assessed under one instrument and one threshold. What the domain holds constant is the assessment basis. A value built partly from CGIAR's automated screening and partly from curator review stays inside the domain and the split is reported; a year assessed under a revised instrument or threshold is a different domain and is not compared with an earlier year without restatement.

B: Combination method. A ratio of sums, formed once: datasets meeting every indicator in the pass set over all registered research datasets, Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100. Never an average of per-repository or per-programme percentages.

C: Levels and operations. The share is computed once, at institutional level, over the cumulative stock of registered datasets at the reporting date, and is recomputed from its own numerator and denominator wherever a narrower view is wanted, never read off or averaged from the institutional figure: a mean of programme shares weights a programme holding nine datasets equally with one holding nine hundred. There is no level beneath the institution, because a dataset enters CIMMYT's holdings rather than belonging to the project or programme that produced it. The denominator is a portfolio of datasets rather than a population measured in the field, so the measurement levels do not apply here and every breakdown is a reporting view. The datasets registered in the reporting year are computed as a subtotal on the same basis, so improvement in current practice stays visible against a large legacy stock. Also report: the denominator itself, the share of holdings assessed, the split between automated screening and curator review, and the registry coverage, with the number of CIMMYT datasets CGIAR records list and the registry does not, since a share taken over an incomplete registry overstates compliance.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. KPI-O44 (the year's count of datasets produced or published following FAIR principles) is this indicator's output companion and KPI-O05 (the share of research datasets disaggregated by sex) is a related data-governance measure; all three read the same registry and connect through the theory of change, never through arithmetic. In particular, do not add O44's annual count into this share or treat the two as interchangeable: O44 counts the year's flow, this indicator states the FAIR share of the whole stock. Shares assessed under different instruments or thresholds are never pooled across years.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: one dataset, one record. De-duplicate by persistent identifier before the share is formed, so a dataset held in two repositories, re-deposited, or versioned counts once; where a dataset has several versions the latest is assessed and the dataset counted once. The named overlap risk in the register is with KPI-O44: the same dataset records appear in both indicators by design, so the two are never summed into a combined figure. Coverage is the share of CIMMYT's actual holdings the registry contains, reported with the value, because datasets that were never registered are invisible to both terms.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion and exclusion: includes research datasets (primary or processed data with a metadata record) registered in the institutional research-data registry, whether generated by CIMMYT staff or by partners under a CIMMYT project agreement, and whether openly available or under managed access, since FAIR does not require openness. The population is the cumulative stock of holdings, not only datasets produced in the reporting period. Excludes non-dataset knowledge products (publications, briefs, software releases) and operational corporate data.
limitations: The value depends on the assessment instrument and threshold. Automated FAIR screening and manual curator review can rate the same dataset differently, and partial compliance (for example findable and accessible but not interoperable) counts as non-compliant under the all-criteria rule. Keep the instrument and threshold constant across years, and re-baseline if they change.

The share is only as complete as the registry. Datasets that were never registered are invisible to both numerator and denominator, and since unregistered data is usually the least governed, an incomplete registry tends to overstate compliance. Report registry coverage alongside the value.

FAIR is not the same as open. A dataset under managed access can be fully FAIR, so this indicator says nothing about how much CIMMYT data is openly downloadable, and it should not be read as an open-data measure.

A rising share can come from curating metadata of existing holdings rather than from changed practice in new research; read it together with KPI-O44 to distinguish stock improvement from new-data practice.

Compliance measures data stewardship, not scientific quality or actual reuse. A movement in the value means the governance of holdings changed; it does not mean the data is better science or that anyone reused it.
subMetrics: None. The four FAIR dimensions (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) are assessment criteria applied jointly within the single compliance test, not separately reported sub-metrics. Where the assessment instrument produces per-dimension scores, they may be used as optional management disaggregations (Section 3), and the count of newly FAIR datasets is a separate indicator with its own sheet (KPI-O44).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner of this reference sheet).
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: Knowledge Management & IT (research-data repository and registry records). Validation: Knowledge Management & IT data curators (FAIR assessment review). Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, per the calculation method above. Approval: head of Knowledge Management & IT, as the corporate data owner for research-data records. Reporting: CIMMYT MEAL unit into institutional reporting.

name: Percentage of field projects with documented environmental and social safeguards, tracked toward full institutionalisation
resultsLevel: Outcome. The Core's results-level test asks whether the indicator reports a delivered result or a change, and reads it from the indicator statement itself for Institutional-branch indicators, because there is no external actor. What this indicator reports is how widely documented safeguards have been adopted across the field portfolio, which is the organization operating differently and is therefore an outcome; the frameworks themselves are the delivered result, counted at output level as KPI-O47. CGIAR's boundary test (products under the research team's control versus behaviour change in external actors) is written for research results and fits an internal compliance indicator poorly, which is why the Core states the institutional reading rather than borrowing that test.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Excellence in Operations.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. What this indicator measures is the coverage of CIMMYT's own safeguard documentation, a governance practice rather than a result delivered to a population, and the area follows the measured object rather than the branch the indicator sits on. Nor is the practice specific to a single area: the documentation set spans environmental protection, social protection and gender, so it serves several equally and none in particular, and the value reports compliance coverage rather than environmental or social results.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator measures an organization's safeguard documentation coverage; the SDG framework tracks country-level outcomes, not institutional compliance shares.
otherFrameworks: IFC Performance Standards on Environmental and Social Sustainability (2012): the benchmark for what adequate safeguard documentation contains. The World Bank Environmental and Social Framework, in effect since October 2018 (World Bank, 2016): the safeguard regime CIMMYT projects meet when World Bank-financed. GRI 2: General Disclosures 2021, disclosures 2-23 (policy commitments) and 2-24 (embedding policy commitments), under which safeguards coverage supports environmental, social and governance disclosure. These frameworks define what safeguard documentation contains and how it is disclosed; none prescribes this percentage indicator, which is CIMMYT-defined.
definition: Measures the share of CIMMYT's safeguard-triggering field projects that hold verified documentation of environmental and social safeguards in the reporting year. Environmental and social safeguards are the documented measures a project puts in place to prevent or manage unintended harm to communities and ecosystems, such as an environmental impact assessment, a waste management plan, informed consent protocols and a gender equality plan, each project holding the set its documentation checklist requires, prepared in accordance with the IFC Performance Standards or equivalent donor frameworks. The indicator tracks adoption of safeguards practice across the field portfolio toward full institutionalisation: documented safeguards as standard practice on every project that needs them.
rationale: Answers whether the compliance and safeguards frameworks CIMMYT has established (measured separately as Vol. 11 · KPI-O47) are applied across the field portfolio, rather than existing on paper. Safeguards protect communities and ecosystems from unintended impacts of field work, and documented safeguards are a standing condition of the public funders CIMMYT works with: the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework is the regime CIMMYT projects meet when World Bank-financed, and equivalent frameworks apply elsewhere. The indicator evidences the 2030 Strategy's Excellence in Operations commitment to "Ensure an operating environment within applicable regulatory, compliance and risk management frameworks", and feeds institutional, donor, and environmental, social and governance reporting.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator). Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate compliance records; projects contribute their safeguard documentation to the institutional register but do not report this indicator themselves.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organization, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems. Individual projects appear in its denominator as records, not as reporting instances.
unit: Percentage of safeguard-triggering field projects
directionOfChange: Increase, toward full institutionalisation. A rising value means a larger share of safeguard-triggering field projects hold complete, verified safeguard documentation.
disaggregationRequired: None. The register lists partner/institution type, but a field project is carried by several partners and has no single partner type to classify it by, so the cut is not required here, a deliberate divergence from that row. The optional cuts below carry the breakdowns a compliance share is managed by.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case. Project type is available as an optional institutional cut below.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Project type; region or country; donor; safeguard type (environmental, social, gender, data). The template's "optional (project-specific)" field does not apply to an Institutional indicator; these are optional institutional cuts the owning function may add. The safeguard-type cut is the most useful for managing the gap: it shows which documentation element is most often missing.
unitOfObservation: Result object: one CIMMYT field project, the project record in the safeguards register that each observation describes. A project is an institutional object the work acts on rather than a person, a place, a post or a body, which is what the result-object value covers.
calculationSummary: Numerator: active field projects whose required safeguard documentation is complete and verified in the institutional register during the reporting year. Denominator: all active field projects screened as safeguard-triggering in the reporting year. Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): the institutional safeguards register within CIMMYT's project management system, holding each project's screening result, the safeguard documents the project's checklist requires, and verification status. Fallback DS2 (lower-resolution instance of the same code): direct documentary review of project files where no central register covers the full portfolio for the year; a value built this way is flagged as fallback-sourced, because screening coverage and verification evidence are weaker. Not applicable DS1: documentation status is an administrative fact read from records, not data collected from respondents. Not applicable DS3: satellite or GIS data cannot show whether a project holds safeguard documents. Not applicable DS4: CIMMYT's internal compliance records are not held by third parties. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced data cannot verify internal documentation.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source. The operative tools are the safeguards screening checklist by project type (which fixes the denominator) and the documentation checklist (which fixes what complete means for the numerator and is applied by legal, the holder of the validation role).
collectionFrequency: Continuous administrative logging: documentary review at project start and during implementation as documents are filed and verified, consolidated by an annual portfolio audit.
referencePeriod: The reporting year; the value is the portfolio's verified documentation status at the annual portfolio review.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual institutional coverage share tracked toward 100 percent; the first year with a complete portfolio screening and audit serves as the reference year, and change is read from the annual series.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable in the template's sense; the indicator is compiled once from corporate records, so there are no project-level indicator instances to pool. Any portion of the portfolio assessed through fallback file review rather than the central register is noted alongside the figure, not blended silently.

B: Combination method. Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level: one numerator and one denominator counted across the whole field portfolio, then the ratio is formed. Never average percentages computed for regions, programmes, or donors; disaggregated views are computed from their own counts.

C: Levels and operations. The share is computed once, at institutional level, over the whole field portfolio, and is recomputed from its own numerator and denominator wherever a narrower view is wanted, never averaged from the region, programme or donor shares beneath it: a mean of regional percentages weights a region running four projects equally with one running forty. There is no level beneath the institution here, because a project does not hold a share of a portfolio coverage figure; a project is one record in the denominator, not a reporting level. The denominator is a portfolio of projects rather than a population measured in the field, so the measurement levels do not apply and every breakdown is a reporting view. A disaggregated external view whose denominator is fewer than ten projects is reported inside a wider grouping rather than on its own, because a compliance rate over a very small denominator identifies the non-compliant project from the rate alone. Also report: the denominator itself, the number of field projects screened against the number active, the number screened as non-triggering, the safeguard-type breakdown showing which documentation element is most often missing, and the portion of the portfolio assessed by fallback file review rather than read from the central register.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no (the default). The upstream output KPI-O47 and this coverage outcome connect as framework built then practice adopted, never arithmetically.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: each project counts once, matched on its unique project identifier, including projects spanning several countries or partners. One named overlap: informed consent protocols can be an element of the documentation set here, while KPI-OC46 measures documented informed consent at research-activity level; the two observe different units (project versus research activity) and must never be summed, and the overlap is named wherever both are reported together.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion and exclusion: includes every active project with field-level implementation activities that the safeguards screening classifies as triggering; excludes desk-based projects and field projects screened as non-triggering. Completeness is assessed against the documentation checklist for the project's type and verified by legal, which holds the validation role, not self-declared.

Missing data: a field project with no screening record counts in the denominator and not in the numerator (treated as triggering and undocumented), so the value can never be improved by leaving projects unscreened.

Repeated observations: each project counts once per reporting year regardless of how many documents it holds; a multi-year project is re-verified and counted in every year it remains active, at its current status.
limitations: Documentation is not implementation: the indicator verifies that safeguard documents exist and passed review, not that the measures they describe are applied or effective in the field. Field-level implementation quality needs monitoring evidence this indicator does not carry.

The denominator is only as good as the screening: weak or inconsistent triggering screens distort the value. The conservative rule (an unscreened field project counts as triggering and undocumented) protects against inflation but makes the value sensitive to screening backlog.

Comparability over time depends on a stable documentation standard: tightening or relaxing the checklist, or changing what complete means, shifts the value without any change in actual practice; note any checklist revision alongside the reported series.

A rising value means documentation coverage improved across the portfolio; it does not mean environmental or social risks were avoided, communities were protected, or donor safeguard audits will be passed. Read it with Vol. 11 · KPI-O47, which reports whether the framework exists.
subMetrics: None. Coverage rates by safeguard type (environmental, social, gender, data) are disaggregations of the same measure, not separately calculated metrics. Related indicators with their own sheets: KPI-O47 (compliance and safeguards frameworks established and operationalised, the output feeding this outcome) and KPI-OC46 (percentage of research activities with informed consent, the neighbouring research-ethics outcome at activity level).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project teams, filing safeguard documents in the project management system as they are prepared. Validation: legal, the owner of the environmental and social safeguards framework. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (annual numerator, denominator, and ratio per the Calculation method). Approval: the head of legal. Reporting: legal to the CIMMYT MEAL unit. The roles are assigned by function, which is what makes them operable before the post titles are settled.
sourceRef: Volume 2 · Capacity, data & institutions — Reference sheet KPI-OC42

name: Percentage of research activities with documented informed consent
resultsLevel: Outcome. The Core's results-level test asks whether the indicator reports a delivered result or a change, and reads it from the indicator statement itself for Institutional-branch indicators, because there is no external actor. What this indicator reports is how widely documented informed consent has been made operational across CIMMYT's research activities, which is the organization operating differently and is therefore an outcome; the research-ethics framework itself is the output, reported by Vol. 11 · KPI-O47. CGIAR's boundary test (control by the research team versus behaviour change in external actors) is written for research results and fits an internal compliance indicator poorly, which is why the Core states the institutional reading rather than borrowing that test.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Excellence in Operations.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. What this indicator measures is the completeness of CIMMYT's own consent documentation, a research-ethics practice rather than a result delivered to a population, and the area follows the measured object rather than the branch the indicator sits on. Nor is the practice specific to a single area: documented consent protects every participant in every area CIMMYT researches and is the precondition for none of them in particular.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator measures research-ethics or consent documentation.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Research Ethics Code (2020), whose section on research involving human subjects makes prior informed consent mandatory for all CGIAR research with people as subjects; the Code anchors its human-subjects provisions in the Belmont Report's principles of respect for persons, beneficence and justice. The Code sets the requirement this indicator monitors; no donor reporting framework carries a percentage indicator of this construct.
definition: Measures the share of CIMMYT research activities involving human participants for which informed consent is documented. Informed consent means that, before data collection or an intervention, participants were informed about the nature, purpose, methods and intended uses of the research, what their participation entails, and any benefits, harms or risks, and gave voluntary permission, in writing or as recorded verbal consent, which they may withdraw at any time; this is the standard set by the CGIAR Research Ethics Code. Documented means the consent record (signed form or recorded verbal consent), or the ethics clearance that waives written documentation, is held in the activity's ethics file. The indicator is a research-ethics compliance measure.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's research involving people meets its own ethical obligation, and CGIAR's, to obtain and document voluntary informed consent: the operational evidence behind the 2030 Strategy's Excellence in Operations objective to "Ensure an operating environment within applicable regulatory, compliance and risk management frameworks". Tracked for institutional assurance, ethics-committee oversight, and donor and partner confidence that research with farmers, households and communities respects participants' rights.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator). Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level from the institution's research-ethics records; there is no project instance to adapt it to.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organization, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems. Research activities appear in its denominator as records, not as reporting instances.
unit: Percentage of research activities
directionOfChange: Reference value: 100 percent. Informed consent is mandatory for all research involving human participants, so the reference is the requirement itself and not a target set here. Any value below 100 identifies protocols with no consent record on file for at least one participant, read as a compliance gap to investigate and close rather than as a performance level to improve incrementally.
disaggregationRequired: None. The register records no required disaggregation for this indicator.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Research programme or organizational unit; country or region; activity type (for example survey, interview, focus group discussion, participatory trial). These cuts serve internal follow-up, locating where documentation gaps sit. The template's "optional (project-specific)" field does not apply to an Institutional indicator; these are optional institutional cuts the owning function may add.
unitOfObservation: Result object: one research activity, counted as its ethics-approved protocol, the ethics-registered record each observation describes. An activity is an institutional object the work acts on rather than a person, a place, a post or a body, which is what the result-object value covers. The individuals who consent are the subjects of the activity, not the unit counted.
calculationSummary: Numerator: research activities involving human participants with complete informed-consent documentation on file for the reporting year's data collection. Denominator: all research activities involving human participants that collected data or ran an intervention during the reporting year. The counting unit is the ethics-approved protocol, which is also the identifier the de-duplication rule uses: a component activity carried out under an approved protocol is part of that protocol's record and is not counted separately, and a protocol is one record in the denominator whatever the number of rounds of collection it runs in the year. Complete means a consent record for every participant from whom data was collected under the protocol that year: the protocol enters the numerator only if no participant record lacks one, or, where the clearance waives written documentation, the clearance is on file (see Eligibility). The test is deliberately strict, because a single participant without a documented consent is the compliance failure the Code defines, and any tolerance below that would report compliance with a threshold the Code does not set. Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): the research-ethics function's records, meaning ethics-review approvals and the activity-level consent files, cross-referenced against the institutional research project or activity registry to construct the denominator of activities involving human participants. Not applicable DS1 (Censuses & surveys): a self-assessment cannot show that a consent record is on file, which is what the numerator counts. Not applicable DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation): consent documentation is not observable remotely. Not applicable DS4 (Secondary & international databases): CIMMYT's internal ethics files are not held by third parties. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): whether a consent record is on file is an internal administrative fact; it cannot be crowdsourced.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source: the Recommended DS2 route compiles existing ethics records and needs no instrument.
collectionFrequency: Continuous filing of consent records as activities run, verified through an annual compliance review of the ethics files against the activity registry.
referencePeriod: The CIMMYT reporting year: each value describes the activities that collected data from human participants during that year.
baselineRequired: No. This is a compliance-level indicator interpreted against the fixed 100 percent expectation, not against a starting value. The first year with a complete activity registry serves as the reference year for any trend reading.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable; this Institutional indicator is drawn once from corporate records, so there are no project instances to pool.

B: Combination method. Computed once at CIMMYT-institutional level from the central ethics records: one denominator, one numerator, never an average of unit-level percentages.

C: Levels and operations. The share is computed once, at institutional level, over every in-scope research activity in the reporting year, and is recomputed from its own numerator and denominator wherever a narrower view is wanted, never averaged from the programme, country or activity-type shares beneath it: a mean of programme percentages weights a programme running three activities equally with one running three hundred. There is no level beneath the institution here, because an activity does not hold a share of an institutional compliance figure; an activity is one record in the denominator, not a reporting level. The denominator is a portfolio of activity records rather than a population measured in the field, so the measurement levels do not apply and every breakdown is a reporting view. Because the expected value is 100 percent, any view is reported with its shortfall as a case list rather than as a rate alone. The case list names activities whose participants' consent is undocumented, so it is held by the research-ethics function and the CIMMYT MEAL unit and is not published: external reporting carries the rate and the shortfall count, never the named cases. A disaggregated external view whose denominator is fewer than ten activities is reported inside a wider grouping rather than on its own, because a rate over a very small denominator identifies the activity from the rate alone. Also report: the denominator itself, the number of in-scope protocols reconciled against the full activity portfolio, the number of protocols cleared with a waiver of written documentation and the number outside the denominator under a waiver of the consent process.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no (the default). The register rolls this outcome up to the Excellence in Operations component directly; it sits alongside the safeguards-coverage outcome (percentage of field projects with documented safeguards, KPI-OC42) in the same indicator group as narrative companions, and the two are never combined arithmetically because they count different units (research activities versus field projects).

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: an activity that serves several projects or programmes counts once, matched on its unique ethics-protocol identifier before the institutional figure is formed; if activities cannot be uniquely identified across programmes, the reported percentage is labelled approximate and the registry gap is raised with the owning function. Overlap with other register indicators: none arithmetic; the double-counting risk is internal (the same activity registered twice), handled by the protocol-identifier rule.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion and exclusion: includes every activity with people as subjects, whether surveys, interviews, focus group discussions, participant observation, multi-stakeholder dialogues, or participatory action and learning (the scope of the CGIAR Research Ethics Code's human-subjects section); excludes activities with no human participants (laboratory and breeding work without farmer participation, remote-sensing analysis, secondary-data analysis). Recorded verbal consent counts as documented, since the Code accepts written or verbal consent; undocumented verbal consent does not. A protocol whose IREC clearance waives written documentation of consent counts as documented when the clearance stating the waiver is on file, with the approved alternative record where the clearance sets one. A protocol whose IREC clearance waives or alters the consent process itself is outside the denominator and is reported as a count beside the value.
limitations: Measures documentation, not consent quality: a signed form does not prove participants genuinely understood the research or felt free to refuse, and strong verbal-consent practice that is poorly filed reads as non-compliance. The indicator is evidence of an operating documentation system, not of ethical practice in itself.

The value is only as good as the denominator: it depends on a complete registry of activities involving human participants. Activities that never entered ethics review are invisible to both numerator and denominator, so an incomplete registry inflates the percentage; the annual review must reconcile the ethics registry against the full activity portfolio.

Ceiling behaviour limits trend reading: with an expected value of 100 percent, year-on-year movements near the ceiling carry little information. Read any shortfall as a case list to investigate (which activities, where, why) rather than as a performance trend; that list stays with the research-ethics function and the CIMMYT MEAL unit, and external reporting carries the rate and the shortfall count only.

Comparability over time depends on the counting unit staying the ethics-approved protocol: counting projects or component activities instead changes both numerator and denominator and breaks the series.
subMetrics: None. The indicator is a single share. The related safeguards-coverage measure (percentage of field projects with documented safeguards) is a separate register indicator, KPI-OC42, with its own reference sheet, not a sub-metric of this one.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
Institutional framework: CGIAR System Organization (2020), CGIAR research ethics code, the informed-consent provisions for research involving human participants, reached through the CGIAR Ethics and Business Conduct portal.

CIMMYT Institutional Research Ethics Committee procedures and guidelines, Version 2.0, October 2018, CIMMYT (the human-subjects clearance procedure; the waiver of written documentation of consent and the waiver or alteration of the consent process, printed pp. 14 to 15); internal document, no public link.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: research or activity teams, filing consent records at the point of data collection. Validation: the CIMMYT Institutional Research Ethics Committee (IREC), verifying files against the activity registry in the annual review. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, per the Calculation method above. Approval: the IREC Chair. Reporting: IREC to the CIMMYT MEAL unit. The roles are assigned by function, which is what makes them operable before the post titles are settled.
sourceRef: Volume 2 · Capacity, data & institutions — Reference sheet KPI-OC46

name: Number of biofortified or nutrient-dense crop varieties disseminated by CIMMYT in intervention areas
resultsLevel: Output. What is counted is a delivered result, a variety placed in circulation by CIMMYT and its contracted delivery partners, not a change in what an external actor does. Farmers choosing to grow the variety is the behaviour change and sits at outcome level (KPI-OC10).
primaryObjective: PO2 Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved).
cgiarImpactArea: Nutrition, Health & Food Security, following what the indicator measures, per the pathway-wide rule.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator measures the dissemination of crop varieties. The nutrition results this indicator feeds are measured downstream by SDG indicator 2.2.3 (prevalence of anaemia in women aged 15 to 49 years, by pregnancy status), which is an impact-level population measure and not a correspondence for this count.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR technical reporting: a disseminated variety is reported under the Innovation Development output category (minimum fields: innovation type, readiness level, contact point), while the subsequent use of that variety is reported separately under the Innovation Use outcome category. Another CGIAR centre runs a germplasm-delivery count carrying "biofortified" as a trait attribute, which supports portability of the disaggregation across centres.
definition: Counts the biofortified or nutrient-dense crop varieties CIMMYT and its delivery partners actively distribute in intervention areas in the reporting year, counted as variety-country dissemination events, not as the quantity of seed moved and not as the number of farmers reached. Dissemination means distribution that puts seed into farmers' hands, or into the hands of the partners who supply them; it is a step beyond release, which only makes a variety available (KPI-O07). "Biofortified or nutrient-dense" covers micronutrient biofortification (provitamin A, zinc, iron) and protein quality, including quality protein maize, recorded with the target nutrient or trait named so the two are never silently pooled.
rationale: Answers how many nutrition-improving varieties CIMMYT moved into farmers' hands, or into the hands of the partners who supply them, in the year, as distinct from how many exist on paper. It is the delivery step between an approved variety and its use in the field, so it tells management and donors whether the biofortification pipeline is converting approvals into distribution, and it sets the varietal base from which farmer cultivation (KPI-OC10) and, further downstream, per-capita availability of biofortified grain (KPI-OC08) are read.
projectSpecificApplication: State the crops and nutrient traits covered, the countries and districts of distribution, the delivery partners involved, and the records evidencing that each variety moved in the reporting year. Do not change the counting unit, the dissemination definition or the nutrient-trait rule; if applying the indicator as defined is not feasible here, raise it with the MEAL focal point.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count serves: for example a contracted dissemination target for a nutrient trait and country, a review of which delivery channels are moving nutrient-dense varieties, or a partner-facing report on seed delivery.
projectTypesNotApplicable: genes and controlled-environment results rather than seed moving to farmers
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose outputs are traits, genes and controlled-environment results rather than seed moving to farmers; and digital agriculture and AI, which delivers advisory content and platforms and distributes no germplasm.
unit: Number of variety-country dissemination events in the reporting year: one count per distinct variety per country of distribution, with the number of distinct varieties behind that figure reported alongside it. The register's Definition cell still carries the earlier distinct-variety unit and a micronutrient-only trait scope; this sheet's unit and scope govern the measurement. Distribution is a national event, and the sibling indicators KPI-O07, KPI-O12 and KPI-O16 all count variety-country, so this indicator is read against them on the same unit. A variety distributed through several channels inside one country counts once there, with the channels recorded as a disaggregation.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more biofortified or nutrient-dense varieties were disseminated in intervention areas.
disaggregationRequired: Required: crop (maize, wheat, other); trait class, meaning the target nutrient or quality trait the variety was bred to enhance (provitamin A, zinc, iron, protein quality, other documented nutritional quality trait). A variety carrying two nutrient traits is assigned to the trait that justified its nutritional classification and listed under the second in a secondary field, so trait subtotals are never summed to the total.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator. Variety is not a cut here: each dissemination event is already one variety in one country, and the distinct-variety figure is reported beside the headline.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: District of distribution (country is part of the counting unit); delivery channel (national research system, private seed company, agrodealer, extension service, project demonstration); genetic unit (hybrid, open-pollinated variety); whether the variety was disseminated for the first time this year or is a continuing variety.
unitOfObservation: The variety-country dissemination event (one variety in one country of distribution), recorded once per country per reporting year. This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of variety-country dissemination events meeting all inclusion rules in the reporting year, with the count of distinct varieties behind it reported alongside. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: administrative and registry data, namely seed dispatch and distribution records and partner or agrodealer distribution reports, matched to CIMMYT breeding programme records (pedigree and breeding line identifiers, released name, nutrient characterisation) that establish the trait. Comparator DS4: national seed system or certified-seed production records listing varieties in circulation, used to place the count against the varieties in national circulation; never pooled, and never reported as a KPI-O06 value. Not applicable DS1: a survey of partners or farmers does not produce the dated dispatch or handover record Eligibility requires; a partner report carrying that detail is DS2 whatever form it arrives in. Not applicable DS3: satellite and geospatial data cannot identify a variety or its nutrient content. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or mobile data cannot evidence the nutrient trait or the distribution channel.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Name the dispatch or distribution records each variety was evidenced from, and how the nutrient trait was documented.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable: the count is read from dispatch and distribution records (DS2).
collectionFrequency: Continuous recording of distribution events by project and partner staff; compiled, verified against characterisation records and de-duplicated annually.
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the distribution took place.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual count of distribution events, so each reporting year starts from zero and the first year reported is the reference point for trend context. Any trend claim must state that the inclusion rules, the nutrient-trait rule and the once-per-variety-per-country-per-year counting unit were held constant across the years compared.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool events across projects after the de-duplication in Block B.

B: Combination method. Sum variety-country dissemination events across crops, countries and projects after de-duplication on the identifier of the released entry plus country of distribution, so one variety distributed in one country under two names or two licensees' brands is one event. The identifier is the cross identifier for a hybrid, or the line or population identifier for an open-pollinated variety, inbred line or population: two distinct hybrids sharing one parent line are two varieties, never collapsed to one on the shared parent's identifier. The distinct-variety figure reported alongside is de-duplicated on the identifier alone, so it is never the sum of the country counts.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying variety-country dissemination events for the reporting year, with the distinct-variety figure alongside it. At institutional level, the de-duplicated sum of those counts, computed from the distribution records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one variety-country is often reported by more than one project. Also report: the boundary with the other two stages, since a variety crossing one mid-year appears in two of the three stage counts for that year and the three are never summed, the number of contributing projects, and the number of varieties excluded under Eligibility and why.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count is never added to KPI-O09 (varieties and lines developed and made available), KPI-O07 (varieties released), KPI-OC10 (share of target farmers cultivating them) or KPI-O16 (improved varieties entering seed multiplication, Vol. 4), which does not count the seed handover that counts here. The same variety legitimately appears in each of those indicators in different years, so the overlap is real and must be named rather than summed; the levels connect through the theory of change, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: the same variety is routinely distributed by two projects or through several partners, so de-duplicate on the identifier of the released entry plus country of distribution before summing; where identifiers cannot be matched, label the pooled number an upper estimate.

The three-stage boundary, stated identically on KPI-O09, KPI-O07 and KPI-O06. A nutrient-dense variety passes through three counted stages, each with one qualifying event and its own evidence: developed and made available (KPI-O09), on a dated distribution, transfer or catalogue record putting the material at a partner's disposal; released (KPI-O07), on an official registration or approval dated inside the year; and disseminated (KPI-O06), on a dated distribution event placing seed with farmers or with the partners who supply them. The events are ordered and mutually exclusive, so no variety sits in two stages on one event: material not yet registered cannot be counted as released, and seed moved before registration is availability rather than dissemination. Each variety counts once per country per stage in a reporting year, and never twice within a stage however many partners or channels are involved. Availability and release each happen once in a country, so the count falls in the year the variety reaches that stage there; dissemination recurs, so a variety distributed in the same country in consecutive years counts in each of those years, with the number disseminated for the first time reported alongside. The three counts are never summed. One variety normally reaches all three stages, usually in different years and sometimes in the same one, so a variety registered in March and distributed in November is one variety counted once under KPI-O07 and once under KPI-O06, not two.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: a nutrient claim meeting the evidence standard in KPI-O07's Eligibility criteria and missing data; the variety is itself a CIMMYT line or population, or CIMMYT germplasm appears in its pedigree as a parent or grandparent, whether or not CIMMYT is named on the national release dossier, the same maximum ancestry depth KPI-O12, KPI-OC12 and KPI-OC14 apply, two generations, a generation being one cross or one line extraction, so for a hybrid the parents are the components of the final cross, and where a component is itself a hybrid its own parents are the grandparents; legally distributable in the country concerned; and, as the evidence of active distribution, at least one dated seed dispatch or handover record naming the receiving party, placing its seed with farmers, or with a partner supplying farmers, inside a CIMMYT intervention area during the reporting year. A demonstration plot alone does not qualify, since a demonstration shows a variety rather than distributing it, and a partner report qualifies only where it carries the dispatch detail; no minimum seed quantity is set.

Exclusion: varieties released but not distributed in the year (KPI-O07 in their release year); breeding lines and experimental materials shared with research partners (KPI-O09); germplasm shipped for research use only; varieties with no documented nutrient enhancement; varieties CIMMYT distributes but had no hand in breeding (neither itself a CIMMYT line or population nor carrying CIMMYT germplasm in its pedigree as parent or grandparent), whose distribution is real work reported separately, not here.

Missing data: a variety with distribution evidence but no nutrient characterisation on record is held out and reported separately, never assumed to qualify, and a distribution whose date cannot be established is held out rather than assigned to the current year.

Repeated observations: one count per distinct variety per country per reporting year, whatever the number of times and through whatever the number of channels it was distributed there; distribution in a further country is a new variety-country event. A variety distributed in consecutive years counts in each of them, so annual figures are not additive; report the number disseminated for the first time alongside the total.
limitations: Counts variety-country dissemination events, not reach. A variety distributed to fifty farmers and one distributed to fifty thousand count the same in a given country. A rise means more nutrition-improving varieties were put into circulation, not that more people obtained or ate them; read it with the cultivation and availability indicators in this pathway.

Annual figures are not additive. The same variety counts again in every year it is distributed, so summing years overstates the portfolio. Compare years, and use the first-time-disseminated figure when the question is how much the varietal set grew.

Nutrient content is classified, not measured in farmers' grain. The trait comes from breeding characterisation, while the level harvested and eaten varies with soil, agronomy, storage, milling and cooking. The count is therefore no evidence of nutrient intake.
Supports a contribution claim only. Distribution runs through national partners, seed companies and extension services, and more than one institution can legitimately report the same variety moving.

The number reflects record completeness as much as activity. Informal farmer-to-farmer seed exchange is invisible to distribution records, and an increase may partly show better reporting by partners rather than more dissemination.
subMetrics: None. Crop and trait class are disaggregations of the variety-country event count, and the distinct-variety and first-time-disseminated figures are the same count under a different de-duplication or inclusion rule. Related indicators hold their own sheets: KPI-O07, KPI-O09, KPI-OC10 and KPI-OC08 (change in per-capita biofortified grain available for consumption).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the biofortification and nutritional quality breeding lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project seed systems and delivery officers, with partner seed producers and extension staff recording distribution events. Validation: project MEAL officer with the breeding data manager, confirming the nutrient characterisation, the distribution evidence and the variety identity. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (per Calculation method above). Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit, and onward to CGIAR technical reporting as an innovation entry.
sourceRef: Volume 3 · Nutrition & food security — Reference sheet KPI-O06

name: Number of biofortified or nutrient-dense varieties containing CIMMYT-derived germplasm officially released in CIMMYT intervention countries
resultsLevel: Output. The variety is a delivered result of the breeding process, and CGIAR's quality assurance guidance names new crop varieties among its output examples. Farmers' cultivation of a released biofortified variety is a behaviour change of external actors and sits at outcome level (KPI-OC10). CIMMYT's own MEAL Framework definition governs the register, so the level the register records stands; CGIAR's control test would read this differently, since the approval decision is taken by an external national or regional authority, and the divergence is handled once in the crosswalk annex.
primaryObjective: PO2 stands as primary: PO2 Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries. The 2030 Strategy does not use the words biofortification, micronutrient or nutrient-dense; that absence is stated here plainly rather than resolved by choosing a different objective. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved).
cgiarImpactArea: Nutrition, Health & Food Security, following what the indicator measures, per the pathway-wide rule.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator counts the release of crop varieties. The nearest correspondence is SDG target 2.2 (end all forms of malnutrition), whose indicators measure nutrition status in the population, for example indicator 2.2.3 (prevalence of anaemia in women aged 15 to 49 years). That is the eventual health result micronutrient breeding serves, several steps downstream of a release, and not a mapping for this count.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR technical reporting: released varieties are reported under the Innovation Development output category. The One CGIAR standard indicator set carries "Number of innovations profiled" in that category; the match is adapted, since CGIAR counts profiled innovations of every kind while this indicator counts approved varieties carrying a nutrient claim. A sister CGIAR centre carries "biofortified" as an attribute disaggregate on its germplasm indicator rather than as a standalone indicator; KPI-O07 stays a separate indicator, reconciled with KPI-O12 through the trait-class vocabulary.
definition: Counts the release events of biofortified or nutrient-dense varieties containing CIMMYT-derived germplasm, officially released in CIMMYT intervention countries in the reporting year: one variety released in one country is one event, and the number of distinct varieties is reported alongside. Release means official registration or approval by the competent national or regional authority, which is the releasing actor, not CIMMYT. A variety counts as biofortified or nutrient-dense when it was bred to carry a higher concentration of a target nutrient (for example provitamin A, zinc, iron, or protein quality) than the varieties it replaces. The nutrient-claim evidence, the ancestry rule and the regional-listing rule are in Eligibility criteria and missing data.
rationale: Answers how many nutrition-targeted varieties CIMMYT's breeding work delivered into national seed systems in the year: the point at which a nutrition-focused breeding investment becomes something a farmer can legally obtain. It isolates the nutrition-targeted part of the release pipeline from the wider count of improved varieties released (KPI-O12), and is the base from which dissemination (KPI-O06) and farmers' cultivation (KPI-OC10) are read.
projectSpecificApplication: State the crops covered, the countries candidates were submitted in, the partner institutions holding the release dossiers, and the records evidencing approval date, pedigree link and nutrient claim. Do not change the release definition, counting unit, nutrient-claim rule or pedigree rule; if applying the indicator as defined is not feasible here, raise it with the MEAL focal point.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count serves: for example a contracted release target for a biofortified crop and country, a review of whether nutrition-targeted pipelines are converting advanced lines into approved varieties, or a nutrition donor's required output indicator.
projectTypesNotApplicable: genes and controlled-environment results and which submits no release dossier
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose outputs are traits, genes and controlled-environment results and which submits no release dossier; and digital agriculture and AI, which delivers advisory content and platforms rather than candidate varieties.
unit: Both figures side by side: variety-country release events as the headline, with the number of unique varieties behind that figure reported alongside it, since one variety can be approved in several countries. This matches KPI-O12 exactly, so the nutrient-dense count can be read as a share of all releases.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more biofortified or nutrient-dense varieties containing CIMMYT-derived germplasm reached official release.
disaggregationRequired: Required: crop; trait class. Trait class here is the target nutrient: provitamin A, zinc, iron, protein quality, or other nutrient (named). A variety counts when its nutrient claim meets the evidence standard in Eligibility criteria and missing data. A variety carrying several nutrient traits is assigned to the one that justified its release and listed under the others in a secondary field, so trait subtotals are never summed.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator. Variety is not a cut here: each release event is already one variety in one country, and the distinct-variety figure is reported beside the headline.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country and region of release; releasing partner type (national research system, university, private seed company); genetic unit (hybrid, open-pollinated variety); nutrient concentration achieved against the programme's breeding target.
unitOfObservation: The release event (one variety, legally available in one country by a national or a regional act). This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of release events in the reporting year meeting the inclusion rules. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: administrative and registry data, namely the official release or approval letter, gazette notice, or national or regional variety catalogue entry issued by the national or regional release authority, matched to CIMMYT breeding records (pedigree and breeding line identifiers, grain quality and nutrient composition data) that establish the CIMMYT-derived material. Fallback DS4: published national or regional variety catalogues and seed-sector registers, each compiled by a third party rather than issued by the release authority, used where the releasing partner's own approval documentation cannot be obtained; flag values from this route as fallback-sourced, since catalogues rarely record pedigree. Fallback DS1: laboratory analysis of grain samples of the released variety, evidencing the nutrient claim under the standard in Eligibility criteria and missing data; it evidences the trait, never the release event, and it never changes the record's source route. Not applicable DS3 and DS5: neither an approval decision nor a grain nutrient concentration can be observed from satellite or geospatial data, or evidenced by crowdsourced and mobile data.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether Recommended DS2 or Fallback DS4 was used, name the authority or catalogue each release was evidenced from, and how the pedigree link and nutrient claim were documented. If Fallback DS4, state why.
collectionInstrument: Applies only to the DS1 fallback: laboratory analysis of grain samples of the released variety for the target nutrient, run by the breeding programme's grain quality laboratory. There is no human respondent. No analysis method is prescribed here, since CIMMYT has not documented one; Eligibility criteria and missing data requires the method used to be named with the claim.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as national or regional authorities issue approvals; compiled, verified against pedigree and nutrient records and de-duplicated annually.
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the official approval date falls, that date being the approving authority's decision date, read from the official release or approval letter, or from a gazette notice or catalogue entry that states it, never the date on which the notice or entry was published. A stated year of release with no fuller date establishes the reporting year on its own.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual count of events, so each reporting year starts from zero and the first year reported is the reference point for trend context. Any trend claim must state that the counting unit, the inclusion rules and the nutrient-claim rule were held constant across the years compared.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Across projects: pool counts from projects that used the Recommended source; a project on the Fallback catalogue route is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, not blended into it, since catalogue-sourced counts carry weaker pedigree and release-event evidence. The route is decided per record, not per project: a project whose records come partly from each route pools its Recommended-sourced records and reports its catalogue-sourced records alongside. A record's route is decided by the evidence for its release event alone: a record whose release event rests on the Recommended DS2 documentation is Recommended-sourced, and one that rests on the Fallback DS4 catalogue route is catalogue-sourced, whatever route evidenced its nutrient claim.

B: Combination method. Sum release events across crops, countries and projects after de-duplication on the identifier of the released entry plus the country of legal availability, so one variety approved in one country under two names or two licensees' brands is one event. The identifier is the cross identifier for a hybrid, or the line or population identifier for an open-pollinated variety, inbred line or population: two distinct hybrids sharing one parent line are two releases, never collapsed to one on the shared parent's identifier.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying release events for the reporting year, with the number of distinct varieties behind that figure reported alongside it. At institutional level, the de-duplicated sum of those counts, computed from the approval records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since a variety co-bred by two projects or two centres produces one approval that both can legitimately report. The distinct-variety figure is de-duplicated on the identifier of the released entry alone, so it is never the sum of the country counts. Also report: the boundary with the other two stages, since a variety crossing one mid-year appears in two of the three stage counts for that year and the three are never summed, the number of contributing projects, the number of approvals excluded under Eligibility and why, the number of release events reported alongside because they rest on the Fallback DS4 catalogue route, and the evidence route behind each nutrient claim.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: no. This count is never added to KPI-O06 (disseminated), KPI-OC08 (per-capita biofortified grain available) or KPI-OC10 (farmers cultivating); the levels connect through the theory of change, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: the largest risk is inside the register. Every release counted here is also a release under KPI-O12 (improved crop varieties released), so the two are never added; this count is the nutrition-targeted subset of that one and applies the same release definition and inclusion rules. The same material may have been counted earlier under KPI-O09 and reappears later under KPI-O06 as it is disseminated. Varieties are frequently co-bred, so two projects or two CGIAR centres can each report the same approval: de-duplicate on the identifier of the released entry plus the country of legal availability before pooling and count a jointly bred release once; where identifiers cannot be matched, label the pooled figure an upper estimate. The same release also appears as an innovation entry in CGIAR technical reporting: one event in two systems, not two releases.

The three-stage boundary, stated identically on KPI-O09, KPI-O07 and KPI-O06. A nutrient-dense variety passes through three counted stages, each with one qualifying event and its own evidence: developed and made available (KPI-O09), on a dated distribution, transfer or catalogue record putting the material at a partner's disposal; released (KPI-O07), on an official registration or approval dated inside the year; and disseminated (KPI-O06), on a dated distribution event placing seed with farmers or with the partners who supply them. The events are ordered and mutually exclusive, so no variety sits in two stages on one event: material not yet registered cannot be counted as released, and seed moved before registration is availability rather than dissemination. Each variety counts once per country per stage in a reporting year, and never twice within a stage however many partners or channels are involved. Availability and release each happen once in a country, so the count falls in the year the variety reaches that stage there; dissemination recurs, so a variety distributed in the same country in consecutive years counts in each of those years, with the number disseminated for the first time reported alongside. The three counts are never summed. One variety normally reaches all three stages, usually in different years and sometimes in the same one, so a variety registered in March and distributed in November is one variety counted once under KPI-O07 and once under KPI-O06, not two.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: the released variety is itself a CIMMYT line or population, or CIMMYT germplasm appears in its pedigree as a parent or grandparent, whether or not CIMMYT is named on the national release dossier, the same maximum ancestry depth KPI-O12, KPI-OC12 and KPI-OC14 apply, two generations, a generation being one cross or one line extraction, so for a hybrid the parents are the components of the final cross, and where a component is itself a hybrid its own parents are the grandparents; a documented nutrient claim, evidenced to the standard below; official registration or approval issued by the competent national authority, or by a regional authority whose listing confers legal availability without a further national act, dated inside the reporting year, making the variety available for multiplication. A nutrient claim is documented when the target nutrient is named and its concentration in the released entry is evidenced by compositional analysis reported against a comparator of the varieties it replaces grown in the same trials, spanning at least two sites and at least two seasons, with the analytical method named and, where a screening method such as energy-dispersive XRF was used, its calibration against a reference method stated; for provitamin A and other carotenoids the interval between harvest and analysis is recorded. Where that evidence sits, the release dossier, the breeding programme's records or laboratory analysis of grain samples of the released variety, does not affect eligibility. A regional catalogue listing that confers legal availability directly across member states, with no further national act required, counts as one release event in each member state so covered that is a CIMMYT intervention country; where a member state's own law requires a further national act before the variety may be multiplied or sold there, that act, not the regional listing, is the release event.

Exclusion: released varieties for which no nutrient claim is made (they count under KPI-O12 only); candidates in trials or undecided at year end; renewals, re-registrations, name changes, administrative transfers and extensions to a further zone of a variety already released in that country, whether or not in a year this indicator reported; nutrient-dense lines shared with partners but not submitted for release (KPI-O09); varieties whose pedigree link to CIMMYT material cannot be documented.

Missing data: an approval whose date cannot be established at all, not even to a year, is held out and reported alongside the count as unconfirmed rather than assigned to the current year; a release whose nutrient evidence is pending is footnoted, not carried in the total; once the date is established or the evidence meets the standard in Inclusion, the release is added to the year its approval date falls in, and a figure already reported for that year is restated under the Core's rules for restated values (Section 4.2); a nutrient claim that does not meet the standard in Inclusion is footnoted as provisional and not carried in the total, on the same rule as a claim whose nutrient evidence is pending.
