Repeated observations: one count per released entry per country, whatever the number of approval decisions, names or licensees behind it, on the key in Aggregation rule Block B; the same variety approved in a second country is a new release event there, and counts once only in the distinct-variety figure.
limitations: Measures delivery into the seed system, not nutrition. A released variety is not yet in any farmer's field, and any nutritional benefit depends on multiplication, adoption, the share of the harvest the household eats, and how much of the nutrient survives processing. A rise means the pipeline converted more candidates into approved varieties, not that anyone's diet improved; read it with KPI-OC10 and the dietary indicators in this pathway.

The count is only as firm as the nutrient threshold behind it. The analysis method is recorded with every value, and the threshold once the eligible-variety list sets one, because what counts as biofortified or nutrient-dense can otherwise differ between crops, countries and years, which limits comparison.

Supports a contribution claim only. Release is decided by a national or regional authority, and the variety is usually the joint product of CIMMYT germplasm and a partner's selection, testing and dossier work, so more than one institution can legitimately claim the same release.
Never add this count to the improved-variety release count (KPI-O12). Every release counted here is also counted there by design, so summing them double counts the same approvals.
Counts are shaped by regulation as much as by science. Release systems differ in speed and stringency, so the same breeding work yields different counts in different countries.
subMetrics: None. Crop and trait class are disaggregations of a single count, and the distinct-variety figure is the same count under a different de-duplication rule. Related indicators hold their own sheets: KPI-O06, KPI-O09, KPI-O12, KPI-OC08 and KPI-OC10.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the maize and wheat quality or nutrition breeding lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: breeding programme product managers and country or partner leads, compiling approval documents, pedigree records and nutrient evidence. Validation: project MEAL officer with the breeding data manager and the grain quality laboratory, confirming approval date, pedigree link, nutrient claim and that the release is not a renewal. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: breeding programme director. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 3 · Nutrition & food security — Reference sheet KPI-O07

name: Number of people in CIMMYT intervention areas reached with nutrition-sensitive information or training
resultsLevel: Output. The count reports a delivered result: people reached with nutrition-sensitive information and training that the CIMMYT team and its implementing partners designed and delivered. Whether the people reached change their nutrition-related knowledge, attitudes or practices is a change, measured at outcome level by KPI-OC06.
primaryObjective: PO2 Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved).
cgiarImpactArea: Nutrition, Health & Food Security: the indicator delivers the nutrition-education step of the food and nutrition security pathway. The register carries no Impact Area column; the value follows the pathway-wide rule, which sets the area by what the indicator measures.
sdgTarget: None. The SDG 2 nutrition indicators measure nutrition and food security status in populations (for example prevalence of undernourishment, food insecurity, malnutrition); no SDG indicator counts an organization's delivery of nutrition information or training.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR technical reporting: no standard indicator corresponds to this reach count. No external framework supplies its counting method either. The reach concept, the significance test, the treatment of cascade delivery and the unique-count rule are CIMMYT's own and are stated in Definition and in Eligibility criteria and missing data.
definition: Counts unique people in CIMMYT intervention areas reached with nutrition-sensitive information or training in the reporting year, counted once per person regardless of the number of sessions. Nutrition-sensitive means the activity carries explicit nutrition content or objectives: for example dietary diversity education, food preparation and utilization training, or promotion of the nutritional value of biofortified or nutrient-dense crops, delivered within CIMMYT's agriculture and food systems work. Reached means direct, identifiable contact significant enough to plausibly change what the person knows or does, on CIMMYT's own convention; the qualifying and excluded forms of contact are listed in Eligibility criteria and missing data.
rationale: Answers how many people CIMMYT's nutrition-sensitive work touched directly each year: the delivery step of the nutrition pathway, and the base against which the change in nutrition-related knowledge, attitudes and practices (KPI-OC06) is read. It gives project management and donors a comparable measure of the breadth of nutrition-sensitive engagement across projects, since crop improvement alone does not improve diets unless people also know and choose to use nutritious food.
projectSpecificApplication: State which nutrition-sensitive activities the project delivers (training courses, counseling, demonstrations, community sessions), the population groups targeted (for example farming households, caregivers, extension agents), the geographic scope, and which attendance or activity registers feed the count. Do not alter the unique-count rule, the significance boundary, or the definition of nutrition-sensitive content; if the indicator as defined is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count informs: for example a donor-required reach indicator, a coverage target for nutrition education, or a trigger to adjust delivery channels or targeting if reach among women or youth stays low.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose work is laboratory and controlled-environment research with no population in an intervention area to reach
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose work is laboratory and controlled-environment research with no population in an intervention area to reach.
unit: Number of individuals (unique persons)
directionOfChange: Increase, read against the delivery plan. A rising value means more people were reached with nutrition-sensitive information or training; it says nothing about whether knowledge or practices changed, which KPI-OC06 measures.
disaggregationRequired: Required: sex, collected as female, male, and prefer not to say, reporting female and male as the register specifies with the third as a labelled residual, the same rule as KPI-O04 so the two people-counting indicators collect identically; age (youth/non-youth, using 15 to 30, stated once in Core Section 4.1; projects record date of birth or exact age so any other donor band, for example a donor band of 15 to 29, can be derived without recollecting data).
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Delivery channel (structured training / counseling or demonstration / information session); topic (dietary diversity, food preparation and utilization, biofortified crop nutrition); participant group (farmer, caregiver, extension agent, partner staff); country or region. A person can appear in more than one channel or topic subtotal, so subtotals are never summed to the headline.
unitOfObservation: Individual
calculationSummary: Value = the count of unique people who received at least one qualifying nutrition-sensitive information or training contact in the reporting year. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: the project's own administrative records: attendance registers, counseling and demonstration logs, and partner activity reports, each carrying a unique identifier, sex, and age. Fallback DS1: a participant or household survey to reconstruct reach where registers are incomplete or lack the fields needed for de-duplication; values from this route are flagged as fallback-sourced and carry recall error. Not applicable DS3: being reached with information or training is not observable from satellite or geospatial data. Not applicable DS4: no third-party database records who CIMMYT reached. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced data cannot verify that an identified individual received a significant nutrition-sensitive contact.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether Recommended or Fallback was used, which registers or partner reports supplied records, and how de-duplication across sessions and partners was done. If Fallback, state why the activity registers were not usable.
collectionInstrument: For the recommended DS2 route: a standard registration and attendance template capturing name or ID, sex, age, session topic, channel, and date. For the DS1 fallback: a short survey module capturing the same fields plus which activity reached the respondent, administered in person or by phone.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as attendance registers and activity records log participation; compiled and de-duplicated annually.
referencePeriod: The reporting year. Each annual value stands alone: the same person can be reached in successive years, so annual values are never summed into a multi-year total.
baselineRequired: No. As an annual output count the value starts from zero each reporting year; the first reported year serves as the reference point for trend context. No change or impact claim rests on this indicator alone.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool counts from projects that used the Recommended source for all their records; a project that used the Fallback survey route for any of its records is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note stating how many records that route supplied, not blended in.

B: Combination method. Sum unique individuals across activities and projects after de-duplication by identifier, so a person reached by two projects counts once in the institutional figure.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of unique people on that project's attendance and activity registers for the reporting year, de-duplicated on the persistent participant identifier the registers carry. At institutional level, the count of unique people across projects, de-duplicated again across registers, since one person reached by two projects is one person and summing project counts would report them twice. Where identifiers cannot be reconciled across registers, the institutional figure is labelled an upper bound on measured coverage rather than presented as a count. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the reconciliation basis, the number of records dropped for want of an identifier, and, where nutrition content was delivered at broadcast scale, the estimated audience as a separate labelled figure.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count does not add to KPI-OC06 or any outcome value; the levels connect through the theory of change, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: de-duplicate by identifier across sessions, partners and projects; where matching is not possible, label the pooled figure an upper bound on measured coverage. Across indicators, overlap is real and named, never summed: a person whose nutrition-sensitive contact was a structured training also meets the definition of KPI-O04 (individuals trained), and may simultaneously count under KPI-O18 (farmers trained in improved practices), KPI-O26 (farmers reached with digital advisory services), or the women and youth training counts (KPI-O28, KPI-O29). The institutional report shows the overlap rather than removing it from either count: it states which of these counts include the same people, and these indicators are parallel views of overlapping populations, never summed and never netted out of one another.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: people in CIMMYT intervention areas directly reached with nutrition-sensitive content delivered by CIMMYT or by partners under a project agreement, including people reached through a deliberate cascade or service-delivery strategy (a trained community facilitator's trainees count; the facilitator counts too).

Exclusion: agronomic training on a biofortified crop, which does not qualify on the crop alone: content qualifies only when it carries explicit nutrition content, meaning diet, food consumption, nutrient quality, food safety or feeding practice, stated in the session or material; brief attendance at a meeting or gathering without structured nutrition content; passive exposure to mass media (radio, broadcast SMS) with no accompanying training or counseling; indirect beneficiaries such as neighbours adopting practices by observation.
limitations: Counts delivery, not learning or behaviour: being reached says nothing about whether diets or practices changed; CIMMYT is accountable here only for coverage. Read it as the reach step of the pathway, alongside KPI-OC06.

A headcount carries no intensity: a single information session and a multi-week nutrition course each count as one person, so the headline can rise while depth of engagement falls. Always read it with the delivery-channel breakdown.

The significance boundary cuts both ways: mass-media exposure is excluded, so a large radio or SMS campaign leaves this indicator flat even if it reaches many people, while a single structured session counts. State the boundary applied so values are comparable across projects and years.

De-duplication quality drives the number: registers with inconsistent or missing identifiers hide repeat participants (overcount) or merge distinct people (undercount), and community sessions often record households rather than named individuals; the identification standard applied must travel with the value.

Spillover is outside the indicator by construction: neighbours who take up a practice by observation are excluded, so the value is bounded by direct, identifiable reach and understates how far the content travelled. Measuring that travel needs a comparison group and a study design, which belongs to impact assessment rather than to routine reporting.
Annual values are not cumulative: the same person can count in successive years, so summing years overstates unique people reached.
subMetrics: None. Information versus training, topic, and delivery channel are disaggregations of the same unique count, not separately calculated metrics. Related indicators have their own sheets: KPI-O04 (individuals trained, the all-topic training count this indicator overlaps), KPI-O26 (digital advisory reach), and KPI-OC06 (change in nutrition-related knowledge, attitudes and practices, the outcome this count rolls up to per the register).
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
Counting rule: No external standard defines this indicator. The reach concept, the significance test and the unique-count and de-duplication rules are CIMMYT's own convention, stated on CIMMYT's authority.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the nutrition research lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project field teams and partner facilitators maintaining attendance registers and activity logs. Validation: project MEAL officer (identity fields complete, significance boundary applied, nutrition-sensitive content confirmed). Calculation: project M&E, applying the unique-count rule; cross-project de-duplication by the CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 3 · Nutrition & food security — Reference sheet KPI-O08

name: Number of nutrient-dense crop varieties or breeding lines developed and made available to partners and farmers
resultsLevel: Output. Developing lines and putting them at partners' disposal is a delivered result of CIMMYT's own breeding and germplasm teams; what partners then do with the material (test, register, multiply it) is a change among partners and is measured at outcome level. A sister CGIAR centre classifies its equivalent indicator, germplasm lines developed and transferred to national agricultural research systems, at output level.
primaryObjective: PO2 Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved), since the same material also carries agronomic traits that reach smallholder farms.
cgiarImpactArea: Nutrition, Health & Food Security. Biofortified and nutrient-dense staples are the micronutrient pathway CGIAR places in this Impact Area, and this indicator counts the material that starts that pathway. The register carries no Impact Area column; the value follows the pathway-wide rule, which sets the area by what the indicator measures.
sdgTarget: None. The indicator contributes to SDG target 2.2 (end all forms of malnutrition), but no SDG indicator counts crop varieties or breeding lines: the indicators under target 2.2 measure malnutrition in people, not the research material intended to reduce it. Do not report this value against an SDG indicator number.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR results framework, innovation development category (a new, improved or adapted output with high potential to contribute to positive impacts when used at scale): the same idea at broader scope, counted as innovations profiled by readiness stage rather than as germplasm made available. A sister CGIAR centre reports a close variant, germplasm lines developed and transferred to national agricultural research systems, disaggregated by crop, attribute (including biofortified), recipient institution and country.
definition: Counts the nutrient-dense crop varieties and breeding lines CIMMYT's breeding programmes developed and made available to partners and farmers in the reporting year, counted once per country of new availability, with the unique-line figure alongside. A breeding line carries a new trait combination breeders can use as a parent or advance towards release; nutrient-dense covers micronutrient biofortification (provitamin A, zinc, iron) and protein quality, including quality protein maize. "Made available" means the material left CIMMYT's pipeline and was put at the disposal of others; the qualifying channels are in Eligibility. It sits upstream of release: material offered to partners, not approved by a registration authority (KPI-O07) and not distributed to farmers (KPI-O06).
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT is keeping the front of the nutrition pipeline full: how much nutrient-dense breeding material reached the partners who can test, register and multiply it in a given year. It is the earliest point at which this work becomes visible outside CIMMYT, and the leading signal for the release, dissemination and adoption indicators downstream, which cannot rise unless this one rose in earlier years.
projectSpecificApplication: State which crops, trait classes and partner countries the project covers, and which availability channel it used (nursery distribution, material transfer on request, or catalogue listing). Do not alter the institutional definition, the nutrient-density criterion or the counting rule: a project reports its lines as an identified subset of the institutional total, never as a separate additional count. If the indicator cannot be applied as defined here, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment the figure serves: a breeding grant with a germplasm-delivery deliverable, a national partner's request for nutrient-dense material to enter its own trials, or a decision on which trait classes and crops to prioritise in the next distribution cycle.
projectTypesApply: seed systems and deployment. This is the one indicator in the pathway a laboratory-stage project can report
because the object counted is germplasm rather than a farm
a population or a delivered service: an edited or characterised line transferred under a material transfer agreement
projectTypesNotApplicable: system change and transformation, and digital agriculture and AI
none of which develops germplasm or operates a channel through which germplasm is made available
projectTypesRaw:
Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; seed systems and deployment. This is the one indicator in the pathway a laboratory-stage project can report, because the object counted is germplasm rather than a farm, a population or a delivered service: an edited or characterised line transferred under a material transfer agreement, with its nutrient result measured, meets the inclusion rules.

Not applicable: applied agronomy and farming systems, system change and transformation, and digital agriculture and AI, none of which develops germplasm or operates a channel through which germplasm is made available.
unit: Number of line-country availability events in the reporting year: the counted unit is the distinct genetic entity made available, whether a fixed advanced line, a hybrid combination or a population, recorded with which of the three it is, counted once per country in which it is first made available. The unique-line figure, de-duplicated on designation and pedigree alone, is reported alongside so both readings are visible.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more nutrient-dense varieties or breeding lines were made available to partners and farmers. The count measures the volume of material offered, not its quality or its eventual usefulness; see Limitations.
disaggregationRequired: Required: crop (scientific name of the taxon, so counts stay comparable where common names differ); trait class (the target nutrient or quality trait: zinc, iron, provitamin A, protein quality, or another documented nutritional quality trait); material type (finished variety or advanced breeding line), because the two are not equivalent products and mixing them makes annual totals unreadable.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator. Variety is not a cut here: each availability event is already one line or variety in one country, and the unique-line figure is reported beside the headline.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Recipient institution and type (national research system, university, seed company, farmer organisation); country of destination; availability channel (nursery, transfer on request, catalogue); additional traits carried, for example drought tolerance or disease resistance.
unitOfObservation: The line-country availability event (one distinct line, hybrid combination or population, identified by pedigree and designation, in one country where it is first made available). This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation, whose definition covers a breeding line.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of line-country availability events in the reporting year: each distinct nutrient-dense variety or breeding line counts in the first year it is made available in each country, and a line already counted may be counted again when made available in a new country, since availability is country-specific and the second country is genuinely new access. The unique-line figure is reported alongside. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: CIMMYT breeding and germplasm distribution records, that is the line register with pedigree and designation, advancement decisions, nursery composition and dispatch lists, material transfer agreements and shipment records, and partner-facing catalogues that record the date each entry was listed. Frame DS1, eligibility evidence only: laboratory analyses of grain nutrient concentration on breeding-trial samples, the evidence behind the nutrient-density inclusion criterion, required alongside the producing route, not a second count. Comparator DS4: published partner or national germplasm catalogues and CIMMYT's published germplasm data portals, used to place the count against the material shown as on offer; these show what is currently on offer rather than what became available in a given year, and are never pooled and never reported as a KPI-O09 value. An entry on CIMMYT's portals that records the date it was listed and the country in which it was made available is a DS2 catalogue record, not a Comparator entry. Not applicable DS3: a transfer to a partner is not observable from satellite, aerial or GIS data. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or mobile data can establish neither the nutrient trait nor the transfer event.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State the extract date and how the count was de-duplicated against the institutional list.
collectionInstrument: Laboratory analysis of grain nutrient concentration on breeding-trial samples, with the analytical method named on the record, together with the distribution record that dates the availability event. Respondent rule: not applicable, the measurement is on grain samples and administrative records, not on people. The concentration threshold is a property of the versioned eligible-variety list proposed on KPI-O07; until that list sets one, no threshold is asserted here.
collectionFrequency: Continuously, as breeding programmes record nutrient analyses, advancement decisions, nursery dispatches and material transfers in their own systems.
reportingFrequency: Annually, extracted once the year's distribution cycle closes, with the extract date held constant across years.
referencePeriod: The reporting year CIMMYT uses for institutional reporting. The value covers availability events dated within that year.
baselineRequired: No for the value itself, which is an annual flow counted from records. Yes for any statement of change, which needs at least one comparable earlier year; earlier years are normally reconstructible from distribution and nursery records. If records do not reach back, the first reported year becomes the reference point and no change claim is made against earlier periods.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool the counts after de-duplication. One line distributed by several projects is one line.

B: Combination method. The institutional figure is the de-duplicated count of line-country availability events across all CIMMYT breeding programmes in the reporting year, with the unique-line figure alongside.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of line-country availability events that project generated in the reporting year, with its unique-line figure alongside. At institutional level, the de-duplicated count across all breeding programmes, computed from the line register itself rather than by adding project figures, since one line is routinely carried by several nurseries, shipments and projects in the same year. A line counts once per country, in its first year of availability there, so neither project nor institutional figures are additive across years. Also report: the boundary with the other two stages, since a variety crossing one mid-year appears in two of the three stage counts for that year and the three are never summed, the number of contributing breeding programmes, and the number of lines held out under Eligibility as pending nutrient verification.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count must never be added to KPI-O07 (nutrient-dense varieties released) or KPI-O06 (nutrient-dense varieties disseminated); the same material normally passes through all three stages in different years, so summing them counts one product up to three times. It rolls up to KPI-O07 as a pipeline predecessor, not as an addend.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: de-duplicate by the line's unique designation and pedigree identifier plus country before pooling, so that a line sent to many partners or nurseries counts once per country, in its first year of availability there; the unique-line figure is de-duplicated on the identifier alone. Where designations are inconsistent across programmes and de-duplication cannot be completed, label the pooled number an upper estimate.

The three-stage boundary, stated identically on KPI-O09, KPI-O07 and KPI-O06. A nutrient-dense variety passes through three counted stages, each with one qualifying event and its own evidence: developed and made available (KPI-O09), on a dated distribution, transfer or catalogue record putting the material at a partner's disposal; released (KPI-O07), on an official registration or approval dated inside the year; and disseminated (KPI-O06), on a dated distribution event placing seed with farmers or with the partners who supply them. The events are ordered and mutually exclusive, so no variety sits in two stages on one event: material not yet registered cannot be counted as released, and seed moved before registration is availability rather than dissemination. Each variety counts once per country per stage in a reporting year, and never twice within a stage however many partners or channels are involved. Availability and release each happen once in a country, so the count falls in the year the variety reaches that stage there; dissemination recurs, so a variety distributed in the same country in consecutive years counts in each of those years, with the number disseminated for the first time reported alongside. The three counts are never summed. One variety normally reaches all three stages, usually in different years and sometimes in the same one, so a variety registered in March and distributed in November is one variety counted once under KPI-O07 and once under KPI-O06, not two.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusions: "made available" is evidenced by distribution in international nurseries and trials, dispatch on request under the standard material transfer agreement of the International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture, or listing in a partner-accessible catalogue; material developed by CIMMYT alone or with partners, carrying a documented enhanced level of a target nutrient or quality trait (an enhanced micronutrient concentration, or protein quality as in quality protein maize), and evidenced by a dated distribution, transfer or catalogue record.

"Made available to partners and farmers" is satisfied by distribution to research and seed-system partners; farmer-accessible availability is not required at this indicator, since whether the material then reaches farmers is what KPI-O06 and KPI-OC10 measure.

Exclusions: material still under internal evaluation; parental or maintainer stocks moved only between CIMMYT sites for internal breeding operations; material whose nutrient trait rests on expectation rather than a measured result; material counted in an earlier year in the same country; material already registered in the country at the date of dispatch and dispatched to a partner supplying farmers, which is dissemination (KPI-O06).
limitations: Counts availability, not use and not nutrition. A line made available may never be released, multiplied, planted or eaten, and micronutrient status depends on diets, consumption patterns and health conditions well beyond CIMMYT's reach. It supports a contribution claim about pipeline delivery only.

The number moves with counting conventions as much as with performance. What qualifies as nutrient-dense, and whether the counted unit is a line, a hybrid combination or a population, can each change the total substantially, so the unit definition, and the threshold once the eligible-variety list sets one, must travel with the figure.

The three biofortification output indicators describe the same material at different stages, so they must never be summed. A rise here will not appear in release or dissemination figures for several years: that is a lag, not an inconsistency.

An increase means more nutrient-dense material reached partners, not that the pipeline improved in quality, since a programme can raise the count by distributing more marginal lines. Read it alongside release, adoption and nutrient-availability indicators.
subMetrics: None. Crop, trait class and material type are disaggregations of one count, not separately calculated metrics. Neighbouring stages have their own sheets: KPI-O07 (released), KPI-O06 (disseminated), KPI-OC10 (share of target farmers cultivating them).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the maize and wheat breeding programmes as technical owners of the method
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: breeding programme staff and the germplasm distribution unit (nutrient analyses, advancement decisions, nursery and shipment records). Validation: the breeding programme's data manager (designations unique, nutrient result on record, availability event dated). Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, per the calculation method above, de-duplicating across programmes. Approval: breeding programme leader or designated approver. Reporting: programme MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 3 · Nutrition & food security — Reference sheet KPI-O09

name: Share of the target population in CIMMYT intervention areas demonstrating improved nutrition-related Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices (KAP) relative to a baseline survey
resultsLevel: Outcome, as recorded in the register: improved nutrition knowledge, attitudes and practices in a target population is a change in capacity and practice among beneficiaries, which is the Core's definition of an outcome. The outreach that precedes it is a delivered result, counted at output level by KPI-O08. CGIAR's quality-assurance outcome definition, a change in the knowledge, attitudes, skills or relationships of external actors, gives the same level.
primaryObjective: PO2 Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved), because better nutrition knowledge and practices in farm households improve how the food and income smallholders generate translate into wellbeing.
cgiarImpactArea: Nutrition, Health & Food Security
sdgTarget: None. No SDG indicator measures nutrition-related knowledge, attitudes or practices. The nearest official indicators sit one level up in this pathway's chain: SDG 2.1.2 (food insecurity, FIES) is measured by KPI-I02, the impact indicator this outcome feeds.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR results taxonomy: the outcome definition, a change in knowledge, attitudes, skills and/or relationships (KASR) of external actors, is the category this indicator evidences (CGIAR Quality Assurance Assessor Guidance, 2024). The FAO KAP manual, Guidelines for assessing nutrition-related knowledge, attitudes and practices (Fautsch Macías & Glasauer, 2014), is the standard measurement guidance for nutrition KAP surveys; it is survey methodology, not a donor reporting framework. No donor reporting framework defines a standardised KAP indicator, so there is no crosswalk to record.
definition: Measures the share of the target population in CIMMYT intervention areas demonstrating improved nutrition-related Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices (KAP) relative to a baseline survey. KAP covers three linked domains: knowledge (what people know about nutrition, for example which foods provide which nutrients), attitudes (what they believe and value about those foods and feeding practices), and practices (what they do, for example what they ate or fed a child in the recall window). Each domain is measured with a standardised survey scale; a person counts as improved when their follow-up score is higher than their own baseline score under the classification rule in Calculation method.
rationale: Answers whether the people CIMMYT reaches with nutrition-sensitive information and training (counted by KPI-O08) end up knowing, valuing and doing something different about nutrition: the behaviour-change step that must happen before better diets and food security can follow. It gives project management and donors evidence of effect rather than reach, and is the register's designated outcome link between nutrition outreach and food-insecurity impact (KPI-I02).
projectSpecificApplication: State the project's target population (for example women of reproductive age, caregivers of young children, or participating farm households), its intervention areas and countries, which nutrition-sensitive activities the KAP measurement is attached to, and the baseline and follow-up survey timing. The KAP modules, scoring, improvement classification and calculation are unchanged; only population, geography and survey timing are project-specific. If applying the indicator as defined is not feasible, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this measure informs: for example a donor-funded nutrition-sensitive component that must demonstrate behaviour change rather than attendance, or an internal trigger to redesign the information and training package if knowledge improves but practices do not.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose work is laboratory and controlled-environment research with no target population to survey at baseline and follow-up
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose work is laboratory and controlled-environment research with no target population to survey at baseline and follow-up.
unit: Percentage of surveyed target persons. On the repeated cross-section fallback, score points: the difference in mean score for each domain.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of the surveyed target population improved on the nutrition-related knowledge, attitudes and practices measured.
disaggregationRequired: Sex and age are required disaggregations, matching the feeding output KPI-O08, which is sex- and age-disaggregated while the register records no disaggregation here: an outcome that cannot be disaggregated the way its own output is cannot be read against it. Sex (female/male at minimum, per the register's own disaggregation rule) and age (youth/non-youth, 15 to 30, stated once in Core Section 4.1; projects record date of birth or exact age so other bands, for example a donor band of 15 to 29, can be derived).
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: KAP domain (share improved in knowledge, in attitudes, in practices separately, which shows where the change is happening); respondent group (for example caregivers of children under two versus other adults); country or region; rural/urban.
unitOfObservation: Individual
calculationSummary: Numerator: surveyed target persons classified as showing improved KAP, meaning their follow-up score exceeds their own baseline score under the improvement rule below. Denominator: all target persons with a completed baseline and follow-up interview. Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100, applying survey weights where a sample design is used. Scoring: each domain (knowledge, attitudes, practices) is scored separately from its own survey module, following the FAO KAP manual's model modules and scoring guidance adapted to the project's nutrition topics. Improvement rule: a person counts as improved when the follow-up score rises in practices plus at least one other domain: higher than their own baseline score in the practices domain and in at least one of knowledge and attitudes; knowing more without doing anything differently does not count. No external standard defines a single "improved KAP" threshold, so this rule is CIMMYT's own convention. Panel requirement and fallback: person-level improvement can only be computed for the same individuals interviewed at baseline and follow-up. Where the panel fails, a repeated cross-section is admitted as a documented fallback: it cannot classify person-level improvement, so it reports, for each domain, the difference in mean score between two samples of the same population, labelled as such, and is never pooled with panel values (see Data source and Baseline required). Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended, DS1 (Censuses & surveys): a panel survey of the target population carrying standardised KAP modules at baseline and follow-up, following the FAO KAP manual's model questionnaires and scoring guidance; the only source that observes the same person's knowledge, attitudes and practices twice. Fallback, DS1 (repeated cross-section): where the panel fails, a repeated cross-section is admitted as a documented fallback, labelled as such, rather than the project reporting nothing: fresh samples of the same target population at baseline and follow-up, using the same modules and scoring. It cannot observe the same person twice, so it yields the difference in mean domain scores between rounds, not person-level improvement, and the design used is reported with every value, because a panel change and a cross-sectional difference are not the same quantity. Improvement against a person's own baseline cannot be reconstructed from any secondary or administrative source. Not applicable, DS2 (Administrative & registry data): training attendance records evidence exposure, not knowledge, attitudes or practices. Not applicable, DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation): what people know, believe and do about nutrition is not observable from satellite or geographic data. Not applicable, DS4 (Secondary & international databases): national nutrition surveys describe general populations and cannot resolve a project's target population against its own baseline. Not applicable, DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): crowdsourced or self-published data cannot apply a standardised scale to a defined panel.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which design the project used, the Recommended panel or the labelled repeated cross-section fallback, and name the rounds. If the fallback was used, state why the panel could not be held and report the difference in mean domain scores as such, never as person-level improvement.
collectionInstrument: The FAO KAP manual (2014) is CIMMYT's standard instrument source: KAP survey modules adapted from its model questionnaires for the project's nutrition topics and target group, with the project's scoring key fixed at baseline. Respondent: the target person directly (for child-feeding topics, the child's caregiver). Mode: face-to-face or phone interview. Projects must adapt the module to local diets and languages, which is exactly when comparability is lost, so the CIMMYT MEAL unit runs the one-time methods review of each project's adapted module before the baseline is fielded, not after the data exist.
collectionFrequency: Baseline and endline; for multi-year projects, a midline round every 2 to 3 years. Keep survey timing constant across rounds relative to the agricultural season, since food practices vary seasonally.
reportingFrequency: Annually; between survey rounds the latest measured value is carried forward with its survey year stated.
referencePeriod: From the project baseline survey to the follow-up survey round; each reported value describes cumulative change since baseline, not change during the reporting year. Within each interview, the recall windows of the KAP modules apply (practices are typically asked over the previous day or week).
baselineRequired: Yes, by construction: the indicator is defined relative to each person's baseline interview, so without a baseline round there is no value at all. No retrospective fallback is acceptable: recalled past knowledge or practices cannot be scored on the same scale as a live interview. Where a project starts without a baseline, the first completed survey round becomes the baseline and the indicator reports from the follow-up round onward; until then, monitoring only, no change claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool individual records from projects that used the Recommended panel design. A project reporting the repeated cross-section fallback is presented alongside the pooled panel figure with a note, never blended in, since a round-level difference and a person-level improvement share are different quantities; a project without both rounds has no value to report at all. Projects measuring different target groups (for example caregivers versus farmers) are pooled arithmetically but the composition is stated, since the mix affects interpretation.

B: Combination method. The institutional value is computed by pooling individual records: sum numerators and denominators across projects, never average project-level percentages.

C: Levels and operations. A share is recomputed at every level from its own numerator and denominator, never averaged from the levels beneath it: a mean of project percentages weights a project of thirty equally with one of three thousand. At project level, panel completers classified as improved over all panel completers for that project. At Regional / Aggregated and institutional level, the summed numerator over the summed denominator, computed from the individual records within the pooling domain of Block A rather than from project shares. Also report: the denominator itself, the attrition rate between rounds, the number of persons excluded under Eligibility, the three domain-level shares alongside the headline, since a knowledge-only gain read as behaviour change is the specific misreading this indicator invites, and the share whose follow-up score fell in practices and in at least one other domain, the mirror of the improvement rule, since without a comparison group it is the only check on how much of the improved share noise alone produces.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This value does not combine arithmetically with KPI-O08 (people reached, output) or KPI-I02 (food-insecurity prevalence, impact); the three connect through the theory of change. The same person legitimately appears in both KPI-O08 (reached) and here (improved); that is the chain working, not double counting, but the two numbers must never be summed.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: where two projects' sampling frames overlap, pool only surveys whose frames partition the domain, or re-derive the design weights for the combined sample; where neither is possible, report the project values separately.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion: members of the target population, which is the population the project plans to reach under KPI-O08, sampled at baseline from the project's target list, not a narrower subgroup; the two indicators are an output and its outcome, so a mismatch in population would mean the outcome measures change in people the output was never meant to count. Where a project's nutrition work targets a specific group such as caregivers of young children, that is recorded as the project-specific application and reported as a subgroup, not as a different population.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only: nutrition knowledge, attitudes and practices also respond to schooling, media, markets, health services and other programmes operating in the same areas; CIMMYT's outreach is one contributor among many.

Practices are self-reported in an interview, and respondents tend to report what they know they should do rather than what they do, especially after training has taught them the desired answer; expect reported practices to overstate actual behaviour change, and treat the practices domain as reported, not observed. The strictly-greater improvement rule is also exposed to regression to the mean: respondents scoring low at baseline drift upward on re-test by chance alone, so the rule classifies a substantial share as improved even where nothing changed, which the design, having no comparison group, cannot separate; the mirror share whose scores fell is reported for that reason.

The value describes panel completers only: people lost between baseline and follow-up (movers, non-responders) often differ systematically from those re-interviewed, so high attrition biases the share in an unknown direction. Always read the value next to its reported attrition rate.

A composite "improved" share hides which domain moved: knowledge typically improves before attitudes and long before practices. Report the domain-level shares alongside the headline value so a knowledge-only gain is not read as behaviour change.

A rising share means more surveyed people scored above their own baseline; it does not mean diets improved, or that dietary energy adequacy, the affordability of a healthy diet or food security improved, which KPI-OC07, KPI-OC09 and KPI-I02 measure.
subMetrics: None. The knowledge, attitudes and practices domain scores are components of the improvement classification and optional disaggregations, not separately calculated metrics. Related sheets: KPI-O08 (people reached with nutrition-sensitive information or training, the feeding output) and KPI-I02 (prevalence of moderate-or-severe food insecurity, FIES, the impact this outcome feeds).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E team and enumerators (baseline and follow-up rounds). Validation: project MEAL officer (module completeness, panel matching, attrition reporting). Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, per Calculation method above. Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 3 · Nutrition & food security — Reference sheet KPI-OC06

name: Share of people in intervention areas meeting or exceeding the minimum dietary energy requirement
resultsLevel: Outcome, as recorded in the register. CIMMYT's own MEAL Framework definition governs the register, so the level the register records stands; where CGIAR's own classification or a donor framework would read this differently, that is recorded as a comparison, not a correction, and the divergence is handled once in the crosswalk annex.
primaryObjective: PO2 Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved).
cgiarImpactArea: Nutrition, Health & Food Security, following what the indicator measures, per the pathway-wide rule.
sdgTarget: SDG target 2.1; indicator 2.1.1 (Prevalence of undernourishment). Record the relationship: SDG 2.1.1 estimates the share of a national population below the MDER using a statistical model of the food consumption distribution; this indicator is its complement (the share at or above the threshold), measured directly among assessed persons in intervention areas. The construct is the same; the measurement approach and population differ.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR standard indicators: "number of people meeting minimum dietary energy requirements", an impact-area indicator under Nutrition, Health and Food Security (direct correspondence). FAO global food security monitoring: the prevalence of undernourishment series published annually in The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World.
definition: Measures the share of people in CIMMYT intervention areas whose dietary energy intake meets or exceeds the minimum dietary energy requirement (MDER). The MDER is the FAO threshold for the minimum amount of food energy (kilocalories per person per day) compatible with good health, set separately for each sex and age group: it takes the lowest healthy body weight for each group and the energy needed at light physical activity, following the human energy requirement norms of the joint FAO, World Health Organization and United Nations University expert consultation. It is deliberately a minimum, not an average, so that people with below-average needs are not wrongly counted as underfed.
rationale: Answers whether people in CIMMYT intervention areas are getting enough food energy for a healthy, active life: the most basic dimension of food security that CIMMYT's work on productive, nutritious staple crops serves. CGIAR tracks the equivalent measure, the number of people meeting minimum dietary energy requirements, among its standard indicators for the Nutrition, Health and Food Security Impact Area, so this indicator feeds directly into institutional and donor reporting.
projectSpecificApplication: State the zone of influence the share is measured over, the population surveyed and the timing of the baseline and endline rounds. The institutional definition, the MDER thresholds and the calculation method are unchanged; only the population, geography and survey timing are project-specific. If applying the indicator as defined is not feasible in this project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here. Example: the share of people in the project's zone of influence meeting the minimum dietary energy requirement, surveyed at baseline and endline.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor requirement this value informs. Example: dietary energy adequacy in the zone of influence reported to the donor, with a falling share during implementation triggering a review of whether the project's production and food-access components are reaching the households that need them.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose work is laboratory and controlled-environment research with no population in an intervention area whose dietary energy intake could be assessed
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose work is laboratory and controlled-environment research with no population in an intervention area whose dietary energy intake could be assessed.
unit: Percentage of people
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of people meet or exceed the minimum dietary energy requirement.
disaggregationRequired: Sex (female/male); age (youth/non-youth, youth defined as 15 to 30, stated once in Core Section 4.1; record date of birth or exact age so other bands, for example a donor band of 15 to 29, can be derived).
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Agroecological zone; rural/urban; household type.
unitOfObservation: Individual
calculationSummary: Numerator: persons whose estimated habitual dietary energy intake (kilocalories per day) meets or exceeds the MDER for their sex and age group. Denominator: all persons assessed in the intervention area. Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100, applying survey weights. Intake estimation: dietary energy intake is estimated from individual dietary intake data (food consumed, converted to kilocalories using food composition tables), or, on the household-approximation fallback in Data source, from household food consumption allocated to members as that fallback states. Thresholds: MDER values per sex and age group follow the FAO methodology, which specifies them for adolescents and adults: the minimum of each group's energy requirement range, at light physical activity, from the FAO/WHO/UNU human energy requirement norms. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1: a population-based household survey in the intervention area carrying an individual quantitative dietary intake module, with intake measured repeatedly (non-consecutive days, for at least a subsample) to estimate habitual consumption, following the measurement principles in the SDG 2.1.1 metadata. Fallback DS1 (household approximation): a documented household-level approximation is authorised as a labelled fallback, not as the standard. Individual intake modules are rarely fielded by agricultural projects, and a standard no project can meet produces no data rather than good data; where only household food consumption data exist, household energy is allocated to individual members by a documented method before comparison against individual thresholds. The method is held constant across rounds, and no sex or age disaggregation is reported from this route, since the allocation, not the data, sets how energy divides between members. The value is reported with its allocation method named and is never presented as an individual intake estimate, since the two are different quantities and the household figure hides intra-household distribution, which is precisely where nutritional vulnerability sits. Fallback DS4: the FAO national prevalence-of-undernourishment series (FAOSTAT Suite of Food Security Indicators), reported as its complement (100 minus the prevalence of undernourishment). Use only where the project cannot field its own survey: the national series is model-based rather than directly measured, cannot resolve a project zone of influence, and carries no sex or age disaggregation of the kind this indicator requires. Flag any value from this source as fallback-sourced. Not applicable: DS2, DS3, DS5. Dietary energy intake is a measured individual condition; it cannot be read from administrative or project records, from satellite or geospatial data, or from crowdsourced observations.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role this project used: Recommended, the labelled household-approximation fallback, or the national-series Fallback. If a fallback was used, explain briefly why individual intake measurement was not feasible.
collectionInstrument: Individual quantitative dietary intake module (for example repeated 24-hour dietary recall), with energy conversion via a food composition table appropriate to the country. Respondent: the individual; a caregiver responds for young children. Mode: face-to-face interview. Only applicable under DS1; write "Not applicable, secondary source" where the national-series Fallback is used.
collectionFrequency: Baseline and endline; for multi-year programmes, a midline every 2 to 3 years. Keep the survey season constant across rounds, since dietary energy intake varies seasonally.
reportingFrequency: Annually; between measurement waves, the latest measured value is carried forward with its year of measurement noted.
referencePeriod: The survey round's intake measurement window, taken to represent habitual daily intake for that year; each reported value describes the round in which it was measured, compared against the pre-intervention baseline round.
baselineRequired: Yes. Past dietary intake cannot be reconstructed reliably by recall, so retrospective baseline reconstruction is not an acceptable fallback for this indicator. Acceptable fallback where no prospective baseline exists: the earliest available survey round treated as a delayed baseline. If none is feasible: monitoring only, no change claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool Recommended-sourced person-level values directly; a project that used a fallback (the household approximation, or national model-based data) is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, never blended in, because its values rest on a different method or resolution.

B: Combination method. Pool at person level using survey weights: the institutional figure is the weighted share across every project that reported via the Recommended source. Never average project-level percentages.

C: Levels and operations. A share is recomputed at every level from its own numerator and denominator, never averaged from the levels beneath it: a mean of project percentages weights a project of three hundred people equally with one of three thousand. At Individual, each person's estimated habitual intake is compared against the MDER for their own sex and age group; no share is reported at that level. At project level, assessed persons meeting or exceeding their MDER over all persons assessed, applying survey weights. At Regional / Aggregated and institutional level, the summed weighted numerator over the summed weighted denominator within the pooling domain of Block A, computed from person records rather than from project shares. The absolute count carried as the sub-metric behaves differently and is the one figure on this sheet that is summed: it is added across projects only where Block E allows their surveys to be pooled, computed from the person records under the pooled sample's weights rather than by adding project counts, because CGIAR's standard indicator set carries the measure as a count. The share is the value to interpret and the count is the value to sum; neither is derived from the other after the fact. Also report: the denominator, the population assessed (for example all household members, or women aged 15 to 49), since shares over different populations pool into one figure whose composition must be stated, the number of persons excluded under Eligibility, and, where household food consumption stood in for individual intake, the allocation method used.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This outcome does not combine arithmetically with the pathway's impact indicator KPI-I02 (prevalence of moderate-or-severe food insecurity, FIES); dietary energy adequacy and experienced food insecurity are different constructs at different levels, connected through the Theory of Change as a narrative, not through arithmetic. The numerator count (people meeting the threshold) is never added to person counts from other register indicators, for example people benefiting from innovations, or households classified by FIES: the same person can legitimately appear under several indicators, and each is reported only under its own.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: where two projects' sampling frames overlap, pool only surveys whose frames partition the domain, or re-derive the design weights for the combined sample; where neither is possible, report the project values separately.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Include persons in sampled households in the intervention area with a completed individual intake record: at least one full 24-hour recall, with a repeat on a non-consecutive day for at least a subsample. On the household-approximation fallback in Data source, include instead persons in sampled households with a complete household food consumption record. Exclude persons whose intake record is incomplete, or, on that fallback, whose household food consumption record is incomplete. Missing data: an excluded person leaves the denominator rather than being imputed, and the excluded share is reported alongside the value. Repeated observations: repeated intake measurements on the same person within a round, recall on non-consecutive days, are one observation, not several; habitual intake is estimated from them by a method that removes day-to-day variation and the method is named with the value. A simple mean of the recall days is not habitual intake.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only: dietary energy adequacy also responds to food prices, incomes, markets, social protection and shocks; CIMMYT is one contributor among many, so pair movements in this indicator with adoption and productivity indicators for the contribution narrative.

Classifying individuals against a group-level minimum threshold carries unavoidable error: actual energy requirements vary from person to person within a sex and age group and cannot be observed, which is why FAO estimates the equivalent national measure as a population-level model rather than counting individuals. Read the value as a population share, never as a diagnosis of named individuals.

Intake measurement error is substantial: recall error, day-to-day variation, and food consumed away from home all bias estimates, and the direction of bias can differ by site; keep the instrument, respondent rules and survey season constant across waves.

Meeting the energy threshold is not the same as eating well: a person can exceed the MDER on a monotonous, micronutrient-poor diet. Interpret alongside the pathway's affordability and biofortified-grain indicators (KPI-OC09, KPI-OC08), which cover economic access to a healthy diet and the supply of biofortified grain, not diet quality.

Directly measured project values and the model-based national Fallback series are not comparable and must never be mixed in one trend line; a gap between them is expected and is not evidence of error.
subMetrics: Number of people in intervention areas meeting or exceeding the MDER. Formula: the numerator of this indicator as an absolute count of people, weighted with design weights that expand the sample to the zone-of-influence population, with the source of that population total named. This is the form in which CGIAR's standard indicator set carries the measure, so the count accompanies the share in institutional reporting.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E team / enumerators. Validation: project MEAL officer. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (per Calculation method above). Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 3 · Nutrition & food security — Reference sheet KPI-OC07

name: Change in per-capita biofortified grain available for consumption in CIMMYT intervention areas
resultsLevel: Outcome
primaryObjective: PO2 Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved).
cgiarImpactArea: Nutrition, Health & Food Security
sdgTarget: None. No SDG indicator measures availability of a nutrient-enriched staple. Nearest: indicator 2.1.1 (prevalence of undernourishment), whose estimation draws on per-capita national food availability from FAO food balance sheets but measures dietary energy, not micronutrients; and indicator 2.2.3 (prevalence of anaemia in women aged 15 to 49), which measures nutritional status, not food supply.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Common Results Framework: contribution evidence towards the impact-level standard indicator on the number of people meeting minimum micronutrient requirements. The match is partial and one-directional, since that indicator counts people against a requirement threshold while this one measures kilograms available per person, with no defined conversion between them. No donor reporting framework carries an equivalent per-capita availability indicator, so there is no further crosswalk to record.
definition: The quantity of biofortified grain available for human consumption per person per year in CIMMYT intervention areas, and its change relative to the baseline year. Biofortified grain is grain of varieties bred for a documented nutritional enhancement in the grain itself, covering micronutrient biofortification (provitamin A, zinc, iron) and protein quality, including quality protein maize, as distinct from nutrients added after harvest through fortification. Availability is the grain left for people in the area to eat once the quantities kept for seed, used as animal feed, lost after harvest, and moved out are taken out, divided by the resident population. It is a supply-side proxy: it shows how much nutrient-enriched staple is there to be eaten, not how much anyone eats or absorbs.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's biofortification work has put more nutrient-enriched staple food within reach of people where it works, rather than stopping at varieties released and seed distributed. Project management uses it to check that release and farmer adoption translate into supply; institutional reporting uses it as contribution evidence towards the CGIAR impact-level measure of people meeting minimum micronutrient requirements, which CIMMYT does not itself measure.
projectSpecificApplication: State the intervention areas covered, the crops and target nutrients or traits counted, the survey rounds used, and the baseline year the change is measured against. Do not alter the numerator and denominator construction, the unit, or the list of quantities removed from availability. Where a component cannot be observed (typically grain moved out of the area), state the assumption used and flag the value as partly estimated; raise feasibility problems with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining the indicator.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this value informs: for example a donor logframe outcome on nutrition-sensitive agriculture, or an adaptive-management trigger where adoption rises (KPI-OC10) while per-capita availability stays flat, pointing to grain being sold, moved out, or used as seed and feed rather than eaten.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose work is laboratory and controlled-environment research with no intervention-area population whose grain availability could be accounted
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose work is laboratory and controlled-environment research with no intervention-area population whose grain availability could be accounted.
unit: Kilograms of biofortified grain available per person per year; the reported change is expressed in kilograms per person per year.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more biofortified grain is available per person per year against baseline.
disaggregationRequired: Crop and target nutrient or trait are required disaggregations: crop (for example maize, wheat) and the target nutrient or trait (zinc, provitamin A, iron, protein quality), because kilograms of different biofortified crops are not nutritionally interchangeable and one pooled figure hides which nutrient gap is addressed. The register sets none; both cuts are CIMMYT's own, applied on the sheet's authority.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Source of the grain (own production; purchased or received within the area); agroecological zone; rural/urban; district or administrative unit within the intervention area.
unitOfObservation: Household
calculationSummary: Numerator: kilograms of biofortified grain available for human consumption in the intervention area in the reference year, calculated as grain harvested there, plus grain brought in, plus the net drawdown of opening stocks (or minus the net addition to stocks), minus quantities retained for seed, used as animal feed, lost after harvest, and moved out. For any seed, feed or loss term the survey did not observe, projects apply FAO's published coefficients where they exist for the crop and country, and otherwise nationally published figures, with the source named against every value; no central CIMMYT coefficient set is issued, since a wrong central figure would propagate silently through every value. Denominator: the resident population of the area in the same year, as the survey's weighted count of resident household members; on the Fallback route only, the census projection or national statistic named in Data source. Value = numerator / denominator, in kilograms per person per year; the reported result is this value minus the baseline year value. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1: a representative household or farm survey in the intervention area combining variety identification with production and utilisation measurement (harvest, opening and closing stocks, seed retained, feed, post-harvest loss, sales, purchases, grain moved in or out). It is the only source observing every term of the numerator and the population it is divided by. Fallback DS2 with DS4: partner, seed-system, and project records of biofortified seed distributed and area planted, converted to grain using documented yield assumptions (DS2), over a population figure from census projections or national statistics (DS4). Use only where a survey is not feasible, and flag the value as fallback-sourced and modelled, since the conversion assumes farmers planted, harvested, and retained the grain rather than measuring that they did. Not applicable DS3: satellite and GIS data map crop area but cannot distinguish a biofortified from a conventional variety of the same crop, and variety identity defines the numerator. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced and mobile data cannot verify variety identity, measure utilisation, or establish a population denominator.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which source role the project used, Recommended or Fallback. If Fallback, state why a survey was not feasible, which records supplied the grain estimate, which yield and loss coefficients were applied, and which population source was used.
collectionInstrument: For DS1: a crop production and utilisation module covering the reference year by crop and variety, plus a household roster for the denominator. Respondent: the member responsible for the crop plots, with whoever manages grain stores consulted on utilisation. Mode: face-to-face interview at a fixed point in the agricultural calendar. Because farmer recall over a long harvest period is a known error source, use physical measurement where resources allow (crop cutting or whole-plot harvest, and weighing of stored grain) and crop cards for crops harvested in stages, following Sapkota et al. (2016) for the crop-cut, whole-plot and crop-card methods. Where farmers cannot reliably name the variety, confirm identity on a sub-sample by genotyping or seed-lot traceback and report how it was done.
collectionFrequency: Baseline and endline; for multi-year programmes, a midline every 2 to 3 years. Hold the survey's position in the agricultural calendar constant across rounds, because grain stocks fall steeply between harvest and lean season.
reportingFrequency: Annually; between measurement waves, the latest measured value is carried forward with its year of measurement noted.
referencePeriod: One full production and consumption year covering all cropping seasons in the intervention area, compared against the same 12-month window in the pre-intervention baseline year.
baselineRequired: Yes. The indicator is defined as a change against a baseline, so without one there is no value to report. Fallback where no prospective baseline exists: recall-based reconstruction of the pre-project year's biofortified production and utilisation in the first survey round, flagged as such. If it is not feasible: report the level in kilograms per person per year as monitoring information, with no change claim.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Across projects: pool Recommended-sourced values directly; a project using the seed-records Fallback is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, never blended into it, since that value is modelled rather than measured.

B: Combination method. Pool at population level: sum the biofortified grain available across reporting projects and divide by the summed covered population, applying survey weights. Never average project-level per-capita values, which over-weights small intervention areas.

C: Levels and operations. A per-capita quantity is a ratio, recomputed at every level from its own numerator and denominator, never averaged from the levels beneath it: a mean of project per-capita figures weights an area of two hundred people equally with one of twenty thousand. The reported change is recomputed the same way, as the difference between two figures each built at that level, never as a mean of project-level changes. At Household, the kilograms of biofortified grain available over that household's resident members, with no change reported unless the household was measured in both rounds. At project level and at Regional / Aggregated, the summed available quantity over the summed covered population within the pooling domain of Block A, and the difference of that figure against the same construction in the baseline year. Also report: the denominator population, the number of households excluded under Eligibility, which components of the balance were estimated rather than observed and on what assumption, and the crop and target-nutrient composition, since a total that moved only because the crop mix changed is not a change in the availability of any one nutrient.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: no. This value is not a roll-up of the variety counts at output level (KPI-O06, KPI-O07, KPI-O09) or of the adoption share (KPI-OC10); varieties, farmers, and kilograms are different units, and the levels connect through the theory of change, not by arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage.
