dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role this project used, Recommended or Fallback; if Fallback, why primary collection was not feasible. Example: "Used Recommended: the project's own baseline and endline household surveys, 1,400 households per round."
collectionInstrument: The 8-item FIES survey module (FAO), household-referenced version, administered verbatim in the respondent's preferred language, with enumerators trained to hold respondents to the 12-month reference period and to the qualifier that experiences count only when caused by lack of money or other resources, not by illness, dieting or fasting. Respondent: the adult responsible for food preparation, or a randomly selected adult household member. Mode: face-to-face preferred; telephone acceptable. The survey-mode rule stands as CIMMYT's convention: modes are not mixed within a round, because mixed-mode administration within one round confounds the estimate, since a difference between rounds cannot then be separated from the difference in mode. The FAO SDG indicator 2.1.2 metadata does not state this rule; this toolbox requires it. The module takes under three minutes.
collectionFrequency: Baseline and endline; for multi-year programmes, a midline every 2 to 3 years. Hold the calendar timing of each round constant, because food insecurity is strongly seasonal.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Between measurement rounds the latest measured value is carried forward with its year of measurement noted; it is not re-estimated.
referencePeriod: The 12 months before data collection, which is the FIES recall window, compared against the pre-intervention baseline round.
baselineRequired: Yes: without a pre-intervention round the value describes a state and supports no change claim. Fallback where no prospective baseline exists: a subnational FIES round covering the intervention area in the pre-intervention period, household-referenced as this indicator is. Recall-based reconstruction is not acceptable here, because the scale already carries a 12-month recall and asking respondents to recall an earlier year compounds the error. If no fallback is feasible: monitoring only, no change claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Across projects: pool Recommended-sourced household records directly; a Fallback-sourced project is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, kept separate rather than blended in, since it sits at a different resolution and confidence level.

B: Combination method. Pool at household level using survey weights: the institutional figure is the weighted prevalence across the pooled household records of every project that reported through the Recommended source. Never average project-level percentages, which would weight a 300-household project the same as a 3,000-household one.

C: Levels and operations. The prevalence is recomputed at every level from the household records themselves, never averaged from the levels beneath it, and the recomputation is not a ratio of two counts: the numerator is a sum of model-estimated probabilities, so each project's Rasch model is fitted, and its local scale equated to the FAO global reference scale, round by round before the thresholds are applied, and a pooled figure is the weighted sum of those equated probabilities over the weighted total of households. Summing numerators computed on scales that were never equated produces a number with no scale behind it. At Household, each household's estimated probability of moderate or severe food insecurity; no prevalence is reported at that level. At project level, the weighted prevalence across that project's sampled households. At Regional / Aggregated and institutional level, the weighted prevalence across the pooled household records within the pooling domain of Block A. Also report: the denominator, the confidence interval, the number of households dropped for incomplete items, and the number of items common to the local and the global reference scale, since a value equated on fewer than four is not comparable with any other.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: No. This value does not combine arithmetically with the pathway's outcome indicators (dietary energy adequacy, affordability of a healthy diet, per-capita staple availability) or its outputs; those measure different constructs on overlapping households, and the levels connect through the Theory of Change not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: projects usually cover distinct geographies, so overlap is uncommon; where two projects' sampling frames overlap, pool only surveys whose frames partition the domain, or re-derive the design weights for the combined sample; where neither is possible, report the project values separately. Named overlap risk: the outcome indicators on dietary energy adequacy and on affordability of a healthy diet are measured on the same households, so one household improving on all three is one result, not three.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Missing data: a household missing more than two of the eight items is dropped from the denominator rather than imputed, since Rasch scoring needs the item set close to complete. This rule is CIMMYT's own convention, not FAO's, and the excluded share is a mandatory reported field alongside the value, because a prevalence computed after dropping a tenth of the sample is a different quantity from one computed on the whole.

Repeated observations: where a household is resurveyed within the same round, only the first completed interview counts. For an individual-level (SDG 2.1.2) figure: multiply each household weight by household size and recompute; do not rescale a household prevalence after the fact.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only. Food insecurity responds to prices, harvests, conflict, health shocks, social protection and labour markets; CIMMYT is one influence among many, and without a comparison group the counterfactual is unknown.

Measures the access dimension of food security as households experience it, not what they ate or its nutritional adequacy. A household can report no food insecurity here and still eat a poor diet. Diet quality and nutritional status are outside this volume: the register carries no dietary-diversity, food consumption score or coping-strategy indicator (HDDS, FCS, CSI), and no micronutrient-adequacy or anthropometric one, and two of the pathway's outcome indicators measure dietary energy sufficiency (KPI-OC07) and the cost of a healthy diet against household income (KPI-OC09). Read this value alongside those two, and make no diet-quality or nutritional-status claim from any of them.

Measurement error concentrates in recall and timing: the 12-month window, the seasonal calendar of the survey and the interview mode all move the value, as does courtesy or stigma bias in reporting hunger to an interviewer from a programme the household benefits from. Keep timing, mode and module wording identical across rounds.

Comparability depends on calibration. Raw item scores are not comparable across countries or scales; a value is comparable only once the local scale has been equated to the FAO global reference scale with at least four common items. Severe food insecurity is also a low-prevalence event, so at project sample sizes its confidence interval is wide and small movements are not signal. Report the interval with every value.

A fall in prevalence means fewer households reported the experiences that define moderate or severe food insecurity in that 12-month window. It does not mean CIMMYT caused the fall, that diets improved, or that the gain will hold through the next poor season.
subMetrics:
None. Moderate and severe are two thresholds on one scale, estimated in the same model, so they are disaggregations rather than separately calculated metrics. The severe-only prevalence is never added to the moderate-or-severe value, which already contains it.

Neighbouring sheets in the same pathway, for the results narrative rather than for arithmetic: the outcome sheets on the share meeting minimum dietary energy requirements, on affordability of a healthy diet and on per-capita staple food availability; and the output sheets on nutrition-sensitive information and training and on biofortified or nutrient-dense varieties.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Mission indicator, so roles are project-level. Data collection: project M&E team and the survey contractor or enumerator team fielding the FIES module. Validation: project MEAL officer, including the Rasch fit checks (equal item discrimination, absence of residual correlation, Rasch reliability) before any value is released. Calculation: the CIMMYT MEAL unit runs the Rasch estimation and the equating to the FAO global reference scale centrally, so the method is identical across projects and every value is comparable with the global series. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit, which pools and reports the institutional figure.
sourceRef: Volume 3 · Nutrition & food security — Reference sheet KPI-I02

name: Number of novel genetic elements (traits, genes, or markers) functionally characterised
resultsLevel: Output. Characterising an element and documenting its effect is a delivered result of the research process itself, not a change in another actor's behaviour, which is CIMMYT's MEAL Framework test for an output. Whether breeders take up the element, and whether varieties carrying it reach farmers, is the outcome question, answered by the downstream indicators in this pathway, not by this count.
primaryObjective: PO2 Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries. Contributing: PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient), since much trait discovery targets heat, drought, pest and nutrient-use traits serving sustainability and climate resilience rather than food security alone.
cgiarImpactArea: Nutrition, Health & Food Security: characterised traits enter breeding pipelines whose destination is productive, nutritious, resilient crops. The evidenced destination varies by trait class, and heat and drought traits point to Climate Adaptation & Mitigation; the pathway-wide rule sets the area by what the indicator measures, which is the characterised trait.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest target is SDG 2.5 (maintain the genetic diversity of seeds and cultivated plants, including through soundly managed seed and plant banks, and promote access to and fair sharing of benefits from genetic resources), but its official indicator 2.5.1a counts plant genetic resources secured in medium- or long-term conservation facilities. That is a conservation stock, not a count of elements whose function has been established, so there is no direct correspondence.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR results framework: no standard indicator counts characterised genetic elements. These results enter CGIAR reporting through two output categories it does define: Knowledge Product (an intellectual asset produced by CGIAR as an output of research and development activities, including data, databases and publications), where the characterisation is reported as a publication or dataset, and Innovation Development (a new, improved or adapted output with high potential to contribute to positive impacts when used at scale), where the element is packaged into something usable such as a validated diagnostic marker. CGIAR's minimum data standard records product type and peer-review status for the first, innovation type and readiness level for the second, so the same result is reported there in a different shape.
definition: Counts novel genetic elements (traits, genes or markers) whose function CIMMYT confirms through characterisation in the reporting year. A gene or marker element is functionally characterised when its effect on a defined trait has been experimentally validated and documented; a trait counted as the element itself, with no locus yet resolved, is functionally characterised when its heritable, transmissible expression is validated and documented in a defined genetic background. Either way, an experiment establishes what the element does, and the protocol, data and result are recorded so another scientist could trace them. Novel means the function was not already established and documented, by CIMMYT or by others, so re-confirming a published gene, marker or trait effect does not count.
rationale: Answers how much new, usable genetic knowledge CIMMYT produced in the year: which traits, genes and markers were shown to do something breeders can act on. It is the first measurable step of the crop improvement pipeline, telling management and donors whether the discovery stage is still producing validated elements, which indicators counting released varieties reveal only years later.
projectSpecificApplication: State the crops, trait classes and genetic materials the project works on, the discovery and validation platforms it uses (mapping populations, association panels, near-isogenic lines, gene editing, marker validation sets), the geographic scope of the trials, and where each confirmed element and its evidence are logged. Do not change the novelty test, the evidence threshold, or the once-per-element rule. If applying the indicator as defined is not feasible, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count serves: a grant with a discovery milestone, a pipeline review deciding which validation platforms to keep funding, or a partner agreement requiring reporting of validated genetic findings.
projectTypesNotApplicable: system change and transformation, and digital agriculture and AI
projectTypesRaw:
Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development.

Not applicable: applied agronomy and farming systems, seed systems and deployment, system change and transformation, and digital agriculture and AI, none of which characterises, conserves or genotypes germplasm.
unit: Number of genetic elements
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more genetic elements have had their function experimentally confirmed. One discovery is counted once at the element level regardless of how many objects it yields, so the value counts elements rather than the products of characterising them.
disaggregationRequired: Required: crop; trait class, on the toolbox's eight-class controlled vocabulary: yield and yield potential; abiotic stress tolerance (drought, heat, waterlogging); biotic stress resistance (disease, pest); nutritional quality (including biofortification); end-use and processing quality; agronomic and adaptation traits; and not trait-targeted (genome-wide characterisation, identity confirmation, diversity assessment). Not yet characterised does not apply: it is the class for uncharacterised genebank holdings (KPI-O14). Named traits are recorded at a second level within a class rather than instead of it, and an element whose confirmed function spans classes is assigned to the class that function serves and listed under the others in a secondary field, so trait-class subtotals may exceed the total and must never be summed. Also required: evidence tier (A or B), on the tiers in Eligibility criteria and missing data. The register requires crop and trait class only, so this cut is CIMMYT's own, applied on the sheet's authority.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Element type (trait, gene, marker); validation approach (mapping population, association panel, near-isogenic lines, gene editing, marker validation set); CIMMYT-led or partner-led; publication status; country or region of the validating trials.
unitOfObservation: The genetic element itself. This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation, whose definition names a genetic element; the compiled research record is where it is observed, not what is counted.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct novel genetic elements whose function CIMMYT confirmed and documented at Tier A or Tier B of the evidence standard during the reporting year. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: CIMMYT research and administrative records, that is the project's trait discovery and validation register, breeding and genomics platform records, laboratory and trial reports, and the institutional publication and dataset log, each entry carrying element identifier, crop, trait class, validation approach, evidence reference and confirmation date. Fallback DS4: secondary and international databases, that is CIMMYT-authored entries in bibliographic repositories and public sequence, marker and gene databases, used only where internal records are incomplete or the work ran through a partner whose records CIMMYT cannot access; such values are flagged as fallback-sourced and are timed by publication date rather than confirmation date, which shifts counts into later years. Not applicable DS1: the trials and genotyping runs that establish function are the evidence behind each entry, not a source for the count itself, which comes from the records those experiments generate. Not applicable DS3: gene, marker or trait function cannot be observed from geospatial or Earth observation data. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced data cannot establish that an element's effect has been experimentally validated.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether Recommended or Fallback was used, which register or repository supplied the element list, and how de-duplication against earlier years was done. If Fallback, state why the project's own records were not usable.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). The count is compiled from research and administrative records, not from an instrument fielded for the indicator; the record template carrying each entry captures the fields listed under Data source.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as research teams log confirmed elements with their evidence; compiled and de-duplicated annually.
referencePeriod: The reporting year, dated by when the validating evidence was confirmed to establish function, not by when the trials began; multi-year validation programmes report in the year of confirmation only. Confirmation is documented internal CIMMYT science-review sign-off; peer-reviewed publication is not required. On the Fallback route, where no internal sign-off is on record, the publication date of the CIMMYT-authored entry stands in for confirmation.
baselineRequired: No. An annual flow count starting from zero each reporting year; the first reported year is the reference point for trend context. Where a project wants a starting position, elements confirmed in the year before it began can be reconstructed from publication and platform records, with the caveat that reconstructed counts are less complete than prospectively logged ones.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool the elements evidenced in CIMMYT's own research records (Recommended); an element evidenced only in external bibliographic repositories or public sequence, marker and gene databases (Fallback) is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, not blended in, because publication-based counts are timed differently and miss unpublished confirmations; an element evidenced on both routes is Recommended-sourced and pooled, and the same project's Recommended-sourced elements stay in the pool. The alongside Fallback figure is reported net of elements already in the pooled Recommended figure, matched on element identity across years, not only within the reporting year, since publication typically lags confirmation by a year or more and an unmatched Fallback element would otherwise reappear the year after its confirmed, pooled year; where the match cannot be made, the Fallback figure is labelled an upper estimate rather than added as if distinct.

B: Combination method. Sum distinct elements across projects after de-duplication by element identity (crop, trait, and the gene or marker identifier or genome position, a genome-position key carrying the reference assembly name and version used to call it, for example wheat IWGSC v1.0 versus v2.1 or maize B73 v4 versus v5, since the same locus falls at different coordinates between assembly versions), so an element confirmed by two projects counts once institutionally. A marker or QTL with no causal gene resolved is keyed on its confidence interval on the named assembly: two records for the same crop and trait whose intervals overlap are one element unless independent validation shows two loci. Element type is recorded against the element and is not part of the key: a trait reported by one project and its underlying gene by another are one element where both records carry the locus. A record carrying a locus is never matched on crop and trait alone, since several genes can control one trait and each counts once; a pooled figure containing such a record with no locus resolved is labelled an upper estimate. A trait counted as the element itself carries no locus by construction and is exempt from that limb: it keys instead on crop, the named phenotype and the donor germplasm the trait was derived from (the accession or line identifier of its source), its own identity rather than a missing locus; the validating background is recorded as evidence, not keyed, so confirmation of the same trait from the same donor in a further background matches the existing record, and it is not on that account labelled an upper estimate.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying functionally characterised genetic elements for the reporting year. At institutional level, the de-duplicated sum of those counts, computed from the records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one functionally characterised genetic element is often reported by more than one project. De-duplication is on element identity, on the key set out in Block B, with element type recorded but not keyed. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the number excluded under Eligibility and why, and the number of elements reported alongside because they rest on the Fallback.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count does not add to the count of improved varieties released, the pipeline stage it feeds, nor to any outcome or impact value in the pathway; the levels connect through the theory of change as a narrative, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: de-duplicate by element identity across projects, partners and years before pooling, and where identity cannot be resolved (the same locus reported under two names) label the pooled figure an upper estimate. Two overlaps must be named and never summed: one discovery can yield a trait, an underlying gene and a diagnostic marker, and this sheet counts it once, at the causal locus where one has been identified; otherwise the marker or the trait, at the finest level the evidence supports, so the element-type breakdown is mutually exclusive and sums to the total, and the trait, gene and marker are never counted as three elements. A later resolution to the causal gene, for example when the gene behind a previously counted marker is identified, updates the existing record rather than creating a second count, on the same pattern as a Tier B to Tier A promotion; where the interval instead resolves to more than one independently validated causal gene, a routine outcome in clustered resistance loci, the first resolved gene updates the record and each additional independently validated causal gene under the same interval is a new element, counted in the year of its own validation and cross-referenced to the superseded record; where two or more are validated in the same reporting year, one of them updates the record and each of the others is a new element in that year. Accessions genotyped in the course of the work belong to the sheet on genebank accessions genetically characterised, a different unit.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: an element counts when its function is novel, meaning not already established and documented anywhere in the public record, by CIMMYT or by anyone else, and when project records hold (a) the trait effect claimed, or for a trait counted as the element itself, the phenotype claimed and the background it is claimed in, (b) evidence reaching Tier A or Tier B of the tiers below, with protocol and analysis identified, and (c) the date that evidence was confirmed, within the reporting year, or, on the Fallback route, the publication date of the CIMMYT-authored entry, within the reporting year. The search establishing novelty is recorded with the element: the databases and literature searched, the terms used and the date. Two prior reports do not defeat novelty: an orthologue whose function was characterised in another species, and a prior report of an unresolved QTL or GWAS hit over the same interval with no Tier A or Tier B evidence behind it; a later Tier A or Tier B validation of that interval is the element's first novel characterisation. A new marker or assay for a gene or locus whose effect is already established in the public record is not a novel element, whatever its own diagnostic performance: the function counted is the locus's effect, and a released marker panel or assay is counted, if at all, as a genomic tool under KPI-O11.

Evidence tiers, required by this toolbox: Tier A, function demonstrated by manipulation of the element itself, by knockout, complementation, allele substitution or an edited line, in the species the element is counted for, against a control differing from the manipulated line only in the element: a null segregant, a non-edited sibling or a near-isogenic comparator, shown in at least two independent events, edited alleles or mutant lines, each against its own control, and reported with effect size and its uncertainty; a single event or line is recorded at Tier C until a second independent event or allele confirms it. Evidence from manipulation in a different species, or against an unrelated wild-type or other confounded-background control, does not reach Tier A; it is recorded at Tier C, and is re-tiered when the effect is confirmed in the target crop against a control of this kind. Tier A does not apply where the element is a trait with no locus yet resolved, since there is no locus to manipulate; that case is evidenced under Tier B. Tier B, the effect confirmed in a population or panel independent of the discovery set and reported with effect size and uncertainty; for a marker, diagnostic performance (sensitivity and specificity, or an equivalent accuracy measure, with its own uncertainty) on an independent validation set; for a trait counted as the element itself, with no gene or marker yet resolved, heritable, transmissible expression demonstrated in a segregating population or sibling group independent of the discovery observation, in a defined genetic background, against a non-expressing comparator genotype in that same background, replicated across at least two independent environments or seasons, and reported with a segregation ratio or heritability estimate and its uncertainty, since there is no effect of the trait on itself to confirm. For the gene/QTL and marker limbs, the validation population or set shares no entries (lines, individuals or families) with the discovery set; independence below concerns relatedness, never re-use. Independence for the gene/QTL and marker limbs above is satisfied by either (a) a panel or set genetically distinct from the discovery panel, meaning a separate germplasm pool or breeding programme with no shared pedigree, or (b) a panel or set that may share ancestry with the discovery panel provided the association test applies a kinship- or structure-corrected model (a mixed linear model with a kinship matrix, Q+K or equivalent); for the marker limb, limb (b) does not apply, and diagnostic performance is established only on a set meeting limb (a), since relatedness inflates a marker's apparent accuracy and no model correction removes that. This independence rule does not reach the trait-as-element limb above, whose within-background segregating-population design has no discovery-versus-validation panel to test for shared ancestry. Tier C, a single-population QTL, a single-panel GWAS hit, a candidate locus, a single manipulated event or line, or manipulation evidence from a different species or against an unrelated wild-type or other confounded-background control, recorded and reportable but never added to the value. The tier reached is recorded for every counted element.

Repeated observations: an element counts once, in the year its function was first confirmed; further validation in more environments, seasons or genetic backgrounds strengthens the evidence without creating a second count, including evidence that lifts an element from Tier B to Tier A, which updates the recorded tier and not the count, and an element confirmed by two CIMMYT projects in one year counts once institutionally. An element characterised jointly with a partner is counted whole, not shared. The partner's role is recorded on the element's record, and the co-characterised share is reportable alongside the count.
limitations: Counts confirmations, not consequences: most characterised elements never reach a released variety. A rise means the discovery pipeline produced more validated findings that year, not that breeding gains or farm results improved; read it with the variety-release and genetic-gain indicators, never in their place.

The novelty test and the evidence tier drive the number, and the tier floor rests on a thin basis: this toolbox sets it at Tier A or Tier B because no cited standard sets one. The FAO Genebank Standards govern the evaluation of accessions and are explicitly not adopted here, two of the remaining sources govern reporting shape rather than method, and none defines a gene-function evidence threshold. Without the floor, and without a firm rule on what counts as previously documented, two teams can report the same year's work as three elements or thirty. Both rules must travel with the value.

The counting convention is set, not left to judgement, and must travel with the value: one discovery counts once, at the finest level the evidence supports, the causal locus where one is identified, otherwise the marker or the trait, so a complex trait controlled by many loci is counted once per independently validated causal gene rather than once for the trait as a whole. A value built on a different convention is not comparable without knowing which rule produced it.
Timing is a choice, not a fact: confirmation accumulates across seasons and locations, and publication-based counts lag record-based counts by a year or more. The two are never blended.

The value reflects where CIMMYT invests, not only how well it performs: crops and traits with richer genomic resources yield confirmed elements faster. The evidence tiers are also easier to reach for large-effect, single-gene loci than for the polygenic traits, yield, drought and heat tolerance among them, that carry most of CIMMYT's breeding value: Tier A manipulation is tractable mainly for major-effect loci and does not apply at all to a trait counted as the element itself, which is Tier-B-only by construction, and Tier B's required panel size grows as effect size shrinks, so the count under-represents polygenic-trait work and a falling value can reflect a deliberate shift to harder, polygenic traits rather than weaker science.
subMetrics: None. Element type, crop, trait class and validation approach are disaggregations of one de-duplicated count, not separately calculated metrics. Neighbouring indicators have their own sheets: platforms or tools released; genebank accessions genetically characterised; and improved varieties released, the pipeline stage this count feeds.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
Characterization and evaluation boundary: FAO (2014), Genebank standards for plant genetic resources for food and agriculture, cited only to mark a boundary, not as this indicator's method; FAO defines characterization as the description of highly heritable characters, by morphological descriptors or molecular markers, and uses evaluation for germplasm performance traits whose expression is environmentally influenced, measured in designed trials; neither FAO limb covers establishing a gene or marker's function by knockout, complementation, allele substitution or independent-panel replication, which is what this indicator counts; FAO's evaluation standards set evidence conditions for the evaluation of genebank accessions, not for the functional characterisation of genes or markers, so this indicator does not adopt them; the evidence threshold counted here is set by this toolbox, in the evidence tiers in Eligibility criteria and missing data, and is not drawn from these standards.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the breeding and genetic resources research leadership as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: research teams and platform leads logging each confirmed element with its evidence. Validation: project MEAL officer with the responsible scientist (evidence present, novelty checked against prior years and the public record, crop and trait class classified); borderline counting-unit cases ruled by the programme lead and recorded with the reason. Calculation: project M&E, applying the once-per-element rule; cross-project and cross-year de-duplication by the CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: project leader, with science-quality sign-off from the research lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 4 · Genetic resources, breeding & seed — Reference sheet KPI-O10

name: Number of genomic, phenotyping, or bioinformatics platforms or tools released
resultsLevel: Output. A released platform or tool is a delivered result of the research process, produced by the research team itself and not a change in another actor's behaviour, which is CIMMYT's MEAL Framework test for an output. Whether other scientists take it up is the outcome question, answered by the downstream indicators in this pathway, not by this count.
primaryObjective: PO2 Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries. Contributing: PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Nutrition, Health & Food Security. The pathway-wide rule sets the area by the object measured, which is a released platform or tool for crop improvement. Platforms built for climate-adaptive trait discovery also serve Climate Adaptation & Mitigation, but one Impact Area is recorded per indicator.
sdgTarget: None. SDG target 9.5 (enhance scientific research and upgrade technological capabilities) is the adjacent target, but its two official indicators measure national research systems, not research tools an organisation releases: 9.5.1 is research and development expenditure as a proportion of GDP and 9.5.2 is researchers per million inhabitants, both compiled for countries by the UNESCO Institute for Statistics. No SDG indicator directly corresponds to this count.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Technical Reporting: a released platform or tool is reported under the CGIAR Results Framework's output result categories, either as Innovation Development (with an innovation type and readiness level) or as a Knowledge Product, depending on its form. No CGIAR standard indicator counts research platforms or tools as such; the closest, "number of innovations profiled", counts innovations of every kind, and "number of other information products published in the reporting year" absorbs tools, toolkits, source code, websites and datasets into a single undifferentiated count that CGIAR's own review criticised for that reason. This is therefore a CIMMYT-defined indicator that feeds those broader CGIAR categories.
definition: Counts the genomic, phenotyping or bioinformatics platforms or tools CIMMYT releases for research use in the reporting year. A genomic tool reads or uses genetic material (a marker panel, a genotyping assay or pipeline, a reference genome assembly); a phenotyping tool measures plant traits in the field, greenhouse or laboratory (a sensor or imaging pipeline, a measurement protocol, a managed screening facility); a bioinformatics tool stores, analyses or serves the resulting data (software, an analytical pipeline, a database or data portal). "Released for research use" means made available beyond the team that built it, with documentation and stated access terms, whether the users are other CIMMYT scientists, national partners, or the wider research community.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT is building and sharing the research infrastructure that makes faster trait discovery and breeding possible: the countable entry point of the upstream science chain that runs on to genetic elements functionally characterised (KPI-O10) and improved varieties released (KPI-O12). Used by project management to track delivery of research-platform commitments, and by institutional and donor reporting to evidence CIMMYT's contribution as a provider of shared scientific capability rather than only of finished varieties.
projectSpecificApplication: State which platforms or tools the project released, the type of each, the crops or research problems they serve, and the intended user group. Do not change the unit, the release test, or the counting rule. If applying the indicator as defined is not feasible, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count informs, for example a donor-funded platform deliverable, or a milestone check: if a planned genotyping or data pipeline is not released on schedule, the downstream characterisation and breeding workplans are reviewed.
projectTypesApply: whose bioinformatics and data platforms are among the objects counted
projectTypesNotApplicable: seed systems and deployment, and system change and transformation
none of which releases a research platform or tool
projectTypesRaw:
Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; digital agriculture and AI, whose bioinformatics and data platforms are among the objects counted.

Not applicable: applied agronomy and farming systems, seed systems and deployment, and system change and transformation, none of which releases a research platform or tool.
unit: Number of releases (first releases and major versions); the number of distinct platforms or tools is reported alongside.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more releases, first releases and major versions alike, of genomic, phenotyping or bioinformatics platforms or tools were made obtainable for research use, with the number of distinct platforms or tools behind that figure reported alongside and never summed into it. It counts release and not uptake; no companion uptake measure exists, and that gap is named in Limitations.
disaggregationRequired: Required: platform or tool type, using the three categories in the title and definition (genomic, phenotyping, bioinformatics). The register records no required disaggregation for this indicator, so this cut is CIMMYT's own, applied on the sheet's authority: without it the count mixes products of very different kinds. A platform spanning more than one type, for example a pipeline that both genotypes and analyses the result, is assigned to the type its primary function serves and listed under the others in a secondary field, on the same pattern KPI-O10 uses for a trait-spanning element, so type subtotals may exceed the total and must never be summed. A platform whose type cannot be determined stays in the total under a not-available category.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Crop or research problem served; intended user group (CIMMYT internal, national research partners, open research community); access terms (open access, licensed, service-based); whether the platform was developed by CIMMYT alone or jointly with partners; country or region where a physical platform is hosted.
unitOfObservation: The release of a platform or tool: a first release or a major version, the platform or tool itself being the distinct item behind the count. This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of releases, a first release plus each major version per Eligibility's major-version rule, of genomic, phenotyping or bioinformatics platforms or tools that CIMMYT, alone or with partners, made available for research use during the reporting year, with the number of distinct platforms or tools behind that figure reported alongside. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: CIMMYT administrative research-output records, that is the project or programme output registry and the institutional innovation and knowledge-product records, each entry carrying the platform name, type, release date, access terms and release evidence, cross-checked against project technical reports. Fallback DS4: public repository and catalogue records (a research repository holding the release under a persistent identifier, code or data repository version records, or the published methods paper), used to reconstruct the count where CIMMYT's own release log is incomplete; any value built this way is flagged as fallback-sourced, because external catalogues do not reliably record which releases are CIMMYT's or when they became available. Not applicable DS1: this indicator counts institutional deliverables from records, not data collected from respondents or measured in the field. Not applicable DS3: satellite or aerial data may be an input to a phenotyping tool, but that describes the tool's content, not how this count is measured. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or citizen-generated data cannot verify an institutional release.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether Recommended or Fallback was used. If Fallback, state why the project's own output registry was incomplete and which external records were used to rebuild the count.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). The registry entry is itself the instrument: each record names the platform or tool, its type, the release date, the intended user group, the access terms or licence, and the release evidence.
collectionFrequency: Continuous: each release is logged as it occurs
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the release became available for research use: for a first release, the year the platform or tool first became available, and for a major version, the year that version became available.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual flow count that starts from zero each reporting year; there is no pre-project stock to establish, and change over time is read from the annual series itself.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: sum the releases evidenced in CIMMYT's own output registries (Recommended); a release evidenced only in public repository or catalogue records (Fallback) is reported alongside the summed figure with a note, not blended in, because external catalogues do not reliably record which releases are CIMMYT's or when they became available; a release evidenced on both routes is Recommended-sourced and summed, and the same project's Recommended-sourced releases stay in the sum. The alongside Fallback figure is reported net of platforms or tools already in the pooled Recommended figure, matched on platform or tool identity plus major-version designation across years, not only within the reporting year, since external catalogue records can lag an institutional release by a year or more; where the match cannot be made, the Fallback figure is labelled an upper estimate rather than added as if distinct.

B: Combination method. Summed: the institutional figure is the sum of qualifying releases across all reporting projects in the year, after de-duplication on the key in Block C, with the number of distinct platforms or tools behind it reported alongside. Never average project-level counts.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying releases of platforms or tools for the reporting year, with the number of distinct platforms or tools behind it reported alongside. At institutional level, the de-duplicated sum of those counts, computed from the records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one released platform or tool is often reported by more than one project. De-duplication is on the persistent identifier or repository handle where the qualifying record carries one, per Eligibility, together with the major-version designation recorded against it under Eligibility's major-version rule: a maintenance release carries the same major-version designation as its parent entry and matches it, one entry; a major version carries a new designation and does not match, a distinct entry. A platform jointly released and given a maintenance update (v1.2, then v1.2.1) therefore still matches on its full key and counts once. Where the repository mints both a version-independent identifier and a separate identifier per version, including a patch or maintenance version, such as a concept DOI alongside a version DOI, the key is the version-independent identifier plus that major-version designation; the full version-specific identifier is recorded as release evidence for that entry, never as the key on its own, since keying on the full version identifier alone would re-key the platform on every maintenance release the repository versions. Where the repository mints only a single, non-versioned identifier, name, type and the major-version designation are the documented fallback key. Where there is no repository at all, as for a genotyping or screening service, the key is likewise name, type and major-version designation, and the dated service or access agreement is the release evidence for that entry. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the number excluded under Eligibility and why, and the number of releases reported alongside because they rest on the Fallback.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count does not combine arithmetically with KPI-O10 (genetic elements functionally characterised) or KPI-O12 (improved varieties released); the three connect through the theory of change as a narrative: tools released, traits characterised, varieties delivered.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: three risks. Within this indicator, a platform released jointly by two CIMMYT projects, or hosted in more than one country, carries one release record and counts once, on the key in Block C, with coverage recorded as a disaggregation; where identifiers cannot be matched, label the pooled figure an upper estimate. Across the register, a released tool co-developed with a partner also meets the definition of KPI-O01 (innovations, including tools, co-developed with partners), and a released database or data portal open to staff across CIMMYT, or across an entire function or region, may also count under KPI-O50 (enterprise knowledge-sharing or data-sharing platforms CIMMYT establishes and maintains, an Institutional-branch indicator in a different results chain), so the shared identifier must mark it against both and institutional roll-ups must not present one product as two or three achievements. In CGIAR reporting, the same platform can be profiled as an innovation and separately published as an information product; report it once, under the category that matches its form.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: a platform or tool counts when it is documented and made available beyond the team that built it, evidenced by a dated release record such as a persistent identifier or repository handle, a versioned public release, a published methods paper describing the tool as available, or a signed service or access agreement. A genotyping or managed screening service CIMMYT operates counts as released on the same test: whether a user beyond the team that built it, inside or outside CIMMYT, can obtain the capability, not whether they can hold a copy of it. Co-developed platforms count once for CIMMYT, with the partner contribution documented.

Repeated observations: each release counts once, in the year it becomes available: a platform or tool counts at its first release and again at each later major version, and is not recounted in later years for continued availability or for maintenance releases. A version is major, and counts as a new release, when it changes what the tool can measure, produce or serve, for example a new capability, a materially different output, or support for new material, rather than only its internal implementation, and it carries its own dated release record: a persistent identifier or a versioned repository release, or, for a service-based platform, a dated service or access agreement recording the change, keyed under the no-repository limb of Block C; a version that changes only the implementation, or that carries no such record, is a maintenance release or bug fix and does not count, per the exclusions above.
limitations: Release is not use: a platform logged as released may be used by dozens of breeding programmes or by no programme outside CIMMYT, and this count cannot distinguish the two. The register carries no companion indicator measuring uptake of released platforms, so no indicator in this pathway measures use.

The counted unit is heterogeneous. A marker panel, a field phenotyping facility and an analytical pipeline are all one unit each, so raw totals are not comparable across projects until the type disaggregation is applied consistently, and a rising count does not mean rising scientific value.

The count is sensitive to how releases are logged: splitting a platform into its component modules inflates the figure, bundling deflates it, and versioning practice varies by product type. The distinct-platform identifier, the dated release-evidence requirement and the major-version test, which counts a materially new capability but not an implementation change, are the controls; read the count together with the list of platforms and releases behind it.

An increase means CIMMYT made more research infrastructure available in that year, not that trait discovery accelerated or that varieties improved. Pair it with KPI-O10 and KPI-O12 for the results chain, and never present the count alone as evidence of scientific progress.

Whether a change is a major version is a judgement, not a fixed test. Whether a change is a new capability, a materially different output, or support for new material, and so changes what the tool can measure, produce or serve, versus only refines how it does so, is a call the releasing team makes at release time; two teams could draw that line differently for a comparable change. The dated release-evidence requirement, a persistent identifier or a service agreement, is what keeps the call auditable rather than a matter of trust, but it does not remove the judgement itself.
subMetrics: None. The three categories named in the title (genomic, phenotyping, bioinformatics) are disaggregations of the same count, not separately calculated metrics. Related indicators in the results chain have their own sheets: KPI-O10 (novel genetic elements functionally characterised) and KPI-O12 (improved crop varieties released), the two outputs this count feeds.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
Definitional anchor: Wilkinson et al. (2016), The FAIR guiding principles for scientific data management and stewardship, the findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable vocabulary for what a well-shared research release looks like; this indicator's own release test is documentation and availability beyond the building team (Eligibility criteria and missing data), not FAIR compliance, which the sheet does not assess and the source itself sets no pass mark for.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the programme science lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project or programme research-output focal point, logging each release with its evidence. Validation: project MEAL officer, cross-checking the log against technical reports and repository records. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (de-duplication across projects and the institutional sum, per Aggregation rule). Approval: project leader or programme science lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.

name: Number of improved crop varieties released
resultsLevel: Output, per CIMMYT's MEAL Framework definition, which governs the register: the variety is a delivered result of the breeding process, and CGIAR's quality assurance guidance names new crop varieties and breeds among its output examples, while farmers' use of a released variety is the behaviour change of external actors and sits at outcome level. The divergence from CGIAR's control test is handled once in the crosswalk annex: the approval decision is taken by an external national or regional authority, and another CGIAR centre classes its equivalent count as an outcome.
primaryObjective: PO2 Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved) and PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Nutrition, Health & Food Security. The pathway-wide rule sets the area by the object measured, which is a released improved variety. Releases carrying stress-tolerance traits also contribute to Climate Adaptation & Mitigation, but the count is reported once, against the primary area.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator measures varietal release. The nearest, SDG indicator 2.5.1 (plant and animal genetic resources secured in medium- or long-term conservation facilities), measures ex situ conservation, which is KPI-O14's subject. SDG indicators 2.3.1 and 2.3.2 measure producers' productivity and income, downstream results of variety use.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR technical reporting: released varieties are reported under the Innovation Development output category (minimum fields: innovation type, readiness level, contact point), with a "genetic innovation" typology under which the number of new or improved lines or varieties is entered. The One CGIAR standard indicator set carries "Number of innovation profiles" under that category; the match is adapted, since CGIAR counts profiled innovations of every kind while this indicator counts approved varieties only. Another CGIAR centre runs a comparable released-variety indicator, which supports portability across centres.
definition: Counts variety releases in the reporting year, that is variety-by-country release events, of improved crop varieties carrying CIMMYT-derived breeding material, with the number of distinct varieties behind that figure reported alongside it. Release means official registration or approval by the competent national authority, or a regional authority whose listing confers legal availability without a further national act, following whatever testing that authority requires, which makes the variety legally available for seed multiplication and sale. CIMMYT's contribution is the germplasm, whoever bred and submitted the candidate; the release decision is the approving authority's. "Improved" means bred, rather than a landrace or a farmer selection.
rationale: Answers how many new improved varieties CIMMYT's germplasm delivered into national seed systems in the year: the point at which upstream science becomes something a farmer can legally obtain. It is the handover measure of the breeding pipeline, reported to donors and CGIAR technical reporting as a research output, and the base from which seed multiplication (KPI-O16), realised genetic gain (KPI-OC11) and the share of releases drawing on genebank material (KPI-OC14) are read.
projectSpecificApplication: State the crops covered, the countries candidates were submitted in, the partner institutions that held the release dossiers, and the records evidencing approval date and pedigree link. Do not change the release definition, the counting unit or the pedigree-traceability rule. If applying the indicator as defined is not feasible, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count serves: for example, a contracted release target for a crop and country, a stage-gate review of which pipelines are converting advanced lines into approved varieties, or a partner-facing report on breeding throughput.
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; seed systems and deployment.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, which produces genes, markers and characterised material rather than release candidates; applied agronomy and farming systems; system change and transformation; and digital agriculture and AI.
unit: Number of variety releases (variety-by-country release events); the number of distinct varieties is reported alongside.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more release events, one variety in one country each, of improved varieties containing CIMMYT-derived germplasm. Variety-country release events and unique varieties are reported side by side and never summed.
disaggregationRequired: Required: crop; trait class, on the toolbox's eight-class controlled vocabulary: yield and yield potential; abiotic stress tolerance (drought, heat, waterlogging); biotic stress resistance (disease, pest); nutritional quality (including biofortification); end-use and processing quality; agronomic and adaptation traits; and not trait-targeted (genome-wide characterisation, identity confirmation, diversity assessment). Not yet characterised does not apply: it is the class for uncharacterised genebank holdings (KPI-O14). Named traits are recorded at a second level within a class rather than instead of it. A variety carrying several traits is assigned to the class that justified its release and listed under the others in a secondary field; subtotals by assigned class sum to the total, subtotals that include secondary listings may exceed it and are never summed.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator. Variety is not a cut here: each release event is already one variety in one country, and the distinct-variety figure is reported beside the headline.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country and region of release; releasing partner type (national research system, university, private seed company); genetic unit (hybrid, open-pollinated variety, inbred line); whether genebank material entered the pedigree (feeds KPI-OC14).
unitOfObservation: The release event (one variety, legally available in one country by a national or a regional act). This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of release events in the reporting year meeting the inclusion rules. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: administrative and registry data, namely the official release or approval letter, gazette notice, or national or regional variety catalogue entry issued by the national or regional release authority, matched to CIMMYT breeding programme records (pedigree and breeding line identifiers, product advancement records) that establish the CIMMYT-derived material. Fallback DS4: published national or regional variety catalogues and seed-sector registers, each compiled by a third party rather than issued by the release authority, used where the releasing partner's own approval documentation cannot be obtained; flag values from this route as fallback-sourced, since published catalogues rarely record pedigree. Not applicable DS1: a release is an administrative act, not a condition observed from respondents or field measurement. Not applicable DS3: an approval decision is not observable from satellite or geospatial data. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or mobile data cannot evidence an official registration.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether Recommended or Fallback was used, name the authority or catalogue each release was evidenced from, and how the pedigree link was documented. If Fallback, state why the partner's approval documentation was not obtainable.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). No DS1 or DS5 route is listed for this indicator.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as national or regional authorities issue approvals; compiled, verified against pedigree records and de-duplicated annually.
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the official approval date falls, that date being the approving authority's decision date, read from the official release or approval letter, or from a gazette notice or catalogue entry that states it, never the date on which the notice or entry was published. A stated year of release with no fuller date establishes the reporting year on its own.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual count of events, so each reporting year starts from zero and the first year reported is the reference point for trend context. Any trend claim must state that the counting unit (release events versus distinct varieties) and the inclusion rules were held constant across the years compared.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Across projects: pool the release events evidenced in documentation issued by the release authority (Recommended); a release event evidenced only in a catalogue or register compiled by a third party (Fallback) is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, not blended in, since catalogue-sourced counts carry weaker pedigree attribution; a release event evidenced on both is Recommended-sourced and pooled, and the same project's Recommended-sourced events stay in the pool.

B: Combination method. Sum release events across crops, countries and projects after de-duplication on the identifier of the released entry plus the country of legal availability, so one variety approved in one country under two names or two licensees' brands is one event. The identifier is the cross identifier for a hybrid, or the line or population identifier for an open-pollinated variety, inbred line or population: two distinct hybrids sharing one parent line are two releases, never collapsed to one on the shared parent's identifier.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying release events for the reporting year, with the number of distinct varieties behind that project's own count reported alongside it. At institutional level, the de-duplicated sum of those counts, computed from the approval records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since a variety co-bred by two projects or two centres produces one approval both can legitimately report. The distinct-variety figure is de-duplicated on the identifier of the released entry alone, so it is never the sum of the country counts. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the number of approvals excluded under Eligibility and why, the number of release events that arise from a regional listing rather than a national act, and the number of release events reported alongside because they rest on the Fallback.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: no. This count is never added to KPI-O13 (elite lines advanced), KPI-O16 (varieties entering multiplication) or KPI-OC11 (genetic gain per year); the levels connect through the theory of change, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: varieties are frequently co-bred, so two projects, two crop programmes or two CGIAR centres can each report the same approval. De-duplicate on the identifier of the released entry plus the country of legal availability before pooling and count a jointly bred release once, naming the contributing programmes; where identifiers cannot be matched, label the pooled figure an upper estimate. Overlap with other register indicators must be named, never summed: the same variety reappears in KPI-O16 as it enters multiplication, may have been counted in an earlier year under KPI-O13, and forms the denominator of KPI-OC14, which must apply exactly the inclusion rules above. Its innovation entry in CGIAR technical reporting is the same event in another system, not an additional release.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: the released variety is itself a CIMMYT line or population, or CIMMYT germplasm appears in its pedigree as a parent or grandparent, the same maximum ancestry depth KPI-OC12 and KPI-OC14 apply, two generations; official registration or approval issued by the competent national authority, or by a regional authority whose listing confers legal availability without a further national act, dated inside the reporting year, making the variety available for multiplication. A generation is one cross or one line extraction, so for a hybrid the parents are the components of the final cross, and where a component is itself a hybrid its own parents are the grandparents. KPI-OC14's pre-breeding provision does not apply here. A release counts whoever held the release dossier; the dossier holder is recorded against the release, not tested. A regional catalogue listing that confers legal availability directly across member states, with no further national act required, counts as N release events, one per member state so covered; where a member state's own law requires a further national act before the variety may be multiplied or sold there, that act, not the regional listing, is the release event.

Exclusion: candidates submitted, in registration trials or undecided at year end; renewals, re-registrations, name changes, administrative transfers and extensions to a further zone of a variety already released in that country, whether or not in a year this indicator reported; advanced lines shared with partners but not submitted (KPI-O13); varieties whose pedigree link to CIMMYT material cannot be documented.

Missing data: an approval whose date cannot be established at all, not even to a year, is held out and reported alongside the count as unconfirmed rather than assigned to the current year; once confirmed, it is added to the year its approval date falls in, and a figure already reported for that year is restated under the Core's rules for restated values (Section 4.2); a release whose trait class has not been assigned stays in the total and is reported under the not-available category, which records a missing cut rather than a ninth class; it is not assigned to not yet characterised, which is a substantive class for material whose traits are not yet known.

Repeated observations: one count per released entry per country, whatever the number of approval decisions, names or licensees behind it, on the key in Aggregation rule Block B; the same variety approved in a second country is a new release event there and counts once only in the distinct-variety figure.
limitations: Measures delivery into the seed system, not use or benefit. A released variety is not yet in any farmer's field and some releases never reach multiplication. A rise means the pipeline converted more candidates into approved release events, not that farmers gained anything yet; read it with KPI-O16 and the adoption and turnover indicators.

Supports a contribution claim only. Release is decided by a national or regional authority, and the variety is usually the joint product of CIMMYT germplasm and a partner's selection, testing and dossier work, so more than one institution can legitimately claim the same release. Pedigree-based de-duplication therefore matters more here than in most output counts.

Counts are shaped by regulation as much as by science. Release systems differ in speed and stringency, so the same breeding work yields different counts in different countries. A regional catalogue listing counts once per member state it covers, so one listing can add many events in one year. Comparisons need the counting unit and inclusion rules attached.

Trait class is assigned, not measured. It comes from the breeding programme's own characterisation, most varieties carry several relevant traits, and programmes may classify the same variety differently.

The count is silent on who gains. Published reviews of seed metrics find that existing measures rarely track whether newly released varieties reach women farmers; pair this count with seed access and adoption indicators before drawing any inclusion conclusion.
subMetrics: None. Crop and trait class are disaggregations of a single count, and the distinct-variety figure is the same count under a different de-duplication rule. Related indicators hold their own sheets: KPI-O13, KPI-O16, KPI-OC11, KPI-OC12 (varietal age in farmers' fields) and KPI-OC14.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the breeding programme product management lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: breeding programme product managers and country or partner leads, compiling approval documents and pedigree records. Validation: project MEAL officer with the breeding data manager, confirming approval date, pedigree link and that the release is not a renewal. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: breeding programme director. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit, and onward to CGIAR technical reporting as an innovation entry.
sourceRef: Volume 4 · Genetic resources, breeding & seed — Reference sheet KPI-O12

name: Number of elite lines or breeding populations advanced through breeding pipelines
resultsLevel: Output. The advancement decision is a documented step of the breeding process itself, a delivered result of research activity rather than a change in what others do, whether CIMMYT takes it or a national partner takes it on CIMMYT material and CIMMYT holds the record. Whether external actors then register, multiply or grow the material is a change outside the research process, measured by other indicators in this pathway.
primaryObjective: PO2 Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved) and PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Nutrition, Health & Food Security. The pipeline supplies the improved varieties through which CIMMYT's breeding work reaches food security outcomes, the pathway PO2 describes. The register carries no Impact Area column; the value follows the pathway-wide rule, which sets the area by what the indicator measures.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest indicator under Goal 2 is 2.5.1(a), plant genetic resources secured in medium- or long-term conservation facilities, which counts accessions held ex situ rather than candidates moving through a breeding pipeline, so there is no direct correspondence.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR: the Innovation Development output category records innovation type and innovation readiness level for each reported output, and advancing an entry a stage is conceptually a readiness-level step; but the standard output indicator for that category is the number of innovation profiles, not a count of breeding lines advanced, so this indicator feeds those fields as supporting evidence rather than mapping one to one. Breeding Program Assessment Tool (BPAT, Gates Foundation and University of Queensland): cultivar advancement pipelines are one of its nine assessment components, the same object counted here, though BPAT scores the process rather than counting throughput. Donor reporting frameworks that stage research outputs by phase reached carry a close variant of this count; the correspondence is partial, since they report an item at the highest phase reached in the year while this indicator counts each documented stage transition.
definition: Counts elite lines or breeding populations advanced from one defined stage of a breeding pipeline to the next during the reporting year, by CIMMYT in its own pipelines or by national partners advancing CIMMYT material under a documented decision held by CIMMYT; it measures pipeline throughput ahead of release. A breeding pipeline is the sequence of testing stages a candidate passes through, from early-generation nurseries through multi-environment testing to entries nominated for registration trials. An elite line is a fixed or near-fixed candidate at advanced stages; a breeding population is a segregating population managed as one unit at earlier stages.
rationale: Answers how much breeding material CIMMYT moved forward each year, the step that connects trait discovery to variety release. It gives breeding programme managers and institutional reporting an annual signal of pipeline health years before a change can appear in variety releases (KPI-O12) or genetic gain per year (KPI-OC11), and shows whether enough advanced material is accumulating to sustain future releases.
projectSpecificApplication: State which crop programmes and pipelines the project covers, which stage transitions it counts, the geographic scope of the testing network, and where stage-gate decisions are recorded. Do not change the documented-decision requirement, the once-per-entry-per-year rule, or the exclusion of entries retained at the same stage; if the project's pipeline has no documented stage gates, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining advancement here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count serves: a donor milestone on pipeline delivery, a check that a trait-specific pipeline (for example heat tolerance) is generating enough candidates, or a trigger to rebalance testing capacity when advancement stalls at one gate.
projectTypesNotApplicable: the other five types. The unit is a stage-gate decision inside a breeding pipeline, and only a breeding project runs one
upstream discovery science supplies material to the pipeline but does not take the advancement decision
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development.

Not applicable: the other five types. The unit is a stage-gate decision inside a breeding pipeline, and only a breeding project runs one; upstream discovery science supplies material to the pipeline but does not take the advancement decision.
unit: Number of entries (elite lines or breeding populations) advanced
directionOfChange: Not directional. Throughput rises when selection intensity falls, so a rising count can mean a weaker filter rather than a stronger pipeline, and reading it as an intended increase would create a standing incentive to advance more material, which is the opposite of what a breeding programme optimises. Read together with genetic gain (KPI-OC11); see Limitations.
disaggregationRequired: Required: crop; trait class, on the eight-class controlled vocabulary set out on KPI-O10; stage transition (the stage the entry moved from and the stage it moved to); material type (elite line or breeding population), required so that a population's transition and a derived line's in the same year are reported apart. The register requires crop and trait class only, so these cuts are CIMMYT's own, applied on the sheet's authority. Stage structures are not shared across crops, so each programme declares its own scheme, in writing, alongside the value: maize, wheat and the smaller pipelines number and name their stages differently, a common scheme imposed across them would either carry no information or misdescribe most pipelines, and the declared scheme is what stops a number being compared across two schemes without the difference being visible.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Pipeline or product profile served; testing network, region or country; breeding programme; whether the entry draws on genebank-derived parent material (links to KPI-OC14).
unitOfObservation: Breeding entry (an elite line or a breeding population). This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation, whose definition names a breeding entry.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of unique entries with at least one documented stage-gate advancement decision dated within the reporting year. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: CIMMYT breeding programme administrative records, that is the breeding data management system, the record of entry identifiers, pedigree, trial and nursery assignments and, where the programme records them there, stage-gate advancement decisions with their dates. Fallback DS1: trial and nursery records compiled directly from the crop programme (trial books, season reports, selection lists) where the central system carries no stage flag; flagged as fallback-sourced. Not applicable DS3: a stage-gate decision is an internal management act, not observable from satellite, aerial or GIS data. Not applicable DS4: secondary and international databases hold released varieties and national registrations, not internal pipeline decisions. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or mobile data cannot record which entries a breeding programme advanced.
