dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether Recommended or Fallback was used, which system or records supplied the entry list, and how entries were de-duplicated across trials and pipelines. If Fallback, state why central breeding records could not be used.
collectionInstrument: For the DS1 fallback: a stage-advancement extraction sheet applied to trial books and selection lists, capturing entry identifier, pedigree, crop, trait class, material type (elite line or breeding population), stage moved from, stage moved to, decision date and the basis of the decision (trial performance, genomic prediction, marker-assisted selection or a combination); desk extraction, with the crop programme's breeding lead confirming the list in writing before it is reported. The DS2 route uses the standard advancement fields of the breeding data management system, where they are populated at the point of decision.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, each decision recorded when taken, in practice once per crop cycle per pipeline; compiled and de-duplicated annually.
referencePeriod: The reporting year, taking the date of the stage-gate decision. Where a crop programme's season calendar straddles the reporting year, the decision date sets the year, not the season the trial was grown in.
baselineRequired: No. An annual flow count starting from zero each reporting year; the first reported year is the reference point for trend context. A claim of improved breeding performance rather than volume belongs to KPI-OC11, measured against its own baseline.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool the entries whose advancement is evidenced in the breeding data management system (Recommended); an entry evidenced only in trial books, season reports or selection lists (Fallback) is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, not blended in, because reconstructed lists risk reading a retention as an advancement; an entry evidenced on both is Recommended-sourced and pooled, and the same project's Recommended-sourced entries stay in the pool.

B: Combination method. Sum unique entries across crop programmes and projects after de-duplication by entry identifier and pedigree, and always report the stage-transition breakdown with the total, since a total without its stage profile is not interpretable: an advancement out of an early nursery and one into registration trials are not the same event.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's unique entries with at least one qualifying stage-gate advancement in the reporting year. At institutional level, the de-duplicated sum of those counts, computed from the records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one advanced entry is often reported by more than one project. De-duplication is on entry identifier and pedigree, per Block B. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the number excluded under Eligibility and why, and the number of entries reported alongside because they rest on the Fallback.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count does not add to KPI-O12 (varieties released) or KPI-OC11 (genetic gain per year); an entry advanced in one year and released some years later is the same material appearing in two indicators at two levels, which connect through the theory of change, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: an entry tested by more than one project, region or pipeline counts once, with its pipeline recorded; where entry identifiers cannot be reconciled across crop programmes, label the pooled figure an upper estimate. The derived-line supersession rule (Repeated observations) applies across projects as much as within one: where a breeding population advances in one project and a line derived from it advances in another in the same reporting year to the same stage-gate, the pedigree link is resolved at de-duplication and only the line's advancement counts; where the two clear different stage-gates, the pedigree link is recorded and both advancements count as distinct events. Overlap with other register indicators must be named and never summed: nutrient-dense breeding lines counted here are also counted by KPI-O09, and entries whose advancement ends in registration cross into KPI-O12 in the release year.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: advanced means a documented stage-gate decision, taken against the crop programme's documented advancement criteria, whether on measured trial performance, genomic prediction, marker-assisted selection or a combination, that moved the entry to the next stage. The decision is taken and recorded by CIMMYT in its own pipelines, or taken and documented by a national partner advancing CIMMYT material with the record held by CIMMYT, and its record carries entry identifier, crop, stage moved from, stage moved to and decision date.

Exclusion: entries retained at the same stage, discarded, or still under evaluation at year end; entries advanced by partner programmes using CIMMYT material where no advancement decision is documented and held by CIMMYT, since counting them undocumented would make the figure unauditable; germplasm distributed without an advancement decision; varieties released, counted by KPI-O12.

Missing data: an entry whose stage moved from, stage moved to or decision date is found neither in the central system nor, through the DS1 fallback, in the programme's trial books and selection lists is excluded and reported as an unverified remainder rather than assumed advanced; an entry missing trait class, or missing material type, stays in the total under a not-available category on the missing field; an entry with a documented decision but no recorded basis for it (trial performance, genomic prediction, marker-assisted selection or a combination) counts, since the transition itself is what the indicator measures, and is flagged with the basis reported as not-recorded rather than assumed.

Repeated observations: one count per entry per reporting year, even where it cleared two gates; each transition appears in its own subtotal, so subtotals may exceed the total and must never be summed. An entry advancing again in a later year counts again in that year, so annual values are not cumulative. A derived line's advancement supersedes its parent population's count only where both clear the same stage-gate in the same reporting year: where a breeding population and a line derived from it both advance to the same stage in one year, only the line's advancement counts. Where the population and a line derived from it clear different stage-gates in the same year, both are distinct stage-transition events and both count; the material-type cut and the stage-transition disaggregation, both required, keep the population's own transition visibly separate from the line's.
limitations: Throughput is not quality. A higher count can come from a larger testing budget or from advancing a greater share of candidates, which lowers selection intensity, rather than from better breeding; read it alongside genetic gain per year (KPI-OC11) and releases (KPI-O12).

Stage definitions are programme-specific. Crops and programmes define and number stages differently, so values are comparable within one pipeline over time but not across crops unless the stage scheme is stated with the number.

The number moves when the gate moves. Merging stages, adding a gate or shifting an advancement threshold changes the count with no change in the underlying breeding, so the stage scheme in force must travel with the value and hold constant across years.

Not cumulative and not a forecast of releases. The same entry can advance in several successive years, and most advanced entries never reach release, so summing years or reading the count as varieties in waiting overstates it.

A rise means more material cleared its stage gates that year. Every counted decision is taken in a CIMMYT pipeline, or taken by a national partner on CIMMYT material and documented and held by CIMMYT, so this is a delivery count, not a contribution claim about farmers, seed systems or on-farm performance.
subMetrics: None. Stage transitions, crops and trait classes are disaggregations of the same unique count, not separately calculated metrics. A stage advancement rate (entries advanced over entries evaluated at that stage) would be a different metric with its own denominator and is deliberately not part of this indicator. Related indicators with their own sheets: KPI-O12, KPI-OC11, KPI-O09 and KPI-OC14.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the crop breeding programme leads as technical reviewers
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: crop breeding programmes, with breeders and data managers recording each stage-gate decision when taken. Validation: breeding programme data manager with the project MEAL officer, checking each record carries entry identifier, crop, both stages and a decision date. Calculation: project or programme M&E applying the unique-entry rule; cross-programme de-duplication by the CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: crop breeding programme lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 4 · Genetic resources, breeding & seed — Reference sheet KPI-O13

name: Number of genebank accessions conserved with long-term viability
resultsLevel: Output. Conserving accessions to standard is a delivered result of CIMMYT's genebank, not a change in behaviour, systems or practice. CGIAR's review of its own standard indicators reached the same conclusion about the equivalent accessions indicator, calling it an indicator of genebank output and advising that it move from impact to output level. Whether conserved material is then used by breeders is an outcome, measured by KPI-OC14. KPI-OC14's headline counts ancestry from any ex situ genebank and so is not a use rate on CIMMYT's own stock; its CIMMYT-genebank cut is the figure that reads against this one.
primaryObjective: PO2 Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries. Contributing: PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Environmental Health & Biodiversity. CGIAR places its own plant genetic accessions indicator here, and conserved crop diversity is the biodiversity CIMMYT directly safeguards. The cited CGIAR review is more critical than that placement suggests: it states the accessions count "is a measure of a genebank output and therefore is not an indicator of Environmental Health and Biodiversity impact", and adds that a better proxy for biodiversity could be defined, so the review questions the fit of the indicator to this Impact Area and not only its results level. The register carries no Impact Area column; the value follows the pathway-wide rule, which sets the area by what the indicator measures.
sdgTarget: SDG indicator 2.5.1, plant component (number of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture secured in medium or long-term conservation facilities), under target 2.5. The correspondence is direct in unit and object: both count unique accessions. The difference must be stated whenever the two are compared: SDG 2.5.1 counts accessions secured in medium- or long-term facilities, on the same base-collection scope this indicator uses, while this indicator additionally requires storage at base-collection conditions, a germination result at or above the regeneration threshold and a sufficient stored quantity, so the CIMMYT figure is a subset of the SDG holdings figure and normally lower.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR results framework: the standard indicator "number of plant genetic accessions available and safely duplicated" is the close variant; it bundles two variables that CGIAR's own review recommended separating, whereas this indicator measures conservation to standard only. FAO World Information and Early Warning System on plant genetic resources (WIEWS): the reporting channel for SDG 2.5.1, using FAO's mandatory passport descriptors (holding institute, accession number, scientific name, storage type). International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture and the Second Global Plan of Action for PGRFA: the FAO Genebank Standards support both, and SDG 2.5.1 counts are reported under the Global Plan of Action monitoring cycle; named here for context only, neither is separately cited, since the Genebank Standards already carries the operative content.
definition: Counts the genebank accessions that, at the reporting date, are held under conditions ensuring long-term viability, meaning viability-tested and stored to standard, whether on the accession's first germination test or after regeneration. It is a stock of conserved diversity at a date, not a count of the year's activity. An accession is a distinct sample of seeds, planting material or plants representing a wild population, a landrace, a breeding line, a breeding population or an improved cultivar (five terms, set out under Disaggregate by, the authoritative statement of the vocabulary), maintained as one managed unit. Conserved with long-term viability is a three-condition test against the FAO Genebank Standards at the reporting date, set out in Eligibility criteria and missing data.
rationale: Answers how much of the crop genetic diversity in CIMMYT's care is secured for future use to standard, not only held. Conserved diversity is the input to every variety CIMMYT later releases, so this stock is the starting point of the breeding pathway and the viability-verified subset of the holdings CIMMYT reports to FAO for SDG 2.5.1.
projectSpecificApplication: State which part of the collection the project covers (crops, taxa, storage type), the reporting date at which the stock is read, and whether the project deposited or funded accessions already inside the institutional total. Do not alter the viability conditions or the counting rule: a project reports its contribution as an identified subset of the genebank total, never as an additional count. If applying the indicator as defined is not feasible, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment the figure serves: a conservation grant with a securing-to-standard deliverable, a regeneration backlog the project was funded to clear, or a decision on where to direct regeneration and duplication effort next.
projectTypesNotApplicable: system change and transformation, and digital agriculture and AI
projectTypesRaw:
Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development.

Not applicable: applied agronomy and farming systems, seed systems and deployment, system change and transformation, and digital agriculture and AI, none of which characterises, conserves or genotypes germplasm.
unit: Number of unique accessions. The criterion is conservation to standard (storage, viability and stored quantity): safety duplication is reported as a companion figure alongside the count, never folded into the criterion (the operative counting rule for a safety-duplicated accession is in Eligibility criteria and missing data), because the two answer different questions, whether the material is alive and whether it would survive the loss of this facility, and a single combined number would let a fall in either look like a fall in the other. The companion figure is the number of accessions in the count that are also safety-duplicated, so the two published figures are the count and its duplicated subset; that subset is the closest CIMMYT figure to CGIAR's standard indicator, which also requires availability for distribution, a condition this sheet does not test. An accession is safety-duplicated where a sample of it is held at a geographically distant site under the same or better storage conditions, under a signed agreement with the repository (FAO standard 4.9.1 and its context text).
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more accessions are held under conditions meeting the long-term viability standard. It can also rise from undetected duplicates or from splitting existing accessions, neither of which adds conserved diversity; see Limitations.
disaggregationRequired: Required: crop; trait class, on the toolbox's eight-class controlled vocabulary: yield and yield potential; abiotic stress tolerance (drought, heat, waterlogging); biotic stress resistance (disease, pest); nutritional quality (including biofortification); end-use and processing quality; agronomic and adaptation traits; not trait-targeted (genome-wide characterisation, identity confirmation, diversity assessment); and not yet characterised. Crop is reported as the scientific name of the taxon. An accession stays in not yet characterised (no genetic or trait characterisation on record) until KPI-O15 records a qualifying characterisation, which normally files it under not trait-targeted, or a documented evaluation assigns it the class of the trait evaluated; an accession documented for traits in more than one class is reported under each and counted once in the headline, so class subtotals can exceed the headline and are never summed to it.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Storage type (seed, field, in vitro, cryopreserved), already a mandatory descriptor for SDG 2.5.1 reporting and so free to record; safety-duplication status; class of accession (biological status), on this pathway's own five-term vocabulary, adapted from the SDG 2.5.1 metadata's four-term definition of an accession (wild population, landrace, breeding line, improved cultivar), to which this pathway adds breeding population: a wild population, a landrace, a breeding line, a breeding population (including synthetics and other heterogeneous non-released populations) or an improved cultivar, matching Definition, with crop wild relative recorded as an optional second-level tag within wild population for material identified to a named crop's wild relative species, and with an accession whose class is not recorded reported under a not-available category; country of origin; base versus active collection.
unitOfObservation: Accession (a distinct sample of seeds, planting material or plants maintained in the genebank as one managed unit). This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of unique accessions qualifying under Eligibility criteria and missing data at the reporting date. This is a stock at the reporting date, not an annual flow. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: genebank management and registry records, that is the accession register with holding institute code and accession number, storage condition logs, germination test results and dates, regeneration records, seed inventory quantities, and safety duplication agreements. Comparator DS4: FAO WIEWS, the SDG 2.5.1 plant component series (https://www.fao.org/wiews/en/), or a published holdings portal such as Genesys (https://www.genesys-pgr.org), one of the published systems through which SDG 2.5.1 data reach FAO, used to place the count against CIMMYT's own prior SDG 2.5.1 submission, read at that submission's vintage; these report holdings rather than viability-verified holdings, and are never pooled and never reported as a KPI-O14 value. Where the genebank system cannot produce a verified extract at the reporting date, no value is reported for that collection and date. Not applicable DS1: no respondent population or field measurement produces this count; the germination tests underneath it are laboratory operations recorded in the genebank's own system, which is DS2. Not applicable DS3: the conservation status of a seed sample in a cold room is not observable from satellite, aerial or GIS data. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or mobile data cannot establish that an accession meets storage, viability and quantity standards.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State the extract date and how the count was de-duplicated.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). The count is compiled from genebank management records (DS2); the measurement underneath those records is a germination test conducted under the FAO Genebank Standards.
collectionFrequency: Continuously in the genebank management system, as accessions are acquired, tested, regenerated and duplicated. Germination tests follow each accession's own schedule: one third of the time predicted for viability to fall to the threshold, never longer than 40 years, and where no prediction exists, 10 years for long-lived and 5 years or less for short-lived species held at minus 18 degrees Celsius in sealed containers.
reportingFrequency: Annually, extracted at a fixed reporting date held constant across years.
referencePeriod: A single reporting date, not a span. The value is the stock standing on that date, and the date travels with the figure.
baselineRequired: Yes for any statement about change, but a prospective baseline is never a constraint here: the genebank's accession register supplies earlier stocks retrospectively. Where records are incomplete: the FAO SDG 2.5.1 series, which carries international centre holdings from a June 2014 reference point, labelled as a holdings baseline. If neither is feasible: report the stock and make no change claim.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: normally one institutional figure produced by the genebank, not a sum of project figures, with projects reporting their accessions as an identified subset of that total. Where more than one collection reports, pool Recommended-sourced records into one de-duplicated count (Block B).

B: Combination method. The institutional figure is the de-duplicated count of accessions meeting the conditions across all CIMMYT genebank collections at a common reporting date.

C: Levels and operations. This is a stock read at a common reporting date, not a flow through the year, and the distinction governs every level. At collection level, the count of accessions qualifying under Eligibility on that date, with the share counted under an overdue-retest flag beside it. At institutional level, the de-duplicated count across CIMMYT's collections at the same date, computed from the genebank documentation system rather than by adding collection figures, since safety duplicates and material held in both a base and an active collection are one accession. There is no project-level figure to add in: a project reports its accessions as an identified subset of the institutional total, never as a further count. Successive years are never summed and their difference is not an achievement, but the net of three movements that change independently: accessions newly qualifying; registered accessions ceasing to qualify; and register changes, where duplicates are detected or accessions are split, merged or removed from the register. An overdue retest moves only the flag, never the count. Also report: the reporting date itself, the three movements behind any year-on-year change, the number of accessions held below base-collection storage conditions, the number held but not verified to standard, the number conserved only as field, in vitro or cryopreserved material, the number of accessions due for regeneration on a viability trigger and, as a separate figure, the number due on a stored-quantity trigger, with the number meeting both, the share of the count resting on a surrogate initial viability value, the viability thresholds applied, each with its scale (per cent germination or per cent of initial viability), the number of accessions counted on it and the allowance, if any, that produced it, and the number of accessions in the count that are also safety-duplicated, as the companion figure.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This stock does not add to KPI-OC14 (a ratio) or KPI-O12 (an annual flow of a different object); the levels connect as a narrative through the theory of change, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: de-duplicate by holding institute code plus accession number, the identifiers FAO requires for SDG 2.5.1. One accession in several storage forms counts once, and an accession and its safety duplicate count once, at the depositing genebank. Undetected duplicate accessions cannot be removed by identifier matching alone, so where no duplicate-detection review has been run, label the figure an upper estimate. Overlap with KPI-O15 (accessions genetically characterised) must be named and never summed: O15 counts accessions characterised during a year, both CIMMYT-held accessions, which overlap this stock, and partner-held accessions outside it.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: accessions in the base collection, and accessions in an active collection only where, in the absence of a base collection for that species, that active collection also performs the base-collection function (FAO's rule for SDG 2.5.1) and is stored to base-collection conditions. All three FAO conditions must hold at the reporting date: base-collection storage (minus 18 degrees Celsius and 15 per cent relative humidity, each plus or minus 3, FAO standard 4.2.3); a most recent germination test at or above the regeneration threshold of 85 per cent of initial viability; or, for a genetically homogeneous accession, typically an inbred line or a pure-line cultivar, whose viability has declined through storage, a reading below that threshold where plant establishment during regeneration remains adequate, evidenced by a curator's determination recorded against the accession, with its date and the germination reading it rests on (without that record the 85 per cent default applies), homogeneity being the test and not the recorded class, so an open-pollinated variety, a synthetic or another heterogeneous population does not qualify for this allowance whatever its class (the examples named and this application of FAO's distinction between homogeneous and heterogeneous samples are CIMMYT's own), and FAO directs that the 85 per cent standard be adhered to for heterogeneous samples; or, for a landrace, a wild-population accession or another specific accession that cannot reach 85 per cent germination even in newly regenerated seed, a physiological ceiling, a lower species- or accession-specific threshold the curator has documented on that basis alone, with no plant-establishment condition attached (FAO, 2014); the curator documents two values separately, a lower initial acceptance value in per cent germination (standard 4.3.2) and a regeneration trigger in per cent of initial viability (standard 4.3.4), and the threshold applied is always stated with its scale; both allowances rest on FAO standards 4.3.2 and 4.3.4 and the context text of section 4.3; and a stored quantity sufficient for at least three sowings of a representative population. Whether that test falls within the accession's scheduled monitoring interval is not a condition of inclusion; it sets the currency flag under Missing data. Initial viability is that of the seed lot in storage; the entry test of a regenerated lot is that lot's initial test and replaces the earlier reference. Initial viability, whether a true initial test or, where none is on record, the first recorded test standing in for it, must itself reach 85 per cent germination, FAO's initial value for most cultivated species, or the curator's documented lower species- or accession-specific value; an accession whose initial viability falls below that value is excluded and reported with the viability-trigger figure, whatever its later tests read. An accession at exactly 85 per cent qualifies, which is CIMMYT's own harmonisation of FAO's wording: standard 4.3.2 says the initial value should exceed 85 per cent, standard 4.4.1 triggers regeneration when viability drops below 85 per cent of initial viability, and the Glossary entry for the regeneration standard says at or below, so this sheet follows numbered standard 4.4.1 for the threshold and, for the initial value, reads "reach" where 4.3.2 reads "should exceed". A surrogate initial value taken later than the true initial test anchors the accession's own regeneration threshold at whatever that later, and typically lower, test read, so two otherwise identical accessions can qualify at different absolute germination depending on when their surrogate was taken; the share of the count resting on a surrogate initial value is flagged and reported with the value, on the same pattern as the overdue-retest flag.

Exclusion: newly acquired accessions not yet cleaned, dried and given an initial germination test, within 12 months of receipt, the allowance FAO standard 4.3.1 sets for that first test; accessions below the viability threshold, or whose initial viability falls below FAO's initial value or the curator's documented lower value, due for regeneration on a viability trigger; and accessions below the three-sowings stored quantity due for regeneration on a stored-quantity trigger; both due for regeneration but reported as two separate figures beside the count, since the first is active allele loss and the second is a stock-management state that, for a rarely requested accession, carries no loss of viability (FAO accepts low seed numbers for such accessions), and bundling them into one regeneration backlog can read a large wild-relative holding as a large deterioration backlog when nothing is deteriorating; an accession meeting both triggers is reported in the viability-trigger figure, and the number meeting both is stated beside the two figures; held but not verified is reserved for accessions with no test at all once that 12-month allowance has expired, so a newly acquired accession still inside its allowance is never counted as held but not verified; material held only in an active (medium-term) or distribution collection where a base collection exists for that species (FAO standards 4.2.3 and 4.2.4), FAO issuing numbered storage standards for base (long-term) and active (medium-term) collections only and treating short-term holding within the active-collection concept, in its Glossary entry for an active collection, so a short-term or distribution holding is handled here as an active-collection holding; "for that species" is this sheet's own operationalisation of which base collection controls, CIMMYT's own convention rather than FAO's explicit wording; accessions held below base-collection storage conditions, whether a base-collection accession whose storage has fallen out of tolerance or an active collection standing in for an absent base collection without being stored to base-collection conditions, reported as a further separate figure beside the count, since SDG 2.5.1 counts this material in a medium- or long-term facility and this indicator does not; accessions conserved only as field, in vitro or cryopreserved material, which the germination and stored-quantity conditions (FAO's standards for orthodox seed) cannot test, reported as a separate figure beside the count by storage type and never as held but not verified; safety duplicates CIMMYT holds on deposit for another institution, which belong to the depositor's count.

Missing data: an accession whose scheduled retest is overdue is counted, with a flag, and the flagged share is reported with the value, so that a monitoring backlog is visible rather than appearing as a smaller collection; an accession with no germination result on record at all, once its 12-month new-acquisition allowance has expired, is excluded and reported alongside the count as held but not verified to standard, except an accession conserved only as field, in vitro or cryopreserved material, which Exclusion reports by storage type, and an accession received in a quantity too small to test and under its first regeneration, which is reported within the stored-quantity regeneration figure. Viability is never imputed.

Repeated observations: one count per accession at each reporting date, whatever the number of storage forms hold it, and an accession safety-duplicated elsewhere counts once, at CIMMYT.
limitations: Counts managed units, not genetic diversity. Undetected duplicate accessions raise the number without adding diversity, and detecting them lowers it without any loss; splitting or merging accessions moves the figure the same way. Year-on-year changes need an explanation of what drove them, not a value alone.

Viability is only as current as the last test. An accession that has deteriorated since its last germination test still counts until the next test detects it, so the figure overstates the collection by an amount that depends on how well the monitoring schedule is kept; the overdue-retest share reported with the value is the measure of that.

Comparability across crops and genebanks is limited. FAO's 85 per cent default applies to heterogeneous material such as wild species and landraces as much as to any other; below it FAO grants two separately conditioned allowances, one for genetically homogeneous accessions conditioned on plant establishment during regeneration and one, set by the curator on a documented physiological ceiling, for material that cannot reach 85 per cent even in newly regenerated seed, and neither is a blanket wild-material or landrace exception. Seed storage behaviour also differs by species, so two totals are not strictly like for like; the thresholds applied, and the allowance, if any, that produced each, travel with the figure. SDG 2.5.1 also counts material held in medium- or long-term facilities below base-collection storage conditions, which this indicator excludes, so the SDG figure runs higher.

A rise means CIMMYT is securing more material to standard, not that any user benefited. Conservation yields benefit only through use, so read this alongside KPI-OC14. This is also a stock at a date, not annual production, so annual values must never be summed.

What drives the number is as much acquisition and regeneration policy as conservation performance. A genebank that acquires aggressively adds accessions that sit outside the count until tested and, where needed, regenerated, so holdings grow ahead of the count; one that defers retesting keeps a larger overdue-retest share rather than a smaller stock, and one that defers regeneration keeps more accessions outside it. Read the count together with the overdue-retest share and the acquisition trend, not as a single unqualified performance signal.
subMetrics: None. The three conservation conditions are inclusion criteria applied to one count, and the overdue-retest flag is a reported share of it; storage type and safety-duplication status are disaggregations. Related indicators have their own sheets: KPI-O15 (accessions genetically characterised), KPI-OC14 (percentage of varietal releases utilising conserved genetic resources), and KPI-O12 (improved crop varieties released).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the CIMMYT germplasm bank as technical owner of the method
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: genebank curators and laboratory staff (germination tests, regeneration, storage and inventory records). Validation: the genebank's documentation or data manager (identifiers complete, test dates within schedule, storage type recorded). Calculation: the genebank's data manager, per the calculation method above. Approval: the genebank head or designated approver. Reporting: genebank focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit. The genebank's SDG 2.5.1 submission to FAO WIEWS is the holdings list that indicator defines, not this count.
sourceRef: Volume 4 · Genetic resources, breeding & seed — Reference sheet KPI-O14

name: Number of genebank accessions genetically characterised
resultsLevel: Output. Genotyping genebank accessions, CIMMYT's own and the partner-held accessions it characterises, and recording the results is a delivered result of the research process, produced by CIMMYT staff and contracted laboratories themselves and not a change in another actor's behaviour, which is CIMMYT's MEAL Framework test for an output. Whether breeders then use the information is the outcome question, answered at KPI-OC14, not by this count.
primaryObjective: PO2 Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries. Contributing: PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Environmental Health & Biodiversity. What is measured is the documentation of conserved crop genetic diversity, and CGIAR places its own plant genetic accessions indicator in this Impact Area (a placement CGIAR's own standard-indicator review questions, since it treats a genebank output as an impact indicator; the tag records the area the output serves). The pathway-wide rule sets the area by the object measured, which is the documented accession; a ruling by contribution pathway would instead choose Nutrition, Health & Food Security, matching the primary objective.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest target is SDG 2.5 (maintain the genetic diversity of seeds and cultivated plants, including through soundly managed seed and plant banks), but its official indicator 2.5.1(a) counts plant genetic resources secured in medium or long-term conservation facilities: accessions conserved, which is KPI-O14, not accessions characterised. No SDG indicator measures characterisation.
otherFrameworks: FAO Genebank Standards for Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture, endorsed by the FAO Commission on Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture: sections 4.5 (orthodox seed collections) and 5.6 (field collections) set characterisation standards, including the benchmark that around 60 per cent of accessions be characterised within five to seven years of acquisition or during the first regeneration cycle, using internationally agreed descriptor lists with data made publicly available. The 60 per cent within five to seven years benchmark is standard 4.5.1 and belongs to orthodox seed collections only; the field-collection standard 5.6.1 reads "All accessions should be characterized". Both are reported against, each labelled with the collection type it applies to, and this indicator's molecular-only share is reported against them as a lower bound. The share is computed on the whole registered collection at the reporting date, while standard 4.5.1 is a rate within five to seven years of acquisition, so the acquisition-year reading is given under Sub-metrics. CGIAR: the standard indicator set carries no characterisation indicator and the reporting fields carry no accession-level record, so there is no counterpart to report into. No donor reporting framework carries a genebank counterpart either.
definition: Counts genebank accessions whose genetic makeup CIMMYT characterises in the reporting year, meaning accessions genotyped or sequenced to document their genetic composition for use in breeding. An accession is a distinct sample of seed, planting material or plants held in a genebank, representing a wild population, a landrace, a breeding line, a breeding population or an improved cultivar (the five-term vocabulary set out on KPI-O14). The international genebank standards treat characterisation as description of germplasm by highly heritable traits, through either morphological descriptors or molecular methods; because this definition rests on genetic composition, the indicator counts only the molecular route.
rationale: Answers how much of CIMMYT's conserved genetic diversity was genetically documented in the year, for genebank management, breeding programme planning, and institutional and donor reporting. Conservation alone does not make an accession usable: a stored sample whose genetic composition is unknown cannot be deliberately chosen as a parent, so characterisation turns a conserved collection into a searchable resource for breeders. It links accessions conserved (KPI-O14) to the share of variety releases drawing on conserved genetic resources (KPI-OC14), and the FAO genebank standards set it as an expectation of every genebank. It also feeds variety release (KPI-O12), as the register records: characterisation is what lets a breeder choose a conserved accession as a parent, and a release KPI-O12 counts that draws on it is read as ancestry at KPI-OC14.
projectSpecificApplication: State which collections and crops the project characterises, the volume and timing planned, and the laboratory doing the genotyping. Do not change the accession-level counting unit, the molecular-characterisation boundary, or the quality-control and identifier requirements; if applying the indicator as defined is not feasible, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count serves: a genetic resources or pre-breeding grant with a characterisation deliverable, a targeted screen of landraces or crop wild relatives, or a decision on where to direct the next round of sequencing investment.
projectTypesNotApplicable: system change and transformation, and digital agriculture and AI
projectTypesRaw:
Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development.

Not applicable: applied agronomy and farming systems, seed systems and deployment, system change and transformation, and digital agriculture and AI, none of which characterises, conserves or genotypes germplasm.
unit: Number of unique accessions
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more accessions have their genetic composition documented and available to breeding. First characterisation only is counted, so re-genotyping an accession already characterised does not raise the value; see Limitations for why the annual flow must eventually fall even at constant effort as the collection becomes covered.
disaggregationRequired: Required: crop; trait class, on the toolbox's eight-class controlled vocabulary set out on KPI-O10. Genome-wide characterisation, identity confirmation and diversity assessment take the vocabulary's not trait-targeted class. Not yet characterised does not apply: it is the class for uncharacterised genebank holdings (KPI-O14). In practice most of the count falls into not trait-targeted, because the sheet's own minimum for a qualifying characterisation, the genebank's documented standard assay for the crop, is normally a genome-wide or identity-confirmation assay rather than one targeting a named trait. Also required: holding genebank (CIMMYT collection or the named partner genebank), so the count for CIMMYT's own collection is always reportable separately, including for the FAO-benchmark view. Also required: method (marker panel, genotyping by sequencing, whole-genome sequencing), since figures from different assays are not comparable (Limitations). The register requires crop and trait class only, so these two cuts are CIMMYT's own, applied on the sheet's authority.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Accession type, on the five-term class-of-accession vocabulary set out on KPI-O14, with crop wild relative recorded as an optional second-level tag within wild population, matching KPI-O14 and KPI-OC14; collection (base or active); sampling scheme (individuals sampled per accession, bulked or individual); region of origin.
unitOfObservation: The individual genebank accession. This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation, whose definition names a genebank accession.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct genebank accessions whose genetic characterisation was completed in the reporting year and qualifies under Eligibility criteria and missing data. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: the genebank documentation system with genotyping laboratory records, including a project's own genotyping records filed against the accession identifier, giving per accession the identifier, crop, date, method or platform, quality control outcome and data location. It is the by-product of genebank operations and the only source confirming both that the work was done and which accession it was done on. Fallback DS4: published genetic resources data portals carrying accession-level genotypic data for CIMMYT collections for work CIMMYT carried out or commissioned, used only where in-house records are incomplete or CIMMYT commissioned a partner institution to run the work and CIMMYT cannot access its records; such values are flagged as fallback-sourced and normally undercount, since not all characterisation data is published and publication lags the work. Not applicable DS1: no survey or field measurement is fielded for this indicator, the laboratory assay being an operational activity whose results reach the indicator through genebank records. Not applicable DS3 and DS5: laboratory characterisation of stored germplasm cannot be observed from satellite or geospatial data, and crowdsourced data cannot establish that a specific accession was genotyped to standard by CIMMYT.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether Recommended or Fallback was used, which system supplied the accession list, and how duplicates were removed. If Fallback, state why genebank and laboratory records were not usable and note the expected undercount.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). Both routes read existing records; the laboratory protocol (assay, plants sampled per accession, quality control thresholds) is documented by the genebank.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as the genebank and its laboratories record completed characterisations against accession identifiers; compiled and de-duplicated annually.
referencePeriod: The reporting year: characterisation completed, quality-checked and recorded within it.
baselineRequired: No. An annual flow count starting from zero each reporting year. Where coverage of the collection is stated, the reference point is the Sub-metrics share computed at the start of the period, on the accessions registered at that date, from the genebank documentation system; if that share cannot be reconstructed, coverage claims are not reportable.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: characterisation is normally run centrally, so most values come from the Recommended source; a project's own genotyping records are Recommended DS2 once filed in the genebank documentation system against the accession identifier, and pooled after de-duplication by holding institute code plus accession number, and a portal-derived fallback value is reported alongside rather than blended in. The route is decided per record, not per project: a project whose records come partly from each route pools its Recommended-sourced records and reports the rest alongside. The alongside Fallback figure is reported net of accessions already in the pooled Recommended figure, matched on holding institute code plus accession number across years, not only within the reporting year, since published portal data can lag an in-house record by a year or more; where the match cannot be made, the Fallback figure is labelled an upper estimate rather than added as if distinct.

B: Combination method. Sum distinct accessions after de-duplication by holding institute code plus accession number, so an accession characterised twice in one year under different funding counts once.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying accessions genetically characterised for the reporting year. At institutional level, the de-duplicated sum of those counts, computed from the records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one genetically characterised accession is often reported by more than one project. De-duplication is on the holding institute code plus accession number in the genebank documentation system, per Block E. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the number excluded under Eligibility and why, the number of detected duplicate pairs, the number of accessions re-run on a newly adopted standard assay, as the separately labelled companion figure, and the number of accessions reported alongside because they rest on the Fallback.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count does not add to KPI-O14, a stock of accessions conserved at the reporting date, nor to KPI-OC14, a percentage. KPI-O15 is an annual flow that includes partner-held accessions and KPI-O14 a stock of CIMMYT's own collection, so a CIMMYT accession legitimately appears in both, and the two are never summed and never divided into one another as a rate; the coverage view in Sub-metrics divides by the collection's holdings, not by KPI-O14. The levels connect as a narrative through the theory of change, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: de-duplicate by holding institute code plus accession number, the key KPI-O14 uses, across projects, funding streams and laboratories before pooling; a bare accession number cannot identify an accession uniquely once partner genebanks are in scope. Where a partner laboratory used its own sample codes and identifiers cannot be reconciled, label the pooled number an upper estimate. The same risk runs across years and is handled by the same key: an accession counted in an earlier year does not re-enter the headline, so the identifier must reconcile across years as well as across projects.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: accessions CIMMYT characterises, by its own laboratories or a laboratory it commissions, whether held in a CIMMYT genebank collection or by a national partner genebank on whose behalf the work is done, in every case with the holding institute code, the quality control result and the accession identifier on record. An accession counts as genetically characterised when it has been genotyped or sequenced on the holding genebank's own documented standard characterisation assay for the crop, that is the marker panel or sequencing platform the genebank has adopted and documented as its characterisation standard for that crop, or on an assay the genebank curator records as at least as informative at the time of the run, with the assay recorded against the accession. No fixed marker-density threshold is set across crops. Where the holding genebank, often a partner collection, has no documented standard assay for the crop, CIMMYT's own documented standard assay for that crop applies instead, recorded as such against the accession. Every counted characterisation also records its sampling scheme, the number of individuals sampled per accession and whether they were bulked into one composite sample or genotyped individually, since the two give different pictures of within-accession heterogeneity and neither is comparable to the other unlabelled.

Exclusion: description from observed plant traits alone; evaluation, the separate activity of testing accessions for agronomic and quality traits in trials; genotyping of breeding lines, trial entries or other material that is not a genebank accession (that belongs to the breeding pipeline indicators); accessions first characterised in an earlier year; runs that failed quality control; genotyping of CIMMYT-held accessions by third parties CIMMYT did not commission, including such data found only in public portals.

Missing data: results that cannot be linked to a valid accession identifier are excluded rather than imputed and reported as an unlinked remainder; accessions missing the crop or trait-class classification stay in the total under a not-available category.

Repeated observations: an accession counts once, in the year of its first characterisation, whatever the number of runs or laboratories it passed through: an accession re-run in a later year on the same documented standard assay for that crop is not newly characterised and does not count again. Genotyping run before the holding genebank documented a standard assay for the crop is a first characterisation, in the year it was run, where the documentation system records it against the accession with its assay and the curator records that assay as at least as informative as the standard assay later documented for the crop, the holding genebank's or, failing one, CIMMYT's; otherwise the accession is uncharacterised for this indicator. Once a genebank adopts and documents a new standard assay for a crop, an accession re-run on that new assay is reported as a separately labelled companion figure, never added to the headline, since a platform upgrade would otherwise produce a step change that reads as new work. Where genotyping detects that two accession records are genetic duplicates, each record counts as its own characterised accession, flagged on both as a detected duplicate pair, since the characterisation work was done once per record and de-duplicating the accessions themselves is KPI-O14's own count to make, not this indicator's. Where genotyping detects a mismatch between an accession's genetic identity and its passport record, and the genotype itself passed quality control on a sound, correctly identified sample, the accession still counts as characterised: identifying a mismatch is a result of characterisation, not a quality-control failure, and it is reported as a corrected or flagged passport record, not excluded. Where the mismatch instead traces to a sampling or handling error, the wrong plant sampled, a mislabelled tube, a swapped plate position, the run is not a result about the named accession at all; it is excluded as a failed run, on the same footing as any other quality-control failure, and the accession is re-sampled.
limitations: Measures documentation produced, not use made of it. A characterised accession is not one that has entered a breeding programme; read this count alongside KPI-OC14, which measures whether releases draw on conserved genetic resources.

Characterisation is not one thing. A low-density marker panel confirming identity and a whole-genome sequence each register as one accession, as do a single plant and a bulk of many, and the minimum that counts, the holding genebank's own documented standard assay for the crop, or one the curator records as at least as informative, holds comparability within one genebank and one assay generation; it does not hold across genebanks, whose documented standards differ, or across a platform upgrade within one genebank, so figures from different genebanks, crops or platform generations are not comparable and the method and holding genebank must travel with the value.

The count is narrower than the genebank's characterisation work. The international standards treat description from observed plant traits and molecular characterisation as one activity; counting only the molecular route understates total effort and is not a measure of how well described the collection is.

The value is an annual flow, not a coverage figure. Each accession enters the headline once, at first characterisation, so successive years count distinct accessions rather than repeat work and may legitimately be added to give a running total of accessions characterised. That total is still not coverage: it includes partner-held accessions and accessions no longer registered, and only the accessions registered in CIMMYT's collection at the reporting date, over that collection's registered holdings, give the coverage view in Sub-metrics. Because the collection is finite and increasingly covered, the annual flow must eventually fall even at constant characterisation effort, once most of the collection is already characterised; a falling value in a well-covered collection is not on its own a sign of reduced effort, and should be read against the coverage share in Sub-metrics rather than the annual count alone.

A rise can reflect sequencing capacity, cost or funding rather than a strategic gain. Interpret movements against which parts of the collection were targeted, since landraces and crop wild relatives add far more new information than already well-described improved material.

Detected genetic duplicates are not removed from this count. Two accession records confirmed genetically identical each count as their own characterised accession, since the characterisation work was done once per record; de-duplicating the accessions themselves is KPI-O14's own count to make, not this indicator's. This headline can therefore modestly over-count distinct germplasm characterised in a year with many newly detected duplicate pairs; the number of detected duplicate pairs is reported alongside the value so the effect is visible rather than silent.
subMetrics: No sub-metric enters the value. Crop, accession type and method are disaggregations of the same distinct-accession count, not separately calculated metrics. One standing ratio is reported beside it, the share of CIMMYT's collection genetically characterised, a view alongside the annual flow rather than part of this value: the distinct accessions registered in CIMMYT's genebank collection at the reporting date that carry a qualifying characterisation from any year, judged under Eligibility criteria and missing data as at the time of the run, divided by all distinct accessions registered in that collection at the reporting date in the genebank documentation system, whatever their viability or test status; safety duplicates CIMMYT holds on deposit for another institution are in neither term. It is never divided by KPI-O14. It is the figure read against the FAO benchmarks, as a lower bound, and partner-held accessions sit outside it. Where compliance with FAO standard 4.5.1 is the question, the same share is computed for the accessions acquired in each year and read against the benchmark by acquisition year, with an accession characterised during its first regeneration cycle counted as meeting the benchmark whatever its acquisition year.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the genetic resources / genebank lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: genebank documentation officers and the genotyping laboratory, recording each completed characterisation against its accession identifier. Validation: genebank curator (quality control passed, identifier valid, crop classified). Calculation: genebank data manager, applying the distinct-accession rule; cross-source de-duplication by the CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: genebank lead. Reporting: genebank focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 4 · Genetic resources, breeding & seed — Reference sheet KPI-O15

name: Number of improved varieties entering seed multiplication and deployment
resultsLevel: Output, per CIMMYT's MEAL Framework definition, which governs the register. The first documented seed production of a variety is a delivered result, the first seed of it available for distribution. Where multiplication is decided and financed entirely by an external seed producer, CGIAR's control-and-externality test would read the entry as an outcome, a divergence Core Section 5.4 records.
primaryObjective: PO2 Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved).
cgiarImpactArea: Nutrition, Health & Food Security. Moving improved varieties into seed production is the delivery step of the food and nutrition security pathway PO2 describes. The register carries no Impact Area column; the value follows the pathway-wide rule, which sets the area by what the indicator measures.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest target is SDG 2.5 (maintain the genetic diversity of seeds and cultivated plants and promote access to genetic resources), but its official indicators measure genetic resources held in conservation facilities (2.5.1) and local and transboundary breeds at risk of extinction (2.5.2), not varieties entering seed production. SDG 2.3's indicators measure producer productivity and income, not the seed pipeline.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR: the Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 minimum data standard records varieties under Output, Innovation Development, with innovation type and innovation readiness level rather than a count of varieties entering multiplication, so this indicator feeds those fields rather than matching a CGIAR standard indicator.
definition: Counts improved varieties that enter seed multiplication and deployment in the reporting year, as variety-country entries, with the number of distinct varieties behind them reported alongside. A variety enters in a country at its first documented seed production event intended for farmer access, in the formal seed system (pre-basic or basic seed, or certified seed, produced by a national agency, a seed company or a CIMMYT project), the informal and community system (community seed producer groups, farmer cooperatives), or the quality declared seed system, the registered and inspected scheme between the two; breeder seed does not trigger entry in any of the three. Only varieties KPI-O12's rules count as released in that country, in whichever year, are eligible.
rationale: Answers how many improved varieties cross from release into seed production each year, the step at which breeding results become something a farmer can plant. It is the conversion check on CIMMYT's science-to-seed pipeline: a released variety that never enters multiplication delivers nothing. It tells management and donors whether releases are being taken up by seed producers; farmer access to improved technological packages (KPI-O20) follows in the same chain.
projectSpecificApplication: State the crops, countries and partner seed producers the project works with, which release and seed certification registers feed the count, and the seasons in its reporting year, under the convention the MEAL unit fixes per country. Do not change the trigger event, the eligibility rule, or the count-once-per-variety-per-country rule. If applying the indicator as defined is not feasible, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count serves: for example an early generation seed production milestone, a seed-system delivery target agreed with a national partner, or a trigger to revisit licensing, partnership or promotion arrangements when released varieties stall before multiplication.
projectTypesApply: whose seed-sector programmes are where multiplication at scale sits
projectTypesNotApplicable: none of which produces or multiplies seed
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation, whose seed-sector programmes are where multiplication at scale sits.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science; applied agronomy and farming systems; and digital agriculture and AI, none of which produces or multiplies seed.
unit: Number of variety-country entries; the number of distinct varieties is reported alongside.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more variety-country entries into seed production for farmer access. Variety-country entries are the headline and re-entry is not counted, so a variety multiplied again in a later year does not raise the value.
disaggregationRequired: Required: crop; trait class, on the toolbox's eight-class controlled vocabulary: yield and yield potential; abiotic stress tolerance (drought, heat, waterlogging); biotic stress resistance (disease, pest); nutritional quality (including biofortification); end-use and processing quality; agronomic and adaptation traits; and not trait-targeted (genome-wide characterisation, identity confirmation, diversity assessment). Not yet characterised does not apply: it is the class for uncharacterised genebank holdings (KPI-O14). Named traits are recorded at a second level within a class rather than instead of it. Also required: seed class at entry (pre-basic or basic, certified, quality declared, none declared), because it links each entry to KPI-O17's class rows from pre-basic seed on; KPI-O17's breeder-seed row has no counterpart here. An entry is recorded at the class of its first documented production event; where several classes begin in that event it is listed under each in a secondary field, and class subtotals are never summed to the total. Foundation and registered seed are recorded as pre-basic or basic, with the national name noted. The register requires crop and trait class only, so this cut is CIMMYT's own, applied on the sheet's authority.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator. Variety is not a cut here: each entry is already one variety in one country, and the distinct-variety figure is reported beside the headline.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country; seed system channel (formal / informal or community-based); producer type (public agency, private seed company, farmer cooperative, community seed group); women-owned or women-led producing enterprise, where the project tracks it.
unitOfObservation: The variety-country entry: one variety entering multiplication in one country, at its first documented seed production event there. This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation; the seed producing entity's records are where the multiplication event is documented, not what is counted.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of variety-country entries into seed multiplication in the reporting year that qualify under Eligibility criteria and missing data, with the number of distinct varieties behind them reported alongside. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: administrative and registry data; the entry's evidence is the production or certification record itself, namely partner seed company production records reported under project agreements and the production records of community seed producer groups and farmer cooperatives kept or reported under project agreements (production registers, distribution lists, field records naming the variety), and national or regional variety release and seed certification registers, supported by CIMMYT breeding programme and seed unit records of breeder and early generation seed dispatch and multiplication or licensing agreements, which establish the chain to a released variety but do not themselves trigger the count. Fallback DS1: a structured reporting form or survey of seed producers, cooperatives and community seed groups, used where a producer keeps no production record of its own and the entry rests on the survey response alone; flagged as fallback-sourced. Comparator DS4: published national seed sector statistics and seed system assessments (seed certification annual reports, African Seed Access Index country reports), used to place the count against national seed production; never a substitute for a production or certification record, never pooled, and never reported as a KPI-O16 value. A certification report that lists the certified production of a variety in the country is a certification record under DS2. Not applicable DS3: the start of seed multiplication of a named variety cannot be observed from satellite or geospatial data. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or mobile data cannot establish the identity, release status or production purpose of a seed lot.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether Recommended or Fallback was used, which registers and partner records supplied the entries, and how variety identity was matched across sources. If Fallback, state why administrative records were not usable.
collectionInstrument: For the DS1 fallback: a seed producer reporting form capturing variety name and national release code (linked by the project seed systems officer to the identifier of the released entry in KPI-O12's release records before the entry is counted), crop, trait class, seed class, country, season, purpose of production and volume. Respondent: the seed production manager of the producing entity, or the chairperson of a community seed producer group. Mode: structured form completed with the project seed systems officer, in person or by phone. The DS2 route draws the same variety identity fields from existing seed unit and certification records.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as production and certification records are generated; compiled and verified annually.
referencePeriod: The reporting year. Where seasons straddle the calendar year, the reporting year follows the season-to-reporting-year convention the CIMMYT MEAL unit fixes per country, held constant across years, so that two projects cannot place one production season in two reporting years.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual count of new entries, so it starts from zero in each reporting year and for each new project; the first reported year serves as the reference point for trend context. No change or impact claim rests on this indicator alone.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool the entries evidenced in production or certification records (Recommended); an entry evidenced only by a producer reporting form or survey (Fallback DS1) is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, not blended in; an entry evidenced on both is Recommended-sourced and pooled, and the same project's Recommended-sourced entries stay in the pool. Two projects supporting multiplication of the same variety in the same country produce one entry, not two.

B: Combination method. Sum distinct variety-country entries after de-duplication on the identifier of the released entry plus country, matching KPI-O12 and KPI-OC14, so one variety multiplied in one country under two names or two licensees' brands is one entry; two distinct hybrids sharing one parent line are two entries, never collapsed to one. The national release code, or crop plus variety name plus country where no code exists, is the lookup that links a production record to its released entry: the cross identifier for a hybrid, or the line or population identifier for an open-pollinated variety, inbred line or population.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's variety-country multiplication entries for the reporting year, with the number of distinct varieties behind that project's own count reported alongside it. At institutional level, the de-duplicated sum of those counts, computed from the seed production and certification records themselves rather than by adding project figures. The distinct-variety figure is de-duplicated on the identifier of the released entry alone, so it is never the sum of the country counts. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the number of entries excluded under Eligibility and why, the number of multiplications of varieties KPI-O12 does not count, reported separately, and the number of entries reported alongside because they rest on the Fallback.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. The register records that this indicator contributes to KPI-O17 (tonnes of quality seed produced) and KPI-O20 (farmers accessing improved technological packages), further steps in the same delivery narrative, not addends: a count of varieties, a tonnage of seed and a count of farmers cannot be combined arithmetically.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: the main overlap is with KPI-O12 (varieties released), where the same variety is counted once at release and again here at entry into multiplication; these are two stages of one pipeline and must never be summed into a total of varieties delivered. De-duplicate on the identifier of the released entry plus country before pooling; where a production record cannot be linked to a released entry, because its release code is missing or its name is inconsistent across national registers, label the pooled figure an upper estimate and state the matching rule used.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusions: varieties officially registered, approved or released, limited to the varieties KPI-O12 counts as released in the country of entry, in whichever year, and not to any improved variety a CIMMYT project multiplies, with evidence of the first documented seed production event intended for farmer access, that is the first production of pre-basic or basic, certified or quality declared seed, or, in the informal and community system, the first documented production for sale or distribution by a community seed producer group or farmer cooperative, whether or not the seed carries a declared class, such as a first seed production field, planted for onward multiplication where the class is pre-basic or basic, or for sale or distribution in the informal and community system. For a hybrid, the trigger is the first production field of that hybrid's own seed, or of a single-cross seed parent produced for that hybrid under a documented production plan; an increase of an inbred parent line alone does not trigger entry for any hybrid, since one line can serve several. A germplasm handover and a signed multiplication or licensing agreement do not trigger the count: both are intentions to multiply, and a variety licensed but never multiplied would otherwise enter the count and defeat the conversion check this indicator exists to make. Nor does breeder seed: it is the maintainer's own increase before a certification scheme or the quality declared seed system takes it up, whoever grows it; once the increase enters the scheme it is pre-basic or basic seed, so a national programme multiplying its own variety in-house stays in breeder seed until then. KPI-O17 uses the same definition. Pre-basic, basic, certified and quality declared seed are the classes produced under the national certification scheme or the quality declared seed system and inspected or labelled by it. Community seed producer groups and quality declared seed count on the same footing as certified production, with the seed system recorded as a disaggregation and the weaker documentation handled by recording the evidence type rather than by exclusion, since in most countries where CIMMYT works, the informal system is how smallholders obtain seed.

Exclusions: varieties still under testing, and varieties with no completed release; seed produced only for research trials, demonstration plots or on-station regeneration; varieties already counted for the same country in an earlier year; seed production in a country where the variety is not released, including early generation seed grown there for export; multiplication a project supports of a variety KPI-O12 does not count, reported separately beside the count and never added to it.

Missing data: a variety with documented multiplication but no verifiable start date is counted in the year its evidence is dated and flagged as date-uncertain; a variety whose release status cannot be verified in a national or regional register is held out and reported separately as pending verification.

Repeated observations: each variety counts once per country, in the year multiplication first begins, not in every year it stays in production; a variety returning to multiplication after leaving production is recorded and reportable, and is not counted again; a variety multiplied by several producers, in several seasons or across several seed classes within the same year counts once for that country; the same variety multiplied in two countries produces two entries, and the number of unique varieties behind the entries is reported alongside the total.
limitations: Entry into multiplication is not farmer access. A variety can enter production and never reach meaningful volume or reach farms at all; read this count only with the seed volume produced (KPI-O17) and farmer access (KPI-O20). This indicator dates its entry to planting of the first seed production field, normally a season or more before the resulting lot passes quality assurance and enters KPI-O17; the two series are roughly one production cycle apart, not year for year, so pair them with that offset in mind, for the classes both count; for a hybrid, KPI-O17's inbred parent-line lots precede the entry here, and KPI-O17 counts seed grown in a country where the variety is not released, which this indicator excludes. KPI-O17 counts only lots produced under a CIMMYT-supported multiplication arrangement, while this indicator counts an entry whoever multiplies, so an entry by an independent producer shows no tonnage there and is not a stalled entry. KPI-O17 also carries a breeder-seed row this indicator never counts, since breeder seed does not trigger entry here.

The trigger is fixed to the first seed production field, chronologically the last of three candidate moments but the first of them to be evidence rather than intention. A breeder seed handover and a signed multiplication agreement can precede that field by years, so a project applying either of those instead would report earlier and higher.

Informal and community-based multiplication is weakly documented, so the count leans toward the formal seed sector and understates community and farmer-to-farmer channels, which in many CIMMYT contexts carry most of the seed farmers plant; community entries evidenced only by the fallback survey are reported beside the pooled count, not in it. The binding constraint is the release gate, not the records: only varieties KPI-O12 counts as released are eligible at all, so the same-footing ruling for informal and community systems under Eligibility criteria and missing data applies only where the multiplied variety is itself formally released; no amount of better documentation brings an unregistered, farmer-selected variety into the count.

Supports a contribution claim only. CIMMYT supplies germplasm, early generation seed and partnership, but the decision to multiply rests with seed producers and national agencies and responds to demand, credit, regulation and price.

A rise means more variety-country entries began production, not that more or better seed reached farmers. A few widely multiplied varieties can serve far more farmers than many varieties with token production runs, so never read this as a measure of seed supply.
