Who obtains the seed is not measured here or anywhere in this pathway (Introduction); a project working on equitable seed access measures it beside its own outputs.
subMetrics: None. Seed class, seed system channel and producer type are disaggregations of the same count, not separately calculated metrics. Neighbouring steps have their own sheets: KPI-O12 (varieties released, the eligible base), KPI-O17 (volume of quality seed produced), KPI-O20 (farmers accessing improved technological packages) and KPI-OC12 (weighted average age of improved varieties in farmers' fields).
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
Counting rule: The seed-class sequence (breeder, pre-basic or basic, certified, quality declared seed) uses the class names national certification schemes and quality declared seed systems use, each lot's class being the one its national scheme declared; neither the OECD Seed Schemes nor FAO's quality declared seed guidance is cited, so the sequence is not attributed to either. The count-once-per-variety-per-country rule is CIMMYT's own convention, stated on CIMMYT's authority; no external standard defines it. The breeder-seed pre-scheme trigger exclusion (Eligibility) is the same type of rule, CIMMYT's own convention on the same authority; no external standard fixes the point at which the maintainer's own increase becomes pre-basic or basic seed.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the seed systems lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project seed systems officer, with partner seed producers and national seed agencies supplying records. Validation: project MEAL officer, checking release status against the national or regional variety register and confirming the trigger evidence. Calculation: project M&E, applying the count-once-per-variety-per-country rule; cross-project de-duplication by the CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: project leader, with the breeding programme lead confirming variety identity. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 4 · Genetic resources, breeding & seed — Reference sheet KPI-O16

name: Volume (tonnes) of quality seed of improved varieties produced
resultsLevel: Output, per CIMMYT's MEAL Framework definition, which governs the register. Producing and quality-assuring a defined tonnage is a deliverable of work CIMMYT and its contracted multipliers carry out, not a change in the behaviour of external actors; whether farmers then obtain and plant that seed is measured at KPI-O20. Where a partner company decides and finances multiplication under a CIMMYT-supported arrangement, CGIAR's control test separating output from outcome is not clearly met, a divergence handled once in the crosswalk annex; seed produced by an independent company with no CIMMYT-supported arrangement is outside this indicator (Eligibility criteria and missing data).
primaryObjective: PO2 Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved).
cgiarImpactArea: Nutrition, Health & Food Security. The pathway-wide rule sets the area by the object measured, which is a tonne of quality-assured seed of an improved variety. Seed volume is the supply step through which improved varieties reach food production, the pathway PO2 describes.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest target is SDG 2.5 (maintaining the genetic diversity of seeds and cultivated plants), but its indicator 2.5.1(a) counts plant genetic resources secured in conservation facilities, a stock of conserved accessions rather than a volume of seed produced for planting.
otherFrameworks: No donor reporting framework carries a counterpart: their crop measures are yield and production of harvested commodities, not of seed. The comparators are national seed-system assessments: the Seed Systems Assessment Tool (SeedSAT), whose categories include early generation and commercial seed production and distribution, and the African Seed Access Index (TASAI), which benchmarks national seed industries including service to smallholder farmers. National certification agencies publish certified volumes on their own definitions.
definition: Measures the volume, in tonnes, of quality seed of improved varieties produced during the reporting year through CIMMYT-supported seed multiplication. Quality seed is seed of a declared class (breeder, pre-basic or basic, certified, or quality declared seed) that has passed the applicable certification or quality-assurance scheme's sampling and testing requirements, or, for breeder seed, the maintainer's documented quality control (Eligibility). Improved varieties are the varieties KPI-O12's rules count as released, in whichever year; for a hybrid, the early-generation classes are the seed of its parent lines (Eligibility). Volume is processed weight per lot at quality-assurance passage, not raw harvested weight.
rationale: Answers how much planting material of CIMMYT's improved varieties became available each year, the step that converts a released variety into something farmers can plant. A variety released but never multiplied in volume delivers nothing, so this figure is the supply-side test of the breeding-to-seed pipeline and the quantity behind the farmer access measured next (KPI-O20). Project management uses it to size multiplication against demand; institutional and donor reporting uses it to show upstream science reached production scale.
projectSpecificApplication: State the crops, varieties, seed classes and countries the project produces seed in, the scheme its lots are declared against, or for breeder seed the maintainer's own documented control and the maintenance records carrying it, the producers involved, and the lot records evidencing the volume. Do not change the tonnes unit, the once-per-lot rule, the processed-seed weighing point, or the requirement that the lot passed a defined quality standard. If applying the indicator as defined is not feasible, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this volume informs: a multiplication target agreed with a donor or national partner, a scaling plan that must produce enough seed to cover a planned area, or a trigger to contract additional multipliers when production falls short of projected demand.
projectTypesApply: whose seed-sector programmes are where multiplication at scale sits
projectTypesNotApplicable: none of which produces or multiplies seed
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation, whose seed-sector programmes are where multiplication at scale sits.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science; applied agronomy and farming systems; and digital agriculture and AI, none of which produces or multiplies seed.
unit: Tonnes of seed (metric tonnes, 1,000 kg), taken as the processed weight at the point the lot passes quality assurance, as recorded for the lot, with no adjustment to a reference moisture; the lot's tested moisture content is recorded beside its weight, with the scheme named, or, for breeder seed, the maintainer's method named. Schemes and methods differ, and a tonnage is meaningless without the moisture basis, breeder seed included.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising class tonnage means more quality seed of that class was produced, taken as the processed weight at the point the lot passes quality assurance. Seed classes are reported separately and never summed into one headline figure (Aggregation rule Blocks C and E); the labelled farmer-ready figure in Aggregation rule Block B is the one two-class figure permitted.
disaggregationRequired: Required: crop; trait class, on the eight-class controlled vocabulary set out on KPI-O10; seed class (breeder, pre-basic or basic, certified, quality declared seed, not stated); where a national scheme uses other class names, a lot is recorded in the row of the class it occupies in the chain, with the national name noted alongside: foundation and registered seed, both grown to produce further seed rather than for farmers, in the pre-basic or basic row. The register requires crop and trait class only, so this cut is CIMMYT's own, applied on the sheet's authority.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Variety; country and sub-national production area; producer type (CIMMYT seed unit, national programme or public enterprise, private company, seed producer group or cooperative, community seed bank); certification scheme applied; sex of the lead producer or of seed producer group members.
unitOfObservation: The seed lot. This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation, whose definition names it, and it is the identity Block B defines and Block E de-duplicates on; the seed producer's records are where the volume is reported, not what is counted.
calculationSummary: Value = the quality-assured weight, in tonnes, of the seed lots of improved varieties produced under CIMMYT support and passing quality assurance in the reporting year, reported per seed class as set out in Aggregation rule Block B. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: seed certification agency or quality declared seed authority records, the breeding programme's own maintenance records for breeder seed, and the production, processing and quality-control registers of CIMMYT seed units and contracted multipliers, each lot carrying crop, variety, seed class, quality-assured weight, tested moisture content, certificate, test reference or maintenance-record reference, the class and lot reference of the source seed, producer, location and date. Fallback DS1: a structured production survey of the seed producers involved, with inspection of store, weighbridge and dispatch records, where a partner's registers are not accessible to CIMMYT. Comparator DS4: national seed authority or seed trade association statistics on seed produced or certified, by variety where published, used to place the figure against national production of the same classes; never a substitute for lot records, never pooled, and never reported as a KPI-O17 value. Values from the fallback are flagged as fallback-sourced. Not applicable DS3: seed volume and certification status cannot be observed from satellite or geospatial data. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or mobile data cannot establish that a seed lot met a quality standard.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether Recommended or the Fallback was used, which registers or respondents supplied the lot list, and how lots were de-duplicated. If Fallback, state why certification and producer records were not available.
collectionInstrument: For the DS1 fallback: a seed producer production questionnaire capturing, per lot, crop, variety, parent line (for hybrid early generation seed), seed class, quality-assurance reference, the class and lot reference of the source seed, processed weight, tested moisture content and date, completed against the producer's own records. Respondent: the producer's production or quality manager. Mode: in person with record inspection, or by phone where records can be transmitted. The DS2 route uses existing certification and producer lot registers, with no separate instrument.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as lots are processed and certified through the season; compiled annually.
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the lot passed quality assurance. Each annual value stands alone and describes production, not sales or planting, which may fall in a later season. KPI-O16 dates its entry to planting of the first seed production field, normally a season or more before the resulting lot passes quality assurance here; pairing the two indicators' series year for year, as the cross-reference between them invites, misreads them by roughly that one-cycle offset, for the classes the two indicators share, that is pre-basic seed on, and for entries produced under a CIMMYT-supported arrangement only. Breeder seed has no counterpart in KPI-O16, since that indicator's trigger excludes it. For a hybrid, the inbred parent-line lots counted here precede its KPI-O16 entry rather than follow it, and seed grown in a country where the variety is not released, such as early generation seed for export, has no KPI-O16 entry there.
baselineRequired: No. An annual flow starting from zero each reporting year; the first reported year is the reference point for trend context. Change in farmer access is measured by KPI-O20 against its own baseline.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool volumes from projects that used the Recommended records; volumes from the Fallback route are reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, not blended in, because survey recall carries different resolution and coverage. The route is decided per record, not per project: a project whose records come partly from each route pools its Recommended-sourced records and reports the rest alongside.

B: Combination method. Sum tonnes within a seed class across producers and projects, after de-duplicating by lot identity (certificate, test reference, lot number or, for breeder seed, maintenance-record reference, plus producer, crop, variety, class). The classes are never summed into one headline tonne figure: the reported value is a set of per-class tonnages, and where a single number is unavoidable it is certified plus quality-declared, labelled as the farmer-ready classes and as an upper bound on the seed planted for a crop, since part of a lot in either class may be sown to produce further seed instead (Limitations).

C: Levels and operations. Tonnes add across producers; what is de-duplicated is the lot, not the variety or producer. At producer level, the quality-assured weight of each lot at the processed-seed weighing point. At project level, the sum of those weights after de-duplicating on lot identity per Block B. At institutional level, the sum across projects on the same basis, within the pooling domain of Block A. Every one of those sums is within a seed class. The per-class figures travel together at every level and are not added to each other, because early-generation and farmer-ready seed are different quantities: one tonne of breeder seed and one tonne of certified seed are not interchangeable, and the first becomes hundreds of tonnes of the second. Also report: the class breakdown, the number of contributing producers and projects, the rejected volume, the unverified remainder and the project-assured volume as three separate figures, the not-stated-class row, the truthfully labelled row, the tonnage reported alongside because it rests on the Fallback, and total national production of the same classes and, where published, of the same varieties, as context from the Comparator.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. Tonnes do not combine with the variety counts of KPI-O16 or the farmer counts of KPI-O20; the levels connect through the theory of change, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: four risks. The same lot reported by both producer and certification agency, resolved by lot identity. Successive classes of one multiplication chain added into one figure, resolved by keeping classes in separate rows and never summing them. Carryover, where seed produced in one year is certified or sold in the next, resolved by fixing the count to the year the lot first passed quality assurance. A lot re-certified across a border, resolved by the originating certificate or lot reference. Where lot identifiers are absent, label the pooled figure an upper estimate. Overlap with other indicators is named, not summed: the varieties behind these lots are counted at release in KPI-O12 and, from pre-basic seed on, at entry in KPI-O16, and the farmers who later obtain the seed are counted in KPI-O20.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Quality assurance means the applicable certification or quality-assurance scheme for every class except breeder seed, for which it means the maintainer's own documented quality control set out in Inclusion below, on this sheet throughout. Four states, kept distinct and never merged: a seed lot that passed quality assurance is counted; a seed lot that failed quality assurance is excluded and reported separately as rejected volume, a real production outcome, not an absence of information; a seed lot with no quality-assurance record at all, whether never submitted or undocumented, is excluded and reported separately as an unverified remainder, since a rejection and a coverage gap are different findings and reporting a rejected lot as if it were merely unverified misreports it as missing information rather than as failed quality; a seed lot assured only under a project's or CIMMYT's own arrangement is excluded and reported separately as project-assured volume (Exclusion below). Inclusion: lots of improved varieties, counting seed produced under a CIMMYT-supported multiplication arrangement, by CIMMYT or by a partner, and not all certified seed of CIMMYT-derived varieties produced anywhere. A CIMMYT-supported multiplication arrangement is a documented agreement (project agreement, contract, licence or memorandum) under which CIMMYT or a CIMMYT project supplies seed, finance, technical or quality-assurance support for the producer's multiplication of the variety; supplying seed to a producer with no such agreement does not bring its later lots into scope. The quality-assurance floor is a national certification scheme or a formally documented quality declared seed system, evidenced by a certificate, test result or quality-assurance record identifying the lot. Breeder seed is the maintainer's own increase, before that scheme takes it up, the same pre-scheme definition KPI-O16 states for its own trigger exclusion; breeder seed is the single named exception to the sole-guarantor rule below: its quality-assurance floor is the maintainer's own documented quality control, a germination, purity, varietal-identity and moisture test to a named method, with the maintenance record identifying the lot in place of a certificate. All declared classes are in scope: breeder, pre-basic or basic, certified, and quality declared, with class as a required disaggregation. For a hybrid, the early-generation classes (breeder, pre-basic and basic seed) are the seed of its parent lines and of any single-cross seed parent, and those lots are eligible where at least one hybrid they are produced for is a variety KPI-O12 counts as released. Each parent-seed lot is recorded once, against the parent line's identifier, with the released hybrids it serves listed beside it; it is never attributed to each hybrid in turn, and the certified row carries the hybrid's own seed. Seed a national seed law allows the producer to label against legal minimum standards without certification (truthfully labelled seed) is neither certified nor quality declared seed: it is reported in its own row beside the class tonnages, with its testing evidence stated, and never added to a class row or to the farmer-ready figure.

Exclusion: lots that failed quality assurance, reported separately as rejected volume; lots never submitted for quality assurance, reported with the unverified remainder; seed assured only under a project's or CIMMYT's own internal arrangement, which does not count in the per-class tonnages because a producer cannot be both the producer and the sole guarantor of quality, and is reported separately as project-assured volume, breeder seed excepted (Inclusion); grain diverted to seed use without testing; varieties KPI-O12 does not count as released; imported finished seed CIMMYT did not help produce; carryover stock that first passed quality assurance in an earlier year.

Missing data: a seed lot without a quality-assurance record is excluded and shown separately as an unverified remainder, never imputed; a seed lot with volume but no seed class is reported in its own not-stated row, never added to a class row or to the farmer-ready figure.

Repeated observations: each physical lot counts once, at its declared class and the processed weight recorded when it passed quality assurance; a seed lot weighed again at dispatch or after storage is not recounted. A lot counts in the country and year in which it first passed quality assurance; a lot re-tested, re-labelled or re-certified on import into another country is the same physical lot and is not counted again, and the importing record carries the originating certificate or lot reference. Where an imported lot carries no originating reference, the pooled figure is labelled an upper estimate. Successive generations of the same seed (breeder into basic, basic into certified) are reported in their own class rows and never summed into one headline tonne figure (Aggregation rule Block C). Inside a class row, a lot grown from seed of its own class, such as a later certified generation or quality declared seed grown from quality declared seed, is its own lot and counts once in that row, with the class and lot reference of its source seed recorded.
limitations: Seed produced is not seed planted for a crop. The volume includes seed that goes unsold, is carried over, degrades in storage, is rejected at market or is sown to produce further seed, so it is an upper bound on what is planted for a crop. Read it only alongside KPI-O20.

Tonnes are not comparable across crops. Seeding rates differ by an order of magnitude, so a tonne of one crop's seed plants far less area, and reaches far fewer farmers, than a tonne of another's. Never convert the total into area or farmers reached; read the crop breakdown.

"Quality" means whichever scheme applied, and for breeder seed, whichever control its maintainer documented; breeder-seed tonnage rests on the maintainer's own control and is the least comparable row in the table. Certification thresholds and testing regimes differ between countries and seed classes, so a cross-country total sums volumes assured against different standards; the schemes applied must travel with the value. The quality-assurance floor also excludes the undeclared informal or community channel that KPI-O16 counts on equal footing: an entry counted in KPI-O16 with no declared class correctly shows zero tonnes here, and the exclusion is methodologically correct, since unassured seed is not quality seed, but it relocates rather than removes the informal-channel bias KPI-O16's own ruling addresses. This tonnage describes the assured segment only.

Quantity of seed produced is a known weak measure of seed system performance: highly aggregated, blind to variety-level detail, and silent on the quality farmers receive and who obtains the seed. It cannot on its own show whether a seed system is working.

Supports a contribution claim only. Volumes produced by companies and national programmes respond to market demand, input prices, subsidies and weather as much as to CIMMYT; a rise in a class's tonnage means more quality seed of that class was produced, not that CIMMYT caused the increase.

No separate planting indicator is carried: what farmers plant is already measured by KPI-O20, KPI-OC16 and KPI-OC12, and a fourth count would rerun the same adoption survey and put one farmer in two adoption counts in the same year.
subMetrics: None. The value is a set of per-class volumes, and crop and trait class are disaggregations of each, not separately calculated metrics. Related indicators have their own sheets: KPI-O16 (varieties entering multiplication and deployment) and KPI-O20 (farmers accessing improved technological packages, the access step this volume feeds).
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
Synthesis rule: The seed-class sequence (breeder, pre-basic or basic, certified, quality declared seed) uses the class names national certification schemes and quality declared seed systems use, each lot's class being the one its national scheme declared; neither the OECD Seed Schemes nor FAO's quality declared seed guidance is cited, so the sequence is not attributed to either, and ISTA below is scoped to testing procedure, not to the class architecture. Breeder seed's pre-scheme quality-assurance floor (Eligibility), the maintainer's own documented control standing in for scheme assurance, is CIMMYT's own convention, stated on CIMMYT's authority; no external standard defines it, and certification schemes require the ISTA Rules from pre-basic seed on, once the scheme has taken the lot up; for breeder seed the maintainer may test to the ISTA Rules or to its own method, and whichever method it used is named on the maintenance record identifying the lot.

Measurement: International Seed Testing Association (2026), International rules for seed testing, procedures for seed lot sampling, germination, purity, varietal identity and moisture testing, applied by national certification schemes when declaring a seed lot to standard; paywalled, and the citation of record for seed quality testing; the 2026 edition is cited for this general description; the edition binding any one lot is whichever its certification scheme has adopted, recorded per lot rather than fixed centrally here.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.

sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project seed systems staff and contracted multipliers maintaining lot registers, plus certification records from the national seed authority. Validation: project MEAL officer, checking each lot carries a quality-assurance reference, seed class and processed weight. Calculation: project M&E summing lot weights by class and crop; cross-project de-duplication by the CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: project leader, with the seed systems lead confirming class assignment. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.

name: Rate of genetic gain delivered per year in CIMMYT breeding pipelines
resultsLevel: Outcome, as recorded in the register: a rate of genetic gain is a change in performance per year, a trend fitted across years of origin rather than a level at one point. Under CGIAR's control-and-externality test the estimate would read differently, since it is fitted from trials the breeding programme itself runs; Core Section 5.4 records that divergence, and a sister CGIAR centre's equivalent indicator carries the same Outcome classification.
primaryObjective: PO2 Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved) and PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Nutrition, Health & Food Security. The pathway-wide rule sets the area by what the indicator measures, which is the rate at which a breeding pipeline delivers an improved trait toward release, on the way to food and nutrition security outcomes. The register carries no Impact Area column; the value follows the pathway-wide rule stated in the opening paragraph of this volume's Introduction.
sdgTarget: None. No SDG indicator measures breeding programme performance. The two nearest in Goal 2 rule themselves out: 2.3.1 is production per labour day of small-scale food producers in constant purchasing-power-parity dollars, a farm-level economic ratio; 2.5.1a counts genetic resource accessions in conservation facilities, a stock of conserved diversity.
otherFrameworks: The Excellence in Breeding Platform's breeding process assessment manual, which sets out genetic gain as the high-level performance indicator for the breeding process. ICARDA's indicator OC-04, realized genetic gains in farmer-relevant conditions, applying the same method in another CGIAR centre's indicator set. CIMMYT's definition is its own, not adapted from a CGIAR standard indicator.
definition: The improvement in a target trait, such as grain yield or drought, heat or disease tolerance, that a breeding pipeline delivers per year. Genetic gain is the change in the average breeding value of a population over at least one cycle of selection for a trait or an index of traits. It is estimated as the trend of genotype means on year of origin in trials of germplasm of different years of origin, never from a single trial, and expressed per year, with a per-cycle form (Unit of measure). A breeding pipeline is the breeding effort, from product design to on-farm testing, focused on one market segment or a group of segments with very similar target product profiles, as ICARDA's indicator OC-04 defines it; its testing stages include the sequence KPI-O13 counts advancement through.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's breeding pipelines are improving the traits they select for, and how fast: putting more of the traits farmers need into each new generation of material. It is the highest-level measure of breeding programme performance, used by breeding leadership to compare crossing, evaluation and selection strategies, and in institutional and donor reporting on CIMMYT's upstream science.
projectSpecificApplication: State which breeding pipeline, crop, trait, stage of testing, target environments and window of years of origin the value covers, and whether it came from the routine trial series or a purpose-run trial comparing material from different eras. Do not change the definition, unit or method here. If the trial data cannot support an estimate, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than substituting a different measure.
projectSpecificRationale: State the decision the value serves: a donor commitment on pipeline performance, a stage-gate review of whether a modernisation investment (new selection method, shortened cycle, new testing network) has raised the rate of gain, or a trigger to revisit the pipeline's design if the trend is flat.
projectTypesNotApplicable: the other five types. The value is estimated from a breeding pipeline's own multi-environment trial series
on germplasm of different years of origin connected by common checks, and only a breeding project runs such a pipeline and its trials
upstream discovery science supplies material to the pipeline but generates no trial series from which a rate of gain could be fitted
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development.

Not applicable: the other five types. The value is estimated from a breeding pipeline's own multi-environment trial series, on germplasm of different years of origin connected by common checks, and only a breeding project runs such a pipeline and its trials; upstream discovery science supplies material to the pipeline but generates no trial series from which a rate of gain could be fitted.
unit: Percentage gain per year in the target trait, relative to a reference mean taken from the permanent checks, not from the first year of the window. Where no permanent check was grown across the whole window, as in a purpose-run era trial or a series reconnected through the relationship matrix, the percentage form is not computed; only the absolute form is reported, listed beside the percentage distribution under Aggregation rule. Where the declared trait is an index of traits whose reference mean is near zero, the percentage form is undefined and only the absolute form is reported, with the index's own composite label standing in place of a single trait class. The absolute form (the trait's own units per year, for example tonnes per hectare per year) is reported alongside it with the reference mean, the cycle length in years and the standard error, since the percentage alone hides all three. The cycle length is the parent recycling interval, the interval at which improved parents re-enter the crossing block, and not the crossing-to-release interval, which carries registration and release delays set by regulators. The per-cycle figure is derived by multiplying by that cycle length and is reported only with it, because the two forms differ by several years and a per-cycle value is meaningless without the interval.
directionOfChange: Increase. Values are signed so that improvement in the declared trait is positive: for a trait where a lower score is better, such as disease severity, lodging or days to maturity, the slope's sign is reversed and the value labelled 'sign reversed, lower is better'. A rising value means the declared trait is improving faster per year. The window is fixed at ten years of origin across all pipelines, so the slope cannot be re-cut over a shorter period until it reads favourably.
disaggregationRequired: Required: crop; trait class, on the eight-class controlled vocabulary set out on KPI-O10. Every value must also be labelled with its genetic unit (hybrid or inbred), its stage of testing (early trials, late trials, registration trials, farmers' fields), its target environments, and its window of years of origin. These are not context: a rate from early-stage trials and one from on-farm testing describe different things and must never be presented as one number.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country or region within the target environments; individual trait within a selection index. Sex and age disaggregation are not applicable: the unit of observation is a trial plot, not a person.
unitOfObservation: Plot. The trial plot is measured; plot values are summarised to across-environment genotype means before the regression, so the genotype is the unit of analysis.
calculationSummary: Recommended method, realized genetic gain, in four steps. (1) Assemble trial data for germplasm of different years of origin from one declared stage of testing, across locations and years representing the pipeline's target environments. (2) Fit a mixed model, y = Xβ + Zd·ud + Zg·ug + ε: β carries the fixed main effects of year of evaluation and genotype, the year-of-evaluation term removing improvement due to non-genetic causes and the genotype term the one step (3) regresses on; ud carries the random non-genetic effects, location and year-of-evaluation-by-location; ug carries the random genotype-by-location and genotype-by-year-of-evaluation interaction effects, not a genotype main effect; X, Zd and Zg are the incidence matrices connecting observations to these effects. Take the genotype means from those fixed-effect predictions across environments. (3) Regress those means on year of origin; the slope is gain per year in the trait's own units. The permanent checks connect the first-stage model only, across years and locations, and are excluded from this second-stage regression, since a check is grown every year and its mean is the most precisely estimated in the set, so under a precision-weighted fit it would carry the greatest weight while representing no cohort of the window. Numerator and denominator: none; the value is a regression slope. The genotype means carry unequal and correlated errors from the first-stage model, since entries of one year of origin share the estimated year-of-evaluation effects: fit the second-stage regression by generalised least squares on the full variance-covariance matrix of the means, or estimate the trend in a one-step model, the alternative the manual of record also describes, in which genotype is not fitted as a fixed effect. The standard error and 95 per cent interval reported come from that fit, never from a regression that treats the means as independent. (4) Where Unit of measure computes a percentage form, divide by the reference mean of the permanent checks, their across-environment mean from the same model fit, averaged where the pipeline keeps two, and multiply by 100 for the percentage form, which is the reported value, gain per year; multiplying by the parent recycling interval in years gives the per-cycle form, reported only alongside the interval used. Fallback method, expected genetic gain from the breeder's equation: R = h²S = i·r·σg (heritability h², selection differential S, selection intensity i, accuracy r, genetic standard deviation σg), rate = R divided by cycle length, in the trait's own units per year. This is a prediction, an indication of direction only, and must be labelled as such. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1: field measurement from the pipeline's own replicated multi-environment trials, carrying a common check set that connects entries across years, plus purpose-run trials comparing material from different eras where a baseline must be built from scratch. Only this source measures the trait on the germplasm whose gain is claimed. Fallback DS2: historical trial results and pedigree or marker-based relationship records already held in the breeding data management system, where no fresh measurement round is possible; always flagged, because historical series often lack the check connectivity the method needs, so genotype itself is fitted as random through an additive relationship matrix (the estimated-breeding-value method) rather than as the fixed effect step (2) uses, and that relationship-based correction shrinks estimates toward zero and so understates gain. Fallback DS4: national variety registration trial series published by a seed authority, testing released varieties outside the programme's management, usable only where each entry's creation year is documented; flagged, because the entry set is small and the traits, protocols and environment coverage are the authority's. Not applicable DS3: satellite and geospatial products cannot resolve the trait performance of one genotype in a trial plot. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced varietal observations are not replicated, calibrated measurements against a common check set, so they cannot support the regression.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role the project used. For a fallback, name which one and why measurement in the pipeline's own trials was not feasible, and repeat the flag in the same sentence as the value.
collectionInstrument: For DS1: the pipeline's replicated multi-environment trial protocol for the declared trait, with a documented check strategy. The manual of record sets the minimum number of checks equal to the years in one breeding cycle at every stage, with two or three times that preferred at early stages, replaces a quarter of them each cycle length, and keeps one or two permanently so all trials stay linked. Respondent rule: not applicable, these are physical measurements on trial plots. Mode: field measurement recorded in the breeding data management system with year of origin, pedigree, location and year of evaluation.
collectionFrequency: Phenotypic data are collected every season through the pipeline's routine trials; the estimate is re-fitted annually on the rolling window.
reportingFrequency: Annually, one value per breeding pipeline, target trait and target set of environments, from late-stage multi-environment testing as the default stage; not per crop and not per market segment, and a pipeline serving more than one target set of environments gives one value per set. Values from other stages of testing are reportable, labelled with the stage, but are never compared with late-stage values, because a gain estimated from early trials and one from on-farm testing are different quantities.
referencePeriod: A fixed ten-year window of years of origin, not ten calendar years, across all pipelines, so that values stay comparable across crops and across reporting years: the ten most recent years of origin with an estimable genotype mean at the declared stage, both endpoints stated with the value; a year with no estimable mean is skipped and named with the value, so the stated endpoints can span more than ten calendar years. The window is not chosen by the pipeline. A slope cannot be computed for a single year, so the period is always multi-year and is stated with every value.
baselineRequired: Yes. A rate is meaningless without its reference: the reference mean and both endpoints of the window must be stated. Fallbacks where a pipeline has no usable historical series: apply the relationship-based correction to reconnect poorly linked years, flagged as likely to understate gain; or run a purpose-built trial comparing material from different eras while the check and connectivity practices are adopted; or, where a single season's selection differential and heritability are known, the breeder's-equation fallback in Calculation method gives a predicted rate, labelled as a prediction rather than a measurement and requiring no trial series of different years of origin at all. If none of the three is feasible, the pipeline can report trial results but not a rate of genetic gain.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Across projects and pipelines: values from different pipelines, crops, traits or target environments are not commensurable, since a slope for one crop and region says nothing about another. Report the set of pipeline-level values; a portfolio view follows Block C.

B: Combination method. Model-based, one fitted value per combination, and not aggregated beyond it: each value belongs to one breeding pipeline, trait, stage of testing and target set of environments, computed once from that pipeline's pooled trial data for that combination; two pipelines sharing a crop, trait and target set of environments, such as hybrid and open-pollinated maize, give two values and never one regression. Never average slopes.

C: Levels and operations. A rate of gain sits at no reporting level. The value is computed once for one breeding pipeline, one trait, one stage of testing and one set of target environments, from that pipeline's pooled trial data for that combination, and it is never averaged, summed or re-weighted upward: a mean of slopes is not a slope, because each is fitted to a different entry set over a different window of years of origin. Where a portfolio view is wanted there is no institutional number to give; report the distribution instead, that is the number of values estimated, the median and the range in the percentage form, with every value's stage of testing and reference mean shown alongside it, since a percentage alone cannot be compared across pipelines with different reference means, and fallback-sourced estimates listed beside the others rather than inside them; values with no percentage form under Unit of measure, listed in absolute form with their trait or index label, and breeder's-equation predictions, labelled predicted whatever source their inputs came from, are also listed beside the distribution, never inside it, and the number of each is stated with it. A lower-level view is re-fitted from that subset's own trial data, never read off a wider estimate. Also report: with every value, its reference mean and the permanent checks it was taken from (where the percentage form is computed), cycle length, window of years of origin, standard error, the entry, environment and year counts, and the number of entries per year of origin, since a slope without them cannot be judged; and, as a connectivity diagnostic distinct from the check count, the number of environments per year of origin in which at least one permanent check was co-tested, since a series can meet the check-count minimum every year while sharing no check between the window's first and last years, which the count alone does not detect.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: no. A slope in trait units cannot be combined arithmetically with the percentage of farmers reported by the impact indicator this one feeds, so that link runs through the theory of change.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: slopes are never summed, so a genotype tested in two pipelines enters each estimate it was tested in; estimates from different stages of one pipeline are alternative views of it, not separate achievements to add. Named overlaps: KPI-O13 counts lines advanced through the same trials, KPI-OC12 measures the age of the varieties this pipeline released, KPI-I06 sits downstream of both. None is additive with a gain rate. A slope whose 95 per cent confidence interval includes zero is reported with that interval and described as not distinguishable from zero, never presented as a rate of gain; outside a purpose-run era trial, an estimate fitted below the stage's minimum check-count requirement set under Collection instrument, the mechanism that maintains connectivity, is flagged on the same basis as a Fallback-sourced value, since low connectivity confounds the estimate with the year effect on the same footing as an unreliable source. Outside a purpose-run era trial, where every entry shares every environment, an estimate in which any year of origin in the window has no environment co-testing a permanent check, or in which no permanent check is shared between the window's first and last years, is flagged on the same basis.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Year of origin means the year the material was created, the year of the cross from which it derives, for every entry in the series including material already released as a variety, matching the manual of record's own worked model, which dates entries by creation year throughout (Reference standards); a pipeline whose records hold only the fixed-line year uses that for every entry and says so with the value, and never mixes the two in one series. The manual separately notes that some programmes instead date released material by its year of release; this sheet does not adopt that alternative, since the release year adds a registration lag that differs between countries and eras and dates the regulatory decision, not the genetics. Inclusions: every entry at the declared stage with a year of origin and a measured value for the declared trait in the declared environments, plus the common checks that connect years. In a hybrid pipeline the entries are hybrids, or testcrosses on the pipeline's declared tester, never inbred lines evaluated per se, and the tester is named with the value.
limitations: The value is a model estimate, not a measurement, and its accuracy rests on two properties of the trial design rather than of the breeding: how well trials cover the pipeline's target environments, and how well common checks connect material from different years. A poorly connected pipeline can report a wrong number confidently, so the entry, environment and year counts and the standard error must travel with every value. Released or advanced material also carries a survivorship confound the manual of record names for this reason: such material represents the tail of its era's trait distribution, not that era's mean, since it is what survived selection into later testing, so the trend can partly reflect which entries survived to be tested, not only genetic gain.

Estimates from different stages of testing are not comparable. Early-stage material represents the breeding population but is tested in few environments; registration and on-farm trials represent the target environments but cover few, already screened entries. Comparing across stages compares trial designs, not breeding performance.

Gain inside the programme's trials is not gain delivered to farmers. It becomes farm-level benefit only if the material is released, multiplied, bought and grown, none of which this indicator measures. Pair it with varietal turnover, seed volume and adoption indicators before any claim about farms.

Comparability rests on two conventions, and this sheet fixes both rather than leaving them to the pipeline: the reference mean is taken from the permanent checks and the cycle length is the parent recycling interval. What remains is that each percentage is relative to its own pipeline's reference mean and its own trait scale, so two pipelines can report identical percentages while differing in real trait improvement; read the absolute form and the reference mean alongside the percentage before comparing them.

A rising rate means the pipeline is improving the declared trait faster than before in the declared environments. It does not mean genetic diversity is maintained, other traits are holding, or farmers are better off; a fall may reflect a change in trial design, checks or testing network rather than in breeding; and a permanent check that loses resistance to a new pathogen race, or whose seed stock drifts, is read as a poorer year and inflates the rate.
subMetrics: None. The annual slope, the cycle length and the reference mean are inputs to one calculation, not separately reported metrics, and none has its own reference sheet. The four levers of the breeder's equation (selection intensity, accuracy, genetic standard deviation and cycle length) are diagnostics that explain why a rate moved, best carried as a narrative note. Related sheets: KPI-O13, KPI-OC12, KPI-I06.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the breeding analytics function as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: breeding trial teams and data managers (plot measurements, year of origin, pedigree, checks). Validation: the pipeline's quantitative geneticist or breeding data specialist (check connectivity, environment coverage, estimability of genotype means). Calculation: breeding analytics function. Approval: breeding programme lead for the crop. Reporting: project or programme MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.

name: Area-weighted average age of CIMMYT-derived improved varieties in farmers' fields
resultsLevel: Outcome, per CIMMYT's MEAL Framework definition, which governs the register: what is measured is a change in what external actors (farmers, and the seed businesses and agrodealers supplying them) choose to plant and sell, not a result CIMMYT delivers directly. CGIAR's control-and-externality test reaches the same classification here, so there is no crosswalk divergence to record. The delivered results upstream, varieties released and quality seed produced, are counted separately at output level.
primaryObjective: PO2 Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved); PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Nutrition, Health & Food Security. The pathway-wide rule sets the area by what the indicator measures, which is the age of the improved varieties reaching and staying in farmers' fields, on the way to food and nutrition security outcomes. The register carries no Impact Area column; the value follows the pathway-wide rule stated in the opening paragraph of this volume's Introduction.
sdgTarget: None. No SDG indicator measures varietal turnover or the age of the varieties farmers grow. The closest target, 2.5 (maintain the genetic diversity of seeds and cultivated plants), is monitored by indicator 2.5.1, a count of genetic resources held in medium- or long-term conservation facilities, and by 2.5.2, the proportion of local and transboundary breeds at risk of extinction, an animal genetic resources indicator: neither measures what is planted.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Excellence in Breeding treats variety turnover as the condition under which genetic gain reaches end users, in its manual on genetic gain as a high-level key performance indicator. The AGRA and CGIAR IMAGE programme (Institutionalizing Monitoring of Crop Variety Adoption using Genotyping) lists varietal age among the genetic-gain metrics national varietal-monitoring systems should produce. ICARDA's indicator OC-10 (Bikara et al., 2024) measures the same quantity, area- or seed-volume-weighted years since official release, direction decrease; it also ages landraces from first planting, which this indicator excludes. There is no normative international standard for varietal age: this indicator rests on CIMMYT's own research practice (see Reference standards).
definition: Measures how old, on average, the CIMMYT-derived improved varieties growing in farmers' fields are, in years, averaged over the area planted rather than over the number of varieties. A variety's age is the reporting year minus the year it was officially released in the country where it is grown. A falling value usually means newer genetics occupy more land (faster turnover within the CIMMYT-derived area), on the reading set out under Direction of change; a rising value means farmers are holding on to older material. Calculated per crop and country.
rationale: Answers whether the improved genetics CIMMYT and its partners develop reach and replace what farmers grow, and how fast. A breeding programme can raise genetic gain per year without any of it arriving on farms, because release, seed multiplication, distribution and farmer choice all sit between the breeder and the field. Average varietal age shows whether delivery from release to the field is working: it is the on-farm counterpart to genetic gain per year (KPI-OC11) and a pre-condition for CIMMYT's productivity claims (KPI-I06), and it serves institutional and donor reporting on the reach of breeding investment.
projectSpecificApplication: State which crops, countries, survey areas and cropping seasons the project covers, and how it establishes that a variety is CIMMYT-derived and what its release year in each country is. Do not change the unit, the weighting basis or the calculation method. If area-weighted measurement is not feasible, use the fallback source below and label the value accordingly rather than redefining the indicator here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor requirement this value informs, for example a varietal turnover target in the project's districts, or an adaptive-management trigger: an average age that stops falling while new releases keep arriving points to a seed multiplication or demand bottleneck rather than a breeding one.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose work is laboratory and controlled-environment research with no farmers' fields to survey
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose work is laboratory and controlled-environment research with no farmers' fields to survey.
unit: Years (area-weighted mean years since release)
directionOfChange: Decrease. A falling value means the CIMMYT-derived varieties in farmers' fields are younger on average, weighted by area planted. Read it with the CIMMYT-derived share of measured area: the mean also falls when CIMMYT-derived material older than the mean leaves the base, and when CIMMYT-derived material displaces landraces or non-CIMMYT varieties it falls if the new variety is younger than the mean and rises if it is older.
disaggregationRequired: Required: crop, per the register, since breeding cycles, release frequency and seed systems differ so much between crops that a pooled cross-crop mean is not interpretable. In addition, country is a required disaggregation alongside crop, because release years are set by national or regional authorities, so one variety carries different ages in different countries and a pooled multi-country mean mixes varieties with different availability dates. The register does not name it; this toolbox requires it, on the sheet's authority. Every value must also be labelled with the weighting basis that produced it, area-weighted (recommended) or quantity-weighted (fallback); a labelling rule rather than a disaggregation, and the two are never combined.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: Variety, for seed systems and deployment and breeding and varietal development projects. Those two types deliver the variety, and which varieties carry the weight is the cut they need; the crop-level mean is unchanged by it.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Agroecological zone or region; variety type (hybrid, open-pollinated variety); seed source (public or private); sex of the plot decision-maker; farm size class.
unitOfObservation: Plot (plot-season), nested within household.
calculationSummary: Numerator: across all measured plots planted to CIMMYT-derived improved varieties, the sum of plot area multiplied by the age of the variety on that plot, where age = reporting year minus the release year in the country where the variety is grown, since release dates differ by years between countries and varietal age is about what farmers in that country have had access to. Denominator: total measured area planted to confirmed CIMMYT-derived improved varieties. Value = numerator / denominator, in years, per crop and country. Where the survey design is not self-weighting, each plot's area enters both terms multiplied by the plot's survey design weight, so the two sums estimate the population's area rather than the sample's. Equivalently: the sum over varieties of (share of area under variety i) x (age of variety i). Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1: household or plot-level adoption survey with variety identification, giving area planted by variety. Because farmers frequently misidentify or cannot name what they grow, this means the survey plus genotyping (DNA fingerprinting) of field samples against a genetic reference library, as in the household surveys with field-sample genotyping behind the Ethiopian varietal turnover estimates and the AGRA and CGIAR IMAGE country surveys. Release years are looked up in the national or regional variety release register (for example KEPHIS in Kenya, the Seed Certification and Control Institute in Zambia) and in seed company catalogues: a Frame DS2 source, supplying each variety's release year and producing no value. Fallback DS2: seed-system volume records (seed company, agrodealer or national distribution data), which yield a quantity-weighted average varietal age. Administrative and low-cost, but a different measure: reported as its own series and never merged into the area-weighted one (see Aggregation rule). Fallback DS4: published national seed-sector statistics, used only where partner distribution records are inaccessible, carrying the same quantity-weighted label. Not applicable DS3: Earth observation can map crop area but cannot identify which variety is planted on it. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced and mobile data cannot establish area planted by variety with the reliability an area-weighted mean requires.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether the Recommended or a Fallback source was used, and label the value area-weighted or quantity-weighted accordingly. If Fallback, state why an adoption survey with variety identification was not feasible and which records were used.
collectionInstrument: Plot roster module in the household adoption survey: crop, measured plot area (GPS), farmer-reported variety name and seed source, plus a leaf or grain sample for genotyping against the crop's genetic reference library. Respondent: the person who makes planting decisions for the plot. Mode: face-to-face with a visit to the plot.
collectionFrequency: With each adoption survey round: at least every 2 to 3 years, since genotyped surveys are costly to field. Where the fallback is used, annually from seed-system records.
reportingFrequency: Annually, published, indicative or withheld under the unidentified-share rule in Eligibility criteria and missing data and the precision bands in Aggregation rule Block E. Between survey rounds the latest measured value is carried forward with the reporting year its ages are anchored to, and its measurement date, stated, and is not re-aged: adding a year to an old value would fabricate a trend.
referencePeriod: The cropping season or seasons falling within the reporting year. Where seasons straddle the calendar year, the CIMMYT MEAL unit fixes per country which cropping seasons a reporting year covers, and the convention is held constant across rounds. Ages are computed against the reporting year the round's season belongs to, so a value carried forward between survey rounds keeps the ages of its round and is not re-aged, under Reporting frequency.
baselineRequired: Yes. A single value means little on its own, since what counts as an old variety differs by crop and country; the value is interpreted through the direction and pace of change. Fallbacks where no prospective baseline exists: an earlier adoption survey round in the same area, an earlier published adoption study, or pre-period seed-system records (quantity-weighted, labelled, and compared only with later quantity-weighted values). If none is feasible: monitoring only, no turnover claim.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool area-weighted values from projects using the Recommended source, per crop and country, on one season-to-reporting-year convention fixed per country by the CIMMYT MEAL unit and part of the pooling domain, so that two projects cannot split one straddling season into two reporting years; each project entering with its survey-weighted area, the area its sample represents rather than the area it measured; a project reporting the quantity-weighted fallback is presented alongside the pooled figure with a note, never blended in; a farmer-reported value is presented alongside the pooled figure with a note, as the quantity-weighted fallback is. Seed distributed in a year is systematically newer than seed already planted on farms, because farmers keep growing and recycling older varieties, so quantity-weighted values read younger, and splicing the two would manufacture a downward trend.

B: Combination method. Pooled and area-weighted: the institutional figure for a crop and country is the survey-weighted total of (area x age) across every plot reported by every project, divided by the survey-weighted total area, the Calculation method's formula at wider scope. Never take an unweighted average of project-level averages, and no figure is computed across crops or across countries: each crop and country is its own domain, and crops and countries are reported side by side.

C: Levels and operations. An area-weighted mean is a ratio of two sums, recomputed at every level from its own numerator and denominator, and never averaged from the levels beneath it. At Farm / Plot, area multiplied by the age of the variety on that plot; no mean is reported at that level. At Project area and at Regional / Aggregated, the survey-weighted sum of area-times-age over the survey-weighted sum of area, per crop and country, within the pooling domain of Block A; values for different countries are reported side by side and never combined. The weighting basis is part of the value: area-weighted and quantity-weighted figures are recomputed and reported as two series and never spliced. Also report: the total measured area behind the mean, the base record count behind the 30-record floor, the unidentified share, the CIMMYT-derived share of measured area and the share that is CIMMYT-derived but not released in country, all defined in Eligibility, the crop and country of every value, and, where the value is carried forward, the reporting year its ages are anchored to and its measurement date.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This value never combines arithmetically with genetic gain per year (KPI-OC11), with variety releases or seed volumes at output level, or with the productivity impact indicator (KPI-I06); those levels connect through the theory of change, not by arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. De-duplicate on the household and plot identifiers plus season within one survey, from Project area level upward, so a plot-season enters the pooled sums once whichever projects file the survey; frame overlap between different surveys is a different problem and is handled as follows. (3) Double counting: since this is a weighted mean rather than a count, overlap distorts the weights rather than inflating a total. Where two projects' sampling frames overlap, each survey's design weights already represent the shared area, so dropping shared plots does not remove the double representation: pool only surveys whose frames partition the domain, or re-derive the design weights for the combined sample; where neither is possible, report the project values separately. Report coverage and precision with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands: 16.5 per cent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 per cent released flagged, above 33.3 per cent not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one de-duplicated plot-season in the mean's base, identified, CIMMYT-derived and carrying a release year, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place. One survey feeding both this indicator and adoption indicators elsewhere in the register is legitimate reuse, since nothing is summed across them.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusions: plots whose variety is identified and confirmed CIMMYT-derived, meaning the variety is itself a CIMMYT line or population, or CIMMYT germplasm appears in its pedigree as a parent or grandparent, matching the maximum ancestry depth used for genebank material in KPI-OC14, two generations (KPI-OC14's pre-breeding provision does not apply); no minimum percentage of CIMMYT parentage is set, since pedigree shares are not reliably recorded. A generation is one cross or one line extraction, so for a hybrid the parents are the components of the final cross, and where a component is itself a hybrid its own parents are the grandparents. The variety also carries a documented release year in the country where it is grown, and the plot has a measured or GPS-measured area. A plot's variety is identified when its field sample matches an entry in the crop's genetic reference library. Where a survey fielded no genotyping, the value is computed on farmer-reported names, labelled farmer-reported, with a farmer-reported name standing in for identification in its unidentified share, and reported beside the pooled genotype-identified figure, never blended into it.

Exclusions: landraces and improved varieties positively confirmed not CIMMYT-derived, which are outside the indicator and are never assigned a nominal age.

Missing data: plots whose sample genotyping could not identify, plots of an identified variety whose CIMMYT-derivation cannot be established from pedigree records, and plots of an identified CIMMYT-derived variety whose release year in the country where it is grown cannot be documented, are dropped from both numerator and denominator and not imputed. Unidentified share = U / (U + B), where U is the survey-weighted area of these dropped plots and B is the survey-weighted area of identified CIMMYT-derived plots with a release year, the mean's own base; the denominator is thus the largest area the mean could possibly cover rather than the crop's total area, and the share describes the area the mean estimates rather than the area measured. Plots of an identified CIMMYT-derived variety confirmed not released in the country where it is grown have no age on this indicator's basis; they are dropped from both terms, do not enter the unidentified share, and their survey-weighted share of the crop's measured area is reported beside the value as "CIMMYT-derived, not released in country". The unidentified share is published with every value, and the value is reported as indicative above 20 per cent and is not published above 40 per cent. The rule applies to every published value on its own unidentified share, pooled values included: a component withheld on its own share does not enter a pool and is listed beneath it. Area of landraces and improved varieties positively confirmed not CIMMYT-derived does not enter the unidentified share. The CIMMYT-derived share of the crop's measured area is reported beside every value. Plots with no measured area are dropped and their number is reported.

Repeated observations: the unit is the plot-season; a plot measured in two seasons of one reporting year contributes both, with their own areas, while a plot revisited within a season contributes only its first complete record. On the quantity-weighted Fallback the record is the seed quantity of one variety distributed in the country in the reporting year: the CIMMYT-derivation and release-year tests apply to the variety, quantity replaces area in both terms and in the unidentified share, which is published on the same 20 and 40 per cent rule and labelled quantity-based, and the plot, measured-area and plot-season rules do not apply. The precision bands and record floor in Aggregation rule Block E apply to survey estimates only.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only. What farmers grow is shaped by national release decisions, seed multiplication capacity, agrodealer stocking, price, familiarity and risk aversion, with CIMMYT one contributor among many; CIMMYT-derived varieties are also released and marketed by national partners under their own names. A fall does not show that yields, incomes or genetic gain improved, on the reading set out under Direction of change: displacement of landraces or non-CIMMYT varieties does not move the mean in one direction only, and rapid churn among varieties of similar performance would also lower the value, so read it with genetic gain per year and with productivity outcomes.

Variety identification is the main source of measurement error. Farmer-reported names cannot carry turnover estimates on their own, because of both non-identification and misidentification; genotyping is the control, but it depends on a complete genetic reference library, and widely grown varieties missing from that library return unidentified samples that are dropped.

Comparability is limited by design: age counts from the release year in the country where the variety is grown, so one variety carries different ages in different countries and registration practice differs between them, and area-weighted and quantity-weighted values are different measures. Compare within crop and country over time.

The mean hides the tail: it can fall while a large minority of the area stays under material 20 years old or more. Where turnover is the management question, read it with the share of area under the oldest cohort.
The value is weighted by hectares, not holdings, so it says nothing about how many farmers grow the varieties; no indicator in this pathway counts them.
subMetrics: None. Crop, country, variety type and seed source are disaggregations of the same weighted mean, not separately calculated metrics. Related indicators carry their own sheets: KPI-OC11 (genetic gain per year), which this one qualifies by showing whether that gain reaches farms, and KPI-I06 (measured smallholder farmers with a detectable increase in agricultural productivity, as a contribution of CIMMYT support), which it feeds.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the CIMMYT crop breeding or seed systems team as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E team and enumerators for the plot roster and sampling; genotyping laboratory or service provider for variety identification. Validation: project MEAL officer for survey data quality; CIMMYT crop breeding or seed systems team for each variety's CIMMYT-derived status and release year. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (area weighting, exclusions, pooling, de-duplication). Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 4 · Genetic resources, breeding & seed — Reference sheet KPI-OC12

name: Percentage of varietal releases utilising conserved genetic resources
resultsLevel: Outcome, per CIMMYT's MEAL Framework definition, which governs the register. Under the CGIAR test of control and externality, what this indicator counts, whether conserved material sits within two generations of the released variety, is fixed by crossing and selection decisions CIMMYT and its partners take, which would point to Output level, although the release event it is read on is an external authority's decision (KPI-O12); the divergence from CGIAR's control test is handled once in the crosswalk annex.
primaryObjective: PO2 Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries. Contributing: PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Environmental Health & Biodiversity. CGIAR files conserved plant genetic accessions under this Impact Area; this indicator measures the use side of the same resource. The food and nutrition security link is carried by the 2030 objective above.
sdgTarget: None. The indicator serves SDG target 2.5 (maintain the genetic diversity of seeds and cultivated plants, and promote access to and benefit-sharing from the use of genetic resources), but no official SDG indicator measures use: 2.5.1(a) counts plant genetic accessions secured in medium- or long-term conservation facilities, a stock of conserved material, and 2.5.2 is the proportion of local and transboundary breeds at risk of extinction, an animal genetic resources indicator.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR results framework: the standard indicator on plant genetic accessions available and safely duplicated, filed under Environmental Health and Biodiversity. This indicator complements it rather than duplicating it, since that one counts what is held and this one measures what is used; CGIAR's own assessment of that indicator found it measures genebank output. International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture: material leaving a genebank for crops in the Treaty's Multilateral System is transferred under the Standard Material Transfer Agreement, so a documented transfer trail exists for the germplasm traced here; named for context only, not separately cited, since the transfer trail itself is evidenced by CIMMYT's own distribution and acquisition records under Data source.
definition: The share of the reporting year's variety releases, counted as variety-country release events on KPI-O12's basis, in which at least one accession obtained from a genebank, or the documented pre-breeding product derived from a landrace or wild-population accession, is documented as a parent or grandparent of the released variety, or the released variety is itself such an accession. An accession is a distinct sample of seeds, planting material or plants maintained in any ex situ genebank, including other CGIAR centres' and national collections, not CIMMYT's own bank alone, per the FAO definition. The indicator asks not how much diversity is stored, but how much reaches a released variety.
rationale: Answers whether conserved genetic diversity is used to produce the varieties farmers receive, which is the evidence that genebanks work as a resource for crop improvement rather than a store. Institutional reporting uses it to complete the conservation narrative accession counts alone cannot tell; genebank and breeding management use it to see whether pre-breeding and germplasm requests translate into released varieties.
projectSpecificApplication: State which crops, breeding programmes and release countries fall within the project's scope, and which reporting year's release events it counts. Do not change the numerator and denominator construction, the accession definition, or the institutional ancestry rule. If pedigree records cannot be retrieved for part of the releases, report the untraceable count alongside the value rather than treating those releases as having no genebank ancestry, and raise the records gap with the MEAL focal point.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this share informs: for example a donor requirement to evidence use of conserved genetic resources, or a decision on pre-breeding investment in landraces and wild populations if the share stays flat while accession requests rise.
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; seed systems and deployment.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, which produces genes, markers and characterised material rather than release candidates; applied agronomy and farming systems; system change and transformation; and digital agriculture and AI.
unit: Percentage of variety releases
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of variety releases drew on conserved genebank material, which is what links conservation to use. Ancestry is counted at parent or grandparent depth; an any-depth rule would count almost any modern cereal variety whose distant pedigree is documented, and would measure record depth rather than use.
disaggregationRequired: Required: crop; trait class, on the eight-class controlled vocabulary set out on KPI-O10; a release carrying several traits is filed under the class that justified its release and listed under the others in a secondary field, as on KPI-O12; class of accession, on the five-term vocabulary set out on KPI-O14 (a wild population, a landrace, a breeding line, a breeding population or an improved cultivar), with crop wild relative recorded as an optional second-level tag within wild population; genebank of origin (CIMMYT germplasm bank; other CGIAR genebank; national or other genebank). Class of accession is required because the headline cannot otherwise separate the use of landraces and wild populations, this indicator's purpose, from that of elite lines routed through the genebank, which reach two-generation depth far more easily. A release whose qualifying accessions (a parent or grandparent, or the released variety itself; for a documented pre-breeding product, the accession it derives from) belong to more than one class is reported under each class it qualifies on and counted once in the headline, so class subtotals can exceed the headline and are never summed to it, and the number of releases qualifying on more than one class is reported beside the cut.
