This deliberately differs from the trait-class rule on KPI-O10, which files an element under a primary class and lists it under the others in a secondary field: no class of accession is primary, because the ancestry rule does not rank the accessions a release drew on. Genebank of origin is the holding genebank recorded for the accession and follows the class-of-accession rule: a release drawing on accessions recorded against more than one genebank is reported under each and counted once in the headline, and the number of such releases is reported beside the cut. Genebank of origin is required because the numerator admits ancestry from any ex situ genebank, so only this cut separates the use of CIMMYT's own genebank, the figure that reads against KPI-O14, from the use of other collections. The register requires crop and trait class only, so these cuts are CIMMYT's own, applied on the sheet's authority.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Release country or region; form of use (the accession, or the documented pre-breeding product derived from it, is a parent or a grandparent).
unitOfObservation: The variety-country release event (one variety, legally available in one country by a national or a regional act), identified by the identifier of the released entry plus the country of legal availability, matching KPI-O12: the cross identifier for a hybrid, or the line or population identifier for an open-pollinated variety, inbred line or population. This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation; the release register is where it is observed, not what is counted.
calculationSummary: Numerator: variety releases in the reporting year for which at least one genebank accession, of any class, or the documented pre-breeding product derived from a landrace or wild-population accession, is documented as a parent or grandparent of the released variety, or the released variety is itself such an accession, established from genebank distribution records linked to breeding pedigree records. Denominator: variety-country release events on KPI-O12's release-event basis, for the same year and scope, less the releases excluded under Eligibility criteria and missing data and those Aggregation rule Block A reports alongside because their pedigree rests on the Fallback, so the denominator is KPI-O12's pooled headline for that scope, not the release events KPI-O12 reports beside it as Fallback-sourced, minus those releases, never a separately tallied release list. The register's denominator is all variety releases; this sheet departs from it by removing releases whose pedigree cannot be retrieved, which cannot be classed as using or not using genebank material, and the untraceable count is reported with every value. Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: administrative and registry data, specifically CIMMYT genebank accession and distribution records, together with the incoming acquisition and standard material transfer records that document material received from other CGIAR centres and national collections, linked to breeding pedigree records and to the official release records that feed KPI-O12. Distribution records alone cannot evidence an accession obtained from another genebank, and the definition admits any ex situ genebank, so the transfer trail is what makes that ancestry documentable. This combined registry is the only source that observes numerator and denominator on the same release events with the same identifiers. Fallback DS4: public genetic-resource and variety information systems, including genebank information systems and national or regional variety release catalogues, used only where ancestry has to be reconstructed outside CIMMYT systems, for example for partner-led or historical releases; any value built this way is flagged as fallback-sourced, because reconstructed pedigrees are systematically incomplete and understate genebank use. Not applicable DS1: neither numerator nor denominator can be obtained from respondents or field measurement, since ancestry and release status are documentary facts, not observable conditions. Not applicable DS3: satellite, aerial and GIS data cannot observe a pedigree or a release event. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced data cannot establish documented ancestry or official release status.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which route each release's pedigree rests on, Recommended or Fallback; for releases on the Fallback, name the public systems that reconstructed the pedigree; and state how many releases stayed untraceable.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). The indicator is built from administrative and registry records (DS2) or published information systems (DS4); no survey module or field instrument is involved.
collectionFrequency: Annually, compiled at year end from genebank distribution, breeding pedigree and official release records.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Because the number of releases in a single year is small, report a three-year pooled share alongside the annual value, the numerators of the three most recent reporting years summed over their denominators summed and never a mean of three annual percentages; one year's share moves sharply on one or two releases and should not be read alone. Both the annual and the three-year figures are computed from the release and pedigree records as they stand at the reporting date, so a restated year enters restated; a restatement of KPI-O12's headline restates this share and any three-year figure the year enters, under Core Section 4.2.
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the release occurred, on the same calendar or fiscal basis as KPI-O12. Ancestry is a historical fact about the variety, so the period applies to the release event, not to when the genebank material was obtained.
baselineRequired: Yes, since the value is only interpretable as a trend. Because the indicator is records-based rather than survey-based, a retrospective baseline is normally feasible: recompute the share for earlier reporting years from the same release and pedigree records. If records do not extend back far enough, monitor forward from the first computed year, with no change claims against earlier periods.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool the releases whose ancestry is evidenced in CIMMYT's linked genebank and breeding records (Recommended); a release whose ancestry is evidenced only in public systems (Fallback) is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, not blended in, and leaves the pooled denominator as well as the pooled numerator; a release evidenced on both is Recommended-sourced and pooled, and the same project's Recommended-sourced releases stay in the pool.

B: Combination method. Pool as one ratio: sum the numerators and sum the denominators across crops, breeding programmes and reporting units, and for the three-year figure across the three years, then divide. Never average crop-level or programme-level percentages, which over-weights crops with few releases.

C: Levels and operations. A share is recomputed at every level from its own numerator and denominator, never averaged from the levels beneath it. The denominator is not a project's own tally of releases: it is the KPI-O12 release list for the same reporting year and scope, less the pedigree-untraceable releases excluded from both terms and the Fallback-sourced releases reported alongside, so both terms are recomputed from that list at each level rather than added up, and a release outside KPI-O12's pooled headline cannot enter this numerator. At project level, that project's releases in the denominator above that meet the numerator rule, over that project's releases in the denominator above. At institutional level, the summed numerator over the summed denominator within the pooling domain of Block A. Also report: both counts rather than the percentage alone, the number of releases whose pedigree could not be traced, which are excluded from both terms and never counted as having no genebank ancestry, the number whose retrieved pedigree has a parent or grandparent of undocumented origin, the number of releases qualifying on more than one class of accession, the number drawing on more than one genebank, and the number of releases reported alongside because their pedigree rests on the Fallback.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. Every release in this numerator is already counted in KPI-O12 (number of improved varieties released), which supplies the denominator, and the same releases may also appear in the genetic gain (KPI-OC11) and varietal age (KPI-OC12) indicators. Those indicators answer different questions about the same events and must never be summed into a combined figure; the levels connect through the theory of change, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: de-duplicate on the identifier of the released entry plus the country of legal availability before pooling, matching KPI-O12's Block B, so a release event reported by more than one programme is counted once while a variety released in several countries keeps one event per country in both numerator and denominator; two distinct hybrids sharing one parent line are two releases, never collapsed to one. Where identifiers cannot be matched across reporting units, label the pooled figure an upper estimate and the share provisional.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: varieties officially registered or approved for multiplication in the reporting year, applying KPI-O12's release definition, so this indicator's denominator is drawn from KPI-O12's release population on one event basis. A genebank accession of any class qualifies only where it is the released variety itself or appears as a parent or grandparent of it, not merely somewhere in its distant ancestry, matching the maximum ancestry depth KPI-OC12 applies, two generations; a released variety that is itself a genebank accession, obtained from a genebank's collection under a distribution or acquisition record dated before its release and released without further crossing, qualifies at depth zero; a line deposited in a genebank as part of, or after, its own release does not. A generation is one cross or one line extraction, so for a hybrid the parents are the components of the final cross, and where a component is itself a hybrid its own parents are the grandparents. The ancestry depth is the single largest determinant of the value. A documented pre-breeding product is material developed to move traits from unadapted genetic resources into a usable genetic background before entry into the mainstream breeding pipeline. Where that product derives from a named genebank accession of landrace or wild population class, with the derivation on record, ancestry depth is counted from the pre-breeding product rather than from the original accession. This is what lets a landrace or wild-population accession routed through pre-breeding still reach a release within two generations, and it does not extend to an elite line or breeding population re-deposited and later redrawn as if newly sourced. Where a synthetic or a wide cross carries no documented pedigree link back to a named accession, it is not counted as genebank-derived.

Exclusion: releases whose pedigree record cannot be retrieved, which leave both numerator and denominator (see Missing data). Two boundary notes, neither an exclusion because neither was ever in the denominator: elite lines and breeding populations advanced but not released (KPI-O13) are not releases, and accessions distributed by the genebank that have not yet produced a release are not releases either.

Missing data: a release is untraceable only when its pedigree record cannot be retrieved at all; it is then excluded from both numerator and denominator, never counted as having no genebank ancestry, and the untraceable count is reported with the value. On the Recommended route the pedigree record is the breeding programme's own record for the released line; on the Fallback route it is the pedigree reconstructed from public systems, a catalogue statement of parentage included. A release with no breeding record retrievable takes the Fallback route where a public system records its parentage, and is untraceable only where neither route retrieves a pedigree. Within a retrieved pedigree, a parent or grandparent with no distribution or incoming transfer record from a genebank counts as not a genebank accession, whether or not the same line is also held as an accession, so an incomplete record lowers the value rather than removing the release, and the number of releases so affected is reported with the value. A release whose qualifying accession is documented as a genebank accession but has no recorded class of accession or genebank of origin stays in the numerator and is reported under a not-available category on the cut concerned.

Repeated observations: one count per variety-country release event, the same release-event basis as KPI-O12, so the two indicators cannot diverge. A variety with several genebank accessions in its ancestry still counts once per release event, and where those accessions belong to more than one class, or are recorded against more than one genebank, the release is reported under each class in the class-of-accession cut and under each genebank in the genebank-of-origin cut while the headline counts it once; a variety released in more than one country counts once per country of legal availability, and its ancestry status carries to each of its release events.
limitations: Measures documented ancestry, not contribution. A variety with one genebank accession as a grandparent counts the same as one bred directly from a landrace for a specific trait; the indicator says nothing about how much the conserved material shaped performance.

The value depends almost entirely on the ancestry rule applied. Counting any genebank accession anywhere in a variety's ancestry would score most documented CIMMYT cereal pedigrees and carry little information; counting only direct parents gives a lower and more informative figure; this indicator counts at parent or grandparent depth, the rule stated under Eligibility criteria and missing data. Values built on different rules are not comparable, and the rule must be stated with every figure. That ancestry rule, where an accession of any class qualifies, structurally favours elite lines routed through the genebank over the pre-breeding pathway this indicator's Rationale names as its purpose: a landrace or wild-population accession normally reaches release through several pre-breeding generations, so it clears two-generation depth only where the pre-breeding provision under Eligibility applies, while an elite line clears it easily. Because depth is counted in crosses, the same source accession sits one generation deeper in a three-way or double-cross hybrid than in a single-cross hybrid or a pure line, so read maize values with the hybrid types released that year. Read the value with the class-of-accession disaggregation, never as a single undifferentiated share; a release qualifying on more than one class, or drawing on more than one genebank, is reported under each, so class and genebank-of-origin subtotals can exceed the headline and are never summed to it. The pre-breeding provision also has no stated limit on how many pre-breeding generations a chain may run before reaching a release: a landrace or wild-population accession's depth is bounded at two generations directly, or unbounded through a documented pre-breeding derivation chain, and this sheet does not fix a ceiling on that chain's length.
Small denominators make the annual value volatile. In a year with few releases, one variety moves the share by a large margin, so read it as a multi-year trend rather than an annual result.

Completeness of records sets a floor on accuracy. Older and partner-led releases, and material acquired before systematic distribution records existed, are weakly documented, and every gap inside a retrieved pedigree pushes the value downwards, while a release whose pedigree cannot be retrieved leaves both terms; report the untraceable count and the number of retrieved pedigrees with a parent or grandparent of undocumented origin, so that a records problem is not read as a use problem.

A rise means a larger share of the year's releases carried documented genebank ancestry. It does not mean the genebank contributed more to yield, resilience or adoption; pair with the genetic gain and conserved-accession indicators for the contribution narrative.
subMetrics: None. The required class-of-accession and genebank-of-origin cuts are disaggregations of one numerator, not separately calculated metrics; class and genebank-of-origin subtotals can exceed the headline and are never summed to it. Related sheets: KPI-O12 (improved crop varieties released), which supplies the denominator; KPI-O14 (accessions conserved with long-term viability) and KPI-O15 (accessions genetically characterised), the conservation and characterisation stages this indicator draws on.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the genebank head and the breeding programme leader as technical reviewers
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: CIMMYT germplasm bank (accession and distribution records) and breeding programme data managers (pedigree and release records). Validation: genebank and breeding data managers jointly, confirming a traceable link from accession to released variety for each release in the numerator. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, per the Calculation method above. Approval: breeding programme leader, with the genebank head confirming the accession side. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 4 · Genetic resources, breeding & seed — Reference sheet KPI-OC14

name: Number of farmers linked to financial services (credit, insurance, savings) through CIMMYT-supported interventions or linkages
resultsLevel: Output. The linkage event is facilitated and recorded through channels the project supports, a direct deliverable of CIMMYT activity, comparable to a partnership arising from a signed agreement, which CGIAR's quality assurance guidance classifies as an output. What the farmer then does with the connection is a change in behaviour, measured at outcome level by KPI-OC17.
indicatorScope: Mission. Measures a result delivered to an external population (smallholder farmers in intervention areas), so the sheet carries the project-specific layer.
domain: Cross-cutting / Common, as recorded in the register.
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Single primary objective (first-listed in the register row per convention). Contributing objective, contribution only: PO4 (agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs. Connecting farmers to finance is the delivery step of the livelihood pathway PO3 describes. One area only; the contribution to Gender Equality, Youth & Social Inclusion is carried by the required sex and age breakdowns. The register carries no Impact Area column; the pathway-wide rule sets Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs for every indicator here.
sdgTarget: None. SDG target 2.3 names access to financial services for small-scale food producers, but its indicators measure production per labour unit (2.3.1) and producer income (2.3.2), not access. SDG 8.10.2 measures the share of all adults with an account at a bank, other financial institution or mobile-money provider (UN metadata sheet Metadata-08-10-02): a population-level rate that cannot be reconciled with a project-facilitated linkage count.
otherFrameworks: No CGIAR Results Framework correspondence.
definition:
Counts unique farmers linked to financial services (credit, insurance, savings) through CIMMYT-supported interventions or linkages in the reporting year, counted once per farmer regardless of the number of services. Linkage means an established connection to a named provider, recorded and dated: the farmer appears on the provider's or the project's record for a specific service, reached through a channel the project supported. A referral or introduction the provider received and recorded qualifies, whether or not the provider has yet acted on it; so do an application taken up, an account opened, a loan approved or disbursed, a policy issued, and savings-group membership recorded. It is not mere awareness.

It is also not what the farmer then does with the connection. Whether the connection becomes a usable financial service the farmer holds is a separate result, measured downstream by KPI-OC17.
rationale: Answers how many farmers CIMMYT and its partners connected to credit, insurance or savings during the year. Financial access lets farming households diversify their livelihood strategies, protect well-being outcomes and manage risks. CIMMYT's own reading adds investment in improved technology. Projects use the count to check delivery and targeting of women and youth; institutionally it is the first, countable step of the pathway from linkage (this sheet) through improved access (KPI-OC17) to income gains (KPI-I03).
projectSpecificApplication: State which services this project links farmers to, the provider types, the countries and intervention areas, the linkage channels (direct facilitation, partner referral, finance bundled with a technology package), and the 12-month window covered. Do not change the institutional definition, unit, or one-farmer-one-count rule. If linked farmers cannot be identified individually, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining the indicator here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this figure serves, for example a contracted number of farmers to be linked, a targeting commitment to women or youth, or a mid-course decision on a provider partnership. Distinct from the institutional rationale above, which is identical for every project.
projectTypesNotApplicable: breeding and varietal development and digital agriculture and AI
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, breeding and varietal development and digital agriculture and AI, which do not broker financial linkages.
unit: Number of farmers (unique individuals)
directionOfChange: Increase, read against the project's targeting plan. A rising value means more farmers were connected to a financial service. It says nothing about whether the farmer then gains or upgrades a usable service, which KPI-OC17 measures.
disaggregationRequired: Required, per the register: sex (female, male) and age (youth, non-youth). Sex follows CGIAR's sex-disaggregated data standards (Doss & Kieran, 2014). The youth band is 15 to 30, stated once in Core §4.1; projects record date of birth or exact age so that other bands (for example a donor band of 15 to 29) can be derived. Each breakdown must sum exactly to the headline value.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator; no cut is specific to one project type.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Service type (credit, insurance, savings). Provider type (bank, microfinance institution, insurer, mobile-money provider, savings group). Linkage channel. Country and intervention area. New versus continuing linkage, where tracked. A farmer linked to more than one service appears under each service type, so the type breakdown may sum to more than the headline.
unitOfObservation: The individual farmer. A farmer linked through more than one channel is one farmer. A farmer linked by two projects is one farmer only where the projects' records can be matched; otherwise the pooled count is an upper bound, as Block E states.
calculationSummary: A count within the reporting year, not a ratio; no denominator. Value = number of unique farmers with at least one recorded linkage event to a financial service provider, established through a CIMMYT-supported intervention or facilitated linkage, dated within the reporting year. The test is that the connection is verified on both sides: the farmer is named and the provider or the project holds the record. A referral the provider never received, a name on a list the project passed on, an awareness or financial-literacy session, and a farmer's stated intention to approach a provider do not count, because none of them evidences a connection that exists. An approved but undisbursed loan does count, the connection being established at approval; whether the loan is disbursed is a question of use, and use is KPI-OC17's. Village savings and loan groups and other facilitated informal savings groups count as providers, with formality recorded as a disaggregation.
dataSource: Recommended, DS2 (Administrative and registry data): the project's own linkage register, one row per linkage event carrying farmer identifier, sex, age, service type, provider, evidence and date. It is the project's own record of the connections it brokered, and it is what the headline counts. Alongside it, provider-aggregated reporting (account-opening confirmations, loan disbursement lists, insurance enrolment registers, savings-group rosters) as a cross-check on the register's coverage, and periodic farmer-level verification on a sample whose size is reported. The provider's client-level records are not required and are not sought: providers are bound by client confidentiality and will not release them to a research organisation, and the indicator does not depend on them, because the project holds its own register of whom it connected. Where a provider does release client-level records they carry a persistent unique farmer identifier and are used to check the register. Internal project and partner systems, no public URL. Fallback, DS1 (Censuses and surveys): a farmer survey in the intervention area asking whether the respondent was connected to each listed service through project-supported channels, used only where the project holds no linkage register of its own, or holds one that no sample can be drawn to verify. Providers withholding client-level records does not trigger this route. An estimate, not a count: the share of sampled target-list farmers reporting a project-supported connection dated in the year, multiplied by the number of farmers on the target list, so it covers the target list only. It must rest on a representative sample of that list, and every value is flagged as fallback-sourced. Not applicable, DS3 (Geospatial and Earth observation): a farmer-provider connection is a transaction, not observable from satellite data. Not applicable, DS4 (Secondary and international databases): financial-inclusion statistics such as SDG indicator 8.10.2 measure population-level account ownership and cannot identify project-linked farmers or resolve an intervention area. Not applicable, DS5 (Citizen-generated and other non-traditional data): crowdsourced observations cannot be matched to the target-farmer list with the identifier quality de-duplication requires. Logs from a project-supported digital finance platform are DS2, not DS5.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which of the three states this project was in: Recommended (its own linkage register, with the provider total as a cross-check and a verified sample), Fallback (DS1 survey), or a provider aggregate with no register, which is reported as an unverified sub-count and never merged into the headline. If Fallback, state why no linkage register was available, or why no sample could be drawn to verify one, and give the sampling design and the achieved sample size.
collectionInstrument: Fallback DS1 route: a financial-services linkage module in the project's household survey, listing credit, insurance and savings and asking whether the respondent established each connection, through which channel and provider, and when. Respondent: the farmer named on the target list, answering for themselves only. Mode: in-person or telephone interview. Recommended DS2 route: the linkage register, capturing per event the farmer identifier, sex, age, service type, provider, evidence and date, and a short verification call or visit to a random sample of register rows, confirming with the farmer the provider, the service and the date; the share confirmed is the verification rate.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as linkage events enter project or provider records; compiled at least once per reporting year, and six-monthly where the project's own cycle or its donor requires it (fallback survey: once per year). A more frequent compile does not change the reported value, which stays annual: the six-month figures are cumulative within the year and the year-end compile is the one that is reported.
referencePeriod: The reporting year (the project's 12-month reporting cycle). A linkage event counts if its recorded date falls inside the window.
baselineRequired: No. An annual count of linkages established through CIMMYT-supported channels is zero by construction before the project starts. The first reporting year anchors the trend. KPI-OC17, which this indicator feeds, carries its own baseline logic; the absence of a requirement here does not remove it there.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One reporting year. Levels widen the set of farmers; they never widen the domain.

B: Combination method: sum. Total = Σ unique farmers linked in the domain. A count of people is added, never averaged, and de-duplication precedes the sum because the same farmer reached twice is one farmer.

C: Levels and operations. Household. The count from the calculation method. Also report: the channels through which the linkages were made.

D: Never pooled. Linkage counts with KPI-OC17's access percentages, which have a different denominator. Farmers linked in different reporting years, which are reported as separate annual counts rather than a cumulative total unless the cumulative basis is stated.

E: Deduplication and coverage. The persistent farmer identifier, applied from Household level upward, so a farmer linked through two channels is counted once, and a farmer linked by two projects is counted once only where the projects' records can be matched. No farmer identifier is shared across projects, so a figure pooled across projects is labelled an upper bound on unique farmers wherever project areas overlap and the records cannot be matched. The Recommended headline is a census of the register and carries no coefficient-of-variation band. Where the Fallback DS1 survey route is used, the value is a sample estimate and carries the same bands used elsewhere in this pathway: 16.5 percent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 percent released flagged, above 33.3 percent not released as an estimate, on at least 30 records; the band travels with every Fallback-sourced value.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: farmers on the project's target list, or identified within the defined intervention area, whose connection is evidenced by one of the record types listed in the Definition, through a channel the project supports. Exclusion: awareness or financial-literacy training with no recorded connection; a referral or name passed to a provider with no record that the provider received it; connections pre-dating the project; farmers who approached a provider entirely outside CIMMYT-supported channels (spillover); organizations, cooperatives as entities, and enterprises. On the Recommended route the headline is the project's own linkage register, counted as the number of unique farmers on it, and it is never an estimate. The register is what the Collection instrument describes: one row per linkage event carrying farmer identifier, sex, age, service type, provider, evidence and date. A provider aggregate cannot carry this indicator's required cuts: it holds no sex and no age, so a headline derived from one cannot be broken down by either, and the requirement that every breakdown sum exactly to the headline could not be met.

The provider total is a cross-check on that register, not the value. Where the provider reports more connections than the register holds, the difference is the register's coverage shortfall and is reported with the value; it is never added to it, because a farmer the project cannot identify cannot be de-duplicated, sexed or aged. Where the register is the larger, the excess is investigated before anything is reported.

The verification sample confirms the register, it does not build the headline: it establishes what share of register entries are real connections, and the verification rate is reported with the value.

Missing data. Two cases, and they are not the same.

Missing records are never imputed. Repeated observations: a farmer linked to several services, or the same service more than once, counts once in the reporting year. Not cumulative: annual values must not be added across years, because continuing linkages would be recounted; the optional new versus continuing disaggregate separates the two where a project tracks it.
limitations: Measures a connection being established, not use or benefit. A linked farmer may never draw the loan, renew the policy or deposit savings, and the count says nothing about loan size, affordability or terms. Read with KPI-OC17 before any statement about access, and with KPI-I03 before any statement about income.

Driven by CIMMYT's activity level and provider behaviour, so it rises when the project facilitates more linkages, not when farmers are better off. Contribution claim only; credit markets, interest rates, regulation and provider strategy shape linkage independently of CIMMYT.

Only as reliable as the records behind it. What forces a survey estimate is the absence of a register the project can verify; values built that way are estimates, not counts, and must be labelled as such, and a provider aggregate with no register is reported only as the unverified sub-count.
A year-on-year rise means more farmers were linked that year, not that cumulative reach grew; annual values do not sum, and the service-type breakdown may exceed the headline by design.
subMetrics: None. The three service types (credit, insurance, savings) are a disaggregation, not separately calculated metrics: same linkage records, same counting rule.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Mission indicator; project-level roles. Data collection: project field team together with the financial providers and partners transacting the linkages. Validation: project MEAL officer (identifier quality, linkage-evidence checks, de-duplication before any figure leaves the project). Calculation: project MEAL officer produces the project count; the CIMMYT MEAL unit performs cross-project de-duplication and pooling. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 5 · Income & livelihoods — Reference sheet KPI-O19

name: Number of market, processing, or storage facilities established or upgraded in intervention areas
resultsLevel: Output
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Contributing: PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator counts agricultural market, processing, or storage facilities. Nearest thematic relatives: SDG target 2.3 (indicator 2.3.1 measures production per labour unit of small-scale food producers; the target text names market access and value addition as means, without a facility indicator) and SDG target 9.1 (indicator 9.1.1 measures the share of the rural population within 2 km of an all-season road).
otherFrameworks: None directly. No donor framework consulted counts physical facilities; they treat marketing, post-harvest handling and storage and value-added processing as categories of practices applied by producers, not as infrastructure counts. CGIAR Results Framework 2025-30: no direct correspondence confirmed, and the 32 CGIAR standard indicators include no facility count, so this reports as a CIMMYT-defined output measure.
definition:
Counts distinct physical market, processing, or storage facilities established or upgraded with CIMMYT support in CIMMYT intervention areas, each counted in the reporting year in which it, or its upgrade, became operational and in use. Facilities include market and aggregation centres, processing units and storage structures.

"Established" means newly constructed, or an existing structure converted to a market, processing or storage function it did not have; "upgraded" means completed physical improvement or equipment installation that adds capacity, function, or quality beyond routine maintenance, or works that return an idle facility to operation. The value is reported as an ordered pair, (established; upgraded), never as one undifferentiated total.
rationale: Answers how much physical market, processing, and storage infrastructure CIMMYT's market-access work put in place or improved each year: the first and most directly manageable step in the market-access results chain, before improved farmer access (KPI-OC21) and income gains (KPI-I03) can be observed. Project teams use it to manage delivery of infrastructure components; institutional reporting uses it to evidence tangible market-systems investment.
projectSpecificApplication: State the project's intervention areas (countries, regions, communities), the facility types supported, and the support modality (direct financing, co-financing or technical design). Do not change the unit, the distinct-facility counting rule, or the establish/upgrade definitions; if the indicator as defined is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor requirement this facility count serves: for example a donor-required infrastructure output indicator, or an internal delivery milestone triggering the follow-on access measurement for KPI-OC21.
projectTypesNotApplicable: applied agronomy and farming systems and digital agriculture and AI
projectTypesRaw:
Seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, breeding and varietal development, applied agronomy and farming systems and digital agriculture and AI, which do not construct or upgrade market infrastructure.
unit: Number of facilities (distinct physical structures), reported as an ordered pair: (established; upgraded)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more supported market, processing or storage facilities, established or upgraded, became operational and in use. Established and upgraded are reported as an ordered pair and never summed, a new structure and an upgrade not being the same result.
disaggregationRequired: Required: facility type (market; processing; storage); establishment status (newly established versus upgraded).
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator; no cut is specific to one project type.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country or region; commodity handled; ownership or management model (cooperative or farmer organization, private, public); capacity class where relevant (for example storage volume band).
unitOfObservation:
Facility (a distinct physical structure). The measurand is a physical asset, so the farm measurement levels do not apply: a facility is not observed at Trial / Station, Farm / Plot or Household level. The facility is the unit of observation and the only level at which the indicator is measured.

Regional / Aggregated and the levels above it are aggregation levels for this indicator, domains over which facilities are counted, not places where one is observed.

A facility is counted once regardless of how many projects contributed to it, so the persistent facility identifier in Block E carries the geographic coordinates rather than the project reference.
calculationSummary:
CIMMYT support means direct financing, co-financing, or technical design of the works, evidenced in a dated record naming what CIMMYT provided, directly or through an implementing partner under a CIMMYT agreement; convening the parties or advising informally does not qualify. The minimum scale is community level or above, for example mills, shellers, seed or grain processing plants, warehouses and community silos: household storage such as hermetic bags and single-household silos is a technology reaching farmers, counted by the technology and access indicators, not a facility here. Each facility counts once per reporting year regardless of the number of works carried out on it.

Value = distinct physical facilities in CIMMYT intervention areas whose establishment or upgrading works, supported by CIMMYT directly or through an implementing partner under a CIMMYT agreement, were completed, and whose establishment or upgrade became operational and in use during the reporting year, counted separately as established and as upgraded and reported as that pair.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: administrative records generated by the works themselves: works contracts, completion and handover certificates, supervision reports, equipment installation records, operating records, partner reporting, and a project facility registry carrying a unique facility identifier, type, and GPS coordinates. Fallback DS1: a site visit substituting for a missing completion or support record (facility inventory confirming existence, completed works and operational status), used where partner-executed works leave no auditable completion record; such facilities are flagged as fallback-sourced. A site visit confirming the operation of a facility whose completion and support are on record is Recommended evidence, not this route. Not applicable DS3: imagery can detect a new structure but cannot confirm an upgrade, the facility's function, or CIMMYT support. Not applicable DS4: no third-party database records which facilities CIMMYT projects established or upgraded. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced reports cannot verify works completion or CIMMYT support.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State how many counted facilities rest on the Recommended records and how many on a site visit substituting for a missing completion or support record (the Fallback), and for the second, why auditable completion or support records were not available.
collectionInstrument: For a site visit, on either route: a facility verification checklist capturing facility identifier and name, type, GPS location, nature of works (new construction or upgrade, short description), completion date, the date the facility, or its upgrade, entered operation and use with its evidence, operational status, and the supporting project. Respondent: facility owner, operator, or works supervisor; mode: site visit with photographic evidence. The DS2 records themselves are compiled from existing works and operating documentation and need no instrument.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, through works supervision and completion records as construction and upgrading proceed; consolidated once per year.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Yearly values are snapshots; cumulative claims require de-duplication by facility identifier across years.
referencePeriod: The reporting year (12 months). Each reported value counts facilities whose establishment or upgrade became operational and in use in that year only, whatever year their works were completed in.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual count of facilities becoming operational that starts from zero at project start. Two related records are still needed: a pre-works condition record for each upgraded facility (photos and a short condition note in the facility file, stating, for an idle facility, since when it has been out of operation), without which an upgrade cannot be distinguished from maintenance; and the companion outcome KPI-OC21 does require baseline data on farmers' pre-intervention access, so plan its baseline alongside this indicator's works documentation.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One reporting year. Levels widen the set of facilities; they never widen the domain.

B: Combination method: sum. Total = Σ distinct facilities established or upgraded in the domain. A facility upgraded twice in one year is one facility; established and upgraded are reported as separate counts and never summed into an undifferentiated total. A facility counted on the Fallback route is summed separately, labelled fallback-sourced, and reported beside the total, never in it.

C: Levels and operations. Facility. The record itself; nothing is combined at this level. Also report: the facility type and whether it was established or upgraded.

D: Never pooled. Facility counts with KPI-OC21's access percentages, which count farmers rather than structures. Established with upgraded facilities in a single total. Facilities of different types where the claim is type-specific.

E: Deduplication and coverage. The persistent facility identifier, carrying geographic coordinates rather than a project reference, so a facility supported by two projects is counted once. Where coordinates are unavailable, the figure is labelled an upper bound on distinct facilities.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion: a facility counts in the year it, or its upgrade, becomes operational and in use, its supported works having been completed, evidenced by an operating record (intake, throughput or fee records) or a documented site visit confirming operation; a handover certificate names the operator but does not evidence use on its own; a completed structure not yet in operation is reported separately as completed-not-yet-operational. Documented completion alone does not qualify it. The year is the year of entry into operation and use, evidenced and documented, not the year works start. Exclusion: facilities only planned or still under construction at year end; routine maintenance and repairs of a facility in operation that restore rather than add capacity, function, or quality (a facility counts as idle, and works returning it to operation as an upgrade, only where it has operated before and did not operate at any time in the 12 months before the works began, as its pre-works condition record shows); facilities supported only through training or advisory services without physical works or equipment; facilities outside CIMMYT intervention areas. Missing data: a facility record without evidence that it is operational and in use is excluded until verified; a record that cannot be matched to a distinct physical facility (no identifier or location) is excluded, or the affected total labelled an upper bound on distinct facilities. Repeated observations: a facility both established and upgraded within the same year counts once, as established; a facility upgraded in successive years counts once in each year in which an upgrade became operational, so yearly values must never be summed across years into a cumulative facility total without de-duplicating by facility identifier.
limitations:
A facility count is a delivery measure, not a functionality measure. The qualification criterion requires the facility to be operational and in use, which is a threshold rather than a measure of how well it works. Governance, throughput, financial sustainability and maintenance are not measured here and are not inferable from the count.

The use side is carried by KPI-OC21, the share of targeted farmers reaching a facility, and the economic side by KPI-OC18 and KPI-OC63. A facility reported here with no movement in OC21 is the pattern to investigate, and the two are read together rather than summed.

A facility count says nothing about how much a facility is used, or about benefit. A counted warehouse can later sit idle or fall out of operation. Farmer access is measured by KPI-OC21 and income effects by KPI-I03; CGIAR's review of its standard indicators warns against extrapolating output and use counts into benefit claims, so never present this figure as farmers served or incomes raised.

The count treats units of very different scale as equal: a village aggregation point and a large processing plant each count as one facility. The headline number is not a measure of capacity, investment value, or throughput; read it with the facility-type disaggregation.

The contribution claim is bounded by the support threshold, not removed by it. Facilities are often co-financed with governments, donors, or private investors, so a facility counts here only where CIMMYT funding or CIMMYT design shaped what was built, evidenced in a dated record. The same facility may still be reported by another organization against its own contribution.

The upgrade boundary is judgment-prone: the line between an upgrade and routine maintenance depends on the upgrade definition, works or equipment adding capacity, function or quality, or returning an idle facility to operation, being applied uniformly. If one project counts a repainted market shed and another counts only new equipment, their numbers are not comparable.

A rise in the value means more supported facilities opened that year; a fall may reflect construction timing or a project cycle ending rather than a performance problem, since opening dates slipping across a year boundary move the annual count without any change in delivery pace.
subMetrics: None. The facility types (market; processing; storage) are disaggregations of the same count, not sub-metrics. Related indicators with their own sheets: KPI-OC21 (percentage of targeted farmers with improved access to a facility established or upgraded through CIMMYT support, the outcome this output feeds per the register roll-up) and, further along the chain, KPI-I03 (the Income & livelihoods pathway impact indicator this chain serves).
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
UN SDG indicator metadata sheets 2.3.1 (2024-07-29 release) and 9.1.1 (2024-09-27 release), UN Statistics Division, cited to document that no SDG indicator corresponds to this one.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project field teams, works supervisors, and implementing partners, at works completion. Validation: project MEAL officer (completion evidence on file, registry completeness, within-project de-duplication, spot verification of partner-executed works). Calculation: project MEAL officer applying the distinct-facility counting rules; CIMMYT MEAL unit for cross-project de-duplication. Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 5 · Income & livelihoods — Reference sheet KPI-O22

name: Percentage of targeted farmers gaining improved access to financial services, as a contribution of CIMMYT support
resultsLevel: Outcome. The result is a change in the relationships and behaviour of external actors: a farmer takes up and maintains a financial service, and a provider serves a new client. Brokering the connection is the delivered result, counted at output level by KPI-O19; the service being taken up, approved and kept usable is the change this indicator measures.
indicatorScope: Mission. It measures a change in the condition of an external population (targeted farmers), so it carries the full project-specific layer below.
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Usable financial services let farmers invest, smooth consumption, and insure against shocks: a direct component of an improving livelihood trajectory. Contributing objective (contribution only): PO4 (agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient), because rural financial inclusion is part of a more inclusive agrifood system. One primary objective only; the register lists PO3 first, and the first-listed objective is primary per the register's convention.
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs. The register carries no Impact Area column; the pathway-wide rule sets Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs for every indicator here.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest reference, SDG indicator 8.10.2 (proportion of adults with an account at a bank, other financial institution, or mobile-money provider), measures population-level account ownership, not attributable improved access among targeted farmers. SDG target 2.3 names access to financial services for small-scale food producers, but its indicators (2.3.1, 2.3.2) measure productivity and income, not finance access. Source: UN SDG indicator 8.10.2 metadata sheet (Metadata-08-10-02), UN Statistics Division, last updated 2026-03-27.
otherFrameworks: No CGIAR Results Framework correspondence: the project's CGIAR crosswalk carries no match.
definition:
The share of targeted farmers with improved access to financial services (credit, insurance, savings) gained through a CIMMYT-supported connection, out of all targeted farmers. Improved access means gaining or upgrading a usable financial service, not a referral, an awareness session, or a pending application.

The boundary with KPI-O19 is the state of the service, not whose act produced it. KPI-O19 counts the connections CIMMYT and its partners established; this indicator counts the farmers who, as a result, gained or upgraded a usable service. A farmer can be linked and hold nothing, and that difference is the result this indicator reports.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's financial-linkage work is translating into farmers who can use credit, insurance, or savings, rather than farmers merely introduced to a provider. Access to finance is a recognised constraint on smallholder investment in improved seed, inputs, and equipment, so this is the enabling step between the pathway's delivery work and its income results. Serves project management, institutional reporting under Primary Objective 3, and donors who require financial-inclusion evidence beyond participation counts.
projectSpecificApplication: Describes the project's targeted farmer population and intervention areas, the service types and providers in scope, and the verification timing; the institutional definition, usability criterion, and calculation method are unchanged. Illustrative example: a project verifies, twelve months after linkage, whether the 4,000 farmers it connected to two microfinance institutions hold an active product, and reports the verified share over its 15,000 targeted farmers.
projectSpecificRationale: States which project decision, donor requirement, or local reporting need the access measure serves. Illustrative example: a project reports this indicator as its donor's required financial-inclusion outcome; a low conversion rate from linkage to active use triggers a review of the partner institution's product terms.
projectTypesNotApplicable: breeding and varietal development and digital agriculture and AI
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, breeding and varietal development and digital agriculture and AI.
unit: Percentage of targeted farmers
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of the targeted farmers holds improved access to a usable financial service. The denominator is the project's defined target population, so the share falls when targeting widens without access keeping pace. It also falls where a service lapses or its provider withdraws it.
disaggregationRequired: Required: sex (female/male); age (youth/non-youth, 15 to 30 as stated once in Core §4.1; projects record date of birth or exact age so other bands, for example a donor band of 15 to 29, can be derived); financial service type (credit / insurance / savings), mirroring KPI-O19's service categories. The register cell lists only sex and age; financial service type is added as required.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator; no cut is specific to one project type.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Provider type (bank / microfinance institution / insurer / savings group / mobile money); formal versus informal provider; new access versus upgraded access; country or region; farm size class.
unitOfObservation: The targeted farmer. The denominator is the project's defined target population, not the number of farmers linked; a farmer who was never linked still sits in the denominator if the project targeted them.
calculationSummary:
Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100. Upgrading is one of three tests: a move from informal to formal provision, a new service type, or a better product on price, term or collateral than the farmer's own previous product of the same type, from the same or another provider: a lower stated interest rate on credit or premium on insurance, a longer tenor or a repayment schedule matched to the crop cycle, or a reduced or removed collateral requirement. Any one of the three qualifies, and which applied is recorded, because the three represent different degrees of change and pooling them unlabelled would hide that.

Numerator: targeted farmers holding improved access to at least one usable financial service (credit, insurance, savings) in the reference period, established through a CIMMYT-supported connection, which is the test, evidenced on the KPI-O19 register or, where that register is incomplete, by the respondent's own report of a project-supported connection, naming the provider and the channel; and verified as usable on the test for its type: credit, a loan disbursed in the 12 months before measurement or outstanding at it; savings or an account, at least one deposit, withdrawal or transfer by the farmer in those 12 months; insurance, a policy in force at measurement or covering a season that ended in those 12 months; counted once per farmer regardless of the number of services. Denominator: all targeted farmers in the project's intervention areas, the full target population, not only O19-linked farmers and not the verification sample.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 + DS1 combined: the KPI-O19 linkage registry (DS2, administrative and registry data, carrying farmer identifier, service type, provider and linkage date) supplies the candidate numerator, L, the farmers on that register who are also in the defined target population, as the aggregation rule defines it; Frame DS2: the target-population register supplies the denominator; a farmer-level verification module (DS1, survey) confirms that linkages matured into usable services and captures upgrades the registry misses. Verification is mandatory on at least a sample, and the sample size is reported: no provider record can establish usability, but requiring farmer-level confirmation for every farmer would make the indicator unreportable, the same trade-off resolved the same way on KPI-O19. A sample is the floor rather than the method: a project able to run the module over every farmer of L does so, which is Route A1 in the aggregation rule. Both parts are needed: the registry alone cannot see usability, and a survey alone cannot connect the change to the CIMMYT pathway. Fallback DS2 only: linkage registry plus written provider confirmations of active accounts or disbursed products, where a verification survey is not feasible; flagged as fallback-sourced, because provider records overstate usability (dormant accounts stay on the books). This route does not verify. The count it produces is an upper bound on verified holders, never a verified count, and it is Route A2 in the aggregation rule. Recommended DS1 over the target population, where a project can field the verification module on the target-population register itself rather than on L: this is the only role that enumerates the target population, and it is Route C in the aggregation rule. The connection test is unchanged; where no register row exists it is evidenced from the respondent's own report, naming the provider and the channel, which on this indicator is Recommended evidence. Recommended DS1 over the target population, sampled rather than enumerated, where a project draws its verification sample directly from the target-population register instead of from L: this is Route D in the aggregation rule, the same design KPI-OC21's Block B uses for its own verification sample. The connection test is unchanged, evidenced on the KPI-O19 register or the respondent's own report where no register row exists. Not applicable: DS3 (geospatial and Earth observation), financial service access cannot be observed from satellite or GIS data; DS4 (secondary and international databases), national financial-inclusion series measure whole adult populations and can neither resolve targeted farmers nor trace access to CIMMYT support, context benchmarks only; DS5 (citizen-generated data), crowdsourcing cannot verify an individual farmer's service status or its link to a CIMMYT intervention.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: States which route the project used (A1, A2, B, C or D), and reports L (the linked set) where the route draws on it, p̂ where Route B or D applies, and the achieved sample size, and the contact rate where Route A1 or Route C could not reach every farmer; if Route A2 (Fallback), why the verification survey was not feasible, with every reported value flagged. Illustrative example: "Used Route B: O19 linkage registry (L = 4,000) cross-checked against a phone verification module administered 12 months after linkage on a sample of 400, p̂ = 0.60, achieved sample 339."
collectionInstrument: A short access-to-finance verification module, appended to the project's farmer survey or administered by phone: service type, provider, the evidence the usability test for its type needs (for credit, the disbursement date and whether the loan is outstanding; for savings or an account, the date of the farmer's last deposit, withdrawal or transfer; for insurance, the period the policy covers), date established or upgraded, prior access status, the terms an upgrade claimed on price, term or collateral needs (the stated interest rate or premium, tenor or repayment schedule, and collateral requirement of both the current service and the farmer's previous product of the same type), and, where no linkage record exists, the respondent's own account of the connection and the channel it came through. Whom it is fielded on follows the route. On Routes A1 and B the frame is L and the respondent is the targeted farmer named in the linkage record. On Routes C and D the frame is the target-population register and the respondent is any targeted farmer, whose connection is then evidenced on the register or on their own report as the Calculation method sets out; Route C enumerates that frame and Route D samples it. Mode: face-to-face or phone. The O19 registry must carry a persistent farmer identifier, sex, age, service type, and linkage date for matching.
collectionFrequency: Annually: the KPI-O19 registry is updated continuously; usability verification runs once per reporting year, with enough lag after linkage (at least one season) for take-up to be observable.
referencePeriod: A point in time, the end of the reporting year. It is observed at each farmer's verification interview, and every 12-month window on this sheet ends on the interview date (on Route A2, on the date of the provider's confirmation). The value is a stock: a farmer holding improved access at that point is in the numerator whether the access was established this year or in an earlier one, provided it passes, at measurement, the usability test the Calculation method sets for its type and represents a gain against the farmer's pre-intervention status. Access newly established or upgraded during the 12 months before measurement is reported alongside as the year's flow, and the two are never added.
baselineRequired: Yes. Improved access is defined against each farmer's pre-intervention access status, collected as a few questions at enrolment or first linkage. Fallback: recall-based reconstruction of prior access during the verification interview, acceptable because holding or not holding a financial service is a low-error recall item. If neither is feasible, the project can report the share with any usable CIMMYT-linked service (an access level), but cannot report improvement. Route A2 is a standing exception, not a case of neither being feasible: it reports an access level only, never improvement, although the enrolment record of prior access exists on it as on every route.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One target population, one reporting year, one country. Levels widen the set of farmers; they never widen the domain. A share is never computed across two target populations. The target population is fixed at design or baseline and does not move mid-stream. Any amendment is documented and dated, and in an amendment year the value is reported on both denominators, so a change in the share cannot be produced by redefining who was targeted.

Weight: one per farmer.

B: Combination method: ratio of sums.

The denominator is always Σ targeted farmers, counted from the target-population register on every route. Routes A1, A2 and B obtain the numerator from L and are bounded by it, so each understates it by the linkage register's coverage of holders; Routes C and D draw on the target population directly and are not so bounded, so the two groups do not return the same value where the register is incomplete.

L, the linked set, is defined once and used everywhere below: the farmers on the project's own linkage register who are also in the defined target population, counted as a stock at the reference point, not as an annual flow. It is not KPI-O19's reported headline, which is an annual count and which admits farmers identified within the intervention area who may sit outside the target list. The multiplier and the sampling frame must be the same object, and that object is L.

A holder, on every route below, is a targeted farmer holding improved access as the Calculation method defines it: a usable service gained or upgraded through a CIMMYT-supported connection. On Route A2 a confirmed holder is a farmer a provider confirms as holding a service, which is why that route reports an access level.

Route A1, the numerator is enumerated by verification. The Recommended route's module is run as a census of L rather than on a sample of it. Numerator = the count of verified holders in L where every farmer of L was reached; where some could not be contacted, they leave both terms of the conversion rate, as on Route B, and Numerator = (verified holders ÷ farmers of L reached) × L, with the contact rate reported. Denominator = Σ targeted farmers. No sampling applies and the value carries no band.

Route A2, the numerator is enumerated from provider confirmations. The Fallback DS2 route's written provider confirmations, which carry no survey and no sample, stand in for the module. They do not establish usability, since dormant accounts stay on providers' books, so the count is an upper bound on verified holders: labelled fallback-sourced on every value and never reported as a verified count. Numerator = the count of confirmed holders in L, so labelled. Denominator = Σ targeted farmers.

Route B, the numerator is estimated from a sample of L, which is the Recommended route's normal case.

p̂ = verified holders in the sample ÷ farmers of L on whom verification was achieved, computed within the design strata and combined across them in proportion to each stratum's share of L; a sampled farmer who could not be contacted leaves both terms, which is the same rule the missing-data field states.

p̂ is a conversion rate within L and is never reported as the share. On the example in Project-specific application, 4,000 linked out of 15,000 targeted at a 60 percent conversion is a share of 16 percent, not 60. Reporting p̂ directly multiplies the value by the reciprocal of linkage coverage, here 3.75.

Route C, the whole target population is enumerated. Numerator = the count of verified holders whose connection is evidenced, on the register or on the respondent's own report as the Calculation method sets out, where every targeted farmer was reached; where some could not be contacted, Numerator = (verified holders with an evidenced connection ÷ targeted farmers reached) × Σ targeted farmers, a farmer not contacted leaving both terms of that rate as on Route D, with the contact rate reported. Enumerating the population rather than the register is what lets a farmer the register missed be found; it does not relax the connection test, and a holder who cannot evidence a project-supported connection stays out of the numerator on every route.

Route D, the target population is sampled directly and no L multiplier applies, the design KPI-OC21's Block B already uses for its own verification sample. p̂ = verified holders with an evidenced connection in the sample ÷ farmers sampled from the target population on whom verification was achieved, computed within the design strata and combined across them in proportion to each stratum's share of the target population; a sampled farmer who could not be contacted leaves both terms, as on Route B. Numerator = p̂ × Σ targeted farmers. Denominator = Σ targeted farmers. Share (%) = 100 × p̂. The connection test is unchanged: a sampled farmer who cannot evidence a project-supported connection stays out of the numerator. Route D shares Route C's frame, the target-population register, but samples it rather than enumerating it, so it can miss a register-missed holder that Route C would catch; a project able to enumerate the whole frame runs Route C instead.

The route is stated with every value, and a Route B or Route D value is labelled estimated and reported with the standard error and the achieved sample size. Dividing a sample count by a population denominator understates the share by the sampling fraction, which is an arithmetic error rather than a conservative choice.

Recompute from farmer records; never average project percentages. The denominator travels with every percentage.

C: Levels and operations. Household. The verified access status of the individual farmer.

D: Never pooled. Access levels, reported on Route A2 or where no baseline was feasible, with counts of improvement. Access percentages with KPI-O19's linkage counts. Populations targeted for different service types where the claim is service-specific.

E: Deduplication and coverage. The persistent farmer identifier, applied from Household level upward. Coverage and precision travel with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands used in official statistics: 16.5 percent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 percent released flagged, above 33.3 percent not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one de-duplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. On Route B the records counted are the farmers of L on whom verification was achieved, not the targeted farmers in the denominator, since the sample is what carries the sampling error. On Route D the records counted are the farmers sampled from the target population on whom verification was achieved, the same logic applied to the target-population frame rather than to L. A Route A1, Route A2 or Route C value carries no band. The floor binds where the bands do, and on a Route A1 or Route C value scaled from the farmers reached, which is not released below 30 farmers reached, in both cases at Project area level and above; a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion/exclusion: village savings and loan groups and other facilitated informal savings groups count as providers, with formality recorded as a disaggregation, since in most of the countries CIMMYT works in the informal group is the financial service within a smallholder's reach; upgrades count (for example informal savings group to formal account, or a better product on price, term or collateral); awareness sessions, referrals without take-up, pending applications, and grants or free input transfers are excluded. Missing data: linked farmers whose usability cannot be verified are excluded from the numerator, never assumed to have access; where verification is sample-based, or a census could not reach every farmer, weights are recomputed over the farmers verified. Repeated observations: one record per farmer per reporting period, using the most recent verification; a farmer appearing in both the O19 registry and the survey is matched by farmer identifier, not double counted.
limitations:
Access is reported; loan quality is not certified. The indicator records that a farmer holds improved access to a usable financial service through a CIMMYT-supported connection. It makes no statement about interest rates, effective cost, collateral terms, repayment burden or whether the borrowing improved welfare. A rise is consistent with a farmer taking on debt that harms them.

The reporting standard applied here is therefore deliberately narrow: verified usable access, with the service type recorded. Consumer-protection assessment sits with the financial provider and its regulator, which CIMMYT neither administers nor supervises, and importing such a framework would place a claim on this sheet that no CIMMYT project collects the evidence to support. The benefit side is carried by the indicators that measure it: KPI-OC18 for sales, KPI-OC63 for margin, KPI-I03 for income.

Supports a contribution claim tied to recorded connections, not a net effect: financial access also improves through market forces such as mobile-money expansion, and without a comparison group the value shows access gained through the CIMMYT pathway, not access that could not have happened otherwise.
Access is not use, and use is not benefit: a usable service does not mean the farmer borrows on fair terms or that credit improves welfare. The income test sits at KPI-I03.

Measurement error runs in a known direction per source: registries and provider records overstate usability (dormant accounts, lapsed policies), while farmer self-reports carry recall and courtesy bias; the verification module and the fallback flag keep the two apart.
Comparability across projects depends on who counts as a targeted farmer: a narrower target population can raise the rate without any change in access.
A rise means a larger share of the target population holds improved access to a usable financial service through CIMMYT-supported connections; it does not mean incomes rose.
subMetrics: None. The service-type, provider, and new-versus-upgraded breakdowns are disaggregations of the same numerator, not separately calculated metrics. Related sheets: KPI-O19 (output) supplies the linkage registry this indicator verifies, so the two sheets must be revised together; KPI-I03 (impact) is the pathway result this indicator enables, measured on its own sheet.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
The usability test for improved access, the three upgrade tests, the full-target-population denominator, the inclusion of facilitated informal savings groups as providers with formality recorded, and the financial-service-type disaggregation are stated as CIMMYT's own convention.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Mission indicator, so roles are project-level. Data collection: project M&E team (O19 linkage registry and verification module). Validation: project MEAL officer (registry-to-survey matching, de-duplication, usability evidence). Calculation: project MEAL officer; the CIMMYT MEAL unit performs cross-project pooling and de-duplication. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 5 · Income & livelihoods — Reference sheet KPI-OC17

name: Percentage change in annual sales value per assisted farm relative to baseline
resultsLevel: Outcome. Farms selling more into markets is a change in performance among beneficiaries, which is the Core's definition of an outcome. It sits between the pathway's delivery outputs and its income impact (KPI-I03).
indicatorScope: Mission. Measures an economic change among an external population (assisted farms), not a property of CIMMYT as an organization, so it carries the project-specific layer.
domain: Cross-cutting / Common, as recorded in the register: sales growth serves projects across domains.
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. One primary objective only; the register lists PO3 first, its primary convention. Contributing objective, contribution only: PO4 (agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs: the market-facing step of the livelihood pathway PO3 describes, and the Impact Area under which KPI-I03 sits. The register carries no Impact Area column; the pathway-wide rule sets it for every indicator here.
sdgTarget: None. The closest is SDG target 2.3 (double the agricultural productivity and incomes of small-scale food producers); its indicator 2.3.2 measures average income of small-scale food producers, not gross sales value, over a nationally defined producer population, not a project's assisted farms. Evidence toward target 2.3, but not reportable as indicator 2.3.2.
otherFrameworks: No CGIAR Results Framework correspondence.
definition: Measures how much the annual value of sales per assisted farm has changed relative to that farm's baseline. Annual sales value is the gross value of all products of the farm's own production (crops, livestock, and livestock products) sold during the 12-month reference year, at the prices actually received, before deducting production costs. Computed as (endline sales value minus baseline sales value) divided by baseline sales value, per assisted farm. A gross market-sales measure, not an income measure: net income is measured at impact level by KPI-I03.
