The unit is the farm, not the organization: supported organizations sit under the agro-enterprise revenue indicator (KPI-OC32).
rationale: Answers whether the farms CIMMYT assists are selling more into markets over time: the observable commercial step between producing more (the Productivity pathway) and earning more (KPI-I03). Gross sales can be observed from transactions and recall within a year, while net income requires costing every input.
projectSpecificApplication: Describes which farms are on this project's assisted list, the areas covered, when the baseline sales year was set, and which products its farms sell. The definition, unit, and calculation method stay unchanged. A project that cannot separate farm sales from the revenue of an associated enterprise raises this with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining the boundary here.
projectSpecificRationale: States the project decision, donor commitment, or reporting need this indicator serves. Example: a market-systems project tracks it because its donor requires a sales-growth result, and because stagnant sales alongside rising yields tells the team the constraint has moved from production to market access.
projectTypesNotApplicable: upstream discovery science and breeding and varietal development
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science and breeding and varietal development, which reach no farms directly; digital agriculture and AI, which reports through the pathways its tools serve.
unit: Percentage change (relative to baseline)
directionOfChange: Increase, read in real terms. A higher value means mean sales per farm on the panel grew more, in real terms, against baseline. A nominal rise smaller than inflation is not an improvement.
disaggregationRequired: Sex and age of the principal farm operator. The register records no required disaggregation for this indicator; both are added as required here, matching KPI-I03 so that the farm-level and person-level indicators can be read together.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator; no cut is specific to one project type.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Product or commodity sold. Farm size class, on the smallholder threshold defined in Annex B; the declared threshold travels with the value. Country and agroecological zone. Marketing channel (CIMMYT-supported versus other).
unitOfObservation:
The assisted farm, operationalised as the farm household's holding. Plot records may underlie the sales figure, but the value is assembled and reported for the holding, and a series is never spliced across measurement levels.

Entity rules. A household operating several plots or several crop or livestock activities is one assisted farm, and its sales are summed across them before the change is computed. A holding jointly managed by two households is one farm, assigned to the household that carries the persistent farm-holding identifier, with the joint arrangement recorded. A household that splits during the reporting window leaves the panel, because the entity whose change is being measured no longer exists; the split is recorded rather than the successor households being treated as continuations. The farm-holding identifier, not the household roster, is what anchors the series.
calculationSummary: Farm-level value (the register formula): (endline sales value minus baseline sales value) / baseline sales value, multiplied by 100, per assisted farm. Project-level value: on the panel of assisted farms with complete sales records at both baseline and reporting year, (sum of reporting-year sales minus sum of baseline sales) / sum of baseline sales x 100: the change in mean sales per farm on the fixed panel, robust to zero baselines and extreme farm-level ratios.
dataSource: Recommended, DS1 (Censuses and surveys): an annual sales module in the project's farm survey, administered to a census of the assisted-farm list or a random or stratified random sample drawn from it; farm record books where kept. Frame DS2 (Administrative and registry data): the project's assisted-farm registry, supplying the sampling frame, farm identifiers, and the sex and age of the principal farm operator. Fallback, DS2: purchase records of CIMMYT-supported off-takers, aggregators, or processors. A proxy: it misses other channels and side-selling, so it understates sales; every such value is flagged fallback-sourced. Not applicable, DS3 (Geospatial and Earth observation): satellites cannot observe what a farm sold or the price received. Not applicable, DS4 (Secondary and international databases): cannot resolve a project's assisted-farm list; national price series may support deflation but cannot produce the value. Not applicable, DS5 (Citizen-generated and other non-traditional data): cannot be matched to the assisted-farm list with the identifier quality the panel requires.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: States how many farms have a sales value from off-taker records, the Fallback, for either year, why a survey was not feasible for them, and which channels those records cover. Example: "Used Recommended: annual sales module, stratified random sample of 420 farms from the assisted registry, weighted to the registry total."
collectionInstrument: DS1 route: a farm sales module asking, per product over the 12-month window: quantity sold, unit, price received, month of sale, and whether the sale ran through a CIMMYT-supported channel. Respondent: the farm member responsible for marketing decisions; the farm identifier, and the sex and age of the principal farm operator, are recorded for matching to registry and baseline. Mode: face-to-face or telephone interview. Fallback route (DS2): no instrument; the channel record must capture, per transaction, farm identifier, product, quantity, value, and date.
collectionFrequency: Baseline before or at the start of assistance, then annually after the main marketing season. Short projects may measure baseline and endline only; the value then describes one interval and carries no trend.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Between rounds the latest measured value is carried forward with its measurement year noted.
referencePeriod: The 12 months prior to data collection (or the last complete production and marketing year), against the same window in the baseline year. Keep the survey month constant across rounds: sales are strongly seasonal.
baselineRequired: Yes, by construction. Fallbacks, in order: (a) recall-based reconstruction of the pre-assistance sales year in the first survey round; (b) if that is not feasible, the project may monitor sales levels but cannot report change against this indicator. Substituting the earliest reporting-year value as a baseline is not permitted: it forces that farm's change to exactly zero and pulls the pooled statistic toward zero by construction.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One currency, one panel of assisted farms, each farm measured against its own entry-year baseline. Cross-country pooling deflates every value to one stated base year common to the pooled countries, on each country's national consumer price index, and converts to US dollars at the average annual market exchange rate for that base year. Purchasing power parity is not used: these indicators measure transacted value, and a PPP conversion answers a different question about what that value buys locally. The rate and its source are recorded with the figure. Projects recruit farms over several years, so a fixed baseline-year panel would exclude every farm that joined after year one, shrinking the sample precisely as the project grew. Farms with different baseline years therefore pool, but only after both of a farm's values are deflated to the same stated base year; without that common base the sums mix price levels and the ratio describes nothing. Levels widen the set of farms; they never widen the domain. No combined figure exists across currencies without a stated conversion.

Weight: the sampling weight where the design is a sample of the assisted-farm list, otherwise none. The change is a ratio of summed sales, not a mean of per-farm percentage changes, so a farm moves it in proportion to its sales, and a market entrant adds its sales to the reporting-year total.

B: Combination method: ratio of sums.

Weighted to the registry total where the design is a sample of the assisted-farm list, on the same rule KPI-I03's Block B applies; a census of the list needs no weight. Both totals are expressed in one currency at constant prices, deflated to a stated base year with the index named. Recompute from farm records; never average project percentages, since projects differ in size and in baseline sales. The panel is balanced: only farms present in both years enter either total. A farm either of whose two sales values comes from off-taker records, the Fallback route, leaves both totals and is reported beside the change with its count, labelled fallback-sourced.

C: Levels and operations. Household. The farm's own sales in each year; the change is not computed at this level for institutional reporting.

D: Never pooled. Nominal with deflated values. Different currencies without a stated conversion and base year. Farms whose values are not deflated to one stated base year: the entry-cohort design in Block A pools farms with different baseline years on purpose, and it is the undeflated comparison that is forbidden, not the different baseline. Sales values with KPI-OC63's margins, which deduct costs, or with KPI-I03's income, which deducts costs and depreciation. Farm sales with KPI-OC32's enterprise revenue, which counts organizations rather than farms.

E: Deduplication and coverage. The persistent farm-holding identifier, not the household roster, applied from Household level upward, so a household operating several plots or crop or livestock activities is one farm and a split household leaves the panel rather than becoming two. A farm household that also operates a supported agro-enterprise is counted here as a farm and at KPI-OC32 as an enterprise, never merged: only sales of the farm's own production enter this indicator, and the enterprise's trading revenue is KPI-OC32's. Coverage and precision travel with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands used in official statistics: 16.5 percent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 percent released flagged, above 33.3 percent not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one de-duplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above, and a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place. A census of the assisted-farm list carries no band.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion: farms on the assisted list, a farm being on it where a dated project record shows it received a defined intervention, not merely that it was contacted, the list frozen for the reporting year; each with 12-month sales records for both periods; all sales of the farm's own production, including in-kind or barter sales valued at local market prices. Exclusion: off-farm income, wages, remittances; resale of goods the farm did not produce; sales of land, farm capital or equipment; revenue of organizations (KPI-OC32). A zero-baseline farm has no defined farm-level percentage; report the share of such market entrants alongside the value. Price treatment: deflate both of a farm's values to one stated base year, common to every country in a pooled figure (Block A), using the national consumer price index. The farm's own baseline year is its comparison window, not its price base: farms enter in different years, and deflating each to its own baseline would pool sums measured at different price levels, which Block A forbids because the resulting ratio describes nothing. Missing data: a farm missing its baseline leaves both terms and is counted in the coverage shortfall. Substituting its earliest reporting-year value as a baseline is not permitted (see Baseline required). Endline non-response is reported as an attrition rate, never imputed. Repeated observations: one value per farm per year, summing all transactions over the 12 months; if a farm is surveyed twice in a round, the first complete record counts.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only. There is no comparison group: the indicator observes only assisted farms, and sales value responds to prices, weather, and market shocks CIMMYT does not control. The CGIAR-commissioned poverty-impact study documents how long and confounded the chain from research to economic benefit is; anything stronger needs an evaluation design this indicator does not provide.

Gross sales are not income. Sales can rise while farm income falls: if input costs rise faster, if the farm sells more but consumes less of its own production, or if extra sales run down stocks. A rise here must never be reported as an income gain; that claim belongs to KPI-I03.

The measure is price-sensitive in two ways. Nominal growth conflates inflation with real change (hence the deflation step), and even real growth can be driven by producer-price movements rather than volume. Where the distinction matters, report volume and price components separately.

Recall-based sales data from farms that keep no records carries substantial error, and the panel design adds survivorship bias: farms lost to attrition are more likely to have performed poorly, inflating the measured change. Report the attrition rate with every value.

A rise means the assisted farms sold more, in real value, than at baseline. It does not mean income, food security, or resilience improved, and per-farm growth says nothing about distribution across farms. Read it beside the pathway's access outcomes (KPI-OC17, KPI-OC21) and KPI-I03 before drawing livelihood conclusions.
subMetrics:
None. Baseline and reporting-year sales values are data points of one change measure, not separate metrics. Two neighbouring sheets matter:

— KPI-OC32 (supported agro-enterprises with a revenue increase): the enterprise-side counterpart; farms here, organizations there. See the aggregation rule for the double-counting boundary.

— KPI-I03 (smallholder farmers with an income increase over their own baseline): the impact this indicator feeds. Sales growth is evidence toward the income claim, not a term in its formula: income adds non-sales returns and subtracts costs.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Mission indicator, so roles are project-level. Data collection: project M&E team and enumerators (sales module); project field team (assisted-farm registry). Validation: project MEAL officer (identifier quality, panel construction, outlier and unit checks, deflation). Calculation: project MEAL officer produces the project value; the CIMMYT MEAL unit performs currency conversion, cross-project de-duplication, and pooling. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 5 · Income & livelihoods — Reference sheet KPI-OC18

name: Percentage of targeted farmers with improved access to a market, processing, or storage facility established or upgraded through CIMMYT support
resultsLevel: Outcome. The result is a change in the behaviour and condition of external actors: farmers reach and use a facility, and an operator serves them. Supporting the works is the delivered result, counted at output level by KPI-O22; farmers reaching, using and continuing to use the facility is the change this indicator measures.
indicatorScope: Mission. It measures a change in the condition of an external population (targeted farmers), so it carries the full project-specific layer below.
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Using market, processing and storage facilities lets farmers sell surplus, add value, and reduce post-harvest losses. Contributing objective (contribution only): PO4 (agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient), because functioning rural market infrastructure is part of a more efficient agrifood system. One primary objective only; the register lists PO3 first, and the first-listed objective is primary per the register's convention.
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs. The register carries no Impact Area column; the pathway-wide rule sets Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs for every indicator here.
sdgTarget: None. SDG target 2.3 names access to markets for small-scale food producers, but its indicators (2.3.1 production per labour unit, 2.3.2 income of small-scale food producers) measure productivity and income. SDG indicator 9.1.1 measures the share of the rural population within 2 km of an all-season road: road access at population level, not attributable access to agricultural facilities among targeted farmers. Sources: UN SDG metadata sheets for 2.3.1 (last updated 2024-07-29) and 9.1.1 (last updated 2024-09-27).
otherFrameworks: No CGIAR Results Framework correspondence: the project's CGIAR crosswalk carries no match, and the 32 CGIAR standard indicators include no market-access measure. No donor framework consulted measures the share of farmers with improved access to a physical facility.
definition: The share of targeted farmers with improved access to a market, processing, or storage facility established or upgraded through CIMMYT support, out of all targeted farmers. Improved access means a facility counted under the pathway's output indicator KPI-O22 is operational, within reach of the farmer's holding, open to farmers of their profile, and used by the farmer in the 12 months before measurement. Availability without use is not access: KPI-O22 already counts the facility.
rationale: Answers whether the facilities CIMMYT helps build or upgrade (counted by KPI-O22) reach farmers, rather than standing idle or serving only a few. Physical access to markets, processing, and storage is a recognised constraint on smallholder commercialisation: the enabling step between infrastructure delivery and income results. Serves project management, institutional reporting under Primary Objective 3, and donors who require evidence beyond facility counts.
projectSpecificApplication: Describes the project's targeted farmer population and intervention areas, facility types supported, and verification timing; the institutional definition, the verified-use test, and the calculation method are unchanged. Illustrative example: a project that upgraded four community storage warehouses verifies, one marketing season after handover, which of its 12,000 targeted farmers stored grain there in the 12 months before verification.
projectSpecificRationale: States which project decision, donor requirement, or local reporting need the access measure serves. Example: a project reports this indicator as its donor's required market-access outcome; a low share two seasons after facility handover triggers a review of facility management, fees, or siting.
projectTypesNotApplicable: applied agronomy and farming systems and digital agriculture and AI
projectTypesRaw:
Seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, breeding and varietal development, applied agronomy and farming systems and digital agriculture and AI.
unit: Percentage of targeted farmers
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of the targeted farmers holds improved access, verified as use of a supported facility. The facilities themselves are counted by KPI-O22, and the two are never combined arithmetically. The value falls where a facility stops operating, where farmers stop using a facility that operates, or where the target population grows.
disaggregationRequired: Required: sex (female/male); age (youth/non-youth, 15 to 30 as stated once in Core §4.1; projects record date of birth or exact age so other bands, for example a donor band of 15 to 29, can be derived); facility type (market / processing / storage), mirroring KPI-O22's required facility-type disaggregation. The register cell lists only sex and age; facility type is added as required.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator; no cut is specific to one project type.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: New versus improved access; country or region; commodity handled; distance or travel-time band to the nearest supported facility; facility ownership model (cooperative, private, public).
unitOfObservation: The targeted farmer. The facility counted by KPI-O22 is not the unit here: O22 counts structures, this counts the farmers reaching them, and the two are never combined arithmetically.
calculationSummary:
Awareness of a facility, or a facility still under construction, does not count. A farmer who already used a facility gains improved access only where that farmer is verified to have used the added capacity, function or quality after the upgrade completed; a completed upgrade does not by itself move prior users into the numerator.

Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100. Numerator: targeted farmers with improved access to at least one market, processing, or storage facility established or upgraded through CIMMYT support (the facilities counted by KPI-O22), verified in the reference period; counted once per farmer regardless of the number of facilities. Denominator: all targeted farmers in the project's intervention areas, the full target population, not only farmers near a facility and not the verification sample.
dataSource: Recommended DS1 + DS2 combined: a farmer-level access module (DS1, survey) verifies whether each targeted farmer it reaches has used a supported facility in the 12 months before measurement, while the KPI-O22 facility registry (DS2, administrative and registry data) confirms which facilities qualify and Frame DS2: the target-population register supplies the denominator. Both parts are needed: the registry alone cannot see farmer-level access, and a survey alone cannot trace the facility to CIMMYT support. Not applicable as a route to this indicator, DS2 + DS3: catchment estimation, counting targeted farmers located within a defined service area of each operational supported facility, the service area being a one-hour travel time by the transport farmers in that area use, not a fixed distance and not varying by facility type, using the registry's GPS coordinates and geospatial analysis of farmer locations. It measures availability, and availability without verified use is excluded from this numerator. It is reported instead of the indicator, never as it, as targeted farmers within the service area of a supported facility, with this indicator recorded as not reportable for that project and period; a flag on a value of a different quantity does not make it this one. Not applicable: DS4 (secondary and international databases), national infrastructure or market-access series can neither resolve a project's targeted farmers nor trace access to CIMMYT-supported facilities, context benchmarks only; DS5 (citizen-generated and other non-traditional data), crowdsourced reports cannot verify an individual farmer's access status.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: States that the project used the Recommended role, since it is the only role that produces this indicator, and the verification timing, and on a census the contact rate. Where farmer-level verification was not feasible, states why, records this indicator as not reportable for the period, and names the catchment estimate reported in its place. Illustrative example: "Used Recommended: annual farmer survey module administered one season after facility handover, matched to the O22 facility registry."
collectionInstrument: A short market-access module, appended to the project's farmer survey or administered by phone: nearest supported facility known and reachable, use in the 12 months before the interview (by facility type), barriers if unused (distance, fees, membership, capacity), access status before the intervention, and, for a farmer who already used the facility before an upgrade, whether the added capacity, function or quality named in the KPI-O22 registry's works description was used after the upgrade completed. Respondent: the targeted farmer. Mode: face-to-face or phone interview. The KPI-O22 registry must carry facility identifier, type, GPS coordinates, completion date, and operational status so responses can be matched.
collectionFrequency: Annually: the KPI-O22 facility registry is updated continuously; farmer-level verification runs once per reporting year, with enough lag after the facility entered use (at least one marketing or post-harvest season) for access and use to be observable.
referencePeriod: A point in time, the end of the reporting year. It is observed at each farmer's verification interview, and every 12-month window on this sheet ends on the interview date. The value is a stock: a farmer holding improved access at that point is in the numerator whether the facility was counted under KPI-O22 this year or in an earlier one, provided the farmer is verified to have used the facility in the 12 months before measurement and represents a gain against the farmer's pre-intervention status. Access newly established or upgraded during the 12 months before measurement is reported alongside as the year's flow, and the two are never added.
baselineRequired: Yes. Improved access is defined against each farmer's pre-intervention access status, collected as a few questions at enrolment or baseline (nearest facility of each type, use, constraints). Fallback: recall-based reconstruction during the verification interview, acceptable because whether a farmer could store, process, or sell nearby is a low-error recall item. If neither is feasible, the project can report the share using a supported facility (an access level), but cannot report improvement.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One target population, one reporting year, one country. Levels widen the set of farmers; they never widen the domain. A share is never computed across two target populations. The target population is fixed at design or baseline and does not move mid-stream. Any amendment is documented and dated, and in an amendment year the value is reported on both denominators, so a change in the share cannot be produced by redefining who was targeted.

Weight: one per farmer.

B: Combination method: ratio of sums.

Where verification is on a sample, the share is an estimate, not a count.

p̂ = sampled farmers verified to have improved access / farmers sampled on whom verification was achieved, computed within the design strata and combined across them in proportion to each stratum's share of the target population; a sampled farmer who could not be contacted leaves both terms

Share (%) = 100 × p̂, labelled estimated and reported with its standard error and achieved sample size. Dividing a sample count by a population denominator understates the share by the sampling fraction, which is an arithmetic error rather than a conservative choice.

Where the module is run on every targeted farmer, the route is a census and no sampling applies: a farmer who could not be contacted leaves both terms of the rate, as on the sample route, so Numerator = (verified users ÷ farmers reached) × Σ farmers in the defined target population, with the contact rate reported.

Recompute from farmer records; never average project percentages. The denominator travels with every percentage.

C: Levels and operations. Household. The verified access status of the individual farmer.

D: Never pooled. Verified use with availability, including the catchment count reported in the indicator's place. Access levels, reported where no baseline was feasible, with counts of improvement. Access percentages with KPI-O22's facility counts. Populations targeted for different facility types where the claim is facility-specific.

E: Deduplication and coverage. The persistent farmer identifier, applied from Household level upward. Coverage and precision travel with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands used in official statistics: 16.5 percent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 percent released flagged, above 33.3 percent not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one de-duplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. A census of the target population carries no band. The floor binds where the bands do, and on a census value scaled from the farmers reached, which is not released below 30 farmers reached, in both cases at Project area level and above; a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion/exclusion: includes access verified through reported use only. Confirmed availability without verified use is excluded from the numerator and reported alongside as a coverage diagnostic, never added to it. Excludes awareness without use, prior users of an upgraded facility not verified to have used the added function, facilities not counted under KPI-O22 by the end of the reference period, and farmers whose access existed unchanged before the intervention. Missing data: farmers whose access cannot be verified are excluded from the numerator, never assumed to have access; where verification is sample-based, or a census could not reach every farmer, weights are recomputed over the farmers verified. Repeated observations: one record per farmer per reporting period, using the most recent verification; a farmer appearing in both facility user records and the survey is matched by farmer identifier, not double counted.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim tied to recorded facilities, not a net effect: market access also changes with roads, trader networks, and prices; without a comparison group the value shows access gained through CIMMYT-supported facilities, not access that could not have happened otherwise.

Use is not benefit: using a warehouse does not mean better prices or lower losses; CGIAR's review of its standard indicators warns that extrapolating use numbers into benefit claims is misleading. The income test sits at KPI-I03.
Measurement error runs in a known direction: farmer self-reports carry courtesy bias when the interviewer represents the project that built the facility.

Comparability depends on two definitions the value is sensitive to: what counts as use, and who counts as a targeted farmer; a target population including communities far from any planned facility mechanically reports a lower share.
A rise means a larger share of the target population uses a supported facility; read a fall alongside the KPI-O22 registry's operational-status field and the module's barriers item.
subMetrics: None. The facility-type and new-versus-upgraded breakdowns are disaggregations of the same numerator, not separately calculated metrics. Verified availability without use is a coverage diagnostic reported beside the value, not a breakdown of it. KPI-O22 supplies the facility registry this indicator verifies against, so the two sheets must be revised together.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
UN SDG indicator metadata sheets 2.3.1 (last updated 2024-07-29) and 9.1.1 (last updated 2024-09-27), UN Statistics Division; document why no direct SDG correspondence is recorded.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Mission indicator, so the roles are project-level. Data collection: project M&E team, administering the access module and maintaining the target-population register alongside the KPI-O22 facility registry. Validation: project MEAL officer (survey-to-registry matching, de-duplication, verification evidence). Calculation: project MEAL officer; the CIMMYT MEAL unit pools and de-duplicates for the institutional figure. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 5 · Income & livelihoods — Reference sheet KPI-OC21

name: Percentage of supported agro-enterprises with a revenue increase (compared to baseline)
resultsLevel: Outcome. An enterprise growing its revenue against its baseline is a change in performance among the enterprises CIMMYT supports, which is the Core's definition of an outcome. It sits between the pathway's market and finance outputs and the decent-jobs impact (KPI-I04).
indicatorScope: Mission. Measures a commercial change among external organizations (the agro-enterprises CIMMYT and its partners support), so it carries the project-specific layer.
domain: System Development, as recorded in the register: it tracks the strengthening of value-chain actors, not a field-level result.
primaryObjective: PO4 Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient. One primary objective only; the register lists PO4 first, its primary convention. Contributing objective, contribution only: PO3 (smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved), because viable enterprises supply inputs, services, and market outlets to the smallholders around them.
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs: enterprise viability is the livelihoods-and-jobs thread, and the Impact Area under which KPI-I04 sits. The register carries no Impact Area column; the pathway-wide rule sets it for every indicator here.
sdgTarget: None. The closest targets are SDG 8.3 (growth of micro-, small- and medium-sized enterprises) and SDG 9.3 (integration of small-scale enterprises into value chains and markets), but their indicators measure different constructs: 8.3.1 is informal employment share and 9.3.1 is small-scale industries' share of industry value added, both national measures that cannot resolve a project's supported list. Evidence toward targets 8.3 and 9.3, not reportable as either indicator.
otherFrameworks: No CGIAR Results Framework correspondence.
definition: The share of supported agro-enterprises whose annual revenue in the reporting year is higher in real terms than in their baseline year. An agro-enterprise is a non-farm business in the agrifood value chain: seed companies, input suppliers and agro-dealers, aggregators, traders, processors, machinery and service providers. Revenue is the gross value of the enterprise's sales of goods and services over a 12-month window, before deducting costs. The indicator is a binary share: each enterprise either recorded an increase or it did not, and the size of the increase does not enter the value. Farms are excluded; farm-level sales growth is measured by KPI-OC18.
rationale: Answers whether the agro-enterprises CIMMYT supports (through partnership, technical assistance, business development, or market linkages) are becoming commercially stronger: the enterprise-viability step between the pathway's delivery outputs and its jobs impact (KPI-I04), since enterprises that grow revenue are the ones positioned to sustain and create employment. Revenue is the measure enterprises themselves record, and the construct donors track for assisted firms.
projectSpecificApplication: Describes which enterprises are on this project's supported list, the countries and value chains covered, and when each baseline revenue year was set; the definition, unit, and calculation method stay unchanged. Example: a project reports the share of the 60 seed companies and grain aggregators on its supported list, each past its first full financial year of support, whose last complete financial year exceeded their pre-support baseline year. A project that cannot separate an enterprise's revenue from an associated farm's sales raises it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining the boundary here.
projectSpecificRationale: States the project decision, donor commitment, or reporting need this indicator serves. Example: a seed-systems project tracks it because its donor requires a private-sector strengthening result, and because a low share mid-implementation tells the team its enterprise support package is not translating into commercial performance.
projectTypesNotApplicable: applied agronomy and farming systems and digital agriculture and AI
projectTypesRaw:
System change and transformation; seed systems and deployment.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, breeding and varietal development, applied agronomy and farming systems and digital agriculture and AI, which do not support agro-enterprises.
unit: Percentage of supported agro-enterprises
directionOfChange: Increase, read in real terms. A rising value means a larger share of supported agro-enterprises grew their revenue against baseline. An enterprise whose nominal revenue rose by less than inflation has not grown.
disaggregationRequired: Required: commodity or value chain the enterprise operates in, as recorded in the register; sex and age of the proprietor(s) for owner-operated enterprises (male / female / mixed, and 15 to 30 / over 30 / mixed, the youth band stated once in Core §4.1), recorded as not applicable where the enterprise is not owner-operated so the gap is visible.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator; no cut is specific to one project type.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Enterprise size class, on the employment bands in general international use: micro (fewer than 10 employees), small (10 to 49), medium (50 to 249), large (250 or more). Enterprise type along the chain (input supply, seed, aggregation, processing, services). Country. Type of support received.
unitOfObservation:
Organization (the supported agro-enterprise). The measurand is an institution, so the farm measurement levels do not apply: an enterprise is not observed at Trial / Station, Farm / Plot or Household level, and an enterprise that is also a farm household is counted here as an enterprise and at KPI-OC18 as a farm, never merged.

The enterprise is the unit of observation and the only level at which the indicator is measured. Regional / Aggregated and above are aggregation levels.
calculationSummary: Numerator: supported agro-enterprises in the denominator whose measured reporting-year revenue exceeds their measured baseline-year revenue, both over a complete 12-month window, the reporting-year value deflated to baseline-year prices on the national consumer price index, averaged over the months of each financial year. Denominator: all agro-enterprises on the project's supported list during the reporting period for which a complete financial year beginning after their support start date has closed, excluding those whose determination rests on a Fallback revenue figure for either year, which are reported beside the share as their own count; not-yet-eligible enterprises are reported separately as a count. Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100.
dataSource: Recommended, DS1 (Censuses and surveys): an annual enterprise revenue module administered to a census of the supported-enterprise list, drawing each figure from the enterprise's own financial records (audited accounts, tax filings, or books) where they exist and from a structured interview where they do not. Frame DS2 (Administrative and registry data): the project's supported-enterprise registry, supplying the frame, the enterprise identifiers, each support start date, which fixes the baseline year, the commodity or value chain the enterprise operates in, and, for an owner-operated enterprise, the sex and age of the proprietor(s). Fallback, DS2: revenue figures submitted through routine partner or grant reporting without project-administered collection; weaker verification, so every such figure is flagged fallback-sourced, and a determination resting on one for either year is reported beside the pooled share, never in it. Not applicable, DS3 (Geospatial and Earth observation): no satellite product observes revenue. Not applicable, DS4 (Secondary and international databases): national statistics cannot resolve a project's supported list or individual enterprises' books; the national consumer price index supplies only the deflator. Not applicable, DS5 (Citizen-generated and other non-traditional data): enterprise financial data is confidential and must be matched to the registry; crowdsourced data can do neither.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: States how many enterprises' determinations rest on a Fallback revenue figure for either year, and why direct collection was not feasible for them. Example: "Used Recommended: annual revenue module administered to all 60 enterprises on the supported registry; 54 provided usable records for both periods, none resting on a Fallback revenue figure."
collectionInstrument: DS1 route: an enterprise revenue module recording, for the 12-month window: total revenue from sales of goods and services, the source of the figure (audited accounts, tax filing, books, or interview estimate), the financial year covered, the commodity or value chain the enterprise operates in, and employee count for the size-class disaggregation. Respondent: the owner, manager, or person responsible for the enterprise's finances, whose sex and age are recorded where the enterprise is owner-operated; the enterprise identifier is recorded for matching to the registry and its own baseline. Mode: face-to-face or telephone interview, with document review where records are shared. Fallback route (DS2): no instrument; the submitted report must state the figure, the period covered, and the figure's source.
collectionFrequency: Baseline at entry to the supported list, then annually after the close of the enterprises' financial year. Short projects may measure baseline and endline only; the value then describes one interval, no trend.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Between rounds the latest measured value is carried forward with its measurement year noted.
referencePeriod: The enterprise's last complete 12-month financial year, compared against the same window in its baseline year (the year before support began). Enterprises with different financial years are each compared against their own baseline window.
baselineRequired: Yes, by construction: without a baseline revenue year the increase cannot be determined. Fallbacks, in order: (a) reconstruct the pre-support year from the enterprise's own accounts or tax filings, which enterprises hold far more often than farms; (b) if that is not feasible, monitoring only, no change claim against this indicator. Substituting the earliest reporting-year figure as a baseline is not permitted: it forces the enterprise's determination to no-increase and biases the share downward.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One reporting year, one frozen supported list, each enterprise carrying its own baseline year. A common baseline year is not required and is not obtainable: enterprises enter the supported list at different dates, and the determination is a within-enterprise comparison, so pooling across baseline years is legitimate here. The base year differs from KPI-OC18's and the difference is deliberate: KPI-OC18 is a ratio of sums across farms, so it deflates every farm to one base year common to the pooled countries, while this indicator's within-enterprise comparison lets each enterprise keep its own. Levels widen the set of enterprises; they never widen the domain.

Weight: one per enterprise. An enterprise's size does not change how much it counts, because the indicator asks how many improved, not by how much.

B: Combination method: ratio of sums.

Denominator = Σ enterprises on the frozen supported list for the reporting period for which a complete financial year beginning after their support start date has closed, including those that closed and those not measured, and excluding those whose determination rests on a Fallback revenue figure for either year, which are reported beside the share as their own count; not-yet-eligible enterprises are excluded from this sum and reported separately as a count

Revenue is deflated to the enterprise's baseline-year prices before the comparison, so a nominal rise below inflation does not qualify. Enterprises that closed, and enterprises with no usable revenue figure for one or both periods, stay in the denominator and never enter the numerator: dropping them would let the indicator improve as the weakest enterprises failed. The coverage rate is reported beside the value. Recompute from enterprise records; never average project percentages. The denominator travels with every percentage.

C: Levels and operations. Enterprise. The revenue comparison for the individual enterprise.

D: Never pooled. Nominal with deflated revenue. Enterprise shares with KPI-OC18's farm sales change, which counts farms. Cohorts whose revenue is not deflated: every enterprise carries its own baseline year by construction, so Block A pools across baseline years on purpose and it is the undeflated comparison that is forbidden. Enterprises supported in different years remain unpooled where the claim is cohort-specific. Determinations resting on a Fallback revenue figure with survey determinations.

E: Deduplication and coverage. The persistent enterprise identifier, applied from enterprise level upward, so an enterprise supported by two projects is counted once. An enterprise that is also a farm household is counted here as an enterprise and at KPI-OC18 as a farm, never merged. Coverage travels with every figure at Project area level and above. The value is a census of the supported list and carries no coefficient-of-variation band. Where projects record different support start dates for one enterprise, the earliest governs both its baseline year and its eligibility.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion: an enterprise is on the supported list where a dated project record shows it received a defined intervention, not merely that it was contacted. The frame is the project's own registry and is frozen for the reporting year, so the denominator cannot drift mid-round. An enterprise counts as supported from the date it enters that registry, but does not enter this indicator's denominator until a complete financial year beginning after its support start date has closed; revenue includes all sales by the enterprise, goods bought for resale among them. An enterprise on the supported list that has not yet completed that year is not-yet-eligible and is reported separately, as a count, never folded into the denominator or read as a zero. Exclusion: farms (KPI-OC18); one-off commercial contacts never on the supported list; non-trading income, in particular grants, subsidies, and asset sales, so that project support payments never register as revenue growth. Missing data: an enterprise with no usable revenue figure for one or both periods stays in the denominator and out of the numerator (unmeasured counts as no increase). A verified closure is a determination of no increase and also stays in the denominator, out of the numerator. An enterprise whose determination rests on a Fallback revenue figure for either year leaves both terms and is reported beside the share as its own count. The coverage rate reported beside the value is the share of the denominator with a determination, closures included. Repeated observations: one determination per enterprise per reporting year; an enterprise reached by several support streams or surveyed twice counts once, using the first complete record.
limitations:
Revenue growth is not profitability. A rise in real revenue does not establish that an enterprise is profitable, viable or hiring; costs are not in the measure. Supported agro-enterprises rarely hold verifiable cost accounts, so this sheet measures the quantity that is reliably recorded rather than the one that would be preferable.

The pathway reports returns net of costs where they can be measured: farm gross margin at KPI-OC63 and farmer net income at KPI-I03, with enterprise revenue here as the gross measure before them. A revenue rise here alongside a flat margin at OC63 is a finding, not an inconsistency.

Supports a contribution claim only. There is no comparison group: the indicator observes only supported enterprises, and revenue responds to demand, prices, competition, and macroeconomic shocks CIMMYT does not control.

The binary construction hides magnitude. An enterprise that grew 1 percent counts the same as one that doubled, and the share can rise while the portfolio's total revenue falls. Read it together with the distribution of increases, reported beside the share for the enterprises in the denominator measured in both periods.

Enterprise-reported financials carry systematic error: many supported enterprises keep partial books, an enterprise reporting to its supporter has reasons to overstate growth, and tax-linked records understate revenue. Recording each figure's source and preferring documents over interview estimates limits, but does not remove, this bias.

Without deflation, inflation alone pushes nominal revenue up and the share drifts toward 100 percent in high-inflation settings; with any-increase counting, even measurement noise registers as growth. The real-terms comparison addresses the first problem and not the second. No minimum threshold is set on top of it, since deflating already removes the inflation a threshold was meant to screen out; deflation cannot remove measurement noise, and a threshold set high enough to screen noise would screen out small true increases with it. The distribution of increases is what tells a reader how much of the share sits close to zero. For traders and aggregators revenue is commodity turnover, which the consumer price index does not strip of commodity-price movements.

A rise means a larger fraction of supported enterprises out-earned their own baseline year, in real terms. It does not mean they are profitable, viable, or hiring, and it says nothing about farmers' incomes. Pair with KPI-I04 for the jobs claim and KPI-I03 for the farmer-income claim.
subMetrics:
None. Baseline and reporting-year revenue are the two data points behind a single binary determination per enterprise; the data-coverage rate is a companion reporting statistic, not a sub-metric.

Two neighbouring sheets matter:

— KPI-OC18 (percentage change in annual sales value per assisted farm): the farm-side counterpart; organizations here, farms there. See the aggregation rule for the double-counting boundary.

— KPI-I04 (decent jobs created in the agri-food system, ILO decent-work criteria): the impact this indicator feeds. Revenue growth is evidence that supported enterprises can sustain and add jobs, not a term in the jobs count.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Mission indicator, so roles are project-level. Data collection: project M&E team (revenue module and document review); partnership team (supported-enterprise registry). Validation: project MEAL officer (registry match, figure-source checks, deflation, closure and duplicate checks). Calculation: project MEAL officer produces the project share; the CIMMYT MEAL unit de-duplicates and pools across projects. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 5 · Income & livelihoods — Reference sheet KPI-OC32

name: Gross margin of target products on assisted farms in CIMMYT intervention areas, per hectare of assessment area for crops and per animal or unit of product for livestock
resultsLevel: Outcome, as the register records it. The CIMMYT MEAL Framework defines outcomes as changes in behaviour, systems, practice, capacity, policy or performance among beneficiaries and partners (Section 2.3), and a margin is a measure of performance among beneficiaries: what the farmer obtains after the costs of obtaining it. The indicator reports that performance as a level in each reference year. A change in margin between two reports is a comparison of two levels, not a value of this indicator: it is read only between values that share every term of the pooling domain except the reference year, deflated to one stated base year as Block E requires. It sits above the productivity outputs that supply the quantity term and below KPI-I03, which converts income change into a headcount.
indicatorScope: Mission. Measures an economic change on assisted farms, not a property of CIMMYT as an organization, so it carries the project-specific layer.
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Contributing, contribution only: PO4.
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs.
sdgTarget: Target 2.3. Not reportable as indicator 2.3.2, which is an average income level for a nationally defined producer population rather than a per-unit margin on assisted farms.
otherFrameworks:
The construct is anchored on CIMMYT's own methodology, the 1988 economics training manual, and demonstrated in CIMMYT's own practice by the Mexico hub network dataset.

A precedent recorded, not followed. A major donor programme retired its farm gross-margin indicators and replaced them with yield indicators; its current handbook does not mention gross margin at all, so the retirement is complete rather than partial. The stated reason was that yield is a simplified productivity measure collecting two of the five data points gross margin required. That reduced a portfolio-wide mandatory indicator from five data points to two. It is a reporting-burden decision, not a finding that the construct is unsound, and the replacement keeps the gross-margin data points feeding it. This indicator is optional rather than mandatory, so the burden reasoning does not carry across.
definition:
The value of production of a target product, less the costs that vary in producing it, expressed per hectare of assessment area for crops and per animal or per unit of product for livestock. Value of production is the harvested quantity valued at the field price; costs that vary are the purchased inputs, hired labour, machinery, and transport and marketing charges attributable to that product, other than the harvest, transport and marketing costs that scale with the quantity harvested, which the field price already nets.

Household and unpaid non-household labour are recorded in hours over the production period the margin covers and valued at their opportunity cost as a separate line, so the margin is reportable both excluding and including it.
rationale: Closes the gap the pathway leaves between what is sold and what is earned. KPI-OC18 measures gross sales, explicitly before deducting production costs, and says so on its own sheet. KPI-I03 measures net income at impact level and reports a headcount share of farmers whose income rose, not a magnitude. Neither answers whether the return over the costs that vary is rising per hectare or per animal, which is the question a farmer faces when deciding whether to keep a practice. Gross margin answers it. It is also what separates a yield gain from a livelihood gain: a yield gain obtained through higher input costs is visible here and nowhere else in the pathway.
projectSpecificApplication: States the target products covered, the geography, the reference year, the output price source and its reference period, and the local wage rate used to value the imputed labour line, with its source, its time basis and its reference period. The definition, the cost lines and the calculation method are unchanged.
projectSpecificRationale: States the project decision, donor commitment or theory-of-change link this indicator informs, and why it is reported by this project rather than a neighbouring indicator in the pathway.
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; breeding and varietal development; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, which harvests no farm production and holds no farm cost records.
unit: Local currency per hectare of assessment area for crops; local currency per animal, or per unit of product, for livestock; current US dollars of the reference year in place of local currency where pooled across countries.
directionOfChange: Increase, read in real terms. A rising value means more of the value of production remains after the costs that vary in producing it. A nominal rise smaller than inflation is not an improvement.
disaggregationRequired: Target product; measurement level; irrigation regime (rainfed / irrigated) for crops; the livestock basis (per animal / per unit of product) for livestock; and whether the reported figure includes or excludes the imputed labour line. All five fail the poolability test: margins for different products, levels, irrigation regimes or livestock bases are never combined, and a margin computed with the imputed line is not comparable with one computed without it. Block A restates each as a pooling-domain prohibition.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: Variety, for seed systems and deployment ² and breeding and varietal development ⁴ projects, with Local as a valid value where the material is an unidentified landrace. Optional for other project types.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Sex and age of the plot or herd manager; farm size class, with the bands stated; agroecological zone, with the classification stated; sex disaggregation of household labour hours. Genuinely optional: a project that does not collect these does not report them.
unitOfObservation: Cost lines and quantity must attach to the same record. A margin assembled from a cost figure and a quantity figure that do not describe the same plot or animal is not reportable. A series is never assembled across levels.
calculationSummary:
The partial budget of CIMMYT (1988), applied to a single product rather than to a comparison of treatments. The field price is "the value of one kilogram of the crop to the farmer, net of harvest costs that are proportional to yield" (Ch. 3); costs that vary are "the costs (per hectare) of purchased inputs, labor, and machinery" attributable to producing that product (Ch. 2).

No cost is deducted twice. Harvest costs proportional to yield are deducted once, in the field price, and never again in the cost lines: hired harvesting labour, harvesting machinery, and transport and marketing costs, where they scale with the quantity harvested, are inside the field price by the 1988 convention, and the cost lines carry only the costs that do not scale with yield. A project that lists them in both places understates the margin. Household and unpaid non-household harvest labour are the exception, valued in the imputed line rather than in the field price, a departure from CIMMYT (1988), which admits opportunity costs among the harvest costs it nets.

The wage rate used to value the imputed labour line is an hourly rate, because the labour is recorded in hours. Where only a daily wage is available it is converted at the hours actually worked in a local working day, which the project states with the value: a daily wage divided by a presentation constant would misstate the hourly rate wherever the working day is not that length. The rate, its basis and the divisor travel with the value.

First, value the production. Value of production = harvested quantity × field price, each disposal channel at its own field price. The field price is the value to the farmer of one unit of the product, net of the harvest, transport and marketing costs that scale with the quantity harvested, other than household and unpaid non-household labour. Production that is consumed rather than sold enters on the same field-price basis: its gross farmgate value is netted of the same costs, so far as that production bore them, the household having harvested it on the same terms as the share it sold. The own-consumed quantity and its value are reported separately from production sold, and the split travels with the margin.

Second, sum the costs that vary. Every line below excludes the harvest costs that scale with the quantity harvested, on the no-double-deduction rule above: purchased inputs; hired labour other than harvesting labour whose charge scales with the quantity harvested; machinery, whether owned, rented or contracted, other than harvesting machinery whose charge scales with the quantity harvested; the transport and marketing charges that do not scale with the quantity harvested, the yield-proportional ones having already been netted out of the field price above and never counted twice; and nothing else.

Indirect expenses are not costs that vary and are not in this sum. Land rental, insurance and maintenance are recorded where the project holds them and reported as their own line beside the margin, never merged into the costs that vary, because they do not move with the quantity produced.

Third, record household labour in hours, by activity, alongside the number of people and the hours worked. Hours are recorded for the production period the margin covers, not for a calendar week, month or year, because a margin is a property of a crop cycle or a livestock production period and a calendar unit would cut across it. The period is stated with the value, in the same units on every value in a series, so two seasons remain comparable; a project needing a calendar figure derives one from the recorded hours and states the conversion. This is the physical record and it is kept whether or not it is valued. It is the same labour-hours module that KPI-O59 and KPI-O60 use as a denominator; the hours are valued here and nowhere else. Unpaid non-household labour is recorded separately, as KPI-O59 records it. The imputed labour line is household labour and unpaid non-household labour, both valued at the rate the Fourth step sets.

Fourth, value the imputed labour line at its opportunity cost. CIMMYT (1988) directs that "the best place to start in estimating an opportunity field price for family labor is the local wage rate (plus nonmonetary payments)", and warns that the rate varies seasonally and is hard to estimate where local labour markets are poorly developed. The rate used, its source and its reference period travel with the value.

Fifth, compute both margins.

Both are divided by the assessment area in hectares, or by the number of animals or units of product, of the same record. The assessment area is Σ harvested area plus Σ established-but-failed area, the same denominator Vol. 7 · KPI-O23 defines and uses at Household level and above, and is the denominator here for the same reason: a margin taken over harvested area alone excludes established-but-failed ground and overstates the result worst in the seasons the measure exists for. Both figures are reported. A single margin figure without its counterpart cannot be compared across farms of different unpaid-labour intensity.
dataSource: Comparator DS4: national cost-of-production statistics, as a plausibility check on the CIMMYT figure, never a substitute for it and never pooled with it.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Names the systems that hold the plot or animal records and the cost module, and the persistent identifiers that link them; states how many records are on each route and, for the Fallback, whether a recalled cost line or the quantity put them there, the livestock basis in use for livestock records, the intercrop apportionment rule where it applies, the basis on which owned machinery is charged, and the method that produced each record's area, as KPI-O23 records it.
collectionInstrument:
The cost module, defined once and attached to the collection instruments of KPI-O23 (plot record) and KPI-O24 (animal record) rather than fielded separately. It records, per record: the quantity of the product by disposal channel, sold and own-consumed, and the price per unit in each channel, received for sales and the local farmgate price for own consumption, with the price's source and reference period, from which each channel's field price is computed as the Calculation method defines it. It records, per record and per activity: purchased inputs with quantity and price; hired labour with hours worked and the amount paid, flagged whether its charge scales with the quantity harvested; machinery use, with the basis of the charge where owned, flagged whether its charge scales with the quantity harvested, since only the lines whose charge does not scale enter the costs that vary; transport and marketing, recorded split into the charges that scale with quantity harvested and those that do not, because only the second group enters the cost lines; household labour, and unpaid non-household labour recorded separately as KPI-O59 records it, in hours, with the number of people and the hours per person; and, separately, indirect expenses.

Attaching the module to the existing records keeps the quantity and the costs on the same plot or animal; no separate instrument is fielded. The output-price and disposal fields above are the module's own: the plot and animal records of KPI-O23 and KPI-O24 carry the quantity and not the price, so the module adds them rather than inheriting them.

Precedent in current CIMMYT practice. The Mexico on-farm hub network dataset (Gardeazábal-Monsalve et al., 2025) implements this structure at scale over 2012 to 2022. Its Costs_and_Revenues file records costs grouped by activity, land preparation, sowing and seed, soil and water analysis, cultural work and physical weed control, input application, irrigation, manual and mechanical harvest, and marketing, plus indirect expenses covering maintenance, land leasing and insurance, with total costs and income both expressed per hectare; and its labour file records hours per hectare per activity, the number of people participating, shift length and days spent. Revenue there includes self-consumption valued at average regional prices, which is a gross price rather than the field price defined above.

Three qualifications on that precedent. Its regional-price valuation of self-consumption is a gross basis, so it is a precedent for collecting the disposal split and not for pricing it; this sheet nets both dispositions to the field price. The dataset cites no methodology source, so it demonstrates the approach rather than defining it; the definitions here rest on CIMMYT (1988). And it records no paid-versus-unpaid flag on manual labour, so separating household labour from hired labour is an extension of current practice rather than a restatement of it.
collectionFrequency: Each season or production cycle for which the project reports the product, on the same schedule as the plot or animal record the cost module attaches to.
referencePeriod: The cropping season or production cycle for the target product, assigned to the reporting year in which it was harvested. Costs are those incurred for that cycle, including pre-season input purchases.
baselineRequired: No. This indicator reports a level.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One target product, one irrigation regime, one measurement level, one livestock basis for livestock, per animal or per unit of product, one currency, one reference year, one treatment of the imputed labour line. Cross-country pooling converts each country's reference-year values, in current local currency, to US dollars at the average annual market exchange rate for the reference year, and the pooled figure is stated in current US dollars of that year. Values compared across years are deflated in local currency on the national consumer price index (Block E), to one base year common to every value compared, and converted, where conversion is needed, at the average annual market exchange rate for that base year. Purchasing power parity is not used: these indicators measure transacted value, and a PPP conversion answers a different question about what that value buys locally. The rate and its source are recorded with the figure. Levels widen the set of records; they never widen the domain. Where a reporting level spans several domains the figures are reported side by side, never summed. No combined figure exists across products, across livestock bases, across currencies without conversion, or between the including-labour and excluding-labour treatments.

Weight: units, hectares for crops and animals or units of product for livestock on the basis the project declared, so a larger holding carries proportionally more of the mean margin.

B: Combination method: ratio of sums.

Units are hectares for crops and animals or units of product for livestock. Area is the assessment area, Σ harvested plus Σ established-but-failed area, as this sheet's Definition and Unit of measure state, and as Vol. 7 · KPI-O23 uses at Household level and above. The full plot area is never the denominator of a pooled figure. The estimator is invariant to staging, so recompute from records; never average means. The value of production, the costs that vary and the imputed labour line are each summed and carried, so an institutional figure is recomputed from components rather than assembled from project margins.

C: Levels and operations.

D: Never pooled. Different target products. Different irrigation regimes, and different measurement levels. Different currencies without a stated conversion and reference year. Margins including the imputed labour line with margins excluding it. Margins computed per animal with margins computed per unit of product. Records on the Recommended route with records on the Fallback route. Nominal margins from different years without deflation to a stated base. Crop margins with livestock margins.

E: Deduplication and coverage. The persistent plot or animal identifier, applied from Farm / Plot upward, with the household identifier carried so a household is counted once. Deflate before comparing across years, in local currency, to a stated base year, stating the index. Coverage and precision travel with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands used in official statistics: 16.5 percent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 percent released flagged, above 33.3 percent not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one de-duplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above, and a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place. Where identifiers cannot be reconciled, the figure is labelled an upper bound on measured coverage.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Include records for the target product in the reference year that carry both a quantity and a complete set of cost lines on the same record.

Exclude records holding a quantity but no costs, or costs but no quantity; they are reported as a coverage shortfall with the count, never imputed from another record. A margin is a difference between two quantities measured on one unit, and substituting either term from elsewhere produces a number describing no farm.

Intercropped plots are reported separately from sole-crop plots, on the assessment area, with the companion crop declared, following KPI-O23. The full plot area is never the denominator of a pooled figure. Costs shared across the intercrop are apportioned by the project's stated rule, and the rule is recorded with the value.

Missing any hours of the imputed labour line where the including-labour figure is reported: the record contributes to the excluding-labour figure only, and the two figures then rest on different record sets, which is stated.

Machinery owned rather than hired is charged on the project's stated basis, and the basis travels with the figure; an owned asset charged at zero overstates the margin.
limitations: Contribution, not attribution. Prices, weather and input markets move alongside the intervention, so a margin change is not evidence that CIMMYT produced it.
A margin is not profit. Costs that vary exclude fixed and overhead costs, so a positive margin does not establish that producing the target product is profitable; the net-income concept is KPI-I03's.

The imputed labour line is a judgement, not a measurement. CIMMYT (1988) is explicit that an opportunity cost for family labour is difficult to estimate where local labour markets are poorly developed, and that wage rates vary seasonally. Reporting the margin both with and without the line keeps the judgement visible rather than concealed in a single number.

Own-consumed production has to be valued, and the price chosen moves the margin. The valuation convention is the field price defined in the Calculation method, applied to sold and own-consumed production; the price fields the Collection instrument records are what fix it, and it is held constant across rounds.

Costs are the noisiest part of a farm survey. Recalled input quantities, shared crop and livestock costs, and machinery charged on an owned asset are all sources of error, so logged records are preferred and recalled values are reported separately.
Not comparable across currencies without conversion, or across years without deflation, and a nominal rise below inflation is not an improvement.
Coverage is not representativeness. A pooled margin describes the records held, not the population of assisted farms, and records carrying a quantity but no costs are excluded rather than imputed.
subMetrics:
Value of production, costs that vary, and the imputed labour line are each retained and reported alongside the margin, not only their difference. A margin reported without its components cannot be recomputed, and an institutional figure is recomputed from the components rather than averaged from project margins.

Relationship to other indicators. KPI-OC18 measures gross sales value before costs and says so; this indicator supplies the cost side that OC18 omits by design. KPI-I03 measures net agricultural income at impact level and deducts hired labour only, following the SDG 2.3.2 convention; because the imputed labour line here is separate and separable, the margin excluding it matches I03 on the treatment of household labour. It does not match it on the rest: I03 values production at farmgate prices and deducts depreciation, while this sheet values at the field price and deducts neither depreciation nor any fixed cost, so the two figures are read together and never as versions of one number. KPI-O23 and KPI-O24 supply the quantity term, and the cost module attaches to their records. KPI-O59, KPI-O60 and KPI-OC62 use the same labour-hours module as a physical denominator and never value it; the valuation belongs here. KPI-OC32 measures agro-enterprise revenue, which is enterprise-level and not a farm margin.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: Content owner: the CIMMYT MEAL unit, with the socioeconomics lead as technical reviewer.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project enumerators and extension agents maintaining the plot and animal records and the attached cost module. Validation: project MEAL officer. Calculation: project MEAL officer, applying the formula in Calculation method. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 5 · Income & livelihoods — Reference sheet KPI-OC63

name: Percentage of smallholder farmers with an agricultural income increase over baseline in CIMMYT intervention areas
resultsLevel: Impact. On the CIMMYT MEAL Framework's test, this is the longer-term population-level change that the adoption and income outcomes contribute to: it counts farmers whose economic condition changed, not a result CIMMYT delivered. CGIAR also places income and poverty results at impact level, so the crosswalk agrees.
primaryObjective: PO3: Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Contributing (contribution only): PO4, Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient.
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs
sdgTarget: None (direct). Closest: SDG indicator 2.3.2 under target 2.3, average income of small-scale food producers, by sex and indigenous status. Not a direct match: 2.3.2 reports an average income level in constant purchasing-power-parity dollars for a nationally defined population, while this reports a share of CIMMYT-targeted farmers whose own income rose. Its income concept is adopted; its population and statistic are not.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Common Results Framework: partial correspondence with the two impact indicators under Poverty reduction, livelihoods and jobs (number of poor people benefiting from relevant CGIAR innovations; number of people assisted to exit poverty), the basis of the register's "contributes CRF-I1/I2" flag. Partial both ways: CGIAR counts poor people, this counts targeted smallholders whether poor or not, and neither CGIAR indicator measures an income increase. CGIAR's own review lists Income among the impact-level themes its standard set does not cover.
definition:
The share of smallholder farmers with an agricultural income increase over baseline in CIMMYT intervention areas. Numerator: smallholder farmers with a measured real increase in net agricultural income over their own baseline; denominator: all target smallholder farmers.

Agricultural income is net, not turnover: production revenue from crops, livestock, fisheries and forestry minus operating costs and depreciation, following the labour-statistics convention behind the matching SDG measure; off-farm wages and remittances are excluded.

The value is a headcount share, not a magnitude, and a contribution claim. Smallholder is defined in Annex B.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's work reaches farmers as income: how many of the smallholders CIMMYT set out to serve now earn more from farming than before. It is the terminal result of the Income and livelihoods chain, and the measure management, funders and CGIAR reporting use to judge whether productivity and market work translated into livelihoods rather than stopping at adoption.
projectSpecificApplication: State the population and geography (target-farmer list, countries, zones), the crop and livestock activities included in agricultural income, the price base, the threshold defining an increase, and the design supporting the contribution claim. Do not change the numerator, denominator, unit or calculation method; if applying the indicator as defined is not feasible here, raise it with the MEAL focal point.
