projectSpecificRationale: State the funder commitment this figure reports against and the project decision it informs, for example whether the share of farmers gaining, rather than the average gain, is the contractual target.
projectTypesNotApplicable: breeding and varietal development and digital agriculture and AI
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, breeding and varietal development and digital agriculture and AI.
unit: Percentage of target smallholder farmers
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of smallholder farmers recorded a real increase in net agricultural income against baseline. Real terms is the qualifying test: a nominal rise below inflation does not count as an increase.
disaggregationRequired: Required: sex (female/male at minimum, per CGIAR's sex-disaggregated data standards); age (youth/non-youth, youth taken as 15 to 30, stated once in Core §4.1). Projects record date of birth or exact age so other bands, for example a donor band of 15 to 29, can be derived. The youth cut carries a second duty: the Gender equality, youth and social inclusion pathway's youth-inclusion thread (KPI-OC26) has no impact indicator of its own, and its impact destination is this indicator and KPI-I04 read at the youth band.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator; no cut is specific to one project type.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Farm size class; agroecological zone; principal commodity or value chain; market-participating versus largely subsistence households.
unitOfObservation: The smallholder farmer or household. The measurements beneath it come from the farm records that establish each farmer's income, and the same entity rules as KPI-OC18 apply: one holding is one farm, and the farm-holding identifier anchors the series.
calculationSummary:
The determination is per farmer, in constant prices, so inflation alone cannot create an increase: did this farmer's own net income rise above the stated threshold between the two rounds, yes or no. A comparison group, where the project holds one, strengthens the contribution claim and is recorded with the figure; it is a reporting condition, not a precondition.

— Denominator: the smallholder farmers on the project's targeting list, on the declared Annex B threshold, not the subset measured. The share is estimated from a representative sample of that list and weighted to it; a convenience sample describes the sample only and cannot be extrapolated.

— Numerator: those farmers whose endline net agricultural income, in the same constant prices as baseline, exceeds their own baseline by more than the stated threshold, estimated from the weighted sample. Net agricultural income = value of production minus operating costs (inputs, own output used as seed or feed, hired labour, rental, transport, marketing and livestock bought) and depreciation. Value of production is all crop, livestock, fisheries and forestry output of the reference year at farmgate prices, whatever its disposal (sold, own-consumed, given away, stored, used as seed or feed), plus the change in livestock numbers over the year, opening and closing herds valued at the same farmgate price per class; crop and other stored output sold from stocks held at the start of the year is not production of the year; animals leaving the herd, sold, slaughtered or given away, enter at their value, the change in livestock numbers netting the opening herd. Depreciation is computed on one method the project states with the value and applies identically in both rounds.

— Threshold: the institutional default is any real increase above zero, fixed and documented before data collection. A project may set a higher threshold and states it with the value, and then also reports the value on the institutional default, so a comparable figure always exists; it may not set a lower one. A default of zero has no noise floor, so the distribution of increases is reported with the percentage, and where the project documents a measurement error for its own instrument the share of farmers exceeding that error is reported beside the headline: without either, survey noise and price rounding are indistinguishable from small gains.

— Retain and report with the percentage: (a) target smallholder farmers; (b) sample size measured; (c) sample farmers with an increase; (d) the deflator used.
dataSource:
Recommended, DS1: farm-economics panel survey of a representative sample of target smallholder farmers at both rounds, capturing production, disposal (sold, own-consumed, given away, stored, used as seed or feed), farmgate prices and input costs by activity, with a comparison group where feasible. Sample drawn from the project's target-farmer list by random or stratified random sampling (strata: zone, farm size, sex where these carry disaggregation requirements). Smallholder status is taken from the targeting list where it records the Annex B variable, and otherwise from the survey's own measurement of it.

Frame DS2: the project's target-farmer list, supplying the sampling frame, the farm-holding identifiers and the denominator population, with the principal farm operator named in the farm registry.

Not applicable, DS1 repeated cross-section: a repeated cross-section cannot produce this indicator. It counts farmers whose own income rose, which requires following the same farmers; a distributional change between two independent rounds is a different quantity and cannot be labelled into this one. Where no panel exists, KPI-OC18 and KPI-OC63 are reported and the income headcount is recorded as not reportable for that project and period.

Fallback, DS2: cooperative, aggregator or contract-farming records, usable only to reconstruct the revenue side and only alongside a DS1 cost module. Never sufficient alone: revenue is not income, and unmarketed production is invisible to it. A farmer whose revenue in either round comes from these records is flagged fallback-sourced, leaves both terms of the share at every level and is reported beside it, with the revenue component and the round named.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State the sampling method and achieved sample size, whether a comparison group was available, and how many farmers' revenue in either round came from the Fallback DS2 records.
collectionInstrument: Farm-economics module inside the project's farmer panel survey: activity-level production and disposal, farmgate prices, input and hired-labour costs, and asset depreciation, opening and closing livestock numbers by class, livestock bought, and crop stocks held at the start of the year with the part of them sold, in both rounds, with a persistent farmer identifier so the rounds link. Respondent: the principal farm operator, the person the project's farm registry names for the farm-holding, as on KPI-OC18, whose sex and age anchor this indicator's disaggregation. Where crop and livestock activities are managed by different household members, both are interviewed for their own activity's production, disposal and cost data, but the principal farm operator is the one identity recorded against the farm for sex and age, whichever manager responds. Mode: face-to-face, trained enumerators.
collectionFrequency: Baseline and endline, with a midline every 2 to 3 years in multi-year projects.
reportingFrequency: At endline, and annually only where a maintained farmer panel supports it. Between waves the latest measured value is carried forward, with its year of measurement stated.
referencePeriod: The interval between this indicator's own baseline and endline rounds. The project sets it, and it is stated in years with every value rather than assumed from a standard length. Each measurement covers a full agricultural year, so seasonal timing does not drive the comparison.
baselineRequired: Yes, mandatory: without a starting income there is no increase to observe. The only fallback where no prospective baseline exists is a recall-based reconstruction of the baseline year, which is weaker for income than for yield because costs are poorly recalled, and which is flagged on every value it produces. A matched comparison group is not a fallback baseline and is not offered as one: measured at endline it observes two groups once, which yields no within-farmer change, and this indicator counts farmers whose own income rose. Its role is the one stated in the Calculation method, a reporting condition that strengthens the contribution claim, never a substitute for the starting income. Otherwise the project can monitor income levels but cannot report this indicator.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One population of smallholder farmers, one reporting window, one currency at constant prices, one qualifying threshold. Each farmer's two rounds are compared in that farmer's own currency, deflated to a stated base year, so no currency conversion enters this indicator: the value pooled across countries is a share of farmers, not an amount of money. One declared smallholder threshold, as Annex B defines it. Values computed on different declared thresholds are never pooled, because a population is not the same population when its boundary moves. The threshold that defines a qualifying increase is part of the domain: a project counting any real gain and a project counting a gain above ten percent are not measuring the same event, and pooling them produces a figure that describes neither. Whether a comparison group was available does not split the domain: every value is a contribution claim, and values from a baseline without a counterfactual enter the pooled figure on the same footing as those with one. Levels widen the set of farmers; they never widen the domain.

Weight: the sampling weight carried by each farmer record; both terms are sums of weighted farmers.

B: Combination method: ratio of sums, weighted to the target list.

The measured panel is a probability sample of the targeting list, and its records carry the sampling weights that raise them to it; the unweighted panel share is not the reported value. The weights are recomputed over the responding panel, less any farmer flagged fallback-sourced, before either sum is taken. On the weights as originally drawn a farmer excluded for a missing round would stay inside the denominator and out of the numerator, counted as no increase, which the missing-data field forbids and which biases the share downward rather than upward. Where the sample is not a probability sample of the list, the value describes the sample only and is labelled as such. Achieved coverage against the targeting list travels with every figure.

Income is net of operating costs and depreciation, with hired labour deducted and household labour not deducted, following the SDG 2.3.2 convention. Values are deflated to a stated base year. Rebuild the share from farmer records; never average project percentages.

C: Levels and operations. Household. The income comparison for the individual farmer or household.

D: Never pooled. Values computed on different qualifying thresholds. Nominal with deflated income. Income headcounts with KPI-I06's productivity headcounts, which count a different qualifying change on the same farmers. Income magnitudes with KPI-OC63's margins, which exclude fixed costs and depreciation. Panels with different windows. Income headcounts with KPI-I04's job counts: a job holder there may be a farmer here, and the two are never added into one people figure.

E: Deduplication and coverage. The persistent farm-holding identifier, applied from Household level upward, with the same entity rules as KPI-OC18. Coverage and precision travel with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands used in official statistics: 16.5 percent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 percent released flagged, above 33.3 percent not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one de-duplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above, and a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
— Inclusions, exclusions, missing data: sampled farmers with usable income data in both rounds are counted. A farmer missing a round, or a component large enough to change the sign of the change, is excluded from the sample denominator rather than imputed, never counted as no increase. A farmer whose revenue in either round comes from the Fallback DS2 records is flagged fallback-sourced, leaves both terms of the share at every level in the same way, and is reported beside it. Farmers who left farming between rounds are retained as no increase, reported separately.

— Repeated observations: one determination per farmer per period across all farm activities; a farmer interviewed twice in a round counts once, from the first complete interview.
limitations:
The named income standard, and where CIMMYT departs from it. The income concept is that of UN SDG indicator 2.3.2: annual income from on-farm production, net of operating costs and depreciation, with hired labour deducted and household labour not deducted, following the income definition of the 17th International Conference of Labour Statisticians. This sheet and KPI-OC63 part on two things a reader must not merge. KPI-OC63's margin excluding imputed labour matches this sheet on the treatment of household labour. They differ on the price basis and on the costs deducted: KPI-OC63 values production at the field price, as its Calculation method defines it, and deducts no depreciation, a gross margin stopping at the costs that vary; this sheet values production at farmgate prices and deducts operating costs and depreciation, on the SDG 2.3.2 convention. A margin from KPI-OC63 is therefore never read as an income figure from this sheet.

The value is not reportable as SDG 2.3.2. That indicator defines small-scale producers as those in the intersection of the bottom 40 percent of the distributions of land, livestock and revenue, and reports an average income level for a nationally representative population. This sheet applies CIMMYT's own smallholder convention and reports a headcount share among assisted farmers. The concept is borrowed; the population and the statistic are not, and the figure is never presented as an SDG return.

On the price base, values are deflated to a stated base year using the national consumer price index, which is published for every country CIMMYT works in and is the series projects can obtain. An agricultural producer price index would track the sector more closely but is unavailable or discontinued in several of them, so it cannot serve as the common deflator.

Contribution, not attribution. Agricultural income also moves with output and input prices, weather, other programmes and off-farm opportunities, and CIMMYT is one contributor among many. A counterfactual strengthens the contribution claim and is recorded with the value; it does not make the claim an attribution claim, which is a third-party impact-study term.

A threshold has a cost in both directions. Requiring a gain above a stated minimum screens out small true gains as well as noise-driven crossings, and it does not stop a noise-driven crossing that happens to clear the minimum. Raising the threshold trades one error for the other rather than removing either.

Net farm income is among the noisiest variables in farm surveys: it depends on valuing own-consumed production and shared crop-livestock costs, and can be negative, so valuation conventions must be fixed in the instrument and held constant across rounds.

Nominal comparisons produce spurious increases: in a high-inflation setting almost every farmer shows higher nominal income, so only the constant-price comparison carries meaning and the deflator must be reported with the value.

The measure is magnitude-blind and welfare-blind: a farmer clearing the threshold narrowly counts the same as one who doubled income, and since only agricultural income is counted, a rising share is consistent with falling total household income. Read it with the sales-value and access outcome indicators, not as poverty reduction.
Panel attrition biases the share upward when the worst-faring farmers drop out, as does drawing the sample where adoption is already high; report attrition with the value.
subMetrics: None. The determination is a single yes or no per farmer across all farm activities. Retained figure (c), the sample farmers with an increase, is the unweighted count behind the weighted numerator, kept for verification and not a separate metric.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
Sources without a link have no durable public URL and are cited by title, edition and publisher.

External alignment: UN Statistics Division (2024), SDG indicator metadata: indicator 2.3.2, the income concept (revenue minus operating costs and depreciation, per the 17th International Conference of Labour Statisticians) and the constant-price unit.

International Labour Organization (2003). Resolution I: Resolution concerning household income and expenditure statistics, Seventeenth International Conference of Labour Statisticians: https://www.ilo.org/media/271131/download. The labour-statistics income concept SDG 2.3.2 and this sheet's net-income definition both rest on.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the impact assessment lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project survey team and enumerators. Validation: project MEAL officer (both rounds complete, deflator applied, identifiers linked). Calculation: CIMMYT impact assessment and MEAL unit. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit, which reports the pooled value institutionally and to CGIAR.
sourceRef: Volume 5 · Income & livelihoods — Reference sheet KPI-I03

name: Number of decent jobs created in the agri-food system through CIMMYT-supported interventions
resultsLevel: Impact. Employment creation is a long-term economic change in the lives of external actors, and the register's roll-up terminal for the Jobs & enterprise indicator group.
indicatorScope: Mission. Measures an economic result delivered to external populations (workers and enterprises in supported agri-food systems), not a property of CIMMYT as an organization.
domain: Cross-cutting / Common, as recorded in the register: employment results serve projects across domains.
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. One primary objective only; the register lists PO3 first, its primary convention, and records the roll-up as PO3 impact: decent employment is a livelihood trajectory improving. Contributing objective, contribution only: PO4 (agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient), because a system generating decent jobs is a more inclusive one.
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs. The register carries no Impact Area column; the pathway-wide rule sets it for every indicator here, and the mapping is direct, since jobs are named in the Impact Area title.
sdgTarget: None. The closest target is SDG 8.5 (full and productive employment and decent work for all women and men). Its indicators measure national labour-market conditions (8.5.1 average hourly earnings, 8.5.2 unemployment rate), and none counts jobs created by an intervention, so the correspondence is at target level only and not reportable as an SDG indicator value.
otherFrameworks: ILO Decent Work Indicators framework (national statistical and legal framework indicators). Cited as a standards-body source because no peer-reviewed source defines the decent-job construct, which is a normative framework rather than a measurement result, and the ILO framework is its authority of record. The 32 One CGIAR standard indicators include no employment indicator, so there is no CGIAR correspondence.
definition:
Counts decent jobs created in the agri-food system through CIMMYT-supported interventions. A decent job is a paid position offering regular payment at or above the legal minimum wage, or the prevailing local wage where none applies, which also passes the three normative criteria and the duration floor: no child or forced labour, no obstruction of workers' rights to organize, safe working conditions, and at least 30 days of work with one employer within a reporting year.

The agri-food system spans on-farm production, agro-processing, input supply, trade and transport of agricultural products, and food services. This five-segment boundary is CIMMYT's convention, following the agri-food value chain (Barrett et al., 2022).
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's agri-food systems work translates into decent employment: labour markets are one of the three poverty-impact channels the CGIAR-commissioned poverty study identifies, beside consumer prices and farm incomes. The CGIAR Impact Area is named Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods and Jobs, yet the One CGIAR standard-indicator review found all its standard indicators concern poverty, none employment, so this indicator fills a recognized gap in institutional and funder reporting.
projectSpecificApplication: Describes which supported enterprises, service businesses, and farm employers this project counts jobs in, in which zones, over which window. Example: a mechanization project counts new hire positions in the machinery-service businesses it incubated, screened against the decent-work checklist. The definition, counting rule, and decency screen stay unchanged; a project that cannot apply the screen raises this with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining what counts as decent.
projectSpecificRationale: States the project decision, donor requirement, or reporting need served. Example: an agro-industry project tracks it because its donor requires an employment result, and because a stagnant job count alongside growing enterprise revenue (KPI-OC32) tells the team growth is not translating into hiring.
projectTypesNotApplicable: seed systems and deployment and digital agriculture and AI
projectTypesRaw:
System change and transformation.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, breeding and varietal development, applied agronomy and farming systems, seed systems and deployment and digital agriculture and AI.
unit: Number of jobs (headcount of created positions), with a full-time-equivalent (FTE) conversion reported alongside where positions are part-time or seasonal.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more positions created through supported interventions passed the decent-work screen and the duration floor. Headcount and full-time equivalent move differently, so both are reported and neither substitutes for the other.
disaggregationRequired: Required: sex (female/male, per CGIAR's sex-disaggregated data standards) and age (youth/non-youth, youth as 15 to 30, stated once in Core §4.1; projects record date of birth or exact age so other bands, for example a donor band of 15 to 29, can be derived), recorded per job holder when the position is filled. Screen outturn (counted / excluded on a fail / unverified), so a headline is always read beside how much of the workforce was screened. The youth cut carries a second duty: the Gender equality, youth and social inclusion pathway's youth-inclusion thread (KPI-OC26) has no impact indicator of its own, and its impact destination is this indicator and KPI-I03 read at the youth band.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator; no cut is specific to one project type.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Agri-food system component (on-farm production, agro-processing, input supply, trade and transport, food services). Formality of the employing entity. Permanent versus seasonal position. Country and value chain.
unitOfObservation:
The job is the unit of observation, recorded within the employer that created it: a supported enterprise, service business or farm employer. The measurand is a position, so the farm measurement levels do not apply.

The employer is the record that holds the positions and carries the persistent identifier; it is not itself the unit counted. Sex and age describe the job holder at filling.

Regional / Aggregated and above are aggregation levels.

Unpaid household labour is not a job. Hours worked by household members on their own holding are counted as labour input by KPI-O59, KPI-O60 and KPI-OC63 and are never converted into employment here; the ILO decent-work boundary is what separates the two, and the two are never summed.
calculationSummary:
Value: the count of new paid positions created in the agri-food system as a result of a CIMMYT-supported intervention, that pass the decent-work screen. A count indicator: no denominator. Duration floor. A position counts where it provides at least 30 days of work with one employer within a reporting year, summed across every engagement of that position with that employer in the year, so a single short harvest engagement does not count on its own while a seasonal position re-engaged across the season's operations does. Without a floor a single day's casual labour becomes a created job. A position that does not reach the floor in the year it was created enters the count in the first reporting year in which it does, and never twice.

Decent-work screen. A decent job is a paid position in the agri-food system offering regular payment (daily, weekly, fortnightly or monthly) at or above the legal minimum wage, or where none applies the prevailing local wage for comparable work, against a full-time workload of 8 hours per day and 40 hours per week. The wage test is applied per hour worked: pay for the period divided by the hours worked in it, against the wage floor converted to an hourly rate on that workload, piece rates included. A day of work, for the duration floor, is a day on which the position was engaged. Positions worked below full time are neither excluded nor fractioned in the headcount: each counts as one job. Their hours enter the FTE series instead. A headline containing a half job is neither series. A position must also involve no child or forced labour, no obstruction of workers' rights to organize, and safe working conditions. Each of those three is recorded per position as pass, fail or unverified, never assumed: the employer's declaration on the record for child and forced labour and for freedom to organize, and the presence or absence of a documented safety arrangement for working conditions.

A position counts only where all three are pass. A fail on any one excludes the position. An unverified on any one sends it to the coverage shortfall rather than the count, because an unverified criterion cannot be treated as passed.

The three outturns, counted, excluded and unverified, are reported together: a headline without its unverified count says nothing about how much of the workforce was screened. The wage floor is the national legal minimum wage published by the country's labour authority for the occupation and period; where none applies, the prevailing local wage for comparable work, with its source and reference period stated on the record. The ILO decent work framework is the conceptual reference; the test above is CIMMYT's operational screen. Social-protection coverage is recorded where a national scheme exists but is not currently a condition of the screen.
dataSource: Recommended, DS1 (Censuses and surveys): an employer/enterprise survey of the supported entities (a census of the supported-entity registry), collecting positions created with hire dates, hours, wages, engagement terms, social-protection status, and job-holder sex and age; recommended because the decency screen requires terms of employment that plain counts do not carry. Frame DS2 (Administrative and registry data): the project's supported-entity registry, supplying the frame and the identifiers the once-per-job rule depends on. Fallback, DS2: partner or enterprise payroll records without a verification survey, usable only where they carry hire dates and enough on wage and terms to apply the screen; every position recorded this way is flagged fallback-sourced. Payroll or contract records sighted during the Recommended survey are part of that route, not this one. Not applicable, DS3 (Geospatial and Earth observation): employment and its terms are not observable from satellite or aerial data. Not applicable, DS4 (Secondary and international databases): national employment statistics cannot resolve project-attributable job-creation events; usable for wage benchmarks only. Not applicable, DS5 (Citizen-generated and other non-traditional data): cannot verify terms of employment or support the identifier quality once-per-job counting requires.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: States how many positions rest on payroll records without the survey (the Fallback), why the survey was not feasible for them, and which decency criteria those records could not verify. Example: "Used Recommended: annual employer survey, census of the 62 supported enterprises on the project registry; no position rests on payroll records without the survey."
collectionInstrument: DS1 route: an employer/enterprise employment module recording, per position created in the window and per earlier position that met the duration floor in no earlier reporting year: role, hire date, hours per week and months per year, wage or pay basis, engagement terms, social-protection status, and job-holder sex and age, with the decent-work checklist applied per position. For the founder of a newly created enterprise: the enterprise's creation date and its supporting record, the days traded in the reporting year, the founder's declaration on child and forced labour and on freedom to organize, and the documented safety arrangement. Respondent: the owner, manager, or personnel record holder. Mode: face-to-face or telephone interview, payroll or contract records sighted where available. Fallback route (DS2): no instrument; the record must carry, per position, entity identifier, role, hire date, hours, pay, the employer's declaration on child and forced labour and on freedom to organize, and a documented safety arrangement, so the same three normative criteria can be applied; a position missing any of them is sent to the unverified category rather than assumed to pass.
collectionFrequency: Annually; aligned to the end of the main season where hiring is seasonal.
reportingFrequency: Annually. The annual value reports the jobs counted in that year; cumulative totals are labelled as such.
referencePeriod: The reporting year: positions that first meet the duration floor in the 12-month reporting period, counted once. Because each job is counted once, a cumulative total since project start can be reported alongside without recounting.
baselineRequired: Yes, at enterprise level: the pre-support employment level of each supported entity, needed to distinguish newly created positions from replacement hiring and turnover. Fallbacks: recall-based reconstruction in the first survey round, or hire-date evidence from payroll records. If neither is feasible, count only positions that are verifiably new (a newly established enterprise, or a documented new function) and note the likely undercount.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One reporting year. Levels widen the set of jobs; they never widen the domain. Headcount and full-time equivalent are two series, never one figure.

B: Combination method: sum. Total = Σ jobs counted in the domain, reported as a headcount and, separately, as an FTE total with the conversion basis stated. A position filled twice in one year is one job. Fallback-sourced positions are summed separately and reported beside the total, never in it.

C: Levels and operations. Job, within its employer. The position record.

D: Never pooled. Headcount with FTE. Jobs with KPI-OC32's enterprise revenue shares. Unpaid household labour hours with employment: the hours counted by KPI-O59, KPI-O60 and KPI-OC63 are labour input, not jobs, and the ILO decent-work boundary separates them. Jobs counted in different years, reported as separate annual counts unless the cumulative basis is stated. Founder self-employment with hired positions. Jobs with KPI-I03's farmer headcount, which may count the same people.

E: Deduplication and coverage. The persistent employer identifier with the position reference, so a job created through two projects is counted once. Where identifiers cannot be reconciled, the figure is labelled an upper bound on distinct positions. The count is a census of the registry and carries no coefficient-of-variation band.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: paid positions newly created in supported agro-enterprises, service businesses, processing, input-supply, trading and storage operations, and new hired-labour positions on farms, where creation is a contribution of the supported intervention, evidenced by a dated record (a new enterprise, or a documented expansion following the support). Exclusion: pre-existing jobs sustained, upgraded, or formalized; replacement hiring; unpaid family labour; positions failing the decency screen (countable separately, never in this value).

Founders. The founder's own self-employment in a newly created enterprise is reported as a separate count beside the headline, never added to it. The enterprise's creation is evidenced as a contribution of the supported intervention by a dated record, as for a hired position. The founder is screened on the three normative criteria, declaring for the enterprise on child and forced labour and on freedom to organize, with safe working conditions evidenced by a documented safety arrangement; a founder with any criterion unverified is reported as unverified beside the founder count, not in it. The duration floor is met where the enterprise has traded on at least 30 days in a reporting year, and a founder is counted once, in the first reporting year in which it is met. The wage floor does not apply, a founder drawing profit rather than a wage. Missing data: a position whose decency criteria cannot be verified is not counted; it is reported in the required unverified category of the screen outturn. Repeated observations: each job is counted once, in the first reporting year in which it meets the duration floor, and only if it passes the decent-work screen in that year; a persisting job is not recounted; a position vacated and refilled is the same job; re-engagement of a seasonal position in a later year is not a new job. Part-time or seasonal positions are also converted to full-time equivalents (FTE) at 2,080 hours per year, reported alongside headcount. The constant is arithmetic on the full-time workload this sheet already defines, 40 hours a week over 52 weeks, and is stated as CIMMYT's convention rather than borrowed.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only, and a gross one: the count records jobs created in supported entities without a counterfactual and does not net out displacement (a job created in a supported mill may come at the cost of one in an unsupported mill).

The decency screen is a project-level approximation of a framework built for national labour statistics. Two of the three normative criteria rest on the employer's declaration, which an employer reporting to its supporter has an incentive to give, so the screen can pass positions that would fail an independent check. Where no declaration or safety record exists the position is unverified and left out of the count, biasing it downward in the most informal settings. The unverified count is published, so the second effect is visible; the first is not measurable from the record.
Counted once, in the year it first meets the duration floor, the value says nothing about whether jobs persist: a growing cumulative count can coexist with net job losses in the same enterprises.

Comparability across projects depends on a uniform counting convention: headcount versus FTE, the seasonal-work threshold, and the strictness of the decency screen each move the count materially. Values from projects that apply a different convention are not comparable and are not pooled.
A rise means the supported segments recorded more decent-job creation; it does not mean net employment in the agri-food system grew, incomes rose (KPI-I03), or poverty fell.
subMetrics: None. Headcount and the FTE conversion are two expressions of the same count; the sex, age, and system-component breakdowns are disaggregations, not sub-metrics.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Mission indicator, so roles are project-level. Data collection: project M&E team with enterprise partners (employer survey, supported-entity registry). Validation: project MEAL officer (decency-screen evidence, hire dates, once-per-job rule, identifier quality). Calculation: project MEAL officer produces the count and FTE conversion; the CIMMYT MEAL unit performs cross-project de-duplication and pooling. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 5 · Income & livelihoods — Reference sheet KPI-I04

name: Number of farmers in CIMMYT intervention areas accessing resilience-building practices packages
resultsLevel: Output
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Contributing: PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient), PO5 (Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities).
cgiarImpactArea: Climate Adaptation & Mitigation
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator counts farmers accessing resilience practices. Nearest thematic relatives: SDG target 2.4 (indicator 2.4.1 measures the proportion of agricultural area under productive and sustainable agriculture, not farmers reached) and SDG target 13.1 (its indicators measure disaster impacts and risk-reduction strategies, not farmer reach).
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Results Framework 2025-30: no direct correspondence confirmed; its Climate Adaptation and Mitigation indicators sit at impact and portfolio-outcome level, while this is a CIMMYT-defined output reach measure.
definition: Counts unique farmers in CIMMYT intervention areas accessing resilience-building practice packages (stress-tolerant varieties, water and soil management, diversification) in the reporting year, counted once per farmer regardless of number of packages. "Access" means the farmer came into direct contact with a significant intervention delivered by CIMMYT and/or an implementing partner: receiving stress-tolerant seed, taking part in a demonstration or hands-on training on a resilience practice, or receiving a targeted advisory service. Access is a reach measure: it records that the offer arrived at the farm gate, not that the farmer went on to apply the practice. Continued application is measured by the companion outcome indicator KPI-OC20, which this output feeds.
rationale: Answers how many farmers CIMMYT's climate-resilience work is reaching each year: the first and most directly manageable step in the resilience results chain, before adoption (KPI-OC20) and resilience impacts can be observed. Project teams use it to manage delivery and coverage; institutional reporting uses it to show the breadth of the resilience portfolio, disaggregated by sex and age so reach to women and young farmers is visible from the start of the chain.
projectSpecificApplication: State the project's intervention areas (countries, regions, communities), the specific practice packages promoted under each practice category of the list version in force, and the delivery channels used (direct, partner-mediated, or both). Do not change the unit, the unique-farmer counting rule, or what counts as access; if the indicator as defined is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor requirement this reach count serves: for example, a donor-required beneficiary reach indicator, or an internal coverage trigger (if reach to women or youth falls below plan, the delivery strategy is reviewed).
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose work is laboratory and controlled-environment research with no farmers
households or land in an intervention area to observe
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose work is laboratory and controlled-environment research with no farmers, households or land in an intervention area to observe.
unit: Number of farmers per reporting year (unique individual people, not households, plots, or farms)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more farmers obtained access to a resilience-building practice package.
disaggregationRequired: Required: sex (female/male); age (youth/non-youth, 15 to 30, stated once in Core §4.1; projects record date of birth or exact age so other bands, for example a donor band of 15 to 29, can be derived).
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Practice-package type, by practice category of the list version in force; country or region; crop; smallholder vs non-smallholder; delivery channel (direct vs partner-mediated).
unitOfObservation: Individual (farmer)
calculationSummary: Value = the count of unique farmers in CIMMYT intervention areas who accessed at least one resilience-building practice package through a CIMMYT or partner intervention during the reporting year. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: administrative and registry data generated by delivery itself: seed and input distribution lists, demonstration and training attendance registers, advisory-service user logs, and partner reporting (including validated sales or service records of supported input suppliers). Fallback DS1: farmer or household survey in the intervention area, used to estimate reach where delivery leaves neither a farmer-level record nor partner records from which reach can be estimated under Eligibility (Inclusion), or to verify registry figures; survey-estimated values are flagged as fallback-sourced. Not applicable DS3: access is a farmer-level event not observable from satellite or GIS data. Not applicable DS4: no third-party database resolves which farmers a CIMMYT project reached. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced data cannot verify that a specific farmer accessed a CIMMYT-promoted package.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether the project reported from the Recommended source (its own and its partners' delivery records) or the Fallback (survey-based estimate), and if Fallback, why delivery left neither farmer-level records nor partner records from which reach could be estimated (for example, a partner that kept neither participant lists nor sales or service records).
collectionInstrument: For DS2 (Recommended): a beneficiary registration record at the delivery point capturing farmer name or unique identifier, sex, age, location, package type, and date of access. For DS1 (Fallback): a short reach-verification module in a farmer survey; respondent: the farmer who accessed the package; mode: face-to-face or phone interview. CIMMYT MEAL issues a harmonized beneficiary registration template carrying the required sex and age fields.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, through delivery and participation records as interventions are implemented; consolidated once per year.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Yearly values are snapshots; they must not be summed across years to claim cumulative unique farmers reached unless farmers carry unique identifiers across years.
referencePeriod: The reporting year (12 months). Each reported value describes reach in that year only.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual reach count that starts from zero at project start; pre-existing access to similar practices outside CIMMYT interventions is not counted. Projects set ex-ante annual reach targets instead. Record that the companion outcome KPI-OC20 (adoption) does require a baseline; plan for it when setting up this indicator's registration records.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: sum Recommended-sourced (registry) values directly; a project that had to use the Fallback (survey estimate) is reported alongside the summed figure with a note, not blended in.

B: Combination method. Sum across projects: the institutional figure is the total number of unique farmers reached across all reporting projects in the reporting year.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of unique farmers on that project's access register for the reporting year, de-duplicated on the project's own farmer identifier. At institutional level, the count of unique farmers across projects, de-duplicated again across registers. No unique farmer identifier or beneficiary registry exists across CIMMYT projects and none is planned, so wherever project areas overlap the institutional figure is labelled an upper estimate rather than presented as a count, unless the overlapping registers share an identifier that reconciles them. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the reconciliation basis, the number of records dropped for want of an identifier, the partner-estimated reach included in the institutional figure (Eligibility, Missing data), and the version of the practice list in force, since the count is defined by it.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count does not add to or divide into KPI-OC20 (a percentage of adopters) or the pathway's impact indicators; the levels connect through the Theory of Change, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: each project reports unique farmers within the year, not contact events; where projects operate in overlapping areas, de-duplicate by farmer identifier before publishing an institutional total, or label the total an upper estimate. Named overlap risks in the register: farmers counted here may also appear in KPI-OC20's numerator (adopters are a subset of those with access). Three reach counts in other pathways cover the same farmers on a different cut and the boundary is stated rather than assumed. KPI-O20 (Innovation development & scaling) counts farmers accessing improved technological packages, and a resilience-building package is also a technological package, so a farmer reached with stress-tolerant seed meets both definitions; the two are reported side by side and are never summed. KPI-O21 counts demonstration and hands-on training participation, and partner-estimated reach, as access, and KPI-O20 counts neither, so the two differ by rule as well as by package. KPI-O26 (Capacity, data & institutions) counts farmers reached with digital advisory services, and a resilience package delivered through a digital advisory channel is counted here for the package and there for the advisory contact; again reported side by side, never summed. KPI-O18 (Innovation development & scaling) counts farmers trained in improved production practices, and a farmer trained on a resilience practice is counted there for the training and here for the access; reported side by side, never summed. Never add this indicator to another farmer-count indicator without de-duplication, and state which boundary was used.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Qualifying packages: The practice categories named in the Definition are illustrative of the one closed, versioned CIMMYT-wide list this pathway shares; the version in force at the reporting date governs what qualifies and travels with the value. A package counts only where the practices in it address a climate risk that is material in that agro-ecology, the same test KPI-OC20, KPI-OC36 and KPI-I12 apply. The project states, for each practice in the packages it reports, the local climate risk it addresses and the basis for calling that risk material, and the statement travels with the value.

Missing data: a delivery record that cannot be linked to a unique farmer is excluded from the unique count, and the number excluded is reported with the value. Partner-estimated reach under Inclusion carries no farmer-level record and is not subject to this rule: it is reported as its own line with its conversion assumption, and a headline that includes it states the share it contributes, and is not verifiably a unique count, since estimated reach cannot be matched against registry farmers. Records missing sex or age stay in the headline count and are reported under "disaggregation not available".

Repeated observations: each farmer counts once per reporting year regardless of packages or contacts; under the optional package-type disaggregation a farmer may appear once per package, so disaggregated counts can sum to more than the headline total and must be labelled accordingly.
limitations: Access is not adoption and not benefit. This indicator shows the offer reached farmers, not that they applied the practices (KPI-OC20) or became more resilient (KPI-I05, KPI-I07). CGIAR's review of its standard indicators warns explicitly against extrapolating reach or use numbers into benefit claims; do not present this figure as "farmers made more resilient".

Double counting is the main measurement error. The same farmer can appear in several distribution lists, projects or years. Without a shared identifier, a cross-project total where project areas overlap is an upper estimate (Aggregation rule, Block C); annual values are not summed across years unless farmers carry unique identifiers across years (Reporting frequency).

Partner-mediated estimates carry assumption error. Where reach is estimated from seed sales or service records (for example, one sale equals one farmer), figures are only as good as the documented assumptions, which need periodic validation through spot surveys.

Comparability across projects depends on a shared definition of a "package" and a shared threshold for what counts as access. If one project counts any field-day attendee and another counts only seed recipients, their numbers are not comparable; apply the counting rules in Section 3 uniformly.
A rise in the value means CIMMYT's resilience offer reached more farmers that year; a fall may reflect a project cycle ending rather than a performance problem.
subMetrics: None. The practice-package types, by practice category of the list version in force, are disaggregations of the same count, not sub-metrics. Related indicators with their own sheets: KPI-OC20 (percentage of farmers adopting resilience-building practices, the outcome this output feeds per the register roll-up), and further along the chain KPI-I05 (households maintaining income through shocks), KPI-I07 (yield loss avoided under climate stress), and KPI-I12 (area with enhanced climate resilience).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project field teams and implementing partners, at the delivery point. Validation: project MEAL officer (registry completeness, de-duplication within the project, spot checks of partner-reported figures). Calculation: project MEAL officer applying the unique-farmer counting rules; CIMMYT MEAL unit for cross-project de-duplication at institutional level. Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 6 · Resilience & climate — Reference sheet KPI-O21

name: Number of anticipatory-action, early-warning, or crisis-response tools or protocols delivered for agrifood systems
resultsLevel: Output. A tool or protocol delivered is a delivered result of the research team. Whether anyone uses it is the outcome question, answered by KPI-OC38, not by this count.
primaryObjective: PO5 Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved), PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Climate Adaptation & Mitigation
sdgTarget: None. SDG target 13.1 (strengthen resilience and adaptive capacity to climate-related hazards) is thematically adjacent, but its official indicators (13.1.1 to 13.1.3) measure disaster impacts and the adoption of national and local disaster risk reduction strategies at country level, not tools an organisation delivers. No SDG indicator directly corresponds to this count.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Technical Reporting: tools and protocols of this kind are reported as Innovation Development outputs (with an innovation readiness level) or Knowledge Products under the CGIAR Results Framework's output result types; no CGIAR standard indicator counts them, so this is a CIMMYT-defined indicator feeding those categories. The WMO Early Warnings for All initiative frames the global agenda these tools serve.
definition: Counts the anticipatory-action, early-warning, or crisis-response tools or protocols CIMMYT delivers for agrifood systems in the reporting year; counts distinct tools or protocols made available to users. An anticipatory-action tool triggers protective action before a predicted hazard materialises, based on a forecast or risk trigger; an early-warning tool turns hazard monitoring into an actionable alert (a drought advisory, a pest-outbreak alert); a crisis-response protocol is a documented procedure a user follows when a shock hits (a seed-system contingency plan). A tool or protocol counts once it is finalised and made available to its intended user (a government agency, a partner institution, or a farming community), whether CIMMYT delivered it alone or with partners.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT is building the instruments agrifood systems need to see shocks coming and act on them: the countable entry point of the crisis-anticipation results chain leading to institutions with strengthened capacity to anticipate and respond to crises (KPI-OC38) and to reduced food-security losses when disruptions hit (KPI-I17). Used by project management to track delivery and by institutional and donor reporting to evidence CIMMYT's contribution to coordinated global action on disruptions and the climate crisis.
projectSpecificApplication: State which tools or protocols the project delivers, the hazard they address, the countries covered, and the intended user of each. Do not change the unit, the delivery test, or the counting rule. If applying the indicator as defined is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count informs (for example, a donor-required deliverable count for a climate-services component, or an internal milestone trigger: if planned tools are not delivered by a set date, the workplan and partner arrangements are reviewed).
projectTypesNotApplicable: upstream discovery science and breeding and varietal development
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI; seed systems and deployment.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science and breeding and varietal development, neither of which delivers anticipatory-action, early-warning or crisis-response capability, which is what this indicator counts.
unit: Number (count of distinct tools or protocols)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more anticipatory-action, early-warning or crisis-response tools or protocols were made available to users.
disaggregationRequired: Required: tool type, using the three categories in the definition (anticipatory-action tool, early-warning tool, crisis-response protocol). The register records no required disaggregation for this indicator, so this cut is CIMMYT's own, applied on the sheet's authority: a total that mixes an early-warning tool with a crisis-response protocol is not interpretable. Each tool takes exactly one type.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Hazard or shock type (drought, heat, flood, pest or disease outbreak, conflict or market disruption); country or region; intended user type (national or local government, research or academic, private sector, civil society or community); crop or farming system covered.
unitOfObservation: The delivered tool or protocol itself. This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct anticipatory-action, early-warning, or crisis-response tools or protocols CIMMYT delivered, alone or with partners, and made available to their intended users within the reporting year. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: CIMMYT project output and deliverable registries logging each tool or protocol, its delivery date, intended user, hazard covered, and the evidence of availability (handover record, release note, launch record), cross-checked against project technical reports. Fallback DS4: partner or platform records (a national meteorological or disaster-management agency's published catalogue, FAO or OCHA anticipatory-action tracking) used to reconstruct the count where CIMMYT's own delivery log is incomplete; any value built this way is flagged as fallback-sourced, because external platforms do not authoritatively record CIMMYT's contribution. Not applicable DS1: this indicator counts institutional deliverables from records, not data collected from respondents. Not applicable DS3: satellite data may be an input inside a delivered tool (a drought monitor), but that describes the tool's content, not how this count is measured. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or citizen-generated data cannot verify an institutional delivery.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which route each tool or protocol rests on; for any on the Fallback, state why the project's own delivery log was incomplete and which external records were used.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). The register entry itself is the instrument: each record names the tool or protocol, tool type, delivery date, intended user, hazard and geography covered, the evidence of availability, and, for an anticipatory-action tool, its trigger and threshold, lead time and pre-agreed action or, for an early-warning tool, its alert threshold and lead time.
collectionFrequency: Continuous: each delivery is logged as it occurs
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the tool or protocol first became available to its intended user
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual flow count that starts from zero each reporting year; there is no pre-project stock of CIMMYT-delivered tools to measure. Change over time is read from the annual series itself.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: sum the tools and protocols evidenced in projects' own delivery registries (Recommended); a tool or protocol evidenced only in external records (Fallback) is reported alongside the summed figure with a note, not blended in, and the same project's Recommended-sourced tools and protocols are summed.

B: Combination method. Summed: the institutional figure is the sum of distinct tools or protocols across all reporting projects in the year, after de-duplication. Never average project-level counts.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying tools and protocols delivered in the reporting year. At institutional level, the de-duplicated sum of those counts, computed from the delivery records themselves rather than by adding project figures. De-duplication is on tool identity, meaning name, type and major version, per Block E. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the number excluded under Eligibility and why, and the number of tools and protocols reported alongside because they rest on the Fallback.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count does not combine arithmetically with KPI-OC38 or KPI-I17; the three connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative: tools delivered, capacity strengthened, losses reduced.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: two named risks. Within this indicator, a tool co-delivered by two CIMMYT projects, or rolled out in several countries, carries one institutional tool identifier and counts once, with country coverage as a disaggregation; if identifiers cannot be matched, label the sum an upper estimate. Across the register, the same deliverable may also qualify as a co-developed innovation (KPI-O01, Innovation development & scaling), as a decision-support tool or assessment delivered to decision-makers (KPI-O32, Policy, finance & market systems) or as a policy-relevant evidence product or decision-support tool (KPI-O39, Policy, finance & market systems); the shared identifier must mark it so the institutional roll-up never presents one product as two achievements.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion: a tool counts when CIMMYT finalises it and makes it available to its intended user, evidenced by a dated handover record, a release or publication record, or an operational launch; co-delivered tools count once, with CIMMYT's contribution documented. An anticipatory-action tool counts under that type only if its delivery record states the trigger (the forecast or monitoring variable and its threshold), the lead time between trigger and expected hazard impact, and the action pre-agreed to follow the trigger. An early-warning tool counts under that type only if its record states the hazard monitored, the alert threshold and the intended lead time of the alert. A record lacking these is counted under the type its content supports, or not counted.
limitations: Delivery is not use: a tool logged as delivered may never be operated, updated, or institutionalised by its recipient, and a tool that is operated may still issue alerts too late to act on, or may not be trusted enough by its intended users to be acted on at all. This count cannot distinguish a national early-warning product in daily use from a pilot used once, and it carries no evidence of timeliness, trust or action taken. The outcome evidence belongs to KPI-OC38.

"Tool or protocol" spans very different products, so raw counts are not comparable across projects until the tool-type disaggregation is applied consistently; one national early-warning system may matter more than five briefing notes.

The count is sensitive to logging granularity: splitting one toolkit into components inflates the figure, bundling deflates it. The distinct-tool identifier and the delivery-evidence requirement are the controls; read the count together with the tool list behind it.

An increase means CIMMYT made more crisis-anticipation instruments available, not that agrifood systems became more resilient; pair with KPI-OC38 and KPI-I17 for the results chain, and never present the count alone as evidence of impact.
subMetrics: None. The three tool types named in the definition (anticipatory-action, early-warning, crisis-response) are disaggregations of the same count, not separately calculated metrics. Related indicators in the results chain have their own sheets: KPI-OC38 (institutions with strengthened capacity to anticipate and respond to agrifood-system crises, the outcome this output feeds) and KPI-I17 (reduction in food-security losses during agrifood-system disruptions, the pathway impact).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E focal point, logging each delivery with its evidence. Validation: project MEAL officer, cross-checking the log against project technical reports. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (de-duplication across projects and the institutional sum, per Aggregation rule). Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 6 · Resilience & climate — Reference sheet KPI-O41

name: Percentage of farmers in CIMMYT intervention areas adopting resilience-building practices
resultsLevel: Outcome. The result is a behaviour change of external actors (farmers choosing to keep using a practice); it answers "who will do what differently" and sits between the output KPI-O21 (packages delivered) and the impact indicators it feeds: KPI-I05, income maintained through a shock; KPI-I07, the yield advantage under a drought or heat stress event; and KPI-I12, land under practice whether or not a shock came.
indicatorScope: Mission. It measures a behaviour change among farmers, an external population, so it carries the full project-specific layer below.
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Sustained practice adoption is the direct behavioural evidence of increasingly resilient livelihood trajectories. Contributing objectives (contribution only): PO4 (practice change is the ground layer of a climate-resilient agrifood system) and PO5 (documented adoption at scale feeds the evidence base for coordinated climate action). One primary objective only; the register lists PO3 first and the first-listed objective is primary, per the register's convention.
cgiarImpactArea: Climate Adaptation & Mitigation, the pathway-wide default for every indicator in this pathway.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest reference, SDG indicator 2.4.1 under target 2.4 (proportion of agricultural area under productive and sustainable agriculture), measures area, not farmers. Source: UN SDG indicator 2.4.1 metadata sheet (Metadata-02-04-01), UN Statistics Division.
otherFrameworks: Under the superseded 2022 arrangement, Action Area outcome indicators STRAFSi 1.1 ("Number of smallholder farmers who have implemented new practices that mitigate climate change risks, disaggregated by gender and type of practice") and STi 1.1 ("Number of farmers using climate smart practices disaggregated by gender") were count-based variants (CGIAR System Organization, 2022). Donor reporting frameworks carry a count of individuals applying improved practices, where this indicator reports a share of a defined target population and counts only continued use after support ends.
definition: The share of farmers in CIMMYT intervention areas adopting one or more resilience-building practices, out of all target farmers. Resilience-building practices are those in the packages whose reach KPI-O21 counts: stress-tolerant crop varieties, improved water and soil management, and crop or income diversification, which reduce the damage shocks cause to production and income. Adoption is continued use: a farmer counts when they keep applying at least one promoted practice on a plot they manage for one full production season after support ends, the continued-use test KPI-OC16 also applies in the Innovation development & scaling pathway. Being reached, trained or given inputs is not adoption; that is what KPI-O21 counts.
rationale: Answers whether farmers in CIMMYT intervention areas are changing how they farm in response to climate risk: the behaviour-change step that turns delivery of varieties, agronomy, and advice (KPI-O21) into resilient livelihoods. Because the criterion is continued use, the value separates lasting practice change from participation effects that fade with the project. Practice adoption is a standard outcome in CGIAR and donor results frameworks, feeding institutional and funder reporting directly.
projectSpecificApplication: Describe the project's target population and intervention areas, and, where the project's own scope is smallholders, declare that scope here with the Annex B threshold it applies; a share over all target farmers and a share over smallholders are reported side by side and never pooled. Also state which promoted packages are in scope, and the project's survey rounds; the institutional definition, adoption criterion, and calculation method are unchanged. Illustrative example: a project measures adoption of stress-tolerant maize and water harvesting among its 12,000 target farmers in three districts, at baseline, endline, and one ex-post round after support ends. Where the project holds a comparison group, describe its design (rollout timing, matching method, or other) and where its results are reported.
projectSpecificRationale: State which project decision, donor requirement, or local reporting need the adoption measure serves. Illustrative example: a project reports adoption as its donor's required climate-resilience outcome indicator, and a low midline rate among women farmers triggers a redesign of its extension delivery.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose work is laboratory and controlled-environment research with no farmers
households or land in an intervention area to observe
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose work is laboratory and controlled-environment research with no farmers, households or land in an intervention area to observe.
unit: Percentage of target farmers
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of the target farmers meet the adoption criterion. The denominator is all target farmers, so the share falls when targeting widens without adoption keeping pace.
disaggregationRequired: Required: sex (female/male); age (youth/non-youth, 15 to 30, stated once in Core §4.1; projects record date of birth or exact age so other bands, for example a donor band of 15 to 29, can be derived); practice category, as the practice-list version in force defines the categories (stress-tolerant varieties, water and soil management and diversification among them). Smallholder status, as Annex B defines it, with the declared threshold travelling with the value: the institutional denominator is all target farmers, and the smallholder population of the impact indicators this indicator feeds is not narrowed at this level.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Crop, agroecological zone, country or region, farm size class, named practice within each category.
unitOfObservation: Individual: each person who manages at least one plot in the target population, with smallholder status recorded as an attribute per Annex B. Where the survey samples households, every plot manager in a sampled household is enumerated and survey weights are carried by individuals.
calculationSummary: Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100, applying survey weights. Numerator: target farmers in current use, at the round, of at least one promoted practice from the KPI-O21 packages that they were not using at baseline, on at least one plot they manage; use present at baseline is reported beside the value as the pre-existing-use share. Denominator: all target farmers in the intervention areas, the target population, not the survey sample and not participants only; estimated from a representative sample. Count each farmer once regardless of number of practices; the practice-category disaggregation keeps single- and multi-practice adoption visible. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1 (censuses and surveys): representative farmer or household survey of the target population, with a practice-adoption module and enumerated practice checklist; the only source that can produce a valid percentage, because the denominator includes farmers the project never touched directly. Fallback DS2 (administrative and registry data): project M&E, partner extension, and input or seed sales records, used only where a survey is not feasible; these cover participants, not the target population, and observe delivery or purchase, not continued use, so a DS2-sourced value overstates adoption and is always flagged and reported separately. Not applicable: DS3, remote sensing cannot identify which farmers adopted (corroboration of area-visible practices only); DS4, no international database resolves CIMMYT intervention areas or the practice list; DS5, crowdsourced reports lack the sampling frame a population percentage requires.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role the project used, Recommended or Fallback; if Fallback, why a survey was not feasible, with every value flagged as fallback-sourced. Illustrative example: "Used Recommended: adoption module in the project's own baseline, endline, and ex-post survey rounds."
collectionInstrument: Farmer or household survey module listing the promoted practices, applied plot by plot. Respondent: the plot manager, including a micro-manager where land is under joint management. Mode: face-to-face or phone interview. Each record carries a persistent farmer identifier linked to the KPI-O21 delivery records for within-project de-duplication and reach-adoption comparison. Because a snapshot convention would count use in the reporting year alone, the module adds continued-use questions: when support ended, and use since.
collectionFrequency: Baseline and endline; for multi-year programmes, a midline every 2 to 3 years. An ex-post round at least one full production season after support ends is the only round that yields the continued-use value; a project without one reports interim values only, and says so.
reportingFrequency: Annually; between waves, the latest measured value is carried forward with its year of measurement noted.
referencePeriod: The 12 months (or most recent completed cropping seasons) before data collection. A value is the continued-use value only where the round was taken at least one full production season after the project's support in the intervention area ended; a value from any earlier round, endline included where it falls before that point, is reported as interim, labelled as such, with the number of seasons elapsed and the share of the numerator whose support ended at least one full season before the round.
baselineRequired: Yes. The baseline records current use of listed practices, since no support has yet ended; it identifies the use present at baseline, which the numerator excludes and which is reported as the pre-existing-use share. Fallbacks where no prospective baseline exists: recall-based reconstruction of pre-intervention practice use, secondary pre-period survey data, or a matched retrospective comparison. If none is feasible: monitoring only, no change or impact claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Across projects: pool Recommended-sourced values directly; a Fallback-sourced project is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, never blended in, since it observes participants and delivery, not the population and continued use. Pool only values judged against the same practice-list version. A value reported as interim (Reference period) is shown beside the pooled figure with its seasons elapsed and is never pooled with continued-use values.

B: Combination method. Pool farmer-level data across projects using survey weights; the institutional figure is the weighted percentage of adopting farmers across all reporting projects' target populations. Never average project-level percentages. Report the weighted numerator alongside the percentage, since a percentage without its numerator cannot be pooled across projects.

C: Levels and operations. A share is recomputed at every level from its own numerator and denominator, never averaged from the levels beneath it. At Farm / Plot, the plot roster establishes which promoted practices were in continued use and no share is reported, since the unit of the share is the farmer. At project level, target farmers meeting the adoption criterion over all target farmers, both estimated with survey weights from the same round. At Regional / Aggregated and institutional level, the summed numerator over the summed denominator within the pooling domain of Block A, computed from farmer records rather than from project shares. Also report: the denominator itself, the mean number of promoted practices in continued use per adopting farmer, as the intensity reading, since one practice on one plot qualifies and no minimum-intensity rule applies, the version of the practice list the numerator was judged against, the number excluded under Eligibility, the non-response share, the pre-existing-use share (target farmers using a listed practice at baseline, over the denominator), and the variety-identification method (self-report, or verified against a reference such as DNA fingerprinting).

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: no. This percentage does not combine arithmetically with KPI-O21 (a reach count on a delivery-based population) or with KPI-I05, KPI-I07, KPI-I12; the levels connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative, not arithmetic, and OC20's numerator must never be divided by O21's count to fabricate a conversion rate. This outcome feeds KPI-I05, KPI-I07 and KPI-I12 at once and its contribution is never apportioned among them: the three measure different results, and splitting a share between them invents a division the data does not carry.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: where intervention areas overlap, the projects are pooled only where their sampling frames assign the overlap area to one of them; otherwise they are reported side by side and not pooled, since a pooled share whose two terms both double count is not bounded in either direction. A farmer counted by both this indicator and KPI-O21 in one year is not double counting; the two are never summed.
