eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion: every farmer in the intervention area's target population is in scope, whether or not they took part in a CIMMYT activity; the denominator is the full target farmer population, not the survey sample and not the participant list. For a target farmer who took part in no CIMMYT activity, support ends when the project's support in that intervention area ends, as the project's records date it. The practice categories named in the Definition are illustrative of the one closed, versioned CIMMYT-wide list this pathway shares; the version in force at the reporting date governs what qualifies and travels with the value. A practice qualifies only where it addresses a climate risk that is material in that agro-ecology, the same test KPI-OC36 and KPI-I12 apply to the same practices; being an improved practice is not sufficient. The project states, for each practice it reports, the local climate risk it addresses and the basis for calling that risk material, and the statement travels with the value. Exclusion: researcher-managed demonstration plots. Smallholder status is recorded per Annex B rather than used to restrict the denominator, and the declared threshold travels with the value.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only: adoption also responds to other actors' extension, input prices, market signals, and recent weather.
Self-reported adoption carries measurement error: farmers may over-report promoted practices (social desirability) and may misidentify varieties.
Values are only comparable if the practice list, adoption threshold, and intervention-area boundary are held constant; a longer practice list mechanically raises the percentage.

The continued-use criterion cannot be fully tested mid-project: only a round at least one full season after support ended shows use beyond support, and a farmer may dis-adopt between waves, so single-wave values are provisional.
A rise means more target farmers report sustained use of the practices; it does not by itself mean resilience improved. Pair with KPI-I05, KPI-I07 and KPI-I12 for the contribution narrative.

Where a project holds, or can establish, a comparison group (a staggered rollout, a matched sample of non-participant farmers, or another quasi-experimental design), its design, and where its results are reported, are stated in Project-specific application. This strengthens the contribution evidence and provides the basis for a third-party impact evaluation; it does not change how this indicator itself is calculated or reported, and a project without one reports the same way.
subMetrics: None. Practice-category breakdowns are disaggregations, not sub-metrics. Related sheets: KPI-O21 shares this indicator's practice list and, within a project, its farmer identifier, and must be revised with it; KPI-I12 carries no comparison group and reads its hectares from the KPI-OC36 plot roster.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Mission indicator, so roles are project-level. Data collection: project M&E team and enumerators. Validation: project MEAL officer, checking the practice checklist against the KPI-O21 package list, the continued-use questions, and the farmer identifiers. Calculation: project M&E; the CIMMYT MEAL unit pools and de-duplicates across projects. Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 6 · Resilience & climate — Reference sheet KPI-OC20

name: Percentage of farming-system area under climate-adaptation practices
resultsLevel: Outcome. Applying adaptation practices on their own plots is a change in practice among beneficiaries, which is the Core's definition of an outcome.
indicatorScope: Mission. The result is a change in how external producers manage their own land, so the sheet carries the full project-specific layer.
primaryObjective: PO4 Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient. Area coverage of adaptation practices directly measures how climate resilient the agrifood system's physical footprint is becoming. Contributing objectives (contribution only): PO3, because the covered hectares are largely smallholder-managed land; and PO5, because documented adaptation coverage feeds the evidence base coordinated climate action draws on. The register lists PO4, PO3, PO5 and the first-listed value is primary, adopted as the register-wide convention.
cgiarImpactArea: Climate Adaptation & Mitigation, the pathway-wide default: the indicator's subject is climate-risk reduction on agricultural land, the core of that Impact Area.
sdgTarget: None. The closest relative, SDG indicator 2.4.1 (proportion of agricultural area under productive and sustainable agriculture), shares the area-share construction but is a composite of 11 themes spanning environmental, economic and social sustainability, not climate adaptation specifically, so it is listed under Other frameworks, not claimed as a direct correspondence.
otherFrameworks: Donor reporting frameworks carry a hectare count rather than a percentage, so the two are not interchangeable. CGIAR Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30, Annex 1: Portfolio Outcome 12, indicator 12.2 Number of hectares of agricultural land under improved management, the nearest CGIAR counterpart. SDG indicator 2.4.1 (see above).
definition: The share of the farming-system area in intervention areas on which at least one climate-adaptation practice was applied during the reporting year. Climate-adaptation practices are practices and technologies promoted with the explicit objective of reducing the risk of climate impacts or minimizing their severity: for example drought- or flood-tolerant varieties, shorter-duration varieties, adjusted sowing dates, crop diversification, agroforestry, and water harvesting. Each physical hectare counts once in the numerator, even where several practices are applied on it, so the value is bounded between 0 and 100 percent. The indicator measures coverage of recognized adaptation practices, not resilience itself.
rationale: Answers whether the climate-adaptation practices CIMMYT and its partners promote are taken up at meaningful spatial scale, moving beyond counting adopting farmers to the share of land covered. The share serves project steering, institutional reporting and donors.
projectSpecificApplication: Describe the intervention areas covered (named and mapped), the producer population whose land forms the denominator, the practice-list version used, and the survey timing relative to the cropping calendar. The institutional definition, unit and calculation method are unchanged; a project that cannot apply them as defined raises it with the CIMMYT MEAL focal point rather than redefining them here.
projectSpecificRationale: State which project decision, donor requirement or national reporting need the coverage share serves. Illustrative example: a project reports the share annually against its donor's coverage target and uses the practice-type breakdown to decide which practices need reinforced extension at midterm.
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, which manages no land in an intervention area.
unit: Percentage of area (hectares under climate-adaptation practices as a share of total farming-system hectares in intervention areas). The hectare numerator is reported alongside the percentage.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of the farming-system area is under climate-adaptation practices.
disaggregationRequired: Required: climate-adaptation practice type (from the practice list); type of area (crop land, cultivated pasture, rangeland or other, each area assigned to one type only); country. The register records no required disaggregation, so these cuts are CIMMYT's own, applied on the sheet's authority, because a share pooled across practice and land types cannot be interpreted or quality-assured.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Sex and age of the plot owner and of the plot manager where land is individually managed; crop or commodity; agroecological zone; irrigated versus rainfed.
unitOfObservation: Plot (aggregated to the intervention area).
calculationSummary: Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100, applying survey weights where a sample survey is the source. Numerator: unique physical hectares in the intervention areas on which at least one practice from the practice list was applied during the reporting year; a hectare counts once regardless of how many listed practices it carries or how many cropping cycles it passes through (because a percentage must stay bounded at 100). A plot enters the numerator with the area under at least one listed practice, which is its whole area only where a listed practice covers the whole plot. Denominator: the sample-weighted total farming-system area of the same plot roster as the numerator, within the declared boundary. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1 (censuses and surveys): sample survey of producers in the intervention areas, sampled to represent the whole farming-system area within the declared boundary rather than activity participants alone, with a plot roster capturing each plot's area and the practices applied during the reporting year, and sample-weighted hectare totals per practice type. Fallback DS2 (administrative and registry data): project M&E records, farm records and partner reporting, acceptable only to establish practice use on plots in the plot roster (Calculation method), with documented assumptions periodically validated through spot surveys; area reported outside the roster enters neither term, and without a plot roster the indicator is not measured. Frame DS3 (geospatial and Earth observation): a satellite land-cover product verifies the roster's denominator area, and any difference between the two is reported with the value; it never replaces the roster denominator and never produces the numerator. DS3 also corroborates the subset of practices with a detectable signal (agroforestry, cover crops, tillage regime); most listed practices (variety choice, sowing dates) cannot be read from imagery, and DS3 use does not make a value fallback-sourced. Not applicable DS4: national and international statistics cannot resolve a project intervention area; context only. Not applicable DS5: the value requires verified plot areas and a defined practice checklist per plot, which crowdsourced data does not provide at auditable quality.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role this project used, Recommended or Fallback; if Fallback, why the survey's practice checklist could not establish practice use on the roster plots, with every reported value flagged as fallback-sourced. A value is fallback-sourced when any part of its numerator came from DS2; DS3 verification or corroboration does not make it fallback-sourced. Example: "Used Recommended: plot-roster module in the annual monitoring survey; DS3 land-cover product to verify the denominator."
collectionInstrument: Plot-roster survey module: for each plot, the area (GPS or geo-referenced polygon measurement preferred; farmer-reported area only if calibrated against GPS on a subsample) and a checklist of practices applied during the reporting year against the practice list. Where a listed practice covers only part of a plot, the area under it is recorded, by the same measurement rule as plot area. Respondent: the plot manager, including a micro-manager where land is under joint management. Mode: face-to-face with on-plot measurement where feasible; phone follow-up acceptable for practice checklists, not for first-time area measurement. A community module for communally managed land records its area under listed practices and its managing body. The same roster carries the continued-use and CIMMYT-linkage flags KPI-I12 reads, so the two indicators are collected in one instrument, never independently.
collectionFrequency: Baseline and then annually where the monitoring survey supports it, aligned with the main cropping season, so that a hectare is read once per reporting year.
reportingFrequency: Annually; where a year is skipped, the latest measured value is carried forward with its year of measurement noted.
referencePeriod: The reporting year (the most recent complete 12-month cropping cycle prior to data collection).
baselineRequired: Yes: the share of area under listed practices at project start. Fallbacks where no prospective baseline exists: recall-based reconstruction of practice use and plot areas for the pre-intervention season, or secondary pre-period data where a national survey carried a comparable practice module for the same area. If neither is feasible: monitoring only, no change or impact claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Across projects: pool Recommended-sourced values directly; a project that used a Fallback is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, never blended silently in. Pool only projects using the same practice-list basis: KPI-OC36's numerator and KPI-I12 use one identical practice list, the closed versioned CIMMYT-wide list this pathway shares.

B: Combination method. Sum unique numerator hectares and sum denominator hectares across all reporting projects, then compute the institutional percentage as the ratio of the two sums; never average project-level percentages. Report the hectare numerator alongside the percentage.

C: Levels and operations. A share of area is recomputed at every level as a ratio of two hectare sums, never averaged from the levels beneath it. The unit is the physical hectare, so the numerator is de-duplicated before it is divided. At Farm / Plot, the plot's area and the practices on it; no share is reported there. At project level and at Regional / Aggregated, unique qualifying hectares over total farming-system hectares, within the pooling domain of Block A and on one practice-list basis. Also report: the hectare numerator alongside the percentage, the denominator's own basis, the practice-list version, and the area-estimation method, since a GPS-measured and a self-reported hectare are not the same measurement.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: no. This share does not combine arithmetically with the pathway's outputs or with KPI-I12; levels connect through the Theory of Change as narrative. Named overlap: KPI-I12's hectares are read from the same plot roster and, on individually managed land, are a subset of OC36's numerator hectares, since KPI-I12 additionally requires a link to CIMMYT's work and continued use; in any joint report KPI-I12's figure must not exceed OC36's numerator on that shared land, and the two must never be summed, which would double-count the same hectares at two levels.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: where two projects' intervention areas overlap, the overlap area is assigned to one project's sampling frame by mapped boundary before summing; overlapping projects whose overlap area cannot be assigned to one sampling frame are reported side by side and not pooled. Named overlap outside this pathway: the same hectare can qualify for KPI-OC33 and KPI-I10, which read the same land as a sustainability rather than an adaptation question. Those totals are never added to this one, and any joint area report states which indicator it is built from.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Qualifying practices: The practice categories named in the Definition are illustrative of the one closed, versioned CIMMYT-wide list this pathway shares with KPI-O21, KPI-OC20 and KPI-I12; the version in force at the reporting date governs what qualifies and travels with the value.

Inclusion: land managed or cultivated by producers in the defined intervention areas; only listed practices applied during the reporting year, and only where the practice addresses a climate risk that is material in that agro-ecology. Being an improved practice is not sufficient. The same practice can be adaptation in one setting and ordinary good agronomy in another: water harvesting counts where water deficit is a documented climate risk for the site, and does not count where it is not. The project states, for each listed practice it reports, the local climate risk that practice addresses and the basis for calling that risk material; that statement travels with the value. Communally managed land is not recorded through household plot rosters; where a project works on it, its area under listed practices is reported beside the value, with its managing body, and enters neither term.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only: practice uptake also responds to weather shocks, prices, subsidies and extension by other actors; this value cannot attribute coverage to CIMMYT alone.

Practices and areas are largely self-reported: recall error and social-desirability bias affect practice checklists, and farmer-reported areas deviate systematically from GPS measurement; hold the area-measurement method constant across waves.

What counts as a climate-adaptation practice is context-dependent: the same practice can serve adaptation, mitigation or general agronomy, so comparability across projects and years depends on the practice list applied consistently.

The percentage is sensitive to its denominator: a change in the intervention-area boundary or producer population moves the value without any change in adoption; hold the boundary constant across waves and report boundary changes explicitly.

A rising value means more of the farming-system area is under listed practices; it does not mean the practices are well implemented or that climate risk has fallen. KPI-I05 measures the share of exposed households maintaining income through a shock, and KPI-I07 the yield advantage of CIMMYT stress-tolerant varieties under a drought or heat stress event, each as a contribution claim; the physical scale of the CIMMYT-linked part is KPI-I12.
subMetrics: None. Practice-type, land-type and country breakdowns are disaggregations, not sub-metrics. Related sheet: KPI-I12 (area of agrifood systems with enhanced climate resilience) is the impact-level companion this indicator contributes to.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Mission indicator, so roles are project-level. Data collection: project M&E team and trained enumerators. Validation: project MEAL officer, who checks the practice list applied, the area-measurement method, and that the denominator boundary matches the previous wave. Calculation: project M&E per the formula above; the CIMMYT MEAL unit pools and de-duplicates across projects. Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 6 · Resilience & climate — Reference sheet KPI-OC36

name: Number of institutions with strengthened capacity to anticipate and respond to agrifood-system crises
resultsLevel: Outcome. The counted change is in the practice of external institutions, a change in practice among partners, which is the Core's definition of an outcome. CIMMYT's own tools are the output level (KPI-O41); whether crises then cost less is the impact level (KPI-I17).
indicatorScope: Mission. The result is a change in what external institutions can do, delivered through projects, so the sheet carries the project-specific layer.
primaryObjective: PO5 Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities. Crisis-capable institutions are the countable form of the coordinated measures PO5 calls for. Contributing (contribution only): PO3, crisis capacity protects the farming populations these institutions serve; PO4, crisis-capable institutions are a property of a climate-resilient agrifood system. One primary objective only; the register lists PO5 first, and the first listed is primary by register convention.
cgiarImpactArea: Climate Adaptation & Mitigation. In-scope crises also include conflict and market disruptions, which touch Nutrition, Health & Food Security; one Impact Area is kept for aggregation, and the pathway-wide rule sets Climate Adaptation & Mitigation for every indicator here.
sdgTarget: None. Nearest relation: SDG indicator 13.1.2 (target 13.1) counts countries adopting national disaster risk reduction strategies, a country-level policy-adoption measure, not an institutional-capacity measure, so no direct correspondence is claimed (UN SDG indicator 13.1.2 metadata sheet, UN Statistics Division).
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Results Framework 2022-24, outcome category Capacity Change ("Changes in capacity of organizations resulting from CGIAR interventions"): partial match. Currency caution: the Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 names no capacity-change outcome category (CGIAR System Organization, 2025), and CGIAR's 2024 QA guidance routes results previously reported as capacity change through the policy-change parameter "capacity development of key actors in a policy process" or the other-outcome category; CGIAR-bound OC38 results follow that routing.
definition: Counts institutions with strengthened capacity to anticipate and respond to agrifood-system crises, disaggregated by the four register institution types; an institution is counted when it meets a defined capacity-strengthening threshold, set out in Eligibility criteria and missing data. Capacity is a potential visible only when used, so the count includes only institutions with verifiable changes in what they do (an early warning system issuing alerts ahead of the hazard, a crisis protocol adopted and exercised, a response plan activated within its own window during a real disruption), never institutions merely reached by training or information. Anticipation covers foresight, risk monitoring and early warning; response covers contingency planning and coordinated response.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's crisis-preparedness work (tools, early warning products, response protocols; see KPI-O41) converts into working institutional capability, the behaviour-change step Primary Objective 5 expects: the Strategy's outcomes state that "foresight on agrifood systems underpins strategic dialogue and informs policy" and that crisis responses are proactive solutions that build resilience. Serves project management and institutional and CGIAR reporting on capacity change.
projectSpecificApplication: State which institutions the project supports, in which countries, with what support package and period; definition, threshold and counting rule are unchanged. Example: a project supporting a plant health agency and two universities to run a wheat-disease surveillance system reports each institution in the year it meets the threshold.
projectSpecificRationale: State which project decision, donor requirement or national reporting need the count serves. Example: a project reports this as its donor's required institutional-capacity outcome and uses the per-institution evidence at midterm to steer remaining support.
projectTypesNotApplicable: upstream discovery science and breeding and varietal development
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI; seed systems and deployment.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science and breeding and varietal development, neither of which delivers anticipatory-action, early-warning or crisis-response capability, which is what this indicator counts.
unit: Number (count of unique institutions)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more institutions meet the capacity-strengthening threshold in the reporting year.
disaggregationRequired: Required (per register): institution type: national/government systems; research/academic; private sector; civil society. Each institution takes exactly one type. Adopted as required: capacity dimension (anticipation / response), since the two are different capabilities and a pooled count hides which one moved. An institution strengthened on both dimensions appears under each; the two dimension counts are not summed and their sum may exceed the headline.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country or region; crisis type (climatic, pest or disease, market or economic, conflict-related).
unitOfObservation: Organization. A national or government "system" (for example a cross-agency early warning system) is counted once per named member institution, not once through its lead: capacity is held by institutions, not by systems, and counting the system once would make the largest interventions look identical to the smallest. Each member institution counts only if it meets all four threshold conditions in its own right; membership of a strengthened system is not itself a capacity gain.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of unique institutions that meet the capacity-strengthening threshold (Eligibility criteria and missing data) in the reporting year. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (administrative and registry data): project M&E and capacity-development records, partner reporting, and the institution's own records (adopted protocols, early warning bulletins issued, activation records, budget or staffing decisions for crisis functions); the threshold is defined by documented practice change, which these records evidence directly. Not applicable: DS1, an external capacity assessment cannot evidence condition (4), which rests on records the institution itself keeps or issues; DS3, capacity cannot be observed from satellite or GIS data; DS4, third-party databases do not record a specific institution's capacity change or CIMMYT's contribution; DS5, crowdsourced data cannot verify it.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Name, for each counted institution, the records that evidence conditions (2) to (4).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2): a documentation-review checklist covering the four threshold conditions, applied to each supported institution.
collectionFrequency: Annual: verification evidence compiled once per year per supported institution.
reportingFrequency: Annual, aligned with institutional and CGIAR reporting cycles.
referencePeriod: The reporting year: each value counts institutions that meet the threshold in that year, on evidence verified before the value is reported.
baselineRequired: Yes, at institution level: every counted institution needs a documented capacity-gap assessment or baseline capacity statement from the start of support, because "strengthened" cannot be substantiated without the prior state; the count itself starts at zero, which is CIMMYT's own counting convention. Fallback: retrospective reconstruction from the institution's own records (organograms, prior protocols, past crisis performance). If no prior-state evidence can be assembled, the institution is monitored but not counted.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Across projects: pool the verified institution records directly. Institutions counted on a retrospectively reconstructed baseline are pooled, because the reconstruction draws on the institution's own records, the Recommended DS2 source; their number is reported under Also report.

B: Combination method. Sum of unique institutions across all reporting projects after de-duplication.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of institutions that met the capacity-strengthening threshold through that project in the reporting year. At institutional level, the de-duplicated count across projects, computed from the institution records themselves rather than by adding project figures. De-duplication is on the legal entity, so a ministry and its national research institute are two institutions and two departments of one ministry are one. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the threshold conditions in force, the number of institutions assessed but not counted, the number counted on a retrospectively reconstructed baseline, the cumulative distinct-institution figure, and, where an institution re-enters for a new and distinct capacity gain, that it is a re-entry rather than a new institution.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: no; O41, OC38 and I17 connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative, since tools delivered do not imply capacity gained, and capacity gained does not imply losses avoided.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: an institution supported by several projects counts once in the reporting year, and one supported in several years enters again only for a new and distinct capacity gain, matched by institution identity before pooling; if matching is not feasible, label the pooled count an upper estimate. Named overlap risk: KPI-O27 (service providers strengthened, Capacity, data & institutions) also counts strengthened organizations under the CGIAR Results Framework 2022-24 capacity-change category; one organization may legitimately appear in both counts for different results, so the two counts are never summed into one "organizations strengthened" figure. KPI-O40 (institutions with strengthened capacity to use CIMMYT evidence, Policy, finance & market systems) may count the same institution for a different capacity; the two counts are never summed.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: institutions of the four register types that meet, in the reporting year, the capacity-strengthening threshold, stated as CIMMYT's own convention for this indicator in four conditions: (1) CIMMYT support to that institution named in a project workplan, with budget or staff time allocated to it, aimed at crisis anticipation or response; (2) a capacity-gap assessment or baseline capacity statement of the institution's prior state (Baseline required); (3) documented evidence of changed practice or performance, being at least one of (a) an early warning system that issued alerts ahead of the hazard it monitors, (b) a crisis protocol adopted and exercised, in a simulation or a real activation, or (c) a response plan activated within the window its own protocol or trigger sets; (4) the change evidenced in a record the institution itself keeps or issues, independently of CIMMYT: a bulletin archive, an activation or after-action log, a protocol adopted by its own governing body, or a budget or staffing decision for a crisis function.

Repeated observations: an institution enters the count once, in the year it first meets the threshold, de-duplicated across projects; a later, distinct capacity gain may re-enter the count, with the cumulative distinct-institution figure reported alongside. A gain is distinct if it is in a capacity dimension, or for a crisis function (a named early-warning product, protocol or response plan), not already counted for that institution; extending a counted function to new areas, hazards of the same class or later seasons is not distinct.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only: crisis capacity is shaped by many actors (governments, FAO, WFP, other donors); the count must never be read as capacity change caused by CIMMYT alone.

The main counting risk is inflation: CGIAR's own review of its standard indicators found capacity-change reporting that in practice counted training reach, funders, or delivery partners; documented practice change is therefore a threshold condition here, not optional.

A count carries no depth or durability information: a modest procedural improvement and a fully functioning national early warning system count equally, and capacity can erode once support ends; read trends with the per-institution verification evidence.

Comparability across institution types is limited: a strengthened ministry and a strengthened civil-society organization are different results at different scales; type-level counts matter more than the headline total.

A rise means more supported institutions showed verifiable capacity gains; it does not mean crises were better anticipated or losses avoided. That claim belongs to KPI-I17, read through the pathway's results chain.
subMetrics: None. The indicator is a single verified count; institution type is a disaggregation, not a sub-metric. Neighbouring sheets, not sub-metrics: KPI-O41 feeds this outcome and KPI-I17 sits above it.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Mission indicator, so roles are project-level. Data collection: project capacity-development lead (administrative evidence). Validation: project MEAL officer, checking the four threshold conditions and baseline statement per counted institution. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, de-duplicating across projects and years. Approval: project team lead (project count); MEAL unit lead (institutional figure). Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 6 · Resilience & climate — Reference sheet KPI-OC38

name: Percentage of smallholder households maintaining income through a climate or economic shock (resilience), as a contribution of CIMMYT support
resultsLevel: Impact
primaryObjective: PO3: Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Contributing: PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient), PO5 (Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities).
cgiarImpactArea: Climate Adaptation & Mitigation. Pathway-wide default. The outcome measured is income, which on its own would point to Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs; the pathway-wide rule sets Climate Adaptation & Mitigation for every indicator in this pathway, and the choice is made once for the pathway rather than sheet by sheet.
sdgTarget: None. The closest target is SDG 1.5 (build the resilience of the poor to climate-related extreme events and other economic, social and environmental shocks), but its official indicator 1.5.1 counts disaster deaths, missing and directly affected persons per 100,000 population: disaster losses, not income maintenance, so no direct correspondence exists.
otherFrameworks: Donor resilience frameworks build household ability-to-recover indices on a shock-exposure and severity roster; those are perception-based measures of recovery, which this indicator does not measure, so the two are not substitutes. CGIAR's standard indicators for Climate Adaptation and Mitigation count people benefiting from climate-adapted innovations or from adaptation plans, adaptation investments, and plans with evidence of implementation; none measures income held through a shock, so no exact CGIAR counterpart exists (Claus et al., 2023).
definition: The share of shock-exposed target smallholder households whose real income over the period after a qualifying climate or economic shock is at or above their income over the same calendar months one year earlier. Numerator: smallholder households maintaining income through a defined shock; denominator: all target smallholder households exposed to the shock. Underlying concept: resilience is treated here as an observed result, income held through a shock that occurred (climate: drought, flood, extreme heat; economic: a sharp input or food price rise), not as a capacity score or preparedness index; it is only observable among target households exposed to a qualifying shock in the recall window. Smallholder is defined in Annex B, and the declared threshold travels with the value. The household's smallholder status is recorded in the survey against the Annex B threshold the project declares; the smallholder population is not narrowed at the outcome or output level.
rationale: Answers whether shock-exposed smallholder households in CIMMYT intervention areas maintain their income through a drought, flood or price shock. This indicator turns that question into a recurring institutional measure for donors and for 2030 Strategy reporting.
projectSpecificApplication: State the project's target population and geography, the shock types monitored, what counts as a defined qualifying shock (for example a declared drought or a stated price-rise magnitude), and the timing of the post-shock measurement round. Do not change the numerator or denominator definition, the unit of measure, or the calculation method; if applying the indicator as defined is not feasible, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the donor commitment or results-framework line this figure reports against, and any project decision it informs (for example, a low post-shock value triggering a review of the resilience-practice package).
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose work is laboratory and controlled-environment research with no farmers
households or land in an intervention area to observe
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose work is laboratory and controlled-environment research with no farmers, households or land in an intervention area to observe.
unit: Percentage of shock-exposed target smallholder households
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of the shock-exposed smallholder households held their income through a defined shock.
disaggregationRequired: Required: sex of household head (female/male), as the register records for this indicator; shock type (climate vs economic), required because Block B reports the mix of shock types behind every pooled value.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Age of household head; specific shock (drought, flood, heat, price spike); agroecological zone; crop system.
unitOfObservation: Household
calculationSummary: Value = (shock-exposed target smallholder households that maintained income / all target smallholder households exposed to the qualifying shock) x 100, applying survey weights. Maintaining income: household income over the post-shock period, from shock onset to the post-shock measurement, deflated to pre-shock prices by the national consumer price index (in-kind income valued at pre-shock local prices), is at or above its income over the same calendar months one year earlier, which is the pre-shock reference period. No global standard sets a tolerance band for income maintenance through a shock, and none is applied here; a project that reports against a band instead reports a different quantity and its values do not pool with these. Two parameters are declared with every value, because the sheet fixes the test and not the thresholds: the qualifying-shock definition and the severity level at which a shock qualifies, taken from the project's documented shock roster; and the interval between shock onset and the post-shock measurement, which also sets the length of both income periods. Whether pre-shock income was measured by a prospective round covering the reference period or reconstructed by recall is stated with the value. Values built on different declarations are reported side by side and never pooled. Where the project holds a users-versus-non-users or counterfactual comparison, it is reported beside the headline as the users' maintained share, the comparable non-users' maintained share and their difference in percentage points, each with its exposed denominator and the design used. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1: household survey in the intervention area combining three linked modules: shock exposure and severity, using the project's documented shock roster with a severity score per shock type, the roster recorded with the value, household income (all sources, cash and in-kind), and use of the CIMMYT innovation(s), with the household's holding size recorded for the Annex B classification, sampled to include both users and comparable non-users so the comparison that strengthens the contribution claim is built into the design. Fallback DS4: national or regional panel surveys carrying shock and income modules (for example the World Bank LSMS-ISA), used only where the project cannot field its own survey; normally cannot resolve a CIMMYT target population or carry a users-versus-non-users comparison, so any fallback-sourced value is flagged and reported separately. Frame DS2, scoped to the users-versus-non-users assignment: project records identify which households use CIMMYT innovations; they supply the arm each household belongs to and never produce the value. Frame DS3, scoped to shock corroboration: satellite rainfall, drought or flood products corroborate that the climate shock the DS1 module records occurred and how severe it was, and the share of DS1-exposed households whose location they do not corroborate is reported with the value; the DS1 shock-exposure module places a household in the denominator, and DS3 measures no income and enters no pooled figure. Not applicable: DS5, household income and its attribution to a specific innovation cannot be established from crowdsourced or incidental data.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role this project used, Recommended or Fallback; if Fallback, explain briefly why primary collection was not feasible and at what resolution the value holds.
collectionInstrument: Household questionnaire with the three linked modules above (shock exposure and severity; income; innovation use), with the household's holding size recorded for the Annex B classification. Respondent: the household head or main income earner. Mode: face-to-face or phone interview, timed after the shock's main income effect has materialised.
collectionFrequency: Baseline and endline; because the indicator is only observable when a shock occurs, add a post-shock survey round when a major qualifying shock hits.
reportingFrequency: Annually. In a year with no qualifying shock the report is "no qualifying shock episode", not zero. In a year with a qualifying shock but no post-shock round, the report is "qualifying shock, not measured". The latest measured value is shown only as a labelled prior episode, with its year and shock.
referencePeriod: The 12 months prior to data collection, which is the shock recall window; household income is compared against the pre-shock reference period set in the Calculation method, which lies 12 to 24 months before data collection.
baselineRequired: Yes: income over the pre-shock reference period (Calculation method) is required for the numerator judgement. A prospective round counts where it covers that period; otherwise it is reconstructed by recall, and which was used is stated with the value. Secondary pre-period data covering the same calendar months (for example an earlier LSMS-ISA wave) or a matched retrospective users-vs-non-users comparison through the same shock are fallbacks where neither is feasible. If none is feasible: monitoring only, no change or impact claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool Recommended-sourced values directly; a project that had to use the Fallback is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, not blended silently into it.

B: Combination method. Pool at household level using survey weights: the institutional figure is the weighted percentage of shock-exposed target smallholder households maintaining income across all reporting projects. Never average project-level percentages. Pooling is legitimate only across projects whose two declared parameters (Calculation method) are the same, and the pooled figure must be reported with the mix of shock types and countries behind it, since the value is conditional on which shocks occurred.

C: Levels and operations. A share is recomputed at every level from its own numerator and denominator, never averaged from the levels beneath it. The denominator here is not the target population but the shock-exposed part of it, so the share exists only for a defined shock and window: at Household, the pre-shock and post-shock income comparison for that household; at project level, exposed households that maintained income over all exposed households, applying survey weights. Above project level the pooling is across episodes, not across households, because a value is conditional on the shock that produced it: pool only estimates built on the same declared parameters, weight by exposed households, and report episodes built on different declarations separately. Also report: the exposed denominator, the shock type and severity that defined exposure, the measurement window, and the number of households excluded at each margin, for want of a pre-shock and for want of a post-shock measurement, and the number kept in the denominator as displaced by the shock, since a value cannot be read without the shock it was measured through.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This value does not combine arithmetically with the pathway's output (farmers reached with resilience practices) or outcome (share applying them) indicators; levels connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative, not arithmetic. KPI-I05 and KPI-I07 are two impact readings of the same shock, and KPI-I12 measures land under practice whether or not a shock came. None of the three is ever reported alone as "resilience": a farm can hold its yield and still lose its income.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: count each household once; where two projects' zones overlap, the overlap is assigned to one project's sampling frame before pooling, and if that is not feasible, the overlapping projects are reported side by side and not pooled. Overlap: households counted here may also appear in KPI-I03 (Income & livelihoods); the two measure different claims (income held through a shock vs income increased) and must never be summed into one beneficiary count.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: target smallholder households exposed to at least one qualifying shock in the recall window, with income measured (or reconstructed) for both the pre-shock reference period and the post-shock period. Consumption expenditure may substitute for household income where income is too unreliable to measure, provided the substitution is declared with the value; income-based and consumption-based values are reported side by side and never pooled.

Exclusion: households not exposed to a qualifying shock; the indicator is undefined for them.

Missing data: a household missing the pre-shock income measure is excluded from the denominator, not imputed. A household missing the post-shock measure stays in the denominator as not maintaining income where the enumerator's tracking record shows it moved away or dissolved because of the shock; otherwise it is excluded and the value is reported as an upper estimate. The two margins, and the number kept as displaced by the shock, are counted and reported separately.

Repeated observations: one determination per household per reporting period; with several qualifying shocks in the window, judge once against the first qualifying shock in the window.
limitations: The value is a contribution claim with or without a comparison group. A users-versus-non-users or counterfactual comparison, where a project holds one, is recorded with the figure and strengthens the contribution claim; it never converts the value into an attribution claim, which belongs to a formal third-party impact assessment. CGIAR's own review of its standard indicators warns that extrapolating innovation-use numbers into benefit claims is misleading (Claus et al., 2023).

Household income is self-reported and noisy for smallholders (seasonal, partly in-kind, multiple sources), and the pre-shock level is often reconstructed by recall of income 12 to 24 months before the interview. Because each household is classified at a threshold, measurement error misclassifies households near it and does not average out: it pulls the share towards 50 per cent, understating a high true share and overstating a low one, and it shrinks any users-versus-non-users difference. Keep instrument and timing rules constant across waves. Households the shock displaced or dissolved are the hardest to trace at the post-shock round, so an estimate resting on those who could be found biases the maintained share upwards in the most severe years.
Values are conditional on the shocks that occurred. Compare across sites or years only where the declared parameters are the same, and treat no-shock years as not observable, not as zero.

Resistance, not recovery: the indicator records whether income was held through the shock, never how long a household took to return to its pre-shock level. Recovery time is a different quantity, measured on an episode clock rather than a reporting year, and no indicator in the register carries it; a high value is not evidence of fast recovery.

A rising value means a larger share of shock-exposed target households kept income, in real terms, at or above its pre-shock level; it does not mean incomes grew, or that CIMMYT caused the stability. The headline is the rate across all exposed target households, users and non-users together; the difference between the two arms, where held, is the figure that speaks to CIMMYT's contribution. Read alongside the pathway's adoption indicators and the income indicators for the full livelihood narrative.
subMetrics: None. Climate-shock and economic-shock values come from the same calculation and are disaggregations, not sub-metrics.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E team / enumerators. Validation: project MEAL officer. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit / impact assessment function. Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit and institutional reporting.
sourceRef: Volume 6 · Resilience & climate — Reference sheet KPI-I05

name: Yield loss avoided under climate stress among smallholders using CIMMYT stress-tolerant varieties, versus non-users
resultsLevel: Impact
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. The indicator measures the smallholder yield advantage under stress, the resilience half of PO3. Contributing: PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient), PO5 (Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities); contribution only, the value is reported against PO3.
cgiarImpactArea: Climate Adaptation & Mitigation
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator measures yield loss avoided under a climate stress event. The closest, 2.4.1 (agricultural area under productive and sustainable agriculture) and 2.3.1 (production per labour unit of small-scale producers), are not with-versus-without measures under stress, so None is recorded rather than a stretched mapping.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Results Framework: no equivalent standard indicator. This indicator contributes evidence to the Climate Adaptation and Mitigation impact indicator "number of people benefiting from climate-adapted innovations", but is not the same measure: that one counts people, this one sizes the yield advantage under stress. Donor reporting frameworks carry a yield level for targeted commodities, rather than an avoided loss under stress.
definition: Measures the yield advantage, under a drought or heat stress event, of smallholder plots planted to a CIMMYT stress-tolerant variety over comparable plots that were not. The value is that advantage as a share of the counterfactual yield, on plots exposed to the same defined event in the same season. Because users and non-users differ in land quality, wealth and management, the value must come from a with-versus-without comparison (a matched comparison group or equivalent statistical design), not a before-and-after difference or a plot's departure from its own normal yield.
rationale: Answers whether smallholder plots planted to CIMMYT's stress-tolerant varieties out-yield comparable plots when drought or heat strikes, the point of breeding for stress tolerance and the evidence donors ask for on climate adaptation. It sizes that advantage by crop, stress type and place, so seed and scaling investment can go where the advantage is largest.
projectSpecificApplication: Describe the crops, stress types, countries and seasons this project covers, which event it treats as qualifying, and which comparison group it uses. The institutional definition, unit and calculation method stay unchanged. If no credible comparison group can be built, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining the indicator.
projectSpecificRationale: State what this project uses the value for: a donor's climate-adaptation reporting requirement, a decision on which varieties to scale, or a management trigger if the measured advantage is smaller than expected.
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, which grows no farmer plots to compare; and digital agriculture and AI, which delivers advisory content rather than the stress-tolerant variety whose effect this indicator estimates.
unit: Percentage yield loss avoided: the users' yield advantage as a share of the counterfactual yield (a relative yield advantage under stress, not a fraction of the loss the comparison group took). Metric tonnes per hectare (t/ha) to two decimal places of avoided loss is reported alongside it, since a percentage on a low base can look large while amounting to little grain. The percentage is the form that enters institutional reporting; the metric tonnes per hectare figure travels with it and never replaces it.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means users of CIMMYT stress-tolerant varieties held a larger yield advantage under climate stress over the non-user comparison.
disaggregationRequired: Required: sex of the plot manager (female/male); age of the plot manager (youth/non-youth, youth defined as 15 to 30, stated once in Core §4.1; projects record date of birth or exact age so other bands, for example a donor band of 15 to 29, can be derived); stress type (drought, heat); crop and trait class (for example drought-tolerant maize, heat-tolerant wheat); stress severity class, as the national meteorological service classes the event. Stress type, crop and severity class are required because values from different stresses, crops and severity classes cannot be pooled (see Aggregation rule).
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: Variety, for seed systems and deployment and breeding and varietal development projects. Those two types deliver the stress-tolerant variety whose effect is being estimated, so which variety carried it is the cut they need.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Agroecological zone; country or district; farm size; variety generation or year of release; irrigated versus rainfed.
unitOfObservation: Plot
calculationSummary: Numerator: mean measured yield of plots planted with a CIMMYT stress-tolerant variety minus the counterfactual mean yield those same plots would have obtained without it, read from comparable non-user plots, both exposed to the same defined stress event in the same season, in metric tonnes per hectare, estimated with a with-versus-without design (randomised or matched comparison where feasible, otherwise a design correcting for selection into adoption such as propensity score matching or endogenous switching regression, with the design and its assumptions reported next to the value). Denominator: that same counterfactual mean yield, in metric tonnes per hectare. Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100; the numerator alone is the absolute avoided loss. Yield here is harvested production divided by area planted, not by area harvested: a stress event can destroy the crop on part of the planted area before harvest, so a denominator of harvested area measures only what survived and cannot see the loss this indicator estimates. Measured by crop cutting or whole-plot harvest where feasible, and farmer-reported harvest with measured area otherwise. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1 (Censuses & surveys): plot-level survey with field measurement covering users and comparable non-users, capturing yield, area planted, variety planted and exposure to the stress event. This is the only source that produces the contrast at plot level. Frame DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation), scoped to the stress event: rainfall-deficit and temperature-anomaly products at plot location, used to verify the event against the national meteorological service's threshold so exposure is not self-reported. The threshold is the national service's, never a global product's own classification. DS3 establishes which plots are eligible and never produces the yield value. Fallback DS2 (Administrative & registry data), scoped to variety identification: certified seed sales, distribution and partner trial records used to truth the variety where DNA fingerprinting was not done; a value resting on them is interim (Collection instrument) and is reported beside the pooled figure. Distribution records used only to draw the survey sample do not make a value fallback-sourced. Comparator DS4 (Secondary & international databases): published impact studies of stress-tolerant varieties, used to place the project's estimate against published estimates for the same crop and stress type; these describe the zones and seasons they were run in, not the project's, and are never a substitute for the project's evaluation, never pooled and never reported as a KPI-I07 value. Where the project cannot mount a plot-level evaluation and holds no earlier estimate of its own, the indicator is recorded as not reportable for that project and period. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): the value needs measured plot yields and a controlled comparison group, which crowdsourced observations cannot supply.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether variety identification rests on DNA fingerprinting or on the Fallback DS2; if Fallback DS2, say why DNA fingerprinting was not done. Name any Comparator DS4 study cited, with its crop, stress type and zone.
collectionInstrument: Plot yield module: crop cut sub-sample or whole-plot harvest where feasible, otherwise farmer-reported harvest weight with GPS-measured area. Variety identification module: variety, seed source and season. DNA fingerprinting is required where the estimate is entered in the pooled figure; truthing against seed records is a labelled fallback for interim reporting, and a value resting on it is reported as interim. Holding module: the plot manager's household holding size, recorded for the Annex B classification. Stress exposure module: event, dates and reported damage, reconciled against the DS3 climate data. Respondent: the plot manager. Mode: face-to-face interview with field measurement at harvest.
collectionFrequency: Event-driven, not routine: measured through an impact evaluation in a season when a qualifying stress event occurs in the project area. Multi-year programmes plan one wave triggered by a stress season, plus endline.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Between waves the latest estimate is carried forward, labelled with its season and source study, never re-dated.
referencePeriod: The cropping season in which the qualifying stress event occurred, with user and non-user yields measured for that same season.
baselineRequired: Yes, as a comparison group rather than a prior-period value: comparable non-users exposed to the same stress event are the counterfactual. Fallbacks where no comparison group was designed in at the start: a matched comparison built from observational user and non-user data, or a design correcting for selection into adoption. If no credible counterfactual can be built, the project may monitor user yields under stress but cannot report an avoided-loss claim from them.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool Recommended-sourced values directly. A value whose variety identification rests on the Fallback DS2, seed-record truthing rather than DNA fingerprinting, is interim and is reported beside the pooled figure, labelled interim, never inside it.

B: Combination method. Each value is an estimated effect from one evaluation, not a count, so aggregation combines estimates and never adds them. Pool only across studies sharing the crop, the stress type, the design, and the severity class the national meteorological service assigns the event, as a ratio of stress-affected-area-weighted means: the weighted mean avoided loss in t/ha over the weighted mean counterfactual yield, reported with the range of study percentages, the number of studies and the stress-affected area behind it. An estimate whose event carries no national severity class is reported separately. Never average raw percentages across crops, stresses, severities or designs; report non-comparable studies separately.

C: Levels and operations. This value is an estimated effect from a comparison design, not a figure at a reporting level, and it is never read off a level above or below the one it was estimated at. It is computed once per evaluation, for one crop, one stress type and one season, from the plots of users and comparable non-users exposed to the same event. Where a wider figure is wanted, estimates are combined, never added: pool only within the pooling condition of Block B, and report studies outside it separately rather than inside the pool. A lower-level view is re-estimated from that subset's own plots. Also report: with every value, the number of studies and plots behind it, the design used and whether the comparison was randomised or matched, the stress event and its severity, the counterfactual yield the percentage is a share of, and the metric tonnes per hectare alongside the percentage.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This value does not combine arithmetically with the resilience-practice access count (KPI-O21), the adoption rate (KPI-OC20) or the area with enhanced climate resilience (KPI-I12); those levels connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative, not by arithmetic. KPI-I05 and KPI-I07 are two impact readings of the same shock, and KPI-I12 measures land under practice whether or not a shock came. None of the three is ever reported alone as "resilience": a farm can hold its yield and still lose its income.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: the same plot or household can fall inside two projects' zones of influence, so de-duplicate by household and plot identifier before pooling. Overlap to name when reporting: the same yield gain can also appear in KPI-I06 (Productivity), and where this evidence supports the CGIAR indicator "number of people benefiting from climate-adapted innovations", the CIMMYT MEAL unit reports that contribution centrally and no project reports it as well.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion: smallholder plots of target crops in CIMMYT intervention areas, exposed to a stress event meeting the national meteorological service's own drought and heat thresholds for the country concerned, named with every value; where no national threshold exists, the dataset and threshold used are stated explicitly. The variety must be identified. A plot is a smallholder plot where its manager's household holding falls below the Annex B threshold the project declares, recorded in the plot survey.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only. Yield under stress also depends on soil, planting date, fertiliser, weeding and event severity, so the advantage reflects the variety as farmers managed it, not genetics alone.

The estimate is only as good as its comparison group. If users hold better land or more resources, the avoided loss is overstated; if they farm marginal plots, it is understated. The design and its assumptions belong next to every reported number.

Exposure has to be defined objectively. If exposure rests on the farmer's self-report, those who lost their harvest recall the season differently from those who did not, and the estimate inherits the bias.

Values are not comparable across crops, stresses or severities. A percentage from a severe drought in maize is a different quantity from one from a mild heat spell in wheat, and neither transfers to a season without stress.

The contrast is the users' yield advantage under stress and includes any advantage the variety also holds in a season without stress; separating stress tolerance from yield potential needs the same contrast in a non-stress season, which this indicator does not require.

A larger avoided loss means the varieties held a larger yield advantage in that population and season. It does not mean incomes rose or food security improved, or that the advantage holds in a harder year; read it with the adoption indicator (KPI-OC20) and the income-through-shock indicator (KPI-I05).
subMetrics: None. The percentage and the metric-tonnes-per-hectare forms are two expressions of the same estimated contrast, both defined in the Calculation method, and drought and heat are disaggregations of that contrast, not separately constructed metrics.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E team and enumerators, with the contracted evaluation partner for plot measurement and comparison-group sampling. Validation: project MEAL officer, with the evaluation partner confirming stress-event classification against the climate data. Calculation: CIMMYT socioeconomics or impact-assessment specialist, who estimates the contrast and reports the design, checked by the MEAL unit. Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 6 · Resilience & climate — Reference sheet KPI-I07

name: Area of agrifood systems with enhanced climate resilience
resultsLevel: Impact
primaryObjective: PO4: Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient. Contributing only: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved), PO5 (Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities).
cgiarImpactArea: Climate Adaptation & Mitigation
sdgTarget: None. No SDG indicator measures area under climate-adaptation practices directly. Closest partial correspondence: indicator 2.4.1 (proportion of agricultural area under productive and sustainable agriculture) under target 2.4, whose eleven themes include Resilience, measured by "risk mitigation mechanisms". Partial in three ways: 2.4.1 is a proportion of national agricultural land, not an absolute area; it assesses risk mitigation mechanisms at holding level, not practice use on land; and it is reported by national statistical offices, not projects.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR standard indicator "#ha under improved management": the nearest CGIAR counterpart, but placed under Environmental Health and Biodiversity rather than Climate Adaptation and Mitigation. The register's definition source also records a contribution to two CGIAR climate-adaptation impact indicators, "number of people benefiting from climate-adapted innovations" and "number of people benefiting from the implementation of adaptation plans"; that link is thematic only, since both count people while this indicator counts hectares, and the figures cannot be converted into one another.
definition: Measures the total area, in hectares, of agrifood system land in CIMMYT intervention areas on which climate-resilience practices or technologies linked to CIMMYT's work are in continued use during the reporting year. Qualifying practices are those promoted with the explicit objective of reducing exposure to climate stress or limiting its severity: stress-tolerant and shorter-duration varieties, adjusted planting calendars, soil and water conservation, crop diversification, agroforestry. Only use observed on the ground counts, never planned or projected coverage. Underlying concept: climate resilience cannot be observed directly, so area under continued use of recognised adaptation practices is the operational proxy for system-level adaptation.
rationale: Answers at what physical scale land management in CIMMYT intervention areas has shifted towards climate adaptation: the land footprint of resilience, alongside the farmer and household counts elsewhere in this pathway. Area is the unit donors and the CGIAR system use for landscape-scale claims, so the value carries CIMMYT's climate-adaptation contribution into institutional reporting and portfolio steering.
projectSpecificApplication: State the geographic scope, which hectare types it covers (crop land, cultivated pasture, rangeland, other), and the reporting years measured, and confirm the practice list is applied unchanged. Do not alter the institutional definition, unit, or calculation method; if the indicator cannot be applied as defined here, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it.
projectSpecificRationale: State the donor commitment or results-framework target this area reports against, and the project decision it informs, for example whether coverage is expanding in the districts with highest climate exposure, or whether practices taken up during the project remain in use after support ends.
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, which manages no land in an intervention area.
unit: Hectares
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more hectares carry a qualifying practice linked to CIMMYT's work in continued use.
disaggregationRequired: Required: the register records none, so both cuts are CIMMYT's own, applied on the sheet's authority: (a) hectare type, as crop land, cultivated pasture, rangeland or other, each area assigned to one type only; (b) practice or technology type, from the practice list. Sex and age are not required: the unit is land, not people, and the sex-disaggregated reach of the same work is measured by KPI-O21 and KPI-OC20.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country and sub-national unit; agroecological zone; area-estimation method (GPS or polygon measurement, or farmer report calibrated against GPS); sex and age of the plot manager where land is individually managed, and of each manager, including a micro-manager, where land is under joint management, so a jointly managed hectare appears under each of its managers and these cuts are never summed to the total.
unitOfObservation: Plot
calculationSummary: Value = the count of unique hectares on which at least one qualifying climate-resilience practice linked to CIMMYT's work was in continued use during the reporting year, applying survey weights where the area is estimated from a sample of producers. A plot enters with the area under at least one qualifying practice linked to CIMMYT's work and in continued use. KPI-OC36 reports the share of farming-system area under the same practice list from the same plot roster; this indicator's hectares are the subset of that roster's qualifying area that is linked to CIMMYT's work and in continued use, so the two reconcile as subset and total but are not the same quantity. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1: the KPI-OC36 plot-roster survey of producers in the intervention areas, which carries the plot roster, the checklist of qualifying practices in use, the CIMMYT-linkage and continued-use flags per practice, and plot area (GPS or geo-referenced polygon measurement preferred; farmer-reported area only if calibrated against GPS on a subsample), with sample weights applied before the total is estimated. Fallback DS2: project M&E records, partner reports and farm records, acceptable only to establish practice use, CIMMYT linkage or continued use on plots in the KPI-OC36 plot roster, with documented assumptions re-validated annually against spot surveys; area reported outside the roster, including area converted from input sales, enters no value, and without a plot roster the indicator is not measured. Fallback DS3: geospatial and Earth observation mapping, only to establish use of a practice with a visible signature (agroforestry, land cover change, irrigated area) on plots in the KPI-OC36 plot roster, and only when calibrated against ground observation; it cannot detect variety choice, planting date or most soil practices, so it never covers the full list alone. Not applicable DS4: national statistics and international databases do not record practice use at plot level or identify land linked to CIMMYT's work. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced observation cannot establish measured hectares to the precision an area claim requires.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role was used, Recommended or Fallback, and which fallback. If a Fallback, state which of practice use, CIMMYT linkage or continued use it established on roster plots, and record the assumptions the estimate rests on (for example, imagery classification accuracy).
collectionInstrument: Plot-level module within a producer survey (DS1): plot roster with a persistent plot identifier, checklist of qualifying practices in use in the reporting year carrying, for each practice on each plot, the continued-use and CIMMYT-linkage flags and the year its use began on the plot, and plot area (GPS or geo-referenced polygon measurement preferred; farmer-reported area only if calibrated against GPS on a subsample). Where a qualifying practice covers only part of a plot, the area under it is recorded, by the same measurement rule as plot area. Respondent: the plot manager, including a micro-manager where land is under joint management. Mode: face-to-face interview with on-plot measurement. The DS2 and DS3 fallbacks replace only the practice-use, CIMMYT-linkage or continued-use flag they establish; the plot roster and plot area are still taken with this module.
collectionFrequency: Annually where a monitoring survey or partner reporting cycle supports it; at minimum baseline and endline, with the year of measurement carried on every value.
reportingFrequency: Annually. The value is a snapshot of one year's coverage, not a running total: annual values must not be added across years into a life-of-project area, because the same hectares recur.
referencePeriod: The reporting year (12 months) in which the qualifying practices were in use. A value measured before one full production season has elapsed since support ended is reported as interim, labelled as such, with the number of seasons elapsed stated, as on KPI-OC20.
baselineRequired: No. Hectares linked to CIMMYT's work are zero before that work began; the area under qualifying practices before it is KPI-OC36's baseline, read from the same roster.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Across projects: pool hectares from projects using the Recommended survey source directly; a Fallback-sourced project is shown alongside the pooled figure with a note on its estimation basis, not blended into it. A value reported as interim (Reference period) is shown beside the institutional figure with its seasons elapsed and is never summed into it.

B: Combination method. Sum hectares into one institutional figure under a unique-area rule: a physical hectare counts once per reporting year across the institution. Never sum practice-type disaggregates to a total.

C: Levels and operations. Hectares sum at project, country, regional and institutional level only after spatial de-duplication at each one. At Farm / Plot, the measured area under at least one qualifying practice linked to CIMMYT's work and in continued use. At project level, the sum of those areas de-duplicated on plot identity. At institutional level, the same sum across projects, with overlapping footprints resolved per Block E. Practice-type disaggregates are never summed to the total, since one hectare can carry several. Also report: the practice-list version, the area-estimation method, and the share of area whose de-duplication could not be verified.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: no. This value does not combine arithmetically with KPI-O21 or KPI-OC20 (which count farmers) or with KPI-OC36 (a share read from the same plot roster whose numerator contains these hectares on individually managed land, so adding them counts the same land twice); the levels connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative, not arithmetically. KPI-I05 and KPI-I07 are two impact readings of the same shock, and KPI-I12 measures land under practice whether or not a shock came. None of the three is ever reported alone as "resilience": a farm can hold its yield and still lose its income.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: overlapping project footprints are resolved before summation by assigning the overlap area to one project's sampling frame, on georeferenced boundaries or a shared plot registry; overlapping projects whose overlap area cannot be assigned to one sampling frame are reported side by side and not pooled.
