Named overlap: KPI-I10 (hectares under improved, sustainable and climate-resilient management) can legitimately cover the same hectare, since an adaptation practice is often also a sustainable land management practice. The two must never be added, and any institutional area total must state which indicator it is built from.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Qualifying practices: the practices named in the Definition are illustrative of the one closed, versioned CIMMYT-wide list this pathway shares with KPI-O21, KPI-OC20 and KPI-OC36; the version in force at the reporting date governs what qualifies and travels with the value.

Inclusions: production land only, being land managed by farmers where the practice is applied, including plots cultivated by lead farmers and their own demonstration plots; communally managed land, rangeland included, and land a producer group farms as a group are reported beside the value, with the body that manages them, and are not summed into it. A practice qualifies only where it addresses a climate risk that is material in that agro-ecology, which is the same test KPI-OC36 applies to the same land; being an improved practice is not sufficient, and the local climate risk the practice addresses is stated with the value. Linked to CIMMYT's work: the qualifying practice is one contained in a package that a person who manages the plot accessed under KPI-O21, in the reporting year or an earlier one, and it was not already in use on the plot before that access. Continued use: KPI-OC20's test, a practice kept on the plot for one full production season after support ends.

Repeated observations: a physical hectare counts once per reporting year, whatever the number of qualifying practices it carries and whatever the number of cropping cycles it takes; the same hectare may appear under several practice-type disaggregates, so those never sum to the total. Double-cropped land is counted once, because the unit is the physical hectare in the reporting year rather than the cultivation cycle.
limitations: Proxy measure, contribution claim only. Area under adaptation practices signals that a system is better prepared, not that it is more resilient; whether farms withstand a shock is tested by KPI-I05 and KPI-I07. Land management also responds to prices, weather, policy and other programmes, so CIMMYT is one contributor among several.

No depth threshold. A hectare with one modest practice counts the same as a hectare under a full adaptation package, so a large total can hide shallow change. CGIAR's own review of its equivalent standard indicator made this criticism, asking for a definition of what counts as improved management; the practice list is the control for it, and works only if applied unchanged.

Measurement error runs in both directions for self-reported plot areas and for the self-reported CIMMYT-linkage and practice-start items, and mostly upward for overlapping footprints that are not de-duplicated: self-reported plot areas are imprecise, satellite classification misreads mixed smallholder landscapes, and overlapping project footprints double-count land unless de-duplicated geographically.
Comparability is conditional: values compare across projects and years only where the practice list is centrally defined and versioned.

A rise means qualifying practices covered more land in that year. It does not mean climate risk fell, does not mean the same hectares stay covered next year, and cannot be accumulated across years. Read with KPI-OC36 for how much of the farming system that represents. KPI-I07 estimates the yield advantage of CIMMYT stress-tolerant varieties under a drought or heat stress event, one practice category of the list, and tests none of the others.
subMetrics: None. The hectare-type and practice-type breakdowns are disaggregations of one measured area, not separately calculated sub-metrics. Related sheets: KPI-OC36 (the share of farming-system area under the same practice list, whose numerator contains this indicator's hectares on individually managed land) and KPI-I10 (overlapping area indicator in the Environmental sustainability pathway), both handled in the aggregation rule.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E team and enumerators, with the geospatial unit where an Earth observation source is used. Validation: project MEAL officer, including the de-duplication check against neighbouring project footprints. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, per the calculation method above. Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit, which reports the institutional total.
sourceRef: Volume 6 · Resilience & climate — Reference sheet KPI-I12

name: Reduction in food-security losses during agrifood-system disruptions in supported systems
resultsLevel: Impact (a change in the food-security condition of external populations during shocks, the longer-term population-level change the pathway's outcomes contribute to)
primaryObjective: PO5: Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved), PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Climate Adaptation & Mitigation, the pathway default. The measured variable is food security and in-scope disruptions include conflict and market shocks as well as climate, so the indicator is filed under one Impact Area and the disruption type travels with the value.
sdgTarget: None. No SDG indicator measures avoided food-security losses during disruptions. Nearest references: SDG indicator 2.1.2 (prevalence of moderate or severe food insecurity, FIES) supplies the underlying food-security metric; SDG target 1.5 (build the resilience of the poor and reduce their exposure and vulnerability to climate-related extreme events and other shocks) describes the result this indicator evidences, but its indicator 1.5.2 measures direct economic loss from disasters, not food security.
otherFrameworks: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC): the crisis-severity framework behind one of the declared triggers. CGIAR's standard indicators for Climate Adaptation and Mitigation count people benefiting from climate-adapted innovations, among others, and none measures food-security losses avoided.
definition: Measures how much less food security deteriorates during an agrifood-system disruption (drought, flood, pest or disease outbreak, market or price shock, conflict-related supply disruption) in systems supported by CIMMYT than in comparable systems without that support. A food-security loss is the increase in the prevalence of moderate or severe food insecurity, measured with the FAO Food Insecurity Experience Scale (FIES, the metric of KPI-I02, Nutrition & food security), between the pre-disruption and the disruption period. The reported value is the avoided loss: the difference, in percentage points, between the loss in comparable non-supported systems and the loss in supported systems during the same episode. Underlying concept: resilience is only observable when tested, so the indicator compares food-security losses in supported and comparable systems during a real shock. A supported system is an agrifood system (country, sub-national region, or value chain) where CIMMYT crisis-anticipation or response work was active before the disruption.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT-supported agrifood systems lose less food security during a crisis than comparable systems: the end result of the chain in which anticipatory tools are delivered (KPI-O41) and institutions build the capacity to use them (KPI-OC38). The pathway's other indicators show that resilience is being built; this one tests whether it reduced losses when a disruption occurred, the evidence institutional reporting, donors, and the case for anticipation over emergency response all need.
projectSpecificApplication: Name the supported system(s) this project claims, the disruption episode(s) measured, the comparison systems, and the timing of the pre-disruption and disruption-period measurements. Do not alter the institutional definition, unit of measure, or calculation method; if applying the indicator as defined is not feasible in this project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the donor requirement or crisis-window reporting commitment this indicator serves in this project, and any project-level decision it informs (for example, whether a measured food-security loss during a shock triggers a review of the project's response components).
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose unit of delivery is a variety rather than a supported system with a measurable disruption episode
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science; and breeding and varietal development, whose unit of delivery is a variety rather than a supported system with a measurable disruption episode.
unit: Percentage points of moderate-or-severe food-insecurity prevalence avoided during a disruption episode
directionOfChange: Increase, the quantity itself being a reduction. A rising value means food insecurity rose less, or fell more, in the supported systems than in the comparison systems during the disruption, so a larger value is a larger loss averted. It is a difference against a comparison, so it moves with the comparison as much as with the supported system.
disaggregationRequired: Required: disruption type (climate extreme; pest or disease outbreak; market, trade or price shock; conflict-related); food-insecurity severity level (moderate or severe; severe).
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so no cut is required by project type; the cuts above apply to every type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Gendered household type; sex of household head; country or supported system; rural/urban; agroecological zone.
unitOfObservation: Household
calculationSummary: Built on the KPI-I02 prevalence, computed for each of the two populations in each of the two periods exactly as KPI-I02's reference sheet specifies, its eligibility and missing-data rules included, all four on one scale equated to the FAO global reference scale. The episode value is a difference in differences: (prevalence change from the pre-disruption to the disruption period in comparable non-supported systems) minus (the prevalence change over the same periods in supported systems). A positive value is the food-security loss avoided in supported systems, in percentage points. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1: household surveys carrying the 8-item FIES module plus a shock-exposure module, fielded in supported and comparison systems before and during the disruption. The only source that can produce a household-level avoided-loss estimate for a defined support boundary. Frame DS2, scoped to the supported-system boundary: administrative records document where support was active before the disruption, which is what places a system in the supported or the comparison arm; they measure no household's food-security status and enter no pooled figure. Frame DS3, scoped to the shock-exposure measure: satellite products characterise the severity and footprint of a climate shock; they measure no food security. Not applicable DS4 for the value: IPC and Cadre Harmonisé phase populations measure a different construct on a coarser scale and resolve no sub-national support boundary; where a crisis-window FIES survey cannot be fielded, the indicator is not measured for that episode. A secondary FIES round serves only as the Baseline fallback. Not applicable: DS5, FIES measures an experienced condition reported by sampled respondents, and crowdsourced data lacks the sampling frame a prevalence estimate requires.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State the survey rounds used and where each was fielded.
collectionInstrument: 8-item FIES experience module (FAO), as specified in the KPI-I02 reference sheet, administered with a shock-exposure module enumerating the shock and stressor types on the project's documented roster, each with its severity score. Respondent: the adult responsible for food preparation, or a randomly selected adult household member. Mode: face-to-face or phone interview, the same in both arms in each period and held constant across periods where feasible; where the disruption round must be by phone after a face-to-face pre-disruption round, the change is reported with the value and the estimate is labelled as resting on an equal mode effect in both arms.
collectionFrequency: Event-driven. A pre-disruption round of the same instrument must exist in both arms, fielded so that its 12-month recall window contains no month of the declared episode; KPI-I02 samples households in CIMMYT intervention areas only, so a project reporting this indicator fields the same module in its named comparison systems, or uses the Baseline fallback for that arm; the disruption-period measurement is fielded during or immediately after each qualifying disruption episode. There is no fixed calendar cycle.
reportingFrequency: Annually. An episode is reported in the year its estimate is completed, labelled with the year of the disruption; a year with a qualifying disruption whose estimate is not complete reports it as pending. A year with neither a qualifying disruption nor a completed estimate reports "no qualifying disruption episode" rather than a value.
referencePeriod: The disruption episode: the 12-month FIES recall window covering the disruption, compared against the most recent pre-disruption round of the same populations whose recall window contains no month of the episode (Collection frequency).
baselineRequired: Yes, and it is binding: without a pre-disruption measurement of the same populations, no loss (and therefore no avoided loss) can be computed. Fallback: a secondary pre-period round of the same instrument covering the same populations, on the same scale. If none is feasible: monitoring only, no avoided-loss or impact claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: episode estimates are not pooled, within a project or across projects.

B: Combination method. Not aggregated. The avoided loss is estimated separately for each disruption episode and supported system, and each episode estimate is reported with its disruption type, trigger, affected population, comparison systems and confidence interval; episode estimates are never averaged or summed, because shocks, periods, and comparison groups differ.

C: Levels and operations. This value is an avoided-loss estimate for one disruption episode in one supported system, and it inherits its metric from KPI-I02: each of the four prevalences it differences is a Rasch-model estimate calibrated to the FAO global reference scale, so all four must be computed on the same equated scale before they are subtracted, and a difference of prevalences from unequated scales is not an avoided loss. There is no household-level value: the unit is the episode. At institutional level, the episode estimates of the cycle, reported side by side, each with the context under Also report. Episode estimates are never summed or averaged. Also report: the number of episodes, the total affected population, the disruption type of each, the comparison systems used, the confidence interval, since severe food insecurity is a low-prevalence event and a difference of two wide intervals is wider still; the excluded share in each arm and period; the fielding dates of the four rounds and the onset date; and the shock-exposure measure that every estimate carries, being, for each arm and period, the share of households reporting each roster shock and the mean severity score, so a small loss caused by a mild shock is not read as resilience.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. KPI-O41 (tools delivered) and KPI-OC38 (capacity strengthened) connect to this indicator through the Theory of Change as a narrative, not arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: where two projects claim overlapping supported systems in the same episode, the episode counts once in the number of episodes; one estimate is computed from the combined sample where both projects surveyed the same periods on the same instrument, and otherwise both estimates are reported under the one episode, labelled as estimates of it; the affected population and households are counted once (de-duplicate by household ID or assign each zone to one project); if de-duplication is not feasible, report the affected population as an upper estimate. Named overlap with another register indicator: KPI-I02 (FIES prevalence) can be computed from the same survey rounds, but the two report different constructs (a prevalence level versus an avoided change) and are never added together.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: households in a CIMMYT-supported food system that was exposed to the episode, and households in comparison non-supported systems exposed to the same episode, surveyed on the same instrument in the same pre-disruption and disruption periods. Both arms are in scope whether or not any member took part in a CIMMYT activity, since the claim is about the system rather than about participants.

Exclusion: only qualifying disruption episodes are measured, and the project declares with the value which trigger it applied: a declared national emergency, a deterioration of one IPC phase or more, or a defined production or price shock. An IPC phase deterioration qualifies an episode only where it is observed across the area containing both arms, never in either arm alone. No institutional trigger threshold is set, so episodes qualified under different triggers are reported side by side and are not pooled. Comparison systems are named in the project's MEAL plan before the disruption episode begins; an episode whose comparison was chosen after onset is reported as monitoring only, with no avoided-loss claim. An episode where either arm's pre-disruption recall window contains a month of the episode is reported as monitoring only. Where no credible comparison system exists, the pre/post change in the supported system alone may be reported, labelled monitoring only, with no avoided-loss claim.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim at best, and only with a credible comparison: food-security outcomes during a crisis also respond to humanitarian assistance, government action, markets, and the severity profile of the shock itself; CIMMYT support is one factor among many.

Disruptions rarely hit supported and non-supported systems with identical severity, so raw comparisons confound support with exposure; the shock-exposure measure reported with the value shows how far exposure differed and does not remove this bias. The difference in differences also assumes that without support food insecurity would have changed by the same amount in both arms, which one pre-disruption round cannot test, and supported systems were chosen for support rather than assigned.

Measurement during an active crisis is error-prone: sampling frames break down, phone surveys under-cover the most affected households, and households displaced out of the frame between rounds leave the disruption-period estimate resting on those who stayed, which biases the prevalence downwards in the most severe episodes; the 12-month FIES recall window can also blur pre-crisis and crisis experiences depending on survey timing.

Values are not comparable across disruption types or episodes: a 5 percentage-point avoided loss in a severe drought and in a mild price shock are different achievements, so episode context must always be reported alongside the value.

A small measured loss in a supported system does not by itself mean the support worked (the shock may have been mild locally), and a large loss does not mean it failed (the shock may have been extreme). Read together with the shock-exposure measure and the pathway's capacity indicator (KPI-OC38). A larger avoided loss means the supported system withstood the disruption better than comparable systems without support; it does not mean food security improved.
subMetrics: None as separately calculated metrics. The underlying food-insecurity prevalence is KPI-I02 (prevalence of moderate-or-severe food insecurity, FIES); see its own reference sheet for the full measurement specification. This sheet adds the episode framing, the comparison logic, and the shock-exposure measure on top of that metric.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E team / enumerators (with crisis-window fielding capacity). Validation: project MEAL officer. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (per the Calculation method above). Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 6 · Resilience & climate — Reference sheet KPI-I17

name: Yield of target crops in CIMMYT intervention areas
resultsLevel: Output. The CIMMYT MEAL Framework defines outcomes as changes in behaviour, systems, practice, capacity, policy or performance among beneficiaries and partners (Section 2.3). A measured productivity level is a state, not a change, so it cannot sit at outcome level regardless of measurement precision. The Framework places delivery and trial results at output level and describes them as "establishing the foundation for outcome-level evidence" (Section 2.2), which is what this indicator supplies to KPI-OC22.
primaryObjective: PO3. Contributing: PO2, PO4.
cgiarImpactArea: Nutrition, Health & Food Security
sdgTarget: Target 2.3
otherFrameworks: None
definition: Yield is the grain harvested from a defined crop-cut sub-plot area, scaled to the plot's harvested area (CIMMYT, 2013). Pooled figures are reported per hectare of assessment area, which is CIMMYT's own convention and is stated in the aggregation rule. The quantity reported is dry yield, obtained by deducting moisture determined from an oven-dried subsample, and re-expressible at any stated moisture percentage.
rationale: Provides the yield achieved in CIMMYT intervention areas at each level measured, and is the base for the yield-change outcome (KPI-OC22) and the productivity impact (KPI-I06). Trial / Station values represent attainable yield under researcher management; Farm / Plot values represent realised yield under farmer management.
projectSpecificApplication:
How this project applies the institutional indicator: the crop, the geography, the period, and the measurement levels observed. Scope only; the unit, measurement basis and calculation method are unchanged.

Farm / Plot: "Yield of maize in the Central Rift Valley under CIMMYT intervention, seasons 2023 to 2025, at Farm / Plot level."

Trial / Station: "Yield of bread wheat entries in an IWIN elite spring wheat yield trial nursery at Ciudad Obregón, 2024/25 cycle, at Trial / Station level."
projectSpecificRationale: States the project decision or funder commitment this figure serves. Example: an agronomy project reports it against a contracted yield gain for a named practice, and uses it to decide whether the practice is carried into the next season.
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science.
unit: Metric tonnes per hectare (t/ha), reported to two decimal places: dry yield, or yield re-expressed at a stated moisture percentage recorded with the value; pooled figures are computed on dry yield. The calculation method below produces kilograms per hectare, which is the unit the CIMMYT yield guide it follows works in; divide by 1,000 for the reported value. Where a value would round to 0.00 t/ha it is reported in kg/ha instead, with the unit labelled.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more grain is harvested per unit of land from the target crop. Values are comparable only on the same moisture basis, which is reported with each value.
disaggregationRequired: Measurement level; crop; irrigation regime (rainfed / irrigated); cropping system (sole crop or intercrop); smallholder status of the holding, as Annex B defines it. The last is required because this indicator measures all producers in the intervention area while the impact indicator it feeds, KPI-I06, counts smallholders only: without the attribute recorded on the plot record, that narrowing cannot happen at any level and the impact figure is not producible. The threshold applied travels with the value.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: Variety, for seed systems and deployment ² and breeding and varietal development ⁴ projects. Local is a valid value where the material is an unidentified landrace.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Sex of plot manager, per Doss & Kieran (2014); age band of the plot manager; farm size class, with the bands stated, for example under 1 ha, 1 to 2 ha and 2 to 5 ha, or the national classification where one is in use; agroecological zone, with the classification stated; variety; cropping season, where the national calendar defines more than one and the season is recorded under Reference period.
unitOfObservation:
Report every level the project measures; measuring all four is not required.

Regional / Aggregated: the reporting area, a measurement level used where CIMMYT measures none of the levels above and the figure is supplied already aggregated, as in seed systems projects receiving it through seed companies or digital projects through ag-tech partners. Total production and total area as supplied, on the area concept the partner used, recorded with the value, with the supplying partner, the method by which they collected it, and the population the figure represents recorded alongside.
calculationSummary:
Yield is a function of the amount harvested and the area it was harvested from. The four steps below follow the CIMMYT yield-and-yield-components guide (CIMMYT, 2013), which requires all weights to be recorded in grams and all areas in square metres; the factor of 10 in the third step converts to kilograms per hectare only when those units are used. They apply at the two levels where a harvest is taken, Trial / Station and Farm / Plot.

Three areas are distinguished and never substituted for one another. The crop-cut sub-plot area, in square metres, is the ground the yield is measured on. The harvested area, in hectares, is the part of the plot actually harvested, and it is the reference for that plot's measured yield: not the area planted and not the area held. The assessment area, in hectares, is the denominator of every pooled figure and is defined in the aggregation rule. The full plot area is the whole area of the plot as held, harvested or not; it is recorded so the harvested area can be derived from it, and it is never the denominator of a pooled figure.

First, determine the crop-cut sub-plot area. Trial / Station: net plot, border rows discarded. Farm / Plot: randomly positioned crop-cut sub-plots (Kosmowski et al., 2021), or whole-plot harvest where the plot is small enough. In both cases the area is dimensioned to the planting geometry rather than to a fixed quadrat, and is scaled up where the plot is large or within-plot variability is high. A crop-cut sub-plot is never less than 1 m², and it is placed blind or by a person independent of the project (Sapkota et al., 2016). For a crop with staggered maturity the sub-plot, or the plot under whole-plot harvest, is harvested at every pick and the picks summed. The guide gives a worked example of three rectangles of 3 m by at least one bed width, or half the sowing-machine width for flat planting, and presents it there as an example rather than a fixed rule (CIMMYT, 2013).

Second, determine the moisture content of the harvested grain, from an oven-dried subsample of about 200 g at 75 °C for 48 h or to constant weight (CIMMYT, 2013). The guide's text gives 48 h or to constant weight for the moisture subsample and 24 h for the 200-grain kernel-weight sample; its figures label both 24 h, and constant weight governs. Oven drying to constant weight is the method of record. A calibrated grain moisture meter, the method CIMMYT's own on-farm platform uses (Gardeazábal-Monsalve et al., 2025), is an accepted method, recorded as meter with the instrument and its calibration basis, its documented error against oven drying being the quality rating. With that error recorded, a meter value enters a pooled figure as a method-of-record value; without it, the value is an undocumented meter value whose bias direction is unknown, so it is reported separately and never enters a pooled figure. Air and sun drying are fallback methods, admitted where neither an oven nor a meter is available, and are recorded as fallback with the value. The guide permits oven, air and sun drying, and the methods do not reach the same residual moisture: a fallback-dried sample retains more water than an oven-dried one, so its moisture is understated and its dry yield overstated.

The subsample's fresh weight is taken at the same time as the total grain weight, since the moisture it gives is deducted from that weight.

Third, calculate the dry yield. This is the base quantity for this indicator; every other moisture basis is derived from it.

Fourth, where the value is reported at a stated moisture percentage, re-express it, and record that percentage with the value.

where m is the moisture percentage the value is reported at.

Conventions in use. The guide works its example at 12 % (CIMMYT, 2013). On CIMMYT's Mexico platform, values are adjusted to 14 % for maize and 12 % for other crops, the common practice in that country (Gardeazábal-Monsalve et al., 2025). This indicator fixes no convention: dry yield is the base quantity and any convention is reached from it by the formula above. Record which convention the value is reported at.
dataSource:
Trial / Station: Recommended DS1: the project's own replicated trial harvest records, or a CIMMYT trial-network nursery.

Farm / Plot: Recommended DS1 for yield: crop cuts or whole-plot harvest on a representative sample of target producers' plots, sampled randomly or stratified from the project's target-farmer list (CIMMYT, 2013; Kosmowski et al., 2021).

Fallback DS1 for yield: a validated survey or recall instrument, admitted only where the instrument is a published validated module, one whose questionnaire and documentation are citable and whose error against direct measurement has been measured in a documented study, that error is reported as the quality rating, and a published method supports the aggregation. Recall values are reported separately and are not pooled with measured ones.

Recommended DS1 for area: the plot measured on the ground or by a walked polygon.

Recommended DS3 for area: the boundary of the identified plot delineated on satellite imagery, as in CIMMYT practice (Gardeazábal-Monsalve et al., 2025).

Fallback DS1 for area: the producer's statement of the plot, harvested or failed area; a harvested fraction or failed area stated by the producer rather than observed at the harvest visit is a stated area. A value built on a stated area is reported beside the pooled figure with a note naming the stated area, and never pooled.

Household: Derived from the household's Farm / Plot records. Frame DS2: the project's farmer register supplies the plot-to-producer link.

Fallback DS1: the household's own report of production and area, under the fallback conditions above, reported separately and never pooled with measured records.

Project area and above: Recommended DS1, aggregated: where the project measures plots itself, the value is computed from its own plot records through the aggregation levels in Aggregation rule, not obtained from a separate source. Trial / Station and Farm / Plot records may both enter on the area each represents.

Regional / Aggregated, partner-supplied: Fallback DS1, partner-aggregated: where CIMMYT measures none of the levels above, the figure the supplying partner aggregated from its own records, admitted with the partner, its collection method and the population the figure represents recorded alongside, as Unit of observation requires, and never pooled with project-measured records.

Comparator DS4: the FAOSTAT national yield series, Production: Crops and livestock products (QCL) (FAO, 2025), cited with its release date, to place the direction of the CIMMYT figure against the national one, never a substitute for it and never pooled with it.

Not applicable: DS2 for the yield value itself: delivery and registration records capture what was distributed, not what was harvested.

DS3 for the yield value: satellite yield estimation is not defensible standalone at smallholder plot scale.

DS5: crowdsourced figures cannot satisfy the instrument and documented-error conditions above.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Per level measured: the source role used, the sampling design, the achieved sample size, and the data quality rating, which is the documented error of the instrument used. Where Fallback DS1 for yield or the household's own report was used, name the validated module and state why direct measurement was not feasible. State whether comparison pairs are held, and whether plot areas come from polygons, satellite delineation or producer statement.
collectionInstrument:
Trial / Station: the trial field book, recording plot dimensions, net harvested area, harvested weight, moisture and the drying method used, design and replicate. IWIN publishes a blank field book with each nursery, usable directly or adapted (Global Wheat Program et al., 2023).

Farm / Plot: a crop-cut module in the agronomic survey, recording sub-plot dimensions, number and placement rule, harvested weight, moisture and the drying method used, full plot area, and the fraction of the plot area actually harvested. Without that fraction the harvested area cannot be derived and the assessment area cannot be summed, so it is a required field rather than a refinement. Establishment status is recorded on the same record, and the established-but-failed area is recorded directly, in hectares or as a fraction of the plot area, with its cause from the Case (a) list; an unharvested remainder not so recorded is neither harvested nor failed and enters no sum, and harvested area, established-but-failed area and that remainder sum to the full plot area. Where the project runs side-by-side comparisons, the plots of one comparison carry a shared comparison-pair identifier and a comparison role, the plot whose yield is reported or the untreated comparison plot, as optional project-specific fields; that is what keeps the comparison plot out of the pooled figure under Block D and lets the difference be reported where a project is contracted to. Where agronomic management data are collected on a plot, a plot polygon is recommended: it fixes the plot area, which is the denominator of every pooled figure, and gives the agronomic record a spatial reference that can be checked against the ground it describes; a project without a measured area reports on the producer-stated area, as the Fallback in Data source. Where both a measured area, on the ground, by polygon or by delineation, and a producer-stated area exist, the measured area is the plot area and the producer statement is retained beside it.

Fallback, where direct measurement was not feasible: the published validated survey or recall module named in Data source, administered as published. Its documented error against direct measurement is recorded as the quality rating for every value it produces, and those values are held so they can be reported separately from measured ones.

Recorded with every value, whatever the instrument. The moisture method, recorded as method of record (oven to constant weight), as meter with its documented error (with the instrument and its calibration basis), as meter without a documented error, or as fallback (air or sun), since the methods do not reach the same residual moisture and the aggregation rule gates on that distinction. The method that produced the plot area, whether measured on the ground, delineated from satellite imagery or stated by the producer, since these carry different and, for producer-stated area, systematic error. The quality rating, being the documented error of the instrument used.

Retain harvested weight, the moisture subsample's fresh and dry weights, crop-cut sub-plot area and harvested area as separate values, not only their ratios. Every record carries a persistent plot identifier, and a persistent farmer identifier where the project operates a farmer register, which is what makes the Household level and KPI-I06 reportable.
collectionFrequency: At harvest, each season for which a value is reported. A project intending to report KPI-OC22 measures in every season of that indicator's window, because it needs at least two measured seasons for the change, three for a change released without the short-series flag, and four for stability. A season missed in a four-season window still leaves three, so the change stays reportable with the gap stated while stability is withheld; a season missed in a three-season window leaves the change reportable but released flagged as a short series, and below two measured seasons KPI-OC22 is unreportable.
referencePeriod: The cropping season, assigned to the reporting year in which its harvest falls. Where the national cropping calendar defines more than one season a year, the season is recorded with the value, named on the national convention in use, Mexico's Primavera-Verano and Otoño-Invierno for example. Seasonal classifications are national and are not harmonised across countries, so the toolbox requires the label and the naming convention rather than a global scheme. The label is what makes the same-season rule on KPI-OC22 and KPI-I06 operable: a comparison over time cannot be held within one season unless the season is on the record. One reported value covers one season. A figure that spans the year's seasons is an annual figure, reported under its own reference period, labelled as one with the seasons it pools named, and never presented as a season value.
baselineRequired: No. This indicator reports a level; KPI-OC22 computes change and carries the baseline requirement
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One crop, one irrigation regime, one cropping system, sole crop or intercrop with the companion crop declared, on a dry basis. Levels widen the set of plots; they never widen the domain. Where a reporting level spans several domains the figures are reported side by side, never summed. No combined figure exists across crops, irrigation regimes or cropping systems.

Weight: hectares of assessment area, so a larger plot carries proportionally more of the mean. Dividing instead by the number of plots would weight plots of different sizes equally.

B: Combination method: ratio of sums.

The assessment area, not the full plot area, is the denominator of every pooled figure. Nothing is pooled below Household, where the value is per hectare of the plot's harvested area. A yield measured per harvested area and then multiplied by the full plot area would credit the plot with production from ground it did not harvest, overstating the pooled mean by the abandoned fraction and doing so worst in bad seasons. Established-but-failed area enters the denominator carrying zero production, so a failed plot pulls the mean down rather than leaving it (the ratio estimator of FAO (2018), Handbook on crop statistics, section 3.2.8; van Bussel et al. (2015) is the precedent for area weighting of yield). The sums run on dry yield, so values reported at different moisture conventions combine without conversion. The estimator is invariant to staging, so recompute from plot records; never average means. Trial / Station is the exception and combines model-based, as below.

C: Levels and operations.

D: Never pooled. Different crops; different irrigation regimes; sole-crop plots with intercropped plots; measured values with recalled values; values built on a stated area with values built on a measured one; meter values without a documented error with any pooled figure; a comparator plot with the plots whose yield is reported; moisture methods across seasons.

E: Deduplication and coverage. De-duplicate on the persistent plot identifier, then the persistent farmer identifier, from Project area level upward. Report coverage and precision with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands: 16.5 % or below released without qualification, above 16.5 % to 33.3 % released flagged, above 33.3 % not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one de-duplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above, and a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place. A figure at Project area level or above rests on a probability sample drawn from a stated frame, designed and estimated per FAO (2018), Handbook on crop statistics, Ch. 3, with the frame, the design and the achieved precision reported with the value; Trial / Station plots entering such a figure form a stratum of their own, enumerated in full, on the area they represent; a figure from a convenience census or a partner's aggregate is a monitoring series with composition unquantified and is reported as such, never as a regional estimate.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Include target-crop plots harvested in the reference season. Intercropped plots are reported separately from sole-crop plots, on the plot's own harvested area rather than on a sole-crop-equivalent area, with the companion crop declared. They are not converted onto a sole-crop-equivalent area and not pooled into the sole-crop mean: a land equivalent ratio requires a sole-crop control from the same site, which an on-farm crop cut does not provide, and pooling different crop combinations onto one derived area compares quantities that are not commensurable.

Establishment decides which of two failure cases a plot falls into, and it is a recorded field rather than enumerator judgement. A plot is established where the crop reached a stand the project's protocol accepts as planted, emergence over the majority of the sown area, assessed at the project's stated post-emergence check.

This is a deliberate departure from the convention used in official crop statistics, which nets disaster-ruined area out of the harvested area. The toolbox enters established failures at zero instead, on its own authority, because a mean computed over survivors describes the plots that came through rather than the intervention. Lodged plots are harvested and retained, with lodging recorded as a percentage of plot area (Berry et al., 2004).

Missing either harvested weight or crop-cut sub-plot area: the plot is excluded entirely, its production and its area both leaving the pooled figures. Dropping one without the other biases the mean. Report the achieved sample size.

Validate against a stated plausibility range by crop and irrigation regime, set by the project for its own context and stated with the value. Published CIMMYT ranges from the Mexico hubs (Gardeazábal-Monsalve et al., 2025, Table 2) are available as a starting point, and are ceilings for that context: a 19,000 kg/ha rainfed maize ceiling would screen nothing in most CIMMYT geographies. Ranges include zero, for crop failure or total loss. A value outside the range is investigated before reporting, not dropped.

Repeated observations: one value per plot per season.
limitations: Contribution, not attribution. Yield responds to weather, input prices, soil and farmer management alongside CIMMYT's interventions, so a level or a gain is never on its own proof of a CIMMYT effect.

Levels are not comparable. A Trial / Station yield above a Farm / Plot yield is the expected result, not a finding. The difference is the on-station to on-farm difference, which is systematic rather than incidental: trial gains do not carry over to smallholder fields at the same magnitude (Laajaj et al., 2020). Where a regional figure combines both, as the aggregation rule permits under area weighting, that figure is interpretable as realised production and is not a statement about either management regime on its own.

Measurement error follows from the method chosen and does not cancel. A crop cut estimates the plot rather than harvesting it: against a full-plot harvest, mean absolute error ranged from 10.6 quintals per hectare for a randomly positioned octant to 23 for farmer estimates, with bias tracking plot size and management (Kosmowski et al., 2021). Whole-plot harvest removes that sampling error. Carletto et al. (2013) show that producer-stated plot area is systematically wrong at smallholder scale, with small plots overestimated and large ones underestimated. A measured area removes this bias.

Method must travel with the value. Crop-cut, whole-plot and survey-derived yields are not interchangeable, and the sub-plot placement and area measurement methods change the error. Plots excluded as total losses are reported alongside the mean, or the figure overstates the true value.

A single season is a level, not performance. Weather dominates short-run yield movement, so one season says what was harvested, not whether the system is improving. That question is KPI-OC22's, and it needs a series.

Coverage is not representativeness. A pooled figure describes the plots measured, not the population of CIMMYT intervention areas, except where the sample was designed to be representative of it. The share of the reporting area covered is reported with the value for this reason, and a wide figure built on a narrow, unrepresentative sample is a common source of overstatement.

Fallback drying biases a pooled figure in a known direction. A fallback-dried sample retains more water than an oven-dried one, so its moisture is understated and its dry yield overstated. A pooled figure containing fallback-dried values reports their share alongside it. Where that share is large enough that the resulting bias could approach the detectability floor, report the figure computed from method-of-record values alone as a sensitivity, and label the combined figure as containing fallback-dried values.

Weighting by the crop-cut sub-plot area would defeat the estimator. Sub-plot areas are near-constant by design, so weighting on them collapses the area-weighted mean back to an unweighted average of plot yields, which is a different quantity and is wrong whenever plots differ in size.

Trial and farm plots combine only under area weighting. They may be pooled at Project area level and above, each entering on the area it represents. Trial plots occupy negligible area against farmers' fields, so a correctly weighted figure is dominated by farm data and remains interpretable as realised production; an unweighted pooling inflates it, since trial plots are researcher-managed and yield higher.
A figure pooled across irrigation regimes or across continents describes no system. The disaggregation by crop and regime is part of the figure, not an optional annex.
Where plot or farmer identifiers cannot be reconciled, the pooled figure is labelled an upper bound on measured coverage.
subMetrics: None.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: Content owner: the CIMMYT MEAL unit, with the agronomy lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Collection: station technicians at Trial / Station; extension agents or trained enumerators at Farm / Plot. Validation and calculation: the project's MEAL role, using the formulas in Calculation method. Approval and reporting: per the project's own reporting line to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 7 · Productivity — Reference sheet KPI-O23

name: Livestock productivity of target species in CIMMYT intervention areas
resultsLevel: Output. The CIMMYT MEAL Framework defines outcomes as changes in behaviour, systems, practice, capacity, policy or performance among beneficiaries and partners (Section 2.3). A measured productivity level is a state, not a change, so it cannot sit at outcome level regardless of measurement precision. The Framework places delivery and trial results at output level and describes them as "establishing the foundation for outcome-level evidence" (Section 2.2), which is what this indicator supplies to KPI-OC25.
primaryObjective: PO3. Contributing: PO2.
cgiarImpactArea: Nutrition, Health & Food Security
sdgTarget: Target 2.3
otherFrameworks: None
definition: Livestock productivity is the output obtained per unit of production from a target species, measured over one production period. It is a ratio whose two terms differ by species and product, milk per cow-day or per completed lactation, liveweight gain per animal-day, eggs per hen-day, and in every case the denominator is the exposure that produced the output, never a count of animals, except on the per-lactation basis, where the completed lactation is the unit and the mean is a mean of lactation totals rather than of rates. The species and product fix both terms and the resulting unit; the table in Calculation method sets them and a project does not choose them.
rationale: Provides the output achieved per unit of exposure of the target species in CIMMYT intervention areas at each level measured, and is the base for the productivity-change outcome (KPI-OC25) and the productivity impact (KPI-I06). Trial / Station values represent output under researcher-managed feeding and management; Farm / Plot values represent output under producer management.
projectSpecificApplication: How this project applies the institutional indicator: the species and product, the geography, the period, and the measurement levels observed. Scope only; the unit, measurement basis and calculation method are unchanged. Where the project's own target population is smallholders, that scope is declared here and Annex B supplies the threshold; the institutional indicator itself does not narrow, and the population a value was computed on is recorded with it so figures on different populations are never pooled.
projectSpecificRationale: States the project decision or funder commitment this figure serves. Example: a project reports it against a herd-productivity target agreed at design, and uses it to decide whether a feeding or health intervention continues.
projectTypesApply: seed systems and deployment where forage or fodder varieties are the intervention
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; system change and transformation; seed systems and deployment where forage or fodder varieties are the intervention.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development, which at CIMMYT is crop breeding; digital agriculture and AI unless the project runs its own animal measurement.
unit: Set by species and product, per the table in Calculation method. One unit per reported value. Values in different units are never combined, and there is no single combined livestock-productivity figure. Tropical livestock units are not a denominator here: the denominator is exposure, cow-days, animal-days or hen-days, which a biomass conversion cannot express. Where a project needs a herd-size class that spans species, for the optional herd or flock size cut, it may state one in tropical livestock units with the coefficient set named, since the factors differ by region.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more product is obtained per unit of exposure of the target species, per cow-day, animal-day, hen-day or completed lactation as the species table fixes. Values in different species and product units are never compared or combined.
disaggregationRequired: Measurement level; species; product; breed type (local, crossbred or exotic); for milk, suckling regime (none, restricted or calf at foot); for growth, weighing method (scale or girth algorithm) and the animal's sex and age class, with the classes stated; smallholder status of the holding, as Annex B defines it. The last is required because this indicator measures all producers in the intervention area while the impact indicator it feeds, KPI-I06, counts smallholders only: without the attribute recorded on the animal record, that narrowing cannot happen at any level and the impact figure is not producible. The threshold applied travels with the value.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Sex of the animal owner, per Doss & Kieran (2014); herd or flock size class; production system; feeding system (grazing, mixed or stall-fed), for projects in which feed is the intervention or an explanatory variable.
unitOfObservation:
The individual animal, at every level, except for layers, whose eggs and hen-days are recorded per flock: there the unit is the flock-period, keyed on the flock identifier and the period's start and end dates. What changes between levels is who manages the animals and which of them are in scope, not the thing observed.

Levels reported: Trial / Station, the animals of a station herd under research management · Farm / Plot, the animals of a producer's herd or flock · Household, the household's animals of the target species, built either by pooling its recorded animals, in which case the observation stays at the animal, or from the household's own report, in which case the reporting method and its quality rating are recorded with the value, and the two are never mixed within one value · Regional / Aggregated, a measurement level used where CIMMYT measures none of the levels above and the figure arrives already aggregated, from a partner that holds animal-level records with an exposure denominator from the species table, a milk-recording scheme for example; deliveries per supplier or per member, as a cooperative holds them, are not this indicator. Reported with the exposure as supplied and its unit named, the supplying partner, the method by which they collected it, and the population the figure represents.

Report every level the project measures; measuring all four is not required.
calculationSummary:
Livestock productivity is a function of the output obtained and the units of production that produced it. Three steps, in order.

First, fix the species, product and unit. The table below fixes the numerator, the denominator and the unit, so none is chosen per project. KPI-OC25 uses the same table.

Wool and fibre are outside the table; a project that needs them adds a citable method rather than an analogy.

Milk taken by the calf is not measured and is outside the numerator: the suckling regime (none, restricted, calf at foot) is a required field on the animal record, values on different regimes are reported separately, and a change of regime within a series splits it as a protocol change does.

Second, measure the output over the production period, by the method that product requires.

Lactation milk yield, where daily recording is not feasible and test-day records are used:

Days represented are the midpoints between consecutive tests. This is the test-interval method.

Days in milk run from the calving date to the dry-off date as recorded. The first test interval is credited from calving and the last to dry-off (Sargent et al., 1968), so the numerator and the denominator cover the same span; midpoint-only crediting leaves the ends of the lactation uncounted in the denominator while their milk sits in the numerator. Where the calving date was not observed, because the cow calved before the project's recording began, the per-day record starts at the first test and credits nothing before it; on the per-lactation basis that lactation is incomplete and is reported separately. Record the number of tests achieved and the lactation length with every value; Migose et al. (2020) supply the evidence that lactation estimates lose accuracy as test-day spacing widens, and are the error source for the below-floor classes.

Average daily liveweight gain:

Both weights must come from the same method: a scale where one is available, otherwise a published heart-girth algorithm calibrated for the breed type and region (Goopy et al., 2018). Record the method with the value. A girth algorithm estimates a liveweight level well; it is weaker for a change, because its error does not cancel across two occasions, and Goopy et al. (2018) set out the constraints on using girth measurements to capture liveweight change. Where gain is the reported metric and a scale exists, use the scale. The Goopy algorithm is calibrated for cattle. For sheep and goats a girth relationship is admitted only where fitted or validated on the breed type and region; Temoso et al. (2017), fitted on communal-rangeland goats and sheep in Botswana, is the precedent for the form, not a relationship to apply elsewhere unvalidated. Where no local relationship exists and no scale is available, gain is not reportable for that flock. For pigs and poultry no calibrated relationship is adopted here, so gain is scale-weighed.

Third, calculate productivity for that species and product:

The metrics of record are the table's: milk, liveweight gain and eggs. Offtake, the weight of animals leaving the herd over a herd count, is not admitted: it moves with prices and household cash needs as much as with productivity, and a herd whose animals cannot be identified and followed across a period, or a layer flock that cannot be identified and followed, reports no value on this indicator.
dataSource:
Trial / Station: Recommended DS1: the station's own individual animal records.

Farm / Plot: Recommended DS1: the project's own test-day milk recording or weighing records, or for layers a daily flock record of eggs collected and hens present, kept on a project-issued form and checked at each enumerator visit, on a representative sample of target producers' animals.

Fallback DS1: producer-reported production, admitted only where the instrument is a published validated module, its error against direct measurement is documented and reported as the quality rating, and a published method supports the aggregation. Reported separately and not pooled with measured values.

Household: Derived from the household's Farm / Plot records. Frame DS2: the project's farmer register supplies the animal-to-producer link.

Fallback DS1: the household's own report, under the fallback conditions above, reported separately and never pooled with measured records.

Project area and above: Recommended DS1, aggregated: where the project measures animals itself, the value is computed from its own animal records through the aggregation levels in Aggregation rule, not obtained from a separate source. Trial / Station and Farm / Plot records are never pooled into one figure and are reported side by side at every level.

Regional / Aggregated, partner-supplied: Fallback DS1, partner-aggregated: where CIMMYT measures none of the levels above, the figure the supplying partner aggregated from its own animal records, admitted with the partner, its collection method and the population the figure represents recorded alongside, as Unit of observation requires, and never pooled with project-measured records.

Comparator DS4: national statistics, to place the direction of the CIMMYT figure against the national one, never a substitute for it and never pooled with it; a national series derived from fixed technical conversion factors rather than from measured output is not used, since it can be flat by construction.

Not applicable: DS2 for the productivity value itself: delivery and registration records capture what was distributed, not what was produced.

DS3: remote sensing does not measure animal productivity.

DS5: crowdsourced figures cannot be tied to an identified animal across a production period.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Per level measured: the source role used, the sampling design, the achieved sample size, and the data quality rating, which is the documented error of the instrument used. Where Fallback was used, name the validated module and state why direct measurement was not feasible.
collectionInstrument:
A herd or flock record carrying animal identifier, species, breed type, parity or age, for dairy animals the suckling regime (none, restricted, calf at foot), and for each observation the date, the measurement method and the value; the calving, dry-off and exit dates, and for layers the daily count of hens present and of hens leaving, by route of exit, each flagged observed or recalled.

Fallback, where direct measurement was not feasible: the published validated module named in Data source, administered as published, with its documented error recorded as the quality rating and its values held so they can be reported separately from measured ones.

Recorded with every value, whatever the instrument. The method used: scale or the named girth algorithm; test-day recording or recall. For a lactation figure, the number of tests achieved and the lactation length, since the accuracy of the estimate depends on test spacing. The quality rating, being the documented error of the instrument used.

Retain the component values, not only the derived figure: test-day yields with their dates, not only the lactation total; both endpoint weights with their dates, not only the gain. Every record carries a persistent animal identifier, or for a layer flock a persistent flock identifier, and a persistent farmer identifier where the project operates a farmer register, which is what makes the Household level and KPI-I06 reportable.
collectionFrequency: Milk: test-day recording through the lactation. Liveweight: at both ends of the defined growth period, at entry for any animal joining after the start, and at exit for any animal leaving before the end. Eggs: continuous flock records. A project intending to report KPI-OC25 measures in every production period of that indicator's window, because it needs at least two measured periods for the change, three for a change released without the short-series flag, and four for stability. A period missed in a four-period window still leaves three, so the change stays reportable with the gap stated while stability is withheld; a period missed in a three-period window leaves the change reportable but released flagged as a short series, and below two measured periods KPI-OC25 is unreportable.
referencePeriod: The lactation, growth period or laying period, assigned to the reporting year in which it ends
baselineRequired: No. This indicator reports a level; KPI-OC25 computes change and carries the baseline requirement
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. The exposure unit is part of the domain: a per-cow-day figure and a per-lactation figure are never summed into one mean, because Σ output ÷ (Σ cow-days + Σ lactations) is not a quantity. Records on different exposure bases are reported side by side. One species, one product, one breed type, one measurement level: station and producer herds are never one domain. For milk, one suckling regime: records under none, restricted and calf at foot are never one domain. For growth, one weighing method: scale and girth-derived gains are never one domain. Levels widen the set of animals; they never widen the domain. No combined livestock-productivity figure exists across species or products.

Weight: exposure, in the unit the species table fixes, so an animal recorded over a long lactation carries more of the mean than one recorded over a short one.

B: Combination method: ratio of sums.

Total exposure = Σ exposure per animal-period record, in the exposure unit the species table fixes: days in milk or completed lactations for dairy, animal-days for growth, hen-days for layers, bird-days for broilers

Dividing by the count of animals is not this estimator: it gives the unweighted mean of per-animal values, which coincides with it only where every animal contributed identical exposure. Records with zero exposure enter neither sum. The estimator is invariant to staging, so recompute from animal records; never average means.

C: Levels and operations.

D: Never pooled. Different species; different products; different breed types; milk records under different suckling regimes; growth records under different weighing methods; station-herd records with producer-herd records; measured values with recalled values.

E: Deduplication and coverage. De-duplicate on the animal-period record key, the persistent animal identifier plus the period start and end dates, or for layers the flock-period key, then on the persistent farmer identifier, from Project area level upward.

Where two records for one animal do not share period boundaries, they are the same animal-period when their date ranges overlap by more than half of the shorter record's days; the record collected under the finer protocol is retained. Report coverage and precision with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands: 16.5 % or below released without qualification, above 16.5 % to 33.3 % released flagged, above 33.3 % not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one de-duplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above, and a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place.

Every reported value carries the exit rate, exits ÷ Σ animal-days at risk in the same period, computed over every animal-period record in scope, including records that enter neither productivity sum, and split by route of exit: died, slaughtered, sold, other disposal. It needs no separate convention, and it is what allows a reader to judge whether turnover produced the result. A growth figure without it is not interpretable.

Every milk value reports the share of its lactations whose calving or dry-off date entered the value flagged recalled; such a date is a date on the measured record, not a recalled value under Block D.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Include target-species animals under the management of producers in the intervention area, and station-herd animals under a tested regime at Trial / Station, during the reference period.

Include animals that exited mid-period on their observed exposure, with the exit date and reason recorded. Under Σ output ÷ Σ exposure a truncated record is not a short lactation, it is fewer days in milk and the milk produced in them, and both terms are observed; excluding it would remove exactly the animals whose loss the figure should register. Nothing is prorated to a standard length.

On the per-lactation basis only, a completed lactation is the unit, so an incomplete one is reported separately and never pooled into the mean. This is a property of that exposure unit, not a rule about survivors.

Missing an endpoint weight: an animal that dies, or leaves without being weighed, has no closing weight, its gain is unobserved and it enters neither sum; an animal weighed at sale, slaughter or transfer has one and enters both sums on its animal-days to that date. Growth figures are therefore conditioned on a closing weight, which is stated wherever they are reported, and the exit rate below is what makes the condition visible. Report the achieved sample size.

The test-day floor is the toolbox's own convention, institutional and not per project. A lactation estimate requires at least three test days, with no inter-test interval exceeding 90 days and at least one test in each third of the lactation; monthly recording is the benchmark. On a lactation begun before the project's recording, the condition on each third is not applied: its recorded span, from the first test to dry-off, must hold at least three test days, with no more than 90 days between consecutive tests or between the last test and dry-off. A lactation below the floor is reported separately and never pooled into the mean.

Below-floor values carry the error of the nearest documented protocol class and say which: the single-test-day class where fewer than three tests were achieved, the recall class where the value was recalled; for the single-test-day class the error is the one Migose et al. (2020) report for that spacing, and for the recall class the documented error of the module used, each restated on the value. The error is stated as a bound rather than a point estimate.

Repeated observations: one value per animal per lactation or growth period, and per flock per laying period. An animal measured across two lactations contributes two values, each labelled with its parity.
limitations: Contribution, not attribution. Productivity responds to feed availability, disease, weather and prices alongside CIMMYT's interventions, so a level or a gain is never on its own proof of a CIMMYT effect.

Levels are not comparable. A station-herd value above an on-farm value is the expected result, not a finding. The difference is the on-station to on-farm difference. Station-herd and producer-herd records are never pooled: the crop condition that licenses pooling trial and farm plots, that trial plots are a negligible area, has no analogue in exposure, so a combined figure would describe neither regime.

Measurement error follows from the method chosen. A lactation estimated from few test days is not the same quantity as one from many, and the usable spacing is documented (Migose et al., 2020). A girth-derived weight and a scale weight are not interchangeable, and a girth equation fitted on temperate commercial cattle does not transfer to African smallholder animals (Goopy et al., 2018). Weigh at a consistent point relative to feeding and watering, or gut fill is recorded as gain.

Herd turnover can produce the whole result. Animals sold, died or culled are not a random sample. Milk and egg figures absorb this, because an exiting animal contributes the output and the exposure it had; growth figures only partly, because a dead or unweighed animal has no closing weight, so a gain is a gain among animals with a closing weight and overstates herd performance by the amount that the animals lost were the poorer ones. The exit rate required in the aggregation rule is reported with every value.

Coverage is not representativeness. A pooled figure describes the animals recorded, not the population of CIMMYT intervention areas, except where the sample was designed to be representative of it. A wide figure built on a narrow, unrepresentative sample is a common source of overstatement.

The data floor is the same for every producer. The test-day floor, the weighing rules and the quality rating apply to a smallholder herd and a commercial one alike; a herd that cannot meet them reports below the floor with the class error stated, so the value stays visible rather than being dropped, and the share of below-floor records is what shows where record-keeping is thin.

Growth promoters and prohibited substances are not detected by this measurement. The indicator records output and exposure, not compliance; a project working where such use is possible records the feeding and health regime as a project-specific field and reads a gain against it.
Averaging per-animal values would be a different quantity. The two totals are retained alongside the ratio so an institutional figure can be rebuilt from them.
Station and producer animals are reported side by side at every level. A station herd under a tested regime is not a statement about producer conditions.
Where animal or farmer identifiers cannot be reconciled, the pooled figure is labelled an upper bound on measured coverage.
subMetrics: By species and product pair, per the table in Calculation method. There is no combined livestock-productivity figure.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.

sheetStewardDataRoles: Collection: station technicians at Trial / Station; trained enumerators or technicians at Farm / Plot level. Validation and calculation: the project's MEAL role, using the formulas in Calculation method. Approval and reporting: per the project's own reporting line to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
