name: Labour productivity in target-crop production in CIMMYT intervention areas
resultsLevel: Output. The CIMMYT MEAL Framework defines outcomes as changes in behaviour, systems, practice, capacity, policy or performance among beneficiaries and partners (Section 2.3). A measured productivity level is a state, not a change, so it cannot sit at outcome level regardless of measurement precision. The Framework places delivery and trial results at output level and describes them as "establishing the foundation for outcome-level evidence" (Section 2.2), which is what this indicator supplies to KPI-OC62.
primaryObjective: PO3. Contributing: PO2, PO4.
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs
sdgTarget: Target 2.3. The construct is that of SDG indicator 2.3.1, "volume of production per labour unit by classes of farming/pastoral/forestry enterprise size", which is measured per day worked. Not reportable as 2.3.1, which is expressed in constant-price value for a nationally defined producer population, while this is a physical quantity for a target crop on assisted plots.
otherFrameworks: None.
definition: The physical output of a target crop obtained per unit of labour applied to producing it, in kilograms per person-day. The numerator is production, the dry yield defined on KPI-O23 multiplied by the harvested area, taken from the same plot record. The denominator is the labour applied to that plot for that crop over the season, measured in person-hours. Person-hours are the measured quantity; the person-day is a presentation unit obtained by dividing by eight. Labour is counted in three categories, hired, household and unpaid non-household, recorded separately and summed, for every person who worked on the plot whatever their age, with the age band on each line.
rationale: Answers what a producer obtains per unit of labour, which yield alone cannot say. A practice that raises yield while raising labour more has lowered the return on the scarcest resource many smallholders hold, and mechanisation is adopted precisely to change this ratio rather than to change yield. It is the base for KPI-OC62 and, with the yield indicator, one of the measures on which the productivity impact indicator can qualify a farmer.
projectSpecificApplication:
How this project applies the institutional indicator: the crop, the geography, the period, and the measurement levels observed. Scope only; the unit, measurement basis and calculation method are unchanged.

Example: "Labour productivity in maize production in the Central Rift Valley under CIMMYT intervention, seasons 2023 to 2025, at Farm / Plot level."
projectSpecificRationale: States the project decision this figure serves. Example: a project introducing a labour-saving implement reports it because a yield gain obtained through more days of work is not a livelihood gain, and output per person-day, this indicator's unit, is what separates the two.
projectTypesNotApplicable: digital agriculture and AI unless the project runs its own ground measurement of labour
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; system change and transformation; seed systems and deployment.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; digital agriculture and AI unless the project runs its own ground measurement of labour.
unit: Kilograms per person-day, on the same basis as KPI-O23: dry yield, or yield at a stated moisture percentage recorded with the value. A person-day is eight person-hours, used for presentation only: the recorded quantity is hours, and the total in hours is reported alongside. No working-day length is assumed in measurement: hours are recorded per activity as performed, whatever the local labour arrangement or the season's demands, and the eight-hour person-day is a fixed constant that carries no information about the length of any actual working day, which is what keeps person-days from two countries commensurable.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more crop output is obtained per person-day of labour applied to producing it. It can also rise because labour was withdrawn rather than because output grew, so it is read alongside the labour input series behind it. A higher value is not by itself a better livelihood outcome: labour use also reflects access to machinery suited to the plot, plot size and fragmentation, and the cropping system, so the ratio is read with the cropping system and, where recorded, the mechanisation status of the plot.
disaggregationRequired: Measurement level; crop; irrigation regime (rainfed / irrigated); cropping system (sole crop or intercrop); smallholder status of the holding, as Annex B defines it. The last is required because this indicator measures all producers in the intervention area while the impact indicator it feeds, KPI-I06, counts smallholders only: without the attribute recorded on the plot record, that narrowing cannot happen at any level and the impact figure is not producible. The threshold applied travels with the value. The hired, household and unpaid non-household split of the denominator, and its split by age band (under 15, 15 to 17, 18 to 30 and over 30, the 15 to 30 span being the Core's youth band, or the date of birth from which the bands are derived, or the national bands where a project must use them, stated with the value), are required sub-metrics reported with every value; the ratio itself is not disaggregated by labour type.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Sex of plot manager, per Doss & Kieran (2014); sex of each worker on the labour line, reported as a split of hours; age band of the plot manager; farm size class, with the bands stated, for example under 1 ha, 1 to 2 ha and 2 to 5 ha, or the national classification where one is in use; agroecological zone, with the classification stated; variety; mechanisation status of the plot.
unitOfObservation: Report every level the project measures; measuring all three is not required.
calculationSummary:
Labour productivity is the harvested quantity divided by the labour that produced it.

First, take the dry yield and the harvested area from KPI-O23 for that plot and season, and recover the production:

Second, sum the labour applied to that plot for that crop over the season, from the labour records of every activity: land preparation, sowing, weeding and cultural work, input application, irrigation, harvest and post-harvest handling. Record hired (paid in cash or kind), household and unpaid non-household labour separately, unpaid non-household being exchange, reciprocal and communal work-party labour and any other unpaid outside worker, never dropped and never filed under either of the others, with each worker's age band.

People × Duration is admissible only where every person listed worked the full duration, and the record says so; otherwise each individual's hours are entered on their own line.

Recorded shift length is used wherever the instrument holds it, and it enters the sum as hours directly, with no eight-hour step. Hours are never imputed. A labour line without recorded hours makes the record incomplete, and the record is excluded under Eligibility rather than filled with an assumed shift length.

Third, compute the ratio.

Machine time is not converted into person-days. Where an operation is mechanised, the operator's time is counted and the machine time is not; the machine's contribution appears as a higher ratio, which is the effect the indicator exists to detect. Machine hours are recorded alongside so the ratio can be read against them.

An intercropped plot is its own case. Its labour serves every crop on the plot while the production counted is the target crop's, so its ratio is computed and reported separately from sole-crop plots, with the companion crop declared, as KPI-O23 reports its yield; it is never pooled with a sole-crop figure.
dataSource:
Recommended DS1: the project's own plot records, carrying the yield from KPI-O23 and the labour lines from the cost and labour module attached to the same record. The numerator takes KPI-O23's route: a plot whose yield came from a KPI-O23 Fallback, or whose harvested area rests on a stated area, is reported beside the pooled figure with a note naming the yield or the area as the Fallback component, and never pooled.

Fallback DS1, recall: a labour module in the project's farmer panel survey in which hours are recalled rather than logged. Admissible only where all three conditions hold, the same three KPI-O23 applies to its own fallback: the module is published and validated, meaning its questionnaire and documentation are citable and its error against logged measurement has been measured in a documented study, the survey experiments of Arthi et al. (2018) and Gaddis et al. (2021) being that documentation for the season-end modules each tested, which the project names from the paper it relies on; that error, stated as a bound rather than a point estimate, is reported as the quality rating on every value the module produces; and its aggregation method is published. A module whose error is not documented is not admissible, because the value cannot then be qualified. Recall values are reported separately and are never pooled with logged ones.

Frame DS2: the project's farmer register supplies the plot-to-producer link.

Regional / Aggregated, partner-supplied · Fallback DS1, partner-aggregated: hours as supplied, a figure in days not being admitted; never pooled with project-measured records.

Comparator DS4: the SDG 2.3.1 national series, to place the direction of the project figure against the national one, never a substitute for it and never pooled with it; national statistics carry no plot-level labour, so DS4 never produces the value.

Not applicable · DS2 for the labour value: delivery and registration records identify who was reached, not how much labour was applied. · DS3: remote sensing does not observe labour. · DS5: crowdsourced labour figures cannot satisfy the documented-error condition.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Names the systems holding the plot records and the labour module, the persistent plot identifier that links them, and, where the fallback route was used, the module and the recall length.
collectionInstrument:
The labour lines of the cost and labour module, attached to the KPI-O23 plot record rather than fielded separately. Per plot and per activity: the activity status (performed and recorded, performed and not recorded, not performed), the date of the activity and the date it was recorded, the number of people who participated, whether every person worked the full duration, the shift length in hours, the hours the activity lasted, each worker's labour category (hired, household or unpaid non-household) and age band on the bands the disaggregation field states, and the area it was performed on with its kind stated (harvested or assessment). Every labour line carries a collection-mode flag, logged or recalled, set from the days between the activity and its recording under the seven-day window in Collection frequency, and where recalled the recall length; the flag is what keeps the two apart in the dataset so they are not pooled by accident. The labour record attaches to the plot, not to a hectare: an established-but-failed plot enters with zero production and all the labour it consumed in land preparation, sowing and weeding, so the effort spent on a plot that produced nothing lowers the ratio in exactly the failure seasons KPI-O23's zero-entry convention exists to expose. Labour per hectare of the area recorded with each line is reportable as a sub-metric and is not the denominator of the ratio. Where the farmer keeps the record it is an activity card, one line per activity, checked by the enumerator at each visit.

Precedent in CIMMYT practice. The Mexico hub logbook (2012 to 2022) records, per activity and per plot, the number of workers, shifts worked, shift length in hours and hours per hectare for manual sowing, input application and weeding, and days worked for manual harvest, captured by extension agents at fortnightly or monthly visits (Gardeazábal-Monsalve et al., 2025). It shows that per-activity labour recording is feasible at scale in CIMMYT's own network. Against this sheet it differs on three points: its harvest labour is a day record, its visit interval exceeds the seven-day window so its lines are recall on this sheet's flag, and it carries no hired-versus-household flag on manual labour. Where an instrument records shifts and a recorded shift length, hours are shifts × shift length × people, which is recorded shift length and not an imputed day; only a record with days and no shift length is a day-only record.
collectionFrequency:
Labour lines are recorded per activity, within seven days of the activity they describe. The rule is a recording window, not a visit calendar. The record may be kept by the farmer on an activity card or made by an enumerator, and either way a line recorded more than seven days after the activity is recall. Where an enumerator makes or checks the record, visits are timed to the crop's activity calendar rather than to a fixed interval, at most seven days after each episode of work. Seven days is the benchmark arm of the experiments that measure recall bias, which used weekly recording through the season against a season-end interview (Arthi et al., 2018; Gaddis et al., 2021). The productivity ratio is computed once per season, as soon as the yield value for the plot is available. A project intending to report KPI-OC62 measures in every season of that indicator's window, because it needs at least two measured seasons for the change, three for a change released without the short-series flag, and four for stability.

One-shot collection at the end of the season is recall, not logging, whatever the instrument is called, and it is admissible only on the fallback route under the conditions in Data source; a season-end interview is not a cheaper version of the same measurement but the arm those experiments show to be biased.

Whether the farmer keeps the card is a project decision taken at design, against the farmers' capacity and willingness to record after each activity; a card that is not realistic gives way to the enumerator route, and the collection mode is recorded on every line either way.
referencePeriod: One crop season, matching the reference period of the KPI-O23 value that supplies the numerator.
baselineRequired: No. This indicator reports a level; KPI-OC62 computes change and carries the baseline requirement
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One crop, one irrigation regime, one cropping system, sole crop or intercrop with the companion crop declared, one cropping season where the national calendar defines more than one. Levels widen the set of plots; they never widen the domain. No combined figure exists across crops, irrigation regimes or cropping systems.

Weight: person-days, so a plot record built on more labour carries more of the mean. Dividing by the number of records would be an unweighted mean of per-record ratios.

B: Combination method: ratio of sums.

The estimator is invariant to staging, so recompute from plot records; never average plot-level ratios: an unweighted mean of ratios weights a small plot equally with a large one and is a different quantity.

C: Levels and operations.

D: Never pooled. Different crops; different irrigation regimes; sole-crop plots with intercropped plots, or intercrops of different combinations; logged labour with recalled labour; measured yield with recalled yield; production on a measured area with production on a stated one; Trial / Station plots.

E: Deduplication and coverage. De-duplicate on the persistent plot identifier, then the persistent farmer identifier, from Project area level upward. Report coverage and precision with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands: 16.5 % or below released without qualification, above 16.5 % to 33.3 % released flagged, above 33.3 % not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one de-duplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above, and a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Include plots with both a dry yield and a complete labour record for the season. A plot missing any activity's labour is excluded rather than imputed, because a partial denominator inflates the ratio. Report the number of plots excluded on this ground alongside the value; a high exclusion rate is itself the finding. Zero is not a valid denominator: a plot recorded with no labour is a recording failure, not a value. Each activity carries an activity status, performed and recorded, performed and not recorded, or not performed: a zero enters only through not performed, and an absent line is performed and not recorded, which excludes the plot. A plot with any line flagged recalled is excluded from the logged figure and counted with the reason; it enters the recall series only where the fallback conditions in Data source hold, which a project's own late card line does not. An established-but-failed plot with a complete labour record is included, at zero production, as KPI-O23 includes it. Intercropped plots enter their own series, never the sole-crop one. Labour CIMMYT itself engages is outside this indicator, and an under-18 hour on it is a safeguarding incident, not a data point.
limitations: Recalled hours are not measured hours. Season-end recall reports more hours per person per plot than weekly recording and lists fewer people and plots at work, so the bias on total hours is not fixed in size or sign, and recalled and logged values are reported separately and never pooled. Where only recall is available, the value is read as indicative.

The ratio moves for two different reasons. It rises when output rises and when labour falls, and a project that mechanises will raise it without changing yield at all. The ratio is therefore read alongside yield, never instead of it.

Labour use reflects farm structure as well as management. Small or fragmented plots may not suit the machinery available in the area, so manual labour can be the feasible option whatever the management, and an intercropped plot may need hand work that a sole crop does not. A difference in the ratio between plots or systems can reflect access to appropriate mechanisation or plot structure rather than efficiency.
A denominator that omits an activity inflates the ratio.

Household labour is counted in hours, not valued. This sheet makes no imputation; valuation belongs to KPI-OC63 in the Income & livelihoods pathway, the only place the toolbox values household labour, which records the wage rate, its source and its reference period with the value.
Family labour hours are hard to attribute where several household members work the same plot intermittently, and children's contributions are systematically under-reported.

Averaging plot-level ratios would be a different quantity, weighting a small plot equally with a large one. The two totals are retained alongside the ratio so an institutional figure can be rebuilt from them.

A crop-cut yield is measured before the producer's own harvest and handling losses, while the labour includes that harvest and handling, so the ratio credits output the producer's harvest may not recover.
subMetrics:
Production, person-days, the hired, household and unpaid non-household split and its age-band split are each retained and reported alongside the ratio, not only their quotient; labour per hectare of the area recorded with each line may be reported beside them. An institutional figure is recomputed from the components rather than averaged from project ratios, and a project that reports only a ratio cannot contribute to one.

Relationship to other indicators. KPI-O23 supplies the numerator and the plot record. KPI-O24 and its labour counterpart carry the livestock thread, which is never pooled with this one. KPI-OC62 carries change and temporal stability. KPI-I06 admits labour productivity as one of the measures on which a farmer can qualify. KPI-OC63, gross margin, in the Income & livelihoods pathway, uses the same module and values the labour this indicator counts in hours.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: Content owner: the CIMMYT MEAL unit, with the farming-systems lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Collection: project agronomists, extension agents and trained enumerators. Validation and calculation: the project's MEAL role, using the formulas in Calculation method. Approval and reporting: per the project's own reporting line to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.

name: Labour productivity in target-species livestock production in CIMMYT intervention areas
resultsLevel: Output. The CIMMYT MEAL Framework defines outcomes as changes in behaviour, systems, practice, capacity, policy or performance among beneficiaries and partners (Section 2.3). A measured productivity level is a state, not a change, so it cannot sit at outcome level regardless of measurement precision. The Framework places delivery and trial results at output level and describes them as "establishing the foundation for outcome-level evidence" (Section 2.2), which is what this indicator supplies to KPI-OC62.
primaryObjective: PO3. Contributing: PO2, PO4.
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs
sdgTarget: Target 2.3. The construct is that of SDG indicator 2.3.1, production per day worked. Not reportable as 2.3.1, for the reasons given on the crop sheet.
otherFrameworks: None.
definition: The physical output of a target species and product obtained per unit of labour applied to producing it, expressed in the product's physical unit per person-day. The unit of record is the herd-window, a producer's animals of one species and product over a stated recording window. The numerator is the physical output those animals produced inside the window, from KPI-O24's records and never its ratio; the denominator is every labour line dated inside the window, measured in person-hours, the person-day being a presentation unit obtained by dividing by eight. Labour is counted in three categories, hired, household and unpaid non-household, recorded separately and summed, for every worker whatever their age, with the age band on each line.
rationale: Answers what a producer obtains per unit of labour spent keeping animals. Livestock labour is continuous rather than seasonal, frequently falls on household members rather than hired workers, and is the constraint that decides whether a herd can grow. Output per unit of exposure alone cannot show whether a practice made the enterprise more or less demanding of the household's time.
projectSpecificApplication:
How this project applies the institutional indicator: the species, the product, the geography, the period, and the measurement levels observed. Scope only; the unit, measurement basis and calculation method are unchanged.

Example: "Labour productivity in milk production among crossbred dairy herds in Nandi County under CIMMYT intervention, 2023 to 2025, at Farm / Plot level."
projectSpecificRationale: States the project decision this figure serves. Example: a project changing herd management reports it because the labour a herd absorbs determines whether the practice is adopted once the project ends.
projectTypesApply: seed systems and deployment where forage or fodder varieties are the intervention
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; system change and transformation; seed systems and deployment where forage or fodder varieties are the intervention.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development, which at CIMMYT is crop breeding; digital agriculture and AI unless the project runs its own animal and labour measurement.
unit: The product's physical unit from KPI-O24 per person-day, litres of milk, kilograms of liveweight gain or eggs per person-day, never KPI-O24's ratio per person-day. A person-day is eight person-hours, used for presentation only: the recorded quantity is hours, and the total in hours is reported alongside. No working-day length is assumed in measurement: hours are recorded per activity as performed, whatever the local labour arrangement, and the eight-hour person-day is a fixed constant that carries no information about the length of any actual working day, which is what keeps person-days from two countries commensurable.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more product is obtained per person-day of labour applied to the target species. It can also rise because labour was withdrawn rather than because output grew, so it is read alongside the labour input series behind it. A higher value is not by itself a better livelihood outcome: labour use also reflects the production system, herd size and access to labour-saving equipment, so the ratio is read with the production system recorded on the record.
disaggregationRequired: Measurement level; species; product; breed type (local, crossbred or exotic); for milk, suckling regime (none, restricted or calf at foot, or mixed where the herd-window's milk records carry more than one); for growth, weighing method (scale or girth algorithm); smallholder status of the holding, as Annex B defines it. The last is required because this indicator measures all producers in the intervention area while the impact indicator it feeds, KPI-I06, counts smallholders only: without the attribute recorded on the animal record, that narrowing cannot happen at any level and the impact figure is not producible. The threshold applied travels with the value. The hired, household and unpaid non-household split of the denominator, and its split by age band (under 15, 15 to 17, 18 to 30 and over 30, the 15 to 30 span being the Core's youth band, or the date of birth from which the bands are derived, or the national bands where a project must use them, stated with the value), are required sub-metrics reported with every value; the ratio itself is not disaggregated by labour type.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Sex of the animal owner, per Doss & Kieran (2014); sex of each worker on the labour line, reported as a split of hours; herd or flock size class; production system; feeding system (grazing, mixed or stall-fed), for projects in which feed is the intervention or an explanatory variable.
unitOfObservation: Report every level the project measures; measuring all three is not required.
calculationSummary:
Labour productivity is the output divided by the labour that produced it.

First, take the output produced inside the window by the herd's animals, from KPI-O24's records: milk credited to the window's days from the test-day record, each day inside the window carrying the daily yield of the test interval it falls in under KPI-O24's test-interval method, from calving where the lactation begins inside the window; eggs from the flock record; gain from animals weighed at both window endpoints, or at entry and at exit or the window's end for an animal present for part of the window, on its days present; in the product's physical unit and never as KPI-O24's ratio.

Second, sum the labour applied to those animals over the window, across every activity: feeding and watering, herding and grazing management, milking, health and veterinary handling, housing and manure management, and the labour of moving animals to market where the project counts it. Record hired (paid in cash or kind), household and unpaid non-household labour separately, unpaid non-household being exchange, reciprocal and communal work-party labour and any other unpaid outside worker, never dropped and never filed under either of the others, with each worker's age band.

Hours are never imputed. A labour line without recorded hours makes the record incomplete, and the record is excluded under Eligibility rather than filled with an assumed shift length.

People × Duration is admissible only where every person listed worked the full duration, and the record says so; otherwise each individual's hours are entered on their own line.

Third, compute the ratio.

Shared labour is apportioned, not double counted. Where one labour episode serves several species, or animals and crops together, it is apportioned on the time actually spent on each where the line separates it, and otherwise the episode is excluded and the exclusion reported. Neither animal-days nor tropical livestock units are a basis: a hen-day is not a cow-day, and tropical livestock unit coefficients are region-dependent (Rothman-Ostrow et al., 2020). This is the principal difference from the crop sheet, where labour attaches to a plot and a season and rarely serves two enterprises at once.

Labour serving several products of one herd, milk and growth from a dual-purpose herd for example, is not apportioned between them: each product's herd-window carries all of it, the herd's other products are recorded with the value, and the hours are never summed across the herd's products.

Admissible only where all three conditions hold, the same three KPI-O23 applies to its own fallback: the module is published and validated, meaning its questionnaire and documentation are citable and its error against logged measurement has been measured in a documented study, the survey experiments of Arthi et al. (2018) and Gaddis et al. (2021) being that documentation for the season-end modules each tested, which the project names from the paper it relies on; that error, stated as a bound rather than a point estimate, is reported as the quality rating on every value the module produces; and its aggregation method is published. A module whose error is not documented is not admissible, because the value cannot then be qualified. Recall values are reported separately and are never pooled with logged ones.

Frame DS2: the project's farmer register supplies the animal-to-producer link.

Regional / Aggregated, partner-supplied · Fallback DS1, partner-aggregated: hours as supplied, a figure in days not being admitted; never pooled with project-measured records.

Comparator DS4: the SDG 2.3.1 national series, to place the direction of the project figure against the national one, never a substitute for it and never pooled with it; national statistics carry no herd-level labour, so DS4 never produces the value.

Not applicable · DS2 for the labour value: delivery and registration records identify who was reached, not how much labour was applied. · DS3: remote sensing does not observe labour. · DS5: crowdsourced labour figures cannot satisfy the documented-error condition.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Names the systems holding the animal records and the labour module, the persistent identifiers that link them, and, where the fallback route was used, the module and the recall length.
collectionInstrument: The labour lines of the cost and labour module, attached to the herd-window record rather than fielded separately. Per herd-window and per activity: the activity status (performed and recorded, performed and not recorded, not performed); for episodic work the date of the work and the date it was recorded, and for continuous work one line per week per activity carrying the week's first and last dates, the collection-mode flag set from the week's first date; the number of people, whether every person worked the full duration, the hours worked, each worker's labour category (hired, household or unpaid non-household) and age band on the bands the disaggregation field states, and, where the episode serves more than one species or enterprise, the time spent on each where the line separates it. Every labour line carries a collection-mode flag, logged or recalled, set from the days between the work and its recording under the seven-day window in Collection frequency, and where recalled the recall length; the flag is what keeps the two apart in the dataset so they are not pooled by accident. Where the household keeps the record it is a weekly activity card, checked by the enumerator at each visit.
collectionFrequency:
Labour lines are recorded per activity, within seven days of the work they describe. Livestock work is continuous rather than episodic, so the record is a weekly card of hours by activity, kept by the household or made by an enumerator; where an enumerator makes the record, visits fall at intervals of no more than seven days and cover the period since the last visit, there being no activity calendar to time them to. A line recorded more than seven days after the work is recall. The productivity ratio is computed once per window, as soon as the output value is available. A project intending to report KPI-OC62 measures in every window of that indicator's series, because it needs at least two measured windows for the change, three for a change released without the short-series flag, and four for stability; a project shorter than two of its declared windows reports this indicator alone.

One-shot collection at the end of the production period is recall, not logging, whatever the instrument is called, and it is admissible only on the fallback route under the conditions in Data source. The experiments that measure recall bias use weekly recording through the season as the benchmark arm and a season-end interview as the biased arm (Arthi et al., 2018; Gaddis et al., 2021); a season-end interview is not a cheaper version of the same measurement.

Whether the household keeps the card is a project decision taken at design, against the household's capacity and willingness to record weekly; a card that is not realistic gives way to the enumerator route, and the collection mode is recorded on every line either way.
referencePeriod: The recording window: twelve months for continuous systems and the batch cycle for batch systems, stated in months with every value and assigned to the reporting year in which it ends. A herd's first milk window opens no earlier than its first test day.
baselineRequired: No. This indicator reports a level; KPI-OC62 computes change and carries the baseline requirement
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One species, one product, one breed type, one window length in continuous systems; in batch systems the window is the batch cycle, and the distribution of cycle lengths is reported with the value. For milk, one suckling regime, as on KPI-O24; a herd-window whose milk records carry more than one regime is classed mixed, a domain of its own. For growth, one weighing method, as on KPI-O24. Levels widen the set of herd-windows; they never widen the domain. No combined figure exists across species or products.

Weight: person-days, so a record built on more labour carries more of the mean. Dividing instead by the number of records would be an unweighted mean of per-record ratios.

B: Combination method: ratio of sums.

C: Levels and operations.

D: Never pooled. Different species; different products; different breed types; milk herd-windows under different suckling regimes; growth herd-windows under different weighing methods; windows of different lengths in continuous systems; logged labour with recalled labour; measured output with recalled, Fallback-sourced or below-floor output; Trial / Station animals.

E: Deduplication and coverage. De-duplicate on the herd-window key, the persistent farmer identifier with the species, the product and the window's start and end dates, and within a herd-window on KPI-O24's animal-period record key, from Project area level upward. Report coverage and precision with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands: 16.5 % or below released without qualification, above 16.5 % to 33.3 % released flagged, above 33.3 % not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one de-duplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above, and a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Include herd-windows with a complete labour record for the window and, for milk and eggs, an output record for every animal on its days present; for growth, an output record for every animal with a closing weight, the gain numerator being conditioned on a closing weight as KPI-O24 conditions it while the labour denominator covers every animal present, the exit rate reported with the value. A herd-window missing the labour record or the output records so defined is excluded rather than imputed, and the number excluded is reported alongside the value. Each activity carries an activity status, performed and recorded, performed and not recorded, or not performed: a zero enters only through not performed, and an absent line is performed and not recorded, which excludes the herd-window. A herd-window with any line flagged recalled is excluded from the logged figure and counted with the reason; it enters the recall series only where the fallback conditions in Data source hold, which a household's own late card line does not. A herd-window whose milk includes a lactation below KPI-O24's floor, or any recalled or Fallback-sourced output, is excluded from the logged figure in the same way and reported separately, as KPI-O24 reports below-floor lactations. A lactation still running at the window's end is judged on its span inside the window, on the floor's interval condition alone: it is below the floor where more than 90 days separate consecutive tests, the first test from the window's start or an observed calving, whichever is later, or the last test from the window's end; one with no test inside the window is below the floor where more than 90 days separate the window's end from the window's start or an observed calving, whichever is later. Where herd composition changed during the window, report the turnover and the exit rate KPI-O24 requires, since a denominator of person-days over a changing herd is not comparable with one over a stable herd. Labour CIMMYT itself engages is outside this indicator.
limitations: Livestock labour resists clean attribution. It is continuous, often shared across species, and frequently performed by household members alongside other tasks, so shared episodes are more common here than in the crop thread, and the hours excluded because the line did not separate them are reported with every value; the output is not reduced with them, which biases the ratio upward. On a dual-purpose herd each product carries all the herd's labour, which biases each product's ratio downward.
Recalled hours are not measured hours, and the gap is wider for continuous tasks than for discrete seasonal ones.
The ratio moves for two reasons, output rising or labour falling, and is read alongside the output indicator KPI-O24 rather than instead of it.

Household labour is counted in hours, not valued. Valuation belongs to KPI-OC63, the gross margin indicator in the Income & livelihoods pathway, which records the wage rate, its source and its reference period with the value.

Women's and children's livestock labour is systematically under-reported in household surveys, which biases the denominator downward and the ratio upward. Sex disaggregation of hours is offered as an optional cut for exactly this reason.
Averaging record-level ratios would be a different quantity. The two totals are retained alongside the ratio so an institutional figure can be rebuilt from them.
subMetrics:
Output, person-days, the window length, the hired, household and unpaid non-household split and its age-band split, and the hours of shared episodes excluded, are each retained and reported alongside the ratio. An institutional figure is recomputed from the components rather than averaged from project ratios.

Relationship to other indicators. KPI-O24 supplies the numerator and the animal record. The crop labour-productivity indicator carries the crop enterprise, which is never pooled with this one. KPI-OC62 carries change and temporal stability for both enterprises. KPI-I06 admits labour productivity as one of the measures on which a farmer can qualify. KPI-OC63, gross margin, in the Income & livelihoods pathway, values the labour this indicator counts in hours.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.

sheetStewardDataRoles: Collection: trained enumerators and technicians. Validation and calculation: the project's MEAL role, using the formulas in Calculation method. Approval and reporting: per the project's own reporting line to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.

name: Change in crop yield and its temporal stability
resultsLevel: Outcome. The change and its temporal stability are a change in performance among the producers measured, which is what the CIMMYT MEAL Framework defines the outcome level by (Section 2.3). It is computed from the output series beneath it and is never derived from a single measured level.
primaryObjective: PO3. Contributing: PO2, PO4.
cgiarImpactArea: Nutrition, Health & Food Security
sdgTarget: Target 2.3
otherFrameworks: None
definition: Two quantities computed from one series of yields (KPI-O23) for a single crop, measurement level and population, across at least two consecutive seasons for the change, released flagged as a short series at two and without the short-series flag from three, and at least four for stability: the change between the reference season and the latest, and the temporal stability of the series, reported as an absolute and a relative measure, which is how consistent yield has been across those seasons. Both are reported.
rationale: Answers whether yield in CIMMYT intervention areas is rising and whether it is becoming more or less reliable. A single season's yield is a level; only a series carries information about performance, because weather variation typically dominates short-run change. Both quantities are reported because a rise in mean yield accompanied by a fall in stability is a different result from a rise in both. Contributes to the productivity impact, KPI-I06, in the results chain, and does not supply its value: KPI-I06 counts farmers whose own productivity rose, which is a per-farmer test rather than a population mean and answers a different question.
projectSpecificApplication:
How this project applies the institutional indicator: the crop, the geography, the seasons in the series, and the measurement level. Scope only; the unit, measurement basis and calculation method are unchanged.

Example: "Change in maize yield and its temporal stability across the 2022 to 2025 seasons in the Central Rift Valley under CIMMYT intervention, at Farm / Plot level."
projectSpecificRationale: States why this project claims a change rather than reporting a level, and the decision the change informs. Example: a project reports it because its funder contracted an improvement over a stated baseline, not a yield figure.
projectTypesNotApplicable: digital agriculture and AI unless the project runs its own ground measurement of yield
any project shorter than two seasons whatever its type
projectTypesRaw:
Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science; digital agriculture and AI unless the project runs its own ground measurement of yield; and any project shorter than two seasons whatever its type, which reports KPI-O23 alone.
unit: Change: metric tonnes per hectare (t/ha) to two decimal places, and percentage of the reference value, both reported. The per-hectare basis is KPI-O23's assessment area at the level reported. The change is computed from KPI-O23's seasonal means, which that method produces in kilograms per hectare; divide by 1,000 for the reported value.
directionOfChange: Increase, for the change and for relative stability. A rising change means yield grew against its reference value, and a rising relative stability means the series varies less around its own mean. Absolute stability, the standard deviation in t/ha, carries no direction of its own: it scales with the level as well as with the variability, and it is read against the level and never as a result in itself.
disaggregationRequired: Measurement level; crop; irrigation regime (rainfed / irrigated); cropping system (sole crop or intercrop).
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: Variety, for seed systems and deployment ² and breeding and varietal development ⁴ projects. Local is a valid value where the material is an unidentified landrace.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Sex of plot manager, per Doss & Kieran (2014); age band of the plot manager; farm size class, with the bands stated, for example under 1 ha, 1 to 2 ha and 2 to 5 ha, or the national classification where one is in use; agroecological zone, with the classification stated; variety. Cropping season is not a cut here. It is part of the pooling domain, so a project measuring two seasons reports two series rather than one series split in two; on KPI-O23, where the value is a single measured level, season is available as a cut.
unitOfObservation: Reported at every level of KPI-O23, Trial / Station, Farm / Plot, Household, Project area, Regional / Aggregated and CIMMYT-wide, for every level at which the project holds a series of at least two measured seasons.
calculationSummary:
Both quantities are computed from one series of KPI-O23 seasonal means, and on the panel route the change's two endpoint means are recomputed over the farmers measured at both. Every rule on that sheet about moisture basis, weighting and excluded plots applies before anything here is computed, in three steps.

First, compute the change, between the reference season and the latest:

On the panel route both means are computed over the farmers measured in both the reference and the latest season, so a farmer who entered or left the panel between them does not move the change.

Report both; a percentage alone conceals the base.

The change is released on a tiered rule. From three or more measured seasons it is released without the short-series flag. At exactly two it is released flagged, carrying a short-series flag which states that two points cannot separate a trend from noise; the flag travels with the value wherever the value is reported. Below two measured seasons no change is computed.

Second, compute the temporal stability, across the seasons in the window, as two measures:

Absolute stability is the variability of the series in the unit of the quantity. Relative stability is the inverse of the coefficient of variation, so a higher value is a more stable series and the measure is scale free, which allows comparison across crops and sites. Report the mean, the standard deviation and the number of seasons alongside both.

Both are reported, and neither alone is sufficient. Neither is free of the level, and they fail in opposite cases: where every value scales by the same factor the standard deviation scales with it and relative stability is unchanged, and where the mean rises and the season-to-season spread does not, the regularity Knapp & van der Heijden (2018) report under Taylor's power law, relative stability rises with no change in variability, so a production gain can appear as a stability gain. Reporting both separates the two effects, and the same study found the two measures disagreeing on the same data, one significant and the other not.

Stability requires four seasons. With two or three, report the change on the tiered rule above and state that stability is not computed: a standard deviation from three values has two degrees of freedom and is neither released as a stability figure nor used as a floor, and the source of this measure admitted only series of four years or more for that reason. The measure follows the treatment of yield stability in Knapp & van der Heijden (2018). KPI-OC25 applies the same statistic to livestock; the measure is general and assumes nothing about what is measured, and its use for livestock rests on the properties of the statistic, with the crop study as the precedent. Use the sample standard deviation, with n − 1 in the denominator, and state it, since at four seasons the choice still moves the value materially. The measure is undefined where the standard deviation is zero; report the series in that case.

Third, test whether the change is detectable. Where the series was assembled from more than one project, and those projects used different protocols, the applicable error is that of the pooled season means rather than of any single protocol. Where it cannot be computed from the pooled records, use the error of the coarsest protocol in the series as a conservative bound and state which was done. A difference smaller than the measurement error of the method that produced it is not evidence of change. A change is detectable only where it exceeds both the measurement error of the difference, built from the protocol evidence on the KPI-O23 sheet, and the season-to-season variation of the series itself, which is the sample standard deviation (n − 1) of the seasonal means in the window. The variation limb applies from four seasons, the length at which that standard deviation is a released stability figure; at two or three seasons the change is tested against the error of the difference alone. Where it fails either test, report no detectable change, with the value shown. Where the documented protocol error is a mean absolute error, as the crop-cut evidence on KPI-O23 is, it is used as the floor as if it were a standard error, which makes the floor approximate in a direction that is not known: for a purely random error a mean absolute error is about four-fifths of the standard error, which sets the floor low, and any systematic component it contains raises the floor; the project states which crop-cut design its own plot geometry is treated as. The first limb compares the change with the error of the difference: where both values were measured under one protocol with independent errors, the protocol error of one value multiplied by the square root of two, and, for two values carrying different documented errors, the square root of the sum of their squares. On the panel route, where the two endpoint means pool more than one farmer, the error of the difference is instead the standard error of the change estimated over the farmers measured at both endpoints, on the same estimator as the means; it carries sampling error and random measurement error together, and the protocol error is not added to it. A series whose yields came from whole-plot harvest and whose endpoint means do not pool more than one farmer carries no documented error, so its change is tested on the variation limb alone, and at two or three seasons is released untested; the value states that the first limb was not applied. The protocol error to compare against is the error of the quantity being compared: a difference between two means over many plots carries a smaller error than a single plot measurement does, and using a single-plot error here would suppress real gains. KPI-I06 applies the two-limb form on the panel route only.
dataSource: All other source roles are inherited, not restated. This indicator is computed from KPI-O23 values, so whatever that sheet admits for a season value is admitted here through it, on the same conditions, and whatever it rules out cannot enter here. Nothing is drawn from a source that did not first pass KPI-O23.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: The seasons in the window, the level, whether the panel is balanced, the protocol used in each season, and any protocol change.
collectionInstrument: None of its own; the instrument is KPI-O23's. What this indicator adds is continuity: the same crop, irrigation regime, level and protocol across every season in the window, protocol here including the drying method, with plot and farmer identifiers carried through so the panel can be constructed. A protocol change mid-window produces an apparent yield change indistinguishable from a real one. A protocol change that cannot be avoided is recorded, and the series is reported in two segments. A switch of drying method is such a change: fallback drying understates moisture and overstates dry yield, so a mid-window switch manufactures an apparent gain or loss. A series never mixes drying methods across its seasons.
collectionFrequency: Every season in the window, from KPI-O23
reportingFrequency: Annually, on a rolling window. Consecutive annual values are not independent observations. Successive windows overlap in all but roughly one season of their span, so they are overlapping estimates of one evolving series. A run of rising annual values is not a run of confirmations.
referencePeriod: Consecutive means consecutive within one season. Where the national cropping calendar defines more than one season a year, the window runs across the same season in successive years, Spring-Summer 2022 to Spring-Summer 2025 and not a mixture, and the season label recorded on KPI-O23 is what the window is built on. A project reporting both seasons reports two series, never one. A window of at least two consecutive cropping seasons for the change, released flagged as a short series at two and without the short-series flag from three, and at least four for stability, ending in the reporting year
baselineRequired: Yes, by construction: the reference season is the baseline. Where the project has no measured season before its intervention began, the change is labelled as measured from the first season observed rather than from a pre-intervention baseline.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One crop, one irrigation regime, one cropping system, one measurement level, one cropping season where the national calendar defines more than one, on the series of one population; a series built across two seasons of the year cannot say whether the season or the year moved, which is why the season is a domain dimension. Levels widen the set of records the series is built from; they never widen the domain.

B: Combination method: not aggregated; recomputed at each level.

Two routes to a series, and the route is a recorded field. The route travels with every figure computed from the series. A farmer panel follows the same identified farmers, on persistent identifiers, in every season; a series in which the reference-season farmers are not the majority of every season's records is not a panel. A series that changes route mid-window is reported in two segments, like a protocol change. At Regional / Aggregated and CIMMYT-wide level the recomputed series is a region series by construction, declared as such, with that route's composition reporting; it is never presented as a panel result, and a panel-route change is never averaged into it.

A region and crop series is a repeated cross-section: each season's value is the KPI-O23 mean for a stated frame, the plots of one crop and one irrigation regime within a stated reporting area, and the frame statement, the sampling design of each round, which is a probability sample from a stated frame designed and estimated per FAO (2018), Handbook on crop statistics, Ch. 3, and each round's achieved composition (plot count, farm count, and area shares by the project's stated strata) are reported with the series. Its change is the change in that area's production of the crop, whoever farms it; entry, exit and crop-switching are part of that change, not error. With every region-route change, also report the change recomputed at reference-season area shares by the stated strata, so the composition component is visible. Where the two differ by more than the detectability band, the composition-adjusted change is the reported figure and the raw change is reported beside it: a difference that large means the change is substantially compositional, and reporting the raw figure as the result would attribute to performance what is a change in who was measured. Where rounds were not drawn by a stated design from a stated frame, the series is labelled a monitoring series with composition unquantified, and its change is not released as a change in the area's yield.

The two routes are never pooled into one figure, because they answer different questions: one is the change for the same producers, the other the change in the area. Which route. The farmer panel is the route of record where the project can hold one: it supports the stronger claim, and it follows identified farmers as KPI-I06 does. KPI-I06 takes no value computed here: it runs its per-farmer test on each farmer's own series from the output indicators. The region series is the route where a panel is infeasible, and the series states that it is, and why; expected farmer recurrence below the panel floor is sufficient reason. A project holding both declares both; a project reporting KPI-I06 reports its panel-route change alongside any region series. A change and a stability figure are properties of a particular series and are never combined from the changes computed below them. At every level the series is assembled from the KPI-O23 values belonging to that level, and the calculation method is applied to it unchanged. A regional change is computed from regional season means, never from the project changes beneath it.

C: Levels and operations. At each level: take the KPI-O23 values that KPI-O23 reports at that level, one per season in the window, then apply the calculation method; on the panel route the change's two endpoint means are recomputed from KPI-O23's records over the farmers measured at both, as the calculation method states. Also report: whether the same plots were measured in every season, and at Trial / Station the adjusted entry means the series was built from. At Trial / Station a series holds only across cycles whose entries are the same; where a nursery's entries change between cycles, the series is built on the common checks alone and the check set is reported.

D: Never pooled. A farmer-panel series with a region series. Changes computed at a lower level; percentage changes across projects, which weight a small project equally with a large one; series that mix measurement levels, different crops, different irrigation regimes or different cropping systems; series that mix moisture methods across their seasons; series that mix cropping seasons on a calendar that defines more than one; series that mix measured season values with recalled ones.

E: Deduplication and coverage. Inherited from KPI-O23: the series is built from records already de-duplicated there. A record is one farmer's series on the panel route and one round's estimate on the region route. Every season or period value entering a series must itself have been releasable under the parent indicator's Block E. Report the number of seasons in the window, whether the panel is balanced, and the coverage of the reporting area at Regional / Aggregated level and above.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Include seasons with a measured KPI-O23 value at the same level, for the same crop, in the same population.

The detectability test is route-specific. On the panel route both limbs above apply, unchanged. On the region route the comparison is between two round estimates, so the change is tested against the combined standard error of the two rounds alone, the square root of (SE of round 1 squared plus SE of round 2 squared), taken from the uncertainty Block E already collects, and the variation limb does not apply; the protocol error is contained in those standard errors and is not added again. Where the rounds share farmers, which a region series admits whenever the reference-season farmers are not the majority of every round, the two estimates are positively correlated and this form overstates the combined standard error: it is conservative, it biases toward finding no detectable change, and a change it rejects on a partially overlapping series is reported as not established rather than absent. A change inside that band is reported as no detectable change.

Exclude nothing by interpolation: a season with no measurement is a gap, not a zero. State the gap.

Missing so many seasons that fewer than two remain measured: no value is computed. Report the KPI-O23 series instead and say why. With exactly three measured seasons the change is computed and released without the short-series flag and stability is not computed; with exactly two the change is computed and released flagged as a short series and stability is not computed. In both cases state that stability was withheld rather than leaving the field blank. The window is defined over consecutive seasons; a single missing measurement inside it does not break the window, but it leaves the remaining values unevenly spaced, which weakens the stability estimate more than it does the change. State the gap with both quantities.

Repeated observations: one value per crop, level and window. State on the panel route whether the panel is balanced and on the region route each round's achieved composition, that is whether the same plots or producers are measured in every season. A balanced panel supports a much stronger claim than a repeated cross-section, and the two are not presented alike.
limitations: Contribution, not attribution, and less securely than a single-season level. Over a window of two to four seasons weather, prices and policy all move alongside the intervention.

Four seasons is the floor for stability; the change is released from two, flagged. A standard deviation from three values is not an estimate to act on, so a two- or three-season series reports the change with stability withheld and said to be withheld. A two-season change is released flagged: two points cannot separate a trend from noise, and the flag travels with the value. The season count is reported with every value.
A change smaller than measurement error is not a change. Report it as no detectable change rather than as a small gain, or the direction of noise becomes a finding.

Where the variation limb does not apply, a favourable season can read as a gain. On the region route, and on the panel route at two or three seasons, a season-to-season difference, in weather for example, is not separated from the change.

A repeated cross-section is not a panel. Where different plots or producers were measured in different seasons, part of the apparent change is compositional, and the sheet states which design was used.

Change and stability can move in opposite directions, and the pair is the result: a mean gain with falling stability transfers risk to the household, which for a smallholder can be worse than a smaller, steadier gain.

Neither quantity uses the whole series. The change is computed from the two endpoints, so a window whose middle seasons were strong and whose endpoints were ordinary reports a small change; and the stability measure does not separate trend from variability, so a series rising steadily across the window scores lower than a flat one. Read the two together, and against the seasonal series, rather than either alone.
A change is a property of one series and cannot be averaged into a larger one. The season means are retained alongside the change so an institutional figure can be rebuilt from them.
subMetrics: Change and temporal stability, reported together. The stability formulas are the same on both routes, and the route is reported with the figure. On the region route the per-round coefficient of variation is reported alongside, because a stable series of unstable rounds is not a stable system. Stability figures are never compared across routes.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
Temporal stability: Knapp & van der Heijden (2018).

All measurement rules are inherited from KPI-O23, including its methods of record; nothing is restated here.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.

projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; system change and transformation; seed systems and deployment where forage or fodder varieties are the intervention.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development, which at CIMMYT is crop breeding; digital agriculture and AI unless the project runs its own animal measurement; and any project shorter than two production periods whatever its type, which reports KPI-O24 alone.
unit: Change: the species and product unit from KPI-O24, and percentage of the reference value, both reported.
