A rising change means livestock productivity grew against its reference value, and a rising relative stability means the series varies less around its own mean. Absolute stability, the standard deviation in the species and product unit, carries no direction of its own: it scales with the level as well as with the variability, and it is read against the level and never as a result in itself.
disaggregationRequired: Measurement level; species; product; breed type (local, crossbred or exotic); for milk, suckling regime.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Sex of the animal owner, per Doss & Kieran (2014); herd or flock size class; production system; feeding system (grazing, mixed or stall-fed), for projects in which feed is the intervention or an explanatory variable.
unitOfObservation: Reported at every level of KPI-O24, Trial / Station, Farm / Plot, Household, Project area, Regional / Aggregated and CIMMYT-wide, for every level at which the project holds a series of at least two measured production periods.
calculationSummary:
Both quantities are computed from one series of KPI-O24 period means, and on the panel route the change's two endpoint means are recomputed over the farmers measured at both. Every rule on that sheet about units, weighing method, test spacing and excluded animals applies before anything here is computed, in three steps.

First, compute the change, between the reference period and the latest:

On the panel route both means are computed over the farmers measured in both the reference and the latest period, so a farmer who entered or left the panel between them does not move the change.

Report both; a percentage alone conceals the base.

The change is released on a tiered rule. From three or more measured periods it is released without the short-series flag. At exactly two it is released flagged, carrying a short-series flag which states that two points cannot separate a trend from noise; the flag travels with the value wherever the value is reported. Below two measured periods no change is computed.

Second, compute the temporal stability, across the periods in the window, as two measures:

Absolute stability is the variability of the series in the unit of the quantity; because that unit differs by species and product, an absolute figure is never compared across them. Relative stability is the inverse of the coefficient of variation and is scale free, which is what allows one measure to serve crops and livestock despite incommensurable units. Report the mean, the standard deviation and the number of periods alongside both.

Both are reported, and neither alone is sufficient. Neither is free of the level, and they fail in opposite cases: where every value scales by the same factor the standard deviation scales with it and relative stability is unchanged, and where the mean rises and the period-to-period spread does not, the regularity Knapp & van der Heijden (2018) report under Taylor's power law, relative stability rises with no change in variability, so a production gain can appear as a stability gain. Reporting both separates the two effects, and the same study found the two measures disagreeing on the same data, one significant and the other not.

Stability requires four periods. With two or three, report the change on the tiered rule above and state that stability is not computed: a standard deviation from three values has two degrees of freedom and is neither released as a stability figure nor used as a floor. Use the sample standard deviation, with n − 1 in the denominator, and state it, since at four periods the choice still moves the value materially. The measure is undefined where the standard deviation is zero; report the series in that case.

Report the length of each period with the series. A crop season is set by the calendar; a lactation or a growth cycle is not, so variation in period length enters the standard deviation and would otherwise be read as instability in production. The same measure is used for crops on KPI-OC22.

Third, test whether the change is detectable. Where the series was assembled from more than one project, and those projects used different protocols, the applicable error is that of the pooled period means rather than of any single protocol. Where it cannot be computed from the pooled records, use the error of the coarsest protocol in the series as a conservative bound and state which was done. A difference smaller than the measurement error of the method that produced it is not evidence of change. A change is detectable only where it exceeds both the measurement error of the protocol used, which for milk depends on test-day spacing (Migose et al., 2020) and for liveweight on whether a scale or a girth algorithm was used (Goopy et al., 2018), and the period-to-period variation of the series itself, which is the sample standard deviation (n − 1) of the period means in the window. The variation limb applies from four periods, the length at which that standard deviation is a released stability figure; at two or three periods the change is tested against the error of the difference alone. The first limb's error is documented for milk and liveweight only, so on the panel route an egg change whose endpoint means do not pool more than one farmer is tested on the variation limb alone, and at two or three periods is released untested; the value states that the first limb was not applied. Where it fails either test, report no detectable change, with the value shown. The first limb compares the change with the error of the difference: where both values were measured under one protocol with independent errors, the protocol error of one value multiplied by the square root of two, and, for two values carrying different documented errors, the square root of the sum of their squares. On the panel route, where the two endpoint means pool more than one farmer, the error of the difference is instead the standard error of the change estimated over the farmers measured at both endpoints, on the same estimator as the means; it carries sampling error and random measurement error together, and the protocol error is not added to it. The error to compare against is the error of the quantity being compared: a difference between two means over many animals carries a smaller error than a single-animal measurement does. KPI-I06 applies the two-limb form on the panel route only.
dataSource: All other source roles are inherited, not restated. This indicator is computed from KPI-O24 values, so whatever that sheet admits for a production period value is admitted here through it, on the same conditions, and whatever it rules out cannot enter here. Nothing is drawn from a source that did not first pass KPI-O24.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: The periods in the window, the level, whether the panel is balanced, the protocol used in each period, any protocol change, and the herd turnover across the window.
collectionInstrument: None of its own; the instrument is KPI-O24's. What this indicator adds is continuity: the same species, product, level and protocol across every period in the window, protocol here including the weighing method, the test-day spacing and the suckling regime, with animal and farmer identifiers carried through so the panel can be constructed and turnover can be seen. A change of weighing method or test-day spacing mid-window produces an apparent productivity change indistinguishable from a real one, on the same reasoning that governs drying method on the crop thread. A protocol change that cannot be avoided is recorded, and the series is reported in two segments.
collectionFrequency: Every production period in the window, from KPI-O24
reportingFrequency: Annually, on a rolling window. Consecutive annual values are not independent observations. Successive windows overlap in all but roughly one period of their span, so they are overlapping estimates of one evolving series. A run of rising annual values is not a run of confirmations, and the values are never treated as repeated measurements of the same quantity.
referencePeriod: Consecutive means consecutive production periods, not calendar seasons, the livestock cycle being set by the animal rather than by the cropping calendar; the crop series at KPI-OC22 and the crop half of KPI-OC62 carry a season rule that does not apply here. A window of at least two consecutive production periods for the change, released flagged as a short series at two and without the short-series flag from three, and at least four for stability, ending in the reporting year. For a single animal a production period is its own cycle, a lactation, a laying period or a growth cycle, so its window can span several calendar years for dairy cattle and camels; the span follows the cycle and is not capped. At every level that pools animals a period is one reporting year's KPI-O24 value, which pools the cycles ending in that year. The actual span is stated with every value, in both periods and calendar years.
baselineRequired: Yes, by construction: the reference period is the baseline. Where the project has no measured period before its intervention began, the change is labelled as measured from the first period observed rather than from a pre-intervention baseline.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One species, one product, one breed type, one measurement level, for milk one suckling regime, on the series of one population. There is no season dimension here, unlike the crop series at KPI-OC22: a lactation or a growth cycle is set by the animal and not by the cropping calendar, and the length of each production period is reported with the series instead. Levels widen the set of records the series is built from; they never widen the domain.

B: Combination method: not aggregated; recomputed at each level.

Two routes to a series, and the route is a recorded field. The route travels with every figure computed from the series. A farmer panel follows the same identified farmers, on persistent identifiers, in every production period; a series in which the reference-period farmers are not the majority of every period's records is not a panel. A series that changes route mid-window is reported in two segments, like a protocol change. At Regional / Aggregated and CIMMYT-wide level the recomputed series is a region series by construction, declared as such, with that route's composition reporting; it is never presented as a panel result, and a panel-route change is never averaged into it.

A region and species series is a repeated cross-section, and a round is one reporting year of recording on a probability sample of holdings drawn at the start of that round: KPI-O24's denominator is exposure, in the unit its species table fixes, which accumulates across a period and cannot be observed at a single survey visit. A single test-day yield or a recalled period total is a different quantity from the parent's and is not a round. Each period's value is the KPI-O24 mean for a stated frame, a defined area, species and product, and the frame statement, the sampling design of each round, which is a probability sample from a stated frame, and each round's achieved composition (animal count, herd count, and exposure shares by the project's stated strata) are reported with the series. Its change is the change in what the area's herds of that species produce, whoever keeps them; entry, exit and herd turnover are part of that change, not error. With every region-route change, also report the change recomputed at reference-period exposure shares by the stated strata, so the composition component is visible. Where the two differ by more than the detectability band, the composition-adjusted change is the reported figure and the raw change is reported beside it: a difference that large means the change is substantially compositional, and reporting the raw figure as the result would attribute to performance what is a change in who was measured. Where rounds were not drawn by a stated design from a stated frame, the series is labelled a monitoring series with composition unquantified, and its change is not released as a change in the area's livestock productivity. A project taking this route has its first round reviewed before the series is relied on.

The two routes are never pooled into one figure, because they answer different questions: one is the change for the same producers, the other the change in the area. Which route. The farmer panel is the route of record where the project can hold one: it supports the stronger claim, and it follows identified farmers as KPI-I06 does. KPI-I06 takes no value computed here: it runs its per-farmer test on each farmer's own series from the output indicators. The region series is the route where a panel is infeasible, and the series states that it is, and why; expected farmer recurrence below the panel floor is sufficient reason. A project holding both declares both; a project reporting KPI-I06 reports its panel-route change alongside any region series. A change and a stability figure are properties of a particular series and are never combined from the changes computed below them. At every level the series is assembled from the KPI-O24 values belonging to that level, and the calculation method is applied to it unchanged. A regional change is computed from regional period means, never from the project changes beneath it.

C: Levels and operations. At each level: take the KPI-O24 values that KPI-O24 reports at that level, one per period in the window, then apply the calculation method; on the panel route the change's two endpoint means are recomputed from KPI-O24's records over the farmers measured at both, as the calculation method states. Also report: whether the same animals were measured in every period, the herd turnover across the window, the length of each period, and the parity distribution of the animals behind each period mean, or for growth their age distribution.

D: Never pooled. A farmer-panel series with a region series. Changes computed at a lower level; percentage changes across projects, which weight a small project equally with a large one; series that mix measurement levels, different species, different products or breed types; series that mix weighing methods, test-day spacing or suckling regimes across their periods; series that mix measured period values with recalled ones.

E: Deduplication and coverage. Inherited from KPI-O24: the series is built from records already de-duplicated there. A record is one farmer's series on the panel route and one round's estimate on the region route. Every period value entering a series must itself have been releasable under the parent indicator's Block E. Report the number of periods in the window, on the panel route whether the panel is balanced and on the region route each round's achieved composition, and the coverage of the reporting area at Regional / Aggregated level and above. Report the calendar span with the period count.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Include periods with a measured KPI-O24 value at the same level, for the same species and product, in the same population.

The detectability test is route-specific. On the panel route the limbs above apply, unchanged. On the region route the comparison is between two round estimates, so the change is tested against the combined standard error of the two rounds alone, the square root of (SE of round 1 squared plus SE of round 2 squared), taken from the uncertainty Block E already collects, and the variation limb does not apply; the protocol error is contained in those standard errors and is not added again. Where the rounds share farmers, which a region series admits whenever the reference-period farmers are not the majority of every round, the two estimates are positively correlated and this form overstates the combined standard error: it is conservative, it biases toward finding no detectable change, and a change it rejects on a partially overlapping series is reported as not established rather than absent. A change inside that band is reported as no detectable change.

Exclude nothing by interpolation: a period with no measurement is a gap, not a zero. State the gap.

Missing so many periods that fewer than two remain measured: no value is computed. Report the KPI-O24 series instead and say why. With exactly three measured periods the change is computed and released without the short-series flag and stability is not computed; with exactly two the change is computed and released flagged as a short series and stability is not computed. In both cases state that stability was withheld rather than leaving the field blank. The window is defined over consecutive periods; a single missing measurement inside it does not break the window, but it leaves the remaining values unevenly spaced, which weakens the stability estimate more than it does the change. State the gap with both quantities.

Repeated observations: one value per species, product, level and window. State whether the panel is balanced. For livestock this matters more than for crops: herds turn over through sale, death and culling, so an unbalanced series can show a rise driven entirely by which animals left.
limitations: Contribution, not attribution, and less securely than a single-period level. Over a window of two to four periods, feed prices, disease outbreaks, rainfall and market conditions all move alongside the intervention.

Herd turnover can produce the whole result. Animals sold or culled are not a random sample of the herd, so an unbalanced series can show a rise driven by which animals left rather than by any animal producing more. Report turnover with the value.

Four periods is the floor for stability; the change is released from two, flagged. A two- or three-period series reports the change with stability withheld and said to be withheld. A two-period change is released flagged: two points cannot separate a trend from noise. The period count is reported with every value.

Parity and age structure can produce the result on a balanced panel. Milk yield rises over the early parities and daily gain falls with age, so the same animals measured across three or four periods drift without any change in management; the parity or age distribution is reported with each period mean and a change is read against it.
A change smaller than measurement error is not a change. Report it as no detectable change rather than as a small gain.

Where the variation limb does not apply, a favourable period can read as a gain. On the region route, and on the panel route at two or three periods, a period-to-period difference, in weather for example, is not separated from the change.
Change and stability can move in opposite directions, and the pair is the result: a herd producing more on average but less predictably is not straightforwardly better off.

Neither quantity uses the whole series. The change is taken between two endpoints, so a window whose middle periods were strong and whose endpoints were ordinary reports a small change; and the stability measure does not separate trend from variability, so a series rising steadily scores lower than a flat one. Read the two together, and against the period series, rather than either alone.
A change is a property of one series and cannot be averaged into a larger one. The period means are retained alongside the change so an institutional figure can be rebuilt from them.
subMetrics: Change and temporal stability, reported together. The stability formulas are the same on both routes, and the route is reported with the figure. On the region route the per-round coefficient of variation is reported alongside, because a stable series of unstable rounds is not a stable system. Stability figures are never compared across routes.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
Temporal stability: the inverse of the coefficient of variation; Knapp & van der Heijden (2018) is the crop precedent; the measure is general and assumes nothing about what is measured, and its use here rests on the properties of the statistic.

All measurement rules are inherited from KPI-O24, including its methods of record; nothing is restated here.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.

name: Change in on-farm labour productivity and its temporal stability
resultsLevel: Outcome. The change and its temporal stability are a change in performance among the producers measured, which is what the CIMMYT MEAL Framework defines the outcome level by (Section 2.3). It is computed from the output series beneath it and is never derived from a single measured level.
primaryObjective: PO3. Contributing: PO2, PO4.
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs
sdgTarget: Target 2.3. Not reportable as indicator 2.3.1, for the reasons given on the output sheets.
otherFrameworks: None.
definition: The change in labour productivity between the first and the latest season or period of a window of at least two measured seasons or production periods, released flagged as a short series at two and without the short-series flag from three, and, where the window reaches four, the temporal stability of the series over it, reported as an absolute and a relative measure. Computed from KPI-O59 and KPI-O60, crop or livestock, on one enterprise, one product, one measurement level and, on the crop enterprise, one irrigation regime and one cropping system, on the livestock enterprise one breed type, one window length in continuous systems and, for milk, one suckling regime. The crop and livestock enterprises are never pooled into a single series.
rationale: A level says where a producer is; a change says whether the intervention moved them, and stability says whether the gain can be relied on. A labour-productivity gain that appears in one season and does not persist into the next has not changed the return on the household's time. The indicator mirrors the crop and livestock change indicators exactly, so that the pathway reports change and stability for whichever productivity measures a project holds.
projectSpecificApplication:
How this project applies the institutional indicator: the thread, the product, the geography, the window and the measurement levels observed. Scope only; the unit, measurement basis and calculation method are unchanged.

Example: "Change in labour productivity in maize production in the Central Rift Valley under CIMMYT intervention, seasons 2023 to 2025, at Farm / Plot level."
projectSpecificRationale: States why this project claims a change in labour return, and the decision it informs. Example: a project reports it where its theory of change rests on labour saved rather than output raised.
projectTypesApply: on the livestock enterprise only where forage or fodder varieties are the intervention
projectTypesNotApplicable: digital agriculture and AI unless the project runs its own ground measurement of labour
any project shorter than two seasons
or two of its declared windows on the livestock enterprise
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; system change and transformation; seed systems and deployment, on the livestock enterprise only where forage or fodder varieties are the intervention, as KPI-O60 admits it.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; digital agriculture and AI unless the project runs its own ground measurement of labour; and any project shorter than two seasons, or two of its declared windows on the livestock enterprise, whatever its type, which reports the output indicator alone.
unit: Change: the enterprise unit (kilograms per person-day, or the product's physical unit per person-day) and percentage of the reference value, both reported with the series they came from. Temporal stability is reported alongside them, on the same series.
directionOfChange: Increase, for the change and for relative stability. A rising change means labour productivity grew over the window, and a rising relative stability means the series varies less around its own mean. Absolute stability, the standard deviation in the unit of the enterprise, carries no direction of its own: it scales with the level as well as with the variability, and it is never compared across enterprises, whose units are incommensurable. As with KPI-O59, a rise in the change can come from labour withdrawn rather than output gained.
disaggregationRequired: Measurement level; enterprise (crop or livestock); product; irrigation regime (rainfed / irrigated) and cropping system (sole crop or intercrop) on the crop thread; breed type and, for milk, suckling regime on the livestock thread.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Sex of the plot or herd manager, per Doss & Kieran (2014); sex of each worker on the labour line, reported as a split of hours; farm size class, with the bands stated, for example under 1 ha, 1 to 2 ha and 2 to 5 ha, or the national classification where one is in use; agroecological zone, with the classification stated; mechanisation status.
unitOfObservation: Reported at every level of KPI-O59 and KPI-O60, Farm / Plot, Household, Project area, Regional / Aggregated and CIMMYT-wide, for every level at which the project holds a series of at least two measured seasons or periods.
calculationSummary:
First, assemble the series at the level being reported, from the labour-productivity output values for that thread, product and level, one value per season or period. On the panel route the population must be the same across the window, and where it is not, say so, report the share of the original population retained and compute the reference and latest values over the farmers measured at both; on the region route each round's composition is reported as Block B requires.

Second, compute the change between the reference value and the latest value:

Report both; a percentage alone conceals the base.

The change is released on a tiered rule. From three or more measured seasons or periods it is released without the short-series flag. At exactly two it is released flagged, carrying a short-series flag which states that two points cannot separate a trend from noise; the flag travels with the value wherever the value is reported. Below two, no change is computed.

Third, compute the temporal stability of the series as two measures, using the sample standard deviation with n − 1:

Absolute stability is the variability in the unit of the quantity and is never compared across enterprises, whose units are incommensurable. Relative stability is scale-free, which is what allows one measure to serve both enterprises.

Both are reported, and neither alone is sufficient. Neither is free of the level, and they fail in opposite cases: where every value scales by the same factor the standard deviation scales with it and relative stability is unchanged, and where the mean rises and the season-to-season spread does not, the regularity Knapp & van der Heijden (2018) report under Taylor's power law, relative stability rises with no change in variability, so a production gain can appear as a stability gain. Reporting both separates the two effects, and the same study found the two measures disagreeing on the same data, one significant and the other not.

Stability requires four seasons or periods. With two or three, report the change on the tiered rule above and state that stability is not computed. The measure is undefined where the standard deviation is zero; report the series in that case.

Fourth, apply the detectability test. A change counts as a change only where it exceeds both the measurement error of the difference and the season-to-season variation of the series itself, which is the sample standard deviation (n − 1) of the series in the window. The variation limb applies from four seasons or periods, the length at which that standard deviation is a released stability figure; at two or three the change is tested against the error of the difference alone. A change inside that band is reported as no detectable change, not as a small gain. The protocol error of a logged labour series is documented for its numerator, eggs and whole-plot harvest apart, and not for its denominator, and a recall series is tested on the same basis, so the first limb is applied as a lower bound, and the error compared against is the error of the quantity being compared. On the crop enterprise, where the yield came from crop cuts, the numerator's error is KPI-O23's crop-cut error, documented per hectare: its random component where the documented figure separates one, and the whole figure where it does not. Multiply it by the harvested area of the plot, or by the mean harvested area of the n plots the level is built on, to give the numerator's kilograms. Divide by that plot's person-days, or by the mean person-days per plot at the reference value and never by the level's total, to express it in the ratio's unit. Divide by the square root of n for a level built on n plots under one protocol, which on the mean harvested area understates the floor where plots differ in size, and multiply by the square root of two for a difference of two values under one protocol. A change below that floor is no detectable change. A series whose yields came from whole-plot harvest carries no documented numerator error, so its change is tested on the variation limb alone, and at two or three seasons is released untested; the value states that the first limb was not applied and carries no provisional flag. On the livestock enterprise the numerator's error is the protocol error of KPI-O24's output, the one KPI-OC25 tests a livestock productivity change against, which for milk depends on test-day spacing and for liveweight on the weighing method: it is converted to the error of the herd-window's output, the conversion stated with the value, then expressed in the ratio's unit, divided by the square root of n and multiplied by the square root of two as on the crop enterprise, with herd-windows in place of plots. A change so tested, on either enterprise, is released carrying a provisional flag, which states that the floor is the numerator's error alone and which is raised once a denominator error is documented; the provisional flag is distinct from the short-series flag: the tiered release above stands, and a change released without the short-series flag from three seasons or periods still carries the provisional one. KPI-OC25 documents no protocol error for eggs, so on the panel route an egg change is tested on the variation limb alone, and at two or three periods is released untested; the value states that the first limb was not applied and carries no provisional flag.

The detectability test is route-specific. On the panel route the limbs apply as stated above. On the region route the comparison is between two round estimates, so the change is tested against the combined standard error of the two rounds alone, the square root of (SE of round 1 squared plus SE of round 2 squared), taken from the uncertainty Block E already collects, and the variation limb does not apply; the protocol error is contained in those standard errors and is not added again. Where the rounds share farmers, which a region series admits whenever the reference farmers are not the majority of every round, the two estimates are positively correlated and this form overstates the combined standard error: it is conservative, it biases toward finding no detectable change, and a change it rejects on a partially overlapping series is reported as not established rather than absent. A change inside that band is reported as no detectable change.

Fifth, report the change and the stability together with the series they came from. Retain the season or period values and their components, not only the change: an institutional figure is recomputed from the series, and a project that reports only a change cannot contribute to one.

The two routes are never pooled into one figure, because they answer different questions: one is the change for the same producers, the other the change in the area. Which route. The farmer panel is the route of record where the project can hold one: it supports the stronger claim, and it follows identified farmers as KPI-I06 does. KPI-I06 takes no value computed here: it runs its per-farmer test on each farmer's own series from the output indicators. The region series is the route where a panel is infeasible, and the series states that it is, and why; expected farmer recurrence below the panel floor is sufficient reason. A project holding both declares both; a project reporting KPI-I06 reports its panel-route change alongside any region series. A change and a stability figure are properties of a particular series and are never combined from the changes computed below them. At every level the series is assembled from the KPI-O59 and KPI-O60 values belonging to that level, and the calculation method is applied to it unchanged. A regional change is computed from regional season or period means, never from the project changes beneath it.

C: Levels and operations. At each level: take the KPI-O59 or KPI-O60 values reported at that level, one per season or period in the window, then apply the calculation method; on the panel route the reference and latest values are recomputed from those sheets' records over the farmers measured at both, as the calculation method states. Also report: whether the same plots or animals were measured throughout, and the hired, household and unpaid non-household labour split with its age-band split.

D: Never pooled. A farmer-panel series with a region series. Changes computed at a lower level; percentage changes across projects, which weight a small project equally with a large one; series that mix measurement levels, the crop and livestock enterprises with each other, irrigation regimes or cropping systems on the crop enterprise, breed types, window lengths in continuous systems or, for milk, suckling regimes and, for growth, weighing methods on the livestock enterprise; series that mix logged labour with recalled labour, or measured output with recalled output; series that mix cropping seasons on a crop enterprise whose calendar defines more than one.

E: Deduplication and coverage. Inherited from KPI-O59 and KPI-O60: the series is built from records already de-duplicated there. A record is one farmer's series on the panel route and one round's estimate on the region route. Every season or period value entering a series must itself have been releasable under the parent indicator's Block E. Report the number of seasons or periods in the window, on the panel route whether the panel is balanced and on the region route each round's achieved composition, and the coverage of the reporting area at Regional / Aggregated level and above.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Include series with at least two measured seasons or periods on the same population, enterprise, product and level for the change, and at least four for stability. With exactly three the change is computed and released without the short-series flag and stability is withheld; with exactly two the change is computed and released flagged as a short series and stability is withheld. In both cases the sheet says so rather than leaving the field blank. The window is defined over consecutive seasons or periods; a single missing measurement inside it does not break the window, but it leaves the remaining values unevenly spaced, which weakens the stability estimate more than it does the change. State the gap with both quantities. Series shorter than two are not reported here; the project reports the output indicator alone.
limitations: Stability is withheld below four seasons or periods, and at four it is imprecise: it is read as a comparator within a project, not as a precise quantity.

Attrition may bias the change, and the direction is not assumed. Producers who leave a panel are not a random subset, but a difference in who remains does not by itself bias the estimate. The share of the original population retained is reported with every value, with the comparison of those retained against those lost that KPI-I06 requires.

The change moves for two reasons, output rising or labour falling, and is read alongside the yield or livestock-productivity change rather than instead of it. A rise driven entirely by mechanisation is a real gain in the return to labour and not a gain in production, and a difference between plots or systems can reflect access to machinery suited to the plot or the cropping system rather than management.

Where the variation limb does not apply, a favourable season or period can read as a gain. On the region route, and on the panel route at two or three seasons or periods, a season-to-season or period-to-period difference, in weather for example, is not separated from the change.

Weather and price shocks enter the series without being attributable to the intervention, which is what the detectability test exists to guard against and why the series is retained alongside the change.

On the livestock enterprise the excluded share moves the change. KPI-O60 excludes the hours of a shared episode the line did not separate and keeps the output, which biases the ratio upward; where the share of hours excluded differs between the first and the latest period, the change moves with it, and the excluded hours reported with every KPI-O60 value are read beside the change.
A change is a property of one series and cannot be averaged into a larger one. The season or period values are retained alongside the change so an institutional figure can be rebuilt from them.
subMetrics:
The series, its mean, its standard deviation, and the components of each season or period value are retained and reported with the change. The stability formulas are the same on both routes, and the route is reported with the figure. On the region route the per-round coefficient of variation is reported alongside, because a stable series of unstable rounds is not a stable system. Stability figures are never compared across routes.

Relationship to other indicators. KPI-O59 and KPI-O60 supply the series. KPI-OC22 and KPI-OC25 carry the same construct for yield and livestock productivity; the three are never pooled. KPI-I06 counts farmers whose own productivity rose and admits labour productivity as one qualifying measure, which is a per-farmer test rather than a population mean and answers a different question.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: Content owner: the CIMMYT MEAL unit, with the farming-systems lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Collection: inherited from the output indicators. Validation and calculation: the project's MEAL role, using the formulas in Calculation method. Approval and reporting: per the project's own reporting line to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 7 · Productivity — Reference sheet KPI-OC62

name: Change in on-farm post-harvest loss of target grain crops
resultsLevel: Outcome. A reduction in the share of the harvest lost is a change in practice and performance among the households measured, which is what the CIMMYT MEAL Framework defines the outcome level by (Section 2.3). The two loss rates the change is computed from are reported with it, as its endpoints; neither endpoint on its own is the outcome.
primaryObjective: PO3. Contributing: PO2, PO4.
cgiarImpactArea: Nutrition, Health & Food Security
sdgTarget: Target 12.3
otherFrameworks: None
definition: For one target grain crop and one population, the post-harvest loss rate, which is the share of the household's harvest of the crop lost on the farm between harvest and the end of the farm storage period, and the change in that rate between a baseline season and the latest season. Loss is the decrease in the weight of grain available for human consumption, measured at a stated moisture content, so that weight lost to drying is not counted as loss (FAO, 2018). It covers five on-farm stages: threshing or shelling, cleaning or winnowing, drying, on-farm transport, and storage. Losses in the harvest operation itself are a sub-metric, outside the rate. Grain cereals and pulses only.
rationale: Answers whether less of what assisted farmers harvest is lost before it can be eaten, sold or kept as seed. Grain lost after harvest is production whose cost the household has already borne and which it cannot use, so a lower loss rate raises the quantity available from the same yield. The indicator measures the practice of handling and keeping grain: drying, threshing, the storage structure, protectants, and the management of moulds and mycotoxins, rather than conditions outside the farmer's control. Contributes to per-capita staple food availability, KPI-OC13, in the results chain, where storage and handling losses are among the quantities deducted in the household's staple food balance, and does not supply its value.
projectSpecificApplication:
How this project applies the institutional indicator: the crop, the geography, the storage period, the stages measured and the measurement route. Scope only; the unit, measurement basis and calculation method are unchanged.

Example: "Change in on-farm post-harvest loss of maize among assisted households in Mashonaland East, 2025 baseline season to 2027 season, storage period of eight months after harvest, physical measurement route."
projectSpecificRationale: States the project decision or funder commitment the change serves. Example: a project distributing hermetic storage bags reports it against a contracted reduction in storage loss, from a baseline of 10 per cent to 7 per cent of the harvest, and uses the stage split to decide whether the next season's support moves to drying.
projectTypesApply: breeding and varietal development where the trait targeted acts after harvest
resistance to storage pests for example
projectTypesNotApplicable: digital agriculture and AI unless the project runs its own household measurement of losses
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; system change and transformation; breeding and varietal development where the trait targeted acts after harvest, resistance to storage pests for example.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science; seed systems and deployment; digital agriculture and AI unless the project runs its own household measurement of losses.
unit: Loss rate: percentage of the household's harvest of the crop, to one decimal place, at each endpoint. Change: percentage points, to one decimal place, latest minus baseline, with the relative change (per cent of the baseline rate) reported beside it. All quantities behind a rate are in kilograms on one moisture basis, dry basis by default, recorded with the value. Rates are ratios of weights on the same basis, so the basis does not move the rate provided it is the same for numerator and denominator.
directionOfChange: Decrease. A falling loss rate means more of the harvest stays available for consumption, sale or seed. The change is latest minus baseline, so an improvement is a negative number of percentage points: a fall from 10.0 to 7.0 per cent is reported as a change of −3.0 percentage points, or −30 per cent of the baseline rate.
disaggregationRequired: Crop; stage (threshing or shelling, cleaning or winnowing, drying, on-farm transport, storage), each reported as its own stage loss rate; storage type, meaning the structure or container the grain was kept in (a traditional granary or crib, woven polypropylene bags, hermetic bags, metal silos, for example), with grain that was never stored reported as its own category; measurement route (physical measurement or farmer declaration). The stage and storage-type cuts are required because a project acts on particular stages, and a change in the rate cannot be read without knowing where in the chain it happened.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: Variety, for breeding and varietal development ⁴ projects whose target trait acts after harvest. Local is a valid value where the material is an unidentified landrace.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Sex of the person who manages the household's grain store, per Doss & Kieran (2014); age band of that person; smallholder status of the holding, as Annex B defines it; storage protectant used (none, synthetic insecticide, botanical or ash, for example); farm size class, with the bands stated; agroecological zone, with the classification stated; share of the harvest sold within three months of harvest.
unitOfObservation:
Household: the household's own harvest of the target crop from the reference season, followed from the end of the harvest operation to the end of the storage period. Grain bought, borrowed or received from other farms, and grain left from an earlier harvest, is not part of it. A household is the level at which the loss rate is computed. A household that keeps the crop in more than one store records each store separately at each visit; its storage loss is the sum over its stores, the storage-type cut is computed on the store records, and the handling stages are recorded once for the household.

Trial / Station is not a level for this indicator. A storage trial, hermetic bags against woven bags on a station for example, measures a treatment effect, which is evidence about an innovation; it is not the loss rate of any farming population and does not enter this indicator at any level.
calculationSummary:
The loss rate is the weight of grain lost across the five stages divided by the harvest it was lost from, in four steps. Every weight is in kilograms at the moisture basis recorded with the value.

First, establish the harvest. The harvest of the crop is taken as grain, and a loss at a stage before threshing or shelling is expressed as its grain equivalent, with the conversion used recorded:

Where the crop is carried, dried or stored on the ear, cob or pod before it is threshed or shelled, the losses at those stages are part of H, since they were lost from the harvest before it reached the thresher; loss in the harvest operation itself is not, being the sub-metric with its own denominator. Where part of the crop is sold or given away before threshing, its grain equivalent is added to H and recorded with the conversion used.

Second, compute the loss at each stage. For threshing or shelling, cleaning or winnowing, drying and on-farm transport, the loss is the quantity lost during the operation, and the stage loss rate is that loss divided by the quantity brought to the operation (FAO, 2018):

Storage is computed over the storage period, from repeated visits, because a storage loss is always related to the quantity in store at the time it is assessed (FAO, 2018). At each visit t the enumerator records the quantity in store, the quantities taken out or added since the previous visit, and the cumulative percentage weight loss w of a sample drawn from the store, measured by the count and weigh method or the thousand grain mass method (FAO, 2018). Then:

where S(t−1) is the quantity in store immediately after the previous visit, w(t) is the cumulative percentage weight loss of the sample at visit t, and w(0) is the reading at the first visit. Both measurement methods express w against the grain's original weight, while S(t−1) is weighed after that loss has occurred, which is why each increment is divided by 100 − w(t−1). The formula is the toolbox's; the guideline gives the percentage loss at each visit (FAO, 2018). Loss before the first visit is not captured, which is why the first visit is within a month of the grain going into store. Grain taken out between two visits is treated as having stayed in store until the later visit, which overstates its loss; the error grows with the interval, which is why visits are at most a month apart. Grain of the household's own harvest added to the store after the first visit is recorded with its date and quantity, enters S from the next visit and the quantity placed in store, and the number of households whose store was topped up is reported with the pooled rate, because later samples mix grain of different ages and the formula does not separate them.

Third, compute the household loss rate. The five stage losses are weights of the same harvest, so they are summed and divided by it, not multiplied as rates:

A household that sold its whole crop at threshing has no storage stage; its storage loss is zero and its harvest stays in H, which is correct for a population rate, since selling early is one of the ways losses are avoided. Grain that deteriorates so far that it is rejected as food counts as lost (FAO, 2018), whatever is then done with it. Where rejected grain is fed to animals or used in another way, the quantity and its use are recorded, because the SDG 12.3.1(a) definition does not count grain that re-enters another use, animal feed for example, as lost (United Nations Statistics Division, 2025). The toolbox counts it, since the question here is what the household loses as food, and reports the rate on the SDG basis beside the headline rate so that both can be read.

Fourth, compute the change between the baseline season and the latest season, each a loss rate pooled as the aggregation rule sets out:

The change is tested before it is called a change. It is detectable only where its absolute value exceeds the standard error of the difference, √(SE of the latest rate² + SE of the baseline rate²), taken from the precision Block E requires for each rate. On the household panel route the standard error of the change is instead estimated directly over the households measured in both seasons, on the same ratio estimator, and replaces the formula above. On that route both endpoint rates are recomputed over the households measured in both the baseline and the latest season, and the change is their difference; each season's rate over its full sample is reported beside them. Where the test fails, report no detectable change, with the value shown.
dataSource:
Comparator DS4: the cumulative weight loss estimates of the African Postharvest Losses Information System (APHLIS, 2023), for cereals in sub-Saharan Africa by province. APHLIS builds its estimates from stage loss figures in the published literature, adjusted for seasonal factors (FAO, 2018), so it is a modelled figure. Its boundary is wider than this indicator's: its cumulative loss runs from harvesting and field drying to market storage (FAO, 2018), while the headline here starts after harvest and ends at the farm store. A comparison states that difference; the APHLIS figure is a regional reference only, never a substitute for the project rate and never pooled with it.

Not applicable · DS2: distribution records of storage technologies show what was handed out, not what was lost. · DS3: no remote-sensing method observes on-farm grain loss. · DS5: crowdsourced figures cannot meet the measurement conditions above.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: The route used (physical measurement or declaration), the sampling design, the achieved sample size, the stages measured, the storage loss method (count and weigh or thousand grain mass), the number and timing of storage visits, and the moisture basis. Where the declaration route was used, state why physical measurement was not feasible and whether a calibration against physical measurement exists for the crop and area.
collectionInstrument:
Physical measurement route: a household post-harvest module recording, at each handling stage as it takes place, the quantity brought to it and the quantity lost, as grain or as grain equivalent with the conversion used, with the unit and its weight in kilograms; and a storage visit form recording, at each visit, the quantity in store, the quantities taken out or added since the last visit and what they were used for, the storage type, any protectant applied, the sample's moisture content, and the count and weigh or thousand grain mass readings. Declaration route: the FAO guideline's farmer modules for harvest and post-harvest operations and for storage, as published (FAO, 2018).

Recorded with every value, whatever the instrument: the route, the moisture basis, the stages covered and the order in which they took place, the storage period in months, and for rejected grain the quantity and what it was used for. Retain each stage's quantity handled and quantity lost as separate values, not only their ratio. Every record carries a persistent household identifier, which is what makes the panel route and de-duplication possible.
collectionFrequency: Each season for which a value is reported: a visit at each handling stage as it takes place, which is one visit at or soon after threshing where the crop is threshed or shelled before it is dried, carried or stored, then storage visits, the first within one month of the crop going into store, on the ear or as grain, and the rest no more than a month apart, to the end of the storage period (FAO, 2018). On the farmer declaration route, one visit at the end of the storage period, or periodic visits where the project can afford them, which improve recall (FAO, 2018).
referencePeriod: The storage period following one harvest of the crop, assigned to the reporting year in which that harvest falls. The storage period is a design length the project fixes for the domain, at least six months from harvest for grains (FAO, 2018), stated in months with the value. A household whose store of that harvest is empty before the period ends has a complete record, not a truncated one: its storage loss runs to the last visit at which grain of that harvest was in store, and it stays in the rate. Where the national cropping calendar defines more than one season a year, the season is recorded with the value, and baseline and latest are the same season in different years.
baselineRequired: Yes, by construction: the baseline season is one endpoint of the change. A baseline from a single season is released flagged, because one season's losses move with that season's humidity and pest pressure; where the project can, the baseline is the pooled rate over two or three consecutive seasons, which is what the FAO guideline recommends for a first set of loss estimates (FAO, 2018). Where no season was measured before the intervention began, the change is labelled as measured from the first season observed.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One crop, one measurement route, one set of stages measured, one storage period length, one moisture basis. Levels widen the set of households; they never widen the domain. No combined figure exists across crops, and a rate built on five stages is never pooled with one built on fewer.

Weight: the harvest, H, with each household's sampling weight where the sample is not self-weighting. A household with a larger harvest carries proportionally more of the rate.

B: Combination method: ratio of sums.

Stage loss rates pool the same way, on the quantity brought to the stage. This is the ratio estimator the FAO guideline sets out for percentage losses (FAO, 2018). Recompute from household records; never average household rates, which would give a household that harvested 50 kg the same weight as one that harvested 5 tonnes.

Two routes to the change, and the route is a recorded field. A household panel measures the same identified households in the baseline and the latest season, and is the route of record because it holds who was measured constant. A repeated cross-section draws a fresh sample each season; its change includes any change in who was sampled, and it is declared as such. The two routes are never pooled into one change.

C: Levels and operations.

D: Never pooled. Different crops; physically measured rates with farmer-declared rates; rates on different storage period lengths; rates built on different sets of stages; the SDG-basis rate with the headline rate; a storage trial's treatment and control results with household records; a panel-route change with a cross-section change. Where a project holds both a measured and a declared rate for the same population, it reports both; a single estimate combining them, weighted by their precision as the FAO guideline describes (FAO, 2018), is admitted only as a labelled modelled figure with the method stated, never as a measured rate.

E: Deduplication and coverage. De-duplicate on the persistent household identifier from Project area level upward. Report coverage and precision with every rate at Project area level and above, the endpoint loss rates, the stage loss rates and the sub-metrics, on the release bands KPI-O23 sets in its Block E: a coefficient of variation of 16.5 per cent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 per cent released flagged, above 33.3 per cent not released as an estimate, and no rate released below 30 household records. The change carries no band and no floor of its own: it is reported where both endpoint rates are releasable, released flagged where either is flagged, and then tested for detectability as Calculation method sets out. On the household panel route the endpoint rates recomputed over the households measured in both seasons each meet the 30-record floor. A figure at Project area level or above rests on a probability sample drawn from a stated frame, with the frame, the design and the achieved precision reported with the value.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Include every sampled household that harvested the target crop in the reference season, whether or not it stored any. Exclude a household whose crop produced no harvest, and report how many there were: with H at zero there is no rate to compute, and the failure belongs to the yield indicators, KPI-O23 and KPI-OC22.

Grain from several sources kept in one store. Where the household's own harvest cannot be kept apart from grain from elsewhere, the storage loss rate measured on the mixed store is applied to the household's own quantity placed in store, and the record says so.

Missing visits. A missed storage visit is not interpolated: the interval runs from the visit before it to the visit after it, and the longer interval is recorded. A household that stops being visited while grain of that harvest remains in its store has a truncated storage loss; it is reported with its period stated and enters the pooled rate only where the period it covers matches the domain. Missing H, or the storage-placement quantity for a household that stored: the household leaves the rate entirely, its losses and its harvest both.

Validate. A loss at a stage can never exceed the quantity brought to it (FAO, 2018). The count and weigh method can return a small negative weight loss where infestation is low (FAO, 2018); the value is recorded as measured and not set to zero, since truncating negatives at zero biases the pooled rate upward. A value outside the project's stated plausible range is investigated before reporting, not dropped.

Repeated observations: one value per household, crop and season.
limitations: Contribution, not attribution. A season's losses move with humidity at harvest, the pest pressure of that year and how long households keep grain before selling it, alongside the practices a project promotes.

Measured and declared losses are not the same quantity. Farmer declarations tend to understate losses against physical measurement (FAO, 2018). Nationally representative surveys in Malawi, Tanzania and Uganda put self-reported on-farm maize losses at 1.4 to 5.9 per cent of the harvest (Kaminski & Christiaensen, 2014), well below most measured and modelled figures. A change from a declared baseline to a measured follow-up is a change of instrument, not of loss.

Losses are concentrated. In the same surveys, losses fell on fewer than a fifth of households (Kaminski & Christiaensen, 2014). A pooled rate can therefore move a long way on a few households, and the share of households reporting any loss is worth reading beside it.

Selling early lowers the rate without any change in storage practice. A household that sells at harvest avoids storage loss, often at a lower price. A fall in the rate driven by more early sales is not the same result as a fall driven by better storage, which is why the stage and storage-type cuts are required and the share sold within three months is available as a cut.

A storage period cut short understates storage loss. Losses in store rise with time, so a rate over four months is not comparable with one over eight, and the period length is part of the pooling domain for that reason.

The storage formula is an approximation. It treats grain taken out between visits as having stayed in store until the later visit, which overstates storage loss, and it does not capture loss before the first visit, which understates it; monthly visits, the first within a month of storage, keep both small. In a store topped up with the household's own grain after the first visit, later samples mix grain of different ages.

Quality loss is only partly captured. The rate measures weight. Grain that stays in use but has lost nutritional or market value, or carries aflatoxin below the point where the household rejects it, is not counted; the aflatoxin sub-metric covers one part of that, where it is tested.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: Content owner: the CIMMYT MEAL unit, with the post-harvest or agronomy lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Collection: trained enumerators at the household, at each handling stage and at each storage visit. Validation and calculation: the project's MEAL role, using the formulas in Calculation method. Approval and reporting: per the project's own reporting line to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
