name: Percentage of measured smallholder farmers with a detectable increase in agricultural productivity
resultsLevel: Impact. The CIMMYT MEAL Framework defines impact as lasting change in agrifood systems, naming changes in productivity first among them (Section 2.4). This indicator counts the farmers in whom that change occurred, which is the distributional question neither an output level nor an outcome change can answer.
primaryObjective: PO3. Contributing: PO2, PO4.
cgiarImpactArea: Nutrition, Health & Food Security. Secondary: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs.
sdgTarget: Target 2.3
otherFrameworks: None
definition:
The share of smallholder farmers in CIMMYT intervention areas whose own productivity series shows an increase large enough to be distinguished from measurement error, over a window of at least four consecutive seasons or production periods. The numerator counts farmers, not plots, animals or hectares, and each is counted once regardless of how many crops or species they produce.

The denominator is the measured panel, the smallholder farmers CIMMYT measured across the window. A farmer who was not measured is unknown, not unimproved, and enters neither term; coverage against the target population travels with every value.

Smallholder is a property of the population, not of the measurement, and is defined in Annex B.
rationale: Answers how many smallholders are better off in production terms, which a mean cannot answer: a population mean can rise while most farmers show no change, if a minority gains substantially. This is the pathway's impact statement and the reason the yield and livestock threads carry farmer identifiers from the plot upward.
projectSpecificApplication:
How this project applies the institutional indicator: the population of smallholder farmers, the geography, the seasons or periods in the window, and the crops or species measured. Scope only; the unit, measurement basis and calculation method are unchanged.

Example: "Share of smallholder maize farmers in the Central Rift Valley under CIMMYT intervention whose own yield rose detectably between the 2022 and 2025 seasons."
projectSpecificRationale: States the impact claim this project made and reports against, and to whom. Example: a project reports it because its results framework carries a farmer-level productivity target that a population mean would not evidence.
projectTypesApply: in each case only where the project measures productivity on identified farmers' own plots or animals across at least four seasons or periods
projectTypesNotApplicable: both of which work upstream of any identified farmer

digital agriculture and AI unless the project runs its own farmer-level measurement panel.

A project that measures productivity but cannot link measurements to identified farmers across seasons reports the output indicators alone and does not report this indicator
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation, in each case only where the project measures productivity on identified farmers' own plots or animals across at least four seasons or periods.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development, both of which work upstream of any identified farmer; digital agriculture and AI unless the project runs its own farmer-level measurement panel.

A project that measures productivity but cannot link measurements to identified farmers across seasons reports the output indicators alone and does not report this indicator.
unit: Percentage of measured smallholder farmers
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of the measured smallholder farmers recorded a productivity gain large enough for the method to detect. The share moves with the detection rule as well as with the gain, so it is not read without the rule that produced it.
disaggregationRequired: Sex of the farmer, male and female at minimum, per Doss & Kieran (2014); age, youth and non-youth on the youth band of 15 to 30, stated once in Core Section 4.1, with the date of birth recorded.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Farm size class, with the bands stated, for example under 1 ha, 1 to 2 ha and 2 to 5 ha, or the national classification where one is in use; agroecological zone, with the classification stated; the measure on which the increase was detected, and the crop or species it was detected on, a farmer who qualified on more than one measure being reported under each measure that qualified them while counted once in the share; whether the farmer produces crops, livestock or both. Cropping season is not a cut here: it is a dimension of each farmer's series under the aggregation rule, and a farmer is counted once whichever season's series shows the increase.
unitOfObservation: The registered farmer: the holder of a persistent farmer identifier in the project's farmer register, whose series, on each measure, is the Household-level method of KPI-O23, KPI-O24, KPI-O59 or KPI-O60 applied to the plots, animals or herd-windows linked to that identifier. The smallholder threshold tests the holding of that farmer's household, Annex B defining a smallholder as a farm household. Sex and age are that person's. A household with more than one registered farmer holding separate plots or animals contributes each as a unit; a household with one registered farmer contributes one. Counting farmers whose own productivity rose requires each farmer to be identified across seasons, so a figure supplied already aggregated cannot contribute.
calculationSummary:
The indicator is the share of the measured farmers whose own productivity rose detectably.

The smallholder threshold, as Annex B defines it, is decided at the reference period and held for the window: a farmer above it at reference is excluded, and one who crosses it later for whatever reason is retained and the count reported. The farmer need not own the land or the animals, and holding or having access to them is sufficient. The share is built farmer by farmer, in three steps.

First, test each farmer for a detectable increase.

The protocol error is expressed in the unit of the farmer's own series before it is compared to anything. An error documented in other units is converted, and a relative error is converted to an absolute one against a stated base, the mean of that farmer's series; the conversion and the base are recorded with the floor. An error quoted in quintals per hectare against a series in kilograms per hectare sets the floor a hundredfold too low.

Labour productivity qualifies a farmer under a restricted rule. No protocol-error figure has been established for logged labour, as KPI-OC62 records, so on both enterprises the first limb runs on the numerator's error as a lower bound, KPI-O23's on the crop enterprise where the yield came from crop cuts, and KPI-O24's on the livestock enterprise, eggs apart, its unit conversion as KPI-OC62 sets out and the square root of k and the square root of two applied once, here, with the verdict flagged provisional.

For each farmer and each crop or species:

computed from that farmer's own values at Household level for any one of the three qualifying productivity measures: crop yield (KPI-O23), livestock productivity per unit of exposure (KPI-O24), or labour productivity, crop or livestock. The measures are never combined into a single figure; the test is applied to each separately and any one pass qualifies the farmer. The farmer passes when, for at least one measure, the change is positive and exceeds both the measurement error of the difference and that farmer's own period-to-period variation, the sample standard deviation (n − 1) of that farmer's series over its four or more periods, applying the same two-part test as KPI-OC22 and KPI-OC25, established from the evidence on the KPI-O23 and KPI-O24 sheets. KPI-OC25 documents no protocol error for eggs, so a farmer's egg series, on either livestock measure, is tested on the variation limb alone, and the verdict states that the first limb was not applied; an egg labour verdict carries no provisional flag. A farmer's series whose yields came from whole-plot harvest carries no documented error, on the yield measure and as the numerator of the crop labour measure, so it is tested on the variation limb alone and the verdict states that the first limb was not applied; a labour verdict on it carries no provisional flag. The applicable error is the error of the household value as computed: the floor for the difference is the random component of the single-plot, single-animal or single-herd-window error, divided by the square root of k where the household value pools k plots, animals or, on livestock labour, herd-windows measured under one protocol, which understates the floor where the plots or animals differ in area or exposure, with k recorded with the verdict, and multiplied by the square root of two; the systematic component is common to both periods, cancels in the difference, and is not part of the floor. Where the documented error does not separate its random and systematic components, the whole figure is treated as random and the floor is conservative, and the sheet says which. Where the documented error is a mean absolute error, as the crop-cut evidence on KPI-O23 is, it is used as if it were a standard error, which makes the floor approximate in a direction that is not known: for a purely random error a mean absolute error is about four-fifths of the standard error, which sets the floor low, and any systematic component it contains raises the floor; the project states which crop-cut design its plot geometry is treated as.

The farmer's own window must be method-consistent. A farmer's series is tested within one moisture method, or on the livestock thread one weighing method and, for milk, one suckling regime; where the method or the regime changed, the test runs on the longest method-consistent segment if it holds four or more periods, and otherwise the farmer is recorded as no detectable change on that measure and the number so recorded is reported. On growth a farmer's series is built within one age and sex class of animal, as KPI-O24 reports it. On milk the verdict records whether the reference and latest values are on lactations of the same parity; where they are not it is flagged parity not held, and the number of such verdicts in the numerator is reported beside the share. Method heterogeneity across farmers remains acceptable, because each farmer is tested against the error of the protocol that produced their own series, not against a common one. A positive difference smaller than that error is recorded as no detectable change and the farmer does not pass.

Second, count each farmer once. A farmer with a detectable increase on maize and on beans counts once. Increases are not summed across a farmer's crops or species, and a farmer is never counted twice for producing more than one thing.

Third, compute the share:

The denominator is the smallholder farmers with a measured series of at least four periods for at least one qualifying measure.
dataSource:
Recommended DS1: the project's own farmer-level series from KPI-O23 and KPI-O24, and from KPI-O59 or KPI-O60 where labour productivity is the qualifying measure, at Household level, across at least four seasons or periods, with persistent farmer identifiers. There is no other admissible source, and a value that is Fallback-sourced on its parent sheet is not admitted: a series any value of which came from a Fallback route, such as the household's own report, a recall module, recalled labour or a stated area wherever it enters the value, is not tested, the farmer is counted in a reported exclusion line with the component named, and a farmer with no admitted series enters neither term.

Frame DS2: the project's farmer register supplies the farmer identifier and the plot-, animal- and herd-window-to-farmer links.

Not applicable · DS2 for the verdict: delivery and registration records identify who was reached, not whose productivity rose. · DS3: remote sensing cannot attribute a change to an identified farmer. · DS4: national statistics carry no farmer identity and no panel. · DS5: a self-reported increase is not a measured one, and this indicator is a headcount built on measurement.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: The smallholder threshold applied, its unit and its source, per Annex B, and the source of each farmer's holding size: a register, a measurement or the producer's statement; the panel size; the number of farmers dropped for a missing endpoint and why; the number excluded as above the threshold; whether the panel is balanced; and the protocol error used as the detectability floor for each crop or species.
collectionInstrument: None of its own; it is computed from the KPI-O23 and KPI-O24 records, and from KPI-O59 and KPI-O60 where labour productivity is the qualifying series. What this indicator adds is a farmer panel: the same identified farmers measured in every season or period of the window, with the identifier carried from the plot or animal record upward. Without it the indicator is unreportable regardless of the volume of productivity data the project holds.
collectionFrequency: Every season or period in the window, from KPI-O23 and KPI-O24, and from KPI-O59 or KPI-O60 where labour productivity is the qualifying measure
referencePeriod: A window of at least four consecutive seasons or production periods, ending in the reporting year
baselineRequired: Yes, by construction: the reference season or period is the baseline. A project with no measured reference cannot report this indicator and says so rather than substituting a recalled starting point.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One population of smallholder farmers, one reporting window. Where the national cropping calendar defines more than one season a year, a farmer's own series is built within one season, on the season label KPI-O23 records; a farmer measured in both seasons carries a series per season and is counted once whichever series shows the increase. One declared smallholder threshold, as Annex B defines it. Values computed on different declared thresholds are never pooled, because a population is not the same population when its boundary moves. Levels widen the set of farmers; they never widen the domain.

Weight: one per farmer.

B: Combination method: ratio of sums.

Rebuild the share from farmers; never average shares. Shares are never averaged across panels of unequal size. The per-farmer test is decided once, at Household level, and travels upward unchanged: the levels above are wider counts of the same decisions, not fresh computations.

C: Levels and operations.

D: Never pooled. Shares, in place of their farmers; farmers counted twice across overlapping projects; decisions taken under materially different detectability floors, reported instead by protocol class; a farmer's series built across different cropping seasons of the year, where the calendar defines more than one, since the test runs within one season on the label KPI-O23 records.

E: Deduplication and coverage. De-duplicate on the persistent farmer identifier before pooling: a farmer reached by two projects is one farmer. Report the denominator with every percentage, and the number of farmers in the numerator whose only qualifying verdict is provisional. Report the range of detectability floors present in the pool. Where identifiers cannot be reconciled, label the figure an upper bound on measured coverage. Rolling-window decisions overlap: where a farmer qualifies on a series that is itself reported on a rolling window, consecutive annual headcounts share most of their evidence and are not independent.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Include smallholder farmers in the project's measured panel with a measurement in the reference period, a measurement in the latest period, and at least two in between, four in all, since the per-farmer test uses that farmer's own period-to-period variation, which is released from four points and not fewer.

Exclude farmers above the smallholder threshold from both numerator and denominator, reported separately as a count so the panel's coverage is legible.
limitations: The measured panel is farmers, and cannot be a region series. This indicator is a share of farmers, so it needs farmer identity: a regional mean can rise while most farmers show no change, if the gain concentrates on a few large holdings. Where a project holds no farmer panel the indicator is not reported, rather than approximated from an area series. The change indicators beneath it (KPI-OC22, KPI-OC25, KPI-OC62) do accept a region series, because a change in a series is defined on any series.

Contribution, not attribution. Productivity moves with weather, prices, input access and household circumstance alongside CIMMYT's interventions, and a share of farmers improving is not evidence that the intervention caused it.

The panel is the population, and it is usually not representative. This is a share of farmers CIMMYT measured, not of farmers in the intervention area, unless the panel was drawn to be representative. State which.

Attrition may bias the result, and the direction is not assumed. Farmers who leave a panel are not a random subset, but a difference in who remains does not by itself bias the estimate (Alderman et al., 2001). Report the attrition count with the value, and the test comparing those retained against those lost.

The detectability floor determines the answer. A project using a coarse protocol has a high floor and counts fewer farmers than a project measuring the same reality carefully, so the protocol and its error must travel with the value or two projects' figures are not comparable.

One detectable increase on one crop, species or measure makes a farmer count. That is an intentionally inclusive criterion: the indicator answers whether anything improved, not whether the farm as a whole improved.
Parity and age can produce the verdict. Milk yield rises over the early parities and daily gain falls with age, so a farmer's own series can drift with no change in management.

A producer whose cycle is longer than a year is measured more slowly. A one-cow dairy household can complete fewer than four lactations in four years and is outside the denominator until its window holds four measured periods.

On livestock labour the excluded share can produce the verdict. KPI-O60 excludes the hours of a shared episode the line did not separate and keeps the output, so a farmer whose excluded share rose between the reference and the latest period can show a detectable increase with no change in output or effort.

A pooled share is conditional on the detectability floors behind it. Each farmer passed or failed against the floor of the protocol their own project used, and a coarse protocol admits fewer farmers than a precise one measuring the same reality. A pooled share therefore combines decisions taken under different thresholds: it moves with the composition of the pool as well as with what happened to farmers, and cannot be compared with a share computed over a different mix. Where the floors differ materially, report by protocol class rather than as one figure.
A share without its denominator cannot be read. At institutional level the panel size is the accurate measure of how much of CIMMYT's reach was measured, not a technical footnote.
subMetrics: None.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
All measurement rules are inherited from KPI-O23 and KPI-O24, and from KPI-O59 and KPI-O60 where labour productivity is the qualifying series.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: Content owner: the CIMMYT MEAL unit, with the agronomy and farming-systems leads as technical reviewers
sheetStewardDataRoles: Collection: as KPI-O23 and KPI-O24, and as KPI-O59 and KPI-O60 where labour productivity is the qualifying series. Validation and calculation: the project's MEAL role, using the formulas in Calculation method. Approval and reporting: per the project's own reporting line to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 7 · Productivity — Reference sheet KPI-I06

name: Number of women engaged in training, producer organizations, or decision-making fora
volumeTitle: Gender equality, youth and social inclusion
resultsLevel: Output. The count reports a delivered result, women's participation in the trainings, producer organizations and fora the project runs, works with or supports, not a behavior change among the women engaged.
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Contributing: PO5 (Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities).
cgiarImpactArea: Gender Equality, Youth and Social Inclusion
sdgTarget: None. The nearest target is SDG 5.5 (women's full and effective participation in decision-making), but its official indicators (5.5.1, seats held by women in parliaments and local governments; 5.5.2, women in managerial positions) measure representation in national institutions, not participation in program activities, so there is no direct correspondence.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30: the minimum data standard for outputs requires gender-disaggregated trained-people counts, which this indicator's training channel can supply for women, on this sheet's own engagement threshold. CIMMYT GEYSI plan: the internal gender register the women's empowerment indicator set derives from.
definition: Counts unique women engaged in CIMMYT training, producer organizations or decision-making fora in the reporting year, counted once per woman regardless of the number of engagements. Engagement means direct, substantive participation: attending a CIMMYT-run or CIMMYT-supported training, taking part in an activity of a producer organization a CIMMYT project works with, or taking part in a decision-making forum convened or supported by CIMMYT, for example a community planning committee, a seed-system platform, or a value-chain governance body.
rationale: Answers how many individual women CIMMYT's work brings into the spaces where knowledge, resources and decisions are shared. CIMMYT's GEYSI plan classifies gender indicators along a Reach, Benefit, Empower, Transform continuum, and this indicator sits at Reach: it establishes the population of women within which later benefit and empowerment changes (KPI-I08) can credibly be claimed. It also feeds the gender-disaggregated participation reporting that CGIAR technical reporting and most donors require.
projectSpecificApplication: State which engagement channels the project runs (training, producer organizations, decision-making fora), the geographic scope, and the partner organizations whose participant records feed the count. Do not change the unique-count rule, the engagement threshold, or the counting basis; if applying the indicator as defined is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count informs: for example a donor-required female-participation indicator, a project inclusion target for training cohorts, or an internal trigger to adjust recruitment or meeting formats if women's participation stays low.
projectTypesNotApplicable: upstream discovery science and breeding and varietal development
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science and breeding and varietal development, which engage no participants directly; digital agriculture and AI, which reports through the pathways its tools serve.
unit: Number of women and girls aged 15 and over (unique individuals)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more women were engaged in training, producer organizations or decision-making fora. A woman engaged through several channels is counted once, so the value counts women rather than engagements.
disaggregationRequired: Required: age (youth/non-youth, using 15 to 30, stated once in Core §4.1; projects record date of birth or exact age so that other donor bands, for example a donor band of 15 to 29, can be derived without recollecting data).
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Engagement channel (training / producer organization / decision-making forum; a woman active in more than one channel appears in each channel subtotal, so channel subtotals may exceed the unique headline count and must never be summed); country or region; new versus continuing participants.
unitOfObservation: The individual woman. A woman engaged through two channels, or by two projects, is one woman. The persistent participant identifier in Block E is what makes that true.
calculationSummary:
The threshold is direct, substantive participation, evidenced by a dated attendance, participation or service record naming the woman (a membership list alone does not evidence engagement): attending a CIMMYT-run or CIMMYT-supported training, taking part in an activity of a producer organization a CIMMYT project works with, or taking part in a decision-making forum convened or supported by CIMMYT that she is registered as a member or participant of. Receipt of a broadcast, and attendance at a one-off event such as a field day or a sensitization meeting, do not count, whether or not attendance was recorded: presence at an event is not direct contact with a service or intervention. This is CIMMYT's own convention for this indicator.

Count of unique women with at least one qualifying engagement in the reporting year. No denominator: an absolute count, not a proportion. Inclusion: women recorded in attendance registers, dated producer-organization participation records or forum participant records of CIMMYT-run or CIMMYT-supported activities, where the engagement meets the substantive-participation threshold in the Definition. Exclusion: brief or incidental contacts; indirect beneficiaries (for example other members of a participant's household); records counting contacts or attendances rather than persons. Missing data: a record that cannot be attributed to an identifiable individual (no name plus identifier sufficient for de-duplication) is excluded from the unique count and reported as an unattributed remainder; a record missing age cannot pass the age floor and is excluded, its count reported alongside. Repeated observations: one count per woman per reporting year, regardless of how many sessions, organizations or fora she took part in; the unique-count rule is applied within each project first, then across projects at aggregation.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: project administrative and registry records: training attendance registers, producer-organization membership and participation lists, and forum participant records, including records kept by partner organizations under the project's guidance, each carrying name, unique participant identifier, sex and age. Fallback DS1: a participant listing exercise (enumeration of the groups the project engaged) to reconstruct the roster where registers were not kept or lack the fields needed for de-duplication; values from this route are flagged as fallback-sourced. Not applicable DS3: participation is not observable from satellite or geospatial data. Not applicable DS4: secondary databases cannot identify which individuals CIMMYT activities engaged. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or self-nominated claims of participation cannot be verified against activity records and would break the unique-count rule.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether Recommended or Fallback was used, which partners supplied records, and how de-duplication across activities and partners was done. If Fallback, state why registers were not available.
collectionInstrument: For the DS1 fallback: a participant listing module administered to engaged groups, capturing name, unique participant identifier, sex, age, activity and date, collected by enumerators in person or by phone; respondent is the participant herself or the group's record-keeper. The recommended DS2 route uses the same identity fields in a standard attendance-register and participation-record template applied by project staff and partners.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as engagements occur (registers and participation records maintained per activity); compiled and de-duplicated annually.
referencePeriod: The reporting year; each annual value stands alone (see Limitations on why annual values are never summed).
baselineRequired: No. As an annual reach count the value starts from zero for each new project and each reporting year; the first reported year serves as the reference point for trend context. No change or impact claim rests on this indicator alone, so no retrospective baseline reconstruction is needed.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One reporting year. Levels widen the set of women; they never widen the domain. Women evidenced only by the DS1 roster reconstruction are Fallback-sourced and reported beside the pooled count with a note; the same project's register-evidenced women stay in it.

Weight: one per woman, so a woman engaged through several channels still counts once.

B: Combination method: sum. Total = Σ unique women engaged in the domain. A count of people is added, never averaged, and de-duplication precedes the sum.

C: Levels and operations. Household. The engagement status of the individual woman. Also report: the engagement channels.

D: Never pooled. Engagement counts with KPI-I08's empowerment measure, which counts a different qualifying change on a subset of the same women. Annual counts from different reporting years; a multi-year figure is counted afresh over the whole period on the persistent participant identifier. Engagement counts with KPI-O29's youth count, which counts a second time every woman aged 15 to 30 engaged through a training program, the channel both sheets count, and with the female subtotals of KPI-O18 and KPI-O04, which count women trained under their own thresholds.

E: Deduplication and coverage. The persistent participant identifier, applied from Household level upward, so a woman engaged by two projects or through two channels is counted once. Where identifiers cannot be reconciled, the figure is labeled an upper bound on unique women. This is a census of the project's engagement records (attendance registers and dated participation records), not a sample estimate: it carries no sampling error and no coefficient-of-variation band.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Include all women and girls aged 15 and over engaged in the reporting year through a channel the project supports, with engagement evidenced by a dated attendance, participation or service record; membership alone does not qualify. Fifteen is the lower bound of the count, and age band is a required disaggregation so participation by adolescent girls is visible rather than merged into an adult total. Girls under 15 are kept in the participation record and reported as a separate count, never in the total.

Exclude women reached by a broadcast with no individual record, since no unique count is possible.

Missing the participant identifier: the record is excluded and reported as a coverage shortfall with the count, never estimated.
limitations: Measures reach, not benefit or empowerment: a woman's presence in a training or forum says nothing about whether she gained skills, resources or influence. Read it only as the first step of the empowerment chain, alongside KPI-OC19 and KPI-I08.

Projects applying different engagement thresholds (for example counting mass-event attendance) produce counts that are not comparable; the threshold in force is CIMMYT's own substantive-participation benchmark (Calculation method), and the applied threshold travels with the value.

De-duplication quality drives the number: without unique identifiers the count inflates through repeat attendances and cross-project overlap; unmatched pooled figures are upper estimates and must be labeled as such, and fallback-sourced counts are reported beside the pooled figure.

Annual values are not cumulative: the same woman can be a continuing participant across years, so summing years overstates total reach; multi-year reach requires de-duplication across the whole period.

A rising count does not mean inclusion improved in relative terms: women's share of participants can fall while the count rises if men's participation rises faster. Report the count alongside women's share where the project tracks all participants.
subMetrics: None. The three engagement channels (training, producer organizations, decision-making fora) are disaggregations of the same unique count, not separately calculated metrics. Related indicators have their own sheets: KPI-OC19 (gender gap in adoption of improved practices, the pathway's outcome-level equity measure) and KPI-I08 (share of women classified as improved in decision-making power over agricultural and household resources, the impact this indicator rolls up to).
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
The participation significance threshold, the unique-count and de-duplication rules, the sex and age disaggregation and the no-summing-across-years rule are stated as CIMMYT's own reach-counting convention.

Doss and Kieran (2014), Standards for collecting sex-disaggregated data for gender analysis: sex categories for disaggregation.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the GEYSI focal point as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project field teams and partner organizations maintaining attendance registers, participation records and membership lists. Validation: project MEAL officer (identity fields complete, de-duplication run, threshold applied). Calculation: project M&E, applying the unique-count rule; cross-project de-duplication by the CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 8 · Gender equality, youth and social inclusion — Reference sheet KPI-O28

name: Number of youth engaged in CIMMYT training, enterprise, or employment programs
volumeTitle: Gender equality, youth and social inclusion
resultsLevel: Output. The count reports a delivered result, young people's participation in the training, enterprise and employment programs CIMMYT or its partners deliver, not a change among youth; the change that follows, youth participation in agrifood value chains, is the outcome, measured by KPI-OC26.
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Contributing: PO5 (Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities).
cgiarImpactArea: Gender Equality, Youth and Social Inclusion
sdgTarget: None (direct). The nearest correspondences are SDG indicator 4.3.1 (participation rate of youth and adults in formal and non-formal education and training in the previous 12 months), which is a population-based participation rate rather than a program participant count, and SDG indicator 8.6.1 (proportion of youth aged 15 to 24 not in education, employment or training), which measures the inverse condition in the general population. Neither corresponds directly to a count of program participants.
otherFrameworks: The participant-not-contact counting rule this indicator follows is CIMMYT's own convention: a person is counted where the record shows participation, not where it shows a contact. CGIAR Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30: the minimum data standard for capacity development outputs requires number of people trained (gender disaggregated), length of training, and delivery method; program records for this indicator should capture those fields so the same records serve CGIAR reporting.
definition: Counts the unique young people who actively participated in a training, enterprise development, or employment program implemented by CIMMYT or its partners during the reporting year. Each youth is counted once per year, no matter how many programs or sessions they took part in. "Engaged" means active, registered participation evidenced by a participation record, not incidental contact such as a one-off public event and not registration or enrollment alone. Youth is defined as 15 to 30 years, stated once in Core §4.1; projects record date of birth or exact age so that other bands (for example a donor band of 15 to 29) can be derived without recollecting data.
rationale: Answers how many young people CIMMYT's work brings into agrifood skills, enterprise, and employment opportunities each year: the first and most controllable step in the youth-inclusion results chain. Project teams use it to manage delivery and coverage of youth-targeted activities; institutional reporting uses it to evidence the youth dimension of CIMMYT's gender, youth and social inclusion commitments before participation outcomes (KPI-OC26) mature.
projectSpecificApplication: State which programs the project counts under each of the three types (training, enterprise, employment), the geographic scope, and any partner-delivered programs included. Do not change the unique-counting rule, the engagement threshold, or the age band. If the project context requires a different youth age range (for example a national youth definition), report against the standard band and note the national band separately; raise feasibility problems with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining the indicator here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count informs: for example a donor-required youth reach indicator, a youth quota in a training component, or a trigger to adjust outreach if youth engagement falls short of plan.
projectTypesNotApplicable: breeding and varietal development and digital agriculture and AI
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, breeding and varietal development and digital agriculture and AI.
unit: Number of youth (individual people)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more young people were engaged in CIMMYT training, enterprise or employment programs. A young person engaged through several programs is counted once, so the value counts people rather than engagements.
disaggregationRequired: Required: sex (female/male at minimum, per CGIAR sex-disaggregated data standards); program type (training; enterprise; employment).
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Age sub-bands (for example 15 to 19, 20 to 24, 25 to 30); country/region; rural/urban; program delivered directly by CIMMYT vs by a partner.
unitOfObservation: The individual young person, with age recorded at first participation in the reporting year so the band is a fact rather than an inference.
calculationSummary: A count, not a ratio; no denominator. Value = unique individuals within the youth age band who actively participated in at least one CIMMYT or partner training, enterprise, or employment program during the reporting year. Inclusion: participants of programs delivered by CIMMYT or by partners under a CIMMYT project whose participation in at least one program activity is recorded, registration or enrollment alone not counting; youth status is determined by age at first participation in the reporting year. Exclusion: incidental contacts (attendance at a one-off public event such as a field day or sensitization meeting, whether or not attendance was registered; exposure to mass media or broadcast advisory content); individuals outside the age band; CIMMYT and partner staff working on the program. Missing data: a participant record without age (or date of birth) cannot be classified as youth and is excluded from the count; report the share of age-unclassifiable records alongside the value. A record without sex stays in the total and is reported under a "sex not available" category. Repeated observations: one count per youth per reporting year across all programs; under the program-type disaggregate a youth may appear once per type, so the disaggregate rows can sum to more than the headline count and must never be added together.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: administrative and registry data generated by delivery itself: training enrollment and attendance registers, enterprise development program records, employment, internship and placement records, and partner participant reporting under CIMMYT projects. Records must carry participant name or unique ID, date of birth or age, sex, program type, and dates, so the same records also satisfy the CGIAR minimum data standard for capacity development outputs. Fallback DS1: a participant verification survey in the program area, used where partner-delivered programs leave no participant-level records or where registries are incomplete; any survey-estimated value is flagged as fallback-sourced. Not applicable DS3: individual program participation and age cannot be observed from satellite or GIS data. Not applicable DS4: no third-party database records who participated in CIMMYT programs. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or self-nominated data cannot verify participation or age against program records.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which source role the project used, Recommended or Fallback. If Fallback, state why participant-level registry data was not available (for example, a partner-run program that reported only aggregate attendance).
collectionInstrument: For DS2: a standard participant registration form or digital registry capturing name or unique participant ID, date of birth or age, sex, program type (training / enterprise / employment), program dates, and location. For the DS1 fallback: a short participation-verification module; respondent: the young person who participated; mode: face-to-face or phone interview.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, through program registration and attendance records as activities are delivered; consolidated once per year.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Yearly values are snapshots and are never summed across years; a multi-year figure of unique youth is counted afresh over the whole period on the persistent participant identifier.
referencePeriod: The reporting year (12 months). Each reported value describes engagement in that year only.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual reach count that starts from zero each reporting year. Projects set ex-ante annual engagement targets instead of a baseline.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One reporting year. Levels widen the set of young people; they never widen the domain. Young people counted only through the DS1 participant verification survey are Fallback-sourced and reported beside the pooled count with a note; the same project's register-evidenced youth stay in it.

Weight: one per young person, so a young person engaged through several programs still counts once.

B: Combination method: sum. Total = Σ unique youth engaged in the domain, age recorded at first participation in the reporting year.

C: Levels and operations. Household. The engagement status of the individual young person. Also report: the engagement type.

D: Never pooled. Counts using different youth age definitions. Engagement counts with KPI-OC26's participation share, which has a denominator. Annual counts from different reporting years. Youth counts with KPI-O28's women's count, which counts every young woman engaged through training a second time.

E: Deduplication and coverage. The persistent participant identifier, applied from Household level upward. Where identifiers cannot be reconciled across projects, the figure is labeled an upper bound on unique youth. The youth definition in force travels with every figure, because a count of youth is meaningless without the band that defined it. The Recommended route is a census of program registers and carries no sampling error. Where the Fallback participant-verification survey draws a probability sample of the program area rather than enumerating the full program population, the resulting value is a sample estimate and travels, at Project area level and above, with the coefficient-of-variation bands used elsewhere in this volume: 16.5 percent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 percent released flagged, above 33.3 percent not released as an estimate, applied only where the estimate is built on at least 30 records.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Include young people engaged in the reporting year under one of the three program types, training, enterprise or employment (a placement, internship or job the program arranged), which are a closed list so counts stay comparable across projects: work that does not fit is recorded under the nearest type and raised.

Include them with age recorded at first participation in the reporting year rather than at reporting, so a participant does not age out of the count between the two.

Exclude participants whose age is unrecorded; they are reported as an unknown-age count alongside, not distributed across bands.

The youth definition in force is stated with the figure.
limitations: Engagement is reach, not benefit. The count shows young people entered CIMMYT-supported programs; it says nothing about skills gained, enterprises surviving, or jobs kept (participation in value chains is KPI-OC26), and CGIAR's review of its standard indicators warns against extrapolating reach numbers into benefit claims.

Double counting is the main measurement error. The same young person can enroll in several programs, projects, and years; without unique participant identifiers, totals beyond a single project-year risk overstating unique reach.

The value is sensitive to the age band and the engagement threshold. A 15 to 30 count is not comparable with a 15 to 29 count (a common donor band), and a count built on a looser threshold, such as one logging every field-day attendee, is not comparable with this one; the threshold in the Definition is fixed across projects and years.
Age data quality bounds the indicator. Registries often record age incompletely or approximately; the youth count is only as reliable as the recorded birth dates behind it.

A rise means more young people were brought into programs that year (or that recording improved); it does not mean youth livelihoods improved, and a fall may reflect a project cycle ending rather than weaker performance.
subMetrics: None. The three program types (training; enterprise; employment) are disaggregations of the same count, not separately calculated sub-metrics. The related outcome has its own sheet: KPI-OC26 (percentage of youth participation in agrifood value chains in CIMMYT intervention areas), the register roll-up destination of this output.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
The youth participant counting logic and the participant-not-contact rule are stated as CIMMYT's own reach-counting convention, on the 15-to-30 youth band stated once in Core §4.1.

CGIAR GENDER Impact Platform, youth research page (youth framing reference; the 15 to 24 working default it supported is superseded by the 15 to 30 band stated once in Core §4.1): https://gender.cgiar.org/gender-research/youth (accessed 29 July 2026).

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project teams and implementing partners maintaining program registration records. Validation: project MEAL officer (completeness of age and sex fields, de-duplication within the project). Calculation: project M&E, consolidating unique counts per the Calculation method. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.

name: Number of GEYSI-responsive policy or investment instruments developed with CIMMYT support
volumeTitle: Gender equality, youth and social inclusion
resultsLevel: Output. A drafted policy analysis, guideline or investment design is a delivered result, and CGIAR's quality-assurance guidance lists policy analyses and institutional innovations among research outputs. The counted object is the developed instrument document with CIMMYT's documented contribution; what external decision-makers then do with it (integrate, adopt, fund) is a change in policy among partners and belongs to KPI-OC39.
primaryObjective: PO5 Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved), PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Gender Equality, Youth and Social Inclusion
sdgTarget: None. SDG target 5.c (adopt and strengthen sound policies and enforceable legislation for the promotion of gender equality) is the matching target, but its official indicator 5.c.1 measures the proportion of countries whose public financial management systems track and publish allocations for gender equality: a property of national fiscal systems, not a count of instruments an organization helps develop.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Results Framework: no CGIAR standard indicator counts GEYSI-responsive instruments at development stage, so this is a CIMMYT-defined indicator. Developed instruments are reportable as CGIAR outputs; the related standard indicator, "number of new or significantly updated policies/strategies/legal instruments/programs/budgets/investments", sits at outcome level (policy change); its general counterpart in this toolbox is KPI-OC37, and KPI-OC39 counts its GEYSI subset, not this count. Bar 1 of the qualifying test, covering the women group, is CGIAR's enhanced gender scoring system at 1B or above. No CGIAR scale equivalent to it exists for youth or for social inclusion more widely, so bar 2, covering the youth group and any other named social group, rests on the structural provision test. CGIAR does tag every output and outcome for gender equality on a three-level scale (not targeted 0, significant 1, principal 2); it cannot serve as a bar here, since it has no youth or social-inclusion counterpart, carries no responsive level, and scores CGIAR's own results rather than external instruments.
definition: Counts the distinct GEYSI-responsive policy or investment instruments developed with CIMMYT support in the reporting year. An instrument is GEYSI-responsive when it clears one of two bars: for women, CGIAR's enhanced gender scoring system at 1B or above; for youth or another named social group, at least one explicit provision, a named action, target, eligibility rule or resource allocation, directed at the group and traceable in its text. Developed means the document was drafted, designed, or formally revised with a documented CIMMYT technical contribution made no later than the instrument's completion date. Later adoption or implementation is measured separately, by KPI-OC39.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's evidence and policy engagement are producing concrete instruments that embed gender equity in agrifood policy and investment, rather than gender commitments remaining declaratory. It is the countable entry point of the gender-in-policy results chain leading to provisions integrated into adopted policies and investment decisions (KPI-OC39) and public policies enacted that support smallholder resilience and to which CIMMYT contributed (KPI-I15). Used by project management to track policy-engagement delivery and by institutional and donor reporting on gender equality and social inclusion at system level.
projectSpecificApplication: State which instruments the project supports, the owning institution of each, the countries and policy scale covered, and the form CIMMYT's contribution takes. Do not change the unit, the GEYSI-responsiveness test, or the counting rule. If applying the indicator as defined is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count informs (for example, a donor-required deliverable under a gender-in-policy component, or an internal milestone trigger: no draft instruments by a set date prompts a review of the engagement strategy with the owning institutions).
projectTypesNotApplicable: seed systems and deployment and digital agriculture and AI
projectTypesRaw:
System change and transformation.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, breeding and varietal development, applied agronomy and farming systems, seed systems and deployment and digital agriculture and AI, which do not develop policy or investment instruments.
unit: Number (count of distinct instruments)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more GEYSI-responsive policy or investment instruments were developed with CIMMYT support. It counts instruments developed; whether one is then adopted and applied is measured by KPI-OC39.
disaggregationRequired: Required: policy scale or level (local / national / global), per the register; and instrument type (policy or strategy, guideline, investment design), since a national policy and a project-level investment design are achievements of very different weight; and the group or groups each instrument qualified under (women; youth; other named social group), an instrument qualifying under more than one appearing in each, so the group subtotals can exceed the count and are never summed.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country or region; sector or value chain; owning institution type (government, development bank or investor, regional body); depth of gender integration (gender responsive vs gender principal (2)), for the women group only, the scale carrying no equivalent for the others.
unitOfObservation:
The policy or investment instrument, recorded under the template's result object value, under which a policy instrument or an investment design falls. The measurand is a document, so the farm measurement levels do not apply: an instrument is not observed at Trial / Station, Farm / Plot or Household level. The instrument is the unit of observation and the only level at which the indicator is measured.

Regional / Aggregated and above are aggregation levels.

An instrument is one record in the reporting year in which its development is completed, and revisions within that year add no record; the version reported is the one meeting the qualification criterion, and the version identifier travels with the count. A substantive strengthening revision completed in a later year creates a new record (Eligibility).
calculationSummary: Value: count of distinct policy or investment instruments that (a) were developed, drafted, or formally revised in the reporting year with a documented CIMMYT technical contribution made no later than the instrument's completion date and (b) contain at least one explicit qualifying provision under the test in the Definition. Inclusion: an instrument counts once the developed document exists (draft policy, published guideline, completed investment design) and both tests are evidenced: CIMMYT's contribution (drafted or redrafted text, analysis the instrument cites, documented participation in its drafting, or the owning institution's written acknowledgment; attendance at a consultation alone is not a contribution) and the qualifying provisions (the specific clauses, targets, or allocations identified in the instrument text, with the group each serves). Co-developed instruments count once, regardless of how many CIMMYT projects contributed. Exclusion: instruments mentioning gender only in preamble or general language with no explicit provision; instruments CIMMYT merely commented on without a substantive documented contribution; instruments still at concept stage with no drafted document. Missing data: a logged instrument without the document or the contribution evidence on file is excluded until the evidence is filed. Repeated observations: each distinct instrument counts once, in the year its development with CIMMYT support is completed; a formal revision completed in a later reporting year counts as a new record only if it is a substantive strengthening revision as Eligibility criteria defines it.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: CIMMYT project policy-engagement and deliverable records logging each instrument, its owning institution, policy scale, the evidence of CIMMYT's contribution, and the qualifying provisions identified in the instrument text with the group each serves, cross-checked against project technical reports. The instrument's own text, where the owning institution has published or formally circulated it, is a Recommended source for the instrument's existence and its provisions, wherever it is retrieved. Fallback DS4: partner records and third-party trackers (partner archives, donor and policy trackers) used to reconstruct the count where CIMMYT's own log is incomplete; an instrument evidenced only this way is Fallback-sourced and reported beside the pooled figure, because such records rarely document CIMMYT's contribution. Not applicable DS1: this indicator counts institutional deliverables from records, not data collected from respondents. Not applicable DS3: geospatial data cannot identify a policy instrument or its provisions. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced data cannot verify an instrument's content or CIMMYT's role in its development.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether Recommended or Fallback was used. If Fallback, state why the project's own engagement log was incomplete and which external records were used.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). The register entry itself is the tool: each record names the instrument, its type, owning institution, policy scale, completion date, the CIMMYT contribution evidence, and the specific qualifying provisions with the group each serves.
collectionFrequency: Continuous: each instrument is logged as its development is completed
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the instrument's development with CIMMYT support was completed
baselineRequired: No. An annual flow count that starts from zero each reporting year; there is no pre-project stock to measure. Change over time is read from the annual series itself.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One reporting year. Levels widen the set of instruments; they never widen the domain.

Weight: one per distinct instrument record.

B: Combination method: sum. Total = Σ distinct instruments meeting the qualification criterion in the domain.

C: Levels and operations. Instrument. The record itself; nothing is combined at this level. Also report: the instrument type and the provision that qualified it.

D: Never pooled. Qualifying with non-qualifying instruments. Instruments developed with instruments adopted, which is KPI-OC39. Recommended-sourced with Fallback-sourced instruments: an instrument evidenced only from partner or third-party records (Fallback DS4) is reported beside the pooled figure with a note and not blended in, and the same project's Recommended-sourced instruments are summed.

E: Deduplication and coverage. The persistent instrument identifier carrying the jurisdiction and the version, so an instrument supported by two projects is counted once. Where an instrument is revised, the qualifying version is named. This is a census of instruments meeting the qualification criterion, drawn from CIMMYT's own engagement records, not a sample estimate: it carries no sampling error and no coefficient-of-variation band.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
The qualifying threshold is two bars over three groups, as the Definition sets out: bar 1 covers the women group, bar 2 the youth group and any other named social group. This paragraph sets out bar 1, CGIAR's enhanced gender scoring system, at 1B or above. This is not the three-level gender equality tagging system (Not targeted 0, Significant 1, Principal 2), which carries no 1B and is used for micro-level monitoring within Initiatives; the enhanced scoring system is the macro-level one and is what this threshold reads. CGIAR scores gender integration on four levels, adapted from the OECD gender equality policy marker and set out in Science Groups Evaluations: Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (CGIAR IAES, 2025):

Gender blind (0) a gender analysis was conducted, its findings used so the intervention does no harm, and gender-disaggregated data is collected.

Gender accommodative / aware (1A) gender equality is an objective but not the main one; at least two explicit gender-specific outputs with adequate funding; data and indicators disaggregated by gender and analyzed.

Gender responsive (1B) at least one explicit gender equality outcome; resident gender expertise or capacity; indicators that monitor participation of and differential benefits to diverse men and women.

Gender principal (2) gender equality is the main objective and fundamental to the design.

An instrument qualifies at 1B or above. At 0 and 1A an instrument can collect sex-disaggregated data and name women while committing to no outcome, which bar 1 excludes. The level assigned, and the provision that carries it, are recorded with each counted instrument.

Three adaptations apply. CGIAR's scale scores Initiatives and projects; this indicator counts policy and investment instruments, so the scoring is applied to the instrument's own text and commitments, not to the team that drafted it. First, of 1B's three published conditions (an explicit gender-equality outcome; resident gender expertise or capacity; indicators monitoring differential benefit to men and women), only the first, the explicit gender-equality outcome, is applied as the bar: an instrument is a document, not a team, so it can state an outcome commitment but cannot itself hold resident staffing capacity or run its own monitoring program. Second, the other two conditions are recorded where the instrument's own text provides for them (for example a resourcing clause naming a gender specialist, or a built-in monitoring requirement) and are not required for a qualifying score, since an external instrument does not carry a delivery team of its own. Third, the conditions of levels 0 and 1A are not prerequisites for 1B; they are recorded where present.

An instrument that mentions women or youth without a named provision does not qualify. A reference in a preamble, a statement of principle, or a disaggregation requirement with no action attached is not a provision. To qualify under bar 2, an instrument must contain at least one of: a named action, a target, an eligibility rule, or a resource allocation, directed at youth or at another named social group and traceable in the text. A provision directed at women is judged under bar 1. An explicit gender-equality outcome is a stated change in women's position the instrument commits to, such as a narrower gender gap in access, income, rights or representation; an activity, a participation count or a disaggregation requirement is not an outcome. A participation quota or target for women alone is a reach target and does not clear bar 1. A provision directed at a group defined by sex and another attribute is judged under bar 1 for the women group; it can qualify under bar 2 only for its non-sex group where that is youth, and never as another named social group by virtue of the sex-defined sub-group. The qualifying provision is quoted or cited by clause in the record, so the judgment is checkable rather than asserted.

Include instruments developed or revised in the reporting year with a documented CIMMYT technical contribution made no later than the instrument's completion date; adoption is not a qualifying event here (see the counting-milestone rule below).

Exclude instruments still at concept stage with no drafted document, and instruments assessed and not qualifying, which are counted separately: the ratio of assessed to qualifying is what shows the criterion is being applied.

The counting milestone is a completed draft or design carrying documented CIMMYT contribution, not a later adoption event: this indicator counts what CIMMYT developed, and whether the instrument is then adopted is what KPI-OC39 counts. The completion date is the date the owning institution finalizes the text or design for its approval route.

A substantive strengthening revision of an already-counted instrument creates a new record, where substantive means a move up CGIAR's enhanced gender scoring system or an expansion of the provision's scope, including to a group the instrument did not previously carry; a revision restating existing provisions does not.

KPI-O42, KPI-OC39, KPI-OC34, KPI-OC37 and KPI-I15 share one instrument identifier, so the development-to-adoption-to-enactment pipeline is traceable, revision records link into a sequence, and one instrument is never reported as several separate results.
limitations: Mentioning a qualifying group is not enough by itself. Eligibility criteria and missing data sets out the two-bar test in full. A reference in a preamble, a statement of principle, or a disaggregation requirement with no action attached does not meet bar 2 (youth or another named social group); a mention of women with no explicit gender-equality outcome does not meet bar 1 (women).

Development is not adoption: a drafted GEYSI-responsive instrument may never be adopted, funded, or implemented, so this count evidences CIMMYT's policy-engagement delivery, not policy change. Adoption evidence belongs to KPI-OC39 and enactment to KPI-I15.

The test requires judgment at the line between general language about women or youth and an explicit provision; the control is the register record naming the specific provisions, so each classification can be audited against the instrument text.

"Instrument" spans products of very different weight, from a national policy to a single investment design, so raw counts are not comparable across projects or years until the scale and instrument-type disaggregations are applied; one national policy may matter more than five guidelines.

Attribution is a contribution claim: instruments are developed by their owning institutions under many influences, and CIMMYT support ranges from leading the drafting to providing one evidence input. The contribution-evidence requirement bounds the claim but does not grade its depth. Nor does the count show that CIMMYT's contribution bore on the provision that qualifies the instrument: unlike KPI-OC39, this sheet binds the contribution to the instrument, not to the qualifying provision.

An increase means CIMMYT supported the development of more GEYSI-responsive instruments, not that gender, youth or inclusion gaps narrowed; pair with KPI-OC39, KPI-I15, and the pathway's empowerment indicators (KPI-O28, KPI-I08) for the results chain.

The two bars sit at different real-world difficulty, which the headline count alone does not disclose. Bar 1 requires an explicit gender-equality outcome, a substantive commitment; bar 2 is any one of four structural provisions (a named action, a target, an eligibility rule, or a resource allocation), a lower and more easily met floor, and bar 1 carries no equivalent lighter-touch alternative. The group each instrument qualified under is a required disaggregation, so the count is always reported broken down by group.
subMetrics: None. Instrument types and policy-scale levels are disaggregations of the same count, not separately calculated metrics. Related indicators in the results chain have their own sheets: KPI-OC39 (policies, investment decisions, or transformation processes integrating gender-equity and social-inclusion provisions, the outcome this output feeds) and KPI-I15 (public policies enacted that support smallholder resilience and to which CIMMYT contributed, the impact the chain reaches in the Policy, finance & market systems pathway).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E focal point, logging each instrument with its evidence. Validation: project MEAL officer, checking the contribution evidence and the qualifying provisions against the instrument text; a boundary case, where the officer cannot tell whether a provision clears its bar, is decided by CIMMYT's gender research lead, with the reason recorded against the instrument. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (de-duplication on the shared instrument identifier and the CIMMYT-wide sum, per Aggregation rule). Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
