name: Time spent on unpaid agricultural and domestic work by household members in CIMMYT intervention areas, by sex
volumeTitle: Gender equality, youth and social inclusion
resultsLevel: Output, as the register classes it. This indicator reports a measured state, the hours as they stand in the reporting period, and makes no claim that anything changed; the change is KPI-OC64, at outcome.
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Contributing, contribution only: PO4.
cgiarImpactArea: Gender Equality, Youth and Social Inclusion.
sdgTarget: Target 5.4. Not reportable as indicator 5.4.1. That indicator is the proportion of time in a day spent on unpaid domestic and care work for a nationally representative population, and excludes unpaid agricultural work. This sheet reports hours per person per week for the households a project reaches, and includes own-use agricultural production. The activity classification is shared; the population, the statistic and the scope are not.
otherFrameworks: The project-level Women's Empowerment in Agriculture Index (pro-WEAI) carries work balance among its instrumental-agency indicators (Seymour et al., 2023, Table A1). No domain count or weight is asserted here.
definition:
Hours per person per week spent on unpaid work, recorded by activity and reported separately by sex. Unpaid work is work performed without payment on the household's own holding or in the household itself, and covers two classes: unpaid agricultural work, own-use production on the household's plots, animals and post-harvest handling; and unpaid domestic and care work, the activities of ICATUS 2016 divisions 3 and 4, the same two divisions SDG indicator 5.4.1 uses.

Hours are recorded and never valued here. Valuation of household labor happens once in the toolbox, at KPI-OC63.
rationale:
Supplies the measured level that KPI-OC64 reports the change in. Without it a change in unpaid work would be computed from whatever each project happened to record, against no fixed activity list, respondent rule or unit.

It also closes a gap the labor thread left open. KPI-O59 and KPI-O60 record hours on target-crop and target-species production as a denominator for productivity, so they capture unpaid agricultural work only where it touches the target product, and they treat sex disaggregation as optional. Unpaid domestic and care work is not captured by them at all. A household can raise its measured productivity while its unpaid burden rises, and neither of those sheets would show it.
projectSpecificApplication: The population is fixed: the households of the people the project reached, drawn from its participant records, surveyed as a census of them or as a probability sample with weights; never a population-based sample of all households in the area. State the geography, the reference period, the household members in scope with the minimum age applied, and whether hours are captured by stylized recall or by diary. The activity classification, the unit and the calculation method are unchanged.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision this figure serves. Example: a project introducing a labor-saving technology reports it because a practice that raises output while shifting hours onto women has not improved the household, and the shift is visible only here.
projectTypesNotApplicable: upstream discovery science and breeding and varietal development
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science and breeding and varietal development, which do not reach households; digital agriculture and AI, which reports through the pathways its tools serve.
unit: Hours per person per week. Reported to one decimal place, separately by sex, and never as a household total: a household figure conceals the distribution, and the distribution is what the measure exists to show.
directionOfChange: Not directional. More hours are not a worse result and fewer are not an improvement in themselves; a fall in a woman's unpaid hours matters only alongside what replaced them. This indicator reports a level, and the interpretation belongs to KPI-OC64 read with the productivity and income indicators.
disaggregationRequired:
Sex. Not optional here, unlike on KPI-O59 and KPI-O60. A figure that is not sex-disaggregated does not answer the question the indicator exists to answer, and cannot be pooled with one that is.

Activity class, agricultural or domestic and care, reported separately and never summed into a single "unpaid work" figure.

Both fail the poolability test, and Block A restates them as pooling-domain prohibitions.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Age band of the household member; ICATUS division within each activity class; whether the household holds a labor-saving technology the project introduced; farm size class, with the bands stated.
unitOfObservation: The individual household member, with hours recorded per person. The measurand is a person's time. The household roster with a persistent member identifier anchors the series, because the same person must be identifiable across rounds for KPI-OC64 to compute a change.
calculationSummary:
First, fix the activity list. Agricultural activities are those already in the labor module for KPI-O59 and KPI-O60, extended to the household's whole holding rather than the target crop or species alone. Domestic and care activities are ICATUS 2016 divisions 3, unpaid domestic services for household and family members, and 4, unpaid caregiving services for household and family members. The list is fixed at baseline and held constant across rounds.

Second, record hours per member per activity. Hours per person per week = Σ hours recorded across the activities in the class, for that person, in the reference week. A weekly total is formed only from contemporaneous recording that covers the full seven-day reference week, or from stylized recall of that week on the Fallback route, and the week's hours are summed directly. A contemporaneous record covering fewer days is reported as same-day observations, the hours recorded for that person on each day covered, flagged as such and excluded from any weekly total or weekly aggregate (see Eligibility criteria and missing data).

Third, record the main activity and childcare separately. Where two activities are performed at once, the main activity is recorded as such, and supervisory childcare performed alongside it is recorded in a separate field. This departs from the main-activity-only convention deliberately: the SDG 5.4.1 metadata states that recording the main activity alone means that, for a respondent cooking while looking after a child, "time spent caring for children is not accounted for", and that this underestimates care time. A measure of women's burden that systematically drops supervisory care would be wrong in a known direction. Supervisory and secondary care hours are recorded and reported as their own figure and are never summed into the primary-activity class total: the two happen at once rather than in sequence, and adding a simultaneous activity's hours to the main activity's would double-count the same clock time.

A 168-hour-per-person-per-week data-quality ceiling applies as a check, not a cap. Total recorded hours for a person in a week (the primary-activity total; supervisory care is checked against the same ceiling separately, since it is a separate figure) cannot exceed 168, the number of hours in a seven-day week. A record exceeding it is flagged for recheck against the source record; it is never silently capped to 168 or accepted as reported, since either would hide a data-entry or unit error rather than surface it.

Fourth, report by sex. The mean for a sex = Σ hours over members of that sex ÷ number of those members. Members with zero recorded hours are included in the denominator; excluding them turns a mean over the population into a mean over participants and inflates it.
dataSource:
Recommended DS1: contemporaneous recording during the reference week, by diary or by a short repeated instrument, so hours are reported as they occur.

Fallback DS1: stylized recall of the reference week, reported separately from contemporaneously recorded values and never blended with them. Recall is a survey mode and takes the survey class. Recall is the practical mode in most settings and the sheet permits it; what it does not permit is presenting the two as one series. A single-day diary, such as the 24-hour diary SDG indicator 5.4.1 and the A-WEAI time module use, is not a route to this indicator: it records one day, not the reference week, and is reported, where collected, as same-day observations under Eligibility's rule.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Name the instrument, the collection mode, the reference week, the minimum age applied, and the system holding the household roster and member identifiers.
collectionInstrument:
The labor module, extended. The module already attached to the KPI-O23 plot record and the KPI-O24 animal record records, per activity, the number of people, the shift length and whether labor was hired or supplied by the household: a headcount and a duration, not a named person. Three additions make it serve this indicator: the domestic and care activities of ICATUS divisions 3 and 4; a required sex field on the person supplying the hours rather than the optional one KPI-O59 and KPI-O60 carry; and a persistent person identifier recorded on every activity record, tying each record to a specific, identifiable household member from the household roster rather than only counting how many people worked. A people-count-plus-shift-length record cannot be matched across survey rounds, and KPI-OC64's paired difference is computed per person, so without this addition the instrument cannot supply the series KPI-OC64 requires.

Extending the existing module is what keeps the agricultural and domestic hours on one instrument and one respondent per member. A separately fielded time-use survey would put the two classes on different samples and weeks, so they could not be read side by side for the same people.

Respondent: each member in scope reports their own hours, interviewed individually. A report by another household member on a member's behalf is recorded with a proxy flag, and proxy-reported hours are reported beside the self-reported figure, never pooled with it.
collectionFrequency: Once per round, on the round schedule of the labor module the questions attach to.
referencePeriod: One stated reference week, repeated at the same point in the agricultural calendar in every round. Unpaid agricultural hours move with the season, so a baseline week in land preparation and an endline week in a slack period would produce a fall that describes the calendar rather than the intervention.
baselineRequired: Yes, where KPI-OC64 is reported. The baseline must be pre-adoption: a baseline taken after a labor-saving technology is in use measures the world the intervention already changed.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One sex, one activity class, one reporting year, one country, one collection mode, one minimum age and one activity list version. Levels widen the set of people; they never widen the domain. No combined figure exists across any of these; the figures are reported side by side, one per domain.

Weight: one per person, multiplied by the household's survey weight where households were drawn as a probability sample, including members recording zero hours; the weights are stated.

B: Combination method: ratio of sums.

Recompute from member records; never average household means or project means.

C: Levels and operations.

D: Never pooled. Sexes. Activity classes. Diary-collected hours with stylized-recall hours, which are not the same measurement. Figures using different minimum ages. Figures using different activity lists. Primary-activity hours with supervisory or secondary care hours. Self-reported with proxy-reported hours. A sample estimate computed without its survey weights. Levels with KPI-OC64's changes.

E: Deduplication and coverage. The persistent household member identifier, applied from Household level upward. Coverage and precision travel with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands used in official statistics: 16.5 percent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 percent released flagged, above 33.3 percent not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one de-duplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above, and a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place. The collection mode and the activity list version travel with the figure. Across projects no union is computed, and a figure combining projects is labeled not de-duplicated across projects.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Include household members at or above the minimum age the project states, present in the household for the reference week. The minimum age is stated and held constant; it is not inferred.

Exclude paid work of any kind, which is not the measurand, and work performed for another household in exchange for payment in cash or in kind.

A member with genuinely zero hours in a class is recorded as zero, not as missing. Zero is a measurement; blank is not, and treating the two alike overstates the mean.

Missing the reference week for a member: that member is excluded from both numerator and denominator for that round and reported as a coverage shortfall with the count.

A contemporaneous record covering fewer than the full seven days of the reference week is reported as same-day observations, not a weekly record (Calculation method): it is excluded from the weekly numerator and denominator for that round and reported separately as a same-day figure, not counted as missing data or a coverage shortfall.

Absent members are excluded with the reason recorded, because seasonal migration removes exactly the people whose absence redistributes work.
limitations: A level, not a verdict. The indicator says how many hours were recorded. It does not say whether that is too many, whether it changed, or whether CIMMYT caused it. The change is KPI-OC64 and it carries its own baseline requirement.

Recall and contemporaneous recording are different measurements. Hours reported from memory after the fact are not the same quantity as hours recorded as they occur; Block D forbids pooling them, and the mode travels with every figure. The direction and size of that difference in CIMMYT settings is unmeasured, so no correction is applied and no equivalence is assumed between the two modes.

Simultaneous activities are the known weakness of any time-use measure. Recording only the main activity underestimates care, on the SDG 5.4.1 metadata's own statement. The separate childcare field reduces the loss; it does not eliminate it, and no time-use instrument does.

Self-report, with the respondent's own interests in it. Hours are reported by the person who worked them; a proxy report by another household member is flagged and kept beside the self-reported figure (Collection instrument).
Coverage is not representativeness. A pooled figure describes the members recorded, not all members of the reached households, unless they were drawn as a probability sample of them and weighted.

Seasonality dominates the agricultural class. A figure from one reference week describes that week. Comparisons across rounds are valid only at the same point in the agricultural calendar, which Reference period requires.

Water and fuel collection sit in neither class. The agricultural class covers own-use production on the household's plots and animals and post-harvest handling, and the SDG 5.4.1 metadata's list of domestic and care activities does not include fetching water or gathering fuel, so those hours are not recorded here.

Own-household scope only, narrower than the SDG 5.4.1 concept it otherwise shares. This indicator measures unpaid work performed on the household's own holding or within the household itself. SDG indicator 5.4.1's own concept of unpaid domestic and care work is not restricted that way: it also covers unpaid care provided to family members living in a different household. Reciprocal or other-household unpaid labor is out of scope here, disclosed as excluded rather than left unstated; it is neither counted toward this indicator nor netted out of it.
subMetrics:
Hours by activity class, by sex, and the count of members recording zero are each retained and reported alongside the mean. A mean without its denominator and its zero count cannot be recomputed, and an institutional figure is recomputed from member records rather than averaged from project means.

Relationship to other indicators. KPI-OC64 reports the change in this level and is computed from this series only. KPI-O59 and KPI-O60 record hours on target-crop and target-species production as a productivity denominator; they overlap with this indicator's agricultural class but are neither a subset nor a superset of it, since they are narrower in scope and wider in labor type, and the two are never summed. KPI-OC63 is the only place in the toolbox where household labor hours are given a monetary value; this sheet records hours and never values them. KPI-I08 measures decision-making power, and time burden is not a proxy for it: a woman may gain hours and lose say.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
Full-week basis: the same SDG indicator metadata, indicator 5.4.1, section 4.c ("Method of computation," PDF pp. 5-6), states that where the reference period is one week, weekly data are averaged over the seven days of the week to obtain the daily average; its diaries are 24-hour diaries (section 3.a). It states no method for building a weekly total from a subset of days; this sheet's rule that a contemporaneous record forms a weekly total only where it covers the full seven-day reference week (Calculation method) is the sheet's own.

Work balance as an empowerment indicator: International Food Policy Research Institute (2024), Project-level Women's Empowerment in Agriculture Index (pro-WEAI), carries work balance among its instrumental-agency indicators (Seymour et al., 2023, Table A1); no domain count or indicator weight is asserted here: https://weai.ifpri.info/versions/pro-weai/

Work-balance name and adequacy formula: Seymour, G., Faas, S., Ferguson, N., Heckert, J., Malapit, H., Meinzen-Dick, R., Quisumbing, A. R., & van Biljon, C. (2023). A multi-country validation and sensitivity analysis of the project-level Women's Empowerment in Agriculture Index (Pro-WEAI) (IFPRI Discussion Paper 2201). International Food Policy Research Institute. Table A1 (Appendix, printed p. 37, PDF p. 44): the current instrumental-agency indicator's name (work balance) and adequacy cutoff; does not reproduce the underlying questionnaire's item-level activity list. https://hdl.handle.net/10568/140313

Precision bands: Statistics Canada quality guidelines, for the coefficient-of-variation release thresholds in Block E, adopted as CIMMYT's own convention for release with Statistics Canada named as the precedent.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: Content owner: the CIMMYT MEAL unit, with the gender research lead as technical reviewer.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Collection: project enumerators fielding the extended labor module. Validation: project M&E officer. Calculation: project M&E, applying the formula in Calculation method. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 8 · Gender equality, youth and social inclusion — Reference sheet KPI-O61

name: Difference (percentage points) between male and female smallholder farmers in the adoption of improved practices in CIMMYT intervention areas
volumeTitle: Gender equality, youth and social inclusion
resultsLevel: Outcome. Adoption is a change in practice among beneficiaries, which is the Core's definition of an outcome; the gap is a contrast between two such outcome rates.
domain: GEYSI, as recorded in the register: it measures equity in adoption, not adoption itself.
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Contributing: none. Household-level gender equity sits under PO3; systemic gender integration in policies and investments is measured separately (KPI-OC39).
cgiarImpactArea: Gender Equality, Youth and Social Inclusion: a direct equity measure.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest SDG gender-in-agriculture indicator, 5.a.1, measures ownership or secure rights over agricultural land by sex, a resource-rights construct, not practice adoption. No SDG indicator measures a sex gap in adoption.
otherFrameworks: The 32 CGIAR Common Results Framework standard indicators include a sex-disaggregated adoption count ("number of people using the innovation, disaggregated by gender") but no gap measure. It supplies the inputs from which this gap is computed but does not report the gap itself, a CIMMYT-defined measure.
definition: The difference, in percentage points, between the share of male and the share of female smallholders among KPI-OC16's eligible population (assisted persons whose direct support ended before the start of the most recent completed cropping season) adopting a named improved practice in CIMMYT intervention areas, computed as the male adoption rate minus the female adoption rate for that practice. Where a project promotes several practices, the gap is computed and reported one practice at a time, never as a single composite across every promoted practice: a composite is dominated by whichever practice is most widespread and can hide the practice where the gap is largest. A derived contrast of two sex-specific rates on the same practice, population and survey round.
rationale: Answers whether the improved practices CIMMYT promotes are taken up by women and men equally, the equity test of adoption: a gap signals that women face steeper constraints (inputs, credit, information, labor, decision-making power) in acting on the same opportunity. CIMMYT tracks it because a productivity gain that widens gender inequality falls short of PO3's inclusive livelihoods aim, and it feeds reporting under the CGIAR Gender Equality, Youth and Social Inclusion Impact Area.
projectSpecificApplication: Describes this project's intervention areas, promoted-practice list, survey timing and the smallholder threshold it declares under Annex B. The definition, unit, and calculation method stay unchanged. A project that can only capture household-level adoption, with no sex recorded for the adopter, raises this with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining the indicator here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision, donor requirement, or reporting need served. Example: a project tracks the gap because its donor requires evidence that scaling benefits women, and a widening gap mid-project triggers a review of how extension, input access, or training reaches female farmers.
projectTypesNotApplicable: none. The gap is computed from KPI-OC16's survey, and any project type can reach farmers with training or an improved package
projectTypesRaw:
Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.

Not applicable: none. The gap is computed from KPI-OC16's survey, and any project type can reach farmers with training or an improved package.
unit: Percentage points (male adoption rate minus female adoption rate)
directionOfChange: Reference value: zero, which is parity. The value is the male adoption rate minus the female rate, so zero means the two rates are equal; the reference comes from the construction of the measure and is not a target set here. A positive value means men adopt at a higher rate. Movement toward zero is an improvement where it comes from a rise in the lower rate, on the cohort comparison (Baseline required); a gap that narrows because the higher rate fell is reported as a narrowing by decline, not as an improvement. A negative value means women adopt at a higher rate and is a reverse gap, not a further improvement.
disaggregationRequired: Required: Age (youth/non-youth), computing the gap within each age band; the youth band is 15 to 30, stated once in Core §4.1, and projects record date of birth or exact age so other bands (for example a donor band of 15 to 29) can be derived. Sex is not a disaggregation here: it is the contrast the indicator is built on, recorded as male/female at minimum per CGIAR's sex-disaggregated data standards.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Practice or technology type of the named item (crop genetics, soil fertility, irrigation, climate adaptation, and so on), as a label on each per-item gap, never a gap computed across items of one type. Country and agroecological zone. Household headship of the adopter, where recorded.
unitOfObservation: The individual smallholder farmer, with sex recorded. The gap is a property of two populations compared at one moment, so both rates must come from the same sample frame; a male rate and a female rate drawn from different frames do not form a gap.
calculationSummary: The gap is computed one named practice at a time, never as a composite across every promoted practice. A named practice is any one item on the project's promoted list, whether an input, a technology, a practice or a variety. Measurement population: the smallholders among KPI-OC16's eligible population, that is, registry persons eligible under KPI-OC16's Eligibility, with the frame drawn, the end of direct support dated, the season test applied and frame errors treated exactly as KPI-OC16's Data source (Frame DS2) sets out. Smallholder status is set from the household's landholding at baseline, recorded by KPI-OC16's adoption module, against the threshold the project declares under Annex B, and is fixed for the person across rounds; where Annex B's two-tier route applies, each tier is its own population and its own gap, reported side by side. Adoption is measured as on KPI-OC16: continued use, beyond the intervention, of the named practice by a farmer who was not using it at baseline; a farmer already using it at baseline stays in that sex's denominator and out of its numerator, and the pre-existing-use share is reported by sex. Male adoption rate: numerator: male smallholder farmers in the measurement population reporting adoption of the one named promoted practice being measured, by individual self-report from each sampled farmer, never one household member reporting for another; denominator: all male smallholder farmers in the measurement population; value = (numerator / denominator) x 100, each term survey-weighted as Aggregation rule Block B sets out. Female adoption rate: computed identically for women, on the same named practice. Indicator value = male rate minus female rate, in percentage points, for that practice. Both rates must come from the same survey round, population frame, and named practice. Inclusion: smallholder farmers in the measurement population only; the declared threshold travels with the value. Exclusion: non-smallholders; registry persons not meeting KPI-OC16's season test; sampled persons found at interview to fail it (frame errors, as on KPI-OC16); individuals whose sex is not recorded (excluded from both rates, their count and share reported as Aggregation rule, Block C sets out); individuals whose smallholder status is not recorded (excluded from both rates, counted by sex). Missing data: individuals with no adoption response are non-respondents, excluded from the denominator; report the non-response share by sex, because differential non-response between men and women biases the gap directly. Repeated observations: each farmer counts once per measurement round in each practice's sex-specific rate; if surveyed twice in a round, the first completed interview counts.
dataSource: Recommended, DS1 (Censuses and surveys): KPI-OC16's adoption survey, fielded on KPI-OC16's sample of its eligible registry subset, recording each farmer's sex, age, household landholding at baseline and adoption of each promoted practice. It is the same instrument that measures the adoption-rate indicator (KPI-OC16), so the gap needs no separate collection. Frame, DS2 (Administrative and registry data): KPI-OC16's registry frame, by pointer to KPI-OC16's Data source (Frame DS2): the eligible registry subset, its end-of-support dating and its season test are KPI-OC16's. Project M&E adoption-monitoring records and partner reports are not a route to the value: monitoring visits over-sample engaged farmers and miss quiet non-adopters, and carry no sampling design the release rule (Aggregation rule, Block E) can apply to; where no survey round was fielded, no gap is reported. Not applicable, DS3 (Geospatial and Earth observation): satellites may observe practices on the land but never the sex of the adopter. Not applicable, DS4 (Secondary and international databases): national surveys cannot resolve CIMMYT intervention areas or the promoted-practice list. Not applicable, DS5 (Citizen-generated and other non-traditional data): cannot be matched to the measurement population with the identifiers and sex records the two denominators require.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State the survey round used. Example: "Used Recommended: adoption module of the project's endline survey round, stratified random sample of 600 farmers (300 women, 300 men) from the registry persons meeting KPI-OC16's season test."
collectionInstrument: The KPI-OC16 adoption module, as KPI-OC16's Collection instrument sets it out, asking per promoted practice: (a) use before the project (baseline reference); (b) use in the most recent completed cropping season; and (c) the season in which project support for it last reached the person (the last project training session, package delivery or purchase through a project partner channel, advisory or mechanization service, or the end of a service period for it; field days, sensitization meetings and other one-off informational contacts not counting), or that support has not ended, or that the person received none. The support-ended season is read as KPI-OC16 reads it for the frame-error test (KPI-OC16 Data source, Frame DS2). Respondent: the individual farmer, self-reporting; interview women and men individually rather than accepting one household member's report for both. Sex, age, and the household's landholding at baseline recorded. Mode: face-to-face or telephone interview.
collectionFrequency: The KPI-OC16 survey rounds: at least one round after direct support ends, typically midline and endline, with both sexes measured in the same round.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Between waves, the latest measured value is carried forward with its measurement year noted.
referencePeriod: As KPI-OC16: use in the most recent completed cropping season before the interview, on the intervention area's declared calendar (KPI-OC16 Data source, Frame DS2), a season being assigned to its harvest year, referenced to the farmer's pre-intervention baseline.
baselineRequired: Yes, in two senses. Each rate needs the per-farmer baseline reference KPI-OC16 requires, with its recall-based fallback stated as such; where none can be established, neither rate is computed and no gap is reported. A narrowing or widening claim also needs a reference gap, and since adoption measured against each farmer's own pre-intervention practice has no pre-intervention value, the reference is the gap at the first round measured after support ended, stated with its round. The later round's gap is then recomputed on persons whose direct support ended before the start of the first round's reference season, so both rounds describe one cohort; no panel design is required; the later round's headline gap is unchanged, and the cohort gap is reported beside it for the comparison. Before a second round, the gap is reported as a level, with no narrowing or widening claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One target population, the smallholders among KPI-OC16's eligible population, one reporting year, one country, one named practice. One declared smallholder threshold, as Annex B defines it; under Annex B's two-tier route each tier is its own domain. Values computed on different declared thresholds are never pooled, because a population is not the same population when its boundary moves. A gap computed across different practices describes no adoption decision. Items on different projects' promoted lists are one named practice only where the CIMMYT MEAL unit, which performs the pooled recalculation (Sheet steward: data roles), records them as one entry; an item not so recorded is reported for its own project and not pooled. Levels widen the set of farmers; they never widen the domain. Where a reporting level spans more than one country or practice, the figures are reported side by side, one per domain, and never summed across them.

Weight: one per farmer within each sex, each sampled farmer carrying KPI-OC16's survey weight, so each rate is the estimated headcount share of its sex in the smallholder eligible population for that practice. The gap is then a difference of two rates and is never itself weighted.

B: Combination method: ratio of sums.

Within a project each sum is survey-weighted over the in-scope sampled farmers and scaled as on KPI-OC16 (Data source, Frame DS2): each sex's smallholder total is KPI-OC16's estimated eligible population multiplied by that sex's weighted smallholder share among interviewed in-scope persons, and its adopters that total multiplied by the weighted share adopting the named practice among that sex's interviewed in-scope smallholders. Across projects the sums are added from project estimates within each country and practice, as KPI-OC16's Block B adds project estimates: no cross-project union is computed, and a project active in the reporting year whose latest round predates it enters with its last measured sums and its round year (the year of its last interview date, as on KPI-OC16), the pooled figure being labeled with the range of round years it combines, and the share of each sex's pooled denominator measured in each round year is reported with it.

Recompute both rates from the summed estimates at the level being reported, then difference them. Never average project-level gaps, and never difference a male and a female rate drawn from different sample frames.

C: Levels and operations. Household. The adoption status of the individual farmer; the gap is not computed at this level.

D: Never pooled. Gaps for different practices. A male and a female rate from different sample frames. Gaps with KPI-I06's or KPI-I03's headcount shares, which count a change rather than a difference between groups. Gaps with KPI-OC64's gap change, which is a change over a window rather than a difference at one moment.

E: Deduplication and coverage. Within a project the registry identifier de-duplicates the frame, as on KPI-OC16; across projects no union is computed, so a farmer can appear in two projects' estimates, and a figure combining projects carries the label Block C sets out. Both rates and both denominators travel with the gap: a gap without its rates cannot be read (Limitations). Coverage and precision travel with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands used in official statistics: 16.5 percent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 percent released flagged, above 33.3 percent not released as an estimate. The bands and the 30-record floor apply to each sex-specific rate separately, a record being one completed interview with a sampled in-scope smallholder of that sex in the measurement round, as KPI-OC16 counts records; a rate built on fewer than 30 records is not released. The gap is released only where both rates are, with its 95 percent confidence interval rather than a coefficient of variation, the gap's variance computed on the survey design, including the covariance between the two rates, never as the sum of their variances alone; the pooled rates' variances are computed from the project estimates' own sampling variances, as on KPI-OC16, and their covariance from the project estimates' own covariances. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Include smallholder farmers in KPI-OC16's eligible population (KPI-OC16's season test, Data source, Frame DS2), with smallholder status set as Calculation method sets out, adoption status recorded and sex recorded, for one named practice; a farmer already using that practice at baseline stays in the denominator and out of the numerator, with the pre-existing-use share reported by sex.

Exclude farmers whose sex is unrecorded, since neither rate can be computed for them, and report their count and share (Aggregation rule, Block C). Exclude farmers whose smallholder status is unrecorded, and report their count by sex. Exclude from both rates registry persons not meeting KPI-OC16's season test, and sampled persons found at interview to fail it, frame errors as KPI-OC16's Data source (Frame DS2) defines them.

Both rates must come from the same frame. A male rate from one survey and a female rate from another do not form a gap, and the sheet forbids differencing them.

Missing a denominator for either sex: no gap is reported.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only. The gap reflects structural constraints (land rights, credit, extension reach, labor burdens, household decision-making) that CIMMYT influences but does not control; a persistent gap does not mean the project failed women, and a narrow gap does not prove the project caused equity.

The gap can narrow for the wrong reason: it shrinks as much when male adoption falls as when female adoption rises. A pooled gap can differ in size and sign from every contributing project's gap where projects reach women and men in different proportions, so the project gaps are reported beside it.

Adoption is self-reported: each farmer reports her or his own use of the practice, and neither one household member's report for another nor household adoption attributed to its head is accepted. The respondent rule is held constant across rounds.

A percentage-point gap ignores base levels: 5 points at 10 percent adoption is a large relative inequity, the same 5 points at 80 percent is small. Comparability across projects is limited when practice lists differ.

A positive value means male smallholder farmers adopted the named practice at a higher rate than female smallholder farmers among assisted persons meeting KPI-OC16's season test. Where support ends later for one sex than the other, that sex is under-represented in the eligible population, so read the gap with the count of registry persons not meeting the season test, by sex. It does not measure empowerment, benefit, or control over the resulting income; those sit with the pathway's impact indicator (KPI-I08).

Where the named practice is a variety, adoption is variety-name-based and self-reported, as on KPI-OC16: farmers frequently misidentify or cannot name what they grow, and field observation cannot verify a variety, so read that gap as a gap in adoption of a variety the farmer names.
subMetrics:
Two, computed within this sheet:

Both rates are computed on the measurement population, the smallholders among KPI-OC16's eligible population; registry persons not meeting KPI-OC16's season test enter neither. Always report both rates alongside the gap; the gap alone cannot be interpreted. Where a project promotes more than one practice, each practice's pair of rates and gap are reported separately; there is no all-practice composite sub-metric. For the general adoption-rate construct (all sexes pooled, across the project's promoted list), see KPI-OC16. KPI-OC19 uses KPI-OC16's survey, eligibility rule, adoption test and weights, applied per named practice to the smallholders in KPI-OC16's eligible population, so its two rates reconcile with KPI-OC16's smallholder cut for that practice, not with KPI-OC16's rate.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Mission indicator, so roles are project-level. Data collection: project M&E team and enumerators. Validation: project MEAL officer (sex and identifier completeness, denominator construction, non-response by sex). Calculation: project MEAL officer produces the two rates and the gap; the CIMMYT MEAL unit adds project estimates within country and practice and recomputes the pooled rates, with no cross-project de-duplication. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.

name: Percentage of youth participating in agrifood value chains in CIMMYT intervention areas (production, enterprise, or employment)
volumeTitle: Gender equality, youth and social inclusion
resultsLevel: Outcome. The indicator reports participation in agrifood value chains among all youth resident in the intervention areas, a population outcome the pathway's youth engagement aims to move; the delivered result that precedes it, young people engaged in CIMMYT programs, is counted at output level by KPI-O29.
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Contributing: PO5 (Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities).
cgiarImpactArea: Gender Equality, Youth and Social Inclusion
sdgTarget: None (direct). The nearest correspondence is SDG indicator 8.6.1 (proportion of youth aged 15 to 24 not in education, employment or training), which measures the inverse condition (non-participation) in the general population across all sectors, not participation in agrifood value chains in intervention areas.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Common Results Framework: impact-level standard indicator "number of youth benefiting from relevant CGIAR innovations" (Gender Equality, Youth and Social Inclusion), which the register flags this outcome as feeding with contribution evidence. Donor participant-share indicators differ in construct, since their denominator is program participants while this indicator's denominator is the youth population in the intervention areas.
definition: The share of youth in CIMMYT intervention areas who participate in agrifood value-chain activities: production for sale, enterprise, or employment. Numerator: youth engaged in at least one of these activities during the reference period. Denominator: all youth resident in the intervention areas. Youth is defined as 15 to 30 years, stated once in Core §4.1; projects record date of birth or exact age so that other bands (for example a donor band of 15 to 29) can be derived without recollecting data. Unlike the youth engagement count (KPI-O29), which counts participants in CIMMYT programs, this indicator measures a condition in the youth population itself: whether young people are taking part in the agrifood economy.
rationale: Answers whether young people in the areas where CIMMYT works are entering and staying in the agrifood economy, rather than exiting to other sectors: the behavior change the youth-inclusion work aims at. Project management uses it to judge whether youth-targeted engagement translates into real participation; institutional reporting uses it as the outcome evidence behind CIMMYT's contribution to CGIAR's youth-benefit reporting. The thread's impact destination is derived rather than separately measured: the required age disaggregation of KPI-I03 and KPI-I04 supplies the youth reading of the income and jobs impacts.
projectSpecificApplication: State the intervention areas covered, the survey rounds used, and which local value-chain activities the project counts under each participation form (production, enterprise, employment). Do not change the numerator/denominator construction, the participation forms, or the age band. If the project context requires a different youth age range (for example a national definition), report against the standard band and note the national band separately; raise feasibility problems with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining the indicator here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this share informs: for example a donor logframe outcome on youth economic inclusion, or an adaptive-management trigger to redesign youth components if participation stays flat while engagement counts (KPI-O29) rise.
projectTypesNotApplicable: breeding and varietal development and digital agriculture and AI
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, breeding and varietal development and digital agriculture and AI.
unit: Percentage of youth
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of the youth resident in the intervention areas are participating in agrifood value chains. The denominator is all youth resident in the intervention areas, so the share falls when that population widens without participation keeping pace.
disaggregationRequired: Required: sex (female/male at minimum, per CGIAR sex-disaggregated data standards).
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Participation form (production; enterprise; employment); age sub-bands (for example 15 to 19, 20 to 24, 25 to 30); rural/urban; value chain or crop; migration status.
unitOfObservation: The individual young person.
calculationSummary: Numerator: youth in the intervention areas who report engaging in at least one agrifood value-chain activity (own or family production for sale, an agrifood enterprise they own or co-run, or paid agrifood employment). Production for own consumption is not participation for this indicator; counting it would saturate the measure. Denominator: all youth resident in the intervention areas, estimated from the same survey's weighted youth population. Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100, applying survey weights. Inclusion: all individuals within the youth age band resident in the intervention areas and captured by the survey design; participation in any of the three forms counts once. Exclusion: individuals outside the age band or resident outside the intervention areas; activity outside the agrifood system. Missing data: a respondent without recorded age is excluded from both numerator and denominator; a youth whose participation status cannot be established is excluded from both numerator and denominator, with the non-response share reported alongside the value. Repeated observations: one count per youth per survey round; only the first completed interview counts. A youth active in several participation forms counts once in the headline share; under the optional participation-form disaggregate they may appear once per form, so the disaggregate rows can sum to more than the headline and must never be added together.
dataSource: Recommended DS1: a representative household or youth survey in the intervention areas carrying a youth participation module: the only source that observes both the numerator (participation) and the denominator (youth population) in one design. Not applicable DS2 and DS4 for the value: project and partner registries count the youth a project reached rather than the youth population's participation, and a census projection is not the survey's weighted youth population, so a registry numerator over a census denominator is not this share; where no survey was fielded, no share is reported. Not applicable DS3: individual participation and age cannot be observed from satellite, aerial, or GIS data. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or self-nominated data cannot verify age or establish a population denominator.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State the survey round used.
collectionInstrument: For DS1: youth value-chain participation module covering the three participation forms over a 12-month recall. Respondent: the young person themselves, not a proxy adult. Where one young person is selected per household, the selection probability enters the survey weight. Mode: face-to-face or phone interview. State whether the module was embedded in a household survey (youth identified from the roster) or run as a dedicated youth survey.
collectionFrequency: Baseline and endline survey rounds; for multi-year programs, a midline every 2 to 3 years. Keep survey timing constant across rounds, because agrifood participation is seasonal.
reportingFrequency: Annually; between measurement waves, the latest measured value is carried forward with its year of measurement noted.
referencePeriod: The 12 months prior to data collection. Each reported value describes participation in that window, compared against the pre-intervention baseline round.
baselineRequired: Yes. This is an outcome share whose interpretation rests on change from the pre-intervention level. Fallbacks where no prospective baseline exists: a recall-based baseline reconstruction in the first survey round (asking about participation before the project began, flagged as recall-based), or a matched comparison area surveyed at the same time. If neither is feasible: monitoring only, no change or contribution claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One population, all youth resident in the intervention areas, one reporting year, one country, one value chain where the claim is chain-specific. Levels widen the set of young people; they never widen the domain. Where a reporting level spans more than one country, the figures are reported side by side, one per country, and never summed across them.

Weight: one per young person, each sampled young person carrying the survey weight, so the share is an estimated headcount over an estimated headcount.

B: Combination method: ratio of sums.

Recompute from youth records; never average project percentages. Where samples are population-based, apply survey weights and state them. The denominator travels with every percentage. A project active in the reporting year whose latest round predates it enters with its last measured sums and its round year, the pooled figure being labeled with the range of round years it combines.

C: Levels and operations. Household. The participation status of the individual young person.

D: Never pooled. Shares using different youth age definitions. Participation shares with KPI-O29's engagement counts, which have no denominator. A sample estimate computed without its survey weights.

E: Deduplication and coverage. On the Recommended route no participant identifier applies: the survey samples the resident youth population, not a participant list. Across projects no union is computed, and a figure combining projects whose intervention areas overlap is labeled not de-duplicated across projects, with the overlap named. The youth definition and the weighting scheme travel with every figure. Coverage and precision travel with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands used in official statistics: 16.5 percent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 percent released flagged, above 33.3 percent not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one de-duplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above, and a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Include young people resident in the intervention areas, on the stated youth definition, with participation status recorded.

Exclude participants outside the age band or resident outside the intervention areas, and report the definition applied with the figure.

Missing the denominator: no share is reported, and the numerator is not published alone.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only: youth participation in agrifood value chains also responds to labor markets, land access, migration, education, and macroeconomic conditions; CIMMYT's engagement work is one contributor among many, and the share can move for reasons unrelated to any intervention.

The value is highly sensitive to the participation definition and the age band. What minimum activity qualifies, and 15 to 30 versus 15 to 29, each shift the share by large margins; values built on different conventions are not comparable.

The denominator moves on its own. Youth migration into or out of intervention areas changes the youth population between rounds, so the share can rise or fall without any change in actual engagement; report the denominator size with each value.

Participation is not benefit. A young person counted in the numerator may be in precarious or unpaid work; this indicator does not show that participation is remunerative or decent, and CGIAR's own assessment of its standard indicators recommends reformulating the youth-benefiting indicator to state how youth are expected to benefit.

A rise means a larger share of surveyed youth reported agrifood value-chain activity in the recall window. It does not mean CIMMYT caused it, and it does not mean youth livelihoods improved; pair with the engagement output (KPI-O29) and the youth cut of the income and jobs impact indicators (KPI-I03, KPI-I04) for the contribution narrative.
subMetrics: None. The three participation forms (production; enterprise; employment) are components of one numerator and are reported as an optional disaggregation, not separately calculated sub-metrics. Related sheets: KPI-O29 (number of youth engaged in CIMMYT training, enterprise, or employment programs), the output that feeds this outcome in the results chain.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
CGIAR GENDER Impact Platform, youth research page (basis of the earlier 15 to 24 working default, superseded by the 15 to 30 band stated once in Core §4.1): https://gender.cgiar.org/gender-research/youth (accessed 29 July 2026).

Strategic mandate: CIMMYT (2023), Science and Innovation for a Food and Nutrition Secure World, PO3 mapping.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E team / enumerators (survey rounds). Validation: project MEAL officer (age and participation module completeness, weighting). Calculation: project M&E, per the Calculation method above. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.

name: Number of policies, investment decisions, or transformation processes integrating gender-equity and social-inclusion provisions
volumeTitle: Gender equality, youth and social inclusion
resultsLevel: Outcome. On the CIMMYT MEAL Framework's test this is a change in policy among partners: governments, investors and institutions integrate GESI provisions into their own policies, investment decisions or change processes, and the formula counts instruments that changed rather than instruments CIMMYT produced.
primaryObjective: PO5 Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved), PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Gender Equality, Youth and Social Inclusion
sdgTarget: None. SDG target 5.c (sound policies and enforceable legislation for gender equality) is the matching target, but its official indicator 5.c.1 measures the proportion of countries whose public financial management systems track and publish allocations for gender equality: a characteristic of national fiscal systems, not a count of instruments an organization's evidence helped change.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Results Framework: this indicator is a GESI-focused application of the CGIAR Policy Change outcome category (instruments modified in design or implementation, with evidence the change was informed by CGIAR research). Results counted here are therefore reportable into CGIAR technical reporting as Policy Change outcomes, carrying the required minimum data standard (policy type, stage, owner). The provisions test is KPI-O42's GEYSI-responsiveness test: two bars over three groups. Bar 1, the women group, is CGIAR's enhanced gender scoring system at 1B or above. Bar 2, the youth group and any other named social group, is the structural provision test, no CGIAR scale equivalent to the gender one existing for either. CGIAR does tag every output and outcome for gender equality on a three-level scale (not targeted 0, significant 1, principal 2); it cannot serve as a bar here, since it has no youth or social-inclusion counterpart, carries no responsive level, and scores CGIAR's own results rather than external instruments. CGIAR's evaluators state that there is no tagging or targeting system for youth and social inclusion.
definition: Counts the distinct policies, investment decisions, or transformation processes that integrated gender-equity and social-inclusion (GESI) provisions in the reporting year, with documented evidence that the integration was informed by CIMMYT. A provision qualifies when it clears the bar Eligibility sets for the group it serves: for women an explicit gender-equality outcome, for youth or another named social group a named action, target, eligibility rule or resource allocation; general gender language does not qualify. Each instrument is counted once, in the year the integration event occurs (formal adoption, investment decision, or documented modification of design or implementation).
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's evidence and engagement change what external institutions adopt and fund: the point where gender equity stops being a CIMMYT deliverable and becomes a commitment owned by a government, investor, or institution. It is the outcome step of the gender-in-policy results chain, between instruments developed with CIMMYT support (KPI-O42) and public policies enacted that support smallholder resilience and to which CIMMYT contributed (KPI-I15), and feeds institutional and donor reporting on gender equality and social inclusion at system level.
projectSpecificApplication: State which instruments or processes the project engages, the owning institution of each, the countries and policy scale covered, and the form of the evidence linking CIMMYT to the GESI integration. Do not change the unit, the provisions test, or the counting rule. If applying the indicator as defined is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count informs (for example, a donor outcome target under a gender-in-policy component, or an adaptive-management trigger: instruments repeatedly stalling before adoption prompts a review of the engagement strategy).
projectTypesNotApplicable: seed systems and deployment and digital agriculture and AI
projectTypesRaw:
System change and transformation.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, breeding and varietal development, applied agronomy and farming systems, seed systems and deployment and digital agriculture and AI.
unit: Number (count of distinct policies, investment decisions, or transformation processes)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more policies, investment decisions or transformation processes carry gender-equity and social-inclusion provisions that CIMMYT informed. Each instrument is counted once, regardless of how many provisions it carries.
disaggregationRequired: Required: policy scale or level (local / national / global), per the register; and instrument category (policy, investment decision, transformation process), since the three are achievements of very different character and weight and a pooled count reads as more policy change than occurred; and the group or groups each instrument qualified under (women; youth; other named social group), an instrument qualifying under more than one appearing in each, so the group subtotals can exceed the count and are never summed.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country or region; owning institution type (government, development bank or investor, regional body, private company); sector or value chain; depth of gender integration (gender-responsive vs gender principal (2)); new instrument vs modification of an existing one.
unitOfObservation:
The policy, investment decision or transformation process, recorded under the template's result object value, under which a policy instrument, an investment decision or a transformation process falls. Organization is not used as a stand-in, since this indicator does not observe an organization. The measurand is an institutional decision, so the farm measurement levels do not apply. The decision is the unit of observation and the only level at which the indicator is measured.

Regional / Aggregated and above are aggregation levels.

KPI-O42 counts the instruments CIMMYT helped develop; this counts decisions that changed. The same document may appear in both, and the two are never summed.
calculationSummary: Value: count of distinct policies, investment decisions, or transformation processes that in the reporting year (a) were formally adopted, decided, or modified in design or implementation, (b) carry at least one provision that clears the bar Eligibility criteria sets for the group it serves, and (c) carry documented evidence that the integration was informed by CIMMYT research, evidence, or engagement. Inclusion: the integration event occurred in the reporting year; each qualifying provision clears the bar Eligibility sets for the group it serves; the CIMMYT link is evidenced and must bind to the specific qualifying provision, not merely to the instrument generally: before-and-after text showing CIMMYT's input shaped the qualifying provision is the strongest evidence, and where that is unavailable, citations, documented participation, or acknowledgment by the owning institution must themselves name the qualifying provision rather than record CIMMYT's involvement with the instrument as a whole. An instrument informed by more than one CIMMYT project counts once. Exclusion: instruments developed but still in deliberation, and instruments developed but never adopted (counted by KPI-O42 where CIMMYT contributed to their development); gender mentioned only in preamble or general language; instruments with GESI provisions but no documented CIMMYT link. Missing data: a logged instrument without the instrument text or contribution evidence on file is excluded until the evidence is filed. Repeated observations: each instrument counts once per reporting year, and further decisions on it in that year add no record; a modification adopted in a later reporting year counts as a new record only if it is a substantive strengthening revision as Eligibility criteria defines it.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: CIMMYT project policy-engagement and outcome-monitoring records logging each instrument, its owning institution, policy scale, the integration event and date, the specific GESI provisions, and the evidence of CIMMYT's contribution, cross-checked against the official instrument or decision documents. The official instrument or decision document (the published policy or regulation, a gazette entry, the adopting body's formal record, or the funder's recorded board or funding approval) is a Recommended source for the integration event and the provision text, wherever it is retrieved. Fallback DS4: partner records and third-party trackers (partner archives, donor and policy trackers) used to reconstruct the count where CIMMYT's own log is incomplete; a decision evidenced only this way is Fallback-sourced and reported beside the pooled figure, because such records rarely document CIMMYT's contribution. Not applicable DS1: this indicator counts institutional decisions read from documents, not data collected from respondents. Not applicable DS3: geospatial data cannot identify a policy instrument or its provisions. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced data cannot verify an instrument's content or the evidence trail linking it to CIMMYT.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether Recommended or Fallback was used. If Fallback, state why the project's own engagement log was incomplete and which external records were used.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). The register entry itself is the tool: each record names the instrument, its category, owning institution, policy scale, integration event and date, the specific GESI provisions, and the CIMMYT contribution evidence.
collectionFrequency: Continuous: each instrument is logged as its integration event is documented
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the integration event (adoption, investment decision, or documented modification) occurred
baselineRequired: No. An annual flow count that starts from zero each reporting year; there is no pre-project stock to measure. Change over time is read from the annual series itself.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One reporting year. Levels widen the set of decisions; they never widen the domain.

Weight: one per distinct decision, so a decision informed by two projects still counts once.

B: Combination method: sum. Total = Σ distinct policies, investment decisions or transformation processes meeting the qualification and evidence requirements in the domain.

C: Levels and operations. Decision. The record itself. Also report: the documented evidence of CIMMYT's contribution.

D: Never pooled. Decisions with the instruments counted at KPI-O42; the same document may appear in both and the two are never summed. Decisions without documented evidence with those carrying it. Recommended-sourced with Fallback-sourced decisions: a decision evidenced only from partner or third-party records (Fallback DS4) is reported beside the pooled figure with a note and not blended in, and the same project's Recommended-sourced decisions are summed. Decisions with KPI-OC37's, KPI-OC34's and KPI-I15's counts: one instrument may be counted by each on the shared instrument identifier; the overlap is named and the figures are never summed.

E: Deduplication and coverage. The shared instrument identifier (official title, issuing body, jurisdiction and version, the key KPI-O42, KPI-OC34, KPI-OC37 and KPI-I15 use), so a decision influenced by two projects is counted once, and a later decision on an instrument already counted (a further approval stage, a ratification) is not counted again unless it is a substantive strengthening revision as Eligibility defines it. This is a census of decisions meeting the qualification and evidence requirements, drawn from CIMMYT's own engagement records, not a sample estimate: it carries no sampling error and no coefficient-of-variation band.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Include decisions taken in the reporting year for which documented evidence of CIMMYT's contribution exists, named in the record.

Exclude decisions where the contribution is asserted but not evidenced; count them separately.

The qualifying bar is two bars over three groups. Bar 1, the women group, is CGIAR's enhanced gender scoring system at 1B, "gender responsive", or above. Of 1B's three published conditions only the first, an explicit gender-equality outcome, is applied, as on KPI-O42; the other two are recorded where the text provides for them and are not required, and the conditions of levels 0 and 1A are not prerequisites. Bar 1 is read on the instrument's text as KPI-O42's Eligibility criteria read it, including what counts as an explicit gender-equality outcome, the treatment of a participation quota for women, and a provision directed at a group defined by sex and another attribute. Bar 2, the youth group and any other named social group, is the structural provision test, a named action, target, eligibility rule or resource allocation directed at that group and traceable in the text. This bar is identical to KPI-O42's, so an instrument cannot clear the output's GEYSI test and fail the outcome's on the same text. The two sheets' contribution tests are not identical and are not claimed to be: KPI-O42 requires a documented CIMMYT contribution to the instrument's development, and this sheet a documented CIMMYT contribution to the decision. Bar 1 is not the three-level gender equality tagging system, which carries no 1B. Gender principal (2) instruments also qualify.

A transformation process is a formally constituted, time-bound institutional change process with its own governance and documentation, such as a national agrifood systems transformation program or a sector reform process. Its integration milestone is the dated approval of the process document carrying the GESI provision, not the launch of the process: without a formal document there is nothing whose GESI content can be read.

The counting event for an investment decision is board or funding approval, not budget allocation and not first disbursement: approval is the point at which the GESI provision became binding, and disbursement can lag by years for reasons unrelated to the provision.

The counting event for a policy, strategy or regulation is its adoption by the authority empowered to adopt it; a later stage for the same version, such as gazettement, ratification or entry into force, is not counted again.

A substantive strengthening revision of an already-counted instrument creates a new record, where substantive means a move up CGIAR's enhanced gender scoring system or an expansion of the provision's scope, including to a group the instrument did not previously carry; a revision restating existing provisions does not.

KPI-O42, KPI-OC39, KPI-OC34, KPI-OC37 and KPI-I15 share one instrument identifier, so the development-to-adoption-to-enactment pipeline is traceable, the revision records above link into a sequence, and one instrument is never reported as several separate results.

A decision and the instrument that carried it are different records: KPI-O42 counts instruments developed, this counts decisions taken, and the same document may appear in both.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only: instruments are changed by their owning institutions under many influences, and "informed by CIMMYT" ranges from leading the technical input to providing one evidence source among several. The documented-evidence requirement bounds the claim but does not grade CIMMYT's share of it.

Integration is not implementation: a GESI provision on paper may never be resourced, enforced, or reach the women and marginalized groups it names, so this count evidences policy change, not changed lives.

The three counted categories (policy, investment decision, transformation process) and the scale range (local to global) span achievements of very different weight, so raw counts are not comparable across projects or years until the scale and category disaggregations are applied.

Classifying a provision as explicit rather than general gender language requires judgment; the control is the register record naming the specific provisions, so each classification can be audited against the instrument text.

An increase means more CIMMYT-informed instruments carried explicit GESI provisions in the year, not that gender gaps narrowed; read alongside KPI-O42 (pipeline), KPI-I15 (enactment), and the pathway's people-level indicators for the full results chain.
subMetrics: None. Instrument categories and policy-scale levels are disaggregations of the same count, not separately calculated metrics. Related indicators have their own sheets: KPI-O42 (the output that feeds this outcome), KPI-I15 (the impact the chain reaches, in the Policy, finance & market systems pathway), and KPI-OC37 (the general policy-change outcome this indicator overlaps with; see Aggregation rule).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E or policy-engagement focal point, logging each instrument with its integration event and evidence. Validation: project MEAL officer, checking the GESI provisions and contribution evidence against the instrument text; a boundary case, where the officer cannot tell whether a provision clears its bar, is decided by CIMMYT's gender research lead, with the reason recorded against the instrument. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (de-duplication across projects on the shared instrument identifier, the overlap with KPI-OC37 named rather than removed, and the CIMMYT-wide sum, per Aggregation rule). Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
