name: Percentage of women in leadership positions at CIMMYT
volumeTitle: Gender equality, youth and social inclusion
resultsLevel: Outcome. The Core reads an Institutional-branch level from the indicator statement itself, because there is no external actor: the share of leadership position holders who are women states how far CIMMYT's recruitment, development and promotion systems give women access to its most senior roles, which reports the organization operating differently, not a deliverable a corporate function produces, so it is an outcome. CGIAR's output/outcome boundary test is written for research results and fits an internal workforce measure poorly.
primaryObjective: Talent Management (institutional component). As an Institutional indicator, this KPI maps to one of the five institutional enabler components rather than to the mission-outcome objectives PO1 to PO5. A gender-balanced leadership pipeline is a core talent-management result: it signals that recruitment, development, and promotion systems give women equitable access to the most senior roles.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. The five CGIAR Impact Areas describe development results delivered to external populations. CGIAR itself keeps its internal workplace gender work (GDI, covering all staff) separate from the Gender Equality, Youth and Social Inclusion Impact Area (GEYSI, covering research beneficiaries); this indicator sits on the internal, workplace side of that line. CGIAR monitors it through its workplace GDI framework and Workforce Data Dashboard, not through Impact Area reporting.
sdgTarget: SDG indicator 5.5.2 (proportion of women in managerial positions), under target 5.5 (ensure women's full and effective participation and equal opportunities for leadership at all levels of decision-making). Correspondence note: SDG 5.5.2 is defined for national labor markets using labor force surveys and the ISCO-08 occupational classification; CIMMYT applies the same construct (share of women among management position holders) at organizational level from HR records. The SDG metadata's recommendation to read the share of women in senior and middle management jointly with the share in total management, to detect a ceiling effect where women cluster in junior management, is applied here by analogy and motivates the required disaggregation below.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR workplace GDI framework and successive Action Plans (2020-21, 2023-24, and the 2025-27 C&E Action Plan), the GDI Matrix of 15 best-practice indicators, and the Workforce Data Dashboard, which reports workforce sex, nationality and other demographics. GRI 405: Diversity and Equal Opportunity 2016 (disclosure 405-1, diversity of governance bodies and employees), a corporate sustainability-reporting comparator for this indicator.
definition: Measures the share of CIMMYT leadership position holders who are women at the reporting date. Numerator: people holding a leadership position who are women; denominator: all people holding a leadership position (a headcount of position holders, not of posts). This is an institutional workforce-diversity measure of CIMMYT as an employer, reported once from corporate human resources records.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's own leadership reflects the gender balance the institution advocates in agrifood systems: an organization asking partners and governments to close gender gaps is accountable for the gap in its own management. The value serves CIMMYT Human Resources and senior management for talent planning, institutional and donor reporting, and CGIAR-level accountability: CGIAR's workplace Gender, Diversity and Inclusion (GDI) framework, now managed by the CGIAR Culture and Engagement (C&E) Function, tracks data on CGIAR leadership, management teams and workforce composition, and GDI is a standing semi-annual item on CGIAR's System Council agenda.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable, Institutional scope. This indicator has no project instance; it is reported once, at CIMMYT-institutional level, from corporate systems.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable, Institutional scope.
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance; it is reported by a corporate function, not by any project type.
unit: Percentage of leadership position holders
directionOfChange: Reference value: 50 percent, which is parity. The reference is what an equal share of leadership position holders means, not a maximum and not a target set here. While women remain under-represented an increase is an improvement, and values at or around parity indicate the desired state. Movement is read against parity rather than as an open-ended increase. Parity is read with the two residual categories in view, since their holders sit in the denominator; their counts are published under the same Human Resources data-protection rules as every other cell.
disaggregationRequired: Leadership tier: senior management versus middle management, the boundary being the HR grade CIMMYT names for it, stated with the value, so the institutional value can reveal whether women's representation thins toward the top (the ceiling effect the SDG 5.5.2 method is designed to expose). Sex recorded as male/female at minimum, following CGIAR's sex-disaggregated data standards; the indicator is itself the sex disaggregation of leadership position holders. Cells are published under CIMMYT's own Human Resources data-protection rules, and this sheet sets no disclosure floor of its own.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Not applicable as a project layer (Institutional scope). Optional institutional cuts: functional area (research versus professional and administrative services), duty station or region (headquarters versus regional offices), staff category (internationally versus nationally recruited), age group.
unitOfObservation:
The leadership position holder (Core value: individual), the person occupying a leadership position at CIMMYT at the snapshot date, counted once even where they hold two leadership roles (see Calculation method). The measurand is a person's appointment, so the farm measurement levels do not apply and no project reports it. The position itself, and its tier, is recorded as an attribute of the holder, not as a separate unit.

This indicator is Institutional scope in a Mission pathway, which is deliberate and not unique: branch states who reports, pathway states what the indicator is about. It is filed here because its subject is gender, and it is reported centrally by the responsible corporate function rather than by any project.
calculationSummary: Inclusion and exclusion: includes every person holding a filled position on CIMMYT's defined leadership position list, being the management team, directors and unit heads. Formal line or budget authority is a condition of every position on the list, not a route onto it: a role carrying it outside those three categories, such as a project leader holding a grant budget or a scientist supervising a team, is not a leadership position here, and scientific seniority alone does not qualify. Where CIMMYT's HR grade structure draws the boundary differently, the grades used are named with the value before reporting. Excludes vacant positions (a vacancy is held by neither a woman nor a man, so it leaves both numerator and denominator). Interim and acting appointments are included and flagged as such, since an acting appointment is who actually holds the authority in the reference period.
dataSource:
Not applicable DS4 (secondary and international databases): external sources such as the CGIAR Workforce Data Dashboard republish center-supplied HR data downstream of this indicator; they can serve as a consistency cross-check but never as the source of CIMMYT's own reported value.

Not applicable DS5 (citizen-generated and other non-traditional data): crowdsourced data cannot establish official position holders.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable, Institutional scope.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). No survey module is used; the instrument is the HR system extract specification: snapshot date, leadership position list, and the fields person identifier, position ID, tier, holder's sex (with its not-recorded and outside-categories values) and appointment status (substantive, interim or acting).
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as a by-product of HR administration; the indicator snapshot is extracted at least annually. The semi-annual extract at 30 June is taken as well, which also aligns with the semi-annual cadence of the GDI item on CGIAR's System Council agenda.
reportingFrequency: Annually, into institutional reporting and CGIAR workforce reporting.
referencePeriod: Point in time: the value describes leadership composition on the snapshot date, 31 December of the reporting year, matching the calendar-year reporting basis used register-wide, not an average over the year. A semi-annual extract at 30 June is reported alongside, so movement within the year is visible rather than only its year-end state.
baselineRequired: Yes: a reference-year value is needed to speak of progress toward parity. If no baseline was fixed at the start of the 2030 Strategy period, reconstruct it retrospectively from HR system position history, which typically permits an exact recalculation for past snapshot dates; this is the standard fallback, valid where the leadership position list is applied to the historical data consistently.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One snapshot date, CIMMYT-wide. This indicator has no project instance and no geographic domain below the institution.

Weight: one per person holding a leadership position. A person formally holding two leadership roles is counted once, against their more senior role; the second role is recorded on the position register, reported alongside as the count of dual-role holders and the second roles they hold, but does not enter this indicator's numerator or denominator a second time. This is a headcount of position holders throughout, at every level, which is what puts the figure on the counting basis of SDG indicator 5.5.2, itself a count of people in managerial positions rather than of posts, without the comparison needing to be asserted separately.

B: Combination method: ratio of sums.

Vacant positions are excluded from both terms and reported separately.

C: Levels and operations. Position holder. The individual person, their more senior leadership post, and their sex. Also report: any second leadership role they hold, on the position register.

No intermediate level applies: this is an institutional figure reported once by the responsible corporate function.

D: Never pooled. Snapshots taken at different dates. Figures using different leadership definitions or grade boundaries. This share with any project-reported gender indicator in this pathway, which measure external populations.

E: Deduplication and coverage. The person identifier from the HR system at the snapshot date, which is what keeps a dual-role holder from entering the count twice. The leadership definition and the grade boundary travel with every figure, because the share moves with where the boundary is drawn. This is a census of CIMMYT's own leadership position holders at the snapshot date, not a sample estimate: it carries no sampling error and no coefficient-of-variation band.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Include people holding a leadership position filled at the snapshot date, on the stated grade or tier boundary.

Exclude vacant positions from both numerator and denominator, reported separately: counting a vacancy in the denominator reports a fall whenever a post empties.

Include interim and acting appointments, flagged as such: an acting appointment is who actually holds the authority in the reference period. Where a substantive holder is on leave and an acting holder is appointed, the acting holder is counted, flagged as acting, and the substantive holder is not; the number of substantive holders on leave, by sex, is reported alongside.

Position holders whose sex is not recorded are reported under a "sex not recorded" residual; position holders who identify outside the sex categories the HR system carries are reported under a separate residual naming that. Both stay in the denominator. Neither is ever redistributed or dropped: an indicator that quietly discards the people its categories do not fit is measuring its categories, not its workforce.

The leadership definition and the grade boundary are stated with every figure.
limitations: Not a field-level gender measure. This indicator measures CIMMYT as an employer. CIMMYT's field-level women's empowerment and gender-gap indicators measure changes among external populations reached by research projects, and the two are never read together.

Its subject is the one CIMMYT itself calls GESI. The toolbox tags this indicator's domain GEYSI, because that is the controlled vocabulary for indicator domains. But what it measures, gender composition in CIMMYT's own workforce, is what CIMMYT publishes under GESI, which its careers page expands as Gender Equity and Social Inclusion (https://www.cimmyt.org/careers/diversity/). The two terms are not competing: GEYSI is the register term for what the research delivers to farmers, GESI is the institutional term for CIMMYT as an employer. This sheet is the one place in the pathway where both apply, which is the clearest statement of why an Institutional indicator sits in a mission pathway.

An institutional indicator in a mission pathway. Branch states who reports an indicator; pathway states what it is about. This one is reported centrally by the responsible corporate function and sits here because its subject is gender, matching eight other Institutional-branch indicators filed in mission pathways for the same reason.

It does not overlap with the workforce indicators. Volume 12 measures the workforce as a system, hiring, growth and retention. This measures the sex composition of one defined tier at one date. Where both are reported, they are read together and never combined, and the leadership definition and grade boundary travel with this figure because the share moves with where that boundary is drawn.

Composition is not equity: the share of leadership position holders who are women says nothing about pay gaps, tenure, workload, real decision-making influence, or workplace culture. Read it alongside broader workplace gender, diversity and inclusion measures rather than as a summary of them.

The value is only as meaningful as the boundary of "leadership position": adding or removing grades or roles from the list changes the value with no real change in the organization. The list must be fixed, published with the indicator, and any revision must trigger a recalculated baseline rather than a silent series break.

Small-denominator volatility: leadership position holders number in the tens, so a single appointment or departure can move the value by several percentage points. Always report the numerator and denominator counts with the percentage, and do not over-interpret year-on-year movements.

A point-in-time snapshot hides flows: a stable share can mask high turnover of women in leadership, and appointment, promotion and exit rates by sex are needed to understand the direction the share will move next.
subMetrics: None. Senior management and middle management shares are disaggregations of the same measure, not separately calculated sub-metrics.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
External alignment: UN Statistics Division (2026), SDG indicator metadata: indicator 5.5.2.

Disaggregation standard: CGIAR Independent Advisory and Evaluation Service (2025), Making CGIAR evaluations gender responsive and inclusive: Integrating gender equality, youth and social inclusion (GEYSI) and gender diversity and inclusion (GDI) into CGIAR evaluations, Workplace GDI definitions, the C&E Function's tracking of leadership and management-team composition, the GDI Matrix of 15 indicators, and the Workforce Data Dashboard.

Comparator disclosure: Global Reporting Initiative (2016), GRI 405: Diversity and equal opportunity 2016, disclosure 405-1 (diversity of governance bodies and employees).

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner of this reference sheet).
sheetStewardDataRoles: As an Institutional indicator, every data role sits with a CIMMYT corporate function, not a project team. Data collection: CIMMYT Human Resources (HR system extract at the snapshot date). Validation: Human Resources records team. Calculation: Human Resources analytics, or the MEAL unit from the validated extract, per the calculation method above. Approval: head of the Human Resources function. Reporting: Human Resources to the MEAL unit for institutional reporting and onward CGIAR workforce reporting.

name: Change in time spent on unpaid agricultural and domestic work in CIMMYT intervention areas, by sex, and in the gap between women and men
volumeTitle: Gender equality, youth and social inclusion
resultsLevel: Outcome. The CIMMYT MEAL Framework defines outcomes as changes in behavior, systems, practice, capacity, policy or performance among beneficiaries and partners (Section 2.3). A change in how a household allocates unpaid work is a change in practice among beneficiaries. It sits above KPI-O61, which supplies the level, and contributes to KPI-I08.
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Contributing, contribution only: PO4.
cgiarImpactArea: Gender Equality, Youth and Social Inclusion.
sdgTarget: Target 5.4. Not reportable as indicator 5.4.1, for the reasons stated on KPI-O61: that indicator is a proportion of a day for a nationally representative population and excludes unpaid agricultural work.
otherFrameworks: No framework cited here carries a change in unpaid hours. The construct rests on KPI-O61's classification, and the change arithmetic follows the pattern KPI-OC62 uses for labor productivity in the Productivity pathway.
definition:
The change in hours per person per week spent on unpaid work, over a window with a pre-adoption baseline, reported separately by sex and as the change in the sex gap.

The level is measured by KPI-O61, which fixes the activity classification, the unit, the respondent rule and the collection mode. This indicator is computed from that series and from no other source.

Hours are never valued here; valuation of household labor happens once in the toolbox, at KPI-OC63.
rationale:
Hours are counted at KPI-O59, KPI-O60 and KPI-O61 and valued once at KPI-OC63; this indicator measures the change in the unpaid burden they represent.

The gap term is what makes it a gender indicator rather than a labor one. A technology can reduce total household hours while leaving women's share untouched, or reduce men's field hours while women absorb the displaced work. Reporting the two sexes separately shows the first; reporting the gap change shows the second.
projectSpecificApplication: State the window, the rounds compared, the geography and the intervention whose adoption the baseline precedes. The definition, the activity classification and the calculation method are unchanged.
projectSpecificRationale: State why this project claims a change in unpaid burden and the decision it informs. Example: a project introducing mechanized weeding reports it because the labor it saves is men's field labor, and whether women's hours moved at all is the question the project cannot answer from yield.
projectTypesNotApplicable: upstream discovery science and breeding and varietal development
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science and breeding and varietal development, which do not reach households; digital agriculture and AI, which reports through the pathways its tools serve.
unit: Hours per person per week, as a difference: the change is reported in hours, not as a percentage. A percentage change on a small base is unstable and conceals the base, and the base is what a reader needs. The gap change is also in hours.
directionOfChange:
Not directional for the level change. Fewer unpaid hours are not automatically an improvement; hours released into paid work, schooling or rest are different results, and this indicator cannot tell them apart.

The gap carries a direction in the domestic and care class only: Decrease. A narrowing gap between women's and men's unpaid domestic and care hours is an improvement, read on the gap's absolute size so the reading holds whichever sex carries the larger burden, in line with target 5.4's promotion of shared responsibility within the household. In the agricultural class the gap change is not directional: women's unpaid own-farm hours can fall because work was lightened or because an activity passed out of their hands, and this indicator cannot tell the two apart.
disaggregationRequired:
Sex, inherited from KPI-O61 and required for the same reason: the gap term cannot be computed without it.

Activity class, agricultural or domestic and care, since a fall in one alongside a rise in the other is the finding most likely to matter and a combined figure hides it.

Both fail the poolability test, and Block A restates them as pooling-domain prohibitions.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Age band; whether the household adopted the labor-saving technology in question, which turns the figure into an adopter-versus-non-adopter comparison where the project holds both.
unitOfObservation: The individual household member, with hours recorded per person, inherited unchanged from KPI-O61. A change is a property of a series, and the series belongs to an identified person, so the persistent household member identifier anchors it. A member who cannot be matched across rounds contributes to no change.
calculationSummary:
First, require a balanced panel. Only members present in every round of the window enter any figure. A mean over members who stayed, compared with an earlier mean over everyone, reports who left rather than what changed.

Second, compute the change per sex.

Third, compute the gap change.

The gap is read on its absolute size, so the sign of the gap itself never enters the change: a negative gap change is a narrowing, whichever sex carries the larger burden. The signed gap is reported alongside, because it says which sex carries the larger burden and that is not the same question. A signed difference cannot carry the direction on its own: where men record more unpaid hours than women in a class, which is routine in the agricultural class in ox-plow and mechanized land-preparation systems, the gap is negative and a further negative change is a widening, not an improvement.

Fourth, apply the detectability test on the panel's own paired difference. The change is a panel-mean statistic, not a single observation, so the relevant precision is the standard error of that paired difference, not the repeatability of one measurement. SE(Change) is the standard error of the mean of the person-level differences (endline hours − baseline hours, per person), computed with the household as the cluster, since the panel takes every member of each household, and on the survey design where households were sampled. A change is reported as detected only where its absolute value exceeds 1.96 × SE(Change), a two-sided test at 5 percent, the threshold this sheet adopts; a project stating a different multiple says so and states why. A change whose absolute value does not exceed the detectability threshold is reported as the measured value with the caveat that it does not exceed the threshold, and is never described as an improvement or a deterioration either way.

Fifth, test the gap change. It is described as a narrowing or a widening only where the gap has the same sign at both rounds and the absolute difference between women's and men's changes exceeds 1.96 × its standard error, computed from the person-level differences with the household as the cluster; otherwise it is reported as the measured value and not described as a narrowing or a widening.

Both period means are retained and reported with the change, so an institutional figure can be rebuilt from them.
dataSource: Inherited from KPI-O61, which assigns all five codes a role: Recommended DS1 (contemporaneous recording), Fallback DS1 (stylized recall, reported separately and never blended with contemporaneous values), Not applicable DS2, DS3 and DS5, and Comparator DS4. This indicator introduces no source of its own; both rounds must come from that indicator, collected on the same coded route, the same instrument, the same activity list and the same mode. A change assembled from a KPI-O61 baseline and a differently collected endline is not a change in unpaid work; it is the difference between two instruments.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Name the rounds compared, their calendar position, the collection mode, and the system holding the household roster and member identifiers across rounds.
collectionInstrument:
None of its own. The instrument is KPI-O61's: the labor module extended with ICATUS divisions 3 and 4 and a required sex field.

What this indicator adds is a requirement on the sampling frame rather than on the instrument: the same members must be reachable in every round, so the household roster carries persistent member identifiers from the baseline onward. A project that fields KPI-O61 without that provision can report levels and can never report this. (KPI-O61's own Collection instrument states the matching requirement at the activity-record level: every record ties to a specific person via a persistent identifier, not only a headcount.)
collectionFrequency: Once per round, inherited from KPI-O61.
reportingFrequency: Annually, once the window is complete.
referencePeriod: A window of at least two rounds at the same point in the agricultural calendar, the first of which is pre-adoption. Three rounds are preferred, because two points cannot distinguish a trend from a single unusual season, and the sheet states which the project held.
baselineRequired: Yes, and it must be pre-adoption. A baseline taken after a labor-saving technology is in use measures the world the intervention already changed, and the change computed from it understates the effect by construction.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One sex, one activity class, one window length, one point in the agricultural calendar, one country, one collection mode, one minimum age and one activity list version. No combined figure exists across any of these; the figures are reported side by side, one per domain. The gap change is reported alongside the two sex changes, never instead of them.

Weight: one per household member, inherited from KPI-O61, multiplied by the household's survey weight where households were sampled, including members recording zero hours.

B: Combination method: not aggregated as such. A change is a property of one series and is recomputed at each level from the member records belonging to that level, never combined from changes computed below it.

Mean change at a level = (Σ endline hours ÷ Σ members) − (Σ baseline hours ÷ Σ members), over the balanced panel in the domain, with hours and members weighted by the household survey weight where households were sampled.

The two period means are ratios of sums and recompute cleanly; the change is their difference. Never average project-level changes.

C: Levels and operations.

D: Never pooled. Sexes. Activity classes. Changes with levels. Windows of different length or at different calendar points. Recall-collected with contemporaneously collected series. Changes computed on unbalanced panels with those computed on balanced ones. Changes from this sheet with the labor-productivity changes at KPI-OC62, which measure output per day rather than hours worked. Self-reported with proxy-reported series. A sample estimate computed without its survey weights. Figures using different minimum ages. Figures using different activity lists.

E: Deduplication and coverage. The persistent household member identifier, applied from Household level upward, with the household identifier carried so a household is counted once. Coverage, attrition and precision travel with every figure at Project area level and above. The period means are released on the coefficient-of-variation bands used in official statistics: 16.5 percent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 percent released flagged, above 33.3 percent not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one de-duplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above, and a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place. The change per sex is not released on these bands: it is released with its standard error, as detected or not detected on the test in Calculation method, and only where both its period means are released. The gap change is released only where all four period means are, and is described as a narrowing or a widening only where it passes the test in Calculation method. The collection mode, the window length, the calendar point, the minimum age and the activity list version travel with the figure. Across projects no union is computed, and a figure combining projects is labeled not de-duplicated across projects.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Include members with a KPI-O61 weekly record (not a same-day observation) in every round of the window, from a pre-adoption baseline.

Exclude members missing any round; report them as attrition with the count and, where known, the reason. Members whose respondent type, self-reported or proxy-reported, differs between rounds are excluded in the same way and counted in the attrition figure with that reason. Attrition in time-use panels is not random: seasonal migration removes the members whose absence redistributes work, which is the effect the indicator is trying to see.

Exclude windows whose rounds fall at different points in the agricultural calendar. KPI-O61 requires the same reference week in every round, and a change computed across different seasons describes the calendar.

Exclude windows spanning a change of collection mode or activity list. A move from recall to contemporaneous recording produces an apparent change that is entirely instrumental.
limitations: Contribution, not attribution. Household labor allocation moves with school terms, off-farm wage opportunities, illness, migration and weather. A change here is not evidence that CIMMYT produced it, and no design in this sheet establishes one.
Fewer hours is not automatically a gain. The indicator sees hours leaving unpaid work; it does not see where they went. Read alongside the income and productivity indicators, or not at all.

A narrowing gap can be produced from either side. The gap narrows if women's hours fall and it narrows if men's rise, and those are different results. Both sex changes are reported so the gap is never read alone.

Panel attrition is not random here. The members most likely to leave a time-use panel are the ones whose movement redistributes work, so attrition is reported with every figure, as a count and a rate.

The balanced panel is a fixed cohort that ages across the window. Requiring members present in every round anchors the panel on the people first enrolled, and those people age as the window elapses. Some transition out of a stage-of-life category that itself changes unpaid-work patterns independent of anything CIMMYT influenced, for example leaving a youth band or marrying. A rising or falling figure may partly reflect this life-stage transition rather than a true within-cohort behavioral change, and the panel alone cannot separate the two.

Same own-household scope as KPI-O61, narrower than SDG 5.4.1. This indicator's change is computed entirely from KPI-O61's series, so its own-household boundary and the resulting exclusion of reciprocal or other-household unpaid labor carry through unchanged; see KPI-O61's Limitations for the full disclosure.
subMetrics:
The two period means per sex, the gap at each round, the panel size and the attrition count are each retained and reported with the change. A change without its period means cannot be recomputed, and an institutional figure is rebuilt from the means rather than averaged from project changes.

Relationship to other indicators. KPI-O61 supplies the level and fixes every measurement convention this sheet inherits. KPI-OC62 carries the same change-and-panel discipline for labor productivity, output per person-day, and the two are never pooled: one measures hours worked, the other output per person-day. KPI-OC63 values household labor hours once, and this sheet never values them. KPI-I08 measures decision-making power and is the impact this indicator contributes to; time released is not empowerment, and a woman may gain hours and lose say. KPI-OC19 reports a cross-sectional adoption gap between women and men, which is a difference at one moment rather than a change over a window.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: Content owner: the CIMMYT MEAL unit, with the gender research lead as technical reviewer.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Collection: as KPI-O61. Validation: project M&E officer. Calculation: project M&E, applying the formula in Calculation method. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.

name: Percentage of women in the target population reporting improved decision-making power over agricultural production, income and resources, with the number reported alongside
volumeTitle: Gender equality, youth and social inclusion
resultsLevel: Impact. A change in women's decision-making power is a long-term change in the condition of external actors; it sits at the top of the women's empowerment results chain and maps to a CGIAR Impact Area.
primaryObjective: PO3 Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved. Contributing: PO5 (Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities). Household-level empowerment sits under PO3; systemic gender provisions in policy and investment are tracked separately under PO5 (KPI-OC39).
cgiarImpactArea: Gender Equality, Youth and Social Inclusion
sdgTarget: None. The nearest candidates measure different constructs: SDG 5.a.1 measures ownership or secure tenure rights over agricultural land, a legal-rights status rather than self-reported decision-making power; SDG 5.5's indicators (5.5.1, 5.5.2) measure representation in parliaments, local governments and managerial positions, not agency within farm and household.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Common Results Framework: impact-level standard indicator, #women's empowerment and inclusion in the agricultural sector, of which this indicator is the CIMMYT adaptation. Pro-WEAI (IFPRI) and its sector versions are widely used across CGIAR evaluations.
definition: The share of women in the measured panel classified as improved in decision-making power over agricultural and household resources, where improved is an analyst-derived transition between two independently self-reported adequacy classifications, one at baseline and one at endline, on two indicators: input in productive decisions (A-WEAI) and ownership of land and other assets (pro-WEAI). A woman reports her input and her ownership at each round; she is never asked whether her decision-making power has improved. Decision-making power is read on these two indicators only; control over the use of income and access to financial services are not measured. Operationalized with these two IFPRI instruments, since CGIAR's own impact indicator fixes no metric.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's work translates into women having a greater say over the resources their livelihoods depend on: the end result the gender equality, youth and social inclusion portfolio serves. CIMMYT's GEYSI plan classifies gender indicators along a Reach, Benefit, Empower, Transform continuum, and this indicator sits at Empower, above the reach count of women engaged (KPI-O28). It feeds CGIAR's Gender Equality, Youth and Social Inclusion impact-area reporting, whose collective 2030 target is closing the gender gap in rights to economic resources for over 500 million women in food, land and water systems.
projectSpecificApplication: State the project's intervention areas and countries, whether every engaged woman was interviewed or a probability sample of the women the project engaged was drawn (state the sampling frame and the weights applied), and the baseline and endline survey timing. The population is fixed: the women CIMMYT engaged, matching KPI-O28's reach population. It is never a population-based sample of all women in the area; only how that fixed population is surveyed (census or probability sample of it) is a project choice. Do not change the self-report basis, the A-WEAI and pro-WEAI modules, or the improvement rule; if applying the indicator as defined is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this measure informs: for example a donor-required empowerment indicator, an evaluation design claiming empowerment effects, or an internal trigger to adjust intervention design if decision-making power is not improving where engagement is high.
projectTypesNotApplicable: breeding and varietal development and digital agriculture and AI
projectTypesRaw:
Applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation.

Not applicable: upstream discovery science, breeding and varietal development and digital agriculture and AI.
unit: Percentage of women in the measured panel. The absolute count is reported alongside, not instead: the share answers how widespread the improvement was and the count answers how many women it reached, and a reader needs both.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of the women in the measured panel are classified as improved in decision-making power over agricultural production, income and resources, on the two-round transition described in Definition. The measure is self-reported, so a change in how the question is asked moves the value as much as a change in the underlying decision-making power does.
disaggregationRequired: Required: age (youth/non-youth, using 15 to 30, stated once in Core §4.1; projects record date of birth or exact age so any other band, for example a donor band of 15 to 29, can be derived without recollecting data). The indicator is women-specific, so sex disaggregation does not apply.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country or region; which of the two decision-making indicators drove the improvement (input in productive decisions; ownership of land and other assets); household type (dual-adult, female-only).
unitOfObservation: The individual woman, identified across rounds so that improvement is measured on the same person rather than between two samples.
calculationSummary: Value = 100 × (unique women meeting the improvement rule) / (women in the measured panel inadequate at baseline on at least one of the two indicators), with the numerator count reported alongside the share. Improvement rule: a woman counts if she is classified adequate at endline on at least one of the two decision-making indicators on which she was inadequate at baseline, with no regression on the other. The indicator set is exactly two: input in productive decisions and ownership of land and other assets, the first fielded with the A-WEAI module and the second with the pro-WEAI module; no other indicator of either instrument, including pro-WEAI's input in livelihood decisions, enters the improvement rule. Adequacy is defined per indicator, since the two are different indicator types and one rule cannot score both. On input in productive decisions, the A-WEAI indicator (Alkire et al., 2013; Malapit et al., 2017, Tables 2.1 and 6.1; see Reference standards and links), scored on this sheet's own adequacy rule: at least some input in decisions for every agricultural activity she participates in, where the A-WEAI questionnaire's lowest response category combines no input and input into few decisions (Malapit et al., 2017, Table 4.3), so any higher response counts as some input. The rule is this sheet's, not the published A-WEAI cutoff, which the A-WEAI carries over unchanged from the WEAI (Malapit et al., 2017); values are therefore never compared with published A-WEAI adequacy headcounts. A woman who takes part in none of the module's agricultural activities has no productive decision to score and is classified inadequate on that indicator at that round; the count of such women at each round is reported alongside. On ownership of land and other assets, an asset-ownership indicator rather than a decision-input indicator, adequacy follows pro-WEAI's own ownership-adequacy criterion for that indicator, not the input scale: a woman is adequate where she owns, solely or jointly, at least one of (1) land, or (2) at least three categories of other assets, with no distinction between small and large asset categories in the current, revised instrument (Seymour et al., 2023, Table A1; see Reference standards and links). The reverse flow is reported alongside the improvement share: the count of women interviewed in every round of the window who were adequate at baseline on an indicator and become inadequate at endline with no offsetting gain on the other, that count as a share of the women interviewed in every round of the window, baseline and endline included, and the difference between the two counts (improved minus regressed), a difference of counts on different bases, not a net rate, so a rising improvement share is never read without knowing whether regression is rising too (see Limitations). Denominator: the measured panel, being the women interviewed in every round of the window, baseline and endline included, who were inadequate at baseline on at least one of the two indicators; women already adequate at baseline on both are excluded from both terms and their count is reported alongside, since they had no room to improve under this rule. Apply survey weights where a probability sample of the engaged-women population, rather than a census of it, was drawn. Inclusion: women the project engaged (KPI-O28's reach population), interviewed in every round of the window, baseline and endline included, answering for themselves. Exclusion: proxy responses (empowerment is self-reported by design); incomplete decision-making modules at either round. Missing data: incomplete modules are excluded, not imputed, since adequacy classification requires the full module. Repeated observations: one count per woman per measurement period; if a woman is re-contacted within a round, only the first completed interview counts.
dataSource: Recommended DS1: individual-level panel survey carrying the two decision-making modules, the A-WEAI module for input in productive decisions and the pro-WEAI module for ownership of land and other assets (IFPRI), with the same women interviewed at baseline and endline. Fallback DS1: a single-round design where no baseline exists: the two decision-making modules administered once, with the woman asked retrospectively whether her input has increased over the period. This produces a different, self-assessed quantity, a retrospective report of change, not this indicator's adequate-at-endline/inadequate-at-baseline transition, because a single round supplies no independent baseline classification and no independent endline classification to compare. Values from this route are reported separately, flagged as fallback-sourced, and are never pooled with Recommended-sourced values (see Aggregation rule Block D). Not applicable DS2: decision-making power is a self-reported perception and cannot be read from project administrative records. Not applicable DS3: not observable from satellite or geospatial data. Not applicable DS4: national surveys carrying empowerment modules cannot resolve CIMMYT intervention areas or track the same women across rounds. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or self-nominated claims cannot be verified against a sampling frame or a baseline state.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether Recommended or Fallback was used. If Fallback, state why no baseline round was fielded and record that the value rests on retrospective self-report.
collectionInstrument: IFPRI survey modules: at minimum the A-WEAI module for input in productive decisions and the pro-WEAI module for ownership of land and other assets, the two indicators the improvement rule is computed on. Respondent: the woman herself, interviewed privately, without other household members present, by a trained enumerator (female enumerators recommended). Mode: face-to-face preferred; phone acceptable where privacy can be assured.
collectionFrequency: Baseline and endline; for multi-year programs, a midline every 2 to 3 years.
reportingFrequency: Annually; between measurement waves, the latest measured value is carried forward with its measurement period noted.
referencePeriod: The project measurement cycle: change between the baseline round and the endline round. Each reported value describes that full period, not a single year.
baselineRequired: Yes. The indicator is a change measure, so a baseline round on the same women is required for the Recommended design. Fallback where no prospective baseline exists: the single-round retrospective self-report design above, reported as fallback-sourced. If neither is feasible: monitoring only, no impact claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One country, one instrument version and indicator set, one window length. Levels widen the set of women; they never widen the domain. Where a reporting level spans more than one country, instrument version or window length, the figures are reported side by side, one per domain, and never summed across them.

Weight: one per woman, each sampled woman carrying her survey weight where the engaged women were sampled. A woman meeting the rule on several measures counts once.

B: Combination method: ratio of sums.

The absolute count is reported alongside as a companion figure, together with the count of women excluded as already adequate at baseline on both indicators and the reverse-flow count (regressed women). Rebuild the share from woman-level records; never average project percentages. Apply survey weights where a probability sample of the engaged women, rather than a census of them, was drawn, and state them. A project whose latest endline predates the reporting year enters with its last measured sums and its endline year, the pooled figure being labeled with the range of endline years it combines.

C: Levels and operations. Household. The improvement status of the individual woman.

D: Never pooled. Shares computed on different indicator sets or instrument versions. Empowerment shares with KPI-O28's engagement counts. A sample estimate computed without its survey weights. Panels of different window length. Recommended-sourced shares with Fallback-sourced values, since the Fallback route computes a different, self-assessed retrospective quantity, not this indicator's baseline-to-endline transition.

E: Deduplication and coverage. Within a project the persistent participant identifier de-duplicates the panel, applied from Household level upward. Across projects no union is computed, and a figure combining projects is labeled not de-duplicated across projects. The instrument version and the indicator set travel with every figure. Coverage and precision travel with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands used in official statistics: 16.5 percent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 percent released flagged, above 33.3 percent not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one de-duplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above, and a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Include women present in every round of the window with responses to both decision-making modules recorded.

Exclude women missing any round; report them as attrition with the count. A share computed over women who stayed, against a baseline over everyone, reports who left.

Exclude windows spanning a change of instrument version or indicator set, which produce an apparent change that is instrumental.

Exclude women adequate at baseline on both indicators: they have no room to improve under this rule, so they are excluded from both numerator and denominator, and their count is reported alongside as a result in its own right, not as missing data.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only: decision-making power also responds to social norms, education, household composition, migration and policy; CIMMYT is one contributor among many, and an evaluation design is needed for any effect claim.

Self-reported measures carry known biases: social desirability, the presence of other household members during the interview, and adaptive preferences (women may report input levels that conform to prevailing norms). Private interviews and consistent enumeration protocols reduce but do not remove these.

Comparability across projects holds only if the same modules and the same improvement rule are used; CGIAR's standard indicator does not fix a metric, so a project using a different empowerment instrument produces values that cannot be pooled with these.
The A-WEAI module was designed for a household's primary adult decision-makers aged 18 and over (Malapit et al., 2017); values for women aged 15 to 17 rest on it outside that design.

An absolute count grows with survey coverage and project reach: a larger value can reflect more women surveyed rather than deeper change. Read it with the share of surveyed women improving, reported alongside.

An increase means more surveyed women crossed the improvement rule; it does not mean household gender gaps closed or that empowerment is adequate in level terms. Pair with the gender adoption gap (KPI-OC19) for the equity reading.

The rule counts gains only unless the reverse flow is read with it, and two further mechanisms can push the share up independent of any real change. Adequacy is a binary cut on a self-reported response, so ordinary response variation around the cut produces apparent "improvements" in both directions, and only the upward ones are counted unless the reverse flow (Calculation method) is reported alongside; and the denominator is selected on baseline inadequacy, which over-represents women whose baseline response was a negative measurement error likely to revert upward at endline (regression to the mean). Report the reverse flow and the already-adequate-at-baseline exclusion count with every value, and read a rising improvement share against a stable or rising regression count before treating it as a real gain.
subMetrics: None. The two decision-making indicators are disaggregations of where improvement occurred, not separately reported sub-metrics. The gender adoption gap is a separate indicator with its own sheet (KPI-OC19).
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
Named measurement standards: the Abbreviated Women's Empowerment in Agriculture Index (A-WEAI) for input in productive decisions, and the Project-level Women's Empowerment in Agriculture Index (pro-WEAI) for ownership of land and other assets. This indicator does not use a bespoke empowerment question. Improvement is determined on those two indicators, on the adequacy rule Calculation method states for each, and the sheet locks the self-report basis, the modules and the improvement rule so that the measure is comparable across projects.

IFPRI, the instrument's version page, for pro-WEAI's domains and module construction: https://weai.ifpri.info/versions/pro-weai/

IFPRI, the questionnaire modules and computation guides behind pro-WEAI (the WEAI Resource Center): https://weai.ifpri.info/weai-resource-center/guides-and-instruments/

Ownership-of-land-and-other-assets adequacy cutoff: Seymour, G., Faas, S., Ferguson, N., Heckert, J., Malapit, H., Meinzen-Dick, R., Quisumbing, A. R., & van Biljon, C. (2023). A multi-country validation and sensitivity analysis of the project-level Women's Empowerment in Agriculture Index (Pro-WEAI) (IFPRI Discussion Paper 2201). International Food Policy Research Institute. Table A1 (Appendix, printed p. 37, PDF p. 44): owns, solely or jointly, land or at least three categories of other assets, no small/large split in the revised instrument. https://hdl.handle.net/10568/140313

Input-in-productive-decisions indicator and its module (A-WEAI): Malapit, H., Pinkstaff, C., Sproule, K., Kovarik, C., Quisumbing, A., & Meinzen-Dick, R. (2017). The Abbreviated Women's Empowerment in Agriculture Index (A-WEAI) (IFPRI Discussion Paper 01647). International Food Policy Research Institute. Table 2.1 (PDF p. 10), Table 4.3 (PDF p. 16) and Table 6.1 (PDF p. 25): the indicator's name, agricultural-decision scope and response categories. https://hdl.handle.net/10568/148376 / Alkire et al. (2013), The Women's Empowerment in Agriculture Index, World Development 52: the original WEAI, from which the A-WEAI carries the indicator. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.worlddev.2013.06.007 (paywalled; cited by DOI).

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.

Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (improvement rule per Calculation method above). Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.

name: Number of agroecological / ecological solution packages validated in farming systems
resultsLevel: Output. A package with a documented performance result from field testing is a delivered result of the research team and its testing partners. Whether farmers then use it is a change in practice, measured further along the pathway.
primaryObjective: PO4 Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient. It sits under the PO4 sub-objective "Ecological solutions are widely deployed, especially in smallholder farming systems, for climate resilience, environmental, economic, and socio-cultural benefits": validation is the step that must be passed before deployment can be claimed. Contributing objective, contribution only: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved).
cgiarImpactArea: Environmental Health & Biodiversity: these packages are designed to improve soil, nutrient, water and biodiversity outcomes in production systems. Many also serve Climate Adaptation & Mitigation; that is a contribution, not a second area.
sdgTarget: None. The closest target is SDG 2.4 (sustainable food production systems and resilient practices), but its official indicator 2.4.1, proportion of agricultural area under productive and sustainable agriculture, measures the share of farmed area meeting sustainability thresholds, not the number of packages proven to work. The research indicators under targets 2.a and 9.5 measure spending and researcher numbers.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR: the Innovation Development output category, "a new, improved, or adapted output of groups of outputs", admits a package, and the Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 requires innovation type, readiness level and a contact point as minimum output-level data. CIMMYT supplies those fields where it reports into that system, but this indicator rests on a documented field result, not on a readiness level.
definition: Counts the package-and-context validations: an agroecological or ecological solution package that completed field testing confirming performance in farming systems in one context (agroecology, cropping system and class of users) during the reporting year. A solution package is a set of agronomic and ecological practices, inputs and management components assembled for use together in a defined cropping system, for example residue retention with reduced tillage and a legume rotation. Validation means field testing under conditions resembling those the intended farmers face has concluded and the package met the performance criteria its protocol set before testing, evidenced by a dated trial or evaluation record. On-station testing and packages still under test at year end do not count.
rationale: Answers whether the ecological and agroecological options CIMMYT develops work in real farming systems before anyone puts them into use with farmers. It is the evidence gate on the sustainable land management pathway: this count shows what was proven, deployment (KPI-O31) shows what was then put into use, and the field-level environmental outcomes show what changed. It serves project pipeline management, deciding which packages go forward and which return for redesign, and institutional and donor reporting on CIMMYT's contribution to more sustainable agrifood systems.
projectSpecificApplication: State the packages under test and their components; the cropping systems, countries and agroecologies covered; the testing network used; and where the performance criteria are recorded. Do not alter the institutional definition, the validation conditions, the unit or the counting rule; if applying it is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point.
projectSpecificRationale: State which donor milestone or results-framework line the count provides evidence for, which project decision it informs (typically which packages are released for deployment), and what a shortfall would trigger, for example a review of trial siting or of package composition.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.  Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure.
unit: Number of package-and-context validations: one solution package validated for one context (agroecology, cropping system and class of users), not trials, sites, seasons or farmers.
directionOfChange: Increase, read together with KPI-O31. A rising value means more package-and-context validations were completed. A count of validated packages that never reach farmers indicates a pipeline not moving to deployment.
disaggregationRequired: Required: none recorded in the register, which reads "n/a". Two are required on this sheet's authority: package theme (soil and nutrient management; water; pest, weed and disease management; diversification and rotations; trees and landscape elements) and country. Agroecology is not a theme category: a package meeting the formal international definition of agroecology is flagged as agroecological, an optional cut. The unit counted is a package, not a person, so sex and age categories do not apply to it; who took part in testing belongs in the participation record under Collection instrument.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Cropping system and main crop; farm scale served; testing sites and seasons behind each validation; partner type that ran the testing; whether women farmers and youth took part in the assessment.
unitOfObservation: Result object: one agroecological or ecological solution package. A package is a countable thing that is not a person, a place or a post, which is what the result-object value covers; evidence is collected at plot level and rolled up to one record per package.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct package-and-context validations meeting four conditions during the reporting year: (a) the package combines agronomic or ecological components intended for use together in a defined cropping system; (b) it was field tested under conditions resembling those its intended users face, on farmers' fields or on a site set up to reproduce them; (c) the protocol stated the performance criteria before testing began; (d) a dated trial or evaluation record shows the package met them. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1 (censuses and surveys, which in the CIMMYT typology includes objective field measurement and on-farm trials): the field testing itself, that is the agronomic and environmental measurements on the trial plots plus the participating farmers' and partners' assessment, recorded against the protocol. Farmer-managed crowdsourced testing is not DS1, whoever runs it; a validation evidenced only by it rests on Fallback DS5 below. Fallback DS2 (administrative and registry data): a partner's own validation record where CIMMYT does not hold the underlying trial data, for example a national research or extension partner that ran the testing. Use only where primary trial data are unavailable, and flag the validation as fallback-sourced, since the criteria applied may differ. Not applicable DS3 (geospatial and Earth observation): satellite and GIS data can show where a practice is visible on the landscape but cannot establish that a package met stated criteria in a controlled comparison. Not applicable DS4 (secondary and international databases): no independent database records CIMMYT validation events; CGIAR systems hold CIMMYT's own submissions. Not applicable DS5 (citizen-generated data) by default: unstructured farmer feedback cannot establish a documented result against pre-stated criteria. Fallback DS5 where the project runs farmer-managed crowdsourced testing, on the same validation conditions as any other design, those the Definition sets; the record says so.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role each validation rests on. For Recommended and for Fallback DS5, give the testing design, number of sites and seasons behind each validated package. For Fallback DS2, explain why primary trial data were unavailable, name the partner that supplied the record, and state which criteria it applied.
collectionInstrument: The testing protocol for each package, carrying the pre-stated criteria and the comparison used (normally the prevailing farmer practice), paired with a structured assessment form completed with participating farmers and partner staff at or after harvest. Respondent: the farmer or farmer group hosting the trial, with the partner staff running it. Mode: field measurement plus face-to-face evaluation.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as trial and evaluation records are produced at the end of each testing cycle; consolidated once a year.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Annual values may not be added across years into a cumulative total unless each package carries a stable identifier allowing duplicates to be removed first.
referencePeriod: The 12-month institutional reporting year in which the validation result was documented. Where testing runs across several seasons, the value belongs to the year the result was confirmed, not the year testing began. A within-year count, not a cumulative stock.
baselineRequired: No. An annual count of validation events starting from zero each year, so there is no prior-period reference value. A prior-year value remains useful for trend comparison, and the pipeline reference point is the project's own cohort of packages under test.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Across projects: sum distinct package-and-context validations evidenced by the Recommended source; a validation evidenced only by a Fallback (a DS2 partner record or DS5 crowdsourced testing) is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note naming its route, not blended in, and the same project's Recommended-sourced validations stay in the pool.

B: Combination method. The institutional figure is the sum of distinct package-and-context validations after de-duplication; never average project counts.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying package-and-context validations for the reporting year. At institutional level, the de-duplicated sum of those counts, computed from the records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one package is often reported by more than one project. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels: a package has no plot and no household, so the levels here are reporting levels. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the validation evidence each package rests on, the number excluded under Eligibility and why, and the number of validations reported alongside because they rest on a Fallback, by route.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: no. This count does not combine arithmetically with KPI-O31 (packages deployed) or with the indicators downstream of it (KPI-OC33, KPI-OC27 to KPI-OC31, KPI-I10). The same package passes through several steps, so adding across levels would count one object more than once; the levels connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: the same package is often tested by more than one project, country or season, and may also be reported by another CGIAR center. De-duplicate before pooling on package title plus cropping system plus lead partner, and label the pooled number an upper estimate. Overlap must be named and never summed: components of a package may separately be counted as innovations co-developed (KPI-O01) and validated through participatory engagement (KPI-O02), so the same object can appear in both counts. The boundary this sheet applies is the object counted, not the stage: KPI-O01 and KPI-O02 count an innovation, this indicator counts a package of components assembled for one cropping system, and one package built from three counted innovations is one package here and three innovations there. Both are reported and neither is netted out. KPI-O11 in Genetic resources, breeding & seed is not an overlap: it counts genomic, phenotyping and bioinformatics platforms and tools at release, which are not agroecological components deployed in a farming system.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion and exclusion: include only packages whose testing concluded with a documented result inside the reporting year; a package is at least two components intended for use together, so a single practice is not a package, and the project MEAL focal point rules borderline cases and records the reason; exclude packages still under test at year end, on-station-only testing, packages that failed their criteria, and packages already counted for the same context in an earlier year.
limitations: Validated is not deployed and not adopted. The count says a package was proven to perform under farmer-like conditions, not that any farmer uses it or benefits from it. Read it as the evidence gate, with KPI-O31 and the outcome indicators.

A count treats unlike things alike. One package may be a two-component soil practice, another a full integrated system for a cropping cycle, and each validation is worth one. No weighting is applied, so read the number with the package-theme split rather than on its own.

Counting and testing conventions move the number more than the science does. Splitting one system into three packages, or defining "performs as intended" loosely, raises the count without raising the evidence, and a researcher-managed plot is not the same test as a farmer-managed one. Record the package boundary, the criteria and the testing design with the value.

A rise means more ecological options were confirmed to work that year, not that farming systems changed; a fall may reflect testing cycles, season quality or project timing rather than weaker performance.
subMetrics: None. Package theme, cropping system, country and agroecology are disaggregations of a single count, not separately calculated metrics. The neighbouring steps have their own sheets: KPI-O31 (packages deployed) and, downstream, KPI-OC33 (cultivated land under improved or sustainable practices) and the field-level environmental outcomes KPI-OC27 to KPI-OC31.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the sustainable agriculture and agroecology research lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project research and agronomy teams with the partner staff and farmers who run the testing. Validation: the responsible scientist confirms the evidence meets the protocol criteria and the project MEAL officer confirms the record is complete. Calculation: project M&E applies the counting rule; cross-project de-duplication by the CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
