name: Number of agroecological or ecological solution packages deployed in farming systems
resultsLevel: Output. A package deployed (assembled, supplied with guidance and materials, delivered through partners) is a delivered result. Whether farmers keep using the package, and at what scale, is a change in practice measured at outcome level (KPI-OC33 and the resource-efficiency outcomes). "Put into use with farmers" can also be read as innovation use, which CGIAR classifies as an outcome; the Calculation method's test, a documented deployment event rather than continued use, is what holds this at output level.
primaryObjective: PO4 Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient. This indicator measures sub-objective 4.1 directly: ecological solutions are widely deployed, especially in smallholder farming systems. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved), since deployment is targeted at smallholder systems.
cgiarImpactArea: Environmental Health & Biodiversity. Ecological solution packages act on soil, nutrient, water and pest management, which is where their measured effect appears in this pathway. Where a package is deployed for climate resilience there is a secondary contribution to Climate Adaptation & Mitigation, carried by the resilience indicators rather than by this count. The register carries no Impact Area column; the value follows the pathway-wide rule, which sets the area by what the indicator measures.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest target is SDG 2.4 (sustainable food production systems and resilient agricultural practices), but its official indicator 2.4.1 measures the proportion of agricultural area under productive and sustainable agriculture: how much farmland already meets sustainability criteria, not how many solutions were delivered. That area concept maps to KPI-OC33 and KPI-I10, not here.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Results Framework: the Innovation Development output category, a new, improved or adapted output or group of outputs with high potential for impact at scale, covers the object counted here; CGIAR has no output-level standard indicator for deployment, and its nearest entries ("Number of innovation packages designed", "Number of innovations being used") sit under Innovation Use at outcome level. Terminology: "solution package" is CIMMYT's own term from the 2030 Strategy, not CGIAR's construct "innovation package", and this indicator is not a scaling-readiness score.
definition: Counts the distinct agroecological or ecological solution packages that CIMMYT and its delivery partners put into use with farmers during the reporting year, counted once per country of deployment. A solution package is a defined bundle of agronomic practices, technologies and management guidance meant to be used together in a stated farming system, for example conservation agriculture combining reduced tillage, residue retention and rotation with the seeding equipment needed to apply it. Deployment means a package that has completed validation (counted at KPI-O30) is delivered into farmer use for the first time in that country, at one or more identified sites that year, with a dated delivery record. Packages still in field testing belong to KPI-O30 and are not counted here.
rationale: Answers how many validated ecological solutions CIMMYT moved into farmers' fields in the year, as distinct from how many it tested. CIMMYT's 2030 Strategy commits to ecological solutions being widely deployed, especially in smallholder farming systems; this is the annual delivery count against that commitment, and the point where the environmental sustainability pathway turns from research output into changes the soil, nutrient, water and pesticide indicators can register.
projectSpecificApplication: State which validated packages the project deploys, in which farming systems, countries and sites, through which delivery route (project or national extension, partner organisation, seed or input supplier), and which records evidence delivery. Do not change the counting unit, the validation prerequisite, or the counting rule below; if applying the indicator as defined is not feasible, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count serves: a donor-required technology-delivery indicator, a scaling milestone in the project results framework, or an internal trigger to review the delivery route if validated packages accumulate without reaching farmers.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.  Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure.
unit: Number of solution packages deployed, counted once per country of deployment. A package deployed in three countries contributes three, in its first deployment year in each; several sites, partners or projects deploying it within one country contribute one.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more validated packages were put into use with farmers.
disaggregationRequired: Required: solution type (soil and nutrient management; water management; pest, weed and disease management; crop diversification and rotation; agroforestry and landscape measures) and country. Agroecology is not a solution-type category: a package meeting the formal international definition of agroecology is flagged as agroecological, an optional cut. The register sets no required disaggregation here; these two are required on this sheet's authority, because the count cannot be interpreted without them.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Farming system or agroecological zone; crop; delivery partner type (public / private); first-time versus continuing deployment. Scale of deployment (sites, farmers or hectares reached) may be reported as context alongside the count but is never the value.
unitOfObservation: Result object: one agroecological or ecological solution package in one country, observed through project and partner deployment records. A package is a countable thing that is not a person, a place or a post, which is what the result-object value covers.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct package-and-country combinations for which a validated solution package has at least one documented deployment event with farmers in the reporting year, counted in that country's first deployment year. One package in three countries is three; one package deployed at many sites in one country is one. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: project and partner administrative records, namely the package or innovation register (package identity and validation record), deployment and delivery logs, extension service delivery reports, and partner reports naming date, site, package and farmers reached. Fallback DS1: a site verification survey confirming with delivering staff and farmers that the package was delivered and is in use, where records exist but lack dated or attributable delivery evidence, or where delivery ran through partners that do not report to project standards; values from this route are flagged as fallback-sourced. Not applicable DS3: satellite and geospatial data can indicate area under a practice, which is what KPI-OC33 and KPI-I10 measure, but cannot identify a bundle as a specific package or attribute its delivery. Not applicable DS4: no third-party database records which CIMMYT packages were deployed, by whom or when. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced observations can suggest a practice is present but cannot verify package identity, validation status or CIMMYT support.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether the Recommended or the Fallback source was used, which registers and delivery records supplied the count, and how deployment was evidenced. If Fallback, state why administrative records could not support the count.
collectionInstrument: For the DS1 fallback: a short site verification checklist recording package identity and components delivered, date, partner, site and farmers reached; respondent is the delivering staff member or the site's lead farmer; administered in person. The DS2 route uses a standard deployment record template (package identifier, validation reference, country, site, date, delivery route, partner) completed as deployment happens.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as project and partner teams record deployment events; compiled and de-duplicated annually.
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which deployment took place, aligned to CIMMYT's institutional reporting year.
baselineRequired: No. An annual delivery count with a baseline of zero, which is CIMMYT's counting convention for a flow. A trend can be read only where the counting rule is held constant; if it changes, the series restarts and the segments must not be joined.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool the package-country records evidenced in project and partner delivery records (Recommended); a record evidenced only through the site verification survey (Fallback) is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, and the same project's Recommended-sourced records stay in the pool.

B: Combination method. Sum distinct packages across projects after de-duplication by package identity and country, so a package deployed by two projects in one country counts once institutionally.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying agroecological or ecological solution packages deployed for the reporting year. At institutional level, the de-duplicated sum of those counts, computed from the records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one package is often reported by more than one project. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels: a package has no plot and no household, so the levels here are reporting levels. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the boundary with KPI-O30's validation stage, since a package crossing it mid-year appears in both counts and the two are never summed, the number excluded under Eligibility and why, and the number of records reported alongside because they rest on the Fallback.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count does not add to KPI-OC33, KPI-I10 or the resource-efficiency outcomes, which measure area and intensity; the levels connect through the theory of change, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: de-duplicate by package identifier and country before summing; where identifier systems differ and packages cannot be matched, label the pooled figure an upper estimate. Overlap with other register indicators must be named, never summed: KPI-O30 counts the same packages one stage earlier, at validation; its components may also be counted as innovations under KPI-O01 and KPI-O02 in Innovation development & scaling, which is overlap by construction and must be stated rather than netted out, on the same object-not-stage boundary KPI-O30 states; KPI-O11 in Genetic resources, breeding & seed is not an overlap, since it counts platforms and tools at release rather than deployed agroecological packages; deployment sites feed KPI-OC33 and KPI-I10, which measure area (a share of cultivated land, and hectares) and are not derivable from this count.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusions: the package completed validation in this or an earlier year, whether or not KPI-O30 pools that validation; delivery is evidenced by a dated record naming the package, site, delivering partner and farmers reached; CIMMYT or a partner under a CIMMYT project agreement supported the delivery.

Exclusions: packages still under field testing (KPI-O30); researcher-managed demonstration or trial plots, which are testing, not delivery; packages promoted only through a publication, training or advisory message with no delivery into farmer use, which belong to the knowledge-product and capacity indicators; packages deployed by other actors with no CIMMYT or partner involvement; individual components counted separately from the package. A package is at least two components deliberately used together and promoted as a set; a single practice is not a package, and the project MEAL focal point rules borderline cases and records the reason.

Missing data: a candidate package with no dated delivery record is excluded rather than estimated, since the claim is documentary; a Fallback site verification checklist recording package, date, site, delivering partner and farmers reached is a dated delivery record for this test; report the number of excluded candidates alongside the value, so weak record-keeping is visible rather than read as low delivery.

Repeated observations: count each package once per country, in the first reporting year its deployment begins, and again only where deployment extends to a further country; several sites, partners or projects deploying it in one country do not multiply the count. The alternative reading, re-counting every year deployment is active, gives a larger and non-comparable series and is not used; packages in active deployment are a cumulative companion figure.
limitations: Counts packages, not scale or benefit. The count is independent of reach and says nothing about effect. Read it alongside the area and intensity indicators in this pathway.

The boundary of a package is a judgement. What one project treats as one bundle another may report as three practices, inflating the count. Comparability depends on applying the definition consistently and naming each counted package in the reporting comment.
Delivery is not sustained use. A package delivered this year may be abandoned next year; continued use and its environmental effects are measured by the outcome indicators.
Contribution only. Deployment runs through national extension systems, partners and input suppliers, and depends on their capacity and on farmer demand.

A rise means more distinct validated solutions reached farmers that year, not that farming systems became more sustainable or that more land is under them. A fall may reflect a portfolio moving from delivery into consolidation rather than weaker performance.
subMetrics: None. Solution types are disaggregations of the same count, not separately calculated metrics. Related indicators have their own sheets: KPI-O30 (packages validated, the preceding stage), KPI-OC33 (proportion of cultivated land under improved or sustainable practices), KPI-OC27 to KPI-OC31 (soil organic carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus use efficiency, water intensity, pesticide intensity), and KPI-I10 (hectares under improved management).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the sustainable agrifood systems / agronomy lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project field teams and delivery partners recording deployment events. Validation: project MEAL officer (validation status confirmed, delivery records dated and attributable, package boundary applied consistently). Calculation: project M&E, applying the once-per-country rule; cross-project de-duplication by the CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the MEAL unit.

name: Change in soil organic carbon stock (t C/ha, 0 to 30 cm) relative to baseline
resultsLevel: Outcome
primaryObjective: PO4 Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient. Contributing objectives: none; the register lists PO4 alone.
cgiarImpactArea: Environmental Health & Biodiversity. Soil carbon is measured here as a property of soil condition in the production system. It also feeds CIMMYT's sequestration reporting, which sits under Climate Adaptation & Mitigation; only one Impact Area can be recorded, and Environmental Health & Biodiversity is taken because what is measured here is soil condition, while the sequestration quantity is KPI-I11's.
sdgTarget: SDG indicator 15.3.1 (proportion of land that is degraded over total land area), target 15.3. Partial correspondence: soil organic carbon stock is the metric the UN Convention to Combat Desertification adopted for the carbon stocks sub-indicator of 15.3.1, so the quantity is the same, but 15.3.1 is a binary degraded / not degraded classification combining three sub-indicators, which this KPI does not compute.
otherFrameworks: UNCCD Land Degradation Neutrality monitoring (carbon stocks sub-indicator). FAO Global Soil Partnership GSOC-MRV, the voluntary protocol this sheet follows. ISO 14064-2:2019, where a project reports the gain as a greenhouse gas removal enhancement rather than as a soil condition.
definition: Measures the change in the amount of organic carbon stored in the top 30 cm of soil in CIMMYT intervention areas, compared with the stock measured at the same locations before the intervention. The stock is the mass of organic carbon per hectare, from the carbon concentration of the fine soil fraction, its bulk density and the thickness of each sampled layer, summed over the 0 to 10 cm and 10 to 30 cm layers. It is reported for a defined interval between two sampling rounds and read as a contribution of improved soil and crop management; a business-as-usual comparison strengthens that reading and is recorded with the figure. Soil carbon moves slowly and varies strongly over short distances, so only a repeat measurement at the same place by the same method is a change.
rationale: Answers whether the soil and crop management practices CIMMYT promotes are building carbon in the soil where they are used, rather than only being adopted. Projects use it to judge whether a practice package works in local conditions, and institutional and donor reporting uses it as the measured evidence behind CIMMYT's contribution to carbon sequestration and soil health.
projectSpecificApplication: State the intervention areas and their hectares, the sampling strata, the practice package the change is read against, the dates of the baseline and follow-up rounds, the laboratory used, and any modelled estimate reported alongside the measured value as labelled context. Do not change the depth interval, stock equation, equivalent-soil-mass basis or unit. If no follow-up round is feasible within the project cycle, raise it with the MEAL focal point.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment the value serves: a logframe outcome on soil health or carbon, a national land-degradation reporting obligation, or a trigger to revisit the residue and tillage components if stocks are flat at the first follow-up round.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.  Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure.
unit: Tonnes of organic carbon per hectare (t C/ha), as the change between two rounds; where an annual rate is needed, that value divided by the years between rounds (t C/ha/yr). The value pooled across intervention areas is that annual rate (Aggregation rule, Block B).
directionOfChange: Increase. A higher value means the soil organic carbon stock in the 0 to 30 cm layer grew more against baseline.
disaggregationRequired: Required: intervention area (the spatial unit the stock is estimated for) and management practice package; a value pooled across different packages cannot be interpreted. The register records no required disaggregation, so these two are adopted as required. Sex and age disaggregation are not applicable: the unit of observation is a sampling location, not a person.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Depth layer (0 to 10 cm, 10 to 30 cm); soil type and climate stratum; crop or rotation; irrigated / rainfed; years since adoption; farm size class.
unitOfObservation: Plot (the sampling location and its stratum within the intervention area)
calculationSummary: A difference between two measured stocks, not a ratio. Stock per layer (t C/ha) = carbon concentration of the fine earth fraction (< 2 mm) in mg C per g (g C per kg) x fine-earth bulk density x (1 minus the volume fraction of coarse fragments) x layer thickness in cm x 0.1, the last term being the factor that converts mg C per cm2 to tonnes of carbon per hectare; this is the GSOC-MRV stock equation adapted from IPCC. Value = the 0 to 30 cm stock (sum of the two layers) at the follow-up round minus the same stock at baseline, on an equivalent soil mass basis using the lighter (lower bulk density) soil as reference mass, area-weighted across strata to one figure per intervention area. In a series of three or more rounds, the reference mass for a stratum is the lowest 0 to 30 cm fine-earth mass observed in any round, and earlier rounds are restated to it when a new round is added. Every change is reported with its standard error and the minimum detectable difference of the design (GSOC-MRV Equation A3.1, at a significance level of 0.05 and a power of 0.80 unless the project states otherwise); a change smaller than the minimum detectable difference is reported as "no change detected at this design" with both numbers, never as a gain or a loss. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1: field measurement, soil sampling with laboratory determination of carbon concentration and bulk density under a stratified design, the only source that observes the stock itself. No modelled route holds a Fallback role on this indicator, because a Fallback is a route that produces the value and a modelled soil-carbon change may not be reported as the value. A soil carbon model (for example RothC, or the IPCC Tier 2 steady-state method) driven by project management records and secondary climate and soil datasets may be run as labelled context alongside the measured value, never in place of it; where no follow-up round is feasible, the indicator is not reported for that period and the model output is published as context with the reason stated. Fallback DS1, scoped to carbon concentration: soil spectroscopy on the sampled composites in place of dry combustion or wet oxidation, which the protocol permits only where evidence shows the method is calibrated for local soils and the agroecological zone; bulk density and coarse fragments are measured as under Recommended DS1. Not applicable DS2: administrative records cannot observe a soil carbon stock; management records serve only as inputs to a model run as context. Not applicable DS3: remote sensing cannot observe a 0 to 30 cm stock at the sampled locations. Not applicable DS4: secondary soil and climate datasets cannot resolve a stock change at fixed locations; they serve only as model inputs for context. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced and other non-traditional data cannot produce laboratory-grade carbon concentration and bulk density from a georeferenced design.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State the role used: Recommended (measured) or Fallback DS1 (spectroscopy). If spectroscopy, cite the calibration evidence. Where a model was run as context, say so, name the model and state that it did not produce the value. Where the baseline was a paired business-as-usual field or a modelled stock, name which, give the years since adoption or the model and its local validation, and state that the value is reported alongside the pooled figure.
collectionInstrument: For DS1: a sampling plan following the GSOC-MRV soil sampling sub-protocol. Stratified simple random sampling, or directed stratified sampling where prior information on variability exists; minimum three strata per intervention area, minimum three and preferably five or more composites per stratum, 5 to 15 cores per composite. Depths 0 to 10 cm and 10 to 30 cm, GPS coordinates recorded so every location can be revisited. Bulk density by intact core (about 100 cm³) or by excavation in stony soils. Laboratory: dry combustion (Dumas) preferred, wet oxidation (Walkley-Black) accepted, following GLOSOLAN standard operating procedures, same method and preferably same laboratory across rounds. On the Fallback DS1 route, carbon concentration is determined by soil spectroscopy on the same composites, with the local calibration evidence Data source requires held with the value.
collectionFrequency: Complete round (carbon concentration and bulk density, both layers) at baseline and at least every four years. Optional particulate organic carbon, and model-based updates where used, every two years.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Between rounds the last measured change is carried forward with its measurement year stated; a modelled interim estimate may sit alongside it, labelled as such.
referencePeriod: The interval in years between the baseline round (time zero) and the follow-up round being reported. The protocol sets a complete round at least every four years, and four years is the institutional minimum interval: a shorter interval is not reported, because soil organic carbon changes slowly against high spatial variability and a shorter interval reports sampling noise as change. Projects shorter than four years do not report this indicator.
baselineRequired: Yes, and not substitutable: a baseline round at time zero is mandatory under the protocol, since the indicator is defined as change from it. Fallbacks where none exists: a paired business-as-usual field in the same soil and climate stratum sampled at the same time (space for time), reported as a difference between treated and business-as-usual stocks at one date rather than a change over time, with the years since the practice package was adopted on the treated field stated and at least four, or a modelled baseline stock from a locally validated model, both flagged; a value computed against either is reported for the project and sits alongside the pooled figure, never in it, since neither is a repeat measurement at the same place. If neither is feasible: report the current stock as a state measure only, with no change claim.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One practice package, on the 0 to 30 cm equivalent-soil-mass basis; weight: hectares of intervention area. Levels widen the set of intervention areas; they never widen the domain: changes under different packages are reported side by side and no combined figure exists. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool measured DS1 values directly; spectroscopy-sourced Fallback values, modelled estimates carried as context, and a change computed against a modelled baseline stock or against a paired business-as-usual field sit alongside the pooled figure with a note, never blended in.

B: Combination method. Pool as an area-weighted mean annual rate: each intervention area's change divided by the years between its rounds, times its area, summed and divided by total area (t C/ha/yr), with the range of intervals and the latest round year stated beside it. Where an absolute figure is wanted, report the summed tonnes of carbon gained with each area's baseline and latest round years. Never average per-hectare values across areas of different size.

C: Levels and operations. Two things are computed and neither may be averaged upward. The level is recomputed at every level from its own measured cores, never from the figures beneath it. The change is recomputed the same way, as the difference between two figures each built at that level from its own records, never as a mean of plot-level changes. At Farm / Plot, the stock at 0 to 30 cm on that plot, on its own sampling design. At Regional / Aggregated and above, the same construction over the summed area within the pooling domain of Block A, differenced against the baseline built identically. Above the intervention area the pooled change is Block B's area-weighted annual rate, each area's rate being its own two-round difference over its own interval, which at a common interval equals the change in the pooled stock divided by that interval. Also report: the area the figure rests on, the units excluded under Eligibility, the measurement or model basis of both terms, and whether the same units were measured in both periods, since a change across a changed panel is not a change on the ground. The minimum detectable difference is reported with every change.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. It does not sum with the count of ecological solution packages deployed that feeds it, nor with the sequestration indicator it rolls up to, which is in carbon dioxide equivalent and carries verification requirements this measurement alone does not meet. The levels connect through the theory of change.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: the risk is hectares, not people. De-duplicate by the georeferenced boundaries of intervention areas before pooling, using the GPS coordinates the protocol requires, and count the same hectares once when their gain enters the sequestration figure; the gain never enters greenhouse gas intensity reporting, whose numerator is gross of soil carbon (KPI-I09). Where boundaries cannot be resolved, label the pooled area and gain an upper estimate. Coverage and precision travel with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands used in official statistics: 16.5 per cent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 per cent released flagged, above 33.3 per cent not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one deduplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above, and a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place. On this sheet a record is one analysed composite sample in one round, summed across the strata and intervention areas of the pooling domain; cores bulked into a composite are not records. At the protocol minimum of nine composites per intervention area, a pooling domain with fewer than four intervention areas is below the floor, so a project that needs a releasable Project-area estimate plans at least 30 composites per round across it. The change between rounds is a derived quantity and carries no floor of its own, though each round's stock estimate must have been releasable.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Missing data: a stratum whose composite is lost or fails laboratory quality control is resampled within the sampling window; if it cannot be, the stratum is dropped from both rounds, its area is reported as excluded, and the change is stated for the remaining area only; its area is never reallocated to other strata, which would impute its change from theirs. Where bulk density was not determined, dry soil mass per known sampled volume may replace it, with the substitution stated.

Repeated observations: one complete round per point in time, first complete set if a stratum is sampled twice, rounds taken within one month of the median sampling day of earlier rounds.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim. A counterfactual, where a project holds one, strengthens that claim and is recorded with the figure; it does not license a stronger term. Soil carbon responds to rainfall, temperature, yields, residue and manure availability and land-use history as well as to management, so without a business-as-usual comparison a measured rise cannot be assigned to the practice package.

Detection is the binding constraint. The smallest detectable difference depends on the number of composites and site variability, and a value below that threshold is not evidence that nothing changed, which is why the protocol samples at four and eight years rather than annually.

Comparability breaks easily. Fixed-depth stocks are biased upward where soil is more compact, which favours reduced-tillage treatments unless the equivalent soil mass adjustment is applied, and wet oxidation recovers only about 75 to 90 percent of total organic carbon. Hold depth basis, laboratory method and laboratory constant across rounds. Measured and modelled values are also not interchangeable: a model output is a projection conditioned on the activity data entered.

A rise means more organic carbon was measured in the top 30 cm of the sampled area at that date. It does not mean permanent removal from the atmosphere: gains reverse if practices lapse, and it is not a verified carbon credit.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
Measurement: FAO (2020), GSOC-MRV protocol: Measurement, monitoring, reporting and verification of soil organic carbon in agricultural landscapes, GSOC-MRV Protocol, June 2020, FAO Global Soil Partnership and Intergovernmental Technical Panel on Soils; monitoring rounds; sampling sub-protocol; stock equation, equivalent soil mass and laboratory methods.

Measurement: IPCC (2019), 2019 refinement to the 2006 IPCC guidelines for national greenhouse gas inventories, Volume 4: Agriculture, forestry and other land use, Ch. 2 Generic Methodologies, Equation 2.25 (annual change in organic carbon stocks in mineral soils) and the 20-year default transition period (2.32 to 2.34); Ch. 5 Cropland, Tier choice and the Tier 2 steady-state method for the 0 to 30 cm layer (5.15 to 5.16).

ISO 14064-2:2019, greenhouse gases, project-level quantification, monitoring and reporting of emission reductions and removal enhancements. Cited by number, part and year; no link.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project soil science / agronomy team and trained field samplers. Validation: project MEAL officer with the laboratory's quality control (strata completeness, duplicates, reference samples). Calculation: project soil scientist, per the Calculation method above. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 9 · Environmental sustainability — Reference sheet KPI-OC27

name: Nitrogen use efficiency (NUE): nitrogen removed in harvested product per unit of nitrogen applied
resultsLevel: Outcome
primaryObjective: PO4 Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient. Contributing objectives: None.
cgiarImpactArea: Environmental Health & Biodiversity
sdgTarget: None (direct). Nearest correspondence: SDG indicator 2.4.1 (proportion of agricultural area under productive and sustainable agriculture), whose sixth sub-indicator, "management of fertilizers", addresses the same concern. The construct differs: SDG 2.4.1 classifies each holding green, yellow or red by how many of eight recommended fertilizer management measures the farmer reports, and returns a share of land area, whereas this indicator is a measured mass balance. The two cannot be converted into one another.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Common Results Framework: the impact-level standard indicator "Tg nitrogen application" (teragrams, that is million tonnes, of nitrogen applied) under Environmental Health and Biodiversity, which this indicator contributes evidence to. CGIAR's own review found that indicator unclear as to what result it proxies and in which direction change is desirable, and recommended revision or removal; a ratio with a defined desirable range answers that critique but does not replace the tonnage series. EU Nitrogen Expert Panel NUE framework (farm level).
definition: Measures how much of the nitrogen supplied to a production system in CIMMYT intervention areas leaves it again in products. Numerator: nitrogen in the products leaving the holding's production system in the reference period, whether sold, consumed by the household or given away. Denominator: total nitrogen brought onto the holding in the same period. A ratio of two masses of nitrogen with no unit of its own; nitrogen not leaving in products stays in the soil or is lost to air and water, so the ratio also indicates loss risk. It is the output-to-input ratio of the EU Nitrogen Expert Panel's farm nitrogen balance, read with the nitrogen surplus (input minus output), not partial factor productivity or a recovery efficiency, which rest on fertiliser alone or on a zero-nitrogen control.
rationale: Answers whether farmers in CIMMYT intervention areas are getting more harvested output from the nitrogen they apply, the change in nutrient management that CIMMYT's agronomy and sustainable intensification work aims at. It serves project management, because it shows whether a recommended practice improves the return on a purchased input, and institutional and donor reporting, because nitrogen not taken up by the crop is the main source of nitrogen losses from agriculture to water and air.
projectSpecificApplication: State the intervention areas, crops and seasons covered, the unit measured (the farm holding; a plot or field observed on its own is reported as a labelled partial account, not as the value), the accounting period (the whole rotation, or a single production year reported as a labelled partial account), and which nitrogen inputs the project could record. Do not alter the numerator and denominator construction, the boundary used for the institutional series, or the requirement to report nitrogen surplus alongside the ratio. Raise feasibility problems with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining the indicator.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this value serves: for example a donor result on sustainable intensification or fertilizer efficiency, or an adaptive-management trigger where the ratio fails to improve after a nutrient recommendation is introduced.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.  Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure.
unit: Ratio: kilograms of nitrogen in products leaving the holding per kilogram of nitrogen brought onto it (dimensionless). The dimensionless ratio is the reported value, with the percentage (ratio x 100, the EU Nitrogen Expert Panel convention) shown alongside for readability, matching KPI-OC29 so the two nutrient sheets are comparable. Nitrogen output and nitrogen surplus, in kg N per hectare per year, are reported alongside it (see Sub-metrics).
directionOfChange: Reference value: a band of roughly 0.5 to 0.9, which the EU Nitrogen Expert Panel illustrates for cropping systems without setting it for CIMMYT's target geographies; the band used is stated with the value. Both ends carry meaning. Below the band, nitrogen is used inefficiently and loss risk is high. Above it, the holding risks drawing nitrogen out of soil reserves faster than it is replaced, which would be degradation rather than efficiency. The register's reading, that a higher ratio indicates more efficient use, is corrected here.
disaggregationRequired: Required: cropping system, reported as the rotation's crop mix rather than as a single crop, since the value is a whole-farm, whole-rotation account and a single-crop cut would ask for a figure the accounting unit does not produce; and nitrogen input type (mineral fertiliser; manure, compost and feed brought in; biological fixation; atmospheric deposition; other), reported as the composition of the denominator (the share of each input), not as a ratio per input type.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Sex of the plot decision-maker; agroecological zone; irrigated or rainfed; farm size class; cropping pattern within the rotation (sole crop, intercrop, rotation position), which is a finer cut than the required cropping-system mix and not a second reading of it; tillage or residue management practice.
unitOfObservation: The farm holding, over the accounting period, matching KPI-OC29. Nitrogen carries over between seasons and between crops, so a plot-season ratio attributes a legume's fixation to one crop and its benefit to another. Where a project can only observe a plot-season, that is reported as a labelled partial account, not as the value.
calculationSummary: Numerator: nitrogen in products leaving the holding's production system in the period: crop products and crop residues sold, consumed by the household or given away, livestock products sold, consumed by the household or given away, and net live animals sold; crops and residues fed to the holding's own livestock are internal transfers, not output. Each product enters as its mass (kg) times its nitrogen concentration (kg N per kg product). Denominator: nitrogen brought onto the holding: mineral fertiliser; manure and compost brought in, net of any sent off; feed and fodder brought in, net of exports; seed and planting material; nitrate in irrigation water; biological fixation; and atmospheric deposition, each as mass times nitrogen concentration. Manure produced on the holding is an internal transfer and not an input. "Applied" in the register title is read as the farm-gate input set: mineral fertiliser, manure and compost brought in, feed and fodder brought in, seed, nitrate in irrigation water, biological fixation and atmospheric deposition, not fertiliser and manure alone: a partial denominator makes efficiency look higher wherever legumes are in the rotation, which would penalise the very practice CIMMYT promotes. Biological fixation follows the method of record's three tiers, with Tier 2, its yield-based regression applied to the measured legume harvest, as the minimum for the institutional series; its Tier 1 per-hectare values are compiled for Europe and are used only as a labelled last resort. The method of record's deposition values cover European regions only and are not used elsewhere; deposition for the site, which no farm-level instrument measures, is taken from a documented regional dataset named with the value. Both estimated terms are reported as a share of the denominator so a reader can see how much of it was not measured. Value = numerator / denominator. Both terms are also reported per hectare per year and their difference is the nitrogen surplus. Nitrogen concentrations follow a tiered approach: Tier 1 general look-up values, Tier 2 validated national or local values, Tier 3 local product analyses (preferred); state the tier used. CIMMYT-validated look-up values are used where they exist for the crop and region, and a documented published look-up table otherwise, with the source and the tier named against every value. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1: farm-level measurement recording every nitrogen input brought onto the holding other than biological fixation and atmospheric deposition, and every product leaving it, each with its mass and nitrogen concentration, from verified farmer field records or a farm survey with crop-cut yield measurement. This is the only source producing both terms for the same unit and period. Fallback DS2: project and partner agronomic monitoring records; flagged as fallback-sourced, because such records often capture recommended rather than applied rates and omit non-fertilizer nitrogen inputs. Not applicable DS3: satellite, aerial and GIS data cannot observe nitrogen applied to a field or the nitrogen concentration of a harvest, so they may support a sampling frame but neither term. Not applicable DS4: national or subnational statistics on fertilizer use and crop production (for example FAOSTAT) cannot produce this ratio at any resolution: they cannot resolve a holding or an intervention area, and a national balance built from them is a cropland balance, not the holding balance this indicator reports. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced and mobile data cannot provide the traceable input quantities and measured harvest masses a mass balance requires.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which source role the project used, Recommended or Fallback. If Fallback, state why farm-level measurement was not feasible, which terms were entered from a tier rather than observed, and at what tier nitrogen concentrations were taken.
collectionInstrument: For DS1: a nutrient balance module recording, per plot and season, every nitrogen-bearing input (mineral fertilizer by product and quantity, manure and compost brought in, seed, nitrate-bearing irrigation water, area under nitrogen-fixing crops), plus harvested yield and the destination of crop products and residues (sold, consumed by the household, given away, or fed to the holding's own livestock); feed and fodder brought in and sent out; livestock and livestock products sold, consumed by the household or given away. Two denominator terms are not observed at the plot and are entered rather than collected: biological fixation, derived from the measured legume harvest (from the recorded area under nitrogen-fixing crops only as a labelled last resort), and atmospheric deposition, taken from a documented regional dataset for the site and recorded with its source. Respondent: the person who makes the fertilizer decisions for the plot, with quantities verified against purchase records where possible. Yield measured by crop cut where resources allow, following Sapkota et al. (2016). Mode: interview at the plot with field measurement.
collectionFrequency: Every production cycle measured, at a minimum a pre-intervention baseline and one follow-up. Where the accounting period is a rotation, once per rotation.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Between measurement periods the latest value is carried forward with its measurement year noted; a rotation-based value is reported against the closing year of that rotation.
referencePeriod: For arable systems with a defined rotation, the whole rotation (commonly 3 to 6 years), because nitrogen applied to one crop is taken up in part by the next; where a project can observe only a single production year, that year is reported as a labelled partial account with the rotation position stated, not as the value. Systems with no defined rotation use one production year, aligned to the harvest calendar of the crops measured.
baselineRequired: Yes. The value is interpretable only as change from the pre-intervention nutrient management of the same units, because absolute levels are driven by soil, climate and crop as much as by practice. Fallbacks where no prospective baseline exists: comparison holdings under prevailing farmer practice, measured over the same years and in the same setting; or recall-based reconstruction of the preceding cycle's inputs and yield, flagged as recall-based. A fallback baseline covering less than the whole rotation carries the same label as the Reference period gives a single year: the change is reported as a labelled partial account, not as the value. If neither is feasible: monitoring only, no change claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. All holdings in scope; weight: nitrogen brought onto the holding, on annualised totals (ratio of sums); the crop mix behind the pooled ratio is reported with it (Block C). (2) Aggregation across projects: pool Recommended-sourced holding accounts covering the full accounting period by summing both terms; a labelled partial account and a project using the Fallback are reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, never blended in.

B: Combination method. Sum the numerator and the denominator across units and divide once: the institutional value is total nitrogen in products leaving the holdings divided by total nitrogen brought onto them, across every unit reported through the Recommended source, each unit's two terms first annualised as in Sub-metrics, which leaves every unit's own ratio unchanged and stops a holding on a six-year rotation weighing twice one on three. Never average unit-level or project-level ratios. Report aggregated nitrogen output and surplus alongside the ratio, in kg N per hectare per year: each holding's annualised totals (Sub-metrics) summed and divided by the summed area, never a mean of holding values, with the crop mix behind it.

C: Levels and operations. A nutrient use efficiency is a ratio, recomputed at every level from its own numerator and denominator, never averaged from the levels beneath it. At Farm / Plot, the nitrogen leaving the holding in products over the nitrogen brought onto it, for the whole holding over the accounting period, which is this sheet's unit of observation; a single plot-season computed on its own is a labelled partial account and not a value at this level. At Household, Regional / Aggregated and above, the summed numerator over the summed denominator within the pooling domain of Block A. Also report: the denominator itself, the units excluded under Eligibility, which components were estimated rather than measured and on what assumption, and the composition of the aggregate, since a ratio that moved only because the mix changed is not a change in any of its parts.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This value does not sum or roll into the greenhouse gas intensity impact indicator (KPI-I09) or the soil organic carbon outcome (KPI-OC27); the connection runs through the theory of change, in that unrecovered nitrogen is the source of nitrogen-related emissions, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: where intervention areas overlap, de-duplicate by plot or farm identifier before summing; if that is not possible, label the pooled figure an upper estimate. Named overlaps: the same plots supply KPI-OC29 (phosphorus use efficiency), KPI-OC27 (soil organic carbon), KPI-OC30 (water intensity) and yield indicators, and sit inside the areas counted under KPI-OC33 and KPI-I10. These are different measurements of the same land and must never be summed into a combined environmental performance figure. Coverage and precision travel with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands used in official statistics: 16.5 per cent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 per cent released flagged, above 33.3 per cent not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one deduplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above, and a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place. On this sheet a record is one farm holding's nitrogen balance for one accounting period, the whole-farm accounting unit this sheet reports on.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Missing data: a holding whose mineral fertiliser, manure and compost, feed, or harvest and product quantities leaving the holding were not recorded is excluded from both terms and counted in the reported excluded share; terms no farm instrument observes (for nitrogen, biological fixation and atmospheric deposition) are entered from the tier stated, with their source. Seed and irrigation-water nitrate not recorded are entered from a documented value for the crop or site, or as zero where none exists, with the basis stated.

Repeated observations: one accounting period per unit; where several crops are grown on the unit within the period, sum all inputs and all outputs and divide once, never averaging crop ratios.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only. The ratio responds to rainfall, soil fertility, pest and disease pressure, fertilizer prices and availability, and to any other advice the farmer receives; CIMMYT's agronomy work is one contributor among several.

A high value is not automatically a good result. Above roughly 90 percent, and wherever inputs are low relative to what leaves in products, the holding's output may be supplied by soil nitrogen reserves that are not being replaced, which degrades fertility over time. Read the ratio only with nitrogen surplus and nitrogen output.

Values computed on different boundaries are not comparable. Whether the denominator counts only applied fertilizer or the full input set, and whether the unit is a crop-season, a farm or a rotation, each change the value materially. Crop-level estimates can over- or understate efficiency because they ignore nitrogen carried between crops in a rotation.

Main measurement error sources: recalled rather than recorded fertilizer quantities; nitrogen concentrations from general look-up tables compiled for other crops and regions; and unmeasured change in soil nitrogen stocks, potentially large after a change in rotation, manure use or tillage.

A rise means more of the nitrogen entering the measured system left it in products. It does not by itself mean losses to the environment fell (surplus can rise at the same time if inputs rose), does not mean yields rose, and does not mean soil fertility was maintained.
subMetrics:
Three companion metrics come from the same data and must be reported with the ratio, which alone can be read in opposite directions:

— Nitrogen output: numerator divided by area, in kg N per hectare per year. Indicates productivity and land use efficiency.

— Nitrogen input: denominator divided by area, in kg N per hectare per year.

— Nitrogen surplus: nitrogen input minus nitrogen output, in kg N per hectare per year. The proxy for nitrogen lost to water and air.

Where the account covers a whole rotation, the three companions are annualised by dividing the rotation total by the number of years in it, with the rotation length stated beside them; the ratio itself is never annualised, being a ratio of two totals over the same period.

Parallel indicator with its own sheet: KPI-OC29 (phosphorus use efficiency), applying the same balance logic to phosphorus.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project agronomy and M&E team. Validation: project MEAL officer, with agronomy sign-off on the completeness of the input item list and the concentration tier used. Calculation: project M&E, per the Calculation method above. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 9 · Environmental sustainability — Reference sheet KPI-OC28

name: Phosphorus use efficiency (PUE): phosphorus removed in harvested product as a share of total phosphorus applied
resultsLevel: Outcome. Farmers changing how much phosphorus they apply relative to what they harvest is a change in practice among beneficiaries, which is the Core's definition of an outcome. It sits above the pathway's outputs, the ecological solution packages validated (KPI-O30) and deployed (KPI-O31); practice adoption is itself an outcome, reported at KPI-OC33, not an output.
primaryObjective: PO4 Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient. One primary objective only. Contributing objectives: None; the register lists no other objective for this row.
cgiarImpactArea: Environmental Health & Biodiversity. Phosphorus surplus is a water-quality and ecosystem pressure, and this is the Impact Area under which CGIAR groups its nutrient and land-management measures. The register carries no Impact Area column, so this is a sheet-level judgement.
sdgTarget: None. The relevant target is SDG 2.4 (sustainable food production systems), but indicator 2.4.1 contains no phosphorus balance. It is a dashboard of 11 sub-indicators, of which sub-indicator 6, "Management of fertilizers", scores each holding green, yellow or red by how many of eight recommended practices the farmer reports following, reported as a share of agricultural land area. That is a practice checklist, not a nutrient mass ratio, so a PUE value cannot be reported as 2.4.1. Evidence toward target 2.4, not reportable as its indicator.
otherFrameworks: EU Nitrogen Expert Panel nutrient use efficiency framework (2016), which supplies the mass-balance method and the requirement to report efficiency together with output and surplus. Its scope is nitrogen; the phosphorus application is by analogy, stated as such throughout this sheet. No CGIAR Common Results Framework correspondence: the CRF environmental impact set holds a nitrogen application tonnage indicator and no phosphorus measure, and the CGIAR standard-indicator assessment names that nitrogen indicator among three requiring fundamental revision or removal.
definition: The ratio of phosphorus contained in product leaving the farm's production system, whether sold, consumed by the household or given away, to total phosphorus entering the farm over the same period, in CIMMYT intervention areas. Both terms are masses of elemental phosphorus (P) per hectare per year. It follows the mass balance principle used for nutrient use efficiency: efficiency rises when more phosphorus leaves in product, when less enters, or both. The ratio is reported with two companion figures without which it cannot be read: phosphorus output per hectare (system productivity) and phosphorus surplus per hectare (phosphorus not removed, and so at risk of loss to water).
rationale: Answers whether farms in CIMMYT intervention areas obtain more harvested product from each unit of phosphorus applied. Phosphate rock is a finite, imported and costly input for smallholders, and phosphorus surplus is a water-quality pressure. With its nitrogen counterpart (KPI-OC28), it is the register's direct evidence that CIMMYT's agronomy makes nutrient use more efficient rather than more intensive.
projectSpecificApplication: State which farms, crops, countries and seasons the project measures; the balance is drawn for the farm holding, and a plot or field observed on its own is reported as a labelled partial account, not as the value; the institutional definition, unit and calculation method stay unchanged. Example: PUE for 400 farm holdings over their full maize-legume rotation, from measured fertiliser application and weighed harvest of every product leaving the farm. A project unable to obtain a phosphorus concentration for a harvested product raises it with the MEAL focal point rather than substituting a different construct.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision, donor commitment or national reporting need served. Example: a sustainable intensification project tracks PUE because its donor requires an input-efficiency result, and because a falling ratio mid-implementation shows its recommended fertiliser blends are adding phosphorus the crop is not taking up.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.  Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure.
unit: Ratio: kilograms of phosphorus in products leaving the farm's production system per kilogram of phosphorus entering the farm (dimensionless), the ratio form the register specifies. The percentage (ratio x 100, the form the source framework prints) is shown alongside for readability but is not the reported value. The ratio is what the mass-balance literature uses and what makes this comparable with KPI-OC28.
directionOfChange: Reference value: 1.0 is the upper reference. Above 1.0 more phosphorus left the farm in product than entered it; in a single period the excess can come from stored produce or a reduced herd, but only soil reserves can supply it for long, so sustained values above it indicate soil mining. The reference is a mass balance, not a target set here. A low value is not automatically a poor result: deliberate rebuilding of a depleted phosphorus reserve reads as low efficiency for as long as it continues. The register's reading, that a higher ratio is preferable, is corrected here on the same reasoning as KPI-OC28. The reference is read on a farm's own ratio; a ratio pooled across farms is read with its crop mix.
disaggregationRequired: Required: none recorded in the register, whose disaggregation field reads "n/a". Cropping system is required on this sheet's authority, reported as the rotation's crop mix rather than as a single crop, since phosphorus requirements and removal rates differ sharply between crops and an institutional ratio cannot be read without the crop mix behind it; a single-crop cut would ask for a figure the accounting unit does not produce.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country and agroecological zone; baseline soil phosphorus status (low, medium, high), which largely determines the achievable ratio; fertiliser source (mineral, organic, or both); irrigated or rainfed.
unitOfObservation: The farm holding. The source framework treats the whole farm as the primary unit because a plot-level balance misses phosphorus carried across a rotation.
calculationSummary: Numerator (P output): sum over all products leaving the farm's production system (sold, consumed by the household or given away) of product mass (kg) times its phosphorus concentration (kg P per kg product), divided by farmed area (ha). Denominator (P input): the same sum over all phosphorus-bearing inputs entering the farm, divided by the same area. "Removed in harvested product" and "applied" in the register title are read as the numerator and denominator above, the farm-gate terms, as KPI-OC28 reads its own title. Value: PUE = P output / P input, a dimensionless ratio, both terms in kg P per hectare per year; the same quantity x 100 is the percentage shown alongside. The farmed area cancels in a farm's own ratio, so where farms are pooled the terms summed are each farm's totals in kg P per year, the account's totals divided once by the years it covers, never its per-hectare terms. Fertiliser is traded as phosphate (P2O5), which is 43.64 percent phosphorus by mass, so every phosphate quantity is converted to elemental P by multiplying by 0.4364 before entering the calculation. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1 (Censuses and surveys): a farm nutrient-balance module run on a sample or census of farms in the intervention area, recording every phosphorus-bearing input and every product removed, with weighed harvests or crop cuts for mass and laboratory analysis of phosphorus concentration where feasible. Frame DS2 (Administrative and registry data): project agronomy records, supplying the farm frame, identifiers, and farmed area as delineated or as stated by the producer, recorded with the companion figures. Not applicable DS3 (Geospatial and Earth observation): satellites can support the harvested mass term through yield estimation but cannot observe phosphorus applied or phosphorus concentration. Not applicable DS4 (Secondary and international databases): national fertiliser use and crop production statistics (for example FAOSTAT) cannot produce this ratio at any resolution: they cannot resolve a farm or an intervention area, and a national balance built from them is a cropland balance, not the farm balance this indicator reports. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated and other non-traditional data): the balance needs quantities measured against a defined farm boundary and area, which crowdsourced observations cannot supply.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State the collection design used. Example: "Used Recommended: balance module with 400 farm holdings over their full rotation; grain phosphorus from laboratory analysis, residue phosphorus from national tables."
collectionInstrument: DS1 route: a farm nutrient-balance module recording, for the period and a defined farmed area, each fertiliser, manure, compost, seed and feed input by name, quantity and stated nutrient grade; each product removed by type and mass; whether residues were removed or returned; and the source tier of each phosphorus concentration. Respondent: the person who makes fertiliser decisions for the holding, with plot register and receipts consulted where available. Mode: face-to-face interview with field measurement of harvested mass and product sampling.
collectionFrequency: Baseline before or at the start of the intervention, then once per agricultural year.
reportingFrequency: Annually; between measured years the latest value is carried forward with its measurement year noted. A rotation-based value is reported against the closing year of that rotation.
referencePeriod: For systems with a defined rotation, the whole rotation, because phosphorus applied to one crop is taken up in part by later ones; where a project can observe only one agricultural year, that year is reported as a labelled partial account with the rotation position stated, not as the value. Systems with no defined rotation use one agricultural year, covering every crop harvested from the farmed area.
baselineRequired: Yes. Without a pre-intervention balance the ratio describes a state, not a change, and a high value may reflect soils that were already phosphorus-rich. Fallbacks: (a) reconstruct the pre-intervention year from input purchase records and recalled application rates and harvests; (b) a matched comparison group outside the intervention area measured in the same season; (c) if neither is feasible, monitoring only, no change claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. All farms in scope; weight: phosphorus entering the farm, on annualised totals (ratio of sums); the crop mix behind the pooled ratio is reported with it (Block C). (2) Across projects: pool Recommended-sourced values directly; a labelled partial account is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, never blended in.

B: Combination method. Pool by summing total phosphorus leaving the farms in product and total phosphorus entering them across contributing farms, then computing one ratio (a ratio of sums, which weights each farm by the phosphorus entering it), each farm's two terms first annualised as in Sub-metrics where its account covers a rotation longer than one year, which leaves every farm's own ratio unchanged and stops a rotation account outweighing a single-year one. Never average farm-level ratios: farms differ greatly in area and application rate, and an average of ratios corresponds to no real system. Report aggregated phosphorus output and surplus alongside the ratio, in kg P per hectare per year: each farm's annualised totals (Sub-metrics) summed and divided by the summed area, never a mean of farm values.

C: Levels and operations. A nutrient use efficiency is a ratio, recomputed at every level from its own numerator and denominator, never averaged from the levels beneath it. At Farm / Plot, the phosphorus in products leaving that holding over the phosphorus entering it. At Household, Regional / Aggregated and above, the summed numerator over the summed denominator within the pooling domain of Block A. Also report: the denominator itself, the units excluded under Eligibility, which components were estimated rather than measured and on what assumption, and the composition of the aggregate, since a ratio that moved only because the mix changed is not a change in any of its parts.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: No. This value does not combine arithmetically with the pathway's outputs, the ecological solution packages validated and deployed, or with any impact indicator; the levels connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative, not arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and boundary: de-duplicate by farm identifier before pooling, since a farm reached by two projects would otherwise contribute twice; where identifiers cannot be matched, label the pooled figure an upper estimate. Named overlaps: KPI-OC28 measures the same farms for nitrogen, so the two ratios describe the same holdings and must never be summed or presented as one nutrient efficiency figure; KPI-OC27 and KPI-OC30 measure the same land, and it sits inside the areas counted under KPI-OC33 and KPI-I10, none of them ever summed with this ratio into a combined figure; KPI-I09, the greenhouse gas intensity, is computed from its own activity data and emission factors, and PUE is not a term in it; the register's route from this indicator to it is removed on this sheet, so there is no roll-up to overlap with either. Coverage and precision travel with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands used in official statistics: 16.5 per cent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 per cent released flagged, above 33.3 per cent not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one deduplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above, and a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place. On this sheet a record is one farm holding's phosphorus balance for one period, the whole-farm accounting unit this sheet reports on.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusions, farms: farms inside the project's declared CIMMYT intervention area. Inclusions, output: harvested crop products and livestock products leaving the farm's production system, whether sold, consumed by the household or given away; crop residues only where they leave the farm. Inclusions, input: mineral and compound fertilisers; manure and compost brought onto the farm, net of any sent off it (manure produced on the farm is an internal transfer, not an input); seed and planting material; purchased feed in mixed systems.

Exclusions: residues returned to the soil and anything else not crossing the farm boundary, since internal transfers are neither a gain nor a loss. A farm with no phosphorus entering from any source, for which the ratio is undefined, is counted and reported separately, not as zero or as perfectly efficient. Concentrations: laboratory analysis of the product where feasible, otherwise validated national tables, otherwise general reference tables; the tier used is reported with the value.

Missing data: a farm whose mineral fertiliser, manure and compost, feed, or harvest and product quantities leaving the farm were not recorded is excluded from both terms and counted in the reported excluded share; terms no farm instrument observes (for nitrogen, biological fixation and atmospheric deposition) are entered from the tier stated, with their source. Seed not recorded is entered from a documented value for the crop, or as zero where none exists, with the basis stated. A mass balance with an incomplete term is biased, not merely noisy, so the share of the sample with a complete balance is reported as a coverage rate.

Repeated observations: one balance per farm per period; multiple visits are combined, never counted twice.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only. Phosphorus use efficiency responds to fertiliser prices and availability, rainfall, soil type and farmers' own crop choices, none of which CIMMYT controls.

The method is transferred from a nitrogen standard and the transfer is imperfect. The published guidance covers nitrogen, where inputs also arrive by biological fixation and atmospheric deposition and losses occur as gases. Phosphorus has neither pathway: it moves in solid form, is lost mainly through erosion and runoff to water, and accumulates in soil. The arithmetic transfers cleanly, the interpretation does not, and the soil reserve term matters far more for phosphorus.

The value depends heavily on the phosphorus concentrations used. Where these come from general reference tables rather than analysis of the actual product, error enters both terms of the ratio, so the tier must be reported and values built on different tiers should not be compared closely.

Comparability is limited by crop, rotation and starting soil status. A farm on phosphorus-rich soil can post a high ratio while applying nothing, and one year of a multi-year rotation can attribute an application to the wrong crop.

Soil phosphorus stock change is not carried as a term: estimating it needs repeated soil testing that projects do not fund, so the balance measures flows, not stocks, and a surplus may be accumulating in soil rather than being lost.

A rise means more phosphorus left the farm in product per unit entering it. It does not by itself mean better management: sustained values above 100 percent mean soil reserves are being run down, raising yields now and lowering them later. A fall is not automatically a poor result either, since deliberate rebuilding of a depleted phosphorus reserve lowers the ratio for as long as it continues. Always read the value with the surplus and output figures, and with the starting soil status.
subMetrics:
The source framework is explicit that the efficiency ratio must not be reported alone, since a high ratio can coexist with very low productivity or with soil depletion. Two companion figures come from the same data and are reported with every value:

— Phosphorus output (kg P per hectare per year) = the numerator above, before division. The productivity of the system in phosphorus terms.

— Phosphorus surplus (kg P per hectare per year) = P input minus P output. The phosphorus not removed in product, at risk of accumulating in soil or being lost to water.

Where the account covers a whole rotation, both companions are annualised by dividing the rotation total by the number of years in it, with the rotation length stated beside them; the ratio itself is never annualised, being a ratio of two totals over the same period.

Neither has its own reference sheet. KPI-OC28 (nitrogen use efficiency) is the parallel indicator for nitrogen, not a sub-metric of this one.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project agronomy and M&E teams. Validation: project MEAL officer (farm identifiers, farmed area, completeness of both terms, phosphate to elemental phosphorus conversion, concentration tier recorded). Calculation: project MEAL officer produces farm and project values; the CIMMYT MEAL unit de-duplicates and pools across projects. Approval: project leader, with the project agronomist confirming the concentration values. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 9 · Environmental sustainability — Reference sheet KPI-OC29

name: Water intensity of food production: litres of water consumed per tonne of food produced
resultsLevel: Outcome. The value describes how external actors, farmers and water user associations, manage water and land in their own fields. Its upstream outputs are the ecological solution packages validated (KPI-O30) and deployed (KPI-O31), the water-management packages among them being what this outcome reads the uptake of; the chain connects through the Theory of Change, not arithmetically.
primaryObjective: PO4 Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient. Contributing objectives: None.
cgiarImpactArea: Environmental Health & Biodiversity
sdgTarget: None at indicator level. The indicator sits under SDG target 6.4 (substantially increase water-use efficiency across all sectors), but SDG indicator 6.4.1 measures water-use efficiency as gross value added per volume of water used, in United States dollars per cubic metre, for whole economic sectors at national scale. That is an economic ratio; this is a physical one. The two are not convertible, and a value reported here must never be presented as an SDG 6.4.1 figure.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR results framework: the impact-area standard indicator on consumptive water use in food production, reported as cubic kilometres rather than as an intensity, and the CGIAR boundary target of less than 2 500 km³ per year. FAO WaPOR, which publishes crop water productivity in kg per m³ for parts of Africa and the Near East. FAO AQUASTAT, which holds national water-use data reported for SDG 6.4.1.
definition: The volume of water consumed to produce one tonne of food in CIMMYT intervention areas, in litres per tonne. Water consumed means water depleted by the production system, that is water lost to the atmosphere as soil evaporation, crop transpiration and canopy interception over the crop cycle. It is not water diverted, delivered or applied: water supplied to a field but not consumed drains or runs off and stays available downstream, so counting applied water would overstate what production costs the water resource. The measure is the reciprocal of water productivity (kilograms per cubic metre), the form FAO and CGIAR normally publish: litres per tonne = 1,000,000 divided by water productivity in kg per m³.
rationale: Answers whether the farming systems CIMMYT works with produce more food from each unit of water they deplete, the question behind CGIAR's environmental boundary for consumptive water use in food production and behind SDG target 6.4.
