Project management uses it to judge whether water-saving agronomy, irrigation scheduling and drought-tolerant varieties change the resource cost of production; institutional reporting uses it as the water strand of CIMMYT's environmental sustainability narrative, alongside the nutrient and emissions strands.
projectSpecificApplication: State the intervention areas, crops, seasons and measurement rounds covered, and whether the water term is measured on-farm, derived from remote sensing, or taken from delivery records on fully irrigated plots only. Do not change the definition of consumed water, the unit or the calculation method. If only water delivered can be obtained, the value is reported on fully irrigated plots only, labelled fallback-sourced.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment the value serves: a donor water-efficiency outcome, an irrigation scheme's water allocation review, or a trigger to revisit irrigation scheduling advice if intensity does not fall while yields rise.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.  Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure.
unit: Litres of water per tonne of food produced (L/t)
directionOfChange: Decrease. A falling value means less water is consumed per tonne of food produced. It can also fall because production rose on unchanged water use, so it is read alongside the production series behind it.
disaggregationRequired: Required: crop; water regime (fully irrigated / supplementary irrigation / rainfed). A litres-per-tonne value is not interpretable without both: crops differ in water demand, and irrigated and rainfed values describe different systems. A combined cross-crop figure is not reported: only the crop-disaggregated series is published, because litres per tonne of maize and litres per tonne of wheat are different quantities and a pooled figure moves whenever the crop mix moves, which reads as a change in efficiency.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Agroecological zone; season; river basin or irrigation scheme; irrigation method (surface, sprinkler, localised); farm size; sex of the plot manager; management practice compared.
unitOfObservation: Plot
calculationSummary: Numerator: total litres of water consumed on the measured plots in the reference period. Consumption is actual evapotranspiration from sowing to harvest of each crop cycle in the period; evaporation during fallow between cycles is excluded from the numerator and, where measured, reported beside the value. It is computed from the field water balance: precipitation plus irrigation applied plus net groundwater contribution plus run-on, minus runoff, minus drainage below the root zone, minus the change in soil water stored in the root zone. Depth converts as 1 mm over 1 hectare = 10 m³ = 10,000 litres. Denominator: tonnes of dry matter of the food product harvested for human consumption (grain; paddy grain for rice) from the same plots in the same period, from fresh weight and measured moisture; the tonnage at a stated market moisture may be published alongside. On intercropped and rotated plots, the cycle's water consumed is apportioned to the food crops by their share of harvested dry matter, with the apportionment stated against the value; the share carried by non-food crops leaves the numerator, as their harvest is outside the denominator. All water consumed in a food crop's cycle is carried by its food product; straw, stover, husks and other residues carry none, whether removed, sold, fed or retained. The dry-matter apportionment applies only between distinct crops sharing a cycle, on each crop's harvested main product. Value = total litres / total tonnes. Where the starting figure is a water productivity value in kg per m³, convert as litres per tonne = 1,000,000 / (kg per m³) and record which of the two was measured. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1: paired field measurement on the same plots, a soil water balance for the numerator (flow-metered irrigation volumes, rainfall, soil moisture profile measurement, reference evapotranspiration from a weather station) and crop-cut harvest sampling for the denominator. Only this source measures both terms on the same area and period. Fallback DS3: remote-sensed evapotranspiration and biomass products, notably FAO WaPOR at its finest available resolution; flagged, because the yield term is modelled from biomass and a harvest index rather than measured, and fine-resolution coverage is limited to selected schemes and countries. Fallback DS2: irrigation scheme delivery records for the numerator with project harvest records for the denominator; always flagged, because delivered volume is not consumed volume: it counts water that drains, leaks or runs off, which overstates the numerator, and omits rainfall the crop consumed, which understates it; admissible only on fully irrigated plots where rainfall in the cycle is negligible, and on any other plot it cannot produce the value. Not applicable DS4: national water-use and production statistics (FAO AQUASTAT, FAOSTAT) cannot produce this indicator at any resolution: AQUASTAT records water withdrawn for irrigation, the quantity SDG 6.4.1 uses, not water consumed, and holds no rainfed consumption. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced and mobile data cannot establish a water balance or a measured harvest weight for a defined plot.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role the project used, and for a Fallback which one and why field measurement was not feasible. If the numerator came from delivery records, say so in the same sentence as the value.
collectionInstrument: For DS1: a plot-level water accounting protocol plus a yield protocol on the same plots. Water: flow meters at the plot inlet, rain gauge or validated gridded rainfall, soil moisture measured through the root zone at the start and end of the cycle, reference evapotranspiration from a local weather station. Output: crop cuts on demarcated sub-plots, weighed fresh, moisture measured, converted to dry matter from measured moisture. Drainage below the root zone, capillary rise and runoff, which these instruments do not measure, are estimated with a documented soil water balance model driven by the measured terms and named with the value; where consumption is instead estimated from reference evapotranspiration and crop coefficients, say so, since that is a modelled estimate of consumption. Respondent rule: the plot manager identifies boundaries, crop, sowing and harvest dates and irrigation events; the physical measurements are taken by the enumerator.
collectionFrequency: Once per crop cycle where field measurement is running; at minimum a baseline and an endline round for any change claim.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Between rounds the latest measured value is carried forward with its year and crop cycle noted.
referencePeriod: One complete crop cycle at minimum, preferably every crop cycle in a full cropping year, so that second cycles are captured. State which basis each value uses.
baselineRequired: Yes. The value is only interpretable as change from a pre-intervention level in the same fields and water regime. Fallbacks where no prospective baseline exists: a first-season measurement before the intervention's practices are applied; a matched comparison area measured in the same season; or a remote-sensing reconstruction for pre-project seasons, flagged as reconstructed. If none is feasible: monitoring only, no change claim.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool Recommended-sourced totals directly; a project reporting from remote sensing or delivery records is reported alongside the pooled figure with its source named, never blended in, because the fallbacks measure different quantities at different resolutions.

B: Combination method. Sum the litres and sum the tonnes across plots, then divide, computed separately for each required disaggregation. Never average project-level or plot-level ratios.

C: Levels and operations. A water intensity is a ratio, recomputed at every level from its own numerator and denominator, never averaged from the levels beneath it. At Farm / Plot, the water consumed over that plot's tonnes of food produced. At Household, Regional / Aggregated and above, the summed numerator over the summed denominator within the pooling domain of Block A. Also report: the denominator itself, the units excluded under Eligibility, which components were estimated rather than measured and on what assumption, and the composition of the aggregate, since a ratio that moved only because the mix changed is not a change in any of its parts.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. The register records this indicator as contributing to the impact-level emissions intensity indicator (kg CO2e per tonne); litres of water and kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent cannot be added or averaged into one figure, so the register's roll-up is removed rather than kept as a narrative link.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: de-duplicate by plot identifier before pooling where two projects work in the same scheme or command area; label the pooled figure an upper estimate for water if de-duplication is not possible. Named overlaps: the same plots and tonnage also appear in KPI-OC28 and KPI-OC29 (nutrient use efficiency), KPI-I09 (emissions intensity) and the productivity pathway's yield indicators. The tonnage is counted once as production; these ratios are alternative resource lenses on the same output and must never be summed into a single efficiency score. Coverage and precision travel with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands used in official statistics: 16.5 per cent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 per cent released flagged, above 33.3 per cent not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one deduplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above, and a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place. On this sheet a record is one plot's water balance and harvested tonnage for one crop over the reference period, every cycle of that crop summed, both terms present.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusions: all plots of the project's food crops in the intervention areas, irrigated and rainfed; failed plots are retained, since they consumed water and produced nothing, and dropping them biases the value downward.

Exclusions: water used after harvest (processing, washing, transport), household and livestock water, non-food crops.

Missing data: a plot missing either term is excluded from both sums and never imputed; report the share excluded.

Repeated observations: where a plot is cropped more than once in the period, every cycle enters both sums and the ratio is computed once from the summed terms. Never average plot-level or season-level ratios.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only. Water intensity moves with rainfall, temperature, crop mix and irrigation infrastructure well beyond any project's reach, and a wet season lowers it with no change in practice. Report the value with its season and rainfall context.

The definition of the water term drives the number. Water consumed, water applied and water diverted into a scheme can differ by a factor of two or more in the same system, and values on different bases are not comparable. Every value must name its basis.

Figures published as water productivity in kg per m³, including FAO WaPOR products, are the reciprocal of this indicator and must be converted, not quoted directly. Remote-sensed values also carry a modelled yield term from biomass and a harvest index, so they estimate the denominator rather than measure it.
Comparability across crops is limited, because litres per tonne depends on crop water demand. Compare like crop with like; no combined cross-crop figure is reported.

A fall means the measured system produced each tonne from less consumed water. It does not mean less water was withdrawn, that basin water availability improved, or that CIMMYT caused the change: water saved in one field can be taken up by expanded irrigated area elsewhere. Pair with practice-adoption and yield indicators for the contribution narrative.
subMetrics: None. The water term and the output term are components of one ratio, reported beside it under Block C, and neither has its own reference sheet. Related sheets: KPI-OC28 and KPI-OC29, which apply the same resource-per-output logic to nutrients on the same plots; KPI-I09, the impact-level intensity measure in this pathway.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
The Agronomic Parameters in SDG Indicator 6.4.1: Yield Ratio and Proportion of Rainfed Production, FAO: the agronomic parameters of SDG indicator 6.4.1, cited for the SDG field. https://doi.org/10.4060/cb8768en

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project field team and enumerators (water balance, irrigation records, crop cuts). Validation: project MEAL officer (plot identifiers, completeness of both terms, dry-matter conversion, exclusion log). Calculation: project data analyst with the irrigation or cropping systems specialist. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 9 · Environmental sustainability — Reference sheet KPI-OC30

name: Change in the quantity of pesticide active ingredient applied per hectare per year
resultsLevel: Outcome. The change in how much pesticide a farmer buys and applies per hectare is a change in practice among beneficiaries, which is the Core's definition of an outcome. It sits above ecological solution packages deployed (KPI-O31) and feeds the agrobiodiversity impact (KPI-I14).
primaryObjective: PO4 Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient. Contributing objectives: None; the register lists PO4 alone.
cgiarImpactArea: Environmental Health & Biodiversity
sdgTarget: None (direct). The nearest correspondence is SDG indicator 2.4.1 (proportion of agricultural area under productive and sustainable agriculture), whose pesticide-risk sub-indicator classifies each farm green, yellow or red by the hazard class of products used and the mitigation measures taken. That is a hazard and practice classification, not applied mass; the two cannot be converted into one another.
otherFrameworks: FAOSTAT Pesticides Indicators domain: "use per area of cropland (kg/ha)", the same construct at national scale, so CIMMYT values are benchmarkable against country and regional averages. Agrobiodiversity Index (Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT): the measurement "avoided over-use of chemical control mechanisms", entered as 100 divided by kilograms per hectare. CGIAR common results framework: no pesticide indicator in the standard set; the nearest, hectares under improved management, defines no practice categories.
definition: The change, relative to a baseline year, in the quantity of pesticide active ingredient applied per hectare of cropland per year in CIMMYT intervention areas. A lower value means less chemical intensity. Active ingredient is the biologically effective substance in the product, as distinct from the formulated product sold to farmers, which also contains adjuvants and carriers. Pesticides follow the FAO reporting scope: insecticides, herbicides, fungicides and bactericides, mineral oils, plant growth regulators, rodenticides, seed treatments and other pesticides, including botanical and biological products, applied to crops, seed or stored produce.
rationale: Answers whether the farming systems CIMMYT works in are becoming less chemically intensive: the outcome integrated pest management, resistant varieties and improved agronomy are expected to produce. Use per area of cropland is the measure FAO uses for pesticide pressure, so a CIMMYT value reads next to national and regional figures.
projectSpecificApplication: Describe the intervention areas, crops and seasons covered, the baseline year, and the survey or trial rounds used. The active-ingredient basis, the cropland denominator and the calculation method stay unchanged.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision, donor commitment or reporting need this indicator serves. Example: a host-plant-resistance project tracks it because flat intensity while adoption rises shows farmers adding the variety on top of their spray routine rather than replacing it.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.  Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure.
unit: Kilograms of pesticide active ingredient per hectare per year (kg a.i./ha/year). The reported value is the change from baseline in that unit, with the level in each year alongside it, since an absolute change conceals the base. Intensity per hectare treated is reported as a companion where projects record it, never as the value; it is defined under Sub-metrics.
directionOfChange: Not directional. The register records a fall as the intended movement; that is corrected here, because where baseline use is already very low and pest damage is the binding constraint a fall is not automatically an improvement. The WHO hazard-class disaggregation carries the direction: a fall in the use of class Ia and Ib products, the World Health Organization's extremely and highly hazardous classes, is an improvement on any reading. The three hazard bins are set out under the required disaggregation.
disaggregationRequired: Required: none set in the register. Two are required on this sheet's authority: pesticide category (insecticides; herbicides; fungicides and bactericides; botanical and biological products; other) and WHO hazard class, in three bins (Class Ia or Ib, highly or extremely hazardous; Class II or III, moderately or slightly hazardous; Class U or unclassified, unlikely to present acute hazard). Total tonnage treats a highly hazardous pesticide and a low-toxicity biological product as equivalent, and a fall in total mass can conceal a shift to more hazardous products, so the hazard cut is what carries this indicator's direction.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Crop; cropping season; agroecological zone; farm size class; sex of the plot manager; application method (knapsack, tractor-mounted, seed treatment); whether the plot is under a CIMMYT-promoted practice.
unitOfObservation: The farm holding (its plots)
calculationSummary: Numerator: kilograms of pesticide active ingredient applied in the intervention area over the reference year, summed across products, crops, plots and application events. Convert each product using its registered label concentration; where none is available, apply FAO's global conversion factors by pesticide type (insecticides 31 percent, herbicides 34, fungicides and bactericides 60, mineral oils 75, plant growth regulators 29, rodenticides 45, seed-treatment fungicides 2, seed-treatment insecticides 9), and the generic 36 percent only where the type is unknown, flagging any value that used generic factors. Denominator: cropland area of the same holdings in hectares (arable land plus permanent crops), counted once for the year, following the FAO use-per-area-of-cropland construct. Value = (numerator / denominator) in the reporting year minus the same ratio in the baseline year. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1: a farm or household survey with a plot-level pesticide application module, or on-farm trial records where CIMMYT staff observe applications directly. It is the only source capturing product identity, concentration, quantity, applications and the holding's cropland area together, which the active-ingredient conversion and the cropland denominator require; treated area is captured with them and reported as the companion intensity. Fallback DS2: project, partner or agro-dealer records of volumes supplied in the area, used only where a survey is not feasible and flagged as fallback-sourced, because product supplied is not product applied and the area it reached is unrecorded. Fallback DS3 (denominator only): geospatial cropland or cropped-area mapping where holding areas are not measured on the ground; it cannot supply the numerator, since applied active ingredient is not observable from satellite or aerial data. Comparator DS4: FAOSTAT Pesticides Use and Pesticides Indicators domains, national kilograms of active ingredient per hectare of cropland, to place the direction of the project figure against the national one, never a substitute for it and never pooled with it; national values cannot resolve an intervention area. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or mobile-generated observations cannot establish product concentration or the holding's cropland area.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which source role the project used, Recommended or Fallback. If Fallback, why direct measurement was not feasible and which records supplied each side of the ratio.
collectionInstrument: For DS1: a plot-level input-use module recording, per application event, the product trade name, its active ingredient and label concentration, the quantity used, the area treated and the date, with a plot roster giving the area of every cropland plot on the holding, sprayed or not, which is the denominator. Respondent: the person who manages the plot and decides on spraying, not a household head by proxy. Mode: face-to-face interview, inspecting product containers where present, since trade names are recalled more reliably than concentrations. On-farm trials use the trial logbook.
collectionFrequency: Annually where a plot-level monitoring panel or trial network exists; otherwise at baseline, midline and endline. Keep the recall window and season coverage identical across rounds.
reportingFrequency: Annually; between measurement waves the latest measured value is carried forward with its year of measurement noted.
referencePeriod: One full cropping year, covering every season on the holding, compared against the same 12-month window in the baseline year.
baselineRequired: Yes, unavoidably: the indicator is defined as a change from baseline, so without one there is no value to report, only a level. Fallbacks: a recall-based reconstruction of the previous cropping year's applications, covering every season on the holding, in the first round, flagged as such; or a matched comparison area measured in the same round, reported as a difference between areas rather than over time. If neither is feasible: report the annual level only, as monitoring, with no change claim.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool Recommended-sourced values directly; a project that used a Fallback is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note on its source, not blended in. A value built against a matched comparison area is a between-area difference, not a change over time: it is reported beside the pooled change with a note and never pooled with it.

B: Combination method. Pool by summing numerators and denominators: the institutional figure is total active ingredient across reporting projects divided by their total cropland area. Never average project-level intensities across projects of unequal area.

C: Levels and operations. Two things are computed and neither may be averaged upward. The level is recomputed at every level from its own application records, never from the figures beneath it. The change is recomputed the same way, as the difference between two figures each built at that level from its own records, never as a mean of plot-level or project-level changes. At Farm / Plot, the active ingredient applied on the holding's plots over the reference year divided by its cropland area, differenced against its baseline value. At Regional / Aggregated and above, the same construction over the summed area within the pooling domain of Block A, differenced against the baseline built identically. Also report: the area the figure rests on, the units excluded under Eligibility, the measurement or model basis of both terms, and whether the same units were measured in both periods, since a change across a changed panel is not a change on the ground.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This value does not combine arithmetically with the count of ecological solution packages deployed (KPI-O31) beneath it; they connect through the theory of change. It does not enter KPI-I14 arithmetically; where the inverted chemical-control score is computed it is published beside KPI-I14's headline.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: where two projects' areas overlap, de-duplicate by plot or holding identifier before summing, so neither the mass nor the hectares count twice; if that is not possible, label the pooled figure indicative. Named overlaps: the same hectares appear in KPI-OC33 and KPI-I10 (sustainable land) and KPI-OC28 and KPI-OC29 (nutrient efficiency); different constructs on a shared land base, never to be summed into a combined environmental figure. Coverage and precision travel with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands used in official statistics: 16.5 per cent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 per cent released flagged, above 33.3 per cent not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one deduplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above, and a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place. On this sheet a record is one holding's pesticide application account for the reporting year, over its cropland area.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: all FAO-scope categories applied to crops, seed or stored produce on the measured holdings inside the project's declared CIMMYT intervention area; botanical and biological products are reported under their own category and are not folded into "other pesticides".

Exclusion: disinfectants are excluded, being FAO's tenth reporting category but not applied to crops for pest control, and including them would inflate a crop-protection intensity figure; non-agricultural applications (public health vector control, household and veterinary use); product bought but not applied in the year; holdings whose cropland area cannot be established.

Missing data: a holding that cannot report quantities is excluded from both numerator and denominator, never entered as zero, and the excluded share is reported with the value.

Repeated observations: all application events on a plot in the year are summed into the numerator while the plot counts once in the denominator; where a holding is surveyed twice in a round, only the first interview counts.
limitations: Mass is not risk. A kilogram of a highly hazardous compound counts the same as a kilogram of a benign one, and low-dose products deliver the same control at a fraction of the mass, so intensity can fall while hazard rises. Read the hazard-class breakdown with the headline value.

Supports a contribution claim only. Pesticide use responds to seasonal pest pressure, weather, prices, subsidies, credit and regulation; CIMMYT is one influence among these, and a mild pest year can move the value more than any intervention.

Measurement error is substantial. Farmers recall product names better than concentrations and volumes, small applications go unreported, and values built partly on generic conversion factors are weaker than those built on label concentrations.

Comparability across sites is limited by what is grown. Horticulture, maize and rainfed wheat carry very different application norms, and an intensity computed over a denominator that counts a twice-cropped hectare once reads higher than one that counts it twice. Compare like cropping systems and state the denominator convention.

A fall means less active ingredient was applied per hectare in the measured area. It does not mean pest damage was avoided, yields held, or farmers are better off. Read it with yield and crop-loss evidence: a reduction obtained at the cost of a crop loss is not a sustainability gain.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
Measurement: Wanner et al. (2024), Pesticides use and trade: Methodological changes and exploration of alternative data sources, active-ingredient basis and conversion factors; use-per-area-of-cropland formula, cropland being arable land plus permanent crops.

Pesticides use, pesticides trade and pesticides indicators 1990 to 2020, FAOSTAT Analytical Brief 46, 2022, FAO: the ten pesticide categories in scope and the kilograms-per-hectare construct (explanatory notes). No link.

Pesticides use and trade 1990 to 2023, FAOSTAT Analytical Brief 109, 2025, FAO: the current published series, for benchmark values only. No link.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E team and enumerators; agronomists for trial logbooks. Validation: project MEAL officer, checking label concentrations, that the plot roster covers every cropland plot on the holding, sprayed or not, the treated areas, and the share of values converted with generic factors. Calculation: project M&E, per the Calculation method above; CIMMYT MEAL unit for the pooled figure. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 9 · Environmental sustainability — Reference sheet KPI-OC31

name: Proportion of cultivated land under improved or sustainable practices
resultsLevel: Outcome. Farmers applying improved practices on their own land is a change in practice among beneficiaries, which is the Core's definition of an outcome.
primaryObjective: PO4 Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient. One primary objective only; the register lists PO4 first, its primary convention. Contributing, contribution only: PO3 (smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved), since sustainable land management protects the productive base livelihoods depend on.
cgiarImpactArea: Environmental Health & Biodiversity: the CGIAR standard indicator this measure feeds (hectares under improved management) sits under that Impact Area in the One CGIAR Standard Indicators report.
sdgTarget: SDG indicator 2.4.1 (proportion of agricultural area under productive and sustainable agriculture), target 2.4. Construct-level correspondence only: 2.4.1 is assessed through a national farm survey scoring 11 sustainability sub-indicators, while this indicator uses a practice-based test in intervention areas. Evidence toward target 2.4, not an official 2.4.1 value.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR standard indicator "hectares under improved management" (Environmental Health and Biodiversity), which KPI-I10 reports directly. The CGIAR Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 captures hectares as an "other quantitative measure of use" under Innovation Use outcomes (Annex 3).
definition: The share of cultivated land within CIMMYT intervention areas on which at least one improved or sustainable management practice was applied during the reporting year. Improved or sustainable practices are land-based practices or technologies promoted or validated by CIMMYT and its partners to raise productivity, resource-use efficiency, or resilience while maintaining the natural resource base: for example conservation agriculture (reduced or no tillage, residue retention), improved soil fertility management, crop rotation and diversification, and improved water management. Each physical hectare counts once, whatever the number of qualifying practices it carries. The rate companion is KPI-I10, whose land scope is wider: this numerator is its cultivated-land component, not its whole total.
rationale: Answers whether the sustainable-production practices CIMMYT develops and promotes are taken up on the land, the adoption step between the pathway's solution-package outputs and its land-scale impact (KPI-I10, which counts the same cultivated hectares and further land types besides). A proportion shows how far adoption has penetrated the intervention area, which an absolute hectare count cannot, and corresponds at construct level to SDG 2.4.1 and the CGIAR standard indicator on hectares under improved management.
projectSpecificApplication: Describe this project's intervention-area boundary, cropping systems, and promoted-practice list; the definition, unit, and calculation method stay unchanged. Example: the share of cultivated land in a project's 12 target districts under at least one practice from its promoted conservation-agriculture package, from its annual probability sample of holdings across the districts, stratified by participation. A package that does not fit this sheet's practice categories is referred to the MEAL focal point rather than redefined here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision, donor commitment, or reporting need served. Example: a project tracks it because its donor requires a land-under-improved-practices result, and because a flat proportion at midline tells the team its scaling model is not converting demonstration into field-level uptake.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.  Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure.
unit: Percentage of cultivated land (hectare-based proportion)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of cultivated land is under practices on the project's declared qualifying list. Unique hectares are counted once per reporting year, so the value does not rise with cropping intensity, and the qualifying list is frozen per project so the numerator cannot be widened mid-window.
disaggregationRequired: Required: none recorded in the register. Practice type is required on this sheet's authority, because a proportion pooled over very different practices is hard to interpret, in six categories: improved variety; soil and nutrient management; water management; pest, weed and disease management; crop diversification and rotation; agroforestry and landscape measures. An item enters the declared qualifying list only if it falls in one of these categories. A hectare carrying practices in several categories counts once in the value and appears in each of its categories, so category areas are not additive. The area whose only qualifying element is an improved variety is reported as a subtotal of the value, with the variety identification method.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Commodity or cropping system. Sex and age of the plot manager (male / female; youth / non-youth on the youth band of 15 to 30, stated once in Core Section 4). Country or agroecological zone.
unitOfObservation: Plot
calculationSummary: Numerator: hectares of cultivated land within the intervention area on which at least one practice from the promoted-practice list was applied during the reporting year. Each physical hectare counts once, whatever the number of practices it carries or cropping cycles it goes through, since a proportion requires unique physical hectares. Denominator: total cultivated land (hectares) within the intervention-area boundary in the same year. Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100, applying sample weights where survey-based. Where only participants were surveyed, the denominator is participants' total cultivated land, the value is reported as the participant-land share, labelled as such, and it is never pooled with boundary shares. The promoted-practice list is declared in the project's MEAL plan before the baseline round and frozen for the project's life; a change is a dated amendment, and the baseline is recomputed on the amended list before any change is claimed. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1 (Censuses and surveys): annual plot-level survey recording, per cultivated plot, the practices applied and the plot area, measured (GPS or tape) rather than farmer-estimated wherever feasible. The survey is a probability sample of cultivated plots or holdings across the whole declared boundary, participants and non-participants alike; the participant registry may stratify it but never frames it alone. A sample drawn from the participant registry alone measures participants' land only. Frame DS2 (Administrative and registry data): project records supplying the promoted-practice list, the boundary, and the participant registry used to stratify the survey. Fallback DS2: project or partner records of the plots on which a listed practice was applied, with their area, spot-checked at least annually; weaker verification, so flagged fallback-sourced and reported alongside the pooled share with a note, never blended in; a Fallback-sourced project's hectares enter neither term of the pooled share. Area converted from input sales is not such a record. Fallback DS3, calibration only (Geospatial and Earth observation): land-cover mapping may estimate the denominator and a few visible practices (residue retention), but only calibrated against ground observations: area is estimated from the reference classification of a probability sample of ground observations, with its uncertainty reported, and is not read off the map; never entered as an independent value. Fallback DS4, denominator only (Secondary and international databases): national or subnational cultivated-area statistics where the intervention area aligns with administrative units; they cannot observe the numerator. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated and other non-traditional data): the indicator needs verified practice status matched to measured plot areas inside a defined boundary, which crowdsourced data cannot provide.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role this project used, Recommended or Fallback; if Fallback, why direct collection was not feasible. Example: "Used Recommended: probability sample of 1,200 holdings across the 12 declared districts, stratified by participation, with both terms estimated from the same sample."
collectionInstrument: DS1 route: a plot-level practice module recording, per plot: practices applied in the reporting year (from the promoted list, with an open category), plot area and how it was measured, crop(s) grown, sex and age of the plot manager. Respondent: the person managing the plot. Mode: face-to-face interview, with plot visits or GPS measurement where required. Fallback route (DS2): no instrument; the record states the area, the basis of the recorded area, and the last spot-check date. The same module carries KPI-I10's hectare-type field, so the two indicators are read from one round of this instrument and neither is collected independently of the other.
collectionFrequency: Annually, after the main cropping season so the year's practice use is observable. Short projects may measure baseline and endline only; the value then describes one interval, no trend.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Between measurement rounds the latest measured value is carried forward with its measurement year noted.
referencePeriod: The reporting year (12 months). A snapshot: it describes practice use in that year only, and successive annual values cannot be summed or averaged into a cumulative figure.
baselineRequired: Yes. The baseline is the proportion already under the promoted practices at project start, rarely zero; practices found already widespread are removed from the promoted list and the baseline recalculated. Fallbacks: (a) reconstruct baseline practice use by recall in the first survey round; (b) use the first reporting-year value as baseline, with the substitution stated. If neither is feasible: monitoring only, no change claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Across projects: pool Recommended-sourced values directly; a Fallback-sourced project is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, not blended in; a participant-land share (Calculation method) is reported alongside the pooled share with a note and never pooled.

B: Combination method. Pool by summing numerator and denominator hectares across contributing projects, then computing one proportion. Never average project-level percentages: intervention areas differ enormously in size.

C: Levels and operations. A share of area, recomputed at every level from its own numerator and denominator, never averaged from the levels beneath it. Both terms are hectares, never counts of farms, because a farm is not a unit of land and a share over farms is a different indicator. At Farm / Plot, qualifying area over that holding's cultivated area. At Regional / Aggregated and above, the summed qualifying area over the summed cultivated area within the pooling domain of Block A, after the de-duplication Block E requires, since a hectare counted by two projects is one hectare. Also report: the denominator area and its source, the area excluded under Eligibility, and the share of the intervention area the figure covers.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: No. The proportion does not combine arithmetically with the pathway's outputs (KPI-O30, KPI-O31) or with KPI-I10; the levels connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative, not arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and boundary: each physical hectare counts once; where intervention areas overlap, de-duplicate by plot identifier or mapped boundary before pooling, otherwise label the pooled figure an upper estimate. Named overlaps: KPI-I10 counts this numerator's hectares as an absolute number and adds land types excluded here, so this numerator is a subset of KPI-I10's total and never equal to it by rule; the two are read from one collection and never added into a single figure; KPI-OC36 can legitimately count the same hectare when a practice is both sustainable and climate-adaptive, so the two proportions answer different questions and are never summed. Coverage and precision travel with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands used in official statistics: 16.5 per cent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 per cent released flagged, above 33.3 per cent not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one deduplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above, and a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place. On this sheet a record is one plot determination for the reporting year, one determination per plot whatever the number of seasons it was surveyed in.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: individually managed cultivated land inside the project's declared CIMMYT intervention area, including demonstration plots cultivated by participating farmers; practices count whether newly adopted or continued, provided applied in the reporting year.

Exclusion: research-station and researcher-managed plots; non-cultivated land; practices already in general use before the intervention, removed from the promoted list so pre-existing habits do not inflate the value.

Missing data: plots with unknown practice status stay in the denominator and out of the numerator; the share of the denominator with measured status is reported alongside as a coverage rate.

Repeated observations: one determination per plot per year; a plot surveyed in two seasons counts once, as under improved practice if any qualifying practice was applied in either season.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only: adoption also responds to input prices, tenure security, labour availability, weather and other programmes, and without a comparison group the counterfactual is unknown.

Counts land under a promoted practice, not verified sustainability outcomes. A hectare under minimum tillage counts even if the practice is poorly applied or its soil effects never materialise; pair with the pathway's condition indicators (soil organic carbon, nutrient-use efficiency, pesticide intensity) before claiming the land is managed more sustainably. For the same reason values are not comparable with SDG 2.4.1, which scores measured criteria rather than practice presence.

Both terms of the ratio carry error: farmer-reported practice use is inflated by courtesy bias toward the promoting organisation, farmer-estimated plot areas are systematically inaccurate, and the denominator often comes from a different source (mapping or statistics) than the numerator (survey). Measured areas and a documented denominator source limit, but do not remove, this error.

Comparability is only as good as the practice lists and boundaries behind the values: projects promote different packages, and any change in the boundary or the promoted list shifts the proportion without any change on the ground. Report such changes with the value.

A rise means a larger share of cultivated land carried at least one promoted practice that year. It does not mean practices persist, whole farms converted, or environmental condition improved; it is a snapshot, and year-on-year values track penetration, not cumulative reach.
subMetrics:
None. Practice-type shares are disaggregations of the same measurement, not sub-metrics.

Neighbouring sheets: KPI-I10 (hectares under improved, sustainable and climate-resilient management, the CGIAR standard indicator), the impact this indicator feeds, whose cultivated-land component is this indicator's numerator and whose total is larger wherever non-cultivated land is reported; KPI-OC36 (percentage of farming-system area under climate-adaptation practices), which can count the same hectare and is never summed with this one; KPI-O30 / KPI-O31 (solution packages validated / deployed), the pathway's outputs whose uptake this indicator measures.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E team and enumerators (plot survey, area measurement); project technical team (promoted-practice list, boundary). Validation: project MEAL officer. Calculation: project MEAL officer produces the project proportion; the CIMMYT MEAL unit de-duplicates overlaps and pools across projects. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 9 · Environmental sustainability — Reference sheet KPI-OC33

name: Number of decision-makers or institutions integrating agroecosystem, biodiversity or soil-health considerations into plans or policies
resultsLevel: Outcome. The counted change happens when an external institution writes agroecosystem, biodiversity or soil-health provisions into its own plan, a change in policy among partners, which is the Core's definition of an outcome; it matches CGIAR's Policy Change outcome category. The upstream delivered results, the evidence products and decision-support assessments handed to those institutions, are counted separately at output level, in the Policy, finance & market systems pathway (KPI-O32 and KPI-O39).
primaryObjective: PO4 Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient. Contributing: PO2 (Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries).
cgiarImpactArea: Environmental Health & Biodiversity
sdgTarget: None. SDG target 15.9 (integrate ecosystem and biodiversity values into national and local planning, development processes, poverty reduction strategies and accounts) is the matching target, but its official indicator 15.9.1 counts countries that set national targets in their national biodiversity strategies and action plans, and countries implementing the System of Environmental-Economic Accounting. Its unit is the country and its reporter is the national government, so it cannot receive a count of institutions whose plans one organisation's evidence helped shape.
otherFrameworks: Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework Target 14 (integration of biodiversity and its multiple values into policies, regulations, planning and development processes across all levels of government and all sectors) is the global commitment this indicator tracks contributions to. CGIAR Results Framework: results here concerning a public plan, policy, strategy or investment also meet CGIAR's Policy Change outcome definition and can be reported there with its minimum data fields (type, stage, owner).
definition: Counts the decision-makers or institutions that integrated agroecosystem, biodiversity or soil-health considerations into a plan or policy of their own during the reporting year, with documented evidence that CIMMYT evidence informed the integration. "Integration" means the adopted or revised document carries a named strategy, objective, target, rule or resource allocation on agroecosystem health, biodiversity or agrobiodiversity, or soil health, not a passing mention. The value counts institution-and-plan pairings: an institution that changes two separate plans is counted twice. An individual decision-maker who owns a binding document is counted in a separate companion count, reported beside the value and never added to it.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's environmental evidence on agroecosystems, biodiversity and soils reaches the plans and policies that govern land use, and whether the institutions making those decisions take it up. It is the point where the science becomes a commitment owned by a government, investor, company or farmer organisation, and the institutional step in the chain running from evidence products, through this uptake, to measured agrobiodiversity in intervention areas (KPI-I14). It feeds institutional and donor reporting on environmental health and biodiversity.
projectSpecificApplication: State which decision-makers or institutions the project engages, which plans or policies are in view, the countries and policy scale covered, and the form of evidence linking CIMMYT to the integration. Do not change the counting unit, the integration test, or the calculation method. If applying the indicator as defined is not feasible in this project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count informs, for example a donor outcome target on policy uptake, or an adaptive-management trigger: engagements repeatedly stopping at draft stage prompt a review of which institutions the project works with.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work does not engage the institutions whose plans this indicator counts
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.  Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work does not engage the institutions whose plans this indicator counts.
unit: Number (count of institution and plan or policy pairings)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more institution-and-plan pairings integrate agroecosystem, biodiversity or soil-health considerations that CIMMYT evidence informed.
disaggregationRequired: Required: policy scale or level (local / national / regional / global), as recorded in the register; and institution type, required on this sheet's authority, using this category list: national agricultural research and extension system (NARES); university or higher education institution; government ministry or public agency; CGIAR centre; international research organisation, non-CGIAR; multilateral or UN agency; regional or sub-regional organisation; private company; financial institution; non-governmental or civil society organisation; farmer organisation or cooperative; foundation; other. If more than 10 per cent of records fall to "other" in a year, the list is revised rather than the institutions reclassified.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country or region; thematic focus (agroecosystem, biodiversity or agrobiodiversity, soil health); instrument type (plan, strategy, policy, regulation, investment design, corporate standard); new instrument versus revision; scorecard level reached (named strategy versus quantified target).
unitOfObservation: Organization, paired with the plan or policy it owns (see Definition for the counting unit).
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct institution and plan or policy pairings meeting all three tests in the reporting year. (a) The plan or policy was adopted, issued or formally revised during the year by the institution itself. (b) It carries an explicit agroecosystem, biodiversity or soil-health provision. The bar is the Agrobiodiversity Index Commitment scorecard, which scores a document occurrence 1 for a mention with no strategy or target attached, 2 where a specific strategy, goal or objective is stated, and 3 where a specific, usually time-bound target is set: this indicator counts level 2 and above, and excludes level 1. (c) Documented evidence links the provision to CIMMYT evidence, engagement or technical advice: citation in the document, recorded CIMMYT participation in drafting, or written acknowledgement by the institution. A before-and-after comparison of the text documents what changed and is filed with one of the three, never in place of them. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: CIMMYT project policy-engagement and outcome-monitoring records, logging each institution, the plan or policy, its scale, the integration event and date, the quoted provision with its scorecard level, and the evidence of CIMMYT's contribution, each record cross-checked against the official document; and official publications of the instrument (government gazettes and ministry archives), for its existence and provisions. A key-informant statement from the institution on how CIMMYT evidence was used belongs in this evidence file, not counted as a separate source. Fallback DS4: third-party policy repositories (FAOLEX for food and agriculture legislation, institutional and corporate strategy publications), used where CIMMYT's own log is incomplete. Flag such values as fallback-sourced: these repositories verify the document and its provisions but rarely evidence CIMMYT's contribution, which must then be established separately. Not applicable DS1: the counted change is read from an institution's own document, not collected from respondents or measured in the field. Not applicable DS3: geospatial data cannot identify a plan or its provisions. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or mobile data cannot verify a document's content or the contribution trail behind it.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State whether Recommended or Fallback was used. If Fallback, state why the project's engagement log was incomplete, which repositories were used, and how the CIMMYT contribution was evidenced.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, secondary and administrative source (DS2 and DS4). The engagement register is the tool, with the fields listed under Data source.
collectionFrequency: Continuous: each pairing is logged as its integration event is documented
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the integration event (adoption, issuance or formal revision of the plan or policy) occurred
baselineRequired: No. An annual flow count starting from zero each reporting year, with no pre-project stock to measure; change over time is read from the annual series. A project claiming it moved an institution records the plan's pre-engagement text as the comparison.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: sum the institution-and-plan pairings evidenced in the project's policy-engagement records (Recommended); an official publication of the instrument (a gazette or ministry archive entry) is a Recommended source for its existence and provisions, and a pairing is pooled where its CIMMYT contribution is evidenced in the project's own records; a pairing whose contribution is evidenced only through third-party repositories (Fallback) is reported alongside the summed figure with a note, and the same project's other pairings stay in the sum.

B: Combination method. Summed: the institutional figure is the sum of distinct institution and plan pairings across all reporting projects in the year, after de-duplication. Never average project-level counts.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of unique institution-and-plan pairings in the reporting year, de-duplicated on the identifier Block E names: one institution that changes two separate plans contributes two, and the same plan reported twice contributes one. At institutional level, the count de-duplicated again across projects on the same pairing, since one institution's one plan reached by two projects is one pairing. The two units, the institution-and-plan pairing and the individual-and-document pairing, are counted and reported separately and never added: an individual and an institution are not commensurable, and a combined total would move with the mix rather than with the work. Where identifiers cannot be reconciled, the institutional figure is labelled an upper estimate. Also report: the two counts side by side, the number of distinct institutions behind the pairings, the number of contributing projects, the number of pairings reported alongside because they rest on the Fallback, the level-3 subtotal beside the level-2-and-above count, and the integration test applied, since the count moves with it.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count never combines arithmetically with KPI-I14 (the agrobiodiversity index); the levels connect as a narrative, not a sum.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: three risks. Two projects engaging the same ministry on the same plan must resolve to one record through a shared institution and plan identifier; where identifiers cannot be matched, label the sum an upper estimate. A national plan covering several project areas is one record, with geography as a disaggregation. Across the register, a CIMMYT-informed national soil-health strategy also meets the definition of KPI-OC37 (public policies, strategies or regulations informed by CIMMYT-generated evidence) and, if it carries gender-equity provisions, KPI-OC39, so those records must share an instrument identifier and the roll-up must never present one instrument as two or three separate policy achievements.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion and exclusion: a plan informed by more than one CIMMYT project counts once; drafts count only in the year they are adopted; provisions with no evidenced CIMMYT link are excluded; documents owned by CIMMYT or by a project it manages are excluded, since the institution must own the plan. An individual decision-maker is recorded in the companion count only where they own a document that carries the provision in a role that makes it binding and no institution counted here issues it; influence with no document does not count.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only: plans are written by their owning institutions under many influences, and "informed by CIMMYT" spans everything from drafting the technical annex to supplying one cited study. The evidence requirement bounds the claim but does not measure CIMMYT's share of it.

Integration is not implementation: a provision on paper may never be funded, enforced, or reflected in what happens on the land, so this count evidences institutional change, not environmental change.

Because the counting unit pairs an institution with a plan, the count rewards institutions holding many planning instruments and is not a count of distinct organisations reached; read it with the institution-type disaggregation before comparing projects or years.

Judging a provision as a strategy rather than a mention requires expert reading, and the scorecard was designed for text mining across whole national policy sets rather than single documents. The control is that each record quotes the provision and states its level, so classifications can be audited.

An increase means more institutions wrote CIMMYT-informed environmental provisions into their plans that year, not that agrobiodiversity or soil health improved; pair it with practice-adoption and agrobiodiversity indicators.
subMetrics: None. Policy scale, institution type, thematic focus and scorecard level are disaggregations of the same count, not separately calculated metrics. Related indicators have their own sheets: KPI-I14 (composite agrobiodiversity index), which this outcome rolls up to; and KPI-OC37 and KPI-OC39, the policy-change outcomes it can overlap with (see Aggregation rule).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E or policy-engagement focal point, logging each pairing with its provision text and contribution evidence. Validation: project MEAL officer, checking the quoted provision and its scorecard level against the official document. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (de-duplication, including against KPI-OC37 and KPI-OC39 records, and the institutional sum). Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 9 · Environmental sustainability — Reference sheet KPI-OC34

name: Greenhouse gas emission intensity of food production: kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent per tonne of food produced
resultsLevel: Impact, as recorded in the register: a condition of the production system in the CGIAR climate mitigation impact area rather than a deliverable or a behaviour change.
primaryObjective: PO4 Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient. Contributing objective: PO2 Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries; a per-tonne measure is the operational form of that planetary boundary clause, but the indicator is reported once, under PO4.
cgiarImpactArea: Climate Adaptation and Mitigation
sdgTarget: SDG target 13.2, indicator 13.2.2 (total greenhouse gas emissions per year). Partial correspondence: the gases and the carbon dioxide equivalent convention are shared, but 13.2.2 is a national annual total in megatonnes compiled under the UN climate convention, not a per-tonne intensity for a defined area, and its metadata fixes the 100-year global warming potentials of the Fifth Assessment Report where this indicator uses the Sixth. Those two differences are why the correspondence is partial rather than a matter of scale: a value here must never be presented as an SDG 13.2.2 figure, and neither figure is converted into the other without first restating it on the other's global warming potential set. Target 2.4 is also relevant, but its indicator 2.4.1 is a land-area share across eleven sub-indicators, none of them greenhouse gases.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR results framework: the climate adaptation and mitigation standard indicator on tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, reported as a total rather than an intensity. UNFCCC national inventories and Nationally Determined Contributions in agriculture, which use the same IPCC methods. FAOSTAT emissions intensity series.
definition: The greenhouse gases released in producing one tonne of food in CIMMYT intervention areas, in kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent per tonne. The boundary is the field: emissions arising in the cropped area during the production cycle, not those from making the inputs before they reach the farm or from handling the harvest afterwards. The value is computed rather than measured gas by gas: activity data (nitrogen applied, days a rice field is flooded, urea and lime used, fuel burned) multiplied by emission factors, each gas converted to a common carbon dioxide equivalent using 100-year global warming potentials. Three qualifiers change the number and must travel with it: boundary, calculation tier and global warming potential set.
rationale: Answers whether food from the systems CIMMYT works with is becoming less emissions-costly per tonne, the question behind CGIAR's climate mitigation impact area and behind national commitments to cut agricultural emissions without cutting output. Projects use it to see whether better nitrogen management, rice water management and residue and tillage practice change the carbon cost of production and not only the yield; institutional reporting uses it as the emissions strand of CIMMYT's environmental sustainability narrative.
projectSpecificApplication: State the intervention areas, crops, cropping years and plots covered; which emission sources were quantified and which are absent from the system (no rice, no liming); and the IPCC tier per source. Do not change the boundary, unit, denominator convention or global warming potential set. Where only some sources can be quantified, attach the source list to the value rather than redefining the indicator here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment the value serves: a low-emission development or climate-finance commitment, a national mitigation target the project reports into, or a trigger to revisit nitrogen advice if intensity does not fall while yields rise.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.  Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure.
unit: Kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent per tonne of food produced (kg CO2e/t)
directionOfChange: Decrease. A falling value means fewer kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent are emitted per tonne of food produced. It can also fall because output rose on unchanged emissions.
disaggregationRequired: Required: crop; and gas or source category (nitrous oxide from nitrogen inputs, methane from rice, methane and nitrous oxide from residue burning, carbon dioxide from urea, lime and fuel). Without the crop split the value is not interpretable, since crops differ in emission profile; without the source split a project cannot see what moved the value or which practice to change. The register records no required disaggregation, so both are adopted as required. A combined cross-crop figure is not reported: only the crop-disaggregated series is published, because a pooled figure moves whenever the crop mix moves and reads as a change in intensity.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Agroecological zone; season; water regime (irrigated, rainfed, flooded rice); nitrogen management practice compared; tillage and residue regime; farm size class.
unitOfObservation: Plot
calculationSummary: Value = total kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent divided by total tonnes, both summed across the measured plots before dividing. Numerator: field emissions estimated as activity data times emission factor, covering direct and indirect nitrous oxide from nitrogen inputs and soil organic matter loss, methane from rice cultivation, methane and nitrous oxide from field burning of crop residues (Chapter 2, Equation 2.27, with the emission factors of Table 2.5 and the combustion factors of Table 2.6; carbon dioxide from burning annual crop residues is not counted, and burned residue leaves the residue nitrogen term), and carbon dioxide from urea and liming, following the IPCC 2019 Refinement, Volume 4, and from field fuel use. Each source follows the equations cited under Reference standards; the methodological companion summarises how they combine. This field fixes what those equations leave open: the global warming potentials, the denominator and the apportionment rule. Nitrous oxide nitrogen converts to nitrous oxide by 44/28; gases convert to carbon dioxide equivalent with the 100-year global warming potentials of the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report, which are fixed institutionally for this indicator (methane from non-fossil sources 27.0, nitrous oxide 273; IPCC Sixth Assessment Report, Working Group I, Chapter 7). Fifth Assessment values are not used, and a series already computed on them is restated on the Sixth or broken at the change year and labelled. Denominator: tonnes of dry matter of the food product harvested for human consumption (grain; paddy grain for rice) from the same plots in the same period, from fresh weight and measured moisture; the tonnage at a stated market moisture may be published alongside. On intercropped and rotated plots the cycle's emissions are apportioned to the food crops by their share of harvested dry matter, with the apportionment rule stated against the value; non-food crops in the rotation carry their share and are excluded from the denominator rather than ignored, since ignoring them would load the whole cycle's emissions onto the food crop. This is the same apportionment rule as KPI-OC30, so the two intensity indicators share one denominator convention. All emissions of a food crop's cycle are carried by its food product; straw, stover, husks and other residues carry none, whether removed, sold, fed or retained. The dry-matter apportionment applies only between distinct crops sharing a cycle, on each crop's harvested main product. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1: plot-level activity data collected for this purpose, paired with crop-cut harvest measurement on the same plots, factors applied at the highest tier the project can justify, and direct chamber flux measurement where a project runs it. Only this source observes both terms on the same area and period. Chamber-measured plots supply the data for a Tier 2 factor; their measured fluxes are not substituted plot by plot into the sum. Fallback DS2: project and scheme administrative records (input distribution registers, irrigation logs, farmer record books) with project harvest records; always flagged, because inputs distributed are not inputs applied to a given field. Fallback DS3: Earth observation products for flooded rice area, cropping calendar and cropped area; flagged, since the numerator becomes partly modelled. Fallback DS4: national statistics and published emissions-intensity series with national production; last resort, since national aggregates cannot be resolved to an intervention area. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced and mobile data cannot establish plot-level nitrogen rates, flooding regimes or measured harvest weights to the standard the calculation requires.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State the role used and, for a Fallback, which one and why plot-level collection was not feasible. Name the calculator used and whether any emission factor is country-specific.
collectionInstrument: For DS1: a plot-level activity data module plus a yield protocol on the same plots. Activity module: crop calendar; input application log (product, nutrient content, rate, date); residue and tillage management, with the share of residue burned; irrigation and, for rice, flooding status before and during the season; lime and urea quantities; machinery hours and fuel; diesel for on-farm irrigation pumps. Respondent: the plot manager, who identifies boundaries, crop, sowing and harvest dates and every application event. Mode: face-to-face interview at the plot, physical measurements by the enumerator. Yield: crop cuts on demarcated sub-plots, weighed fresh, moisture measured, converted to dry matter from measured moisture. Factors applied through an IPCC-based calculator such as FAO EX-ACT. EX-ACT applies Tier 1 defaults unless Tier 2 parameters are entered; record which were overridden. EX-ACT ships Fifth Assessment global warming potentials as its defaults, so the Sixth Assessment values this sheet fixes are entered as an override before any run, and the override is recorded with the result so a reader can tell which set produced the number.
collectionFrequency: Once per cropping year where plot-level activity data collection is running; at minimum a baseline and an endline round for any change claim.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Between rounds the latest value is carried forward with its cropping year, tier and boundary noted.
referencePeriod: One complete cropping year, so that second cycles, the pre-season water regime of rice fields and off-season operations are captured. Where only one crop cycle is covered, state that basis.
baselineRequired: Yes. The value is only interpretable as change from a pre-intervention level in the same fields, at the same boundary and tier. Fallbacks where no prospective baseline exists: a first-season computation from activity data collected before the practices are applied; a matched comparison area in the same season; or a recall-based reconstruction, flagged as such. If none is feasible: monitoring only, no change claim.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool Recommended-sourced totals directly; a project reporting from administrative records, Earth observation or national statistics is reported alongside the pooled figure with its source named, never blended in. Values computed at different IPCC tiers are pooled only with the tier mix per source stated with the figure.

B: Combination method. Sum the kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent and sum the tonnes, then divide, computed separately for each required disaggregation. Never average project-level or plot-level ratios.

C: Levels and operations. An emissions intensity is a ratio, recomputed at every level from its own numerator and denominator, never averaged from the levels beneath it. At Farm / Plot, the kg CO2e emitted over that plot's tonnes of food produced. At Household, Regional / Aggregated and above, the summed numerator over the summed denominator within the pooling domain of Block A. Also report: the denominator itself, the units excluded under Eligibility, which components were estimated rather than measured and on what assumption, and the composition of the aggregate, since a ratio that moved only because the mix changed is not a change in any of its parts.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. KPI-OC28, the one input indicator beneath this one, measures a different physical quantity and cannot be added to or averaged with carbon dioxide equivalent; the levels connect through the theory of change, not arithmetically.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: de-duplicate by plot identifier before pooling where two projects work in the same intervention area, and label the pooled figure an upper estimate if that is not possible. Named overlaps: the same plots and tonnage also appear in KPI-OC28, KPI-OC29, KPI-OC30, KPI-I10 and the productivity pathway's yield indicators. The tonnage is counted once as production; these ratios are alternative resource lenses on one output and must never be summed into a single efficiency score. The principal double-counting risk is soil carbon: a gain counted as a removal in KPI-I11 must not also be netted off this numerator. Field emissions on CIMMYT-operated plots also fall in KPI-O45 Scope 1 and are never summed with it. Coverage and precision travel with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands used in official statistics: 16.5 per cent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 per cent released flagged, above 33.3 per cent not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one deduplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above, and a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place.
