On this sheet a record is one plot's activity data and harvested tonnage for one crop over the reference period, every cycle of that crop summed, both terms present.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusions: all plots of the project's food crops in the intervention areas, failed and low-yielding plots retained, since they emitted while producing little.

Exclusions: input manufacture and transport before the farm gate, outside the headline value; where a donor requires the wider boundary, a cradle-to-farm-gate figure is reported alongside as a labelled companion; post-harvest processing, storage and transport; household and livestock emissions unless livestock products enter the denominator, in which case the Chapter 10 livestock methods apply and the fact is stated; soil organic carbon stock change is not netted off here, since KPI-I11 measures it.

Missing data: a plot missing either term is dropped from both sums, never imputed; report the share dropped and the share of the numerator computed on default rather than local factors.

Repeated observations: every crop cycle on a plot enters both sums and the ratio is computed once from the totals; never average plot-level or season-level ratios. State the tier and emission factor per source. The institutional minimum is the IPCC 2019 Refinement's disaggregated Tier 1 factors, applied to activity data that distinguish climate zone, fertiliser type, rice water regime before and during the season, and organic amendments; the aggregated single defaults are not used. Carbon dioxide from urea, lime and fuel is computed from quantities applied or burned with the IPCC default factors, which are not provisional. Where a change is claimed for a practice Tier 1 cannot represent (nitrification or urease inhibitors, placement, timing, a non-linear nitrogen-rate response), the source it acts on is computed at Tier 2 or 3 for that claim; at Tier 1 the value is reported but that practice's effect is not claimed from it.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only. Emission intensity moves with rainfall, temperature, fertiliser prices, subsidy policy and the yields those produce, all beyond a project's reach. Report the value with its season and context.

At Tier 1 the value responds to nitrogen rate, fertiliser type, climate zone, rice water regime and organic amendments; it does not respond to inhibitors, placement or timing, which only Tier 2 or 3 capture, and the wide uncertainty on default nitrous oxide factors passes into the ratio.

The ratio can fall while total emissions rise, because intensity improves whenever production grows faster than emissions. Always publish the numerator and denominator with the ratio, or an expansion of cropped area will read as mitigation.

Boundary, tier and global warming potential set drive comparability: a field-boundary value is not comparable with a cradle-to-farm-gate footprint, values at different tiers are not comparable with each other, and changing the global warming potential set shifts every value with nothing changing in the field.

A fall means each tonne harvested from the measured fields carried less estimated emissions at that boundary and tier. It is not a verified emission reduction and cannot be claimed or sold as a carbon credit, which requires the verification standard applied to KPI-I11. A soil carbon loss is not visible in this value.
subMetrics:
None with their own reference sheet. Two components are reported alongside the ratio, never instead of it: total field emissions in kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent, and total production in tonnes. Emissions per hectare uses the same numerator with a different denominator and is a separate measure.

Related sheets: KPI-OC28, KPI-OC29 and KPI-OC30 apply the same resource-per-output logic to the same plots; KPI-I11 covers verified removals; KPI-I10 counts the same area on a different basis.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
Measurement: IPCC (2019), 2019 refinement to the 2006 IPCC guidelines for national greenhouse gas inventories, Volume 4: Agriculture, forestry and other land use, Chapter 11, IPCC; Equation 11.1 direct nitrous oxide and the 44/28 conversion (11.6 to 11.8); Equations 11.9 and 11.10, indirect nitrous oxide (11.22 to 11.23); sections 11.3 and 11.4, carbon dioxide from liming and urea, both recorded as "no refinement" so the 2006 Guidelines methods stand (11.27).

IPCC 2019 Refinement, Volume 4, Chapter 5 (Cropland): Equations 5.1 and 5.2, methane from rice and the adjusted daily emission factor with its scaling factors (5.49 to 5.51). https://www.ipcc-nggip.iges.or.jp/public/2019rf/vol4.html

IPCC 2019 Refinement, Volume 4, Chapter 2 (Generic Methodologies): Equation 2.27, greenhouse gas emissions from fire (2.50), with the emission factors of Table 2.5 (2.54) and the combustion factors of Table 2.6 (2.55), applied here to field burning of crop residues. https://www.ipcc-nggip.iges.or.jp/public/2019rf/vol4.html

2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories, Volume 4 (AFOLU), Chapter 11, sections 11.3 and 11.4: carbon dioxide from liming and from urea application, the methods the 2019 Refinement leaves unrefined. No link.

2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories, Volume 2 (Energy), Chapter 3 (Mobile Combustion): carbon dioxide from fuel burned in field machinery. No link.

IPCC Sixth Assessment Report, Working Group I, Chapter 7: the 100-year global warming potentials fixed for this indicator, methane from non-fossil sources 27.0 and nitrous oxide 273. No link.

Accounting standard: International Organization for Standardization (2019), ISO 14064:2019: Greenhouse gases, ISO 14064-1:2019, greenhouse gases, organization-level quantification and reporting of greenhouse gas emissions and removals, where a project reports its result as a formal greenhouse gas assertion rather than a management indicator.

ISO 14064-2:2019, greenhouse gases, project-level quantification, monitoring and reporting of emission reductions and removal enhancements. No link.

EX-ACT (Environmental eXternalities ACcounting Tool) user guide, FAO: IPCC-based calculator covering the gases and pools of this boundary, the carbon dioxide equivalent unit and the 100-year global warming potential convention. https://openknowledge.fao.org/collections/e970a448-d1c8-4cce-8368-bbdeec41e9d7

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project field team and enumerators. Validation: project MEAL officer (plot identifiers, data completeness, dry-matter conversion, exclusion log). Calculation: project cropping systems or greenhouse gas specialist, recording the tier per source. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 9 · Environmental sustainability — Reference sheet KPI-I09

name: Number of hectares under improved, sustainable and climate-resilient management
resultsLevel: Impact, as recorded in the register and as classified by CGIAR, which lists hectares under improved management among its impact-level standard indicators and among the common impact indicators in its results management framework. CGIAR's own control-and-externality test reads this as an outcome, but CGIAR files it at impact as a measure of the state of the land.
primaryObjective: PO4 Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient. One primary objective only; the register lists PO4 first, its convention for the primary. Contributing, contribution only: PO3 (smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved), since productive, climate-resilient land is the base smallholder livelihoods rest on.
cgiarImpactArea: Environmental Health & Biodiversity, the Impact Area under which CGIAR files its own hectares-under-improved-management standard indicator.
sdgTarget: SDG indicator 2.4.1 (proportion of agricultural area under productive and sustainable agriculture), target 2.4. Construct-level correspondence only, and the units differ: 2.4.1 is a national proportion from a farm survey scoring 11 sustainability sub-indicators, while this is an absolute area under promoted practices. Report as evidence toward target 2.4, never as an official 2.4.1 value.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR standard indicator "hectares under improved management", reported directly by this indicator. ICARDA indicator IM-02 (area of land under improved management), a sibling CGIAR centre's version of the same standard indicator.
definition: The total area of land, in hectares, within CIMMYT intervention areas on which at least one improved, sustainable or climate-resilient management practice was applied during the reporting year. A hectare qualifies on application at any point in that year, as on KPI-OC33, and counts once, whatever the number of practices or cropping cycles it carries. The indicator reports the CGIAR standard indicator "hectares under improved management". CGIAR has not defined "improved management" operationally, so this sheet adapts another CGIAR centre's practice-based test, admitting, unlike it, demonstration plots cultivated by participating farmers: land positively affected by practices or technologies promoted or validated by CIMMYT and its partners.
rationale: Answers how much land CIMMYT's sustainable-intensification work has changed: the headline scale measure of the Environmental sustainability pathway, and a CGIAR standard indicator, so it feeds CGIAR portfolio reporting directly and is comparable across centres. It stands with KPI-OC33, which reports the adoption share on cultivated land: that share's numerator is this indicator's cultivated-land component, and this total is larger wherever the hectare-type disaggregation below records land KPI-OC33's cultivated-land scope excludes.
projectSpecificApplication: Describe this project's boundary, farming systems, promoted-practice list and measurement timing; the institutional definition, unit and calculation method stay unchanged. Example: hectares on participants' land in its 12 target districts under at least one practice from the project's conservation-agriculture and drought-tolerant-variety package, from the annual participant survey. A package that does not fit these practice categories is referred to the MEAL focal point rather than redefined here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision, donor commitment or reporting need served. Example: the donor sets an area target for land under improved management, and area reached against area targeted shows whether scaling partners are delivering at the pace assumed at design.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.  Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure.
unit: Hectares
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more hectares are under improved, sustainable and climate-resilient management. Unique hectares are counted once per reporting year, and this indicator and KPI-OC33 are read from one data collection: KPI-OC33's numerator is this total's cultivated-land component, so the two are never summed.
disaggregationRequired: Required: none recorded in the register. Two are adopted as required. The first is practice type, without which an aggregate figure mixes very different interventions, in six categories: improved variety; soil and nutrient management; water management; pest, weed and disease management; crop diversification and rotation; agroforestry and landscape measures. An item enters the declared qualifying list only if it falls in one of these categories. A hectare carrying practices in several categories counts once in the value and appears in each of its categories, so category areas are not additive. The area whose only qualifying element is an improved variety is reported as a subtotal of the value, with the variety identification method. The second is hectare type (crop land, cultivated pasture, rangeland, conservation or protected area, freshwater or marine ecosystem), since an area falls in exactly one type and the mix determines how the number reads.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Commodity or farming system. Sex and age of the plot manager (male / female; youth / non-youth on the youth band of 15 to 30, stated once in Core Section 4), with communally managed land reported separately as association-applied. Country, region or agroecological zone. Area estimation method (measured versus farmer-reported), a data-quality flag.
unitOfObservation: Plot
calculationSummary: Value = the count of unique physical hectares inside the intervention-area boundary carrying at least one practice from the promoted-practice list during the reporting year, with sample weights applied where the count is survey-estimated. KPI-OC33 is a proportion of cultivated land only; its numerator is this indicator's cultivated-land component and is never derived from this total. The promoted-practice list is declared in the project's MEAL plan before the baseline round and frozen for the project's life; a change is a dated amendment, and the baseline is recomputed on the amended list before any change is claimed. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1 (Censuses and surveys): an annual plot-level survey recording, per plot, the practices applied and the plot area, measured by GPS or tape wherever feasible; the same collection that produces KPI-OC33. Where the survey is framed on the participant registry, it measures participants' land only, and the value is the qualifying area on that land; extending it to non-participants is projection, not sampling. Frame DS2 (Administrative and registry data): project records supplying the promoted-practice list, the boundary and the participant registry used to stratify the survey. Fallback DS2: project or partner records of the plots on which a listed practice was applied, with their area, spot-checked at least annually; the value is flagged fallback-sourced. Area converted from input sales is not such a record. Fallback DS3, calibration only (Geospatial and Earth observation): land-cover mapping can extend a survey-based count across unsurveyed parts of the area, where the survey is a probability sample of the declared boundary, and observe a few visible practices such as residue retention, but only as calibration input tied to ground observation: area is estimated from the reference classification of a probability sample of ground observations, with its uncertainty reported, and is not read off the map. A satellite-derived figure is never a standalone value. Not applicable DS4 (Secondary and international databases): third-party statistics cannot observe which land carries a CIMMYT-promoted practice inside a project boundary. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated and other non-traditional data): the indicator needs verified practice status matched to measured areas inside a defined boundary, which crowdsourced observations cannot supply. Across every route: a projected or modelled hectare estimate may not be reported as the value. An impact indicator counts realised benefit, and a projected area is a projection of adoption rather than an observation of it. Extrapolation from a probability sample of the declared boundary to that boundary is permitted, because that is sampling and not projection, and the sampling basis is reported with the value.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role this project used, Recommended or Fallback; if Fallback, why direct collection was not feasible. Example: "Used Recommended: plot-level survey of 1,200 participant households with GPS-measured plot areas; the value is the qualifying area on participants' land and is not extended to non-participants."
collectionInstrument: DS1 route: a plot-level practice module recording, per plot, the practices applied in the reporting year (from the promoted list, with an open category), the plot area and how it was measured, the hectare type, the farming system, and the sex and age of the plot manager. Respondent: the plot manager. Mode: face-to-face interview, with plot visit and GPS measurement where feasible; communal areas via key-informant interview with the managing body plus mapped boundaries. The cultivated-land rows of this same module are what KPI-OC33's numerator is read from, so the two indicators are read from one round of this instrument and neither is collected independently of the other. Fallback route (DS2): no instrument; the record states the area, the basis of the recorded area, and the last spot-check date.
collectionFrequency: Annually, after the main cropping season, when the year's practice use is observable. Short projects may measure at baseline and endline only; the value then describes those two points and no trend between them.
reportingFrequency: Annually. Between measurement rounds the latest measured value is carried forward with its year of measurement noted.
referencePeriod: The reporting year (12 months), with a hectare qualifying on a practice applied at any point in it. A snapshot: it describes land under improved management in that year only, and successive annual values are neither summed nor averaged.
baselineRequired: Yes. The baseline is the area already under the promoted practices at project start, rarely zero; practices found already widespread are removed from the list and the baseline recalculated. Fallbacks where no prospective baseline exists: reconstruct practice use by recall in the first survey round, or take the first reporting-year value as baseline and state the substitution. If neither is feasible: monitoring only, no change claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Across projects: sum Recommended-sourced values directly; a Fallback-sourced project is reported alongside the total with a note, not blended in.

B: Combination method. Sum hectares across contributing projects after de-duplication; the institutional figure is a total area, never an average.

C: Levels and operations. A qualifying area in hectares, summed at every level and de-duplicated before each sum, never a count of farms or holdings. At Farm / Plot, the qualifying area of that holding. At project level, the sum of those areas after de-duplicating on the plot identifier per Block E, since one hectare under two practices is one hectare and not two. At institutional level, the sum across projects on the same basis, de-duplicated again, because intervention areas overlap and adding project figures would count shared ground twice. Where plot identities cannot be reconciled across projects, the institutional figure is labelled an upper estimate. Also report: the practice breakdown, the basis on which area was measured (ground survey, delineation or producer statement), the area excluded under Eligibility, and the number of contributing projects.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: No. The value does not combine arithmetically with the pathway's outputs (KPI-O30, KPI-O31) or with KPI-OC33, whose numerator is this total's cultivated-land component expressed as a share of cultivated land, so adding them would count the same land twice; the levels connect through the Theory of Change not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: the count is of unique physical hectares, so where intervention areas overlap, de-duplicate by plot identifier or mapped boundary before summing, and where that is impossible label the total an upper estimate. Named overlap risks: KPI-OC33, whose numerator hectares are the cultivated-land part of this total and are therefore already inside it; and KPI-OC36 and KPI-I12 in the Resilience & climate pathway, which can legitimately cover the same hectare qualifying here as climate-resilient management. Neither is ever summed with this indicator. Coverage and precision travel with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands used in official statistics: 16.5 per cent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 per cent released flagged, above 33.3 per cent not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one deduplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above, and a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place. On this sheet a record is one plot determination for the reporting year, on the unique-hectare basis Block C requires.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: inside the project's declared CIMMYT intervention area, individually managed cultivated land; demonstration plots cultivated by participating farmers; communally managed rangeland, conservation areas and freshwater or marine ecosystems, reported as association-applied; practices newly adopted and practices continued from earlier years, if applied in the reporting year.

Exclusion: researcher-managed and research-station plots; land outside the boundary; practices already in general use before the intervention, removed from the promoted list so pre-existing habits do not inflate the value.

Missing data: land of undetermined status is left out rather than imputed, making the value a conservative undercount; report the share of the area with determined status alongside it.

Repeated observations: each hectare counts once per reporting year, whatever the number of practices or cycles it carries, on the same unique-hectare basis as KPI-OC33. Where several people cultivate one plot, divide the area between them before assigning sex and age categories.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only. Land management also responds to prices, tenure security, labour availability, weather and other programmes, and without a comparison group the counterfactual is unknown.

Counts land under a promoted practice, not verified environmental improvement, and no threshold sets how much improvement qualifies: a large area weakly improved and a small area deeply improved enter the same total, a limitation another CGIAR centre records against the same indicator. Pair with the pathway's condition indicators (soil organic carbon, nutrient-use efficiency, water intensity, pesticide intensity) before claiming land is managed more sustainably.

Measurement error runs both ways: farmer-reported practice use is inflated by courtesy bias toward the promoting organisation, farmer-estimated areas are systematically inaccurate and satellite-derived areas carry classification bias unless ground-calibrated, while land of undetermined status is excluded rather than imputed, pushing the value down.

Comparability is only as good as the practice lists and boundaries behind the values: a change in either moves the number with nothing changing on the ground, and projects promote different packages. Report such changes with the value.

A rise means more land carried at least one promoted practice that year. It does not mean the practices persisted, that whole farms converted, that CIMMYT caused the change, or that soil, water or biodiversity condition improved. Annual values are snapshots of the same land, not new area each year, and are never summed.
subMetrics:
None. Practice-type and hectare-type breakdowns are disaggregations of one measurement, not separately calculated metrics.

Neighbouring sheets: KPI-OC33, the outcome level below this indicator, a rate over cultivated land whose numerator is this indicator's cultivated-land component, meaning the crop-land and cultivated-pasture hectare types of the required cut and none of the other three; KPI-O30 / KPI-O31 (solution packages validated / deployed), the outputs whose uptake this area measures; KPI-OC36 and KPI-I12 in the Resilience & climate pathway, which overlap the climate-resilient clause.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E team and enumerators (plot survey, area measurement, communal-area key informants); project technical team (practice list, boundary). Validation: project MEAL officer, including the de-duplication check against neighbouring projects. Calculation: project MEAL officer for the project total; CIMMYT MEAL unit for de-duplication and summing across projects. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit, which reports the institutional total into CGIAR portfolio reporting.
sourceRef: Volume 9 · Environmental sustainability — Reference sheet KPI-I10

name: MRV-verified soil and biomass carbon sequestration (tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent)
resultsLevel: Impact
primaryObjective: PO4 Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient. Contributing objectives: none; the register lists PO4 alone.
cgiarImpactArea: Climate Adaptation & Mitigation
sdgTarget: None. No SDG indicator measures project-level carbon sequestration. The nearest is SDG indicator 13.2.2 (total greenhouse gas emissions per year, target 13.2), a national annual total in megatonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent compiled from country submissions to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, reported with and without land use, land-use change and forestry. It is not a project-level removals figure.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Common Results Framework, climate adaptation and mitigation impact indicator "tonnes carbon dioxide equivalent"; this KPI operationalises the sequestration side of it, which CGIAR's own review found needs exactly this clarification. FAO Global Soil Partnership RECSOIL scheme. ISO 14064-2:2019 and ISO 14064-3:2019, where the gain is reported as a quantified removal enhancement with an independent verification statement.
definition: The carbon, in tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, additionally stored in soil and woody biomass across CIMMYT intervention areas over the verification interval being reported, beyond what would have been stored without the intervention: a difference from the business-as-usual baseline, not a finding of crediting additionality unless the verifying standard tested it. Only carbon measured, reported and verified under an MRV protocol counts, verification meaning third-party verification against a recognised carbon-crediting or greenhouse-gas accounting standard by a body accredited under it and independent of those who monitored and reported, with standard and verifier named against the value. Sequestration is a flow, net of the change business as usual would have produced.
rationale: Answers how much climate mitigation CIMMYT's work on soils, cropping systems and trees on farms has contributed to, in the one unit donors, national inventories and carbon markets all recognise. Because it is verified against a baseline by an independent party, it is the only indicator in this pathway that can carry a defensible mitigation claim; the practice-adoption and soil-condition indicators feeding it cannot.
projectSpecificApplication: State the MRV protocol followed and who verifies, the intervention areas and their hectares, the pools included, the baseline year and monitoring round dates, and whether the value is measured or modelled. Do not change the pools counted, the netting rule, the conversion factor or the unit. If verification cannot be arranged within the project cycle, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than reporting an unverified estimate as the verified value; the measured sequestration is still reported, labelled unverified and outside the verified headline.
projectSpecificRationale: State the commitment the value serves: a donor mitigation target in tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, a national contribution or land-restoration reporting obligation, or a results-based finance agreement whose disbursement depends on it.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.  Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure.
unit: Tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) over the verification interval; where a rate is needed, that value divided by the hectares it rests on and by the interval's years (tCO2e per hectare per year).
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more carbon dioxide equivalent was sequestered and verified under an MRV protocol.
disaggregationRequired: Required: carbon pool (soil organic carbon; above-ground woody biomass; below-ground woody biomass) and intervention area, each as gross removals, since the deductions are project terms and are divided neither between pools nor between areas; and measurement basis (measured or modelled, verified or unverified). A value whose biomass term rests on Earth observation (Fallback DS3) is modelled, since imagery yields biomass only through a calibrated model. A total that hides the pools counted and how they were established is not comparable with another project's. The register records no required disaggregation, so these three are adopted as required. Sex and age are not applicable: the unit of observation is a sampling location, not a person.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Practice package (conservation agriculture, residue retention, agroforestry, cover cropping); country and agroecological zone; soil type; irrigated or rainfed; years since adoption.
unitOfObservation: Plot (the sampling or inventory location and its stratum within a delineated intervention area)
calculationSummary: Value = the sum, across all intervention areas and included pools, of the net additional carbon stock change over the verification interval, converted to carbon dioxide equivalent. Soil pool: the difference between the intervention-scenario stock and the business-as-usual stock at the round being reported, minus the same difference at the previous verified round (zero at baseline), in t C/ha, multiplied by each area's hectares and by 44/12. Both soil terms are on KPI-OC27's equivalent soil mass basis and reference mass; a business-as-usual term at fixed depth is converted before differencing, and the conversion is stated. Biomass pools, woody biomass only (trees on farms, agroforestry and perennial woody crops): the difference between carbon stocks measured at the previous verified round and the round being reported (stock-difference method) or annual gains minus annual losses (gain-loss method), converted the same way. Project greenhouse-gas emissions are then subtracted: the increase in emissions under the intervention relative to business as usual inside the boundary, with the tier per source stated, on KPI-I09's inventory basis, reported as a named term; a decrease is not added, since it belongs to KPI-I09. Leakage means indirect greenhouse-gas emissions or soil organic carbon losses occurring outside the project's boundaries but still attributable to its activities. The method of record does not estimate leakage; a project that generates land-use-change leakage is not eligible (see Eligibility), and a quantified deduction is made only where the project's crediting or accounting standard defines one, in which case the amount and the standard that set it are reported beside the figure. Other potential sources of leakage are identified and stated with the value in words. The reported figure is net of both terms on this basis, never gross removals, whatever the protocol's own minimum requires. The value is the net removals as verified, on the verifying standard's global warming potential set, named with the value; where that set is not the 100-year set of the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report, the project-emissions deduction restated on the Sixth Assessment values is reported beside it for reading against KPI-I09 and is not the verified value. Under a crediting standard, the value is the verified net removals after the standard's uncertainty deduction and before withholding to a non-permanence buffer; the buffer withholding and credits issued are reported beside it as named terms. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1: field measurement, soil sampling with laboratory determination of carbon concentration and bulk density plus biomass inventory plots, under the MRV protocol's sampling design. The only source that observes the carbon itself. Recommended DS2 alongside it, since neither alone produces the indicator: project management and activity records, supplying the historic and intervention activity data the baseline scenario and the carbon model require, plus the verification records and statement. Fallback DS4 with DS2: a carbon model (RothC, Century, DNDC, or the IPCC Tier 2 steady-state method) or an ex-ante carbon balance tool, driven by project activity data and secondary climate and soil datasets where a full measurement round is not feasible, so that the intervention-area stock change itself is modelled; always labelled as modelled. A business-as-usual term modelled under the verifying standard's own method, against intervention-area stocks measured at baseline and at the round reported, is part of the Recommended route and does not make a value modelled; where any intervention area has no stock measured at baseline, a modelled business-as-usual term is on this Fallback route and the value is modelled. Recommended DS1 for area: the boundary of each intervention area walked on the ground as a georeferenced polygon. Recommended DS3 for area: the boundary of each intervention area delineated on satellite imagery, which measures the hectares the Calculation method multiplies. Fallback DS3: Earth observation tracking woody biomass, permitted for carbon estimation only with evidence of local calibration. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced and other non-traditional data cannot produce laboratory-grade carbon determinations or a statement an independent verifier would accept.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State the route each term of the value rests on (soil, woody biomass, area and, where modelled, the business-as-usual term), Recommended or Fallback, name the verifying entity, and state whether the value was verified. For a term on a Fallback, say why it could not be taken on the Recommended route.
collectionInstrument: Soil pool: a stratified sampling plan following the MRV protocol's soil sampling sub-protocol, depths 0 to 10 cm and 10 to 30 cm, bulk density on the same layers, georeferenced locations so points can be revisited, laboratory determination by dry combustion (preferred) or wet oxidation, same method and preferably same laboratory across rounds. Biomass pools: permanent inventory plots recording species and diameter at breast height, converted with allometric equations and a carbon fraction, below-ground biomass from a root-to-shoot ratio. Verification: an accredited entity independent of the above.
collectionFrequency: Soil pool: complete round at baseline and at least every four years, with model-based updates every two years. Biomass pools: inventory at baseline and at each monitoring round. Verification: at each round for which a value is claimed.
reportingFrequency: Annually. A verified increment is reported in the year its verification is completed; in the years between verified rounds the last verified figure is shown with its verification year and is not a new increment, so annual figures are never summed. An interim modelled estimate may sit alongside it, labelled as such, and is never a verified value.
referencePeriod: The verification interval: the years between the previous verified round (the baseline, for the first round) and the round being reported. A measured soil figure covers at least four years, the shortest interval KPI-OC27 reports.
baselineRequired: Yes, and not substitutable: the indicator is net additional carbon relative to a baseline, so without one there is no value to report. Fallbacks where no prospective baseline exists: a business-as-usual scenario reconstructed from five years of documented historic activity data, the protocol's standard baseline period, or a paired business-as-usual field in the same soil and climate stratum sampled at the same time. If neither is feasible, monitor carbon stocks as a state and report no sequestration.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One verifying protocol and one permanence condition; weight: none, verified tonnes are summed. (2) Across projects: sum verified Recommended-sourced values directly; modelled values, including values whose biomass term rests on Earth observation, and unverified values sit alongside the pooled figure with a note, never blended in.

B: Combination method. Sum within each combination of verifying protocol and permanence condition, never an average. The institutional figure is published as one net total per protocol and permanence condition, naming both, with each pool's gross removals and the deductions for project emissions and, where the standard defines one, leakage beside it as components; no total across protocols is published. The institutional figure for a year is the sum of the increments whose verification completed in that year; a carried-forward figure is shown per project and never enters it.

C: Levels and operations. A verified quantity adds. At site or project level, the tCO2e verified under the MRV protocol for the verification interval, on the area and the pools the protocol covers. At institutional level, the sum across projects after de-duplicating on the site identifier per Block E, within the pooling domain of Block A. Quantities verified under different protocols or permanence assumptions are never pooled, because a tonne with a hundred-year permanence condition and a tonne without one are not the same tonne. Also report: the protocol and its version, the pools included, the permanence and reversal conditions, the area the figure rests on, and the value's measurement basis (measured or modelled, verified or unverified).

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: no. It does not sum with the soil organic carbon change indicator feeding it, which is the same soil carbon expressed per hectare rather than as total removals, nor with hectares under improved management; those levels connect as a theory-of-change narrative, and the same physical carbon is counted once.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: the risk is hectares and claims, not people. De-duplicate by the georeferenced boundaries of intervention areas before summing; never add a cumulative total to the interval increments composing it; and where a credit for the same carbon has been sold, retired or transferred, report it and flag the double claim, naming the holder, and never exclude it; the host country's national inventory is not a double claim. Where boundaries or external claims cannot be resolved, label the total an upper estimate. Carbon counted as a removal here is never also netted off KPI-I09's numerator, which reports gross field emissions; that sheet states the same prohibition from its own side, and the pair of statements is what stops one tonne being counted twice. Coverage and precision are inherited rather than restated: this value is a derived quantity, a net stock change, so it carries no floor of its own and every value entering it must itself have been releasable under the Block E that produced it. The soil term is read from KPI-OC27's per-hectare measurement and is releasable on that sheet's bands; on the modelled Fallback route no KPI-OC27 value exists, and the value sits beside the pooled figure with the model's validation evidence in place of a release band. The biomass term this sheet measures directly is released on the same coefficient-of-variation bands at Project area level and above, a record being one permanent inventory plot measured in one round. A biomass term from Earth observation (Fallback DS3) sits beside the pooled figure with its local calibration evidence in place of a release band. Report the number of rounds, the area basis and the share of the area with a valid measurement with every figure at Project area level and above.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusions: hectares inside delineated intervention areas with a documented baseline, an eligible practice in place since that baseline, and completed independent verification for the verification interval.

Exclusions: areas with no baseline; areas whose land use changed during the interval; unverified gains, reported separately; and projects that generate land-use-change leakage, or expect to, which are not eligible for this indicator, since land-use-change leakage is an eligibility test and not a deduction. Documented reversals are subtracted. Where a credit for the same carbon has been sold, retired or transferred, the hectares are reported and the claim flagged, naming the holder: excluding them would understate what CIMMYT's work achieved, and reporting them silently would contribute to double counting. That the removal also falls within the host country's national inventory is expected, is stated once with the value, and is not a double claim.

Missing data: no imputation; a stratum or plot without a valid measurement is dropped, its hectares removed from the area basis, and coverage stated.

Repeated observations: each hectare counts once per verification interval. The headline is the verified increment for the interval, reported in the year its verification completes and labelled with the interval it covers. In a year with no newly verified round, no new verified value is reported: the last verified increment is shown, labelled carried forward with its interval, and is never summed with another year's figure. A multi-year total is the sum of the increments of non-overlapping intervals; the cumulative total since baseline is reported alongside, labelled cumulative. The two are published together and never substituted for one another.
limitations: Verification is the binding constraint, and it has a strict meaning: whoever monitors and reports cannot also verify. Most CIMMYT projects do not fund independent verification, so a low value may reflect a missing verifier rather than missing sequestration.

Additional means additional to a constructed counterfactual, built from historic activity data and, for the soil pool, usually from a model. The figure is only as credible as that counterfactual and that model choice, and it supports a contribution claim, not proof of what would otherwise have happened.

Sequestration is neither permanent nor a carbon credit. Gains reverse if practices lapse, soil carbon saturates as stocks approach equilibrium, and a tonne verified here is not tradeable unless generated under a crediting standard.

Comparability breaks easily. Protocols differ in the pools they count and in gross versus net treatment, measured and modelled values are different quantities, and soil measurement detects change only over several years. State the protocol, pools, interval and measurement basis with every figure.

A rise means more carbon was verifiably held in the soils and woody biomass of the measured areas than the counterfactual holds, net of the emissions caused in achieving it. It does not mean CIMMYT's practices caused all of it, that the gain is permanent, or that a tonne here can be sold or offset against an emission elsewhere; and a fall may be a lapsed practice, a saturating stock, or a verifier who could not be engaged. Pair it with the practice-adoption and soil-carbon indicators for the contribution narrative.

ISO 14064-2:2019 (project-level quantification, monitoring and reporting of greenhouse gas emission reductions and removal enhancements) and ISO 14064-3:2019 (validation and verification of greenhouse gas statements). No link.

name: Agrobiodiversity index score
resultsLevel: Impact. It measures the condition of an ecological system, the longer-term change the pathway's outcomes contribute to, and reports into a CGIAR impact area as a state-of-environment measure. The register rolls two outcomes into it: change in pesticide intensity (KPI-OC31) and institutions integrating biodiversity considerations into plans or policies (KPI-OC34).
primaryObjective: PO4 Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient. Contributing objective: PO2 Food and nutrition security in the global south is ensured within planetary boundaries, contribution only, since crop and species diversity in production underpins dietary diversity and the planetary-boundary condition PO2 attaches to food security.
cgiarImpactArea: Environmental Health & Biodiversity
sdgTarget: None (direct). No SDG indicator is a composite agrobiodiversity score. The nearest correspondence is a supplementary series of SDG indicator 2.4.1 under target 2.4, "proportion of agricultural land area that has achieved an acceptable or desirable level of use of agro-biodiversity supportive practices", which scores farms against a checklist of biodiversity-supportive practices at ecosystem, species and genetic level: practice adoption, not the diversity present, so the two are not interchangeable. SDG indicators 2.5.1 (genetic resources secured in conservation facilities) and 2.5.2 (local breeds at risk) concern conserved genetic resources rather than diversity in production; SDG indicator 15.5.1 (Red List Index) concerns wild species extinction risk.
otherFrameworks: Agrobiodiversity Index (Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT): the source of the components, the standardisation and the thresholds, applicable at country, company and project level. Its pillar layer is not applied here, and this indicator's value is not an Agrobiodiversity Index score (see Calculation method). Convention on Biological Diversity: the three levels of biodiversity in agriculture (genetic, production system, ecosystem) that the components span. CGIAR common results framework: no equivalent, its Environmental Health and Biodiversity standard indicators being hectares under improved management, consumptive water use, deforestation, nitrogen application and genebank accessions, none of them a diversity measure.
definition: A single composite score, on a scale of 0 to 100, describing the diversity of crops, varieties, species and habitats present in a defined CIMMYT intervention area during the reference year. Component measurements (for example crop and varietal diversity, species richness, and the share of farmland carrying natural vegetation) are each measured in their own units, converted to a common 0 to 100 scale against fixed lower and upper thresholds, then weighted and averaged into one score. A measurement on which a lower raw value indicates improvement, such as pesticide applied per hectare, is standardised and subtracted from 100 so it points the same way; that score is published beside the index and does not enter it. A higher score means greater agrobiodiversity.
rationale: Answers whether the farming landscapes CIMMYT works in are becoming more, or less, biologically diverse: the long-run environmental result that diversified cropping, improved varieties, conservation agriculture and reduced chemical use are meant to produce together. One score lets very different environmental measures be read side by side over time, and lets CIMMYT report against the CGIAR Environmental Health and Biodiversity impact area with a headline figure rather than a list of unconnected measures.
projectSpecificApplication: State the boundary the score is computed for, the farming systems inside it, the reference year, the survey and land-cover rounds used, and which components the project can populate. The scale, the standardisation rule and the weighting stay unchanged; a project does not redefine the index, it reports which components it filled.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision, donor commitment or reporting need this serves. Example: a landscape diversification project tracks it because a rising score driven only by field-margin vegetation, while crop and varietal diversity stay flat, shows the project changing the landscape around the fields but not what farmers plant in them.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI.  Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work has no field in an intervention area to measure.
unit: Index score, 0 to 100 (dimensionless). Report it with the number of component measurements it was built from, and with the component scores themselves; a composite alone cannot be interpreted.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means greater measured agrobiodiversity inside the boundary.
disaggregationRequired: Required: the component score for every component that entered the index, published alongside the headline value; the composite is not disaggregated by crop, and the varietal-diversity component names the species it is computed for. The register records crop and trait class; neither is meaningful for a landscape-level composite, whose diversity components are computed across species.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Agroecological zone; farming system (irrigated, rainfed, mixed crop-livestock); land-holding size class; component category (varietal diversity, species diversity, habitat) where a project reports several sub-areas.
unitOfObservation: Community. The index is computed for a delineated intervention area or landscape; component measurements are collected at plot and farm level and aggregated to that area before standardisation.
calculationSummary: Value = a standardisation of each component followed by a weighted average of the component scores; each component carries its own arithmetic (see Sub-metrics). Step 1, delineate the intervention area as one fixed boundary, held constant across rounds. Step 2, measure each component in its native unit inside that boundary. Step 3, identify any component on which a lower raw value indicates improvement in agrobiodiversity; the inversion is not performed here but in Step 4, after standardisation. Step 4, standardise each measurement to 0 to 100 against a fixed lower and upper threshold: standardised score = ((M − lower) / (upper − lower)) × 100, where M is the raw measurement; for a component identified in Step 3 the component score is 100 minus that standardised score, which is the reverse-standardisation this index uses throughout. Set thresholds from the theoretical best and worst where the measure has them (0 and 100 percent for a share), otherwise from the best and worst observed in the comparison set, and freeze them for the life of the series. A raw value beyond a frozen threshold is scored at that threshold, 0 or 100, and flagged; thresholds change only with a new series version, never within one. Step 5, the reported value is the mean of the computed core component scores, each at weight 1, following the source methodology, whose sensitivity analysis over 20 countries found weights had very little effect on scores or rankings. Step 5 flattens the source methodology deliberately, and the sheet states it rather than implying otherwise. The source averages indicator scores into three pillar scores first and takes the mean of the three as a "Status" score, while its headline index score is built from the commitment and action pillars and excludes the status pillars. The four core components are status components, so this value is the source's status score computed in one step, not the source's index score, and it is reported under this indicator's own name and never as an Agrobiodiversity Index score. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1 for the diversity components: a farm and plot inventory recording the crop species and varieties grown and the area under each, inside the delineated boundary; the only source resolving varietal composition at the scale the index is computed for. Recommended DS3 for the habitat component: land-cover mapping giving the share of farmland with natural vegetation, which no interview can supply. A project normally uses both, one per component group. Fallback DS2: project, partner or national seed-system records of varieties supplied in the area, for varietal composition where no inventory is feasible, flagged as fallback-sourced, since seed supplied is not seed planted. Fallback DS4: published global datasets (FAOSTAT crop and livestock production for species diversity), only where project measurement is impossible, since they resolve to national or coarse grid level. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced species records are presence-only with unknown sampling effort, so they cannot produce area-weighted diversity measures or a standardised score.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role the project used for each component group, Recommended or Fallback, and if Fallback, why direct measurement was not feasible. A score mixing Recommended and Fallback components is reported with that composition stated.
collectionInstrument: For DS1: a plot-level crop and variety inventory recording, per plot, the species and named variety planted, the area under each and the season, plus a farm-level listing of non-crop habitat features. Respondent: the person who manages the plot and chooses what is planted. Mode: face-to-face interview with plot listing, since variety names are unreliable without plot-by-plot prompting. The Agrobiodiversity Index data gathering questionnaire (Annex 2 of the source methodology) supplies the project-level template. For DS3: geographic information system processing of land-cover products, not an interview instrument.
collectionFrequency: Baseline and endline at a minimum, and every 3 to 5 years for long programmes: crop, varietal and habitat composition change slowly, so annual measurement mostly returns sampling noise. Land-cover components may be refreshed annually where satellite products allow, but the composite is recomputed only when all its components are refreshed.
reportingFrequency: Annually; between measurement waves the latest computed score is carried forward with its year of measurement noted.
referencePeriod: One full cropping year inside the fixed boundary, compared against the same window in the baseline year. Land-cover components describe the same year.
baselineRequired: Yes. The score is interpretable only as a movement, and a movement is real only if the component set and thresholds are identical in both years; rescaling thresholds mid-series creates change that did not happen. Fallbacks where no baseline was computed at project start: reconstruct the habitat component from archived satellite imagery for the pre-intervention year and the crop and varietal components from a recall inventory of the pre-intervention season, both flagged as reconstructed; or score a matched comparison landscape in the same round and report a difference between areas rather than over time. If neither is feasible: report the score as a level, monitoring only, with no change claim.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool Recommended-sourced scores directly; a project that used a Fallback for any component is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note on which components were fallback-sourced, not blended in. A value built against a matched comparison area is a between-area difference, not a change over time: it is reported beside the pooled change with a note and never pooled with it.

B: Combination method. Index scores are never summed. The source methodology defines the index for a single area and sets no pooling rule, so this pooling convention is CIMMYT's and is stated as such: pool as a mean of area-level scores weighted by agricultural land area, only across areas scored with the same components and thresholds. Scores built on different component sets are listed separately, not averaged.

C: Levels and operations. The index is computed once, at the level its components are defined for, and no average of index scores is ever presented as an index for the wider area: a mean of index scores is not an index, because the components carry different weights and denominators beneath it. The one figure that is an average of scores is the cross-area pooled value of Blocks A and B, which is reported as an area-weighted mean of area-level scores and labelled as that, never as this index computed for the wider area. Where a lower-level figure is wanted it is recomputed from that level's own components, never read off the wider score. Also report: the component values with the score, the version of the scale in force, the sampling design each component rests on, and any component that was unavailable and how it was treated, since a composite with a silent missing component is not comparable with one that has all of them.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This value does not combine arithmetically with the outcomes beneath it, change in pesticide intensity (KPI-OC31) and institutions integrating biodiversity considerations (KPI-OC34); they connect through the theory of change as a narrative.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: two projects in the same landscape must not each contribute a score for it, so delineate one union boundary and compute a single score. The same hectares also appear in hectares under improved management (KPI-I10) and cultivated land under sustainable practices (KPI-OC33), different constructs on a shared land base that must never be added to this score. Where boundaries cannot be reconciled, label the pooled figure indicative. Coverage and precision travel with every figure at Project area level and above, on the coefficient-of-variation bands used in official statistics: 16.5 per cent or below released without qualification, above 16.5 to 33.3 per cent released flagged, above 33.3 per cent not released as an estimate. The bands apply only to estimates built on at least 30 records, a record being one deduplicated observation unit of the pooling domain, counted per period; below 30 the estimate is not released. The floor binds only where the bands do, at Project area level and above, and a derived quantity carries no floor of its own. Coefficients of variation are read to one decimal place. On this sheet a record is one plot or farm inventory observation of a component, counted per component; the composite is a derived quantity and carries no floor of its own, and the pesticide score published beside it, drawn from KPI-OC31, must itself have been releasable there.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: all land and production inside the project's declared CIMMYT intervention area in the reference year.

Exclusion: land outside that boundary, and any component with no fixed threshold pair, which cannot be standardised. Thresholds are set centrally by the CIMMYT MEAL unit for all projects and frozen for the life of the series, never derived per project from local best and worst values: local thresholds would make every project's score a comparison with itself, so the same score would mean something different in each place and could never be pooled or compared.

Missing data: a component with no data is dropped from the mean rather than scored zero (a zero reads as absent diversity, not absent measurement), and the count of contributing components is reported with the value. A headline composite is published only where at least three of the four core components (crop species richness, crop species diversity, varietal diversity, habitat) are computable; below that the components are published on their own and no headline score is given, because a two-component composite is not the same construct as a four-component one and must not carry the same name. The two optional components are published beside the headline and never enter it.

Repeated observations: a plot, farm or landscape unit measured more than once in a reference period enters once, using the round designated for that reporting year.
limitations: A composite hides its parts. Very different landscapes can reach the same score, and a rise driven by field-margin vegetation while varietal diversity falls is not the change intended. Never publish the score without its component scores and the count of components used.

The value depends on choices made outside the measurement. Thresholds drawn from observed values depend on the comparison set, which is why they are frozen for the life of the series, and dropping an unmeasured component changes the mean, so two scores are comparable only if built from the same components with the same frozen thresholds. Weighting matters less: the source methodology's sensitivity test found weights had little effect on scores or rankings. Two of the four core components measure crop species, so species diversity carries half the equal-weight composite.

Supports a contribution claim only. Agrobiodiversity responds to prices, land pressure, market demand for uniform produce, policy and climate. CIMMYT is one influence among these, and its own work often puts improved varieties on more land, which can lower some components while raising others.

Measurement error concentrates in the varietal component: farmers misname varieties, recycled and mixed seed lots blur variety boundaries, and area shares are estimated rather than surveyed. It is the least reliable input and is checked against seed-system records where they exist.

A rise means more measured diversity inside the boundary that year. It does not mean better yields, diets, resilience or income, and it is not evidence of species conservation in the wider ecosystem. Read it with productivity and food-security indicators before drawing a system conclusion.
subMetrics:
The index is composed of separately calculated component measurements. The set below is the standard construction from the source methodology; the four core components and their equal weights are adopted here. Each is standardised by the Step 4 formula before entering the index.

— Crop species richness: count of crop species grown in the delineated area during the reference year.

— Species diversity in production: Shannon index over the area shares of each species, H = −Σ pi ln pi, where pi is the share of production area under species i. The source methodology uses Shannon where pre-calculated diversity values exist and Gini-Simpson elsewhere.

— Varietal diversity: Gini-Simpson index over the area shares of each variety within the main species, 1 − Σ pi². Varieties are recorded by their released-variety identifier where the country's release catalogue supplies one, and by farmer-reported name with the catalogue match stated where it does not, so the component is traceable to the varieties CIMMYT breeds and releases rather than to a name recorded at interview.

— Habitat quality (landscape complexity): percentage of agricultural land in the area carrying more than 10 percent natural vegetation, from land-cover data, computed over grid cells of one stated size, frozen with the thresholds for the life of the series. Narrow features such as field margins and hedgerows need a land-cover product of 10 m resolution or finer; a coarser product measures landscape-scale habitat only.

— Underutilised or local species (optional): share of production area under species outside the 15 globally dominant food species. Published beside the headline; never a component of it.

— Avoided over-use of chemical control (optional, inverted): drawn from KPI-OC31, which has its own reference sheet. The source methodology's measurement table defines this measurement as 100 divided by kilograms of pesticides per hectare, which is the inversion it applies here; its standardisation section states only that negatively-associated measurements are pointed in the same direction and sets no general inversion formula. CIMMYT does not adopt that expression: it is unbounded above and undefined where pesticide use is zero, so a project that eliminates pesticides could not report the component and one that halves an already low rate would double it. The rule this sheet applies is therefore the Step 4 standardisation run in reverse: the component is standardised against its fixed lower and upper thresholds and the standardised score is subtracted from 100, which is bounded, defined at zero use, and consistent with the 0-to-100 scale the rest of the index is built on. This is a stated divergence from the source's measurement expression, not a gap in the source, and no institutional inversion rule beyond it is claimed. Published beside the headline; never a component of it.

Crop species richness and species diversity are computed on a fixed sampling effort, the same number of randomly selected plots in every area and round, stated with the value; values built on unequal effort are not pooled or compared.

Related sheets: KPI-OC31 and KPI-OC34, the outcomes the register rolls up into this indicator; KPI-I10 and KPI-OC33, sustainable land management on the same hectares.

Method: Bioversity International (2018), The Agrobiodiversity Index: Methodology report, indicator framework; status indicator types and the alpha, beta and gamma diversity distinction; Gini-Simpson and Shannon calculation rules; inversion, thresholds, the standardisation formula, indicator and pillar scores and the weight-of-1 sensitivity result; measurement list and data sources for the country and project applications.

FAOSTAT, Crops and livestock products (QCL) data domain, FAO: national production and area series, the DS4 species-diversity fallback. https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/QCL

ESA Climate Change Initiative land cover, European Space Agency: the land-cover layer for the DS3 habitat component. https://www.esa-landcover-cci.org/

Strategic mandate: CIMMYT (2023), Science and Innovation for a Food and Nutrition Secure World, PO4 and PO2 mapping.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E team and enumerators for the crop and variety inventory; project or CIMMYT geospatial analyst for the land-cover component. Validation: project MEAL officer, checking boundary consistency across rounds, variety naming, and that thresholds match the baseline. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, which holds the component set, thresholds and weights so that scores stay comparable across projects. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
