name: Number of agroecosystem or land-use decision-support tools or assessments delivered to decision-makers
resultsLevel: Output. A tool or assessment delivered to decision-makers is a delivered result of the research team. Whether decision-makers act on it is the outcome question, answered by KPI-OC37, not by this count.
primaryObjective: PO4 Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient. Contributing: PO5 (Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities).
cgiarImpactArea: Recorded per tool or assessment and reported as a distribution, under the pathway-wide rule. An agroecosystem or land-management tool serves Environmental Health & Biodiversity; a climate decision-support product serves Climate Adaptation & Mitigation, so the tag varies by item as what is measured varies by item. No single value is forced on the indicator.
sdgTarget: None. SDG indicators 2.4.1 (area under productive and sustainable agriculture) and 15.3.1 (proportion of degraded land) measure land condition and practice at country level, not evidence instruments an organisation delivers; no SDG indicator directly corresponds to this count.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Technical Reporting: products of this kind are reported under the CGIAR Results Framework's output result types as Knowledge Products or Innovation Development outputs (with an innovation readiness level). The nearest CGIAR standard indicator, the count of other information products published in the reporting year, counts publications rather than tools handed to a defined user, so this is a CIMMYT-defined indicator feeding those CGIAR categories.
definition: Counts the agroecosystem or land-use decision-support tools or assessments CIMMYT delivers to decision-makers in the reporting year; counts distinct tools or assessments handed to a defined user. A decision-support tool is an instrument that turns data or evidence into an actionable recommendation for a specific agroecosystem or land-use decision, for example crop-suitability targeting, land-use planning, or choosing among sustainable intensification options. An assessment is a structured, documented evaluation of an agroecosystem or land-use question (a land-suitability assessment, a trade-off or targeting analysis) prepared for a named decision-maker. A product counts once it is finalised and handed to a defined user with authority to act on it.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT is putting usable agroecosystem and land-use evidence instruments into the hands of the people who decide how land is managed: the countable entry point of the evidence-to-policy results chain leading to public policies, strategies, and regulations informed by CIMMYT evidence (KPI-OC37) and, beyond that, to enacted policies that support smallholder resilience (KPI-I15). Used by project management to track delivery against workplans and by institutional and donor reporting to evidence CIMMYT's contribution to sustainable, climate-resilient agrifood systems.
projectSpecificApplication: State which tools or assessments the project delivers, the agroecosystem or land-use decision each one supports, the countries covered, and the defined user of each. Do not change the unit, the delivery test, or the counting rule. If applying the indicator as defined is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count informs (for example, a donor-required deliverable count for a land-use planning component, or an internal milestone trigger: if planned tools are not delivered by a set date, the workplan and partner arrangements are reviewed).
projectTypesNotApplicable: none. Any project type can produce a decision-support tool
projectTypesRaw: Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI. Not applicable: none. Any project type can produce a decision-support tool.
unit: Number (count of distinct tools or assessments)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more agroecosystem or land-use decision-support tools or assessments were handed to a defined user.
disaggregationRequired: Required: product type, using the two categories in the definition (decision-support tool, assessment). The register currently records no required disaggregation for this indicator; this requirement is set on the sheet's authority.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country or region; decision scale the product serves (farm, landscape or watershed, national); decision-maker type (national or local government, extension service, research or academic, private sector, civil society or community); agroecosystem or land-use theme covered (for example soil and land management, crop suitability, land-use planning).
unitOfObservation: The delivered tool or assessment itself. This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct agroecosystem or land-use decision-support tools or assessments CIMMYT delivered, alone or with partners, and handed to their defined users within the reporting year. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: CIMMYT project output and deliverable registries logging each tool or assessment, its delivery date, defined user, the decision it supports, and the evidence of delivery (a dated handover, release or launch record naming the receiving user), cross-checked against project technical reports. Fallback DS4: recipient or partner records (a ministry's published tool catalogue, a partner's handover record), each counted only where it names the receiving user, used to reconstruct the count where CIMMYT's own delivery log is incomplete; any value built this way is flagged as fallback-sourced, because external records do not authoritatively document CIMMYT's contribution. Not applicable DS1: this indicator counts institutional deliverables from records, not data collected from respondents. Not applicable DS3: satellite or GIS data may be an input inside a delivered tool (a land-suitability map), but that describes the tool's content, not how this count is measured. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or citizen-generated data cannot verify an institutional delivery.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which route each tool or assessment rests on; for any on the Fallback, state why the project's own delivery log was incomplete and which external records were used.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). The registry entry itself is the record: each entry names the tool or assessment, product type, delivery date, defined user, the decision and geography it covers, and the evidence of delivery.
collectionFrequency: Continuous: each delivery is logged as it occurs
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the tool or assessment was first handed to its defined user. The reporting year is the calendar year, register-wide.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual flow count that starts from zero each reporting year; there is no pre-project stock of delivered products to measure. Change over time is read from the annual series itself.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: sum the tools and assessments evidenced in projects' own delivery registries (Recommended); a tool or assessment evidenced only in external records (Fallback) is reported alongside the summed figure with a note, not blended in, and the same project's Recommended-sourced products are summed.

B: Combination method. Summed: the institutional figure is the sum of distinct tools or assessments across all reporting projects in the year, after de-duplication. Never average project-level counts.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying decision-support tools or assessments for the reporting year. At institutional level, the deduplicated sum of those counts, computed from the records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one tool is often reported by more than one project. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels: a tool has no plot and no household, so the levels here are reporting levels. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the split between tools and assessments, the number excluded under Eligibility and why, and the number of tools and assessments reported alongside because they rest on the Fallback.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count does not combine arithmetically with KPI-OC37 or KPI-I15; the three connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative: decision-support products delivered, policies informed, policies enacted.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: two named risks. Within this indicator, a product co-delivered by two CIMMYT projects, or rolled out in several countries, carries one institutional product identifier and counts once, with country coverage as a disaggregation; if identifiers cannot be matched, label the sum an upper estimate. Across the register, the same deliverable may also qualify under KPI-O39 (policy-relevant evidence products, syntheses, or decision-support tools delivered to policymakers and global fora), KPI-O33 (transdisciplinary or participatory research products), KPI-O41 (anticipatory-action, early-warning, or crisis-response tools), or KPI-O01 (innovations co-developed with partners). The boundary with KPI-O39 is subject versus audience: a product with a specific agroecosystem or land-use focus counts here whoever receives it, and where the same product is delivered to a policy audience it also counts under KPI-O39, for a different reason. The two are never summed, and the shared product identifier must mark a product counted in both so the institutional roll-up never presents one product as two achievements.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: a product counts when finalised and handed to a defined user, evidenced by a dated handover record, release record or operational launch record that names the receiving user; a publication record naming no receiving user evidences availability, not delivery. Co-delivered products count once, with CIMMYT's contribution documented.

Exclusion: products still under development, internal pilots not yet handed over, routine re-issues of an already-counted product (the same seasonal advisory re-run), and policy-evidence products without an agroecosystem or land-use focus (those belong to KPI-O39).

Missing data: a logged entry with no evidence of delivery is excluded until the evidence is filed; nothing is counted on intention.

Repeated observations: each distinct product counts once, in the year it is first handed to its user, and is not recounted in later years. A major new version counts again; a rollout to an additional country does not, and is reported as reach against the original.
limitations: Delivery is not use: a tool or assessment logged as delivered may never inform an actual decision, so this count cannot distinguish a land-use planning tool in routine government use from one handed over and shelved. The uptake evidence belongs to KPI-OC37.

"Tool or assessment" spans very different products, from a national land-use planning platform to a single targeting analysis, so raw counts are not comparable across projects until the product-type disaggregation is applied consistently; one widely used tool may matter more than five one-off assessments.

The count is sensitive to logging granularity: splitting one toolkit into components inflates the figure, bundling deflates it. The distinct-product identifier and the delivery-evidence requirement are the controls; read the count together with the product list behind it.

The boundary with KPI-O39 is subject versus audience, so a product can count in both; the shared product identifier is what keeps a combined reading from presenting one product as two, and a product logged under different identities defeats it silently.

An increase means CIMMYT handed more decision-support products to decision-makers, not that land-use decisions or policies improved; pair with KPI-OC37 and KPI-I15 for the results chain, and never present the count alone as evidence of impact.
subMetrics: None. The two product types named in the definition (decision-support tool, assessment) are disaggregations of the same count, not separately calculated metrics. Related indicators in the results chain have their own sheets: KPI-OC37 (public policies, strategies, or regulations informed by CIMMYT-generated evidence, the outcome this output feeds) and KPI-I15 (public policies enacted that support smallholder resilience, the pathway impact).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E focal point, logging each delivery with its evidence. Validation: project MEAL officer, cross-checking the log against project technical reports. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (de-duplication across projects and the institutional sum, per Aggregation rule). Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.

name: Number of transdisciplinary or participatory research products produced to inform agricultural decisions
resultsLevel: Output. A synthesis, analysis or model is a delivered result, a product the research team finalizes. Participation of external actors in producing it does not make it an outcome; no actor outside the team has yet done anything differently. The behavioural change (decision-makers using the evidence) is captured at outcome level by KPI-OC37.
primaryObjective: PO4: Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient. The anchor is sub-objective 4.3 (increased transdisciplinary and participatory research drives evidence-based decision making in the agricultural sector), which this indicator measures directly. Contributing objective: PO5 (global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures), via sub-objective 5.1, foresight on agrifood systems underpins strategic dialogue and informs policy.
cgiarImpactArea: Recorded per product, not one value for the indicator. This count is topic-agnostic: a participatory foresight model may concern climate adaptation, a co-created seed-market synthesis livelihoods, an agroecosystem analysis environmental health, so no single Impact Area is inherent to it. Each product is recorded per product and reported as a distribution, tagged to the Impact Area of its subject at reporting, without a single default for the pathway.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator counts an organization's research or evidence products, so no direct correspondence exists.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Results Framework: Knowledge products is one of the official output result categories in CGIAR technical reporting, defined as an intellectual asset produced by CGIAR as an output of research and development activities, with models, reports, and data tools among the listed examples. Eligible KPI-O33 products therefore also feed CIMMYT's knowledge-product reporting to CGIAR. The correspondence is partial, not direct: CGIAR counts all information products published, while this indicator counts only products that are transdisciplinary or participatory in production and decision-oriented in purpose.
definition: Counts the distinct research products (syntheses, analyses, models) that CIMMYT produces in the reporting year through transdisciplinary or participatory research, with the stated purpose of informing agricultural decisions. Transdisciplinary means the product was developed by integrating several academic disciplines together with the knowledge of non-academic actors (for example farmers, extension services, agribusinesses, or policymakers); participatory means the intended decision-makers or users were directly involved in the product's design or production. Each distinct product counts once, whatever its format or the number of projects that report it. The definition rests on CIMMYT's own authority; no external standard defines this count.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT is producing the co-created, decision-oriented evidence its 2030 Strategy commits it to. Strategy sub-objective 4.3 states that "transdisciplinary and participatory research drive evidence-based decision making in the agricultural sector"; this indicator counts the products that carry that commitment into practice. It is the production end of the pathway’s evidence-to-policy chain: these products are among the inputs behind the outcome indicator KPI-OC37 (public policies, strategies, or regulations informed by CIMMYT-generated evidence). The count shows the volume of decision-oriented evidence produced; whether decisions draw on it is measured at outcome level, not here.
projectSpecificApplication: A project applies the indicator to its own portfolio: it counts the eligible products its teams publish or formally deliver in final form during the reporting year, names the agricultural decisions and decision audiences each product is meant to inform (for example a national fertilizer subsidy review, a seed-sector investment plan, farm-level rotation choices), and keeps the institutional eligibility criteria, unit, and calculation method unchanged. Only the topics, geography, and decision audiences are project-specific.
projectSpecificRationale: A project tracks this indicator to evidence its research-into-use strategy for donors that require co-creation or stakeholder engagement in research design, and to manage its own engagement effort: a low count against plan signals that planned syntheses, analyses, or models are stalled or are being produced without the participatory process the project promised.
projectTypesNotApplicable: none. Any project type can produce a transdisciplinary or participatory research product
projectTypesRaw: Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI. Not applicable: none. Any project type can produce a transdisciplinary or participatory research product.
unit: Number of products (count of distinct eligible research products in the reporting year)
directionOfChange: Increase, read with the volume caveat in section 6 (Limitations and interpretation). A rising value means more transdisciplinary or participatory research products were produced. The count also rises when CIMMYT produces more research overall, so it is read alongside KPI-OC37 before growth is treated as progress toward evidence-based decision making.
disaggregationRequired: Required: product type (synthesis / analysis / model). The register specifies no required disaggregation for this indicator; the requirement is set on this sheet's authority, as KPI-O32 sets its own on identical reasoning, because this sheet's Limitations state the count cannot be read without it.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Decision audience (farmers and farm advisors, national decision-makers, global fora); country or region; crop or farming system; partner type engaged in production.
unitOfObservation: The research product. This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation, whose definition covers a delivered knowledge product alongside innovations, varieties and tools.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct research products published or formally delivered in final form in the reporting year that meet all three eligibility criteria: (a) produced by CIMMYT, alone or with partners; (b) produced through a transdisciplinary or participatory process, evidenced by documentation of non-research actors or intended users engaged in the product's design or production; (c) intended to inform an identifiable agricultural decision or decision audience. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): project M&E records and CIMMYT publication and repository records, logging each product with its identifier, the date it was published or formally delivered in final form, type, decision audience, and the documented evidence of the transdisciplinary or participatory process. Fallback DS4 (Secondary & international databases): CGIAR system-level results-reporting records of CIMMYT knowledge products, used only where project records are incomplete; these capture only products already reported to CGIAR and usually carry no evidence of the participatory process, so a product found there counts only where the process documentation that Eligibility criteria and missing data requires is held; any value built this way is flagged fallback-sourced. Not applicable DS1 (Censuses & surveys): the count is an administrative fact evidenced in records, not a condition reported by survey respondents. Not applicable DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation): the production of research products cannot be observed remotely. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): not a viable record of CIMMYT's own product portfolio.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which route each product rests on. Expected default: Recommended, the project's own M&E product log; for any product found only in CGIAR reporting records, explain why the project's own records were not usable.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source. The indicator is compiled from existing DS2 records, not collected with a DS1 or DS5 instrument.
collectionFrequency: Continuous administrative logging: project teams record each product, its type, decision audience, and process evidence as it is published or formally delivered in final form; compiled once per year.
referencePeriod: The CIMMYT reporting year in which the counting event falls. The counting event is fixed: the date the product is published or formally delivered in final form, whichever comes first, so a product developed across two years is counted exactly once and in one year. The reporting year is the calendar year, register-wide.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual count; the previous year's value is the reference for trend. Where a multi-year trend is wanted, the first year with a complete product log and a stable eligibility test serves as the reference year.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: sum the products evidenced in projects' own M&E and repository records (Recommended); a product evidenced only in CGIAR system-level records (Fallback) is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, not blended silently into it, and the same project's Recommended-sourced products are summed.

B: Combination method. Distinct eligible products are summed across projects and programs after de-duplication by product identifier (DOI, repository handle, or title and year); counts are summed, never averaged.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying transdisciplinary or participatory research products for the reporting year. At institutional level, the deduplicated sum of those counts, computed from the records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one product is often reported by more than one project. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels: a product has no plot and no household, so the levels here are reporting levels. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the participation form each product rests on, the number excluded under Eligibility and why, and the number of products reported alongside because they rest on the Fallback.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no, the default for the whole register. This output count is not added to the outcome indicator KPI-OC37 (policies informed by CIMMYT evidence); they connect through the pathway’s theory of change as a narrative (evidence produced, then evidence used), not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: two named overlap risks inside the indicator group. First, a co-created model or assessment could qualify here and under the register's count of agroecosystem or land-use decision-support tools delivered to decision-makers (KPI-O32); second, a participatory synthesis aimed at policymakers could qualify here and under the register's count of policy-relevant evidence products delivered to policymakers and global fora (KPI-O39). The KPI-O32/KPI-O39 boundary is subject versus audience with dual counting, so one product can legitimately appear in more than one of these counts for different reasons; the three counts are therefore never summed into a single evidence-products total without de-duplication on the shared product identifier, and where identifiers cannot be reconciled any combined figure is labelled an upper estimate. A product co-produced with another CGIAR center is counted once by CIMMYT and flagged as co-produced, so CGIAR-level aggregation can de-duplicate across centers.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion and exclusion: includes syntheses, analyses, and models meeting all three criteria; excludes conventional research publications without a documented participatory or transdisciplinary process; excludes drafts and interim versions; does not exclude a product because it is also counted elsewhere: the test here is the documented participatory or transdisciplinary process, so a product meeting it counts here whether or not the same product is counted as a land-use decision-support tool (KPI-O32) or as an evidence product delivered to a policy audience (KPI-O39), the three counts being de-duplicated rather than summed (see Aggregation rule). An update of an already-counted product is the same product unless it is a substantially new piece of work.
limitations: Output-level only: the count evidences that decision-oriented products were produced, not that any decision-maker read or used them. A product can meet every eligibility criterion and still inform no decision; uptake is measured at outcome level by KPI-OC37, and a rising count with a flat KPI-OC37 signals a production-to-use gap, not success.

Eligibility is a process quality, not a property visible in the product itself: without a consistently applied evidence test for "transdisciplinary or participatory", the count drifts toward counting all knowledge products, and comparability across projects and years depends on every team applying the same test to the same documentation standard.

The units are heterogeneous: a short co-created synthesis and a multi-year participatory foresight model each count as one, so movement in the count reflects the product mix as much as the volume of effort; the required product-type disaggregation is what reads the mix.

The neighbouring counts overlap by design: a product can satisfy this indicator's process test and also count at KPI-O32 for its subject or at KPI-O39 for its audience, so the three are never summed without de-duplication on the shared product identifier. The residual risk is therefore not reclassification between them but inconsistent application of that identifier: where the same product is logged under different identities, de-duplication fails silently and a summed figure overstates production.
subMetrics: None. Syntheses, analyses, and models are product types within the same count (the required disaggregation), not separately calculated metrics. The downstream outcome, public policies, strategies, or regulations informed by CIMMYT evidence, is the separate indicator KPI-OC37 with its own reference sheet.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E teams (product logging with process-evidence documentation). Validation: project MEAL officer (eligibility check against the three criteria). Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (de-duplication and the distinct-product count per the Calculation method). Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 10 · Policy, finance & market systems — Reference sheet KPI-O33

name: Number of market or business-model innovations (sustainable sourcing, inclusive platforms) piloted
resultsLevel: Output. A piloted innovation is a delivered result of an activity the research and project team designs, resources and runs; the behaviour change of external market actors that follows is captured by the outcome indicators of this pathway.
primaryObjective: PO4, Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient. The indicator most directly serves strategic objective 4.4 (market driven systems and emerging models harnessed to improve agrifood systems and their sustainability). Contributing objectives: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved: inclusive platforms create the market opportunities objectives 3.2 and 3.3 call for) and PO5 (Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities: value-adding market models support objective 5.3).
cgiarImpactArea: Recorded per innovation and reported as a distribution, under the pathway-wide rule. A piloted market innovation can serve more than one Impact Area (an inclusive platform: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs; a sustainable sourcing arrangement: also Environmental Health & Biodiversity), so the tag varies by item as what is measured varies by item. No single value is forced on the indicator.
sdgTarget: None. No SDG indicator counts piloted market or business-model innovations; the SDG framework measures market outcomes (for example smallholder income) rather than the institutional outputs that precede them.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Results Framework, Innovation Development output category: CGIAR defines an innovation as "a new, improved, or adapted output... such as technologies, products and services, policies, and other organizational and institutional arrangements with high potential to contribute to positive impacts when used at scale", which covers market and business-model innovations. When reported into CGIAR technical reporting, each innovation-development result must carry an innovation type, an innovation readiness level, and a contact point (CGIAR Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30, Annex 3).
definition: Counts the market or business-model innovations piloted by CIMMYT in the reporting year, counted once per distinct innovation at pilot stage. A market or business-model innovation is a new or adapted way of organizing how a value chain sources, trades, delivers services, or distributes value: examples include sustainable sourcing arrangements (buyers committing to grain produced under verified sustainable practices) and inclusive market platforms (trading or service arrangements designed so smallholders, women, and youth can participate). Pilot stage means the innovation is being tested with real market actors under real transaction conditions at limited scale, and is not yet in routine operational use; once in operational use it is counted by KPI-O36, not here.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT is generating and market-testing new business and market arrangements that could make value chains more sustainable and inclusive, the front end of the market-systems change the 2030 Strategy commits to ("market driven systems and emerging models are harnessed to improve agrifood systems and their sustainability", strategic objective 4.4). For institutional management the count shows the size of the pilot pipeline that feeds deployment (KPI-O36) and, further downstream, value chains adopting sustainable or inclusive models; a thin pipeline today predicts weak market-systems outcomes in later years.
projectSpecificApplication: Each project counts the market or business-model innovations it pilots within its own value chains, countries, and reporting period. The institutional definition, the pilot-stage boundary, and the distinctness rule are unchanged; only the commodity, geography, and partner set are project-specific. If a project's context makes the pilot-stage boundary genuinely ambiguous (for example a phased commercial rollout), raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining the stage here.
projectSpecificRationale: States why the project tracks the indicator: to evidence delivery of its market-systems components to donors, and to manage its own pipeline, since it shows which planned pilots launched in the year, and supports decisions on which pilots to extend, redesign, or close before committing scale-up resources.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work reaches no market and pilots no business model
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI. Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work reaches no market and pilots no business model.
unit: Number of innovations (count)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more market or business-model innovations are at pilot stage. It is explicitly a stock, so a multi-year pilot is counted every year it stays active; a reader assuming a flow would take a stable figure for no new piloting.
disaggregationRequired: Commodity or value chain; innovation readiness level (required metadata for any innovation-development result entering CGIAR technical reporting). An innovation piloted in more than one value chain in the same year is listed under each of them, so value-chain subtotals may exceed the total and are never summed.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country or region; innovation type (sustainable sourcing arrangement, inclusive platform, service or financing model); lead partner type (private company, cooperative, public agency).
unitOfObservation: Result object, the template value, instantiated as the individual market or business-model innovation and counted from records. An innovation is a countable thing that is not a person, a place or a post, which is what the result-object value covers; "organization" is not used as a stand-in, since this indicator observes no organization.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct market or business-model innovations with an active pilot during the reporting year. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (administrative and registry data): CIMMYT project M&E records: pilot design documents or protocols, partner agreements, pilot monitoring reports, and the project's innovation-tracking records. These are the records the inclusion criteria above require, so the recommended source doubles as the evidence base. Fallback DS2 (partner-held administrative records): where a partner implements the pilot and CIMMYT's own records are incomplete, the partner's pilot documentation may substantiate the count. Values substantiated only by partner records are flagged as fallback-sourced, because CIMMYT cannot fully verify completeness. Not applicable: DS1 (censuses and surveys), the indicator counts CIMMYT's own documented pilots, not conditions reported by a surveyed population; DS3 (geospatial and Earth observation), a business arrangement is not observable from imagery; DS4 (secondary and international databases), no third-party database records CIMMYT's pilot portfolio; DS5 (citizen-generated data), pilot status is an internal program fact that crowdsourced data cannot establish.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which route each innovation rests on; for any on the Fallback, state why CIMMYT documentation was incomplete and which partner records were used.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source.
collectionFrequency: Continuous recording in project M&E systems as pilots start, evolve, and close; consolidated once per year for reporting.
reportingFrequency: Annually, into institutional and donor reporting.
referencePeriod: The reporting year. The value describes pilots active at any point during that year. The reporting year is the calendar year, register-wide.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual output count; the prior year's value is the natural comparator and no pre-intervention baseline is needed to interpret it.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One reporting year, and pilots at pilot stage only. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool the innovations evidenced in CIMMYT's own records (Recommended); an innovation evidenced only in partner records (Fallback) is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, not blended in, and the same project's Recommended-sourced innovations are pooled.

B: Combination method. Sum: the count of distinct innovations across projects, after the de-duplication Block E requires. Never averaged.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's distinct innovations at pilot stage in the reporting year. At institutional level, the deduplicated sum of those counts, computed from the innovation records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one innovation is often piloted by more than one project and in more than one country. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels: an innovation has no plot and no household, so the levels here are reporting levels. The annual value is a stock of active pilots, not a flow, so successive years are never summed into a cumulative total. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the innovation-readiness breakdown, the number excluded under Eligibility and why, and the number of innovations reported alongside because they rest on the Fallback.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count does not add to the deployed-innovations count (KPI-O36) or to the value-chains-adopting outcome (KPI-OC35); pilot, deployment and adoption measure different stages and connect through the theory of change, not through arithmetic. An innovation that advances from pilot to deployment mid-year may legitimately appear in both counts for that year; the two are reported side by side and never summed. Values from different years are never summed either, because the value is a stock.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: the same innovation piloted by two projects or in two countries counts once in the institutional figure, de-duplicated on innovation name and description before summing, and the pooled number is labelled an upper estimate where names cannot be matched. One named overlap risk: a market or business-model innovation may also qualify for the co-developed innovations count (KPI-O01), since both count innovations at output level; it counts in both, for different things, and the two are never summed. No primary-count rule is applied, because forcing each innovation to one indicator would mean a co-developed innovation being piloted disappears from one count or the other for no reason a reader could follow; institutional reporting notes the cross-reference so a combined reading de-duplicates.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion criteria: CIMMYT designed or co-designed the innovation and leads or co-leads the pilot; the pilot involves real market actors and real transactions (not a simulation or design workshop); the pilot is documented (pilot design or protocol, partner agreement, monitoring records). One innovation piloted in several sites or countries counts once; sites are not innovations.

Exclusion criteria: innovations still in design with no live market test; innovations already in routine operational use (counted under KPI-O36); agronomic or technological innovations without a market or business-model component (counted in the Innovation development & scaling pathway); multi-stakeholder platforms or innovation hubs as structures (counted under the platforms indicator, KPI-O35), although a business model piloted through such a platform counts here.
limitations: Measures CIMMYT's delivery, not market change: a rising count means more pilots were run, not that value chains became more sustainable or inclusive. Uptake by market actors is what the outcome indicators of this pathway measure.

The unit is judgment-sensitive: deciding whether a bundled arrangement is one innovation or several, or whether an adapted model is new, requires a consistent distinctness rule; without one, counts are inflated or deflated by how records are written rather than by what was done.

The pilot-versus-deployed boundary is the main comparability risk: unless the stage rule is applied consistently, innovations drift between this indicator and KPI-O36 and both counts lose meaning. The boundary is documentary (a pilot under way here, the documented move to operational use at KPI-O36), not a readiness-level band.

The count carries no quality or scale signal: a small single-buyer sourcing trial and a national platform pilot each count as one. Read the number together with its readiness-level and value-chain disaggregations, never alone.
A year-on-year fall does not necessarily indicate reduced activity: pilots graduating to deployment shrink this count while growing KPI-O36. Interpret the two indicators together as a pipeline.
subMetrics: None. Innovation type (sustainable sourcing, inclusive platform) and value chain are disaggregations of the same count, not separately calculated metrics.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project teams (pilot leads maintain pilot documentation). Validation: project MEAL officer (checks each counted innovation against the inclusion criteria and evidence). Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (institutional de-duplication and consolidation). Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 10 · Policy, finance & market systems — Reference sheet KPI-O34

name: Number of multi-stakeholder platforms or innovation hubs established for system transformation
resultsLevel: Output. An established platform or hub, like a partnership arising from a signed memorandum of understanding, is a delivered result of the research team and its founding partners. What members then do differently is the outcome question, answered by KPI-OC35, not by this count.
primaryObjective: PO4 Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved), PO5 (Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities).
cgiarImpactArea: Recorded per platform and reported as a distribution, under the pathway-wide rule. An inclusive market platform serves Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs; a platform anchored on sustainable sourcing or climate services principally serves Environmental Health & Biodiversity or Climate Adaptation & Mitigation, so the tag varies by item as what is measured varies by item. No single value is forced on the indicator.
sdgTarget: None. The closest SDG framing is target 17.16, which calls for multi-stakeholder partnerships that mobilize and share knowledge, expertise, technology and financial resources; its official indicator 17.16.1 counts countries reporting progress in multi-stakeholder development effectiveness monitoring frameworks, not platforms an organization establishes, so no direct correspondence exists.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Technical Reporting: a newly constituted platform or hub is reportable under the CGIAR Results Framework's output result types, most naturally as an Innovation Development output, since CGIAR's definition of that category expressly includes new organizational and institutional arrangements. At outcome level, CGIAR's capacity-change category tracks capacity change in networks such as multi-stakeholder platforms, which concerns how an established platform later performs, not its establishment. No CGIAR standard indicator counts platform establishment itself, so this is a CIMMYT-defined indicator feeding those CGIAR categories.
definition: Counts the multi-stakeholder platforms or innovation hubs established for system transformation with CIMMYT as founder or co-founder, or substantially co-designed by CIMMYT with its design role documented in the constituting record, in the reporting year; counts distinct platforms or hubs established. A multi-stakeholder platform is a standing, formally constituted arrangement convening member organizations from several distinct categories of the confirmed 13-category partner and institution list around a shared agenda for transforming an agrifood system. An innovation hub is a standing physical or virtual center where those actors jointly develop, test, and adapt innovations for a defined territory or value chain.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT is putting in place the standing coordination structures through which agrifood-system actors can act together on sustainable and inclusive change: the countable entry point of the market-systems results chain leading to value chains adopting sustainable or inclusive models (KPI-OC35) and to a growing share of market volume flowing through sustainable or inclusive models (KPI-I13). Used by project management to track delivery against workplans and by institutional and donor reporting to evidence CIMMYT's convening role in system transformation.
projectSpecificApplication: State which platforms or hubs the project establishes, the system-transformation agenda each serves, the countries or territories covered, and the stakeholder groups convened. Do not change the unit, the establishment test, or the counting rule. If applying the indicator as defined is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count informs (for example, a donor-required milestone on establishing an innovation hub in each target region, or an internal trigger: if a planned platform is not constituted by a set date, the partnership strategy and workplan are reviewed).
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work convenes no multi-stakeholder platform in a value chain
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI. Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work convenes no multi-stakeholder platform in a value chain.
unit: Number (count of distinct platforms or hubs established)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more multi-stakeholder platforms or innovation hubs were established, not that they function (see Limitations).
disaggregationRequired: Required: structure type, using the two categories in the definition (multi-stakeholder platform, innovation hub). The register currently records no required disaggregation for this indicator; this requirement is set on the sheet's authority.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country or region; scale the structure operates at (local or territorial, national, regional or global); commodity or value-chain focus; stakeholder categories represented, on the confirmed 13-category partner and institution list.
unitOfObservation: Organization: the platform or hub as a constituted body with its own membership and governance.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct multi-stakeholder platforms or innovation hubs formally established in the reporting year with CIMMYT as founder or co-founder, or with CIMMYT's substantial co-design documented in the constituting record; formal founder status is not required, because it depends on a government's or partner's legal drafting conventions rather than on the work done. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: CIMMYT project records logging each platform or hub, its establishment date, membership roster, governance document, first-convening record, and CIMMYT's founding or co-design role, cross-checked against project technical reports and partner reporting. A national registry entry is also a Recommended source, for establishment, wherever it is retrieved: a platform or hub whose CIMMYT founding or co-design role is documented in the project's own records and whose establishment is evidenced only by such an entry is Recommended-sourced. Fallback DS4: the platform's own published records (charter, website) used to reconstruct establishment where CIMMYT's project records are incomplete; any value built this way is flagged as fallback-sourced. Not applicable DS1: this indicator counts institutional arrangements from records, not data collected from respondents. Not applicable DS3: satellite or GIS data cannot evidence the constitution of a platform. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced data cannot verify an institutional establishment.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which route each platform or hub rests on; for any on the Fallback, state why the project's own records were incomplete and which external records were used.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). The project's log entry for each platform or hub is the record: each entry names the platform or hub, structure type, establishment date, membership, governance document, first convening, and CIMMYT's founding or co-design role.
collectionFrequency: Continuous: each establishment is logged as it occurs
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the platform or hub was formally established. The reporting year is the calendar year, register-wide.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual flow count that starts from zero each reporting year; there is no pre-project stock to measure. Change over time is read from the annual series.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: sum the platforms and hubs evidenced in projects' own records (Recommended); a platform or hub evidenced only in its own published records (Fallback) is reported alongside the summed figure with a note, not blended in, and the same project's Recommended-sourced platforms and hubs are summed.

B: Combination method. Summed: the institutional figure is the sum of distinct platforms or hubs established across all reporting projects in the year, after de-duplication. Never average project-level counts.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying multi-stakeholder platforms or innovation hubs established for the reporting year. At institutional level, the deduplicated sum of those counts, computed from the records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one platform is often reported by more than one project. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels: a platform has no plot and no household, so the levels here are reporting levels. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the split between platforms and hubs, and the number still active at year end, the number excluded under Eligibility and why, and the number of platforms and hubs reported alongside because they rest on the Fallback.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count does not combine arithmetically with KPI-OC35 or KPI-I13; the levels connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative: platforms and hubs established, value chains adopting sustainable or inclusive models, market volume shifting to sustainable and inclusive models.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: two named risks. Within this indicator, a platform co-founded by two CIMMYT projects, or spanning several countries, carries one institutional identifier and counts once, with country coverage as a disaggregation; if identifiers cannot be matched, label the sum an upper estimate. Across the register, the same arrangement may plausibly qualify under KPI-O37 (multi-stakeholder fora convened, which counts events), KPI-O34 or KPI-O36 (market or business-model innovations, which cover commercial platforms such as inclusive sourcing arrangements), or KPI-O01 (innovations co-developed with partners, since CGIAR's innovation definition includes institutional arrangements). The precedence rule: a standing multi-stakeholder structure counts here; single convened events go to KPI-O37 and market-facing platform businesses to KPI-O34 or KPI-O36; the shared identifier must mark the entry so the roll-up never presents one arrangement as two achievements.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion: a platform or hub counts when the establishment test is met within the reporting year: documented membership from at least three distinct categories of the confirmed 13-category partner and institution list (the confirmed threshold, counted on the same taxonomy KPI-O40 uses, so a membership cannot pass under one list and fail under another), a documented governance arrangement (terms of reference, charter, or memorandum of understanding), and the first convening held; co-founded structures count once, with CIMMYT's founding or documented co-design role recorded in the constituting record.
limitations: Establishment is not functioning: a platform counted here may convene once and stall, so the count says nothing about whether the structure stays active, retains members, or changes anything in the system it was built for. The system-change evidence belongs to KPI-OC35 and KPI-I13.

"Platform or hub" spans very different structures, from a village-level innovation hub to a national multi-stakeholder platform, so raw counts are not comparable across projects until the type and scale disaggregations are applied; one durable national platform may matter more than several short-lived local ones.

The count is sensitive to what is treated as distinct: splitting one platform's country chapters into separate entries inflates the figure, bundling a network of hubs into one deflates it. The single institutional identifier and the establishment-evidence requirement are the controls; read the count together with the list of structures behind it.

The boundary with convened events (KPI-O37) and commercial platform innovations (KPI-O34, KPI-O36) rests on the standing-structure test; until applied consistently, the counts can drift or overlap, so the precedence rule must be enforced through the shared identifier.

An increase means CIMMYT and partners constituted more standing coordination structures, not that agrifood systems transformed; a high count with no movement in KPI-OC35 suggests platforms are being created rather than used. Never present this count alone as evidence of system change.
subMetrics: None. The two structure types named in the definition (multi-stakeholder platform, innovation hub) are disaggregations of the same count, not separately calculated metrics. Related results-chain indicators have their own sheets: KPI-O36 (market or business-model innovations deployed, the companion output), KPI-OC35 (value chains adopting sustainable or inclusive models, the outcome this output feeds), and KPI-I13 (percentage of market volume or value flowing through sustainable or inclusive models, the pathway impact).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E focal point, logging each establishment with its evidence. Validation: project MEAL officer, cross-checking the log against project technical reports and founding documents. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (de-duplication across projects and the institutional sum, per Aggregation rule). Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.

name: Number of market or business-model innovations (sustainable sourcing, inclusive platforms) deployed
resultsLevel: Output. Deployment is a delivered result, carried out and documented within the project's own delivery system; chain-level adoption by external market actors is a change, measured at outcome level by KPI-OC35.
indicatorScope: Mission. Measures a result delivered into external market systems through project implementation, so it carries the full project-specific layer.
primaryObjective: PO4 Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient, grounded in sub-objective 4.4 ("Market driven systems and emerging models are harnessed to improve agrifood systems and their sustainability"). The register's PO3 and PO5 are contributing objectives only: deployed models widen smallholder access to services, income and market opportunities (3.2, 3.3) and support value-adding opportunities that make farming attractive (5.3).
cgiarImpactArea: Recorded per innovation and reported as a distribution, under the pathway-wide rule. A deployed market innovation can serve more than one Impact Area (an inclusive platform: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs; a sustainable sourcing arrangement: also Environmental Health & Biodiversity), so the tag varies by item as what is measured varies by item. No single value is forced on the indicator.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator counts market or business-model innovations deployed by a research organization. The nearest neighbour, target 9.3 (small-scale enterprises' access to finance and integration into value chains and markets), measures enterprise outcomes, not innovation outputs: 9.3.1 is the share of small-scale industries in industry value added, 9.3.2 the share with a loan or line of credit (SDG 9.3.1 metadata sheet, UNIDO custodian).
otherFrameworks: CGIAR standard results reporting: the Innovation Development result category explicitly includes "other organizational and institutional arrangements" (One CGIAR Standard Indicators report), which covers market and business-model innovations; this indicator reports a subset restricted to the deployment milestone. The CGIAR Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 applies the same output/outcome split, innovation development versus innovation use. CGIAR's Scaling Readiness scoring is not adopted here: CIMMYT reports into that system where required but does not use self-assessed readiness levels as KPI evidence.
definition: Counts the market or business-model innovations CIMMYT moves from pilot to operational use during the reporting year. A market or business-model innovation is a new or significantly improved way of organizing how agricultural products, services or finance are sourced, traded or delivered (the register's examples: sustainable sourcing arrangements, inclusive market platforms); the novelty is the commercial or institutional arrangement, not a production technology. "Deployed" means the innovation has left its pilot setting and operates under real transaction conditions, with actual buyers, sellers or service users at operating volumes. Each distinct innovation is counted once, in the year it is first deployed.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's market-systems work produces arrangements that operate in the market, rather than pilots that end when project support ends. The pilot-to-operational transition is where a market innovation stops being a research activity and becomes a functioning piece of a value chain, making the count the direct output evidence for 2030 Strategy sub-objective 4.4.
projectSpecificApplication: Describe which innovations this project deploys, in which commodity or value chain and countries, with which operating partners (off-takers, platform operators, aggregators, financial institutions), and state the deployment evidence applied (see Calculation method). Do not restate or alter the institutional definition, unit or counting rule; if the deployment test cannot be applied in this context, raise it with the MEAL focal point.
projectSpecificRationale: State why this project tracks the indicator: the donor requirement or workplan milestone it evidences, and the decision it informs (for example, a pilot not deployed within its planned window triggers a business-case review before further investment).
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work reaches no market and pilots no business model
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI. Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work reaches no market and pilots no business model.
unit: Number of innovations (distinct market or business-model innovations)
directionOfChange: Increase, with a caveat. A rising value means more market or business-model innovations moved from pilot into operational use. The count rewards deployment volume and tests neither scale, viability nor persistence; a rising count with no movement in KPI-OC35 describes models that operate but are not spreading.
disaggregationRequired: Required: commodity or value chain, as recorded in the register; a count pooled across value chains cannot otherwise be interpreted. An innovation first deployed in more than one value chain in the same year is listed under each of them, so value-chain subtotals may exceed the total and are never summed.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country and sub-national location; innovation type (sustainable sourcing arrangement / inclusive market platform / other business or service model); operating partner type (private company, cooperative or farmer organization, public entity, financial institution); intended CGIAR Impact Area.
unitOfObservation: The innovation. This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation.
calculationSummary:
Value = the count of distinct innovations that, during the reporting year, (a) meet the definition in Section 1, (b) previously operated at pilot stage, (c) moved into documented operational use, and (d) carry a documented CIMMYT contribution: CIMMYT design or technical input to the model or to its move into operational use, evidenced in a dated record; convening the parties, hosting a discussion or commenting on someone else's design does not qualify.

Deployment evidence. A dated record showing the model running on the counting party's own account and resources, financed and operated without CIMMYT carrying it: a dated deployment record plus an operating agreement naming the entity running the innovation, plus evidence of real transactions at operating volumes on that entity's account. Operational use is about who bears the cost and the risk; a declaration of intent to operate does not count, and licensure, certification or regulatory clearance alone is market availability, not operation. A Scaling Readiness level is deliberately not offered (see Other frameworks).

Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource:
Recommended, DS2 (Administrative and registry data): the project's own innovation register, evidenced per counted innovation by the dated deployment record, the operating agreement naming who runs the innovation, and the operational evidence required by the deployment test (transaction records, platform activity, sourcing contract volumes).

Fallback, DS4 (Secondary and international databases): CGIAR institutional results records reporting the same innovations, only where a project kept no register; flag values as fallback-sourced, since they may lag the reporting year and lack the operational evidence required here.

Not applicable, stated explicitly: DS1 (Censuses and surveys): deployment is established from documentation, not respondent interviews. DS3 (Geospatial and Earth observation): a business model is not an observable surface feature. DS5 (Citizen-generated and other non-traditional data): crowdsourced data cannot evidence a milestone or an operating agreement.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role this project used, Recommended or Fallback; if Fallback, explain briefly why the project could not maintain its own innovation register.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2 recommended; no DS1 or DS5 source listed). Verification is documentary review against the Calculation method criteria.
collectionFrequency: Continuous recording as innovations reach deployment, compiled once per reporting year.
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the innovation first met the deployment test: a within-year count of deployment events, not a cumulative stock. The reporting year is the calendar year, register-wide.
baselineRequired: No. The baseline is zero by construction: each year counts innovations reaching the milestone within that year. Prior-year values serve trend comparison; a partial start-up year is noted separately, not annualized.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Across projects: sum distinct innovations from projects using the Recommended source; a project on the Fallback is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, not blended in.

B: Combination method. The institutional figure is the sum of distinct innovations across projects after de-duplication; never average project counts.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying market or business-model innovations that moved into operational use in the reporting year. At institutional level, the deduplicated sum of those counts, computed from the records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one innovation is often reported by more than one project. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels: an innovation has no plot and no household, so the levels here are reporting levels. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the boundary with KPI-O34's pilot stage, since an innovation crossing it mid-year appears in both counts and the two are never summed, the number excluded under Eligibility and why, and whether any contributing value was Fallback-sourced.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: No. This count does not combine arithmetically with KPI-O34, KPI-OC35 or KPI-I13: the same innovation legitimately appears under O34 in its pilot year and here in its deployment year, so summing the two double-counts it. Levels connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative. Progression ratios (share of a piloted cohort later deployed) require cohort tracking by a stable identifier, never dividing one indicator's same-year value by another's.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: a real risk. The same model may be deployed by several CIMMYT projects, with another CGIAR center, or across several value chains. Count each distinct innovation once institutionally, de-duplicating by innovation identifier where one exists, otherwise on innovation name and description, as on KPI-O34, and label the pooled number an upper estimate where identifiers cannot be matched. Overlap with KPI-O35 is resolved by KPI-O35's precedence rule: an inclusive market platform counts here only if not counted there as a platform or hub. The boundary with the innovation pathway is different in kind: this indicator counts a way of organising how products, services or finance are sourced, traded or delivered, while that pathway counts a technology, practice or tool. A hybrid (a digital platform that is both a tool and a business model) counts in both, for its two different aspects, and the two are never summed.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion and exclusion. Include new and significantly improved sourcing arrangements, market platforms and business or service models, digital or organizational. Exclude: innovations still at pilot stage (KPI-O34). A prior count under KPI-O34 is not required: a model piloted before the register existed, or piloted elsewhere and deployed with the documented CIMMYT contribution the Calculation method requires, counts here on its own deployment evidence. Also exclude: production technologies, practices and tools; platforms and hubs as convening institutions (KPI-O35); knowledge products; innovations already counted in an earlier year.

Missing data. An innovation with no documented deployment evidence is excluded rather than estimated; report the number of excluded candidates alongside the value.

Repeated observations. Each distinct innovation is counted once, in the first year it meets the deployment test. Deployment in a further country or value chain does not count again, as a pilot in a further country does not on KPI-O34.
limitations: Deployment is not adoption, and supports no claim of benefit. The count says CIMMYT moved a model into operational use; it does not say value-chain actors adopted it independently (KPI-OC35), that meaningful volume flows through it (KPI-I13), or that farmers gained income from it.

The counted objects are not equivalent. One entry can be a national sourcing arrangement, another a district-level aggregation service; the total is not a measure of effort, reach or expected benefit, and no weighting is applied.

The pilot-to-operational boundary rests on the rule the sheet states, applied by the project MEAL officer and recorded with the reason. A permissive reading lets projects count late-stage pilots, a strict one penalizes weak documentation, so counts are not reliably comparable until one documentary test applies everywhere.

Persistence is not captured. An innovation counted as deployed stays counted even if it ceases operating the next year; any cumulative "models deployed to date" claim needs a companion check of whether earlier models still operate.
subMetrics:
None. Commodity or value chain, country, innovation type, partner type and intended Impact Area are disaggregations, not sub-metrics.

Related indicators, each with its own sheet: KPI-O34 (innovations piloted), KPI-O35 (platforms or hubs established), KPI-OC35 (value chains adopting sustainable or inclusive models, the outcome this output feeds), KPI-I13 (share of market volume or value through sustainable or inclusive models, the pathway’s impact measure).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E officer, jointly with the responsible market-systems lead. Validation: project MEAL officer, against the deployment test and evidence. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (counting rule and cross-project de-duplication). Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit, which publishes pooled and fallback-sourced figures separately.
