name: Number of policy dialogues, technical advisory engagements, or multi-stakeholder fora convened by CIMMYT with decision-makers and global bodies
resultsLevel: Output. An output is a delivered result, a product or service, and CGIAR's quality-assurance guidance lists policy analyses and partnerships arising from a signed memorandum of understanding among its output examples. Convening an event is such a service: CIMMYT decides to hold it, organises it, and can evidence that it took place. What the participating decision-makers then do with the engagement (use the evidence, change a policy) is a change, and belongs to KPI-OC37. CGIAR's 2025-30 reporting arrangement notes that workshop and meeting results often sit close to activities; the inclusion tests in the calculation method are what separate a countable engagement from routine project activity.
primaryObjective: PO5 Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved), PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Recorded per engagement and reported as a distribution, under the pathway-wide rule. An engagement may concern climate, nutrition, livelihoods or markets, so the tag varies by item as what is measured varies by item, and the topic disaggregation carries it. No single value is forced on the indicator.
sdgTarget: None. SDG target 17.16 (multi-stakeholder partnerships that mobilize and share knowledge, expertise, technology and financial resources) is the matching target, but its official indicator 17.16.1 counts countries reporting progress in multi-stakeholder development effectiveness monitoring frameworks: a property of countries' monitoring systems, not a count of events an organisation convenes.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Results Framework: no CGIAR standard indicator counts convened events; the standard output categories are knowledge products, innovation development, and capacity sharing. The 2025-30 CGIAR Results Framework is adding a partner engagement/partnership building result category, created because many 2022-23 "other" results were events such as workshops and meetings; once its data standard is finalized, this indicator's event records are mapped to it, not restructured to match it: the construct here is CIMMYT's role in the event, and an upward reporting format does not redefine it.
definition: Counts the distinct policy dialogues and multi-stakeholder fora that CIMMYT convenes, and the technical advisory engagements it delivers on request, with decision-makers and global bodies in the reporting year. Convened means CIMMYT organised or co-organised the event with a documented convening role: initiating it, setting or co-setting the agenda, and bringing the participants together; attending or presenting at an event convened by others does not count. The counted object is the event itself, whether a convened dialogue or forum or an advisory engagement, not the participants and not the evidence products presented there (counted by KPI-O39).
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT is creating the engagement spaces through which its evidence and advice reach the people who make policy and investment decisions. It is the countable entry point of the policy-influence results chain: convened engagement carries evidence to decision-makers, who may use it (policies informed, KPI-OC37), leading to enactment (KPI-I15). Used by project management to track engagement delivery and by institutional reporting on CIMMYT's contribution to informed, coordinated global action.
projectSpecificApplication: State which dialogues and fora the project convenes and which advisory engagements it delivers, the decision-makers and bodies targeted, the countries and policy scale covered, and CIMMYT's role in each (sole convener or co-convener, and with whom, or the body that requested the advice). Do not change the unit, the convening test, or the counting rule. If applying the indicator as defined is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count informs (for example, a donor-required policy-engagement deliverable, or an internal milestone trigger: no dialogues convened by a set date prompts a review of the project's engagement strategy with the targeted institutions).
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work convenes no policy dialogue or forum and delivers no technical advisory engagement
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI. Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work convenes no policy dialogue or forum and delivers no technical advisory engagement.
unit: Number (count of distinct convened events and technical advisory engagements)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means CIMMYT convened more policy dialogues or multi-stakeholder fora, or delivered more technical advisory engagements. More events is not more influence; see Limitations.
disaggregationRequired: Required: policy scale or level, on CGIAR's four levels (local / national / regional / global), set on this sheet's authority. The four levels match KPI-OC37 and KPI-I15, so an engagement, the instrument it informs and the instrument enacted are filed at one scale. Also required: engagement type (policy dialogue / technical advisory / multi-stakeholder forum), because a one-day policy dialogue and a year-long technical advisory engagement are not the same object and a pooled count reads as more convening than took place.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country or region; topic or Impact Area served; convening role (sole convener / co-convener); participant institution type (national government, regional body, global body, private sector, civil society); one-off event vs standing platform.
unitOfObservation: The convened event or technical advisory engagement itself. This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct events that took place in the reporting year and meet all four inclusion tests. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: CIMMYT project and program engagement records logging each event with its date, type, convening documentation or, for an advisory engagement, the request and the record of what CIMMYT provided, participant record, policy scale, and purpose, cross-checked against project technical reports. An official communiqué or published proceedings issued by the convening or host body is also a Recommended source, for the event having taken place and for who took part, wherever it is retrieved: an event whose CIMMYT role is documented in the project's own records and whose occurrence is evidenced only by such a publication is Recommended-sourced. Fallback DS4: other external records (co-convener or host records, partner websites) used to reconstruct the count where CIMMYT's own log is incomplete; any value built this way is flagged as fallback-sourced, because external records rarely document CIMMYT's role, which then needs separate evidencing. Not applicable DS1: this indicator counts institutional events from records, not data collected from respondents. Not applicable DS3: geospatial data cannot identify an event or CIMMYT's role in it. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced data cannot verify an event's purpose, participants, or CIMMYT's role.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which route each event rests on; for any on the Fallback, state why the project's own engagement log was incomplete and which external records were used.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). The event log record is the tool: each record names the event, date, engagement type, CIMMYT's role, participant categories, policy scale, purpose, and the supporting documentation.
collectionFrequency: Continuous: each event is logged as it takes place
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the event takes place. The reporting year is the calendar year, register-wide.
baselineRequired: No. An annual flow count that starts from zero each reporting year; there is no pre-project stock to measure. Change over time is read from the annual series itself.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: sum the events evidenced in projects' own engagement records (Recommended); an event evidenced only in external records (Fallback) is reported alongside the summed figure with a note, not blended in, and the same project's Recommended-sourced events are summed.

B: Combination method. Summed: the institutional figure is the sum of distinct events across all reporting projects and programs in the year, after de-duplication. Never average project-level counts.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying policy dialogues and multi-stakeholder fora convened, and technical advisory engagements delivered, in the reporting year. At institutional level, the deduplicated sum of those counts, computed from the records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one engagement is often reported by more than one project. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels: an engagement has no plot and no household, so the levels here are reporting levels. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the split by engagement type, the number of distinct institutions engaged (a different count from this one), the number excluded under Eligibility and why, and the number of events reported alongside because they rest on the Fallback.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count never combines arithmetically with KPI-OC37 or KPI-I15; the same policy engagement is intentionally visible at more than one level (the dialogue counted here, the informed policy there), and the levels connect as a narrative, not a sum.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: three named risks. First, within this indicator, an event co-convened by several CIMMYT projects, or a regional forum spanning several countries, carries one institutional event identifier and counts once, with country coverage as a disaggregation; if identifiers cannot be matched, label the sum an upper estimate. Second, across the register, a convened event sits in exactly one count: a training workshop belongs to the capacity outputs, a structured donor engagement event to the institutional donor-relations count (KPI-O55), and a dialogue where evidence products are delivered is one event here while the products count under KPI-O39; the event identifier marks such records so one gathering is never presented as two achievements. Third, people engaged through these fora (for example women in decision-making fora, KPI-O28) are counted by person-level indicators with no arithmetic link to this event count.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion: an event counts when (a) CIMMYT convened or co-convened it, evidenced by convening documentation (concept note, invitation issued by or with CIMMYT, agenda-setting role). A technical advisory engagement is not held to the convening test and qualifies instead on a documented request or terms of reference from the receiving body, and a dated record of what CIMMYT provided. Informal advice given in a meeting does not count, because there is nothing to verify and nothing a reviewer could revisit; (b) participants include decision-makers: officials or representatives of institutions holding authority over policy, regulation, public investment or programme design, the definition KPI-O40 uses; (c) it has a documented policy or technical-advisory purpose; and (d) it took place, not merely planned, within the reporting year. A standing platform or recurring forum counts once per reporting year as one convened forum, with its number of sessions recorded as a note, not as additional events.
limitations: Convening is not influence: this count evidences that CIMMYT created and delivered engagement spaces, not that decision-makers used what they heard. Evidence use belongs to KPI-OC37 and enactment to KPI-I15; a rising count with a flat KPI-OC37 over several years signals engagement that is not converting.

Events differ enormously in weight, from a district dialogue to a standing global forum, so raw counts are not comparable across projects or years until the scale and engagement-type disaggregations are applied; a count target can also incentivise many small events over fewer consequential ones.

Co-convened events blur attribution: CIMMYT's role ranges from initiating and hosting to being one of several co-conveners, and the convening-documentation requirement bounds the claim but does not grade its depth.
The boundary with routine activity is judgment-based; the decision-maker-participation and documented-purpose tests are the control, and each inclusion can be audited against the event record.

The standing-platform rule (one forum per year regardless of sessions) keeps the unit comparable, but it means the count understates engagement intensity; use the sessions note, not extra events, to show it.
subMetrics: None. The three engagement types and the policy-scale levels are disaggregations of the same count, not separately calculated metrics. The results chain continues in KPI-OC37 (public policies informed by CIMMYT evidence, the outcome this output feeds) and KPI-I15 (policies enacted supporting smallholder resilience, the impact the chain reaches), each with its own sheet. Sibling outputs feeding the same outcome: KPI-O39 (policy-relevant evidence products delivered) and KPI-O40 (institutions whose capacity to generate, access or use CIMMYT evidence has been strengthened).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: the project or program focal point who convenes the event or delivers the advisory engagement, logging it with its documentation. Validation: project MEAL officer, checking each record against inclusion tests (a) to (d) in Eligibility criteria and missing data. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (de-duplication and the institutional sum, per Aggregation rule). Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.

name: Number of investment cases, financing instruments, or co-investment partnerships developed by CIMMYT for smallholder-focused systems
resultsLevel: Output. Developing a case, designing an instrument or formalizing a partnership are delivered results CIMMYT documents within its own delivery system; CGIAR's guidance lists partnerships arising from a signed memorandum of understanding as outputs. Commitment and disbursement by a financier follow the delivery and are not part of it: disbursement is measured at impact level by KPI-I16, and commitment or financial close by no indicator in this register.
indicatorScope: Mission. The indicator measures a result CIMMYT's research-for-development work delivers toward external financiers (investors, development finance institutions, donors, lenders) for smallholder-focused agrifood systems through project implementation in specific countries, so it carries the full project-specific layer.
primaryObjective: PO5 Global community takes informed, coordinated, and consolidated measures to systematically overcome agrifood system disruptions, the impacts of the climate crisis, and structural inequalities. The single primary objective, grounded in sub-objective 5.5, "Policies and investments prioritize smallholder agriculture": developing the cases, instruments and partnerships that direct investment toward smallholder systems is what this indicator counts. The register also lists PO3 and PO4, both contributing objectives only: financing widens smallholder access to services and income opportunities and strengthens provider institutions (sub-objectives 3.2, 3.3), and mobilised investment is one of the market-driven models improving agrifood systems (sub-objective 4.4).
cgiarImpactArea: Recorded per counted instrument and reported as a distribution, under the pathway-wide rule. An instrument financing smallholder enterprise serves Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs; a climate-finance instrument serves Climate Adaptation & Mitigation, so the tag varies by item as what is measured varies by item. No single value is forced on the indicator.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator counts investment cases, financing instruments or partnerships developed. The nearest neighbour, SDG target 2.a (increase investment in agricultural productive capacity in developing countries), carries indicator 2.a.2, which measures gross disbursements of official flows to the agriculture sector (SDG 2.a.2 metadata sheet, OECD custodian): a flow value whose partial correspondence attaches to the downstream volume indicator KPI-I16, not to this count.
otherFrameworks: No donor framework counts financing instruments developed; the established indicators measure the value of finance mobilised, which in this register is KPI-I16. The downstream boundary is the disbursement test: value counts only once funds are disbursed, not on a commitment or a written agreement. Which flows qualify as finance, and how finance source is classified, are defined on KPI-I16, not here; this sheet counts the instruments, not the money. CGIAR standard results reporting: climate adaptation investments in US dollars is a standard indicator (One CGIAR Standard Indicators report); that correspondence is also downstream, attaching to KPI-I16.
definition: Counts the distinct investment cases, financing instruments and co-investment partnerships CIMMYT develops for smallholder-focused systems during the reporting year. The three instrument types are: an investment case, a documented, evidence-based proposition a financier can appraise; a financing instrument, a designed financial mechanism intended for deployment by a financing institution (a blended-finance facility design, a credit or guarantee product, an insurance product structure); and a co-investment partnership, a formalized arrangement in which CIMMYT and one or more external funders agree to jointly finance smallholder-focused work, evidenced by a signed agreement or memorandum of understanding. Smallholder is defined in Annex B.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT is building the financial architecture that lets its innovations reach smallholder farmers at scale: the evidence and instruments that make smallholder agriculture investable. It is the direct output evidence for the 2030 Strategy commitment that "Policies and investments prioritize smallholder agriculture" (sub-objective 5.5) and the pipeline-stage counterpart of the finance leveraged (KPI-I16), serving project management, institutional reporting and donors.
projectSpecificApplication: Describe which instruments this project develops, for which smallholder-focused system (country, commodity or value chain), with which prospective financiers, and state the development evidence applied per instrument type (see Calculation method). Do not restate or alter the institutional definition or counting rule; if the development test cannot be applied in this project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State why this project tracks the indicator: which donor requires evidence of investment-mobilisation work, which workplan milestone the count evidences, and what project decision it informs (for example, an investment case finding no financier interest within its planned window triggers a review).
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work develops no investment case or financing instrument
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI. Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work develops no investment case or financing instrument.
unit: Number of instruments (distinct investment cases, financing instruments, or co-investment partnerships)
directionOfChange: Increase, with a stated caveat. A rising value means more investment cases, financing instruments or co-investment partnerships were developed. The count contains no test of financier uptake, so it is read together with KPI-I16: a rising instrument count with no movement there describes a pipeline being built but not converting.
disaggregationRequired: Required: instrument type (investment case / financing instrument / co-investment partnership), as recorded in the register. This is the disaggregation institutional comparison depends on, since the three types are different objects at different distances from actual money.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country or region; commodity or value chain; finance type (public, private, blended; agricultural, climate); counterpart or financier type; intended CGIAR Impact Area.
unitOfObservation: The instrument (one distinct investment case, financing instrument, or co-investment partnership). Recorded under the Core's result object value, whose definition covers an investment instrument.
calculationSummary:
Value = the count of distinct instruments that, during the reporting year, (a) meet the definition in Section 1 including the smallholder-focus test, (b) were developed with CIMMYT having authored or co-authored the instrument's technical design, evidenced in the document itself (convening the parties, hosting the discussion or reviewing a draft is recorded but does not qualify), and (c) reached a documented development milestone.

Development milestone. Investment case, finalized and formally transmitted to at least one named prospective financier (dated transmittal record); financing instrument, design completed and accepted for appraisal by the institution that would deploy it; co-investment partnership, signed agreement or memorandum of understanding. All three stop short of disbursement, which belongs to KPI-I16. The test each counted instrument met is recorded with the count.

Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource:
Recommended, DS2 (Administrative and registry data): the project's own instrument register, evidenced per counted instrument by the instrument document itself (investment case, term sheet or design document, signed agreement) plus the milestone evidence the development test requires.

Fallback, DS4 (Secondary and international databases): CGIAR institutional results records or co-investor records already reporting the same instruments. Use only where a project kept no register, and flag the value as fallback-sourced, since those records follow their own cycles and typically lack milestone evidence.

Not applicable, stated explicitly: DS1 (Censuses and surveys): development is established from documentation, not from a sampled population. DS3 (Geospatial and Earth observation): an instrument is not an observable surface feature. DS5 (Citizen-generated data): cannot evidence a documented milestone or a signed agreement.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role above this project used, Recommended or Fallback. If Fallback, explain briefly why the project could not maintain its own instrument register.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable: the recommended source is DS2 and no DS1 or DS5 source is listed. Verification is by documentary review against the Calculation method.
collectionFrequency: Continuous recording as instruments reach their milestone, compiled once per reporting year.
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the instrument first met its development milestone: a within-year count of development events, not a cumulative stock. The reporting year is the calendar year, register-wide, and is uniform across projects.
baselineRequired: No. The baseline is zero by construction: each reporting year starts from zero. A prior-year value remains useful as a trend comparison. Where a project starts part-way through a year, report the first full reporting year and note the partial year separately rather than annualizing.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: sum the distinct instruments from projects that used the Recommended source; a Fallback-sourced value is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, not blended in.

B: Combination method. The institutional figure is the sum of distinct instruments across projects after de-duplication; never average project counts.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying investment cases, financing instruments or co-investment arrangements developed for the reporting year. At institutional level, the deduplicated sum of those counts, computed from the records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one instrument is often reported by more than one project. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels: an instrument has no plot and no household, so the levels here are reporting levels. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the split by instrument type, the number excluded under Eligibility and why, and whether any contributing value was Fallback-sourced.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count never combines arithmetically with KPI-I16, a US dollar volume: a count and a value must never be presented as one number. The pathway has no outcome indicator between this output and KPI-I16, so the two connect only as narrative; the missing step is named rather than filled with an indicator CIMMYT could not populate.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting, a real risk in three directions. Within the indicator: the same instrument is often developed by more than one CIMMYT project or with another CGIAR center; count it once, de-duplicating by instrument title and type, and label the pooled number an upper estimate where records cannot be matched. Against KPI-O42: a GEYSI-responsive investment instrument can qualify under both sheets; carry an overlap flag so the two counts are never summed without removing it. Against Resource mobilization: an agreement that both funds CIMMYT work and commits co-investment to a smallholder system is counted on one side only, by where the funding is directed.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion and exclusion. Include all three instrument types, whether the prospective finance is public, private or blended. Exclude: concept notes short of the milestone; proposals and agreements funding CIMMYT's own operations; public policy and regulatory instruments (KPI-OC37, KPI-I15); the finance mobilised (KPI-I16); and any instrument counted in an earlier year.

Missing data. An instrument with no documentary evidence of its milestone is excluded rather than estimated; report the number of excluded candidates alongside the value so a low count caused by weak record-keeping is visible.

Repeated observations. Each distinct instrument is counted once, in the first reporting year it meets its milestone; revisions, renewals and extensions are not recounted.
limitations: Development is not mobilisation, and supports no claim of benefit. The count says CIMMYT produced cases, designs and agreements; it does not say any financier committed or disbursed funds (disbursement is KPI-I16; commitment is measured by no indicator), nor that smallholders gained access to finance. An instrument can be developed and never reach financial close.

The counted objects are not equivalent. A multi-million dollar co-investment partnership and a single transmitted investment case each count as one; without the required instrument-type disaggregation the total cannot be read as a measure of effort or expected finance, and no weighting is applied.

The "developed" threshold rests on the rule the sheet states, applied by the project MEAL officer and recorded with the reason. A permissive reading lets projects count polished concept notes; a strict reading penalizes weakly documented projects. Counts are not comparable across projects or years until one test per instrument type is applied everywhere.
subMetrics:
None. The indicator is a single count; instrument type, country, value chain, finance type, counterpart type and intended Impact Area are disaggregations, not sub-metrics.

Related but separate indicators, each with its own sheet: KPI-I16 (US dollar volume of finance and co-investment leveraged, this output's downstream impact counterpart) and KPI-O42 (GEYSI-responsive policy or investment instruments). The overlap with KPI-O42 is flagged in Block E.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E officer, jointly with the responsible finance or partnerships lead. Validation: project MEAL officer, against the development test and milestone evidence. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, applying the counting rule and cross-project de-duplication. Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit, which publishes the pooled figure and any fallback-sourced figures separately.
sourceRef: Volume 10 · Policy, finance & market systems — Reference sheet KPI-O38

name: Number of policy-relevant evidence products, syntheses, or decision-support tools delivered by CIMMYT to policymakers and global fora
resultsLevel: Output. An evidence product prepared and delivered to a policy audience is a delivered result. Whether policymakers read, cite or act on the evidence is a change in the behaviour of external actors, measured at outcome level (KPI-OC37).
primaryObjective: PO5 Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities. Contributing: PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Recorded per product and reported as a distribution, under the pathway-wide rule. Evidence products span all five Impact Areas depending on topic, and CGIAR reporting tags each result's Impact Area contribution per product, so the tag varies by item as what is measured varies by item. No single value is forced on the indicator.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest target is SDG 17.14 (enhance policy coherence for sustainable development), but its official indicator 17.14.1 measures the number of countries with policy-coherence mechanisms in place, a country-level institutional property collected from national governments; no SDG indicator counts an organisation's evidence products delivered to policy audiences.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR: the One CGIAR standard indicator set counts "Number of other information products published in the reporting year" under the Knowledge Product output category (an intellectual asset produced by CGIAR as an output of research and development activities); products counted by this indicator will normally also be reported there, but the CGIAR count requires publication only, while this indicator requires documented delivery to a policy audience. The CGIAR Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 minimum data standard specifies the metadata each knowledge product carries in CGIAR reporting (product type, publication date, repository handle, accessibility, licence).
definition: Counts policy-relevant evidence products, syntheses or decision-support tools CIMMYT delivers to policymakers and global fora in the reporting year; counts distinct products delivered to a policy audience. Qualifying products are knowledge products prepared for policy use: policy briefs, evidence syntheses, technical and foresight analyses, modelling or scenario results, and decision-support tools such as dashboards or planning instruments. A product counts only when its delivery to an identified policy audience is documented: a government body, ministry or regulator, a regional or intergovernmental body, or a recognised global forum or policy process.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's research is reaching the bodies and fora where policy decisions are made: the supply step of the evidence-to-policy pathway. CIMMYT's knowledge products are public goods, and delivering them to policymakers and global processes is how the organisation equips the global community to act on food-system disruptions, the climate crisis and structural inequalities. The count establishes the evidence base against which policy influence (KPI-OC37, policies informed by CIMMYT evidence) and enactment (KPI-I15) can be read.
projectSpecificApplication: State which policy audiences the project serves (national ministries, regional bodies, global fora), the product types it plans to deliver, and which records will evidence delivery. Do not change the product-type list, the documented-delivery requirement, or the distinct-product counting rule; if applying the indicator as defined is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count informs: for example a donor-required deliverable schedule of policy briefs, a national policy process the project is contracted to support with evidence, or an internal trigger to review engagement strategy if products are produced but not taken up by the intended audience.
projectTypesNotApplicable: none. Any project type can produce a policy-relevant evidence product
projectTypesRaw: Upstream discovery science; breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI. Not applicable: none. Any project type can produce a policy-relevant evidence product.
unit: Number of products (distinct evidence products, syntheses or decision-support tools)
directionOfChange: Increase, within the delivery scope this output claims: more evidence reaching policy audiences. Volume alone does not indicate influence (see Limitations).
disaggregationRequired: Required: policy scale/level of the receiving audience (local / national / regional / global).
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Product type (policy brief / evidence synthesis / technical or foresight analysis / decision-support tool); country or region; delivery channel (direct transmittal to a government body / presentation at a global forum or intergovernmental process / delivery on official request); topic or CGIAR Impact Area contribution.
unitOfObservation: The distinct evidence product. This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation, whose definition covers a delivered knowledge product alongside innovations, varieties and tools; it is read from the delivery record.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct qualifying products delivered in the reporting year. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: administrative and registry records: the project's M&E deliverable log and CIMMYT's publication and repository records, paired with delivery evidence (transmittal correspondence, forum agendas and presentation records, official requests, tool deployment records). Frame DS4: CGIAR repository and reporting-system records (repository handles and knowledge-product metadata reported to CGIAR), used where project delivery logs are incomplete to list the products for which delivery evidence is then sought; a listing evidences that a product exists and was published, not that it reached a policy audience, so a listed product counts only on the delivery evidence Eligibility criteria and missing data requires. Not applicable DS1: the count is read from institutional records, not collected from survey respondents. Not applicable DS3: delivery of an evidence product is not observable from satellite or geospatial data. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or citizen-generated data cannot verify what CIMMYT delivered to whom.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which deliverable log and repository supplied the product list, and what delivery evidence was held for each counted product.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as projects log product completion and delivery; compiled and de-duplicated annually.
referencePeriod: The reporting year; each annual value stands alone. Annual values are not summed across years without de-duplicating products first. The reporting year is the calendar year, register-wide.
baselineRequired: No. As an annual delivery count the value starts from zero each reporting year; the first reported year serves as the reference point for trend context. No change or impact claim rests on this indicator alone.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool counts from every contributing project.

B: Combination method. Sum distinct products across projects and programs after de-duplication by product identity (title, repository handle or DOI), so a product co-produced by two projects counts once in the institutional figure.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying policy-relevant evidence products, syntheses or briefs for the reporting year. At institutional level, the deduplicated sum of those counts, computed from the records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one product is often reported by more than one project. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels: a product has no plot and no household, so the levels here are reporting levels. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the split by product type, and the number excluded under Eligibility and why.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count does not add to KPI-OC37 or KPI-I15; output, outcome and impact connect through the theory of change, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: de-duplicate by product identity across projects and years. Overlap with sibling indicators must be named, never summed: a land-use decision-support tool delivered to a policy audience counts under KPI-O32 as well, subject there and audience here; a participatory research product informing agricultural decisions is counted by KPI-O33, a convened dialogue or forum by KPI-O37 (the event, not the products tabled at it), and an agenda-shaping product without a specific policymaker audience by the institutional KPI-O58. A product may also appear in CGIAR knowledge-product reporting; that is a separate reporting stream, not an addition to this count.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: products of the named types, produced by CIMMYT or with CIMMYT as named lead or co-producer, whose delivery to an identified policy audience in the reporting year is documented at the evidence floor this sheet sets: a dated transmittal record naming the recipient body, or a documented presentation at a convened policy forum with the audience recorded. A response to an official request, a tool handover or a deployment for a policy user qualifies on the same terms, dated and naming the receiving body; an undated record, or one naming no recipient, does not evidence delivery.

Exclusion: peer-reviewed journal articles as such (they are counted in CGIAR publication reporting; an article counts here only if it was itself formally transmitted to a policy audience); blogs, newsletters, press items and general communications products (CGIAR quality assurance treats these as linked evidence, not stand-alone results); internal documents; agenda-shaping thought-leadership products without a specific policymaker audience, which belong to the institutional indicator KPI-O58. An agroecosystem or land-use subject is not an exclusion: a land-use tool delivered to a policy audience counts here for its audience and under KPI-O32 for its subject, and the two are never summed.
limitations: Measures delivery, not influence: a delivered product says nothing about whether it was read, cited or used. Policy use is KPI-OC37's outcome; read this count only as the supply step of the evidence-to-policy pathway.

Product counts reward volume: many short briefs count more than one substantial synthesis, and product significance varies enormously. Pair the count with its product-type disaggregation and, where possible, with qualitative evidence of engagement.

The delivery boundary is evidence-dependent: informal channels (advisory conversations, embedded staff, technical committees) move evidence into policy without a documentable transmittal, so the count understates real evidence flow; conversely a documented delivery to an uninterested recipient still counts.

Comparability across projects depends on discipline about the product-type list and the delivery-evidence standard; CGIAR's own review found that unspecified information-product counts mix dozens of product types and lose comparability.

A rise in the count means CIMMYT placed more evidence into policy spaces, not that policy improved or that CIMMYT caused any policy change; the contribution narrative runs through KPI-OC37 and KPI-I15.
subMetrics: None. Product types, policy scales and delivery channels are disaggregations of the same count, not separately calculated metrics. Related indicators with their own sheets: KPI-O32, KPI-O33, KPI-O37, KPI-O40, and KPI-OC37 (policies informed by CIMMYT evidence), the outcome this count feeds in the results chain.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the policy engagement / foresight lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project teams maintaining deliverable logs and delivery evidence; CIMMYT publications and repository staff for product metadata. Validation: project MEAL officer (product type qualifies, delivery documented, no duplicate). Calculation: project M&E applying the distinct-product rule; cross-project de-duplication by the CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 10 · Policy, finance & market systems — Reference sheet KPI-O39

name: Number of institutions whose capacity to generate, access, or use CIMMYT evidence has been strengthened
resultsLevel: Output. The count reports a delivered result: entities that received defined, documented capacity-strengthening support. Whether an entity then uses evidence differently is a change, measured at outcome level (KPI-OC37). The counting boundary sits at delivery of support meeting the defined threshold, which is what keeps the indicator at output level.
primaryObjective: PO5 Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved), PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Recorded per counted institution's evidence-use domain and reported as a distribution, under the pathway-wide rule. Evidence-use capacity is domain-agnostic: the same strengthened ministry may apply CIMMYT evidence to food-security, livelihoods or climate policy, so the tag varies by item as what is measured varies by item. No single value is forced on the indicator.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest target is SDG 17.9 (enhance international support for capacity-building in developing countries), but its official indicator 17.9.1 measures the dollar value of official development assistance for technical cooperation, not entities strengthened, so there is no direct correspondence.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR: the results framework carries a capacity-change outcome standard indicator (change in capacity of key individuals, organizations and networks); this count feeds that field as supporting output-level evidence rather than mapping one-to-one, since the CGIAR indicator claims capacity change while this one counts support delivered. The boundary this sheet draws is the same one a capacity-strengthening measure needs: intentional resources, jointly defined priorities and a documented process are in; untailored open training and individual professional development are out. Measured performance improvement would place the indicator at outcome level, and this one counts support delivered.
definition: Counts institutions whose capacity to generate, access or use CIMMYT evidence was strengthened in the reporting year, counted once each against a defined capacity threshold. An institution is an organization holding authority over policy, regulation, public investment or programme design; the decision-makers within it are the people through whom its capacity changes, but individuals are not counted as a second unit, since a count mixing a ministry with a single trainee would weigh them the same. Capacity to generate, access or use evidence covers three abilities: generating, producing or commissioning analysis with CIMMYT data, methods or tools; accessing, locating CIMMYT evidence relevant to a decision under way; and using, applying that evidence in the policy process, from agenda-setting through design to review. An institution counts as strengthened when CIMMYT (or a partner acting on its behalf) delivered structured, documented support against needs identified with the institution during the reporting year.
rationale: Answers how many policy actors CIMMYT equipped each year to work with its evidence. Evidence products and dialogues only translate into evidence-informed policy if decision-makers can absorb, appraise and apply what they receive, so this count is the absorptive-capacity link of the research-to-policy pathway: it establishes the population of strengthened policy actors whose use of evidence in actual policy instruments is measured at outcome level (KPI-OC37), and contributes evidence toward the CGIAR capacity-change outcome category.
projectSpecificApplication: State which institutions the project supports, the policy domain and geographic scope, the forms of support delivered, and the records documenting each entity's support against the defined threshold. Do not change the once-per-entity rule, the threshold requirement, or the exclusion of incidental contact; if the indicator as defined is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count informs: a donor-required capacity-strengthening indicator, a policy-engagement strategy investing in specific ministries or agencies, or a trigger to rebalance support where targeted institutions are not progressing toward the threshold.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work engages no decision-maker or institution in that capacity
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI. Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work engages no decision-maker or institution in that capacity.
unit: Number of institutions
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more institutions met the capacity threshold for strengthened capacity to generate, access or use CIMMYT evidence. Each institution counts once in a year, regardless of how many capacity dimensions were strengthened.
disaggregationRequired: Required: partner/institution type, on the confirmed 13-category list (government ministry or agency, parliamentary body, regulatory authority, subnational government, regional or global body, and private-sector or civil-society umbrella organization among its categories).
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Capacity dimension strengthened (generate / access / use; an entity supported on several dimensions appears in each subtotal, so dimension subtotals may exceed the unique count and are never summed); sex and age composition of the individuals who received the support inside each counted institution (male/female at minimum), reported as a characteristic of the support delivered and never as a cut of the institution count, since individuals are not a counted unit here; policy scale (local / national / regional / global); country or region; newly versus previously strengthened.
unitOfObservation: Organization. The settled rule is institutions only, disaggregated by type using the confirmed 13-category list; individuals are not counted as a second unit, since a count mixing a ministry with a single trainee weighs them the same.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of unique institutions that received structured, documented capacity-strengthening support from CIMMYT in the reporting year and met the defined capacity threshold. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: project administrative and M&E records: capacity development plans or agreements with each entity, training and advisory registries, and tool-deployment records, each carrying the institution's name, type, headquarters-or-branch counting level, location, capacity dimension, capacity need and dates of support. Fallback DS1: a structured verification interview with the supported entity, used where project records are incomplete or support ran through an intermediary partner whose records CIMMYT cannot access; values from this route are flagged as fallback-sourced. Not applicable: DS3, DS4, DS5. Capacity strengthening of specific policy actors by CIMMYT is not observable from satellite data, appears in no secondary or international database, and cannot be verified through crowdsourced data.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role each institution rests on, which records supplied the entity list, and how de-duplication was done; for any on the Fallback, why project records were not usable.
collectionInstrument: For the DS1 fallback: a verification questionnaire capturing the capacity need identified with the institution, the support received, its form, dates, capacity dimension, and the institution's type and headquarters-or-branch counting level; respondent is the decision-maker or an authorized representative of the institution, in person or by phone. The recommended DS2 route uses a standard capacity-strengthening record template capturing the same fields at delivery.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as projects log capacity-strengthening activities and completion; compiled and de-duplicated annually.
referencePeriod: The reporting year; each annual value stands alone (see Limitations on why annual values are never summed). The reporting year is the calendar year, register-wide.
baselineRequired: No. As an annual delivery count the value starts from zero each reporting year; the first reported year is the reference point for trend context. Change in evidence use is measured at KPI-OC37 against its own evidence-of-contribution rule.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool the institutions for which project records evidence the need, what was delivered, who received it and the date under Eligibility (Recommended); an institution for which any of these rests only on the Fallback verification interview is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note naming it, never blended in; the same project's record-evidenced institutions stay pooled.

B: Combination method. Sum unique institutions across projects after de-duplication by identity (institution name and location).

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of unique institutions that met the capacity threshold in the reporting year, deduplicated on the identifier Block E names. At institutional level, the count deduplicated again across projects, since one institution engaged by two projects is one institution. Institutions are the only counted unit: individual decision-makers supported inside an institution change that institution's capacity and are never counted as a second unit, since an individual and an institution are not commensurable and a mixed total would change with the composition of the count. Where identifiers cannot be reconciled, the institutional figure is labelled an upper bound. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the number of institutions reported alongside because they rest on the Fallback, and the cumulative distinct-entity figure across years alongside the annual count, matching KPI-O27. The threshold is fixed for the register and is not a per-project choice.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count does not add to KPI-OC37; the output and outcome connect through the theory of change, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: de-duplicate by entity identity across projects and partners; never count both an institution and its individual members for the same organizational support; where two projects strengthened branches of the same national body, state the counting level (headquarters or branch) and apply it consistently, otherwise label the pooled figure an upper estimate. Across indicators, overlap is named, never summed: the same decision-makers may appear in KPI-O37 (dialogues), KPI-O39 or KPI-O32/KPI-O33 (products and tools), or KPI-O04 (trainees); those count events, products and trainees, different units from the entities counted here, and none may be combined with this count. The policy instruments these entities go on to shape belong to KPI-OC37.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Repeated observations: one count per entity per reporting year, whatever the number of support activities it received. An entity counted in an earlier year counts again only where new defined support meeting the threshold is delivered in that year, and the cumulative distinct-entity figure is reported alongside the annual count, matching KPI-O27, so a reader can separate the year's work from the stock of entities ever strengthened; an entity supported by two CIMMYT projects in the same year counts once at institutional level; when an institution was supported as an organization, its individual members are not additionally counted.
limitations: Measures support delivered, not evidence used: capacity is potential, visible only when exercised, so a strengthened entity is one that received defined support, not one that demonstrably changed how it makes policy; read this count only alongside KPI-OC37.

One institution is not one scale of influence: a national ministry and a subnational agency each count as one, so the headline number says nothing about the reach or authority behind it; read it through the required partner/institution type breakdown, and through the headquarters-or-branch counting level the aggregation rule fixes.

The capacity threshold drives the number, which is why it is fixed institutionally rather than per project (see Eligibility criteria): without a firm minimum, light-touch contact inflates the count; with a per-project minimum, the figures could not be pooled at all.

Annual values are not cumulative: the same institution can receive support across several years, so summing years overstates the distinct entities strengthened; multi-year totals require de-duplication across the whole period.
subMetrics: None. Institution types and capacity dimensions are disaggregations of the same unique count, not separately calculated metrics. Related indicators have their own sheets: KPI-O37 (policy dialogues and fora convened), KPI-O39 (policy-relevant evidence products delivered), KPI-O04 (individuals trained), and KPI-OC37 (the outcome this count feeds in the results chain).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the policy engagement / partnerships lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project teams and implementing partners maintaining capacity-strengthening records per entity. Validation: project MEAL officer (documentation complete, threshold applied, unit and type classified). Calculation: project M&E, applying the unique-count rule; cross-project de-duplication by the CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 10 · Policy, finance & market systems — Reference sheet KPI-O40

name: Number of thought-leadership and advocacy products (flagship reports, position papers, policy briefs) produced to shape the global agrifood agenda
resultsLevel: Output. The count reports a delivery, thought-leadership and advocacy products CIMMYT produced and released, and the Core reads an Institutional-branch level from the indicator statement itself: a count of deliverables a corporate function produced is an output. Whether anyone reads, cites or takes up the products is a change, and their media and agenda uptake is measured by the outcome indicator KPI-OC61.
indicatorScope: Institutional. Measures CIMMYT's own production of agenda-shaping publications, a corporate communications and thought-leadership activity, not a result delivered to an external population. Reported once, at Center level, from CIMMYT's own publication and communications records; no project-specific layer.
primaryObjective: Influence & Advocacy, the institutional enabler component the 2030 Strategy names "Influence and Advocacy for Impact". Not a PO1 to PO5 mission objective: institutional indicators map to one of the five enabler components, and the register's Strategy Component column for this row reads Influence and Advocacy for Impact. Contribution by cross-reference only: agenda-shaping work reinforces the mission objectives, most directly PO5 (the global community takes informed, coordinated measures), but that link runs through the mission-branch policy indicators, not through a second primary tag here.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable (the default for Institutional indicators unless a genuine direct link exists). Producing advocacy publications is a way of working across all five Impact Areas rather than a result within any one of them: the products may address climate, nutrition or inclusion, but the indicator measures CIMMYT's publishing activity, not an Impact Area result.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator corresponds to a count of an organization's own thought-leadership or advocacy publications; the SDG framework measures development results, not institutional communications output, so None is recorded rather than a stretched mapping.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR technical reporting uses Knowledge products as one of its output result types, defined in the One CGIAR Standard Indicators report as "an intellectual asset produced by the CGIAR, as an output of research and development activities", with reports and briefs among the named examples, and carrying a standard indicator counting other information products published in the reporting year. The CGIAR Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 retains the category and sets its minimum metadata in Annex 3. KPI-O58 counts a deliberately narrower, agenda-shaping subset of that broad category, so values reported here nest inside, but never equal, CIMMYT's total knowledge-product reporting to CGIAR.
definition: Counts the distinct thought-leadership and advocacy products that CIMMYT produces and publicly releases in the reporting year to shape the global agrifood agenda: flagship reports, position papers, policy briefs and comparable institutional publications whose purpose is to influence how the global or regional agrifood debate is framed. A product counts once, in the year of its first release, regardless of how many formats, languages or channels carry it. The indicator is deliberately narrower than a count of all CIMMYT knowledge products: peer-reviewed articles and routine research outputs are excluded.
rationale: The 2030 Strategy's Influence and Advocacy for Impact component commits CIMMYT to invest in focus areas "to shape the global agrifood systems agenda" in pursuit of its vision to be a "global thought leader and change agent". This indicator is the countable trace of that commitment: it tells the Influence and Advocacy component, institutional reporting and funders how much agenda-shaping material CIMMYT put into the global debate each year, and supplies the production base whose media and agenda uptake the outcome indicator KPI-OC61 measures. The strategy also states that CIMMYT "will not engage in lobbying or intervene in political processes", so influence is tracked as published evidence and argument, never as political activity.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional scope): agenda-shaping publications are issued in CIMMYT's institutional name, not by projects.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Number of products (count of distinct products first released in the reporting year).
directionOfChange: Not directional. A rising count is an increase in advocacy effort, not in influence, and volume of products without reach means little; treating an increase as the intended movement would reward publishing more. Read together with KPI-OC61, which carries the reach reading.
disaggregationRequired: Required: product type, the register's own required disaggregation. A closed list: flagship report; position paper; policy brief; other agenda-shaping product (a bounded residual, each product named when reported). Sex and age do not apply: the unit is a document, not a person.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional scope; no project layer).
unitOfObservation: The individual product (document). This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct products meeting every inclusion criterion, first publicly released in the reporting year. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative and registry data): CIMMYT's own publication repository and communications records, maintained by the communications and knowledge-management function. Each record supplies what the calculation needs: title, product type, first release date, publisher, plus the metadata CGIAR already requires for knowledge products (product type with peer-review status, publication date, handle, accessibility, license), so this indicator adds only a classification step, agenda-shaping or not, to records CIMMYT keeps anyway. Fallback DS4 (Secondary and international databases): CIMMYT's knowledge products as recorded in CGIAR's results reporting systems, used only if the internal repository is incomplete; a value built this way must be flagged, because CGIAR's category is broader and the agenda-shaping subset must be re-identified product by product. Not applicable: DS1 (Censuses and surveys), DS3 (Geospatial and Earth observation) and DS5 (Citizen-generated data): whether CIMMYT released a publication is a documented fact in its own records, not something surveys, satellites or crowdsourcing can establish.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). The operation is a query of the publication repository and communications records with the inclusion and exclusion filters applied, followed by document review of any ambiguous record.
collectionFrequency: Continuous. Records are created as products are released; the indicator is extracted once per reporting year and can be extracted more often without additional collection.
referencePeriod: The reporting year: a product counts if its first public release date falls within that year. The reporting year is the calendar year, register-wide.
baselineRequired: Yes. A count of this kind is only readable against previous years, so the first year extracted under this definition is the reference point. Fallback: reconstruct earlier years retrospectively from the publication repository, feasible because release dates are permanent attributes of the record; if the classification cannot be applied consistently to earlier years, monitor from the first year onward and make no change claims against the earlier period.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: Not applicable. This is an Institutional indicator reported once at Center level; there are no project instances to pool. For portability across CGIAR centers, do not sum center counts without deduplication: a jointly branded flagship report would be counted by every publishing center.

B: Combination method. Sum: the count of distinct qualifying products first released in the reporting year, deduplicated on the product identifier. Never averaged.

C: Levels and operations. Computed once, at institutional level, as the count of distinct thought-leadership and advocacy products first publicly released in the reporting year, deduplicated on the product identifier per Block E. There is no level beneath it, because no programme or unit holds a share of an institutional count. Where a view by product type or audience is wanted, it is recomputed from that subset's own records, never taken as a share of the institutional figure. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels. Also report: the split by product type, the number excluded under Eligibility, and that the uptake of these products is KPI-OC61 and is never combined with this count.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This output count does not add to its outcome KPI-OC61 (reach and uptake of CIMMYT thought leadership); the two connect as a narrative, production then reach, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: deduplicate by product, so translations, format variants and channel re-releases of one product count once. Two named overlap risks: a policy brief can both shape the open agenda and be delivered to specific policymakers, and a product doing both counts in both, for its two different audiences. The overlap is named on the shared product identifier and the two counts are never summed; and every product counted here also sits inside CIMMYT's broad knowledge-product reporting to CGIAR, so this count must never be added to a total knowledge-product count, in which it is already contained.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: issued in CIMMYT's institutional name, alone or as a named publisher on a co-published product (no lead-publisher test is applied; joint products are flagged as such); publicly released, not internal; stated purpose is to inform or shape the global or regional agrifood agenda (flagship report, position paper, policy brief or comparable product); first release date in the reporting year.

Exclusion: peer-reviewed journal articles and other routine research knowledge products (reported to CGIAR under the broad knowledge-product category, not here); internal strategies, project reports and donor deliverables; marketing and event materials; translations, reprints or format variants of a product already counted.

Missing data: a record lacking a release date or product type is verified against the document itself before counting; a record that cannot be verified as a released CIMMYT product is not counted; no imputation.

Repeated observations: each product counts once, in the year of first release; a recurring series (for example an annual flagship report) counts each substantively new edition as a new product, while a re-issue with no substantive new content does not count again.
limitations: Measures production, not influence. A count of releases says nothing about whether anyone read, cited or acted on them; read it only together with KPI-OC61 (reach and uptake) before making any statement about CIMMYT's thought leadership.

The count moves with the classification boundary. "Agenda-shaping" is a judgement, and a wide reading of the residual category inflates the count without any change in activity; a closed product-type list, applied by one function, keeps the series comparable across years.

Counts fragment easily. Splitting one argument across three briefs triples the count; the product-type disaggregation makes this visible but does not prevent it, so a year-on-year jump is checked against the underlying product list.

The overlap with KPI-O39 is by design: a product that shapes the open agenda and is also delivered to a policy audience counts in both, so a combined reading de-duplicates on the shared product identifier and never sums the two.

By design this indicator claims nothing political. The 2030 Strategy rules out lobbying, so a movement in this count must never be presented as evidence of policy change; policy outcomes are measured in the mission branch of the register.
subMetrics: None. The product-type breakdown is a disaggregation of the same count, not a separately calculated metric. Reach, citations and media uptake are not sub-metrics here; they constitute the outcome indicator KPI-OC61, which has its own reference sheet.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: the CIMMYT communications and knowledge-management function, as custodian of the publication repository and release records. Validation: the same function, confirming each counted record is a released, CIMMYT-branded, agenda-shaping product and flagging any product also delivered to a policy audience (KPI-O39). Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, applying the inclusion, exclusion and deduplication rules. Approval: the senior manager accountable for the Influence and Advocacy component. Reporting: CIMMYT MEAL unit into institutional reporting.
sourceRef: Volume 10 · Policy, finance & market systems — Reference sheet KPI-O58

name: Number of value chains adopting sustainable or inclusive models
resultsLevel: Outcome. Adoption is a change in the behaviour and relationships of external market actors, which is the Core's definition of an outcome: the chain's actors, not the research team, decide to run the model.
indicatorScope: Mission. Measures a behaviour change among external market actors delivered through project implementation, so it carries the full project-specific layer.
primaryObjective: PO4 Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient, grounded in sub-objective 4.4 ("Market driven systems and emerging models are harnessed to improve agrifood systems and their sustainability"). The register's PO3 and PO5 are contributing objectives only: adopted inclusive models widen smallholder access to services, income and market opportunities (3.2, 3.3) and create the value-adding opportunities that make farming attractive (5.3).
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs, the pathway ruling's fixed value for the market-systems indicators: whatever the commodity or the model type, the measured result is market performance for smallholders, so one value fits every counted adoption.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator counts value chains adopting sustainable or inclusive models. The nearest neighbour, target 12.6, encourages companies "to adopt sustainable practices", but its indicator 12.6.1 counts individual companies publishing sustainability reports (custodians UNCTAD and UNEP): a corporate reporting behaviour, not chain-level adoption of a business model.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR standard results reporting: this indicator reports within the Innovation Use result category, defined as "the extent to which an innovation is being used, by which type of users and under which conditions" (One CGIAR Standard Indicators report); the CGIAR Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 applies the same split, innovation development at output level and innovation use at outcome level.
definition: Counts the value chains that adopt a sustainable or inclusive model during the reporting year, where the adoption was informed by CIMMYT's work. A value chain is the connected set of actors that move a commodity from production to consumption: producers, aggregators, processors, traders, buyers and their service providers. Adoption means the chain's own actors run the model in their regular commercial operations, independently of CIMMYT project delivery. The boundary with KPI-O36 is the level of the counted behaviour: a model run on a single operator's own account is a deployment (KPI-O36); adoption here is chain-level, the model running in the chain's regular commercial operations. A model that operates only because a CIMMYT project runs it counts in neither. Each value chain is counted once in the reporting year, whatever the number of qualifying models it adopts.
rationale: Answers whether the market and business models CIMMYT develops and deploys are taken up by value-chain actors themselves: the behaviour-change evidence between CIMMYT's own deployment work (KPI-O36) and the share of market volume flowing through such models (KPI-I13), and the outcome evidence for 2030 Strategy sub-objective 4.4.
projectSpecificApplication: Describe which value chains this project works in (commodity, countries, market segment), which sustainable or inclusive models it promotes, which chain actors are expected to adopt them, and the adoption evidence applied (see Calculation method). Do not restate or alter the institutional definition, unit or counting rule; if the adoption test cannot be applied in this context, raise it with the MEAL focal point.
projectSpecificRationale: State why this project tracks the indicator: the donor requirement or results-framework line it reports against, and the decision it informs (for example, a deployed model with no independent adoption after a set period triggers a redesign or exit review).
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work operates in no value chain that could adopt a sustainable model
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI. Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work operates in no value chain that could adopt a sustainable model.
unit: Number of value chains (distinct value chains adopting at least one qualifying model)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more value chains adopted at least one qualifying sustainable or inclusive model. The count says how many chains adopted, not how deeply; KPI-I13 carries the depth reading.
disaggregationRequired: Required: commodity or value chain, as recorded in the register: the institutional figure must decompose into the named chains behind it (for example wheat in Ethiopia), or a pooled count cannot be interpreted or de-duplicated.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country and sub-national market; model type (sustainable sourcing arrangement / inclusive market platform / other business or service model); adopting-actor type (private company, cooperative or farmer organization, public entity, financial institution); intended CGIAR Impact Area.
unitOfObservation: The value chain. This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation.
calculationSummary:
Value = the count of distinct value chains that, during the reporting year, (a) are delineated as commodity by country, which is also the de-duplication key, (b) meet the adoption test below, and (c) have a documented CIMMYT contribution to the adopted model ("informed by CIMMYT"), which means documented CIMMYT design or technical input to the model, evidenced in a dated record. Convening the parties, hosting a discussion or commenting on someone else's design does not qualify, and prior counting under KPI-O34 or KPI-O36 is not required.

Adoption evidence. Documented evidence that at least two of the chain's actors run the model in regular commercial operations at operating volumes on their own account, without CIMMYT executing any part of it; a model run by a single operator is a deployment (KPI-O36) and does not count here. Adoption is a behaviour, and the only evidence that it occurred is the model in use at a scale that is not a pilot; institutionalization or dissemination independent of CIMMYT (non-donor financing, incorporation into policies or guidelines, market introduction) corroborates adoption but does not substitute for operation at operating volumes.

Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource:
