Recommended, DS2 (Administrative and registry data): the project's own adoption register with partner reporting, evidenced per counted chain by a dated adoption record, documentation that chain actors operate the model (sourcing contracts, platform transaction records, certification or policy documents, financing agreements), and the documented CIMMYT contribution.

Fallback, DS1 (Censuses and surveys): structured key-informant interviews with the chain's lead actors, only where partner documentation is not accessible, used to obtain dated written confirmation from at least two of the chain's actors that they run the model in regular commercial operations at operating volumes on their own account; a chain evidenced only this way is Fallback-sourced, since self-reported adoption without operating records is weaker evidence.

Not applicable, stated explicitly: DS3 (Geospatial and Earth observation): a business model is not an observable surface feature. DS4 (Secondary and international databases): results databases republish the same project reporting and add no independent evidence of adoption. DS5 (Citizen-generated and other non-traditional data): crowdsourced data cannot evidence which model a chain operates or CIMMYT's contribution to it.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which route each chain rests on; for any chain on the Fallback, explain briefly why partner documentation could not be obtained.
collectionInstrument: For the DS1 fallback only: a structured key-informant interview protocol covering the model in operation, volumes transacted, independence from CIMMYT delivery, and the CIMMYT contribution. Respondent: the person responsible for the model's operation in each adopting actor. Mode: face-to-face or phone interview, with documentary follow-up wherever possible. Not applicable when the Recommended DS2 source is used.
collectionFrequency: Continuous recording as adoption evidence is obtained, compiled once per reporting year.
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the adoption event falls: a within-year count of chain-years in which a chain adopted, not a cumulative stock, so a chain adopting two models in one year is one count and not two, and a chain adopting a further distinct model in a later year generates a new event in that year. The reporting year is the calendar year, register-wide.
baselineRequired: No. The baseline is zero by construction: each year counts chains meeting the adoption test within that year. Prior-year values serve trend comparison; a partial start-up year is noted separately, not annualized.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Across projects: sum distinct chains evidenced in projects' own adoption registers (Recommended); a chain whose adoption is evidenced only through the Fallback key-informant confirmations is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, not blended in, and the same project's Recommended-sourced chains are summed.

B: Combination method. The institutional figure is the sum of distinct value chains across projects after de-duplication; never average project counts.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying value chains adopting sustainable or inclusive models for the reporting year. At institutional level, the deduplicated sum of those counts, computed from the records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one value chain is often reported by more than one project. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels: a value chain has no plot and no household, so the levels here are reporting levels. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the models adopted, the number excluded under Eligibility and why, and the number of chains reported alongside because their adoption rests on the Fallback confirmations.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: No. This count does not combine arithmetically with KPI-O36 or KPI-I13: the same model legitimately appears under O36 in its deployment year and here when a chain adopts it. Levels connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative; adoption ratios require cohort tracking by a stable identifier, never dividing one indicator's same-year value by another's.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: the main risk of this indicator. Several CIMMYT projects, or CIMMYT and another CGIAR center, often work in the same value chain, and each may claim the adoption. Count each distinct chain once institutionally, de-duplicating on the delineation the Calculation method sets, commodity by country, and label the pooled number an upper estimate where chain delineations cannot be reconciled. Market segment is deliberately not part of the key: it is finer than most project records can support and would let one chain be counted several times by slicing it.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion and exclusion. Include adoption of any sustainable or inclusive model informed by CIMMYT, whether or not first deployed under KPI-O36. Exclude: chains where the model operates only inside CIMMYT project delivery; adoption events with no documented CIMMYT design or technical input to the model, evidenced in a dated record; expressions of interest, signed intentions or pilots that have not met the adoption test.

Missing data. A candidate chain with no documented adoption evidence is excluded rather than estimated, except that a chain whose adoption is evidenced only by the Fallback confirmations in Data source is reported as Aggregation rule Block A sets out; report the number of excluded candidates alongside the value.

Repeated observations. A chain adopting more than one qualifying model in the same year counts once (register rule). A chain counted in an earlier year counts again in a later year when it adopts a further, distinct model: the indicator measures adoption events, and a chain taking up a second model has adopted twice.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only. "Informed by CIMMYT" is a documented contribution, not attribution: chains adopt models in response to prices, buyers, regulation and competitors as much as to research evidence.

The counted objects are not equivalent. One adopting chain can be a national wheat economy, another a district-level horticulture chain; the count carries no information on chain size, volume or number of actors, so it is not a measure of reach or benefit. KPI-I13 carries the volume narrative.

The adoption boundary rests on the rule the sheet states, applied by the project MEAL officer and recorded with the reason. The two-actor minimum fixes when a chain has adopted but not how much of it: a chain in which two actors run the model and one in which most do count the same, and KPI-I13 carries the depth reading.

Persistence is not captured. A chain counted as adopting stays counted even if its actors abandon the model the next year; any cumulative "chains adopting to date" claim needs a check of whether earlier adoptions still operate.

A rise means more chains met the documented adoption test, not that sustainability outcomes improved. Whether the adopted models deliver environmental or inclusion benefits is measured by the environmental sustainability and income indicators, not by this count.
subMetrics:
None. Commodity or value chain, country, model type, adopting-actor type and intended Impact Area are disaggregations, not sub-metrics.

End-user adoption is deliberately not counted in this pathway. A count or share of farmers, enterprises, cooperatives or institutions adopting CIMMYT-enabled market, policy or financial innovations was considered and is not added here. Adoption in this pathway is measured at the level the innovation operates at: the value chain adopting the model (this indicator) and the share of market volume flowing through those models (KPI-I13). A person-level or enterprise-level adoption count is the construct KPI-OC16 already carries in Innovation development & scaling, and running it in both pathways creates the counting overlap the sheets here exist to prevent, with no way to tell the two totals apart. The cross-reference is stated and the indicator is not duplicated.

Related indicators, each with its own sheet: KPI-O35 (multi-stakeholder platforms or hubs established), KPI-O36 (market or business-model innovations deployed, the output feeding this outcome), KPI-I13 (share of market volume or value through sustainable or inclusive models, the pathway’s impact measure).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E officer, jointly with the responsible market-systems lead and reporting partners. Validation: project MEAL officer, against the adoption test and the contribution evidence. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (counting rule and cross-project de-duplication of chains). Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit, which publishes pooled and fallback-sourced figures separately.
sourceRef: Volume 10 · Policy, finance & market systems — Reference sheet KPI-OC35

name: Number of public policies, strategies, or regulations informed by CIMMYT-generated evidence
resultsLevel: Outcome. A public body modifying a policy, strategy or regulation is a change in policy among partners, which is the Core's definition of an outcome; CGIAR's quality-assurance guidance uses policy actors using research knowledge as its canonical outcome example, and expressly rules that briefing papers aimed at influencing someone else's policy are outputs, not policy-change outcomes.
primaryObjective: PO5 Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities. Evidence-informed public instruments are the concrete form informed, coordinated measures take. Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved), because the instruments this chain feeds support smallholder resilience (KPI-I15); and PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient), because policy and regulation are the system levers that make agrifood-system change durable.
cgiarImpactArea: Recorded per instrument and reported as a distribution, under the pathway-wide rule. A policy may concern climate, nutrition, livelihoods or markets, so the tag varies by item as what is measured varies by item, and CGIAR tags each policy-change result's Impact Area individually at reporting. No single value is forced on the indicator.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest target is SDG 17.14 (enhance policy coherence for sustainable development), but its indicator 17.14.1 counts countries with policy-coherence mechanisms in place, a country-level property reported by national governments (custodians UNEP and OECD); no SDG indicator counts policy instruments informed by an organisation's research evidence.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Results Framework: direct correspondence to the standard outcome indicator "Number of new or significantly updated policies / strategies / legal instruments" under the Policy Change outcome category; this sheet reuses that category's definition verbatim, labeled CGIAR, so values feed CGIAR technical reporting without translation. The CGIAR Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 minimum data standard specifies the metadata each policy-change result carries (policy type, stage, owner).
definition: Counts public policies, strategies, regulations, programs, budgets or investments informed by CIMMYT-generated evidence in the reporting year, with documented evidence of CIMMYT's contribution; the wider CGIAR scope applies, because a budget line is often where a policy takes effect and a narrower reading would exclude the clearest evidence of influence. The indicator reuses the CGIAR policy-change definition, explicitly labeled CGIAR: policy instruments, local to global, modified in design or implementation, with evidence that the change was informed by CGIAR research. "Informed" therefore means more than exposure: the instrument itself, or how it is implemented, changed, and a documented evidence trail links that change to CIMMYT evidence. Producing evidence aimed at influencing a policy is not policy change: briefing papers are outputs, counted under KPI-O39; an instrument counts here only once it demonstrably changed.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's evidence is changing the content or implementation of public decisions, the influence step of the evidence-to-policy pathway: KPI-O37 and KPI-O39 count the engagements convened and the evidence delivered, this indicator counts the instruments that changed with a documented CIMMYT contribution to the change, and KPI-I15 counts those enacted. Because the definition is CGIAR's own policy-change standard, values report directly into CGIAR reporting and are comparable across centers, serving institutional reporting under Primary Objective 5 and donor reporting on policy influence.
projectSpecificApplication: State which policy processes and jurisdictions the project engages (for example a national fertilizer subsidy reform, a regional seed regulation harmonisation), which CIMMYT evidence streams feed them, and which records will document the contribution. Do not change the modified-instrument requirement, the documented-evidence requirement, or the counting rules; if the indicator as defined is not feasible in the project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision or donor commitment this count informs: for example a donor-required policy-influence outcome, a national process the project is contracted to inform, or an internal trigger to review the engagement strategy when evidence is delivered (KPI-O39) but no instrument moves within a set period.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work informs no public policy instrument directly
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI. Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work informs no public policy instrument directly.
unit: Number of policy instruments (distinct public policies, strategies, regulations, programs, budgets or investments)
directionOfChange: Increase, within the influence scope this outcome claims: more public instruments carrying CIMMYT evidence. The count says nothing about the significance or implementation of any instrument (see Limitations).
disaggregationRequired: Required: policy scale or level, on CGIAR's four levels (local / national / regional / global), set on this sheet's authority. A regional instrument is reported at regional: folded into national or global it is misfiled either way, and two projects filing the same instrument at different levels by choice is the comparability defect this cut exists to prevent.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Policy type, using the CGIAR typology (policy or strategy / legal instrument / program, budget or investment); policy stage (research taken up, change not yet enacted / enacted / evidence of policy impact); country or region; topic or CGIAR Impact Area contribution; implementing owner.
unitOfObservation: The policy instrument. This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation, whose definition covers a policy instrument alongside innovations, varieties and tools; it is read from the documentary record the owning organisation holds.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct qualifying policy instruments in the reporting year. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: administrative and registry records: the project's policy-engagement log and an evidence dossier per counted instrument (the instrument text or its official announcement, plus the contribution evidence listed in the calculation method). Fallback DS1: structured key-informant interviews with policy actors, in the style of outcome harvesting, used where the instrument changed but no documentary acknowledgement of CIMMYT's contribution exists; interview-established contribution is flagged fallback-sourced and read with lower confidence. A written confirmation from the policy owner obtained through such an interview is the first evidence form in Eligibility criteria and missing data and is read as DS2 evidence, not as a Fallback. Not applicable DS4 as a standalone source: official gazettes and policy databases evidence that an instrument exists or changed, never that CIMMYT contributed, so they serve inside the DS2 dossier, not as an independent source. Not applicable DS3: policy change is not observable from satellite data. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced data cannot verify a documented link between CIMMYT evidence and a public instrument.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which route each instrument rests on, which engagement log supplied the candidate list, and what contribution evidence was held per instrument; for any resting on interview evidence alone, why documentary evidence was unavailable.
collectionInstrument: Applicable to the DS1 fallback only: a key-informant interview protocol asking who changed what, in which instrument, and what role CIMMYT evidence played. Respondents: officials of the owning organisation or documented process participants. Mode: face-to-face or remote interview, with written notes retained as evidence. For the Recommended DS2 source: not applicable, administrative source.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as projects log policy engagements and contribution evidence; compiled and de-duplicated annually.
referencePeriod: The reporting year of the modification; each annual value stands alone. The modification date is the date of the dated document that first shows the changed text or the changed implementation; where that document is the enacted instrument itself, the instrument can enter this count and KPI-I15 in the same year. Annual values are not summed across years without de-duplicating instruments first. The reporting year is the calendar year, register-wide.
baselineRequired: No. As an annual count the value starts from zero each reporting year; the first reported year serves as the reference point for trend context. No change or impact claim rests on this indicator alone.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: sum distinct instruments whose contribution is evidenced in the project's dossier (Recommended); an instrument whose contribution is established only by the Fallback key-informant interview, with its written notes retained, is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, not blended in, and the same project's Recommended-sourced instruments are summed.

B: Combination method. Sum distinct instruments across projects and programs after de-duplication on the shared instrument identifier, the persistent identifier carrying the instrument's official title, issuing body, jurisdiction and version, the same key KPI-O42, KPI-OC39, KPI-OC34 and KPI-I15 use, so a policy informed through two CIMMYT projects counts once institutionally and the informed-to-enacted chain resolves to one instrument across sheets.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying policy instruments (policies, strategies, regulations, programs, budgets or investments) informed by CIMMYT evidence for the reporting year. At institutional level, the deduplicated sum of those counts, computed from the records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one policy instrument is often reported by more than one project. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels: a policy instrument has no plot and no household, so the levels here are reporting levels. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the stage each instrument had reached, since informed and enacted are different claims and KPI-I15 carries the second, the number excluded under Eligibility and why, and the number of instruments reported alongside under Block A.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count does not add to KPI-O37, KPI-O39 or KPI-I15; the levels connect through the theory of change, not through arithmetic. In particular, an instrument counted here as informed may later be counted under KPI-I15 when enacted: that is the chain progressing, and the two indicators are never summed into one policy total.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: de-duplicate on the shared instrument identifier across projects, countries and years before summing; where two centers claim the same instrument in CGIAR reporting, the contribution is named jointly, not counted twice. Overlap with sibling indicators is named, never summed: enacted instruments belong also to KPI-I15, budget or investment mobilisation to KPI-I16, decision-maker capacity to KPI-O40, convened dialogues to KPI-O37. If de-duplication is not feasible, label the pooled number an upper estimate.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: public policies, strategies, regulations, programs, budgets or investments, at any scale from local to global, modified in design or implementation during the reporting year, with a documented evidence trail linking the modification to CIMMYT-generated evidence. The evidence forms rank, strongest first: documented use of CIMMYT evidence in the instrument's development (recorded CIMMYT participation in drafting, or written confirmation from the policy owner); a third-party evaluation describing the contribution; acknowledgement of CIMMYT by the issuing body; and citation of CIMMYT evidence in the instrument. The minimum qualifying form is a citation in the instrument itself, and the form relied on is recorded with the count so a total built on citations reads differently from one built on drafting participation. Attendance at a process, and any contribution asserted without one of the four forms, are below the line, except that a contribution established by the Fallback key-informant interview in Data source, with its written notes retained, is reported beside the pooled count as Aggregation rule Block A sets out. The contribution documented must have taken place before the modification; the document evidencing it may be dated later, as the missing-data rule allows. This is the same documented-contribution test KPI-O42 applies in Gender equality, youth and social inclusion, on that sheet's own qualification scale; the Fallback interview exception above is this sheet's own.

Exclusion: briefing papers and evidence products as such (outputs, KPI-O39); participation in a process that produced no modified instrument (the convening is KPI-O37); budget and investment mobilisation, measured in USD under KPI-I16.

Missing data: a candidate instrument without documented contribution evidence is excluded and may be tracked as pipeline; an instrument reported beside the pooled count under the Inclusion rule's Fallback exception is not among the excluded. When one of the four evidence forms is filed later, the instrument enters the count in the year of the modification, and that year is restated, the same treatment KPI-I15 gives a late-evidenced enactment.

Repeated observations: one count per instrument per distinct modification, in the year of the modification, not the year its evidence was filed, which is how KPI-I15 dates an enactment; multiple evidence products informing one instrument count once, and an instrument counted in an earlier year is not recounted unless a substantively new modification, informed by new CIMMYT evidence, is documented.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only: policies change through many actors, interests and evidence streams; the documented-evidence requirement establishes that CIMMYT contributed, not the size of CIMMYT's share in the change.

A count rewards number, not significance: a subnational strategy and a national regulation count equally. Read the count with its scale and type disaggregations and a short narrative per counted instrument.

The evidence boundary cuts both ways: informal influence often leaves no citable trail and is undercounted, while a courtesy citation can overstate influence; CGIAR's own review found several reported policy changes lacked linked evidence, which is why undocumented claims are excluded.

A modified instrument is not an implemented one: design changes can remain unresourced or unenforced. Enactment is KPI-I15's question, and evidence of the policy's impact on people or the environment is a further, separate evidence standard.

A rise means more documented instances of CIMMYT evidence entering public instruments, not that policies improved or that outcomes for farmers changed; the contribution narrative runs through KPI-I15 and the pathway’s finance and market-systems indicators.
subMetrics: None. Policy type, stage and scale are disaggregations of the same count, not separately calculated metrics. Related indicators with their own sheets: KPI-O37 (dialogues convened), KPI-O39 (evidence products delivered), KPI-O40 (decision-maker capacity strengthened), and KPI-I15 (policies enacted supporting smallholder resilience), the impact this outcome feeds in the results chain.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetSteward: CIMMYT MEAL unit (content owner), with the policy engagement / foresight lead as technical reviewer
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project teams maintaining policy-engagement logs and evidence dossiers; key-informant interviews by project M&E staff where the fallback applies. Validation: project MEAL officer (instrument qualifies, modification documented, evidence meets the standard, no duplicate). Calculation: project M&E applying the distinct-instrument rule; cross-project de-duplication by the CIMMYT MEAL unit. Approval: project leader. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit, which reports the result into CGIAR technical reporting.
sourceRef: Volume 10 · Policy, finance & market systems — Reference sheet KPI-OC37

name: Reach and uptake of CIMMYT thought leadership (citations, media reach, references in global or regional agrifood agendas)
resultsLevel: Outcome. The Core reads an Institutional-branch level from the indicator statement itself. The counted events (a researcher citing CIMMYT work, a journalist covering it, an agenda body referencing it) are behaviours of the actors CIMMYT's products address, not deliveries by CIMMYT, so the indicator is an outcome. The products themselves are the delivered result, counted for agenda-shaping products by the paired output (KPI-O58).
primaryObjective: Influence & Advocacy (institutional component). This indicator does not map to a mission Primary Objective (PO1 to PO5); it measures the reach of the advocacy function that supports them. Its subject matter serves the agenda-shaping ambitions the Strategy describes under Influence and Advocacy for Impact.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. Institutional indicators carry no Impact Area by default, and no single Impact Area applies: CIMMYT thought leadership spans food security, climate, livelihoods and inclusion.
sdgTarget: None. No SDG indicator measures an organization's citation, media or agenda reach.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Performance and Results Management Framework 2022-2030, which lists the uptake of knowledge products among its output and outcome indicators, measured through Open Access status, citation indices and the Altmetric attention score. The citation channel corresponds to the citation-index measure, so its value feeds CGIAR-level reporting on knowledge-product uptake.
definition: Measures the reach and uptake of CIMMYT thought leadership: how far CIMMYT's evidence, analysis and positions travel beyond the organization, and how much external audiences engage with them. It is measured through three channels: citations of CIMMYT publications in the scientific literature, media reach (coverage of CIMMYT in news and specialist media), and references to CIMMYT work in global or regional agrifood agenda documents. It is a composite influence and reach measure: an institutional advocacy outcome, deliberately distinct from policy enactment, which is measured separately. "Thought leadership" here follows the 2030 Strategy's stated vision of CIMMYT as a global thought leader and change agent for climate resilient, sustainable and inclusive agricultural development: the products counted are flagship reports, position papers, policy briefs, peer-reviewed publications and public commentary intended to shape the global agrifood agenda, not project deliverables to a contracted client.
rationale: Answers whether the thought-leadership products CIMMYT invests in are taken up by researchers, media and agenda-setting bodies. This is the outcome half of the Influence and Advocacy narrative: the paired output indicator counts the agenda-shaping products CIMMYT produces (KPI-O58), whose uptake this indicator reads in its media and agenda channels, while its citation channel reads uptake of CIMMYT's indexed journal publications, which KPI-O58 does not count. The 2030 Strategy commits CIMMYT to advocacy through evidence while stating explicitly that CIMMYT will not engage in lobbying or intervene in political processes; influence is therefore measured as reach and uptake of evidence, never as political outcomes. Serves institutional reporting and the Communications and advocacy functions' own management.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional scope). This indicator measures a property of CIMMYT as an organization, reported once at Center level from corporate records; no project instantiates it, so there is no project-specific layer.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Count, reported per channel: number of citations (citation channel); number of media items, split into the news-media and social-media sub-channels and never merged, with estimated audience reach beside the news-media count where the monitoring source provides it (media channel); number of agenda documents referencing CIMMYT (agenda channel). The three channel counts use different units and are reported side by side, not summed into a single score (see Calculation method).
directionOfChange: Increase, for each channel separately. A rising value means more citations, more news-media or social-media items, or more references in agrifood agenda documents.
disaggregationRequired: Channel (citation / media / agenda). This is the indicator's core disaggregation: an institutional figure that hides which channel moved is not interpretable.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: The template's "optional (project-specific)" field does not apply to an Institutional indicator; these are optional institutional cuts the owning function may add: geography of the citing or covering source (global / regional / national), product cited (flagship report, journal article, policy brief).
unitOfObservation: Secondary dataset: one citation record, media item or agenda document, each read from an external source CIMMYT does not produce. That is what distinguishes it from the result-object value used for CIMMYT's own outputs.
calculationSummary:
Value = the count of citations, the count of media items and the count of agenda documents referencing CIMMYT, reported side by side as three channel counts rather than a blended index (see Aggregation rule, Block B).

Citation channel: number of citations, in documents published during the reporting year, to CIMMYT publications held in the CIMMYT repository, counting citations to indexed journal publications only, from Scopus as the indexing authority.

Media channel: number of distinct media items mentioning CIMMYT or its work published during the reporting year, from media monitoring, reported in two sub-channels that are never merged: news media (news articles, broadcast segments, specialist-press pieces) and social media (public posts and threads), because a news article and a social post reach different audiences with different durability. Estimated cumulative audience reach is reported alongside the news-media count where the monitoring source provides it, as a supplementary audience-size figure; it does not de-duplicate syndication, and a wire story carried by twelve outlets counts twelve times in the item count under the per-outlet rule in Eligibility criteria.

Agenda channel: number of distinct global or regional agrifood agenda documents published during the reporting year that reference CIMMYT evidence, products or positions.

Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS4: secondary databases and third-party services: Scopus for the citation channel, read against the CIMMYT repository's indexed journal publications, and a contracted media monitoring service for the media channel. CIMMYT already monitors public mentions of CIMMYT in newspapers and on social media, so the media channel has a source of record from the first reporting year under one of the two routes. Recommended DS2: administrative records: the Communications function's own tracking log for the agenda channel (systematic annual review of a defined list of global and regional agenda documents, recording each reference to CIMMYT), and, where CIMMYT runs media monitoring in-house, its own systematic monitoring records. Fallback DS2, media channel only: where no systematic media monitoring was in place for the year, clippings assembled after the fact, reported with the coverage stated as partial and not comparable with years compiled from the channel's Recommended source. The citation channel has no fallback: a year without Scopus access is reported as not measured. Not applicable DS1: reach and uptake are recorded events in external media and literature, not respondent-reported data; no survey measures this construct as defined. Not applicable DS3: no geospatial or Earth observation source can measure citations, media coverage or agenda references. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced or citizen-generated data does not systematically capture this construct. The social-media sub-channel is sourced from media monitoring, a curated product and not citizen-generated data, under either route.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, secondary source.
collectionFrequency: Annual, compiled once per year from the citation index, media monitoring records and the agenda-document review.
reportingFrequency: Annual, into institutional reporting alongside the other Influence & Advocacy component indicators.
referencePeriod: The reporting year (calendar year). Each channel value describes engagement events in documents and media items published during that year.
baselineRequired: Yes. The first full reporting year measured with the Recommended sources serves as the institutional baseline for each channel. Until a second comparable year exists, the value is reported as a level with no change claim. If the sources of record change (a different citation index or monitoring service), the baseline resets for the affected channel, since counts are not comparable across sources.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One reporting year and one set of sources of record, per channel. There are no project instances to pool: the value is compiled once from corporate sources. A media-channel year compiled wholly or partly from clippings (Fallback) is reported with that noted and with the months each source covered, and is not treated as comparable with years compiled from the channel's Recommended source; a monitoring gap left unfilled is reported as partial coverage. A change of citation index or monitoring service starts a new domain for that channel.

B: Combination method. None across channels. The institutional figure is the set of three channel counts, each a simple count within its channel. There is no defensible weighting for combining citations, media items and agenda references into one number, so no blended score is computed: weights would be arbitrary and would hide which channel moved.

C: Levels and operations. Each channel count is computed once, at institutional level, over the reporting year, from that channel's source of record. There is no level beneath the institution: a citation is an event in an external index, not a share any unit holds, and no project reports an instance of this indicator. Where a view by geography or by product is wanted it is recomputed from that channel's own records, never taken as a share of the channel total. The three channels are never added, averaged or indexed together, and a summary that reports one channel alone is not this indicator. Also report: all three channel values together with the source of record for each, any channel not measured in the year, the estimated audience reach beside the news-media count where the monitoring source provides it, and, for the citation channel, the number of publications in the citation population at the extraction date.

D: Never pooled. Aggregation across results levels: no. This outcome is never combined arithmetically with the paired product count (KPI-O58, an output): the two count different objects. KPI-O58 excludes peer-reviewed journal articles, so its products reach this indicator through the media and agenda channels only, while the citation channel counts citations to the indexed journal publications in the CIMMYT repository. Across indicators, a CIMMYT reference in a policy document may count here in the agenda channel and also serve as evidence for KPI-OC37, which counts policies informed by CIMMYT evidence; the two measure visibility and documented policy contribution, and are never added.

E: Deduplication and coverage. Within each channel, de-duplicate on the rules the calculation method sets: a media narrative syndicated across outlets counts once per distinct outlet, an agenda document counts once whatever the number of times it references CIMMYT, and self-citations are excluded where the index supports it. The same underlying event may legitimately appear in more than one channel, and that is acceptable precisely because the channels are never summed. Coverage is the share of the year the sources of record cover, reported with the value.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion and exclusion: the citation population is the CIMMYT repository, and only indexed journal publications in it count, with Scopus as the indexing authority; a working paper, report or other grey-literature output that Scopus does not index does not count even when cited. Citations by CIMMYT authors to CIMMYT work (self-citations) are excluded where the index supports it, and the exclusion applied is recorded with the value, since the construct is external uptake. CIMMYT's own press releases, website and social channels do not count as media items. A news-media item is a news article, broadcast segment or specialist-press piece; a social-media item is a public post or thread by an account other than CIMMYT's own. The two are counted and reported as separate sub-channels and never merged into a single media figure. An agenda document is a global or regional agrifood agenda document, for example an intergovernmental declaration, a regional agricultural strategy or a flagship report of an international body. A reference in an agenda document counts regardless of whether CIMMYT sought it.

Missing data: a channel not measured in a given year is reported as "not measured", never imputed as zero; the other channels are still reported.

Repeated observations: a citation is counted in the publication year of the citing document, not the year the cited work was published, so each year's figure is that year's new citations; the extraction date, and the date at which the repository population was taken, are recorded with the value. A media narrative syndicated across multiple outlets counts once per distinct outlet. An agenda document counts once, even if it references several CIMMYT products.
limitations: Reach is not influence on decisions. A citation, media item or agenda reference shows attention to CIMMYT's work, not that anyone acted differently because of it; documented policy contribution is measured by separate indicators (KPI-OC37, KPI-I15), and this indicator supports no attribution claim beyond visibility.
The three channel counts are in different units and are never summed or averaged into one score.

All three channels carry coverage bias: Scopus, like any citation index, favours English-language journal literature, and restricting the citation channel to indexed journal publications means CIMMYT's grey literature is outside the count by design rather than undercounted by accident; media monitoring depends on the outlet list it covers, typically thinner for Global South and non-English media; the agenda channel depends on which documents are scanned. Values are comparable over time only while the sources and the agenda-document list stay constant.

The counts are volume-driven. The citation count grows with CIMMYT's cumulative indexed output, which rises every year, so it can rise while uptake per publication is flat; it is read beside the size of the citation population reported with it. The media and agenda counts rise when CIMMYT releases more agenda-shaping products (KPI-O58), so they are read beside that count before a rise is read as wider uptake.

A movement means external visibility changed, nothing more: media reach can rise on controversy as well as on merit, an item syndicated across outlets counts once for each outlet that carries it, and citation counts lag publication by one to three years, so this year's value partly reflects earlier years' output.
subMetrics:
Three channel sub-metrics, each reported separately; none has its own reference sheet.

— Citations: count of citations in documents published in the reporting year to indexed journal publications held in the CIMMYT repository, per Scopus.

— Media reach: count of distinct media items mentioning CIMMYT in the reporting year, reported as two sub-channels, news media and social media, never merged; estimated cumulative audience reach beside the news-media count as a supplementary figure where available.

— Agenda references: count of distinct global or regional agrifood agenda documents published in the reporting year that reference CIMMYT evidence, products or positions.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Institutional indicator; corporate functions rather than project roles. Data collection: CIMMYT Communications function (media monitoring and agenda-document review) and the function managing bibliometric records (citation channel). Validation: Communications lead for the media and agenda channels; bibliometric record owner for citations. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, per the Calculation method above. Approval: head of the Communications / Influence and Advocacy function. Reporting: CIMMYT MEAL unit into institutional reporting.

name: Percentage of market volume/value flowing through sustainable or inclusive models
resultsLevel: Impact. The indicator describes a long-term systemic property of the market itself, neither a delivered result (output) nor a behaviour change of identified actors (outcome, measured by KPI-OC35). The share moves only through the aggregate weight of many independent transactions, which is the systemic change the results chain builds toward.
indicatorScope: Mission. Measures a systemic state of external market systems that CIMMYT's work supports, so it carries the full project-specific layer.
primaryObjective: PO4 Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient, grounded in sub-objective 4.4 ("Market driven systems and emerging models are harnessed to improve agrifood systems and their sustainability"). The register's PO3 and PO5 are contributing objectives only: inclusive models widen smallholder access to services, income opportunities and market opportunities (3.2, 3.3), and value-adding market models help make farming an attractive career (5.3).
cgiarImpactArea: Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs, the pathway ruling's fixed value for the market-systems indicators: whatever the commodity, the measured result is market performance for smallholders, so one value fits the share this indicator reports.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator measures the share of market volume or value flowing through sustainable or inclusive business models. The nearest neighbour, SDG 2.4.1 (proportion of agricultural area under productive and sustainable agriculture, custodian FAO), measures sustainability as a share of land area, not of market transactions, so there is no direct correspondence.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR standard results reporting: no CGIAR standard indicator corresponds. The nearest CGIAR category, Innovation Use ("the extent to which an innovation is being used, by which type of users and under which conditions", One CGIAR Standard Indicators report), is operationalised as counts of users, innovations or area, not a market share; this indicator is CIMMYT-defined.
definition: Measures the share of the total market volume or value in supported systems that is transacted through sustainable or inclusive market models during the reporting year. A "sustainable or inclusive model" is a market or business-model arrangement, such as a sustainable sourcing arrangement or an inclusive market platform, recorded under KPI-O36 (deployed) or KPI-OC35 (adopted by a value chain); a "supported system" is a commodity value chain or market system, within a defined geography, where CIMMYT's market-systems work operates. The share can be computed on a volume basis (physical quantity) or a value basis (monetary worth); every reported figure states its basis, and the two are never mixed.
rationale: Answers whether the market models CIMMYT helped create have moved beyond deployment and adoption to carrying real commercial weight: what share of the market flows through them. That is the systemic end point of the pathway’s market thread and the impact evidence, for institutional reporting and donors, of the 2030 Strategy's commitment to harnessing market-driven systems and emerging models.
projectSpecificApplication: Describe the supported systems this project measures (commodity or value chain, countries, market-shed boundary), the qualifying models operating in them, the basis used (volume or value), and the transaction node applied (see Calculation method). Do not restate or alter the institutional definition, unit or calculation method; if the share cannot be estimated in this context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State why this project tracks the indicator: the donor requirement or impact claim it evidences, and the decision it informs (for example, a share that stays flat while KPI-OC35 adoption counts rise triggers a review of whether adopted models are operating at meaningful scale).
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work puts no volume through a market
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI. Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work puts no volume through a market.
unit: Percentage (of market volume, or of market value, in supported systems; the basis is stated with every figure)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of market volume or value flows through sustainable or inclusive models.
disaggregationRequired: Required: commodity or value chain, as recorded in the register, and the measurement basis (volume or value) stated with every reported figure; a share pooled across value chains or bases cannot otherwise be interpreted.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country and market shed; model type (sustainable sourcing arrangement / inclusive market platform / other); producer type supplying the qualifying models, smallholder versus non-smallholder where records allow, with smallholder as Annex B defines it and the declared threshold travelling with the value.
unitOfObservation: The supported market system (a commodity value chain within a defined geography). This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation.
calculationSummary:
Numerator: market volume (or value) transacted through qualifying sustainable or inclusive models in the supported system during the reporting year, from the qualifying models' operating records. Denominator: total market volume (or value) in the same supported system, for the reporting year from market statistics, or from the most recent market assessment, whose year is reported with the value. Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100, computed per supported system on a single stated basis.

Basis rule: value (USD) is the default because it pools across commodities; volume (metric tons) is acceptable within a single commodity where price data are unreliable. Never mix bases. Where the basis is value, numerator and denominator are converted to nominal USD at the average market exchange rate for the reporting year, the convention KPI-I16 applies, from the rate source CIMMYT's institutional reporting fixes, applied identically to both terms and to every system in a pooled figure, and the conversion basis is reported with the value.

Measurement node: numerator and denominator are measured at the same point in the chain, by default the first point of sale by producers (farm gate or first aggregation), stated per system. Summing seller-side transactions along the whole chain instead is legitimate only if applied identically to both terms, and a single node is the cleaner test.

Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: This indicator needs two data streams. Recommended, DS2 (Administrative and registry data) for the numerator: transaction records of the qualifying model operators (sourcing contract volumes, platform transaction logs, aggregator and off-taker records), combined with DS4 (Secondary and international databases) for the denominator: national production and market statistics (FAOSTAT, national statistical office series), scoped to the supported system. These series measure national production, not first-sale market volume in the supported market shed, and the two are not the same quantity even where the unit string matches. Where a DS4 series cannot be scoped to the market shed and to the measurement node the Calculation method fixes, the denominator is taken from the Fallback market assessment instead; a value left standing on an unscoped national series is reported as an upper bound on the denominator and therefore a lower bound on the share, with the substitution stated.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which role supplied the numerator and which the denominator, Recommended or Fallback; if Fallback, explain briefly why operator records or market statistics could not be used.
collectionInstrument: Applicable to the DS1 fallback only: structured market-assessment instrument covering sales volume and value by marketing channel. Respondents: qualifying model operators, traders, aggregators and other market actors in the supported system. Mode: face-to-face interview with review of the respondent's sales records. Under the Recommended sources, no instrument applies (documentary compilation).
collectionFrequency: Numerator: annually, from qualifying models' operating records. Denominator: annually where market statistics allow; otherwise from a market assessment repeated every 2 to 3 years, with the assessment year stated.
referencePeriod: The reporting year: 12 months of transactions in the supported system, compared against the pre-intervention baseline share. The reporting year is the calendar year, register-wide.
baselineRequired: Yes. An impact claim needs the pre-intervention share. Fallbacks where no prospective baseline exists: reconstruct it from qualifying models' historical records plus secondary market statistics for the pre-period, or use the earliest measured share as the baseline. If neither is feasible: monitoring only, no change or impact claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Across projects: pool systems whose numerator and denominator both come from the Recommended sources; a system any term of which came from the DS1 Fallback, including a denominator taken from the Fallback market assessment under Data source, is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note naming the fallback-sourced term, not blended in, since a survey-based estimate carries different error than records plus statistics. A system whose denominator rests on an unscoped national series is also reported alongside the pooled figure, labelled a lower bound on the share, and never enters the pooled sums.

B: Combination method. The institutional figure is computed by summing numerators and summing denominators across supported systems on the value basis, then dividing; never average system-level percentages. Volume-based shares aggregate only within a single commodity.

C: Levels and operations. A share is recomputed at every level from its own numerator and denominator, never averaged from the levels beneath it. This share is weighted by volume or by value, not by a count of models or actors, so both terms are summed quantities and never counts. At supported system level, qualifying throughput over total throughput in that system for the period. At every aggregation level above the supported system, the summed numerator over the summed denominator within the pooling domain of Block A, and volume and value are two shares, never one: they are reported side by side and never averaged together, because a metric ton and a dollar are not the same denominator. A change in the pooled share between two years is stated only over the systems in the pooled figure in both years; systems entering or leaving the pool are reported separately. Also report: the denominator itself and its source, which basis the share is on, and the share of the system the market statistics cover, since a share over an incomplete market overstates penetration.

D: Never pooled. (1) Across results levels: No. This share does not combine arithmetically with KPI-O34, KPI-O36 or KPI-OC35: a deployed innovation, an adopting value chain and a market share are different objects, connected through the Theory of Change as a narrative, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: where two CIMMYT projects support the same value chain in overlapping geographies, the system is consolidated into one numerator and one denominator before pooling, so the same market is never counted twice; within a system, sequential-model volume counts once (see Calculation method). Where overlapping system boundaries cannot be consolidated, state with the pooled figure that the boundary overlap is unresolved: counting the overlap twice raises or lowers the share depending on the share inside it, so the direction of the error is unknown. KPI-OC35 counts adopting value chains, delineated as commodity by country, and this indicator weighs the market sheds within them, so one adopting chain can contain several supported systems here; the two are never summed or combined into one composite.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion and exclusion: a model qualifies if it is recorded under KPI-O36 (deployed) or KPI-OC35 (adopted by a value chain), and its operation in the supported system is documented; the list of qualifying models per system is recorded with the value. Models without documented transaction records, and transactions outside the system boundary, are excluded rather than estimated.

Missing data: where the denominator cannot be credibly estimated, that system is excluded from the pooled figure and reported separately as "numerator only, share not computable"; the denominator is never guessed.

Repeated observations: each transaction counts once; volume passing through two qualifying models in sequence (a platform selling into a sourcing arrangement) enters the numerator once, at the measurement node.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only. Market shares move with prices, policy, competing channels and many independent actors; the pathway chain (deployment, adoption, share) carries the contribution narrative, not this number alone.

The denominator is usually the weakest number. Total market volume or value in systems with large informal trade is estimated, not counted; the share inherits the full error of the market-size estimate, which can exceed the year-on-year change being reported.

Shares are not comparable across systems or bases. Shares of markets of different size are different achievements, and pooled value-basis figures are dominated by the largest, highest-priced systems. On the value basis the numerator is priced at the qualifying models' own transaction prices and the denominator at market prices, so a price premium paid through the models raises the value share above the volume share, and a rising premium raises it with no change in volume.

The classification boundary rests on the rule the sheet states, applied by the project MEAL officer and recorded with the reason. What counts as a "sustainable or inclusive model" determines the numerator; a rising share can reflect reclassification of existing channels rather than real change, so the list of qualifying models per system must be recorded and stable within a series.

A rising share means the models carry more market weight, not that participants benefit. It says nothing by itself about farmers' prices, terms of inclusion or environmental performance; pair with the pathway’s income, gender and sustainability indicators for the benefit narrative.
subMetrics:
None. Commodity or value chain, basis, country, model type and producer type are disaggregations, not sub-metrics.

Related indicators, each with its own sheet: KPI-O34 (innovations piloted), KPI-O35 (platforms or hubs established), KPI-O36 (innovations deployed), KPI-OC35 (value chains adopting sustainable or inclusive models, the outcome this impact weighs). This sheet is the pathway’s terminal impact measure for the sustainable markets thread.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project M&E officer with the market-systems lead, compiling operator records and market statistics (or fielding the fallback assessment). Validation: project MEAL officer, against the qualification list, node and basis rules. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (share computation, system consolidation, cross-project pooling). Approval: project team lead. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit, which publishes pooled and fallback-sourced figures separately.
sourceRef: Volume 10 · Policy, finance & market systems — Reference sheet KPI-I13

name: Number of public policies enacted that support smallholder resilience and to which CIMMYT contributed
resultsLevel: Impact, as the register sets it, and the sheet reports at that level. CGIAR treats policy change as an outcome result type and places "policy enacted" at stage 2 of a three-stage scale whose stage 3 is evidence of the policy's impact on people or the environment. The register instead reads enactment as the level above policies merely informed (KPI-OC37, outcome), defensible as CIMMYT's own ordering.
primaryObjective: PO5 Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities. Contributing: PO3 (smallholder resilience and livelihood trajectories) and PO4 (more inclusive, productive, sustainable and climate resilient agrifood systems).
cgiarImpactArea: Recorded per instrument and reported as a distribution, under the pathway-wide rule. An instrument supporting climate resilience serves Climate Adaptation & Mitigation, which is also where CGIAR's closest correspondence (plans with evidence of implementation) sits; one raising smallholder incomes serves Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs, so the tag varies by item as what is measured varies by item. No single value is forced on the indicator.
sdgTarget: None. SDG target 13.2 (integrate climate change measures into national policies, strategies and planning) is the closest target, but its indicator 13.2.1 counts countries with reports submitted under the Paris Agreement, a property of treaty reporting rather than a count of enacted policies to which an organisation contributed.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Results Framework: policy change is a reported result category and this indicator corresponds to its stage 2, policy enacted, with the same requirement of evidence linking research to the instrument, reported by CGIAR at outcome level.
definition: Counts the distinct public policy instruments formally enacted during the reporting period that carry at least one provision supporting smallholder resilience and to which CIMMYT made a documented contribution. Instrument covers the three policy types used across CGIAR reporting: a policy or strategy, a legal instrument (a law or a government regulation), or a program, budget or investment. Enacted means formal adoption or entry into force by the authority empowered to do so, evidenced by the published instrument, a gazette entry, a legislative record or the adopting body's formal announcement; a draft, a bill in passage or an announcement of intent does not count.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's evidence and engagement travel far enough for a public authority to commit itself in a formal instrument that helps smallholder farmers withstand and recover from shocks. It is the endpoint of the policy influence chain and separates influence that changed a document from influence that stopped at a conversation, which is what institutional and donor reporting needs to show.
projectSpecificApplication: State which enacted instruments the project counts, the jurisdictions and policy scale covered, the resilience provisions concerned, and the form CIMMYT's contribution took in each case. Do not change the unit, the enactment or contribution tests, or the counting rule. If applying the indicator as defined is not feasible here, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it.
projectSpecificRationale: State the project decision, donor commitment or country reporting need this count serves, for example a donor policy-result deliverable, or an internal trigger where a target instrument misses enactment by a set date and the project reviews its engagement with the responsible ministry.
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work contributes to no enacted policy instrument directly
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI. Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work contributes to no enacted policy instrument directly.
unit: Number (count of distinct enacted policy instruments)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more public policies supporting smallholder resilience were formally adopted or entered into force with documented CIMMYT contribution. More instruments is not more resilience; see Limitations.
disaggregationRequired: Required: policy scale or level, on CGIAR's four levels (local / national / regional / global), set on this sheet's authority. The four levels match KPI-OC37, so a regional instrument is filed at regional on both sheets. Also required: policy type, on the same three-way split KPI-OC37 uses (policy or strategy / legal instrument / program, budget or investment).
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country or region; adopting body type (ministry, legislature, regulator, regional or global body); resilience theme (climate adaptation, risk management and insurance, seed or input systems, social protection); form of CIMMYT contribution; presence of gender-equity or social-inclusion provisions.
unitOfObservation: The enacted policy instrument. This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct public policy instruments enacted in the reporting period that meet all four inclusion tests. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: CIMMYT project and programme policy-engagement records, holding for each instrument its title, jurisdiction, adopting body, enactment date and evidence, the resilience provision cited and the documented CIMMYT contribution, cross-checked against technical reports. The official publication that evidences enactment (the published instrument, a gazette entry, a legislative record or the adopting body's formal announcement) is also a Recommended source, for the enactment and the provision it contains, wherever it is retrieved: an instrument whose CIMMYT contribution is documented in the project's own records and whose enactment is evidenced only by an official publication is Recommended-sourced. Fallback DS4: national or regional legal and policy registries, other published policy documents and third-party evaluations, used where CIMMYT's own records are incomplete; values built this way are flagged as fallback-sourced, since external registries evidence that an instrument exists but rarely evidence CIMMYT's contribution, which must then be established separately. Not applicable DS1: enactment is a documented public act, not a quantity measured from respondents; interviews with policy actors may sit inside an evidence pack but do not generate the count. Not applicable DS3: Earth observation cannot establish that an instrument was adopted or that CIMMYT contributed. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced data cannot verify legal enactment or contribution.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which route each instrument rests on; for any on the Fallback, say why the project's own engagement records were incomplete and which registries or other external sources were used.
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). The evidence pack is the tool: one record per instrument carrying the identifier fields, scale and type, the enactment evidence in one of the forms Eligibility test (b) names, the resilience provision referenced, and the contribution evidence in one of the four forms the Eligibility criteria rank, with the form recorded.
collectionFrequency: Continuous: each instrument is logged with its evidence pack as enactment occurs
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which enactment took place. A programme reporting over its full life labels the value cumulative with its year range. The reporting year is the calendar year, register-wide.
baselineRequired: No. An annual flow count starting from zero each year; there is no pre-project stock to measure and change is read from the multi-year series. A project claiming change against the pre-project policy environment needs a documented policy-landscape review at project start.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: sum the instruments evidenced in projects' own engagement records (Recommended); an instrument evidenced only from external registries (Fallback) is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, not blended in, and the same project's Recommended-sourced instruments are summed.

B: Combination method. Summed: the institutional figure is the sum of distinct enacted instruments across all reporting projects and programmes in the year, after de-duplication on the shared instrument identifier, the persistent identifier carrying the instrument's official title, issuing body, jurisdiction and version, the same key KPI-O42, KPI-OC39, KPI-OC34 and KPI-OC37 use. Never average project-level counts.

C: Levels and operations. At project level, the count of that project's qualifying enacted public policy instruments supporting smallholders for the reporting year. At institutional level, the deduplicated sum of those counts, computed from the records themselves rather than by adding project figures, since one instrument is often reported by more than one project. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels: an instrument has no plot and no household, so the levels here are reporting levels. Also report: the number of contributing projects, the enactment date and the evidence of CIMMYT's contribution, since this is a contribution claim and not an attribution claim, the number excluded under Eligibility and why, and the number of instruments reported alongside because they rest on the Fallback.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count never combines arithmetically with KPI-OC37, KPI-OC39 or the policy outputs KPI-O37, KPI-O39 and KPI-O40; the same policy process is deliberately visible at several levels, which connect through the theory of change, not as a sum.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: an instrument to which several projects or countries contributed carries one shared instrument identifier and counts once, with jurisdiction and scale as disaggregations; a regional instrument counts once at regional scale and a national transposition separately; where identifiers cannot be matched, label the sum an upper estimate. Across the register, one instrument legitimately appears here, in KPI-OC37 as informed, and where it carries gender-equity provisions in KPI-OC39, since those measure different attributes of it; the counts must never be added into one policy total.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: (a) public, adopted by a public authority at any scale from local to global, and of one of the three policy types; (b) enacted in the period, evidenced by the published instrument, gazette entry, legislative record or the adopting body's formal announcement; (c) carries at least one provision that reduces smallholders' exposure to, or supports recovery from, agricultural and food-system risks, shocks and stresses, with smallholder as Annex B defines it. A provision is a named action, an eligibility rule, a resource allocation, or a standard or entitlement directed at that effect and traceable in the instrument's text. An instrument that mentions resilience, shocks or smallholders without a named provision does not qualify: a reference in a preamble, a statement of principle, or a general commitment with no action attached is not a provision. The qualifying provision is quoted or cited by clause in the record, so the judgement is checkable rather than asserted. The test is applied by the project MEAL officer with the responsible CIMMYT policy or impact specialist, the same pair the steward field names, and a disputed case goes to the CIMMYT MEAL unit; (d) CIMMYT's contribution documented in one of four forms, ranked strongest first: documented use of CIMMYT evidence in the instrument's development (recorded CIMMYT participation in drafting, or written confirmation from the policy owner); a third-party evaluation describing the contribution; acknowledgement of CIMMYT by the issuing body; or citation of CIMMYT evidence in the instrument. The minimum qualifying form is a citation in the instrument itself, the form relied on is recorded with the count, and the ranking is the one KPI-OC37 applies, so an instrument informed and later enacted is judged on one standard. The contribution documented must have taken place before enactment; the document evidencing it may be dated later. Attendance at a process, and any contribution asserted without one of the four forms, do not qualify.

Exclusion: drafts, bills not passed, instruments in consultation, pledges and announcements of intent; private or internal organisational policies; instruments with no traceable CIMMYT contribution; renewals with no substantive change. Instruments assessed against the provision test and not qualifying are counted separately and reported alongside the value: the ratio of assessed to qualifying is what shows a reviewer that the test is being applied rather than assumed. This is the same machinery KPI-O42 applies to its gender-responsive provision test.

Missing data: an instrument lacking either evidence is not counted until it is filed; filed later, it counts in its actual year of enactment and that year is restated.

Repeated observations: an instrument counts once institutionally even where several projects contributed, matched on the shared instrument identifier (official title, issuing body, jurisdiction and version). The identifier deliberately carries no enactment date, because an informed-stage record on KPI-OC37 has no enactment date to match on and a key containing one could never link the two records. The count itself still falls only in the year of enactment; a later amendment counts separately only where it creates or substantively changes a provision meeting test (c) and was itself enacted with a documented CIMMYT contribution; otherwise it is a revision of the counted instrument.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only: enactment depends on politics, coalitions, timing and other actors, and CIMMYT is one contributor among many. The documented-contribution test bounds the claim, it does not grade how decisive the contribution was, and it never licenses saying CIMMYT caused the policy.

Enactment is not implementation and not resilience: an adopted instrument may go unfunded or unapplied. A rise here means public authorities committed on paper in ways CIMMYT helped shape, not that smallholders became more resilient; pair it with the resilience and livelihood indicators for claims about effects.

Counts carry no weight: a district by-law and a national law count the same, so values are not comparable across projects or years until the scale and type disaggregations are applied, and a numeric target can reward many small instruments over one consequential one.
Policy cycles run over years, so annual values are small and volatile; read a multi-year series, and expect restatement when contribution evidence is filed after the year of enactment.

Contribution evidence is documentary and unevenly available: instruments rarely name the research they drew on, so the count reflects where acknowledgement was obtainable as much as where influence happened.
subMetrics: None. Policy scale and policy type are disaggregations of one count, not separately calculated metrics. The chain reaching this indicator runs from the outputs KPI-O37, KPI-O39 and KPI-O40 (engagements convened, evidence products delivered, decision-maker capacity strengthened) through the outcomes KPI-OC37 and KPI-OC39, each with its own sheet.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project or programme policy-engagement lead, assembling the instrument record and evidence pack. Validation: project MEAL officer with the responsible CIMMYT policy or impact specialist, verifying enactment, the resilience provision and the contribution evidence. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (de-duplication and institutional sum). Approval: project leader, or programme director where an instrument spans several projects. Reporting: project MEAL focal point to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 10 · Policy, finance & market systems — Reference sheet KPI-I15

name: Volume of agricultural and climate finance and co-investment (USD) leveraged for smallholder-focused systems through CIMMYT engagement
resultsLevel: Impact, the level the register records. CGIAR's own indicator review reads investment mobilisation as an outcome-like result; the register places disbursed finance at impact, above the instruments developed (KPI-O38), and no indicator measures the step between them.
primaryObjective: PO5: Global community takes informed, coordinated, consolidated measures to overcome disruptions, climate crisis, structural inequalities (specifically its objective that policies and investments prioritize smallholder agriculture). Contributing: PO3 (Smallholder farmers and their livelihood trajectories are resilient and significantly improved), PO4 (Agrifood systems are rendered more inclusive, efficient, productive, sustainable and climate resilient).
cgiarImpactArea: Recorded per financing and reported as a distribution, under the pathway-wide rule. A disbursement into smallholder enterprise or livelihoods serves Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs; a climate-tagged financing serves Climate Adaptation & Mitigation, so the tag varies by item as what is measured varies by item. No single value is forced on the indicator. The correspondence to the CGIAR standard impact indicator "US dollars of climate adaptation investments" runs through the required climate-tagged cut rather than through the Impact Area assignment: the climate-tagged share is what feeds the CGIAR figure, and the correspondence stays partial because CIMMYT counts agricultural and climate finance together.
sdgTarget: None (direct). Closest references: SDG target 2.a (increase investment in agriculture; indicator 2.a.2, total official flows to the agriculture sector) and target 13.a (climate finance mobilisation).
