Both track official flows at country level; neither measures finance leveraged through a research organization's engagement, so no direct correspondence exists.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR standard impact indicator "US dollars of climate adaptation investments" under the Climate Adaptation and Mitigation Impact Area (partial, climate-tagged share only). No other framework carries this construct as a single measure: the leveraged/accessed distinction, the disbursed-not-committed rule, the formal-institution boundary and the in-kind valuation convention are stated on this sheet and are CIMMYT's own.
definition: The volume of agricultural and climate finance and co-investment (USD) leveraged for smallholder-focused systems through CIMMYT engagement over the period; a measure of investment mobilised into agrifood systems, distinct from resourcing CIMMYT the organization. "Leveraged" means the financing was disbursed by a third party (private investor, financial institution, government, or development funder) to actors in smallholder-focused agrifood systems, and CIMMYT's engagement is documented as having contributed to mobilising it. Two boundary rules define the concept: only finance disbursed counts, not commitments or pledges; and finance received by CIMMYT itself never counts here, because that is resource mobilisation for the organization, tracked by separate institutional indicators.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's evidence, investment cases, and convening mobilise finance into smallholder agrifood systems: the investment half of the 2030 Strategy's objective that "policies and investments prioritize smallholder agriculture" (the other half is tracked by the policy indicators KPI-OC37 and KPI-I15). Used for institutional and donor reporting, and contributes to CGIAR reporting on climate adaptation investments (partial correspondence, see Other frameworks).
projectSpecificApplication: State the geographies, value chains, and engagement types covered; the deal registry the project maintains; and which financiers' disbursement confirmations it draws on. Do not alter the institutional definition, unit, or calculation method above; if applying the indicator as defined is not feasible in this project's context, raise it with the MEAL focal point rather than redefining it here.
projectSpecificRationale: State the donor commitment or partnership objective this figure reports against, and any project-level decision it informs (for example, whether mobilised co-investment is a contractual results target).
projectTypesNotApplicable: whose laboratory and controlled-environment work mobilises no agricultural or climate finance
projectTypesRaw: Breeding and varietal development; applied agronomy and farming systems; seed systems and deployment; system change and transformation; digital agriculture and AI. Not applicable: upstream discovery science, whose laboratory and controlled-environment work mobilises no agricultural or climate finance.
unit: US dollars (USD), nominal. Convert local currency at the average market exchange rate for the reporting year (more frequently under rapid devaluation or appreciation).
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more agricultural and climate finance and co-investment was leveraged for smallholder-focused systems through CIMMYT engagement. Amounts disbursed in local currency are converted to US dollars, so the value also moves with the exchange rate.
disaggregationRequired: Required: finance type (debt; non-debt, including equity and formal leasing; in-kind co-investment valued at market rates); finance source (private sector; public and development finance), which is where private-sector investment leveraged is read off, as a cut of this total rather than as a separate indicator; climate-tagged vs. general agricultural finance (the climate-tagged share is what feeds CGIAR climate-investment reporting; the tagging rule is the one CIMMYT applies for that reporting and travels with the value).
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, so there is nothing for a type-specific cut to be required by; the required cuts above apply to every project type that reports this indicator.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Country or region; value chain; recipient size class (individual/microenterprise, small and medium enterprise, large enterprise); sex and age of recipient proprietors where recipients are enterprises or producers.
unitOfObservation: The financing transaction (disbursement). This is a result object, one of the Core's permitted values for Unit of observation; "organization" is not used as a stand-in, because what each record describes is a disbursement event, not the recipient, and recipients may also be individuals or producer groups per the optional disaggregation.
calculationSummary:
Value = sum of the USD value of qualifying financing disbursed during the reporting period. A financing qualifies when all three tests are met: (a) disbursed, an actual outlay of cash or in-kind investment to the recipient, not a commitment, pledge, or loan in process; (b) smallholder-focused, the financed activity's intended primary beneficiaries are smallholder producers as Annex B defines smallholder, or the enterprises and systems serving them; the same population KPI-O38 uses, so the pipeline and the dollars are read on one definition; (c) CIMMYT-leveraged, CIMMYT's contribution to mobilising the deal is documented in the deal record. Whole-counting, not a share. A qualifying disbursement enters at its full value, and every disbursement on a deal that meets test (c) qualifies, whichever co-financier made it; CIMMYT does not apportion a deal by contribution share or by financier, because no defensible basis exists for splitting a mobilisation between the parties that produced it. This is CIMMYT's own convention, not an imported one, and the counterfactual caveat under Limitations follows from it: the figure is finance CIMMYT contributed to mobilising, never finance CIMMYT caused.

Leveraged, not accessed. Leveraged is the test above: a third party disbursed and CIMMYT's engagement is documented as having contributed to mobilising it. Accessed is what a recipient reports receiving, from any source and for any reason, and it is a wider quantity. Only leveraged finance enters the value; an accessed figure obtained through the fallback survey is reported separately, labelled as such, and never added.

Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: administrative and partnership records: the project's deal registry, signed co-investment and partnership agreements, financier and partner disbursement confirmations, and programme records documenting CIMMYT's role in each deal. Fallback DS1: survey of recipient enterprises or producers on financing accessed (value, type, source), used only where financier confirmations cannot be obtained; recipient self-reports are less verifiable than financier records, so flag any survey-sourced value as fallback-sourced. The survey evidences the disbursement, never the CIMMYT-contribution test: a recipient knows what it received, not what mobilised it, so test (c) is met from the deal record in every case and a survey value with no deal record behind it does not count. Comparator DS4: national and international agricultural-finance statistics, which place the reported figure against the wider flow and never enter the value, since they cannot isolate CIMMYT-attributable transactions. Not applicable: DS3, finance flows cannot be observed from satellite or geospatial data; DS5, crowdsourced or citizen-generated data cannot verify financial transactions.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: State which source role this project used, Recommended or Fallback. If Fallback, briefly explain why financier or partner disbursement confirmations were not obtainable, and name the disbursements whose value came from the recipient survey.
collectionInstrument: For the Fallback DS1 only: a financing-access module administered to recipient enterprises or producers, recording value disbursed, finance type, source, and timing. Respondent: the proprietor or finance manager of the recipient enterprise. Mode: interview with supporting documentation check (loan agreement, disbursement receipt). Not applicable where the Recommended DS2 route is used.
collectionFrequency: Annually (continuous deal-registry maintenance, annual consolidation).
referencePeriod: The reporting year (disbursements made within the year). Cumulative totals over the engagement or strategy period may be reported additionally, always labelled as cumulative. The reporting year is the calendar year, register-wide.
baselineRequired: No. The baseline is zero at the start of the engagement or reporting period, CIMMYT's counting convention for a flow; the indicator measures a flow, not a change against a pre-existing stock.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: pool values from projects using the Recommended DS2 route directly; a project that had to use the Fallback survey route is reported alongside the pooled figure with a note, not blended silently into it.

B: Combination method. Sum the USD value of distinct disbursements across deals and projects; absolute volumes add directly.

C: Levels and operations. A monetary volume adds. At project level, the sum of qualifying financing disbursed in the reporting period, each amount converted to USD at the stated rate and date basis. At institutional level, the sum across projects on the same basis, after the de-duplication Block E requires, since one financing arrangement is often reported by more than one project. A monetary volume is not observed at the farm measurement levels: a disbursement has no plot and no household. Values on different currency or deflation bases are never pooled, and a series compared across years states whether it is nominal or real and against which base year, because a change driven by the exchange rate is not a change in finance leveraged. Also report: the conversion basis and rate source, the number of contributing projects, the volume excluded under Eligibility, and the split by finance type, since a bare total hides which type of finance moved.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. Investment cases and instruments developed (KPI-O38) count CIMMYT outputs and never convert into or add to this USD figure; the two connect through the results chain not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting, three named risks. First, within the register: a government budget or investment commitment that CIMMYT evidence informed may be counted in the policy indicators (KPI-OC37 policies informed, KPI-I15 policies enacted) and, once disbursed, here as finance leveraged; both may be reported but never summed. Grant income to CIMMYT never enters this indicator: it is resource mobilisation for the organization, tracked by separate institutional indicators. Second, across instruments: when finance passes through an intermediary (a facility capitalised by a donor that then on-lends), count the disbursement to the end recipient, not both flows. Third, across projects and organizations: where two CIMMYT projects, or CIMMYT and a partner, contributed to the same deal, each disbursement counts once institutionally; a partner claiming the same dollars in its own reporting is noted, not netted out. If de-duplication is not feasible, label the pooled figure an upper estimate.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Repeated observations: each disbursement is recorded under its deal and identified by financier, recipient, date of the outlay (the financier's value date for cash, the delivery date for in-kind co-investment) and amount; it counts once, in the reporting year of that date. A multi-year facility contributes each year's disbursements to that year, and the same tranche is never counted twice across years or finance types. Report alongside the value: the number of deals and of distinct recipients, for interpretation.
limitations: Supports a contribution claim only: most CIMMYT engagement is evidence, investment-case development, and convening rather than a monetary commitment such as a guarantee, so there is no counterfactual showing the finance would not have flowed anyway. The documented-contribution requirement bounds, but does not eliminate, over-claiming when many actors work on one deal.

Volume says nothing about quality or reach: a large total concentrated in a few large deals can coexist with unchanged access to finance for smallholders. Read alongside the pathway’s policy indicators and the adoption and reach indicators for the systems-change narrative.

Double counting is the main measurement risk: the same dollars can appear across intermediaries, across projects, across partner organizations' reports, and across the policy and finance indicators of this register. The aggregation rule's de-duplication steps are therefore mandatory.

The climate-tagged share depends on the classification rule applied: financiers tag climate finance differently, so the split between climate and general agricultural finance is not comparable across sources without one harmonised tagging rule.

Counting only disbursements avoids inflation from unrealised pledges but lags deal-making: a weak year can reflect disbursement timing rather than reduced mobilisation, and a strong year can include disbursements on deals originated in earlier years.
subMetrics: None. Finance type, source, and the climate-tagged share are disaggregations of the same USD total, not separately calculated metrics. The count of deals and recipients reported alongside the value is interpretive context, not a sub-metric.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: project and partnership leads maintaining the deal registry and obtaining financier and partner disbursement confirmations. Validation: project MEAL officer (verifying disbursement documentation and the documented CIMMYT contribution for each deal). Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (per the Calculation method above). Approval: program leader. Reporting: CIMMYT MEAL unit to institutional and CGIAR reporting.
sourceRef: Volume 10 · Policy, finance & market systems — Reference sheet KPI-I16

name: Annual Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG)/sustainability report published
resultsLevel: Output. The Core reads an Institutional-branch level from the indicator statement itself: the published annual ESG or sustainability report is a deliverable of a corporate function, so the indicator is an output. By design in this pathway, producing the disclosure is the output and the institution-wide disclosure-and-verification share (KPI-OC40) is the outcome.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Excellence in Operations.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. The indicator measures a corporate disclosure event, an internal enabler, not a result delivered to an external population. The report's content includes climate figures, but those are measured by their own indicators (institutional greenhouse gas emissions, KPI-O45, and reduction versus baseline, KPI-OC45); the publication event itself has no direct Impact Area link.
sdgTarget: SDG target 12.6 (encourage companies to adopt sustainable practices and integrate sustainability information into their reporting cycle); indicator 12.6.1 (number of companies publishing sustainability reports). The correspondence is by analogy at entity level: 12.6.1 counts companies, and CIMMYT is a non-profit international research organization, but this indicator records exactly the entity-level fact 12.6.1 aggregates, and this sheet adopts the 12.6.1 metadata's definitions of what counts as publishing sustainability information.
otherFrameworks: GRI Standards (Global Reporting Initiative): the most widely used sustainability-reporting framework; GRI 1: Foundation 2021 defines what reporting in accordance with the GRI Standards requires. The SDG 12.6.1 minimum reporting recommendations (UNCTAD and UNEP, the indicator's custodian agencies) define a core ESG content set aligned with GRI, the IIRC integrated-reporting framework and SASB, and serve as this sheet's content benchmark.
definition: Records whether CIMMYT publishes an annual Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG)/sustainability report covering the reporting year: the corporate disclosure deliverable, scored as produced and on time. The value is binary: Yes if a publicly accessible institutional report covering the reporting year, with environmental, social and governance content, is released within six months of the close of that reporting year; No otherwise. Following the reading used for SDG indicator 12.6.1, "publishing a sustainability report" means publishing sustainability information: a stand-alone ESG/sustainability report or an equivalent clearly identified sustainability section of the institutional annual report both qualify, because the substance is the disclosure, not the binding of the document.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT delivers its own corporate sustainability disclosure each year: the visible accountability deliverable of an organization whose mission is sustainable agrifood systems. The 2030 Strategy's Excellence in Operations objectives commit CIMMYT to "ensure clarity in processes to enable better decision making and greater accountability" and to an operating environment "within applicable regulatory, compliance and risk management frameworks"; the annual ESG report is where that accountability becomes public and checkable. It is also the disclosure vehicle behind the outcome indicator KPI-OC40 (share of CIMMYT's ESG indicators publicly disclosed and independently verified): this indicator shows the deliverable was produced, KPI-OC40 shows how much of the ESG framework it discloses and verifies.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator). Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate records; there is no project instance to adapt it to.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Binary (Yes/No). Yes = the report covering the reporting year was published, publicly and on time.
directionOfChange: Reference value: Yes, in every reporting year. Yes is the state the Definition describes, a report published publicly and on time, and not a target set here. The informative event is a No, whether the report is missing or late, which signals a missed corporate deliverable and triggers follow-up.
disaggregationRequired: None. The register specifies no required disaggregation; a single institutional binary has nothing to disaggregate.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Timeliness (the publication date, read against the six-month deadline); report form (stand-alone report versus sustainability section of the annual report); assurance status of the disclosed content (recorded here as context, measured by KPI-OC40). Note: the template's "optional (project-specific)" field does not apply to an Institutional indicator; these are optional institutional annotations.
unitOfObservation: Organization (CIMMYT as a single institutional entity).
calculationSummary: Value = Yes if a report meeting all inclusion criteria is publicly released by the publication deadline; otherwise No. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): CIMMYT corporate publication records: the published report itself, its release date, and its public location. The indicator is self-evidencing; the deliverable is the evidence. Fallback DS4 (Secondary & international databases): the global report aggregators and ESG platforms that the SDG 12.6.1 custodian agencies mine, used only if the corporate record were somehow unavailable; coverage of non-profit research organizations on these platforms is not assured, so any value built this way is flagged as fallback-sourced. Not applicable DS1 (Censuses & surveys): publication is a verifiable corporate fact, not a condition reported by respondents. Not applicable DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation): a disclosure event cannot be observed remotely. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): not relevant to a corporate publication record.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source. The indicator is compiled from the DS2 publication record, not collected with a DS1 or DS5 instrument.
collectionFrequency: Annually, once, at the publication deadline.
referencePeriod: The reporting year the report covers, which is not necessarily the year of publication: a report on year N published early in year N+1 scores year N. Timeliness is judged by the publication date relative to the close of the covered year.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual binary deliverable; the publication record of prior years provides the track record, and the meaningful comparison is against the expectation of a Yes every year, not against a baseline value.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable; this is an Institutional indicator with no project-level instances.

B: Combination method. Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level as a single binary fact; there is nothing to pool, sum or average.

C: Levels and operations. Reported once, at institutional level, as the status of one report at one publication deadline. There is no level beneath it: no unit, programme or site holds a share of an institutional publication status, and a binary has no combination method, so a percentage of units reporting Yes would be a different indicator and is not computed. Where the indicator is reused across CGIAR centers each center's status is reported separately; statuses are never blended into one figure or counted into a rate. Also report: the publication date against the deadline, the assurance status of the report, and which inclusion criteria were met where the answer is No, since No without the failing criterion cannot be acted on.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no, the default for the whole register. The report is the disclosure vehicle whose content the outcome indicator KPI-OC40 scores (share of ESG indicators disclosed and independently verified); the two connect through the results chain as a narrative, never arithmetically.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: not applicable to the binary itself. Named content overlap for quality assurance: the report reproduces values measured by other register indicators, notably institutional greenhouse gas emissions (KPI-O45), emission reduction versus baseline (KPI-OC45) and sustainable procurement (KPI-OC44). Those values are reported once, by their own indicators; this indicator records only that the disclosure vehicle exists and is never added to any of them.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion criteria: (a) issued by CIMMYT at institutional level; (b) covers the reporting year being scored; (c) publicly accessible; (d) contains environmental, social and governance content, benchmarked against the SDG 12.6.1 minimum reporting recommendations (governance and institutional disclosures, economic performance, environmental disclosures including energy, water, emissions and waste, and social disclosures including occupational health and safety, employment and diversity); (e) released within six months of the close of the reporting year, that is by 30 June where the reporting year is the calendar year. Where CIMMYT reports in accordance with the GRI Standards, the GRI content index is the content benchmark for criterion (d) and the SDG 12.6.1 recommendations are the floor beneath it; the benchmark applied is stated with the value.
limitations: Publication is not quality: a thin report scores Yes as readily as a comprehensive, assured one. What share of CIMMYT's ESG framework is disclosed and independently verified is measured by KPI-OC40; always read the pair together.

The series has a ceiling: once annual publication is routine, the value is a flat Yes and carries no improvement signal. Its function is a compliance floor, and the informative event is slippage (a No, or a late report), not the repeated Yes.

"On time" means published on or before 30 June following the close of the calendar reporting year. The publication date is reported alongside the binary, so a Yes that arrived late and a Yes that arrived early are distinguishable without a second indicator.

A Yes evidences corporate delivery, not performance: the indicator is fully under CIMMYT's control and says nothing about whether the organization's environmental or social footprint improved. Footprint movement is read from KPI-O45 and KPI-OC45, not from this indicator.

Comparability across years requires stable criteria for what counts as the report: switching between a stand-alone report and a sustainability section of the annual report is acceptable under the SDG 12.6.1 reading, but the change of form should be noted in the series so year-on-year statements stay interpretable.
subMetrics: None. "Produced" and "on time" are two conditions of the single binary value, not separately reported metrics. If reviewers want timeliness read separately, it is recorded as the optional timeliness annotation in Measurement basics rather than as a sub-metric. The disclosure-quality dimension deliberately lives in a separate indicator, KPI-OC40, which has its own reference sheet.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Institutional indicator; roles sit with CIMMYT's enabling units. Data collection: communications, as the enabling unit that produces CIMMYT's institutional corporate reporting, compiling the report and logging its publication date and public location. Validation: communications together with the contributing content owners, finance and procurement (economic performance, procurement), human resources (employment, diversity, occupational health and safety), legal (governance and compliance disclosures) and the corporate function owning the greenhouse gas inventory (environmental disclosures). Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, scoring the binary against the criteria in Calculation method. Approval: the Director General, as owner of CIMMYT's institutional corporate reporting, with publication reported to the Board of Trustees. Reporting: communications to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 11 · Institutional performance & operations — Reference sheet KPI-O43

name: Absolute gross greenhouse gas emissions (tCO2e) across Scopes 1, 2 and 3 of CIMMYT's institutional operation
resultsLevel: Output. The measured inventory value is a deliverable produced by CIMMYT (Output); the change it enables, the percentage reduction versus baseline, is tracked separately as the outcome (KPI-OC45). CGIAR's formal output/outcome test (control by the research team versus behaviour change in external actors) is written for research results and fits institutional indicators imperfectly, since there is no external actor; the level here rests on the deliverable-versus-change logic.
primaryObjective: Excellence in Operations (institutional enabler component). As an Institutional indicator it does not map to a mission Primary Objective (PO1 to PO5); institutional indicators map to one of the five enabler components of the 2030 Strategy, and the register assigns this indicator to Excellence in Operations.
cgiarImpactArea: Climate Adaptation & Mitigation. Institutional indicators default to Not applicable, but this is the recognised exception: an institutional GHG footprint has a genuine direct link to the Climate Adaptation & Mitigation Impact Area, since the inventory measures CIMMYT's own contribution to, and management of, greenhouse gas emissions.
sdgTarget: None. SDG target 13.2 and indicator 13.2.2 (total greenhouse gas emissions per year) concern national inventories compiled under the UNFCCC, not organizational footprints; an organizational Scope 1-3 inventory has no direct SDG indicator correspondence, so None is recorded rather than a stretched mapping.
otherFrameworks: The GHG Protocol Corporate Standard is the near-universal basis for organizational climate disclosure: CDP climate disclosure, science-based target setting, and corporate ESG and sustainability reporting all require or accept Scope 1-3 inventories prepared to it. No donor results framework carries this indicator; it enters donor reporting through institutional sustainability and ESG channels.
definition: Measures the absolute gross greenhouse gas emissions, in tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e), generated by CIMMYT's own institutional operation in the reporting year, covering all three scopes defined by the GHG Protocol Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard: Scope 1 (direct emissions from sources CIMMYT owns or controls, such as fuel burned in vehicles, generators and field stations), Scope 2 (indirect emissions from purchased electricity, heat and steam), and Scope 3 (all other indirect emissions occurring in CIMMYT's value chain, such as business travel, procurement of goods and services, and commuting). "Gross" means before subtracting any offsets, credits or removals: the inventory reports what CIMMYT's operation emitted.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT measures and manages the climate footprint of its own operation, a basic credibility test for a research organization whose mission includes climate adaptation and mitigation. The annual inventory is the factual basis for institutional sustainability reporting to donors and for ESG-style disclosure, and it supplies the values from which the companion outcome indicator, percentage GHG reduction versus baseline (KPI-OC45), is calculated. Without a complete, consistently bounded inventory, no decarbonisation claim can be substantiated.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional scope). This indicator measures a property of CIMMYT as an organization, reported once at Center level from corporate systems; no project instantiates it, so there is no project-specific layer.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) per reporting year. All greenhouse gases in the inventory are converted to CO2 equivalent using published global warming potential values, with the source and vintage of those values stated in the inventory report.
directionOfChange: Decrease. A falling value means fewer tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent measured under the stated inventory boundary and method; a change of boundary, Scope 3 coverage or method moves the value in either direction without any change in emissions, so the boundary is stated with every value.
disaggregationRequired: Required: by scope (1, 2, 3), with Scope 2 reported on both location-based and market-based methods and Scope 3 broken out by category. The GHG Protocol requires the three scopes reported separately and never netted against each other. Scope 2 on both methods is a requirement, not a choice: location-based uses grid-average emission factors, market-based uses supplier-specific factors where contractual instruments exist, and a Scope 2 figure that does not state which basis it uses is not comparable. Scope 3 is broken out by GHG Protocol category (the standard defines 15). Recommended: by site or country of operation, for internal management.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional scope; no project layer).
unitOfObservation: Organization (CIMMYT at Center-institutional level; underlying records at site and transaction level).
calculationSummary: Total = Scope 1 + Scope 2 + Scope 3, each scope calculated as the sum over its emission sources of (activity data x emission factor), expressed in tCO2e. Activity data (litres of fuel, kWh purchased, kilometres travelled) come from corporate records; emission factors come from published sources named in the inventory report; a category estimated from spend is the Fallback in Data source. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): CIMMYT's own corporate records are the primary source for all three scopes: fuel purchase and fleet records and refrigerant logs (Scope 1), electricity and energy invoices and meter readings (Scope 2), travel bookings, procurement and finance records (Scope 3 activity data). Emission factors applied to these activity data are taken from published factor sets named in the inventory report. Fallback DS4 (Secondary & international databases): where activity-level records are unavailable, above all for Scope 3 procurement categories, spend-based estimation using published environmentally extended input-output emission factors is the accepted fallback; any value built partly on it is flagged as fallback-sourced, with the spend-based categories and their share of the total named, since it carries materially higher uncertainty. Not applicable: DS1 (Censuses & surveys), DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation), DS5 (Citizen-generated data): an organization's fuel use, energy purchases and value-chain activity cannot be measured by household surveys, satellite observation or crowdsourced data.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, secondary source. The recommended source is DS2 administrative records compiled through the inventory process; no survey module or primary-collection instrument is involved.
collectionFrequency: Annual. Underlying activity data (fuel, energy, travel, procurement) accumulate continuously in corporate systems and are compiled into the inventory once per year.
reportingFrequency: Annual, into institutional sustainability and ESG reporting.
referencePeriod: The reporting year (CIMMYT's annual reporting cycle): each value describes the emissions generated by operations during that single year.
baselineRequired: No, for reporting the annual level: each year's inventory stands alone as a complete measurement. However, the GHG Protocol requires a documented base year with a recalculation policy for tracking performance over time, and the companion outcome indicator (KPI-OC45) cannot be computed at all without one; whether CIMMYT has fixed a base year is an open item below. If no base year exists, the level can be reported but no reduction claim can be made.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: Not applicable. The inventory is compiled once at Center level from corporate systems; there are no project instances to pool.

B: Combination method. Sum: Total = Scope 1 + Scope 2 + Scope 3, each scope being the sum over its emission sources of activity data multiplied by its emission factor, in tCO2e. Never averaged, and never added to another organisation's total.

C: Levels and operations. The three scopes add within CIMMYT: the institutional figure is their sum, computed once from corporate records. There is no level beneath it, and a scope is not a level: Scope 2 is a category of the same total, not a site's share of it. Where a view by site, scope category or emission source is wanted it is recomputed from that subset's own activity data, never taken as a share of the total. The total is never summed with another organisation's total, because Scope 3 contains other organisations' Scope 1 and 2 by design and the sum would count the same physical emissions twice. A CGIAR-level figure is built by consolidating the underlying records under one boundary and one Scope 3 category coverage, with inter-center transactions identified and removed, never by adding published center totals. Also report: the scope-by-scope breakdown, the organizational boundary and consolidation approach, the Scope 3 categories included, and the emission-factor source and vintage, since a total computed on different factors is a different total.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: No. The tCO2e value is not added to any outcome or impact figure. It relates to its companion outcome, KPI-OC45 (percentage GHG reduction versus baseline), by derivation, not addition: OC45 is calculated from this indicator's baseline-year and reporting-year values.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: Scope 3 by design overlaps with other organizations' Scope 1 and 2 emissions, so CIMMYT's total must never be summed with partner or supplier inventories. No overlap exists with the mission-branch environmental indicators (for example GHG emission intensity of production systems, KPI-I09): those measure farming-system emissions under a field-level boundary, this indicator measures CIMMYT's own operation under an organizational boundary, and the two must never be combined into one emissions figure.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion and exclusion: the organizational boundary is set by one of the GHG Protocol's consolidation approaches (operational control, financial control, or equity share), applied consistently across all three scopes and stated in the report; the approach is operational control, documented in the inventory. Scope 3 categories are screened for relevance; excluded categories are listed with the reason for exclusion, so an omission is always visible. Offsets, credits and removals are excluded: the indicator is gross emissions.

Missing data: where activity data are unavailable for a source, emissions are estimated (for example spend-based estimation for procurement categories) and the estimated share of the total is disclosed; missing data are never silently treated as zero.

Repeated observations: not applicable in the survey sense; the inventory is compiled once per reporting year. Three cases trigger a documented recalculation of base year emissions rather than being absorbed into the trend: structural changes in the reporting organization that have a significant impact on base year emissions, including mergers, acquisitions, divestments, and the outsourcing or insourcing of emitting activities; changes in calculation methodology or improvements in the accuracy of emission factors or activity data that result in a significant impact on base year emissions data; and the discovery of significant errors, or of a number of cumulative errors that are collectively significant. CIMMYT develops and documents a base year recalculation policy, states the significance threshold it applies, discloses it with the inventory, and applies the policy consistently to both increases and decreases. A factor update that reflects a change of emissions to the atmosphere rather than a change in measurement is not among the triggers, and the base year is not recalculated for it.
limitations: Absolute emissions track organizational scale as much as climate performance: growth in staff, field operations or programme volume can raise the total even while efficiency improves, and a shrinking budget can lower it with no management action. Read the level together with the reduction trend (KPI-OC45) before drawing conclusions.

Scope 3 is estimated rather than metered for most categories, and spend-based estimation is materially less precise than metered activity data. The required scope breakdown shows which component a movement in the headline came from; where it came from Scope 3, it is a movement in the least certain component, and the breakdown is read before the total is interpreted.

Comparability over time and across CGIAR centers depends on a consistent organizational boundary and consistent Scope 3 category coverage; expanding coverage (adding a previously unmeasured category) raises the reported total while representing better measurement, not worse performance, and must be footnoted as such. A year-on-year movement driven by a change in calculation methodology, or by an improvement in the accuracy of an emission factor or of activity data, is not a change in emissions to the atmosphere. Where such a change has a significant impact on base year emissions, the base year is recalculated so that the movement does not enter the trend. An emission factor that changes because the underlying reality changed is different in kind: under the location-based method, a grid average factor falling as the grid decarbonises is a real change of emissions to the atmosphere, and it is counted as an increase or decrease in the emissions profile over time rather than recalculated away.

This is CIMMYT's corporate footprint only. It says nothing about the emissions or mitigation performance of the farming systems CIMMYT's research targets, which are measured by mission-branch environmental indicators under a different boundary.

A decline means the measured inventory fell under the stated boundary and method; it does not by itself demonstrate decarbonisation. A credible reduction claim requires the same boundary, a fixed base year, and disclosure of any method or factor changes.
subMetrics:
The headline value is the sum of three separately calculated components, each reported in its own right per the GHG Protocol:

— Scope 1 (tCO2e): sum of direct emissions from owned or controlled sources = sum over sources of (activity data x emission factor).

— Scope 2 (tCO2e): indirect emissions from purchased electricity, heat and steam; calculated and reported twice, location-based and market-based, as the GHG Protocol requires. The location-based figure is the one designated for the headline sum, and the designation holds across years. It is designated because the location-based method rests on the grid average factor for a site's location, while the market-based method rests on contractual instruments a site may or may not hold. A market-based total can therefore combine sites measured on different bases, and a location-based total cannot. The market-based figure is reported in full alongside it. Changing the designation is a change in calculation methodology and is assessed for a documented base-year recalculation under the rule in Eligibility.

— Scope 3 (tCO2e): sum over the relevant GHG Protocol value-chain categories of (activity data or spend x emission factor), with excluded categories listed and justified.

None of the three has a separate KPI sheet; they are components of this inventory and are reported as its required breakdown.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Institutional indicator; roles sit with CIMMYT's enabling units. Finance and procurement owns the greenhouse gas inventory. Data collection: finance and procurement; human resources for headcount and the commuting basis; knowledge management and IT for data-centre and equipment energy. Validation: the inventory owner, with periodic independent verification consistent with ISO 14064-3:2019. Calculation: the inventory owner, applying the method above. Approval: finance and procurement, as inventory owner, approves the inventory; the Director General, as owner of CIMMYT's institutional sustainability reporting, approves its use in that reporting, with the inventory reported to the Board of Trustees. Reporting: CIMMYT MEAL unit into institutional Excellence in Operations reporting.
sourceRef: Volume 11 · Institutional performance & operations — Reference sheet KPI-O45

name: Number of grievance cases received, processed, and resolved
resultsLevel: Output. Note: CGIAR's output/outcome boundary test (control by the research team versus behaviour change in external actors) is written for research results and fits an internal operations indicator poorly; the Output classification records the indicator's position as a deliverable of CIMMYT's own operations.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Excellence in Operations.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. The indicator measures a property of CIMMYT as an organization (the operation of its own accountability mechanism), an internal enabler rather than a result delivered to an external population, so the Institutional default applies.
sdgTarget: None. SDG target 16.6 (develop effective, accountable and transparent institutions at all levels) is thematically adjacent, but its official indicator 16.6.2 measures the proportion of a population satisfied with their last experience of public services, from citizen surveys, not an organization's grievance-case throughput, so no official SDG indicator directly corresponds.
otherFrameworks: UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (OHCHR, 2011), Principle 31, which sets the effectiveness criteria for non-judicial grievance mechanisms (legitimate, accessible, predictable, equitable, transparent, rights-compatible, a source of continuous learning). GRI 2: General Disclosures 2021, disclosures 2-25 (processes to remediate negative impacts, which cover grievance mechanisms) and 2-26 (mechanisms for seeking advice and raising concerns). Both frameworks concern mechanism quality and disclosure; neither prescribes this count itself.
definition: Counts the grievance cases received, processed, and resolved through CIMMYT's grievance mechanism in the reporting year. A grievance case is a complaint or concern formally lodged through the mechanism's designated channels and registered in its case system, whether raised by staff, partners, or other affected parties. The indicator is a throughput measure of the accountability mechanism: it reports three companion counts (cases received, cases processed, cases resolved) that together show the mechanism is operating and at what volume, not how well it performs for complainants.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's formal accountability channel is functioning and in use: a grievance mechanism that receives, processes, and closes cases is the operational evidence behind the 2030 Strategy's Excellence in Operations commitments to "ensure clarity in processes to enable better decision making and greater accountability" and to operate "within applicable regulatory, compliance and risk management frameworks". Tracked for institutional reporting, donor and partner assurance, and environmental, social and governance disclosure, where a working grievance channel is a standard expectation.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator). Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate systems; there is no project instance to adapt it to.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Number of cases, reported as three companion counts for the reporting year: cases received, cases processed, cases resolved.
directionOfChange: Not directional. A rise in cases received can mean more grievances or more trust in the mechanism; a fall can mean fewer problems or a channel people avoid. What is interpretable is the relationship among the three counts: whether the backlog grows.
disaggregationRequired: Case category, on a fixed institutional list: workplace conduct; safeguarding, including harassment and abuse; research integrity; procurement and supplier; partner and community; other. The split is required because a pooled grievance count cannot be acted on, and because the UN Guiding Principles' Principle 31 makes a grievance mechanism a source of continuous learning only if its caseload can be read by type. Small-cell suppression applies: any category with fewer than five cases in the reporting year is reported inside "other" rather than separately, so that a category cut can never identify a complainant. The floor applies to each of the three counts separately, and where "other" would itself hold from one to four cases, the smallest published category is merged into it.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Channel of receipt; duty station or region; resolution-time band. All cuts carry the same five-case suppression floor as the required category split. The template's "optional (project-specific)" field does not apply to an Institutional indicator; these are optional institutional cuts the owning function may add.
unitOfObservation: The grievance case (the registered case record).
calculationSummary: Value = the count of cases received, the count processed and the count resolved, reported as three separate annual figures. Received: distinct new cases formally lodged and registered in the mechanism's case system during the reporting year. Processed: cases whose intake and substantive review were completed during the year, whatever year they were received; a case still under active handling at the close of the year is backlog, not a processed case, and is reported as such. Resolved: cases closed with a documented resolution outcome during the year, regardless of the year they were received. Alongside the three counts, report the cohort resolution share: the proportion of cases received in the reporting year that were resolved within 90 days of receipt, computed 90 days after the close of the year so that every case in the cohort has had the full window. The three counts show the mechanism is running; the cohort share is the only figure among them that shows how it performs for a complainant. It is a companion figure to this indicator, never added to the counts. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): the grievance mechanism's case registry or case-management system, recording case identifier, date received, category, processing status, and closure date and outcome. Fallback DS2 (lower-resolution instance of the same code): manual case logs kept by the owning office where no centralized case system covers the full year; a value built from these must be flagged as fallback-sourced, because de-duplication across channels and closure evidence are weaker. Not applicable DS1 (Censuses & surveys): the count is an administrative fact; surveys can measure awareness of or satisfaction with the mechanism, but they do not feed this count. Not applicable DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation): not relevant to case records. Not applicable DS4 (Secondary & international databases): CIMMYT's internal case registry is not held by third parties. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): a grievance enters this indicator only once formally registered.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source. The indicator is compiled from existing DS2 case records, not collected with a DS1 or DS5 instrument.
collectionFrequency: Continuous administrative logging: each case is registered, updated, and closed in the case system as events occur.
referencePeriod: The CIMMYT reporting year, which is the calendar year, register-wide. Received, processed and resolved are flows within the year; the stock of cases still open at the close of the year is reported alongside them as backlog, since three flows without the stock cannot show whether the mechanism is keeping pace. The cohort resolution share is computed 90 days after the close of the year and reported with the following year's return.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual institutional count; the previous year's values are the reference for trend. Where a multi-year trend is wanted, the first year with complete case-registry records serves as the reference year.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable; this Institutional indicator is drawn once from corporate systems, so there are no project instances to pool. Any period built from fallback manual logs is noted alongside the figure rather than blended silently.

B: Combination method. Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level: cases are summed across channels, units, and duty stations after de-duplication by case identifier; counts are never averaged.

C: Levels and operations. Computed once, at institutional level, as the count of distinct grievance cases in the reporting year, deduplicated on the case identifier per Block E. There is no level beneath it, because no unit or programme holds a share of an institutional count. Where a view by unit, function or region is wanted, it is recomputed from that subset's own records, never taken as a share of the institutional figure. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels: a grievance case has no plot and no household. Also report: each of the three counts side by side with the others, since received, processed and resolved describe different populations; the number of cases excluded under Eligibility; and the share of the year's caseload carried over from prior years.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no (the default). The register rolls this output up to the Excellence in Operations component directly, with no downstream outcome indicator; it contributes to the institutional accountability narrative, not to any arithmetic total with other indicators.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: the same grievance lodged through more than one channel, or transferred between offices, is counted once, matched on the unique case identifier before the institutional counts are formed; if a common identifier cannot be applied across all channels, the reported counts are labelled an upper estimate. The three companion counts must never be summed with each other: received, processed, and resolved describe overlapping sets of cases, and adding them would count the same case up to three times.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion and exclusion: includes every case registered through the mechanism's designated channels, including anonymous cases where the mechanism registers them; excludes complaints raised informally and never registered, and duplicate lodgings of the same grievance.

Missing data: a registered case with incomplete fields still counts (existence in the registry is the fact being counted); a case that cannot be verified in the registry does not.

Repeated observations: one grievance lodged through several channels or escalated between units counts once, de-duplicated by unique case identifier; a case spanning years counts once as received (intake year) and once as resolved (closure year).
limitations: Throughput, not effectiveness: the three counts show the mechanism operates and at what volume, but say nothing about whether it is trusted, fair, or safe to use. The cohort resolution share adds timeliness and nothing more. Mechanism quality is assessed against the UN Guiding Principles' Principle 31 effectiveness criteria, which require different evidence again (user feedback, accessibility, outcome quality).

Direction is ambiguous by construction: more cases received can signal worsening conduct or growing trust in and awareness of the channel; fewer cases can signal fewer problems or a chilling effect. Never read the received count alone as good or bad news.

Underreporting is structural: the indicator captures only grievances formally lodged. Fear of retaliation, lack of awareness, or inaccessible channels suppress case numbers, so a low count is not evidence of few grievances.

The three counts are not a within-year cohort: cases resolved this year may have been received last year, so resolved divided by received is not a resolution rate, and a year with many resolutions may be clearing backlog.

Comparability over time depends on a stable case definition and channel scope: adding intake channels, changing case categories, or reorganizing the owning office shifts the counts without any change in underlying conduct; note such changes alongside the reported values.
subMetrics:
None. The cohort resolution share required in the Calculation method is a companion figure reported with the indicator, not a sub-metric of it: it is built from the same case records but answers a different question, and it is never added to or divided into the three counts.

A within-year "resolution rate" (resolved divided by received) is excluded and must not be published: the cases resolved in a year include cases received in earlier years, so its numerator and denominator are drawn from different populations. Where the case system carries a received and a closed date on every case, a median time to resolution is reported on the same receipt-year cohort as the resolution share, never on the cases closed in a year, which span several intake years.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, OHCHR, 2011, Principle 31 (effectiveness criteria for non-judicial grievance mechanisms): https://www.ohchr.org/sites/default/files/documents/publications/guidingprinciplesbusinesshr_en.pdf. GRI 2: General Disclosures 2021 (disclosures 2-25 and 2-26), via the GRI Standards English-language library: https://www.globalreporting.org/how-to-use-the-gri-standards/gri-standards-english-language/. UN SDG indicator 16.6.2 metadata sheet (last updated 2023-03-31), UN Statistics Division, cited as the adjacency reference for the "None" SDG determination, not as a mapping; cited from the project's SDG metadata library, which lists no public URL.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Institutional indicator; roles sit with CIMMYT's enabling units. Data collection: legal, as the enabling unit administering the grievance mechanism and holding the single institutional case registry, registering each case and logging its closure; human resources handles workplace-conduct and safeguarding cases within its own scope and files them to the same registry, so a case appears once whichever door it came through. Validation: legal, cross-checking registry completeness and de-duplication by case identifier before the counts are formed. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, compiling the three annual counts, the backlog and the cohort resolution share per the Calculation method. Approval: head of legal, with the annual figures reported to the Board of Trustees as part of institutional accountability reporting. Reporting: legal to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.

name: Compliance and safeguards frameworks (environmental and social safeguards, conflict of interest, research ethics) established and operationalised
resultsLevel: Output. Note: CGIAR's output/outcome boundary test (control by the research team versus behaviour change in external actors) is written for research results and fits an internal governance indicator poorly; the Output classification records that the frameworks are deliverables of CIMMYT's corporate functions, while their subsequent coverage across projects, partnerships and research activities is measured by the downstream outcome indicators.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Excellence in Operations.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. The indicator measures a property of CIMMYT as an organization (the existence and operation of its own compliance frameworks), an internal enabler rather than a result delivered to an external population, so the Institutional default applies.
sdgTarget: None. SDG target 16.6 (develop effective, accountable and transparent institutions) is thematically adjacent, but no official SDG indicator measures the establishment status of an individual organization's internal compliance frameworks.
otherFrameworks: IFC Performance Standards on Environmental and Social Sustainability (2012), Performance Standard 1, the widely used international benchmark for an organization-level environmental and social risk-management framework (policy, identification of risks, management programme, monitoring). GRI 2: General Disclosures 2021, disclosures 2-23 (policy commitments) and 2-24 (embedding policy commitments), which distinguish adopting a policy from operationalising it, the same two-stage logic this indicator uses. CIMMYT's conflict-of-interest and research-ethics frameworks are shown as aligning with the CGIAR Ethics Framework (CGIAR System Organization), the system-level instrument covering research ethics and conflict of interest across the centers; the environmental and social safeguards framework aligns with IFC Performance Standard 1, named above. None of these instruments prescribes this milestone indicator itself.
definition: Reports whether each of CIMMYT's three compliance and safeguards frameworks (environmental and social safeguards; conflict of interest; research ethics) is established and operationalised. A framework is established when its policy is formally approved by the competent CIMMYT governance body, its procedures are documented, and a responsible unit is designated; it is operationalised when those procedures are demonstrably in routine use (screenings, reviews or ethics clearances being conducted and logged, staff informed of their obligations, and status reported to management). The indicator is the governance-infrastructure deliverable of the compliance system: it records that the frameworks exist and function, not how widely or how well they are applied.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT has the governance infrastructure its compliance obligations require: the 2030 Strategy's Excellence in Operations component commits CIMMYT to "ensure an operating environment within applicable regulatory, compliance and risk management frameworks" and to systems that "build trust and accountability between staff and with CIMMYT partners". Tracked for institutional reporting and for donor and partner assurance, where documented safeguards, conflict-of-interest controls and research-ethics oversight are standard due-diligence expectations. The frameworks are also the precondition for the three coverage outcomes that depend on them (KPI-OC42, KPI-OC43, KPI-OC46).
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator). Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate systems; there is no project instance to adapt it to.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Status per framework, on a three-stage milestone scale (Not established / Established / Operationalised), reported side by side for the three frameworks. May be summarised as the number of frameworks operationalised (0 to 3), always accompanied by the per-framework statuses.
directionOfChange: Reference value: all three frameworks at the operationalised stage. The reference is the terminal state of the milestone scale, not a target set here. A framework moving up the scale has passed a documented governance milestone, and once all three are operationalised continued reporting evidences maintenance. A regression, such as a policy lapsing without re-approval or reviews ceasing, moves a framework back down the scale and is the informative event.
disaggregationRequired: None. The register records no required disaggregation; the per-framework status is part of the indicator's own structure (three companion statuses), not a disaggregation applied to a single value.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Duty station or region, for the operationalisation evidence only (whether procedures are in routine use beyond headquarters). The template's "optional (project-specific)" field does not apply to an Institutional indicator; this is an optional institutional cut the owning functions may add.
unitOfObservation: The framework (each of the three assessed policy systems).
calculationSummary: Milestone status assignment. For each of the three frameworks, assign the highest stage for which documented evidence exists at the reference date. The criteria below are the evidence checklist, applied unchanged each year, with each assignment recording which document or log satisfied each criterion so a status can be re-derived rather than re-argued. Established requires a policy document formally approved by the competent CIMMYT governance body, documented procedures, and a designated responsible unit. Operationalised additionally requires all three of the following within the reporting year: safeguard screenings, conflict-of-interest reviews or ethics clearances conducted and logged; staff communication or training on obligations delivered; and framework status reported to CIMMYT's Management Committee. A framework meeting some but not all three operationalisation criteria stays at Established, and the criteria it met are recorded. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): the corporate policy register and the owning functions' records, namely approved policy documents and governance approval minutes (establishment evidence) and screening logs, conflict-of-interest review records, ethics committee decisions, training or communication records, and management reports (operationalisation evidence). Fallback DS2 (lower-resolution instance of the same code): signed annual attestations by the owning functions where consolidated records are incomplete. An attestation can evidence the staff communication or training criterion and the Management Committee reporting criterion for Operationalised, but not the first, which requires the screenings, reviews or clearances themselves to be logged; a status built on attestation without underlying logs must be flagged as fallback-sourced, because operationalisation evidence is weaker. Not applicable DS1 (Censuses & surveys): framework status is a documentary fact; staff surveys can evidence awareness but do not establish status. Not applicable DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation): not relevant to policy records. Not applicable DS4 (Secondary & international databases): CIMMYT's internal policy status is not held by third parties. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): status cannot be crowdsourced.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source. The indicator is compiled from existing DS2 policy and compliance records, not collected with a DS1 or DS5 instrument.
collectionFrequency: Annual status assessment by the owning functions, compiled from continuously maintained administrative records.
referencePeriod: Status as at the end of the CIMMYT reporting year; operationalisation evidence is drawn from activity within that year.
baselineRequired: No. This is a milestone status indicator; the first annual status assessment serves as the reference point, and prior-year status is the comparison for all later years.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable; this Institutional indicator is drawn once from corporate systems, so there are no project instances to pool. Any framework whose status rests on fallback attestation is noted alongside the reported statuses rather than blended silently.

B: Combination method. Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level as three companion statuses; statuses are never averaged into a score, and the 0-to-3 summary count is only reported with the per-framework statuses attached.

C: Levels and operations. A staged status is assigned once, at institutional level, per framework: the highest stage for which documented evidence exists at the reference date. The three statuses are reported side by side and are never averaged, scored or summed into a single figure: the stages are ordered but the distance between them is not a quantity, so a mean of stages is not a stage. Where a summary is wanted, the count of frameworks at Operationalised may be given, and only with all three per-framework statuses printed beside it, because the count alone cannot distinguish a framework that has not started from one a stage short. There is no level beneath the institution: a stage is a property of the framework, not a share any unit holds. Also report: the reference date, the evidence relied on for each assignment, and any status resting on attestation rather than on a document.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no (the default). This output feeds the three downstream outcome indicators (percentage of field projects with documented safeguards, KPI-OC42; percentage of private-sector partnerships subject to conflict-of-interest review, KPI-OC43; percentage of research activities with informed consent, KPI-OC46) through the Theory of Change as a narrative (frameworks must exist before coverage can be measured), never arithmetically.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: the boundary with neighbouring indicators is definitional. Coverage evidence (how many projects, partnerships or research activities the frameworks reach) belongs to KPI-OC42, KPI-OC43 and KPI-OC46 and must not be re-reported here as additional status evidence; the grievance mechanism (KPI-O46) and audits are separate instruments outside this indicator. Within the indicator, each framework is scored once; a single document serving two frameworks (for example a combined ethics and conflict-of-interest policy) is credited to each framework it demonstrably covers, which is a shared evidence base, not double counting of a reported unit.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion and exclusion: only the three named frameworks count; related instruments (grievance mechanism, procurement standards, audit function) are covered by other indicators and are excluded here.

Missing data: a stage without documented evidence is not credited; an undocumented claim of operationalisation scores Established at most.

Repeated observations: status is assessed once per reporting year against the same criteria; a framework revised or re-approved during the year is scored on its year-end status.
limitations: Existence, not effectiveness: an operationalised framework can still be poorly applied, under-resourced, or ignored in practice. How far the frameworks reach is measured by the downstream coverage indicators (KPI-OC42, KPI-OC43, KPI-OC46), and even full coverage does not prove the quality of individual reviews or clearances.

Stage assignment still rests on judgment at the margin: the evidence checklist fixes what must be shown, but whether a training round or a screening log is substantial enough to count is the assessor's call. Recording the evidence behind each criterion is what keeps that call reviewable.

Milestone indicators saturate: once all three frameworks are operationalised the value stops moving, and continued green status is easy to read as progress when it only evidences maintenance. The informative signals after saturation are regressions and the downstream coverage trends.

A status upgrade means a governance milestone was passed with documented evidence; it does not mean compliance conduct improved, risks declined, or incidents fell. Pair with the coverage indicators and the grievance and audit indicators for the institutional accountability narrative.
subMetrics: None with their own formulas. The three per-framework statuses are components of this single indicator, not separately calculated sub-metrics. The three downstream coverage measures are separate indicators with their own sheets. Two sit in another volume, because the register homes them with the research activities they cover rather than with the frameworks that authorise them: Vol. 2 · KPI-OC42 (field projects with documented safeguards) and Vol. 2 · KPI-OC46 (research activities with informed consent). KPI-OC43 (private-sector partnerships subject to conflict-of-interest review) is in this volume.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
The indicator definition and stage scale are stated on CIMMYT's own authority. The operative standards are CIMMYT's own three framework documents, each cited by title and approval date as the corporate policy register records it; for research ethics that document is CIMMYT Institutional Research Ethics Committee procedures and guidelines, Version 2.0, October 2018, together with the CIMMYT research ethics policy it implements.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Institutional indicator; roles sit with the enabling unit owning each framework. Data collection: legal, for both the environmental and social safeguards framework and the conflict-of-interest framework, maintaining the corporate policy register, the screening logs and the review records; the CIMMYT Institutional Research Ethics Committee (IREC), for research ethics, maintaining its clearance decisions and its procedures document. Validation: the same owners, checking their evidence against the stage criteria. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, compiling the three annual statuses per the Calculation method. Approval: head of legal for the first two frameworks and the IREC Chair for the third; the consolidated three-framework status is approved by the Management Committee and reported to the Board of Trustees, which is the body that endorsed the establishment of IREC. Reporting: legal and IREC to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
