name: Number of internal and external audits conducted and reports issued
resultsLevel: Output. Note: CGIAR's output/outcome boundary test (control by the research team versus behaviour change in external actors) is written for research results and fits an internal operations indicator poorly; the Output classification records the indicator's position as a deliverable of CIMMYT's own assurance systems. External audits are performed by independent parties; what the count reports is the audit engagement CIMMYT commissioned and the report issued, which is the delivery.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Excellence in Operations.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. The indicator measures a property of CIMMYT as an organization (the volume of its own audit and assurance activity), an internal enabler rather than a result delivered to an external population, so the Institutional default applies.
sdgTarget: None. SDG target 16.6 (develop effective, accountable and transparent institutions at all levels) is thematically adjacent, but no official SDG indicator measures an individual organization's audit counts, so no direct correspondence exists.
otherFrameworks: Global Internal Audit Standards (The Institute of Internal Auditors, 2024, effective January 2025), which govern how the internal audit function plans, performs, and reports engagements. International Standards on Auditing (IAASB/IFAC), which govern the conduct of external financial audits. Both frameworks define how audits are performed and reported; neither prescribes this count itself.
definition: Counts the audit engagements conducted at CIMMYT and the audit reports formally issued during the reporting year, reported as two companion counts (audits conducted; reports issued) and split by audit type (internal; external). An internal audit is an engagement carried out by or on behalf of CIMMYT's internal audit function under its approved audit plan; an external audit is an engagement carried out by an independent external party, such as the statutory financial audit or a donor-commissioned project audit. The indicator is a volume measure of the assurance activity itself: it shows that independent review of CIMMYT's operations is taking place and at what intensity, and it generates the audit recommendations whose implementation is tracked by the companion outcome indicator KPI-OC47.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's independent assurance activity is operating at its planned volume: regular internal and external audits are the operational evidence behind the 2030 Strategy's Excellence in Operations commitments to "Ensure an operating environment within applicable regulatory, compliance and risk management frameworks" and to "Ensure clarity in processes to enable better decision making and greater accountability". Tracked for institutional reporting, board and audit-committee oversight, and donor assurance, where evidence of a functioning audit cycle is a standard expectation.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator). Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate systems; there is no project instance to adapt it to.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Number of audit engagements and number of audit reports, reported as two companion counts for the reporting year: audits conducted; reports issued.
directionOfChange: Not directional. Audit volume follows the risk-based audit plan, statutory obligations and donor requirements: more audits can mean stronger assurance coverage or a heavier compliance burden, and fewer can mean a rationalised plan or an assurance gap. What is interpretable is the count of internal engagements conducted against the approved internal audit plan; the external count follows statutory and donor requirements.
disaggregationRequired: Audit type: internal / external. The indicator title names both categories, they have different owners (the internal audit function versus external audit firms and donors), and their counts carry different assurance meanings, so they are reported separately and never merged into a single undifferentiated figure.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: For internal audits: engagement theme (financial, operational, IT, safeguarding). For external audits: commissioning party (statutory, donor, certification body). Reports issued may also be cut by the year the underlying audit was conducted, which makes the lag between fieldwork and reporting visible. The template's "optional (project-specific)" field does not apply to an Institutional indicator; these are optional institutional cuts the owning function may add.
unitOfObservation: The audit engagement (the registered engagement record).
calculationSummary: Value = the count of audits conducted and the count of reports issued, reported as two separate annual figures. Audits conducted: distinct audit engagements whose fieldwork was completed during the reporting year, counted by engagement. Fieldwork completion is the basis, not the year the engagement was commissioned and not the year its report issued: commissioning counts work that has not happened, and the issue year is already the second count, so using it would make the two figures the same number told twice. Reports issued: final audit reports formally issued during the reporting year, regardless of the year the fieldwork took place. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): the consolidated audit register maintained by the owning corporate function, recording engagement identifier, type (internal/external), commissioning party, fieldwork completion date, and report issue date; internal engagements from the internal audit function's own records, external engagements from Finance and audit-committee records. Fallback DS2 (lower-resolution instance of the same code): separate manual logs held by the internal audit function and Finance where no consolidated register covers the full year; a value built from these must be flagged as fallback-sourced, because de-duplication across the two logs and issue-date evidence are weaker. Not applicable DS1 (Censuses & surveys): the count is an administrative fact, not a respondent-reported one. Not applicable DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation): not relevant to audit records. Not applicable DS4 (Secondary & international databases): CIMMYT's audit activity is not held by third parties. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): an engagement enters this indicator only once formally commissioned and registered.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source. The indicator is compiled from existing DS2 audit-register records, not collected with a DS1 or DS5 instrument.
collectionFrequency: Continuous administrative logging: each engagement is registered, updated, and closed in the audit register as events occur.
referencePeriod: The CIMMYT reporting year. Both counts are flows within the year; because reports are often issued in the year after fieldwork, the two counts do not describe the same set of engagements and are never combined into a ratio.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual institutional count; the previous year's values and the approved audit plan are the reference for interpretation. Where a multi-year trend is wanted, the first year with a complete consolidated audit register serves as the reference year.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable; this Institutional indicator is drawn once from corporate systems, so there are no project instances to pool. Donor-commissioned project audits are commissioned per project but are counted once each in the corporate register. Any period built from fallback manual logs is noted alongside the figure rather than blended silently.

B: Combination method. Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level: engagements are summed across units, duty stations, and commissioning parties after de-duplication by engagement identifier; counts are never averaged.

C: Levels and operations. Computed once, at institutional level, as the count of distinct audit engagements and audit reports issued in the reporting year, deduplicated on the engagement identifier per Block E. There is no level beneath it, because no unit or programme holds a share of an institutional count. Where a view by unit, function or region is wanted, it is recomputed from that subset's own records, never taken as a share of the institutional figure. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels: an audit engagement has no plot and no household. Also report: the two counts side by side rather than combined, since an engagement and a report are different objects; the split between internal and external; the number of engagements in the approved internal audit plan; and any engagement whose fieldwork spanned the year end and the year it was assigned to.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no arithmetic aggregation (the default: each level measures something different). The link to the outcome indicator KPI-OC47 is data lineage, not addition: the reports issued under this indicator are the source of the audit recommendations whose timely implementation OC47 measures, so the two connect through the results chain as a narrative, never as a sum.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: an engagement appearing in more than one log (for example a donor audit recorded by both Finance and the audited program) is counted once, matched on the engagement identifier; a joint internal-external engagement is assigned to one type, not both. Internal and external counts are disjoint and may be summed into a total, but the two companion counts (conducted; issued) must never be summed with each other, since they describe overlapping sets of engagements. No overlap with another register indicator: the nearest neighbours KPI-O46 (grievance cases) and KPI-O47 (compliance frameworks) count different objects, and KPI-OC47 consumes this indicator's outputs rather than recounting them.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion and exclusion: includes engagements under the approved internal audit plan, the statutory external financial audit, donor-commissioned project audits, and other formally commissioned external assurance engagements; excludes advisory or consulting reviews that issue no findings report, management self-assessments, and informal spot checks. Three boundary cases are excluded and stated so the series stays stable: investigations, which are triggered case work rather than planned or statutory assurance; certification assessments, which test a management system against an external standard on a certifier's terms and not on CIMMYT's assurance plan; and follow-up or verification reviews, which re-examine an engagement already counted and would count the same risk area twice. Follow-up reviews are recorded and reported alongside the two counts, never inside them.
limitations: Activity volume only, not assurance quality or effect: the counts show that audits happen, not whether their scope was adequate, their findings serious, or their recommendations acted on. Performance of the assurance cycle is read from KPI-OC47, not from this indicator.

Engagements are heterogeneous: a full institutional statutory audit and a narrow donor project audit each count as one, so the count weights very different levels of effort and coverage equally; the internal/external split and the optional theme cuts mitigate but do not remove this.

The two companion counts are not a within-year cohort: reports issued this year often stem from fieldwork completed last year, so "issued divided by conducted" is not a completion rate, and a year with many issued reports may be clearing a reporting backlog.

Audit volume is partly externally driven: statutory requirements and donor portfolios set much of the external count, so a change can reflect the shape of the funding portfolio rather than any change in CIMMYT's assurance posture.

Comparability over time depends on holding the engagement-type boundary: follow-up reviews, investigations and certification assessments are excluded for that reason, and admitting any of them later would lift the series without any change in underlying assurance activity. Any boundary change is noted alongside the reported values and the prior year restated.
subMetrics: None. Audits conducted and reports issued are companion counts of the same assurance activity, not separately calculated sub-metrics, and the internal/external split is a disaggregation. The share of audit recommendations implemented on time is a separate indicator with its own sheet, KPI-OC47.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Institutional indicator; roles sit with corporate functions. Data collection: internal audit, which owns the consolidated audit register and records its own engagements; finance supplies the statutory and donor-commissioned external engagements into the same register. Internal audit holds the register because it is the only function that sees both sides of the assurance cycle through the audit committee, and a register split between two owners is the reliable way to lose a donor audit. Validation: internal audit, cross-checking completeness and de-duplication across the internal and external entries. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, compiling the two annual counts per the Calculation method. Approval: head of internal audit, with the annual figures reported to the audit committee of the Board of Trustees. Reporting: internal audit to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 11 · Institutional performance & operations — Reference sheet KPI-O48

name: Number of enterprise systems or digital tools developed, deployed, or upgraded to support CIMMYT's mission and research for development (R4D)
resultsLevel: Output. CGIAR's boundary test (an output is a product delivered under the control of the responsible team; an outcome is a change in the behaviour of actors the team cannot directly control) is written for research results and fits internal operations indicators imperfectly, since there is no external actor. Read from the indicator statement, as the Core requires for an Institutional-branch indicator, a system brought into operational use is a deliverable of CIMMYT's ICT and enabling functions, so Output stands; whether staff and programmes work on unified platforms (KPI-OC48) is the organization operating differently and sits at outcome level.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Excellence in Operations.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. The indicator measures a property of CIMMYT's own operational infrastructure, an internal enabler rather than a result delivered to an external population; better systems serve every Impact Area indirectly, which is not a direct link.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator counts an organization's internal enterprise systems; SDG target 9.c (access to information and communications technology) concerns population-level network coverage, not institutional system deployment, so it is thematically adjacent only.
otherFrameworks: None. No donor or reporting framework prescribes a count of enterprise systems or digital tools brought into operational use; the indicator is defined on CIMMYT's own authority.
definition: Counts the distinct enterprise systems or digital tools that reached operational use during the reporting year, whether newly developed, deployed for the first time, or substantially upgraded. An enterprise system is a corporate software platform serving the organization as a whole (for example finance, human resources, procurement, project management, or data management platforms); a digital tool is a smaller application or service supporting CIMMYT's operations or its research-for-development work. "Reaching operational use" means the system is live and available to its intended users, not in pilot, prototype, or development status. Each distinct system or tool counts once in the year, whatever the number of stages (development, deployment, upgrade) it passed through in that year.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT is delivering the operational systems its 2030 Strategy commits to under Excellence in Operations, whose first objective is "Effective systems and tools are developed and maintained", with the specific commitments to "Create and maintain accessible, secure, and flexible tools for supporting CIMMYT's mission" and to "Implement an ICT infrastructure to support CIMMYT's digital transformation and capacity to exploit big data for R4D". The annual count is the delivery volume behind the outcome indicator KPI-OC48 (percentage of staff or programmes operating on unified data/ICT platforms): the count shows what the ICT function put into operation, the share shows whether the organization converges on those platforms.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator). Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate ICT records; there is no project instance to adapt it to.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Number of systems or tools (count of distinct enterprise systems or digital tools reaching operational use in the reporting year)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more enterprise systems or digital tools reached operational use. The count also rises when many small tools are released rather than few significant ones, and a proliferation of separate tools can work against the unified-platform outcome KPI-OC48.
disaggregationRequired: Delivery stage (developed / deployed / upgraded) and owning function. The stage split is required because the same system can enter the count in two different years on two different grounds, and a pooled figure hides which; the owning-function split is required because a count with no owner attached cannot be reconciled against the application inventory. Each counted system takes one stage, the first it passed through in the year in the order developed, deployed, upgraded: one newly developed and first deployed in the same year is recorded as developed, and one first deployed and upgraded in the same year is recorded as deployed.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: System category (enterprise system versus digital tool); primary purpose (corporate operations versus R4D support); provider (CIMMYT-delivered versus One CGIAR global service). Note: the template's "optional (project-specific)" field does not apply to an Institutional indicator; these are optional institutional cuts the ICT function may add for management use.
unitOfObservation: Result object: one enterprise system or digital tool, the individual application or platform each record describes. It is a delivered asset rather than a person, place or organization, which is what the result-object value covers.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct enterprise systems or digital tools that reached operational use during the reporting year through new development, first deployment, or a substantial upgrade released to production. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): CIMMYT's ICT project and release-management records and the institutional application inventory (portfolio register), listing each system, its owning function, and its go-live or major-release date. Fallback DS1 (Censuses & surveys): a structured annual return completed by enabling-unit heads and programme ICT focal points listing the systems and tools their units brought into operational use, used only where release records or the application inventory are incomplete; flag any value built this way as fallback-sourced, since self-reported returns apply the substantial-upgrade threshold less consistently than release records. Not applicable DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation): internal system deployment cannot be observed remotely. Not applicable DS4 (Secondary & international databases): no third-party database records CIMMYT's internal system deployments. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): not relevant to an internal ICT record.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Applicable only when the fallback DS1 return is used: a structured annual reporting template listing each system or tool, its delivery stage (developed / deployed / upgraded), its go-live date, and its intended user group. Respondent: the head of each enabling unit or the programme ICT focal point. Mode: form-based self-completion, reconciled against the application inventory by the ICT function. When the Recommended DS2 source is used, not applicable, administrative source.
collectionFrequency: Continuous administrative logging: ICT project, release, and application-inventory records capture each go-live as it occurs; compiled once per year.
referencePeriod: The CIMMYT reporting year in which the go-live or release event falls, so each counting event is attributed to exactly one year.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual institutional count; the previous year's value is the reference for trend. Where a multi-year trend is wanted, the first year with a complete application inventory and a stable substantial-upgrade rule serves as the reference year.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable. This is an Institutional indicator compiled once from corporate ICT systems; there are no project-level instances to pool. If part of a year's figure had to rely on the fallback unit returns, that portion is noted alongside the figure rather than blended silently.

B: Combination method. Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level: distinct systems and tools are summed across units and functions after de-duplication against the application inventory; never averaged.

C: Levels and operations. Computed once, at institutional level, as the count of distinct enterprise systems or digital tools reaching operational use in the reporting year, deduplicated on the system identifier per Block E. There is no level beneath it, because no unit or programme holds a share of an institutional count. Where a view by unit, function or region is wanted, it is recomputed from that subset's own records, never taken as a share of the institutional figure. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels: an enterprise system or digital tool has no plot and no household. Also report: the split between new development, first deployment and substantial upgrade, since a system may be counted in more than one year on different grounds; the number excluded under Eligibility; and the systems retired in the year, which the count does not net off.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no, the default for the whole register. This count is the delivery effort behind KPI-OC48 (share of staff or programmes on unified platforms), but the two are never combined arithmetically; they connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative (delivery enables convergence), and they can legitimately move in opposite directions, since many separate new tools can lower platform unification.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: a system used by several units (for example an enterprise resource planning platform shared by finance and procurement) is matched by its application-inventory identifier and counted once; a system is never counted twice in one year for passing through more than one delivery stage. One named overlap risk inside the register: a knowledge-sharing or data-sharing platform could plausibly be counted here and under KPI-O50 (enterprise knowledge-sharing / data-sharing platforms or communities of practice). The assignment rule is by event, not by asset: this indicator counts the delivery event in the year a platform goes live or takes a major release, KPI-O50 counts the active service in every year it is maintained and used. One platform can therefore appear in both indicators in the same year without being double counted, because they are counting different things about it; the two counts are never summed. Knowledge management and IT arbitrates, since it holds both the application inventory and the platform registry and is the only function that can see a candidate in both.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion and exclusion: includes systems and tools commissioned or operated by CIMMYT for its corporate operations or in direct support of its research-for-development work, evidenced by a go-live or release record. A substantial upgrade is a major release in ICT's release records, meaning a release that changes the platform the system runs on or gives users a function they could not perform before; where a system carries a version scheme, the major-version increment is the test. Excludes routine patches and maintenance releases, security updates, configuration changes, licence renewals, pilots and prototypes not yet in production, and tools developed as research outputs for external users, which are counted by the mission-branch innovation indicators in Vol. 1 and never here, so that one delivery is never counted in both branches.

Systems delivered to CIMMYT through One CGIAR global services count in the year CIMMYT brings them into operational use for CIMMYT users, and are flagged as CGIAR-provided in the count. The 2030 Strategy commits CIMMYT to leveraging those shared services, so excluding them would make the count fall as the strategy succeeds.
limitations: Output-level only: a system reaching operational use evidences delivery, not adoption or usefulness. Whether staff and programmes work on the platforms is measured separately by KPI-OC48, and user satisfaction is not measured by either.

The count weighs unequal things equally: a global enterprise resource planning migration and a small single-team tool each count as one, so a rising count can reflect many minor releases rather than growing operational capability. Read the count with its delivery-stage and category disaggregations.

More is not automatically better: a proliferation of separate tools can fragment the ICT landscape and pull against the unified-platform objective. A rising KPI-O49 with a flat or falling KPI-OC48 suggests fragmentation, not progress.

The major-release test fixes the boundary between a substantial upgrade and routine maintenance, but it inherits whatever versioning discipline each system carries: a platform with no version scheme is judged on the functional test, and the fallback self-reported returns apply either test less consistently than ICT's own release records.
The definition rests on CIMMYT's own authority; no external methodological standard for counting enterprise system deployments exists, so the value cannot be benchmarked against other organizations.
subMetrics: None. The delivery stages (developed, deployed, upgraded) and the system-versus-tool split are disaggregations of the same count, not separately calculated metrics. The related measure KPI-OC48 (percentage of staff or programmes on unified data/ICT platforms) is a separate outcome indicator with its own reference sheet, not a sub-metric of this count.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Institutional indicator; roles sit with knowledge management and IT, the enabling unit the 2030 Strategy names for CIMMYT's systems and data, and the same function that owns the platform registry behind KPI-O50. Data collection: knowledge management and IT, logging each release and maintaining the application inventory. Validation: the same function, reconciling against the inventory and applying the major-release test. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, de-duplicating and counting distinct systems per the Calculation method. Approval: head of knowledge management and IT. Reporting: knowledge management and IT to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 11 · Institutional performance & operations — Reference sheet KPI-O49

name: Number of enterprise knowledge-sharing / data-sharing platforms or communities of practice established and maintained
resultsLevel: Output. The count reports a delivery, the knowledge-sharing or data-sharing platforms and communities of practice CIMMYT established and kept active, and the Core reads an Institutional-branch level from the indicator statement itself: a count of deliverables a corporate function produced is an output. Whether staff then share more and collaborate better is the organization operating differently and belongs to KPI-OC49.
indicatorScope: Institutional. Measures a property of CIMMYT as an organization: the managed infrastructure it operates for internal knowledge and data sharing. Reported once, at Center level, from CIMMYT's own administrative records; no project-specific layer.
primaryObjective: Excellence in Operations (institutional enabler component). As an Institutional indicator it does not map to a mission Primary Objective (PO1 to PO5); the register's Primary Objective column is accordingly blank for this row. Within the component it serves objective 2 (enabling activities streamlined to enhance collaboration and effectiveness), sub-objective 2.2 on information and data sharing.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable (the default for Institutional indicators unless a genuine direct link exists). Internal knowledge-sharing infrastructure is an organizational enabler; it delivers no direct result in any of the five Impact Areas.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator corresponds to a count of an organization's internal knowledge-sharing platforms or communities of practice; the SDG framework measures development results, not institutional operations, so None is recorded rather than a stretched mapping.
otherFrameworks: None. No donor or external reporting framework uses a count of internal enterprise platforms or communities of practice as a standard indicator; the definitional anchor is internal, the CIMMYT 2030 Strategy's Excellence in Operations objectives.
definition: Counts the distinct enterprise knowledge-sharing or data-sharing platforms and communities of practice that CIMMYT has established and maintains, and that are active in the reporting year. A knowledge-sharing or data-sharing platform is a managed digital service through which staff across the organization find, exchange or re-use information and data, for example an institutional knowledge base, a shared data catalogue or repository, or a moderated collaboration workspace. A community of practice is an organized, ongoing group of staff, open beyond a single project team, that convenes around a shared professional domain to exchange experience and develop common ways of working, with a named convener and a stated purpose.
rationale: The 2030 Strategy's Excellence in Operations component sets the objective that enabling activities across CIMMYT are streamlined to enhance collaboration and effectiveness, with the sub-objective to "promote information and data sharing to foster a collaborative culture", and describes enabling units as central to creating the culture and spaces where collaboration happens. This indicator counts the concrete spaces CIMMYT builds and keeps alive for that sharing. It tells operations management and institutional reporting how much managed sharing infrastructure exists, and supplies the enabling base whose behavioural effect is measured by the outcome indicator KPI-OC49, the staff-reported collaboration and information-sharing score from the annual culture and engagement survey.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional scope): enterprise platforms and communities of practice are Center-level assets; no project instantiates this indicator.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Number of platforms or communities of practice (count of distinct active entries in the reporting year).
directionOfChange: Not directional. Overlapping platforms fragment knowledge, and consolidation onto the unified platforms KPI-OC48 tracks can legitimately reduce this count, so what is interpretable is the platform list behind the count, with the entries newly established and those that lapsed.
disaggregationRequired: Required: platform type (knowledge- or data-sharing platform, or community of practice); owning function, the corporate function whose staff manage the platform or convene the community. Sex and age do not apply: the unit is an organizational asset, not a person.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional scope; no project layer).
unitOfObservation: The individual platform or community of practice, an organizational asset recorded in CIMMYT's administrative systems. The template's fixed list has no platform or organizational-asset option before the result object value was added; the platform is recorded under result object.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct platforms and communities of practice meeting every inclusion criterion and active in the reporting year. This is a stock, not an annual flow. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative and registry data): the platform and service registry, community terms of reference and convener records, and usage or activity logs held by CIMMYT's knowledge management and IT function, which the 2030 Strategy names among the Center's enabling units. These records establish existence, ownership, enterprise scope and reporting-year activity. Fallback DS1 (Censuses and surveys): a structured inventory canvass of function and program focal points, used only where no central registry yet covers all candidate entries; any value built this way is flagged as fallback-sourced, since self-listing without registry evidence weakens the activity check. Not applicable: DS3 (Geospatial and Earth observation), DS4 (Secondary and international databases) and DS5 (Citizen-generated data): whether CIMMYT operates an internal platform or community is a documented fact in its own records, not something satellites, external databases or crowdsourcing can establish.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
collectionInstrument: For the DS1 fallback only: a short structured inventory form capturing name, purpose, owner or convener, membership scope, platform type, owning function and activity evidence for the reporting year. Respondent: the knowledge-management or unit focal point for each function or program. Mode: form circulated and returned once per reporting year. The Recommended DS2 route needs no instrument: it is a registry query with the inclusion and exclusion filters applied, plus document review of ambiguous entries.
collectionFrequency: Continuous registry maintenance by knowledge management and IT, verified through an annual inventory check before reporting.
referencePeriod: The reporting year: an entry counts if it meets the activity criterion at any point within that year. The year boundary is the calendar year, register-wide.
baselineRequired: No. Each year's value is a self-standing stock of active sharing infrastructure, interpretable without a prior-period reference; the first full inventory year anchors trend reporting. If a trend claim is wanted before two inventory years exist, prior-year status can be reconstructed from registry and activity logs; where reconstruction is not feasible, monitor only and make no change claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: Not applicable. The indicator is reported once at Center level; there are no project instances to pool. For portability across CGIAR centers, each center counts the platforms and communities it manages or co-manages, and a center that only participates counts none; because a co-managed platform then appears in the count of every center that co-manages it, center counts are never summed into a system figure. If part of a year's count had to rely on the fallback canvass, the entries counted from it are noted alongside the figure rather than blended silently.

B: Combination method. Sum: the count of distinct platforms and communities of practice active in the reporting year, deduplicated on the platform identifier. A stock, not a flow, so successive years are never added.

C: Levels and operations. Computed once, at institutional level, as the count of distinct platforms and communities of practice active in the reporting year, deduplicated on the platform identifier per Block E. There is no level beneath it, because no unit or programme holds a share of an institutional count. Where a view by unit, function or region is wanted, it is recomputed from that subset's own records, never taken as a share of the institutional figure. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels: a platform or community of practice has no plot and no household. Also report: that this is a stock and not an annual flow, so successive years are never summed; the number newly established and the number that lapsed; the activity test applied, since the count moves with it; and the platforms counted as co-managed, each with its co-managing centers named.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: No. This output count does not combine arithmetically with its outcome KPI-OC49 (staff-reported collaboration and information-sharing score); the two connect as a narrative, spaces built and maintained, then sharing behaviour, not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: deduplicate by registry entry, so modules, mirror sites and tool migrations of one platform count once. One named overlap risk inside the register: KPI-O49 counts enterprise systems or digital tools developed, deployed or upgraded; a data-sharing platform can legitimately appear in KPI-O49 in the year of its deployment event and here in every year it is maintained and active. The two counts measure different things, delivery events versus active services, and must never be summed; state the overlap wherever both are reported together.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: established, owned, hosted or convened by CIMMYT, alone, as managing partner, or as a co-managing center of a CGIAR-wide platform; enterprise scope, meaning open to staff across CIMMYT or across an entire function or region, not restricted to one project or team; a named owner or convener; documented activity in the reporting year (content or data updates, exchanges, or convenings on record).

Exclusion: single-project workspaces and team channels; one-off events, webinars or mailing lists with no ongoing convening; generic corporate infrastructure (email, standard office tools) not configured as a distinct knowledge- or data-sharing service; platforms or communities owned by partners or by CGIAR bodies where CIMMYT only participates; archived or dormant entries.

Missing data: an entry with no activity evidence for the reporting year, from the registry or on the Fallback inventory form, is counted as not active, not treated as missing; no imputation.

Repeated observations: each platform or community counts once per year whatever the number of members, sessions or modules it has; a community that changes hosting tool remains one community; a platform and the community meeting on it count as two entries only if the registry records distinct owners and purposes.
limitations: Counts infrastructure, not behaviour. An active platform count says nothing about whether staff find, share or re-use knowledge; read it only together with KPI-OC49 (staff-reported collaboration and information-sharing score) before making any claim about a collaborative culture.

The count moves with its definitional boundaries. Until the activity threshold and the enterprise-scope boundary are fixed and applied by one function, values are not comparable across years or across centers: a wide reading of "active" or "enterprise" inflates the count with no change in real infrastructure.

More is not automatically better. Overlapping platforms fragment knowledge and dilute participation, and consolidation onto unified platforms (the improvement KPI-OC48 tracks) can legitimately reduce this count while making sharing work better; a falling count is therefore not evidence of decline, nor a rising count evidence of progress, without the platform list behind it.

The boundary with KPI-O49 is an assignment rule, not a natural fact. A data-sharing platform is also an enterprise system; if the two sheets' rules are applied inconsistently, entries migrate between the indicators and both series bend without any real change in operations.
subMetrics: None. The splits by platform type, owning function and establishment status (new vs continuing) are disaggregations of the same count, not separately calculated metrics. Staff use of these spaces and satisfaction with them are not sub-metrics here; they belong to the outcome indicator KPI-OC49, which has its own reference sheet.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Institutional indicator; the responsible corporate function is knowledge management and IT. Data collection: the knowledge management and IT function, as custodian of the platform and service registry, community records and activity logs. Validation: the same function's leadership, confirming enterprise scope, ownership and reporting-year activity for each counted entry. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, applying the inclusion, exclusion and deduplication rules. Approval: the senior manager accountable for the Excellence in Operations component. Reporting: CIMMYT MEAL unit into institutional reporting.
sourceRef: Volume 11 · Institutional performance & operations — Reference sheet KPI-O50

name: Number of structured learning / after-action reviews conducted and improvement actions logged
resultsLevel: Output
primaryObjective: Excellence in Operations (institutional enabler component). The indicator serves the component's second 2030 objective, that enabling activities across CIMMYT are streamlined to enhance collaboration and effectiveness, and specifically its sub-objective 2.3: incorporate learning and make timely adjustments as needed for continuous improvement and increased agility (CIMMYT, 2023). As an Institutional indicator it maps to one of the five institutional enabler components, not to a mission Primary Objective (PO1 to PO5); the register's Primary Objective column is accordingly blank for this row.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. Internal learning reviews are an organizational enabler; they deliver no direct result in any of the five CGIAR Impact Areas, and no genuine direct link exists (unlike, for example, an institutional greenhouse gas footprint indicator, which does link directly to Climate Adaptation and Mitigation).
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator corresponds to the number of internal organizational learning reviews an institution conducts.
otherFrameworks: None. After-action reviews are a widely used organizational learning practice across development agencies and the private sector, but no donor or external reporting framework carries a count of learning reviews conducted as a standard indicator; the definitional anchor is internal (the CIMMYT 2030 Strategy's Excellence in Operations component), and the definition stands on CIMMYT's own authority.
definition: Counts the number of distinct structured learning reviews or after-action reviews completed by CIMMYT in the reporting year, with the resulting improvement actions logged. A structured learning review or after-action review is a facilitated, documented session held after a project phase, a major event, a process failure, or a defined period of implementation, in which the team compares what was intended with what happened, identifies why the two differed, and records the changes to make as improvement actions in an action log. A review counts only when it is both completed and its improvement actions are logged; each distinct completed review counts once.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT systematically turns its operational experience into recorded commitments to improve: the practice the 2030 Strategy's Excellence in Operations component calls for under its objective to incorporate learning and make timely adjustments for continuous improvement and increased agility. Tracked for institutional reporting as the output half of the continuous-improvement pair: this indicator counts the reviews and the actions they log, while KPI-OC50 measures the share of those logged actions implemented within the agreed timeline. Without this count there is no verifiable evidence that structured learning happens at all, and no denominator for the implementation rate downstream.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional scope). This indicator measures a property of CIMMYT as an organization, reported once at Center level from corporate records; no project instantiates it, so there is no project-specific layer.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Number of reviews (count of distinct completed reviews with improvement actions logged, per reporting year).
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more structured reviews were completed with their improvement actions logged. Where the year's review triggers are recorded, the count is read against them, since a count carries no coverage information.
disaggregationRequired: Required: organizational unit conducting the review; review type or trigger (project or phase closure, event, incident or process failure, periodic learning review).
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional scope; no project layer).
unitOfObservation: Organization (CIMMYT at Center-institutional level). The record counted is the individual completed review, evidenced by its written report and its entries in the improvement-action log.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct reviews completed in the reporting year that meet all inclusion criteria. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative and registry data): CIMMYT's own review records, specifically the written review reports together with the central improvement-action log or tracker in which each review's actions are registered. These records establish, for every counted review, that it took place, that it was structured, when it was completed, and that actions were logged. Fallback: None applicable. The existence and content of internal review records can be verified only from CIMMYT's own records; no lower-resolution or third-party substitute exists. Not applicable: DS1 (Censuses and surveys), a staff survey could recall that reviews happened but cannot substitute for the verifiable written record and action log the definition requires; DS3 (Geospatial and Earth observation), internal organizational events are not observable from satellite or GIS data; DS4 (Secondary and international databases), no external database records CIMMYT's internal learning reviews; DS5 (Citizen-generated and other non-traditional data), crowdsourced or informal reports cannot evidence a structured, documented review.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, secondary source. The recommended source is DS2 administrative records; verification is by review of each report and its action-log entries against the three inclusion criteria in Eligibility criteria and missing data, not by a survey module or primary-collection tool.
collectionFrequency: Continuous: each review's report and action log entries are recorded at the time the review is completed. The count is compiled once per year.
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the review was completed and its actions were logged.
baselineRequired: No. Each year's count is self-standing and interpretable on its own. The first assessed year anchors the trend for subsequent years; no change or improvement claim should be made until at least two years are on record under the same counting rules.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: Not applicable in the mission sense; the indicator is reported once at Center level. If the indicator is reused across CGIAR centers for portability, report each center's count separately; do not sum counts across centers whose counting rules have not been harmonized.

B: Combination method. Sum: the count of distinct qualifying reviews completed in the reporting year, deduplicated on the review identifier.

C: Levels and operations. Computed once, at institutional level, as the count of distinct structured learning or after-action reviews completed in the reporting year, deduplicated on the review identifier per Block E. There is no level beneath it, because no unit or programme holds a share of an institutional count. Where a view by unit, function or region is wanted, it is recomputed from that subset's own records, never taken as a share of the institutional figure. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels: a review has no plot and no household. Also report: the number of reviews excluded under Eligibility and why; and the number of improvement actions the reviews generated, reported beside this count rather than inside it.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: No. This output-level count does not combine arithmetically with KPI-OC50 (percentage of improvement actions from learning reviews implemented within the agreed timeline); the two connect through the results chain as a narrative, reviews log actions and OC50 tracks whether those actions get implemented. There is one deliberate data linkage, which is not aggregation: the improvement actions logged by the reviews counted here feed the denominator of KPI-OC50, so the two sheets must draw on the same action log.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: count each review once regardless of how many units, countries, or projects it covered; a joint review of one event or one multi-country project closure is one review. Deduplicate by review ID in the central log. If reviews are compiled from unit-level lists rather than a central log, the same joint review can appear on several units' lists, so the compiled count must be deduplicated by event and date before reporting; if deduplication is not possible, label the figure an upper estimate.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion criteria: (a) the review is structured, meaning it followed a defined method (a facilitated session working through intended versus actual results and reasons for the difference) and produced a written record; (b) the review was completed within the reporting year; (c) at least one improvement action from the review is logged in the improvement-action log or tracker; a review that found nothing to improve meets this criterion by logging that finding as its action.
limitations: Counts activity, not quality or effect: a review can be completed and logged without being candid, well facilitated, or consequential. Whether logged actions change anything is measured downstream by KPI-OC50, not here.

The count is sensitive to where the "structured" bar is set: applied loosely, routine meetings with notes get counted and the figure inflates; applied strictly, genuine learning sessions without a formal report are missed. Consistent application of the three inclusion criteria (defined method, written record, logged action) is what makes years comparable.

A rise in the count can reflect better recording rather than more learning, especially in the first years after a central log is introduced; interpret early-year trends as changes in documentation practice as much as changes in behaviour.

An absolute count carries no coverage information: it does not show how many project closures, incidents, or other review triggers went unreviewed. A high count alongside low review coverage of major closures would still be a weak learning practice; where possible, read the count against the year's trigger events.

Comparability across organizational units and across CGIAR centers depends on a shared definition of what counts as a structured review and a shared logging discipline; without these, differences in counts reflect definitional drift rather than real differences in learning practice.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Institutional indicator; there is no project team, so roles sit with corporate functions. Data collection: the unit conducting each review files its report and registers its improvement actions in the central log. Validation: the central log owner verifies each entry against the three inclusion criteria. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (annual compilation and deduplication per the Calculation method). Approval: head of the corporate function that owns the log. Reporting: CIMMYT MEAL unit into institutional Excellence in Operations reporting.
