name: Percentage of CIMMYT's Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) indicators that are publicly disclosed and independently verified
resultsLevel: Outcome. The share expresses an institution-wide practice (verified public disclosure as CIMMYT's normal way of reporting), not a single deliverable, which distinguishes it from the report-published output (KPI-O43). Note: CGIAR's output/outcome boundary test (control by the research team versus behaviour change in external actors) is written for research results and fits an internal operations indicator poorly; the Outcome classification records the indicator's position in the institutional results chain, not a claim about external behaviour change.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Excellence in Operations.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. The indicator measures a property of CIMMYT as an organization (the transparency and assurance of its own corporate reporting), an internal enabler rather than a result delivered to an external population, so the Institutional default applies. Any Impact Area link (for example the greenhouse gas inventory to Climate Adaptation & Mitigation) belongs to the underlying disclosed indicators, not to this disclosure share.
sdgTarget: None. SDG target 12.6 (encourage companies to adopt sustainable practices and integrate sustainability information into their reporting cycle) is thematically adjacent, but its official indicator 12.6.1 counts the number of companies publishing sustainability reports; it does not measure the share of an organization's ESG indicators that are disclosed and independently verified, so no official SDG indicator directly corresponds.
otherFrameworks: GRI 2: General Disclosures 2021, disclosure 2-5 (external assurance) requires organizations to describe their practice for seeking external assurance of sustainability reporting; this indicator quantifies that practice. ISAE 3000 (Revised) (IAASB) is the assurance standard most widely used for independent verification of ESG disclosures; ISO 14064-3:2019 is the verification standard for the greenhouse gas component. These frameworks govern how disclosure and verification are done; none prescribes this percentage itself, which is defined on CIMMYT's own authority.
definition: Measures the share of the ESG indicators in CIMMYT's ESG framework that are both publicly disclosed and independently verified in the reporting year. Publicly disclosed means the indicator's value is published in a publicly accessible CIMMYT report or channel, such as the annual ESG/sustainability report (the output tracked as KPI-O43). Independently verified means a competent third party, independent of CIMMYT, has provided assurance or verification of the disclosed value against a recognized assurance standard. Both conditions must hold for an indicator to count in the numerator: an indicator that is disclosed but not verified, or verified only internally, does not count.
rationale: Answers how much of CIMMYT's ESG reporting an external reader can rely on without taking CIMMYT's word for it: disclosure makes the information public, and independent verification makes it credible. It is the transparency-and-assurance measure of the 2030 Strategy's Excellence in Operations objective to "Ensure an operating environment within applicable regulatory, compliance and risk management frameworks". Tracked for institutional reporting, donor and partner assurance, and board oversight of corporate accountability.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator). Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate systems; there is no project instance to adapt it to.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Percentage of ESG indicators
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more of CIMMYT's ESG framework is both publicly reported and externally assured. The denominator is every indicator in the adopted framework, so the share falls when the framework expands faster than disclosure and verification follow.
disaggregationRequired: Disclosure status, on three values: disclosed and verified / disclosed only / not disclosed. One cut yields both companion shares (the share disclosed, and the share of disclosed indicators that are verified), and without it a low headline value cannot be read as a disclosure gap or a verification gap, which are different problems with different owners. Assurance level (limited / reasonable / other recognized verification) is also required for the verified group, since the headline treats the three alike.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: ESG pillar (environmental / social / governance); assurance provider. The template's "optional (project-specific)" field does not apply to an Institutional indicator; these are optional institutional cuts the owning function may add.
unitOfObservation: The ESG indicator (an entry on the framework's authoritative list).
calculationSummary: Numerator: number of ESG indicators in CIMMYT's adopted ESG framework whose values for the reporting year are (a) published in a publicly accessible CIMMYT channel and (b) covered by an independent third-party assurance or verification engagement against a recognized standard. Denominator: all ESG indicators in the adopted framework. Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): corporate records held by the owning function, namely the authoritative ESG framework indicator list, the published ESG/sustainability report and any other public disclosure channels, and the third-party assurance statements or verification certificates naming the indicators covered. Fallback DS2 (lower-resolution instance of the same code): where no consolidated ESG register exists, a compilation built indicator by indicator from publication locations and verifier correspondence; flag any value built this way as fallback-sourced, since denominator coverage and verification evidence are weaker. Not applicable DS1 (Censuses & surveys): disclosure and verification status are documentary facts, not survey responses. Not applicable DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation): not relevant to corporate reporting records. Not applicable DS4 (Secondary & international databases): the status of CIMMYT's own disclosures is not held by third-party databases. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): an indicator's status is established from official records only.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source. The indicator is compiled from existing DS2 corporate records, not collected with a DS1 or DS5 instrument.
collectionFrequency: Annually, compiled when the annual ESG/sustainability reporting cycle and its assurance engagement close.
referencePeriod: The CIMMYT reporting year: the value describes the disclosure and verification status of that year's ESG indicator values. An assurance statement is attributed to the year whose disclosures it covers, not the year it is signed, on the same basis as the report itself under KPI-O43. The cut-off is the publication date of the ESG/sustainability report for that year: assurance obtained after that date is attributed to the year it covers only if the value is restated, and otherwise it is not credited to any year's value.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual institutional share; the previous year's value is the reference for trend. Where a multi-year trend is wanted, the first year with a confirmed framework list and complete disclosure and assurance records serves as the reference year.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable; this Institutional indicator is drawn once from corporate systems, so there are no project instances to pool. A year compiled from the fallback source is noted alongside the figure rather than blended silently into a trend.

B: Combination method. Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level: a single percentage over the framework list, never averaged with anything.

C: Levels and operations. The share is computed once, at institutional level, over CIMMYT's adopted ESG indicator set, and is recomputed from its own numerator and denominator wherever a narrower view is wanted, never averaged from the views beneath it: a mean of unit shares weights a unit of three equally with one of three hundred. There is no level beneath the institution here, because an ESG indicator is one record in the denominator, not a reporting level. The denominator is a portfolio of records rather than a population measured in the field, so the measurement levels do not apply and every breakdown is a reporting view. Also report: the denominator itself, the number of indicators in the adopted set, the share carrying independent assurance, and any indicator whose publication channel changed in the year.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no (the default). The annual ESG/sustainability report (KPI-O43) feeds this outcome through the results chain not through arithmetic: publishing the report is one act of disclosure, while this share measures how much of the framework that act, plus verification, covers.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: each framework indicator is counted once, matched by its identifier on the authoritative list, regardless of how many channels publish it or how many engagements assure it. Overlap with other register indicators: the greenhouse gas inventory (KPI-O45) and GHG reduction outcome (KPI-OC45) measure emissions content; this indicator scores the inventory only as one framework entry's disclosure and verification status, so no value is counted twice.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion and exclusion: only indicators on the framework's authoritative list count in either term; disclosure to a single donor, an intranet, or an internal dashboard is not public disclosure; internal audit, self-assessment, or review by an affiliated body is not independent verification. Both limited and reasonable assurance count as independent verification, as do verifications against a recognized sector standard such as ISO 14064-3:2019 for the greenhouse gas component; the level obtained is reported for every verified indicator rather than used as a gate, because requiring reasonable assurance would score the assurance level almost all ESG engagements actually carry as no assurance at all. Partial assurance earns no credit: where an engagement covers only part of an indicator's reported value, that indicator counts as disclosed and not verified, and the partial coverage is reported.

Missing data: an indicator whose disclosure or verification status cannot be evidenced (no traceable published value, no assurance statement naming it) counts as not meeting the criteria and stays in the denominator, which is never reduced for missing evidence.

Repeated observations: each framework indicator counts once per reporting year, whatever the number of channels publish it or engagements assure it. If the framework list changes during the year, the list in force at year end is used and the change is noted alongside the value. Where the framework itself lists a component separately, as it does for each greenhouse gas scope, each component is its own framework entry and is scored on its own.
limitations: Measures transparency and assurance, not ESG performance: a 100% value means every framework indicator is published and externally verified, not that emissions, safeguards, or governance results are good. Performance sits in the underlying indicators themselves.

The value is only as meaningful as the denominator: a narrow framework list flatters the share, and adding or removing framework indicators shifts the value without any change in disclosure practice. Report the framework size alongside the percentage and note list changes.

Verification depth varies: limited assurance, reasonable assurance, and ISO 14064-3 verification make different-strength claims, and the binary disclosed-and-verified test treats them alike. The headline percentage hides how strong the assurance behind it is, which is why the assurance-level split is required rather than optional.

Scoring partial assurance as no credit is deliberately strict and will understate assurance effort in the early years, when an engagement may reach only part of a large indicator. The alternative, crediting partial coverage, would let a single assured line stand for a whole disclosure; the strict rule is the one that cannot be gamed, and the reported partial coverage is where the effort shows.

A rise means broader verified disclosure; it can reflect more indicators disclosed and assured or a reduced framework list, so check the companion shares and the framework size before reading it as improved accountability.
subMetrics: None. The two companion shares (percentage of framework indicators publicly disclosed, and percentage of disclosed indicators independently verified) are status disaggregations of the same framework list, not separately calculated sub-metrics. Reported alongside the headline value, they show whether a low value is a disclosure problem or a verification problem.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Institutional indicator; roles sit with CIMMYT's enabling units. Data collection: communications, which owns CIMMYT's adopted ESG indicator framework and its institutional corporate reporting, maintaining the authoritative framework list and the record of where each indicator's value was published; finance, which commissions and holds the third-party assurance engagements and their statements. Validation: communications and finance jointly, checking each framework entry's status against the published report and the named coverage of each assurance statement. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, per the Calculation method above. Approval: the Management Committee, which adopts the framework list that forms the denominator, with the value reported to the Board of Trustees. Reporting: communications to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 11 · Institutional performance & operations — Reference sheet KPI-OC40

name: Percentage of private-sector partnerships subject to conflict-of-interest (COI) review
resultsLevel: Outcome. The Core reads an Institutional-branch level from the indicator statement itself, because there is no external actor: a delivered framework is an Output (KPI-O47), while a percentage stating how widely a practice has been adopted across the organization is an Outcome, since what it reports is the organization operating differently, here whether the functions that form partnerships changed how they work. CGIAR's output/outcome boundary test (products under the research team's control versus behaviour change in external actors) is written for research results and fits an internal compliance indicator poorly.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Excellence in Operations.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. The indicator measures a property of CIMMYT as an organization, so the Institutional default applies: COI review protects the integrity of research that serves the Impact Areas, but the value reports internal control coverage, not a development result.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator measures an organization's conflict-of-interest review coverage; the closest SDG terrain (target 16.5 on corruption, target 16.6 on accountable institutions) tracks country-level outcomes, not an institution's internal control coverage.
otherFrameworks: GRI 2: General Disclosures 2021, disclosure 2-15 (Conflicts of interest): the standard under which an organization discloses its processes for preventing and mitigating conflicts of interest. ICMJE Recommendations, Disclosure of Interest: the journal-side regime for declaring competing interests in research publication. CGIAR Ethics Framework (CGIAR System Organization): the system-level ethics reference CIMMYT's conflict-of-interest framework aligns with. None of the three prescribes this percentage indicator, which is CIMMYT-defined.
definition: Measures the share of CIMMYT's private-sector partnerships active in the reporting year that carry a documented conflict-of-interest review. A conflict of interest arises when a private partner's commercial interest in research outcomes could improperly influence, or appear to influence, CIMMYT's research decisions, results, or public positions. The review is performed before a partnership is approved, on the basis of interest declarations and a risk classification, with the decision and any conditions documented; high-risk partnerships go to CIMMYT's conflict-of-interest committee and the remainder are cleared by a documented desk review in legal. Both tiers count as reviewed. The indicator is a compliance-control coverage measure: it reports how much of the private-sector portfolio passed through the control, not what the reviews found.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's control against private-sector conflicts of interest is applied across the partnership portfolio, rather than existing on paper (the compliance frameworks themselves are measured separately as KPI-O47). Conflicts of interest with commercial partners are a scientific-integrity and reputational risk, and a documented review process protects the credibility of CIMMYT's research. The indicator evidences the 2030 Strategy's Excellence in Operations commitment to "Ensure an operating environment within applicable regulatory, compliance and risk management frameworks" and feeds institutional, donor, and environmental, social and governance reporting.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator). Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate legal and ethics records; individual projects do not report this indicator.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Percentage of private-sector partnerships
directionOfChange: Reference value: 100 percent. The control is defined over the whole population it measures: every partnership entering the denominator is one the review rule covers, so the reference comes from the rule and not from a target set here. A value below 100 identifies partnerships approved without the documented review the rule requires, read as non-conformance and never as progress toward institutionalisation, because the denominator is not a roll-out schedule.
disaggregationRequired: Partner/institution type, per the register, and COI risk level. The risk-level split is required because the headline share does not say where the unreviewed remainder sits: two percentage points missing from the low-risk tier and two points missing from the high-risk tier are the same number and not the same problem.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Research area; region or country; agreement type. These are optional institutional cuts the owning function may add; the template's "optional (project-specific)" field does not apply to an Institutional indicator.
unitOfObservation: The private-sector partnership (the agreement record in the partnership register).
calculationSummary: Numerator: private-sector partnerships active in the reporting year with a documented, completed COI review on record (interest declarations on file and the review decision recorded), made at approval or at the latest material change, or, for a partnership approved before the conflict-of-interest framework took effect, at any time since. Denominator: all private-sector partnerships active at any point in the reporting year, per the register definition, not only those newly entering approval that year. A new-partnerships-only denominator would let a multi-year agreement pass through the control once and then sit outside the measure for the rest of its life, which is the opposite of what a coverage indicator is for. Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): the institutional partnership register plus the ethics/COI committee's records: interest-declaration forms, committee minutes and decisions, and partnership contracts, which is where prior fact-sheet practice locates the data. Fallback DS2 (lower-resolution instance of the same code): direct documentary review of partnership contracts and committee files where no central register covers the full portfolio for the year; a value built this way is flagged as fallback-sourced, because denominator completeness and verification evidence are weaker. Not applicable DS1: review status is an administrative fact read from records, not data collected from respondents. Not applicable DS3: satellite or GIS data cannot show whether a partnership was reviewed. Not applicable DS4: CIMMYT's internal partnership and committee records are not held by third parties. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced data cannot verify internal review records.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source. The operative tools are the interest-declaration form, the COI risk-classification screen by partner type and research type (which fixes review depth), and the committee's documented review-and-decision protocol (which fixes what a completed review means for the numerator).
collectionFrequency: Continuous administrative logging: reviews are performed and documented at partnership approval and on material change, consolidated by an annual portfolio review of the partnership register.
referencePeriod: The reporting year; the value is the portfolio's verified review-coverage status at annual consolidation.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual institutional coverage share whose design intent is sustained full coverage; the first year with a complete partnership register and consolidated committee records serves as the reference year, and change is read from the annual series.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable in the template's sense; the indicator is compiled once from corporate records, so there are no project-level indicator instances to pool. Any portion assessed through fallback file review is noted alongside the figure, not blended silently.

B: Combination method. Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level: one numerator and one denominator counted across the whole private-sector partnership portfolio, then the ratio is formed. Never average percentages computed per region, partner type, or risk tier; disaggregated views are computed from their own counts.

C: Levels and operations. The share is computed once, at institutional level, over all private-sector partnerships in scope for the year, and is recomputed from its own numerator and denominator wherever a narrower view is wanted, never averaged from the views beneath it: a mean of unit shares weights a unit of three equally with one of three hundred. There is no level beneath the institution here, because a partnership is one record in the denominator, not a reporting level. The denominator is a portfolio of records rather than a population measured in the field, so the measurement levels do not apply and every breakdown is a reporting view. Also report: the denominator itself, the number of partnerships in scope, the number excluded under Eligibility.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no (the default). The upstream output KPI-O47 (compliance and safeguards frameworks established) and this coverage outcome connect as a narrative, control built then control applied, never arithmetically.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: each partnership agreement counts once, matched on its unique agreement identifier; a partner holding several distinct agreements contributes one count per agreement, and a single agreement spanning several projects or countries still counts once. One named boundary: KPI-OC42 (safeguards coverage, unit: field project) and KPI-OC46 (informed consent, unit: research activity) are neighbouring compliance-coverage outcomes on different units; the three are reported side by side and never summed.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion and exclusion: includes formal agreements with private-sector entities recorded in the institutional partnership register (or, for a year the register does not cover in full, identified by the documentary review of contracts and committee files that Data source names as the Fallback) that give the partner a role in, or a claim over, research outcomes: research collaboration, co-development, licensing, and material transfer to a commercial party. Excludes partnerships with public, academic and civil-society partners, and excludes supplier and procurement contracts, which are purchasing relationships rather than partnerships and whose sustainability dimension is measured by KPI-OC44. The denominator is the full private-sector portfolio, not a risk-scoped subset: risk tiering sets how deep a review goes, never whether a partnership is in scope. Legal holds the authoritative partnership register, sets the risk thresholds and maintains them, with the threshold definitions approved by the Management Committee.
limitations: Review is not absence of conflict: the indicator verifies that a review took place and was documented, not that conflicts were correctly identified, well managed, or eliminated. The quality and independence of the review need audit evidence this indicator does not carry.

The denominator is only as good as the partnership register: private-sector engagements formalised outside the register escape the count entirely. The conservative rule (an unregistered review counts as no review) protects against inflation but makes the value sensitive to registration and filing backlogs.

Comparability over time depends on holding the scope and the risk thresholds still: changing which agreement types count as a private-sector partnership, or moving the boundary between the committee tier and the desk-review tier, shifts the value without any change in actual practice. Note any such change alongside the series and restate the prior year.

The expected value is at or near 100 percent once the control is established, so the series carries little information most years; the meaningful signal is a dip, which flags a governance gap to investigate. A high value does not mean research integrity improved; read it with KPI-O47 and internal audit findings for the accountability picture.
subMetrics: None. Coverage rates by risk level or partner type are disaggregations of the same measure, not separately calculated metrics. Related indicators with their own sheets: KPI-O47 (compliance and safeguards frameworks established and operationalised, the output feeding this outcome), KPI-OC42 (field projects with documented safeguards), and KPI-OC46 (research activities with informed consent), the neighbouring compliance-coverage outcomes.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Institutional indicator; roles sit with CIMMYT's enabling units. Data collection: legal, which holds the institutional partnership register and files the interest declarations, contracts and review decisions as partnerships are formed. Validation: legal together with CIMMYT's conflict-of-interest committee, which reviews the high-risk tier and confirms that every partnership in the year carries a completed review record at its assigned tier. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, forming the annual numerator, denominator and ratio per the Calculation method. Approval: the Executive Office. Reporting: legal to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 11 · Institutional performance & operations — Reference sheet KPI-OC43

name: Percentage of procurement from certified sustainable suppliers
resultsLevel: Outcome. The Core reads an Institutional-branch level from the indicator statement itself, because there is no external actor: a delivered system or count is an Output, while a percentage stating how widely a practice has been adopted across the organization is an Outcome, since what it reports is the organization operating differently, here whether buying behaviour across the whole organization changed. CGIAR's output/outcome boundary test (products under the research team's control versus behaviour change in external actors) is written for research results and fits an internal operations indicator poorly.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Excellence in Operations.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. The indicator measures a property of CIMMYT as an organization, so the Institutional default applies: sustainable purchasing serves environmental and social ends, but the value reports a procurement practice share, not an environmental or social result.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest SDG indicator, 12.7.1, counts countries implementing sustainable public procurement policies and action plans; it is a national policy measure, not an organizational procurement share, so no direct correspondence exists.
otherFrameworks: GRI 308: Supplier Environmental Assessment 2016 and GRI 414: Supplier Social Assessment 2016, Global Reporting Initiative: the standard disclosures for supplier sustainability screening; their headline disclosures count new suppliers screened, whereas this indicator measures a value share, so the correspondence is thematic, not one-to-one. Supply Chain Sustainability: A Practical Guide for Continuous Improvement, Second Edition, UN Global Compact and BSR: the practice guide for embedding sustainability in procurement. SDG target 12.7 (promote sustainable procurement practices): the indicator supports this target directionally without mapping to its official indicator. None of these frameworks prescribes this percentage; the indicator is CIMMYT-defined.
definition: Measures the share of CIMMYT's total procurement, by value, sourced from certified sustainable suppliers during the reporting year. A certified sustainable supplier is a supplier holding a valid certification under a sustainability standard CIMMYT recognizes. The recognized list covers six scheme families: environmental management system certification, Fairtrade, Forest Stewardship Council (FSC), Rainforest Alliance, organic certification, and social or labour standards certification. The definition is CIMMYT's own; no external framework prescribes this indicator. The list is maintained by finance and procurement, reviewed once a year before the reporting cycle closes, and it travels with the value: any addition or removal applies to the next reporting year, with the prior year restated on the new list so the series stays readable.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's purchasing practice matches the standards it asks of its own science: a responsible supply chain is part of the institution's environmental and social footprint. The 2030 Strategy names procurement among the enabling units and commits them to the Excellence in Operations objective that "Enabling units enhance the sustainability, results, and impact of CIMMYT's scientific research"; this indicator evidences that commitment in the one corporate function that buys on the institution's behalf, and feeds institutional and environmental, social and governance reporting.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator). Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate procurement records; there is no project instance to adapt.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Percentage of total procurement value
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of procurement value comes from certified sustainable suppliers.
disaggregationRequired: Procurement category and certification type. Category is required because certification availability is uneven across what CIMMYT buys, so the headline share cannot say whether a low value reflects reluctance or an unavailable market. Certification type is required because the value moves with the recognized list, and a share whose composition is invisible cannot be checked against a list revision.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Supplier region or country; a supplier-count view (share of suppliers certified) alongside the value share. The template's "optional (project-specific)" field does not apply to an Institutional indicator; these are optional institutional cuts finance and procurement may add. Within the required category cut, the three highest-impact categories to watch are agrochemicals, field equipment and laboratory supplies.
unitOfObservation: The procurement commitment (the purchase order in the procurement system), with certification status read from the supplier record.
calculationSummary: Numerator: total committed value of procurement in the reporting year with suppliers holding a valid recognized sustainability certification on the commitment date. Denominator: total committed value of all procurement in the same year. Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100. Value is measured on a committed basis, dated by purchase order, not on a paid or invoiced basis. The indicator is about the sourcing decision, and the purchase order is when that decision is made; an invoice basis would attribute a choice to whichever year the money happened to move. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): CIMMYT's procurement records in the enterprise resource planning system (transaction values by supplier) joined to the supplier register carrying each supplier's certification classification and certificates on file. Fallback DS2 (lower-resolution instance of the same code): direct documentary review of contracts and supplier certificates where the supplier register does not yet classify certification status for the full supplier base; a value built this way is flagged as fallback-sourced, because classification coverage is weaker. Not applicable DS1: procurement value and certification status are administrative facts read from records, not data collected from respondents. Not applicable DS3: satellite or GIS data cannot show who CIMMYT buys from. Not applicable DS4: the value cannot be compiled from third-party databases, although certifiers' public registries support validation of individual certificates. Not applicable DS5: crowdsourced data cannot verify procurement records.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source. The operative tools are the supplier pre-qualification process, which captures sustainability certifications at onboarding, and the supplier register's certification classification, which fixes who counts in the numerator.
collectionFrequency: Continuous administrative logging in the procurement system as transactions are processed, with the supplier register's certification classification updated at least annually and at supplier onboarding.
referencePeriod: The reporting year, which is the calendar year, register-wide; the value describes the procurement CIMMYT committed to within it.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual institutional share; the first year in which the supplier register carries a certification classification serves as the reference year, and change is read from the annual series. Reporting starts from that first classified year rather than waiting on a sustainable procurement policy: the baseline is what tells CIMMYT where a target should sit, and a policy written without one sets its target blind.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable in the template's sense; the indicator is compiled once from corporate records, so there are no project-level indicator instances to pool. Any portion of the supplier base classified through fallback file review rather than the register is noted alongside the figure, not blended silently.

B: Combination method. Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level: one numerator and one denominator summed across all offices, country operations, and procurement categories, then the ratio is formed. Never average percentages computed per office or category; disaggregated views are computed from their own value totals.

C: Levels and operations. The share is computed once, at institutional level, over the total value of procurement in the reporting year, and is recomputed from its own numerator and denominator wherever a narrower view is wanted, never averaged from the views beneath it: a mean of unit shares weights a unit of three equally with one of three hundred. There is no level beneath the institution here, because a transaction is one record in the denominator, not a reporting level. The denominator is a portfolio of records rather than a population measured in the field, so the measurement levels do not apply and every breakdown is a reporting view. This share is weighted by value, not by transaction count, so it is recomputed from summed values and never from a count of certified suppliers: one large contract and one small one are not two equal units. Also report: the denominator itself, the total procurement value the share rests on, the share of spend with suppliers whose certification could not be verified, and the certification schemes recognised, since the share moves with the list.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no (the default). This purchasing-practice outcome connects to the wider Excellence in Operations narrative (systems built, practice shifted) as a narrative, never arithmetically.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: each commitment counts once, matched on its unique purchase order identifier; a supplier serving several offices or categories creates no double count because values, not suppliers, are summed. No other register indicator counts procurement value, so cross-indicator double-counting risk is low; the institutional greenhouse gas footprint indicator covers purchased goods within its scope 3 boundary, but the two report different units (tCO2e versus percentage of value) and are never summed.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion and exclusion: includes purchases of goods and services processed through CIMMYT's procurement system, individual consultancy contracts included, since a consultancy is a service CIMMYT buys and sourcing it is a purchasing choice. Excludes sub-grants to partner institutions, which pass research funding on under a grant agreement rather than buying anything, and inter-CGIAR transactions, which are internal to the system and would be counted a second time by the receiving center. Certification is evidenced by a valid certificate on file in the supplier register or, under the Fallback in Data source, among the contracts and supplier certificates reviewed, verified against the certifier where possible, never self-declared.
limitations: Certification is a proxy for supplier practice, not proof of it: schemes differ widely in scope (environmental, social, product-level) and rigour, and holding a certificate says nothing about the footprint of the specific goods bought. The value share measures where money went, not the impact it caused.

The value depends entirely on the qualifying-certification list: broadening or narrowing what CIMMYT recognizes shifts the value with no change in purchasing behaviour. Keep the list stable across years and note any revision alongside the reported series.

Certification availability is uneven across categories and regions: small local suppliers, particularly in the Global South, often lack access to certification schemes, so pushing the share up can conflict with local-sourcing and supplier-development goals. Read the value with the category and region cuts, not alone.

The denominator boundary moves the value materially, which is why it is fixed here rather than left to each reporting cycle: consultancies in, sub-grants and inter-CGIAR transactions out, on a committed basis. Any later change to that boundary requires the prior year to be restated, or the series breaks without appearing to.
A rising share means spending shifted toward certified suppliers; it does not mean CIMMYT's supply-chain impacts fell, and a flat share may hide real improvement inside uncertified suppliers.
subMetrics: None. The value share and the supplier-count share are alternative views of the same measure, not separately calculated metrics; the indicator is defined on value, and any supplier-count view is reported as a complementary disaggregation. Certification-type shares are disaggregations, not sub-metrics.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
The indicator's definition and calculation rest on CIMMYT's own authority; the standards above frame supplier sustainability assessment but do not prescribe this measure.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Institutional indicator; roles sit with finance and procurement, the enabling unit the 2030 Strategy names. Data collection: procurement, maintaining the supplier register, the certification classification field in the enterprise resource planning system, and the certificates on file, populated at supplier onboarding and refreshed annually. Validation: procurement with finance, verifying certificates against the certifiers' own registries and checking that the purchase-order population for the year is complete. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, forming the annual numerator, denominator and ratio per the Calculation method. Approval: head of finance and procurement. Reporting: procurement to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.

name: Percentage reduction in CIMMYT's institutional greenhouse gas emissions (Scopes 1 to 3) relative to the base year
resultsLevel: Outcome. The Core reads an Institutional-branch level from the indicator statement itself: a measured deliverable (the annual inventory, KPI-O45) is an Output, while a change versus baseline expressing institution-wide performance is an Outcome. CGIAR's formal output/outcome test (control by the research team versus behaviour change in external actors) is written for research results and fits institutional indicators imperfectly, since there is no external actor here; the level rests on the deliverable-versus-change logic.
primaryObjective: Excellence in Operations (institutional enabler component). As an Institutional indicator it does not map to a mission Primary Objective (PO1 to PO5); institutional indicators map to one of the five enabler components of the 2030 Strategy, and the register rolls this indicator up to Excellence in Operations.
cgiarImpactArea: Climate Adaptation & Mitigation. Institutional indicators default to Not applicable, but the institutional GHG footprint is the recognised exception: reducing CIMMYT's own emissions is a direct, if modest, contribution to the Climate Adaptation & Mitigation Impact Area, and the indicator evidences that the institution manages what it asks others to manage.
sdgTarget: None. SDG indicator 13.2.2 (total greenhouse gas emissions per year) concerns national inventories compiled under the UNFCCC, not organizational footprints; a corporate reduction-versus-base-year figure has no direct SDG indicator correspondence, so None is recorded rather than a stretched mapping.
otherFrameworks: Reduction against a fixed base year is the form required by the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard for tracking emissions performance over time, and it is the form in which corporate climate targets and disclosures (for example CDP climate disclosure and science-based target setting) are expressed. No donor results framework carries this indicator; it enters donor reporting through institutional sustainability and ESG channels.
definition: Measures the percentage by which CIMMYT's institutional greenhouse gas emissions, in tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) across Scopes 1, 2 and 3, have fallen relative to a fixed base year. The numerator is the reduction in tCO2e versus the base year; the denominator is base-year tCO2e, both taken from the annual institutional inventory (KPI-O45). It is the institutional decarbonisation trend: where the inventory reports what CIMMYT's operation emitted in a year, this indicator reports whether that footprint is shrinking, and by how much, against a fixed starting point.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT is decarbonising its own operation, not merely measuring it: the level (KPI-O45) shows the footprint, this indicator shows the direction and pace of change. A reduction against a fixed base year is the standard form in which organizations state and track climate commitments, so this is the figure donor, ESG and institutional sustainability reporting will ask for, and the credibility test behind any public climate positioning by a center whose mission includes climate adaptation and mitigation.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional scope). This indicator measures a property of CIMMYT as an organization, reported once at Center level; no project instantiates it, so there is no project-specific layer.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Percentage (%) reduction in tCO2e relative to the base year. A positive value means emissions fell below the base year; a negative value means they rose above it, and is reported as such, not suppressed.
directionOfChange: Increase, the quantity itself being a reduction. A rising value means gross emissions in the reporting year stand lower against the base year, further below it or less far above it, both measured on one organizational boundary and one Scope 3 category coverage.
disaggregationRequired: Required: by scope (Scope 1, Scope 2, Scope 3), each scope's reduction computed against its own base-year value, because the three scopes have different drivers (fleet and facilities, purchased energy, travel and procurement) and different levers, and a headline reduction can hide a rising scope. Recommended: by site or country of operation, for internal management.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional scope; no project layer).
unitOfObservation: Organization (CIMMYT at Center-institutional level).
calculationSummary: Value = ((base-year tCO2e - reporting-year tCO2e) / base-year tCO2e) x 100. Numerator: base-year emissions minus reporting-year emissions, in tCO2e, gross of any offsets, credits or removals. Denominator: base-year emissions in tCO2e. Both terms are the total Scope 1 + 2 + 3 values from the institutional inventory (KPI-O45), and both must be computed under the same organizational boundary, the same consolidation approach and the same Scope 3 category coverage; if coverage differs, the base year is recalculated to the current coverage before the percentage is computed, per the GHG Protocol base-year recalculation requirement. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): both terms of the calculation come from CIMMYT's institutional GHG inventory, which is compiled from corporate records (fuel and fleet records, energy invoices, travel bookings, procurement and finance records) as specified in the KPI-O45 reference sheet; this indicator is derived entirely from those inventory values. Fallback DS4 (Secondary & international databases): applies only upstream, where the inventory itself falls back on spend-based estimation with published emission factors for categories lacking activity data; a reduction value computed from an inventory carrying that flag inherits it, with the spend-based categories named for both years, since a factor-set update can move a spend-based figure with no operational change. Not applicable: DS1 (Censuses & surveys), DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation), DS5 (Citizen-generated data): an organizational emissions trend is computed from the corporate inventory and cannot be measured by surveys, satellite observation or crowdsourced data.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, secondary source. The indicator is calculated from the institutional inventory; no primary-collection instrument is involved.
collectionFrequency: Annual, following the compilation of the institutional inventory (KPI-O45) for the reporting year. No separate data collection takes place for this indicator.
reportingFrequency: Annual, into institutional sustainability and ESG reporting, alongside the absolute inventory value.
referencePeriod: The reporting year, compared against the fixed base year. Each reported value describes cumulative change since the base year; the change against the previous year is reported alongside it and is not the indicator.
baselineRequired: Yes, definitionally: the base year is the denominator, so without a documented base year and inventory the indicator cannot be computed at all. No default base year may be adopted in place of a formal designation. The base year and its recalculation policy are a formal designation by CIMMYT under the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard, and until that designation is made no reduction is computed. The earliest complete inventory year (all three scopes, documented boundary) is the year to put forward for designation. If no complete prior-year inventory exists, the level (KPI-O45) can be monitored but no reduction can be reported, and no decarbonisation claim can be made.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: Not applicable; the value is computed once at Center level and there are no project instances to pool. If CGIAR compares or combines decarbonisation performance across centers, percentage reductions must never be averaged across centers: a system-level figure is recomputed from CGIAR inventories consolidated under KPI-O45's rule, with consistent base years, because averaging percentages weights a small center's footprint equally with a large one's.

B: Combination method. A ratio of two totals from KPI-O45, formed once: (base-year tCO2e minus reporting-year tCO2e) over base-year tCO2e. Percentages are never averaged, across centers or across years.

C: Levels and operations. The value is computed once, at institutional level, from KPI-O45's base-year and reporting-year totals, both built under the same organizational boundary, the same consolidation approach and the same Scope 3 category coverage. Where coverage has changed, the base year is recalculated to the current coverage before the percentage is computed, and the recalculation is reported: a reduction produced by measuring less of the inventory is not a reduction in emissions. There is no level beneath the institution, and percentages are never averaged across centers or across years: a system figure is recomputed from CGIAR inventories consolidated under KPI-O45's rule, because averaging shares weights a small center's footprint equally with a large one's. A negative value, meaning emissions rose, is reported as such and never suppressed. Also report: the base year and whether it was recalculated, the boundary and coverage of both terms, the absolute tCO2e behind the share, and the change against the previous year, computed as ((previous-year tCO2e - reporting-year tCO2e) / previous-year tCO2e) x 100 with both years complete for every scope, on one boundary and on one Scope 3 category coverage.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: No. This outcome is not added to its output counterpart; it is arithmetically derived from KPI-O45's base-year and reporting-year values, and the two connect through that derivation and the results narrative, never through addition.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: a percentage is not additive, which removes most double-counting risk; the residual risks are inherited from the inventory (Scope 3 overlaps with partners' Scope 1 and 2, so CIMMYT's trend must never be combined with partner or supplier trends) and boundary confusion with the mission branch: this indicator must never be combined with field-level emissions indicators such as GHG emission intensity of production systems (KPI-I09), which measure the farming systems CIMMYT's research targets under a different boundary, not CIMMYT's own operation.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Repeated observations: not applicable in the survey sense; one value is computed per reporting year against the fixed base year, and a base-year recalculation (triggered by a structural change, a change in calculation methodology, an improvement in the accuracy of emission factors or activity data, or the discovery of significant errors, each judged against the disclosed significance threshold, and never by a factor update that reflects a change of emissions to the atmosphere) is documented and applied retrospectively so the trend stays comparable, rather than being absorbed into the series.
limitations: Supports an institutional performance reading, not a climate-impact claim: this measures the emissions of CIMMYT's own operation, and is not a measure of the emissions outcomes of CIMMYT's research, which the mission branch measures under a different boundary.

The value is highly sensitive to the base-year choice and to boundary consistency: an unusually high base year flatters every later value, and expanding Scope 3 coverage without recalculating the base year shows a spurious emissions rise. A change in calculation methodology or an improvement in the accuracy of emission factors or activity data requires a documented base-year recalculation before the trend is interpreted, judged against the disclosed significance threshold. A factor update that reflects a change of emissions to the atmosphere does not, because recalculating for it would remove from the trend the decarbonisation this indicator exists to report.

Reduction can reflect contraction rather than decarbonisation: a smaller budget, fewer staff or less fieldwork lowers emissions with no management action, while institutional growth can mask real efficiency gains. Read alongside organizational scale, and where needed an intensity view (for example tCO2e per unit of budget), before crediting climate management.

Scope 3 is estimated rather than metered for most categories, and spend-based estimation is materially less precise than metered activity data. This value is a difference between two inventories, so that imprecision enters twice, once in the base year and once in the reporting year. The required per-scope reductions show which component the headline movement came from; where it came from Scope 3, a few percentage points are within estimation noise and should not be read as decarbonisation in either direction, and the per-scope figures are read before the headline is interpreted.

A positive value means gross measured emissions fell below the base year under a consistent boundary; it does not mean CIMMYT is carbon neutral or on a science-based trajectory, and because offsets are excluded, no offsetting activity changes this value.
subMetrics: None. Both terms of the calculation are values of KPI-O45 (absolute institutional GHG emissions), which carries its own reference sheet; the per-scope reductions are disaggregations of this indicator, not separately defined sub-metrics.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Institutional indicator; roles follow the inventory's corporate ownership, since this indicator is derived from it. Data collection: none of its own; activity data are collected into the KPI-O45 inventory by finance and procurement, with human resources and knowledge management and IT supplying their own activity data. Validation: finance and procurement as the inventory owner, including verification that base-year and reporting-year values share one boundary. Calculation: the inventory owner, applying the formula and recalculation rule above. Approval: the Director General, as owner of CIMMYT's institutional sustainability reporting, with the value reported to the Board of Trustees. Reporting: CIMMYT MEAL unit into institutional Excellence in Operations reporting.

name: Percentage of internal and external audit recommendations implemented within the agreed timeline
resultsLevel: Outcome. Note: CGIAR's output/outcome boundary test (a change in the behaviour of external actors that the research team cannot directly control) is written for research results and fits an internal operations indicator poorly, since there is no external actor. Read from the indicator statement, as the Core requires for an Institutional-branch indicator, audit reports issued are the delivered result (the output, KPI-O48), while the share of recommendations implemented on time reports management units across CIMMYT changing their practices, which is the organization operating differently and therefore an outcome.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Excellence in Operations.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. The indicator measures a property of CIMMYT as an organization (how promptly it acts on audit findings), an internal enabler rather than a result delivered to an external population, so the Institutional default applies.
sdgTarget: None. SDG target 16.6 (develop effective, accountable and transparent institutions at all levels) is thematically adjacent, but no official SDG indicator measures an individual organization's audit-recommendation follow-up rate, so no direct correspondence exists.
otherFrameworks: Global Internal Audit Standards (The Institute of Internal Auditors, 2024, effective January 2025), which require the internal audit function to monitor and confirm the implementation of recommendations or management action plans. International Standards on Auditing (IAASB/IFAC), under which external auditors communicate findings and follow up on prior-period matters. Both frameworks require follow-up on recommendations; neither prescribes this percentage itself.
definition: Measures the share of audit recommendations, from both internal and external audits, that CIMMYT implemented within the timeline agreed between the auditors and management. The numerator is audit recommendations implemented on time; the denominator is all audit recommendations falling due in the reporting year, drawn from the recommendations generated by the audit engagements counted under the companion output indicator KPI-O48. It is an accountability and continuous-improvement measure: it shows whether the findings of independent review change how CIMMYT operates, and how promptly.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT acts on the findings of its own assurance system, closing the loop that starts with the audits counted under KPI-O48: conducting audits demonstrates oversight, while implementing their recommendations on time demonstrates accountability and continuous improvement. This is the operational evidence behind the 2030 Strategy's Excellence in Operations commitments to "Ensure an operating environment within applicable regulatory, compliance and risk management frameworks" and to "Ensure clarity in processes to enable better decision making and greater accountability". Tracked for institutional reporting, board and audit-committee oversight, and donor assurance, where the follow-up rate on audit recommendations is a standard due-diligence question.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator). Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate systems; there is no project instance to adapt it to.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Percentage of audit recommendations (implemented on time as a share of all recommendations due in the reporting year).
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of the audit recommendations due in the year were implemented by their due date.
disaggregationRequired: Audit type: internal / external, mirroring the split carried by KPI-O48; the two streams have different owners and different assurance meanings. Recommendation priority or risk rating (e.g. high / medium / low, as assigned by the auditors), because timely closure of high-priority recommendations is the signal oversight bodies act on.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Responsible unit or function (which part of CIMMYT owns the corrective action); age band of overdue recommendations (e.g. under 6 months, 6 to 12 months, over 12 months past due); year of the originating audit. The template's "optional (project-specific)" field does not apply to an Institutional indicator; these are optional institutional cuts the owning function may add.
unitOfObservation: The individual audit recommendation (the registered recommendation record).
calculationSummary: Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100, computed once per reporting year from the recommendations-tracking register. Numerator: audit recommendations whose implementation was completed on or before their assessment date, the completion date being the one recorded in the register with its supporting evidence accepted at closure verification. Denominator: all audit recommendations whose agreed or default due date falls within the reporting year, from both internal and external audits. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): a consolidated audit-recommendations tracking register maintained by the owning corporate function, recording for each recommendation an identifier, the source engagement (linking to the KPI-O48 audit register), audit type, priority rating, agreed management action and owner, agreed due date, implementation and closure date, and the evidence accepted at closure. Fallback DS2 (lower-resolution instance of the same code): per-report follow-up matrices or separate manual logs held by the internal audit function and Finance where no consolidated register covers the full year; a value built from these must be flagged as fallback-sourced, because de-duplication across logs and evidence of closure dates are weaker. Not applicable DS1 (Censuses & surveys): implementation status is an administrative fact evidenced in records, not a respondent-reported condition. Not applicable DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation): not relevant to audit records. Not applicable DS4 (Secondary & international databases): CIMMYT's recommendation follow-up is not held by third parties. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): a recommendation enters this indicator only through the formal audit and follow-up process.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source. The indicator is compiled from existing DS2 register records, not collected with a DS1 or DS5 instrument.
collectionFrequency: Continuous administrative logging: recommendations, agreed actions, due dates, and closure evidence are recorded in the recommendations-tracking register as events occur, with periodic follow-up verification by the owning function.
referencePeriod: The CIMMYT reporting year: the value describes the cohort of recommendations that fell due within that year, whatever year their originating audit took place.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual institutional accountability ratio; prior-year values are the reference for interpretation, and the first year with a complete consolidated recommendations register serves as the reference year for any multi-year trend.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable; this Institutional indicator is drawn once from corporate systems, so there are no project instances to pool. Recommendations from donor-commissioned project audits are counted once each in the corporate register. Any period built from fallback manual logs is noted alongside the figure rather than blended silently.

B: Combination method. Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level: the percentage is computed from the pooled numerator and pooled denominator across all units, duty stations, and audit types after de-duplication by recommendation identifier; percentages are never averaged across units or audit types.

C: Levels and operations. The share is computed once, at institutional level, over all audit recommendations due in the reporting year, and is recomputed from its own numerator and denominator wherever a narrower view is wanted, never averaged from the views beneath it: a mean of unit shares weights a unit of three equally with one of three hundred. There is no level beneath the institution here, because a recommendation is one record in the denominator, not a reporting level. The denominator is a portfolio of records rather than a population measured in the field, so the measurement levels do not apply and every breakdown is a reporting view. Also report: the denominator itself, the number of recommendations due, the share implemented late against on time, and the number still open past their assessment date, since a rising share with a growing overdue tail is not improvement.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no arithmetic aggregation (the default: each level measures something different). The link to KPI-O48 is data lineage, not addition: the audit reports counted there generate the recommendations whose timely implementation this indicator measures, so the two connect through the results chain as a narrative, never as a sum, and this indicator's denominator must reconcile to the reports issued under KPI-O48.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: a recommendation appearing in more than one log (for example a donor-audit recommendation tracked by both Finance and the audited program) is counted once, matched on the recommendation identifier; where one report finding carries several sub-actions, the register's recommendation-level entry is the counting unit, not each sub-action. No overlap with another register indicator: KPI-O48 counts engagements and reports (different objects), and the nearest indicator group neighbours KPI-O46 (grievance cases) and KPI-O47 (compliance and safeguards frameworks) count different objects again.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion and exclusion: includes every recommendation issued in a final audit report, or in a management letter belonging to an engagement, counted under KPI-O48, whether or not a management action or a due date has been agreed for it; excludes recommendations that management formally declined with a documented risk-acceptance sign-off, and recommendations withdrawn or superseded by the auditors, since neither can fall "due". A decline, withdrawal or supersession recorded after a recommendation's assessment date does not remove it from that year's denominator. Rule for rescheduled deadlines: a recommendation is assessed against its original agreed due date. An extension formally approved, with documented justification, before the original date falls due resets the assessment date; an extension approved after that date has passed does not, because approving an extension for a deadline already missed is retrospective reclassification of exactly the event the indicator exists to detect. This is the rule KPI-OC50 applies to improvement actions, and the two are the same mechanism with different sources. The number of recommendations granted an extension is reported alongside the value, since a rate held up by extensions is not the same achievement as one held up by delivery. Excluded recommendations are reported too: a share raised by declining recommendations is not a share earned.

Missing data: an item with no agreed deadline is not excluded. It takes a default due date of twelve months from the date of the audit report or management letter that raised it, enters the denominator in the year that default date falls, and cannot enter the numerator unless its implementation was completed on or before that date. Excluding it would reward never setting a deadline, which is the most common way an action quietly never happens. The number of items carrying a default due date is reported alongside the value, because a default is a symptom rather than a deadline.

Repeated observations: each recommendation enters the denominator exactly once, in the year its assessment date falls: the original or default due date, or the revised date where an extension has reset it under the rule above; a recommendation closed late does not re-enter the calculation in a later year, and a finding repeated by a subsequent audit is registered as a new recommendation with its own due date.
limitations: Timeliness of documented closure only, not depth of change: a recommendation can be closed on time with a minimal fix that leaves the underlying risk in place, so the indicator is only as strong as the evidence standard applied at closure verification.

Recommendations are heterogeneous: a minor process note and a critical control failure each count as one, so an aggregate rate weights very different risks equally; the priority disaggregation mitigates but does not remove this.

The measure is sensitive to how deadlines are set and renegotiated: lenient initial timelines or routinely extended due dates inflate the rate without any change in responsiveness. The calculation fixes assessment to the original due date and admits only extensions approved before it lapsed, and the extension and exclusion counts are reported beside the value so that a rate propped up either way is visible.

The denominator is shaped by the audit cycle, not by management performance: a year with few audits or few maturing recommendations yields a small denominator and a volatile percentage, so read the value together with the KPI-O48 volumes and the absolute counts behind the ratio.

A rise means a larger share of due recommendations was closed on time in that year's cohort; it does not by itself mean the control environment improved, and a fall driven by one large audit with many recommendations may reflect assurance coverage widening rather than accountability weakening.
subMetrics: None. The internal/external and priority splits are disaggregations of the same ratio, not separately calculated sub-metrics. The volume of audits generating the recommendations is a separate indicator with its own sheet, KPI-O48.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Institutional indicator; roles sit with the same functions that own the audit register behind KPI-O48, since the recommendations come out of those engagements. Data collection: internal audit, which owns the consolidated recommendations-tracking register and records follow-up on its own engagements; finance feeds follow-up on external and donor-commissioned audit recommendations into the same register. Validation: internal audit, verifying closure evidence against the agreed action and de-duplicating across the internal and external entries. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, per the Calculation method above. Approval: head of internal audit, with the annual value reported to the audit committee of the Board of Trustees, which is the body the follow-up rate is reported for. Reporting: internal audit to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
