name: Percentage of CIMMYT staff or programmes operating on unified data/ICT platforms
resultsLevel: Outcome. CGIAR's boundary test (an output is a product delivered under the control of the responsible team; an outcome is a change in the behaviour of actors the team cannot directly control) is written for research results and fits internal operations indicators imperfectly, since there is no external actor. Read from the indicator statement, as the Core requires for an Institutional-branch indicator, a delivered platform is the output (KPI-O49), and the share of staff and programmes operating on unified platforms states how widely that system has been made operational across the organization, which is the organization operating differently, so Outcome stands.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Excellence in Operations.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. The indicator measures a property of CIMMYT's own operational infrastructure, an internal enabler rather than a result delivered to an external population; an integrated digital backbone serves every Impact Area indirectly, which is not a direct link.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator measures an organization's internal digital integration; SDG targets on information and communications technology (for example 9.c and 17.8) concern population-level access and use, so they are thematically adjacent only.
otherFrameworks: None. No donor or reporting framework prescribes a share of staff or programmes on unified platforms; the indicator is defined on CIMMYT's own authority.
definition: Measures the share of CIMMYT staff, or of CIMMYT programmes, that operate on the organization's unified data and information and communications technology (ICT) platforms. A unified platform is a corporate system designated by CIMMYT as the shared institutional platform for a given function, intended to replace fragmented local alternatives. The designated set is one platform per covered corporate function: enterprise resource planning, document and data management, project management, and collaboration. Knowledge management and IT maintains the list, versions and dates each revision, and has each version approved by the Management Committee, so that a share is always readable against the list it was measured on. The list covers corporate functions only; research-data platforms are outside it, and how well research data is governed is measured separately by Vol. 2 · KPI-O44 and Vol. 2 · KPI-OC41. Platforms provided to CIMMYT through One CGIAR global services are eligible for the designated list on the same terms as CIMMYT-run ones, flagged as CGIAR-provided, consistent with the treatment of the same platforms under KPI-O49. The indicator is a digital-integration measure: it tracks how far the organization has converged on its designated shared platforms, not how many platforms exist.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's people and programmes are converging on the shared corporate platforms its 2030 Strategy commits to under Excellence in Operations, whose first objective is "Effective systems and tools are developed and maintained", including the commitment to "Implement an ICT infrastructure to support CIMMYT's digital transformation and capacity to exploit big data for R4D". It is the adoption counterpart to the delivery count KPI-O49 (number of enterprise systems or digital tools developed, deployed, or upgraded): KPI-O49 shows what the ICT function put into operation, this indicator shows whether the organization works on it. Serves institutional management and reporting on the digital-transformation agenda.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator). Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate ICT records; there is no project instance to adapt it to.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Percentage of staff, or percentage of programmes. Both bases are reported, separately, and the staff basis is the headline, because its denominator is unambiguous while programmes differ so widely in size that a programme share weights a four-person programme against a four-hundred-person one. The two are never merged, and each reported value states the basis it was computed on.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of staff, or of programmes, uses at least one designated platform; how far each covered function has converged is read from that platform's own share.
disaggregationRequired: Unit or function, on the staff basis; and designated platform, each platform's share computed on the same denominator. Convergence is uneven by construction: a pooled share cannot say which part of CIMMYT still works outside the designated platforms, and because use of any one platform enters the headline, only the per-platform shares show which covered functions have converged.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Duty-station type; programme type; provider (CIMMYT-run versus One CGIAR global service). Note: the template's "optional (project-specific)" field does not apply to an Institutional indicator; these are optional institutional cuts the ICT function may add for management use.
unitOfObservation: Individual (the staff member) on the staff basis; organization (the programme, as an organizational unit of CIMMYT) on the programme basis.
calculationSummary: Numerator: number of CIMMYT staff (staff basis) or CIMMYT programmes (programme basis) with evidenced use of at least one designated unified data/ICT platform at the measurement date. Denominator: all CIMMYT staff (staff basis) or all CIMMYT programmes (programme basis) at the same date. Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100. The two bases answer different questions (workforce integration versus programme integration) and are never merged into one figure or one time series; each reported value states its basis. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): CIMMYT's corporate ICT records, specifically identity and access-management records, platform account and licence registers, and usage logs, matched to the human resources staff list (staff basis) or the programme portfolio register (programme basis). Fallback DS1 (Censuses & surveys): a structured return by unit heads or programme leads, or an all-staff survey, giving the platform account identifiers of each unit, programme or staff member, used only where account and usage records cannot be matched to the staff list or programme register, to complete that match; use is still evidenced from system records as Eligibility criteria and missing data requires, a record matched this way is flagged as fallback-sourced, since a match reported by a unit is less reliable than one made in system records, and a record the return cannot match stays in the denominator only. Not applicable DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation): internal platform use cannot be observed remotely. Not applicable DS4 (Secondary & international databases): no third-party database records CIMMYT's internal platform use. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): not relevant to an internal ICT record.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Applicable only when the fallback DS1 return is used: a structured reporting template listing, per unit, programme, or staff member, the account identifier on each designated platform. Respondent: the unit head or programme lead (or each staff member, if run as an all-staff survey). Mode: form-based self-completion, reconciled against ICT account records by the ICT function. When the Recommended DS2 source is used, not applicable, administrative source.
collectionFrequency: Annually, as an end-of-year snapshot compiled from ICT identity, account, and usage records.
referencePeriod: The measurement date (a snapshot at the end of the reporting year); each reported value describes platform use at that date.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual institutional snapshot; the previous year's value is the reference for trend. The first year with a confirmed designated-platform list and a stable activity threshold serves as the reference year for multi-year trend statements.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable. This is an Institutional indicator compiled once from corporate systems; there are no project-level instances to pool. If part of a year's figure had to rely on the fallback returns, that portion is noted alongside the figure rather than blended silently.

B: Combination method. Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level: the share is calculated directly from the full staff list or programme register, never averaged across units.

C: Levels and operations. The share is computed once, at institutional level, over all CIMMYT staff, or all programmes, on the stated basis, and is recomputed from its own numerator and denominator wherever a narrower view is wanted, never averaged from the views beneath it: a mean of unit shares weights a unit of three equally with one of three hundred. There is no level beneath the institution here, because a staff member or a programme is one record in the denominator, not a reporting level. The denominator is a portfolio of records rather than a population measured in the field, so the measurement levels do not apply and every breakdown is a reporting view. The staff basis and the programme basis are two indicators, never one: they are reported side by side and never averaged or combined, because a programme is not a number of people. Also report: the denominator itself, which basis was used, the denominator on that basis, and the platforms counted as unified, since the share moves with the list.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no, the default for the whole register. This share is the adoption result of the delivery count KPI-O49, but the two are never combined arithmetically; they connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative (delivery enables convergence), and they can move in opposite directions, since many separate new tools can lower platform unification.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: staff are matched by their unique corporate identity across platforms, so a person using three unified platforms counts once; programmes are matched by their portfolio-register identifier. The staff basis and the programme basis are never mixed within one series, and a figure on one basis is never compared against a figure on the other. No other register indicator counts staff or programmes on platforms, so there is no cross-indicator overlap to de-duplicate.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion and exclusion: the denominator includes all active staff (or all active programmes) at the measurement date; "operating on" a unified platform means evidenced use, not an account: at least one login or transaction on the designated platform within the 90 days before the measurement date, read from system records. An account with no activity in that window is a licence, not a user, and counting it would let the share rise on provisioning alone. Excludes former staff and closed programmes.
limitations: Being on a platform is not the same as using it well: the indicator shows convergence onto designated systems, not proficiency, data quality, or productivity gains from integration. A rising share means more of the organization works on the designated platforms; it does not mean operations became more efficient, or that the designated platforms are the right ones. It supports a digital-integration claim only, and the efficiency claim needs KPI-O49 and operational performance evidence beside it.

The value depends entirely on which platforms are designated as "unified": adding or removing a platform from the designated list changes the share without any change in behaviour, so the list must be fixed and versioned, and values are comparable only across years measured against the same list.

The two bases measure different things: a large programme and a small one weigh equally on the programme basis, and staff shares can rise through staff turnover (new joiners onboarded directly onto unified platforms) rather than through migration of existing work. State the basis with every figure and read staff and programme shares together.

The 90-day activity window is a compromise: it is strict enough that provisioning alone cannot lift the share, and loose enough to keep occasional legitimate users in the numerator, but a staff member on parental leave or long fieldwork falls out of it through no change in how they work. Apply the window identically every year, and read a fall against the leave and field calendar before reading it as regression.

Platform convergence is not data governance. Whether the research data held on those platforms is findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable is measured by KPI-O44 and KPI-OC41 in the Capacity, data & institutions pathway, and this indicator makes no claim about it: an organization can converge onto one system and manage the data on it badly.
subMetrics: None. The staff basis and the programme basis are two measurement bases of the same indicator, reported separately with their basis stated, not separately calculated sub-metrics. Per-platform shares are disaggregations of the same measure. The paired delivery count KPI-O49 (number of enterprise systems or digital tools developed, deployed, or upgraded) is a separate output indicator with its own reference sheet, not a sub-metric.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Institutional indicator; the data owner is knowledge management and IT, the enabling unit the 2030 Strategy names for CIMMYT's systems and data, and the same function that owns the designated-platform list and the application inventory behind KPI-O49. Data collection: knowledge management and IT, from identity, account and usage records, with human resources supplying the staff-list denominator and the programme portfolio register supplying the programme denominator. Validation: knowledge management and IT, matching platform records to the staff list or programme register and applying the 90-day activity test. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit, per the Calculation method. Approval: head of knowledge management and IT. Reporting: knowledge management and IT to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.

name: Staff-reported collaboration and information-sharing score (CIMMYT culture and engagement survey)
resultsLevel: Outcome. The Core reads an Institutional-branch level from the indicator statement itself: institution-wide changes in how the organization operates (here, how staff collaborate and share information) are outcomes, and counts of deliverables are outputs. Note: CGIAR's output/outcome boundary test (control by the research team versus behaviour change in external actors) is written for research results and fits an internal culture indicator poorly; the actors whose attitudes and relationships change are CIMMYT's own staff, not external actors, so the Outcome classification rests on that reading rather than on the external-actor test.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Excellence in Operations. The indicator measures the 2030 Strategy's Excellence in Operations objective that enabling activities across CIMMYT are streamlined to enhance collaboration and effectiveness, and specifically its sub-objective on promoting information and data sharing to foster a collaborative culture. As an Institutional indicator it does not map to the mission Primary Objectives PO1 to PO5; the register carries the component mapping instead..
institutionalComponent: Excellence in Operations. The indicator measures the 2030 Strategy's Excellence in Operations objective that enabling activities across CIMMYT are streamlined to enhance collaboration and effectiveness, and specifically its sub-objective on promoting information and data sharing to foster a collaborative culture. As an Institutional indicator it does not map to the mission Primary Objectives PO1 to PO5; the register carries the component mapping instead.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. The indicator measures a property of CIMMYT as an organization (its internal collaboration culture), an internal enabler rather than a result delivered to an external population, so the Institutional default applies.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator measures an organization's internal collaboration or information-sharing culture.
otherFrameworks: None. Staff engagement and culture surveys are widespread organizational practice, but no donor or reporting framework carries this composite.
definition: The staff-reported collaboration and information-sharing score from CIMMYT's culture and engagement survey, fielded roughly every two years: a composite survey-based score of how well staff collaborate and share information across the organization. The survey asks all CIMMYT staff to rate their own working experience, and the responses to the collaboration and information-sharing items are combined into one score for the wave year; a higher score indicates that staff experience the organization as more collaborative and better at sharing information. This is one instrument, not two: the survey reported as the CIMMYT culture and retention survey in the 2030 Strategy and the culture and engagement survey named in the register are the same all-staff instrument, and it is the same instrument that supplies the staff engagement and inclusion index (Vol. 12 · KPI-OC53) from a different item block.
rationale: Answers whether the enabling activities CIMMYT is streamlining, its systems, processes, knowledge-sharing platforms, and learning routines, are experienced by staff as a more collaborative organization: the staff-eye evidence behind the Excellence in Operations 2030 objective to "Promote information and data sharing to foster a collaborative culture". Tracked for senior management and enabling-unit leads as a repeatable check, run roughly every two years, on whether investments in operational systems translate into a culture where information moves and people work across units.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator). Reported once, at CIMMYT-institutional level, from a corporate all-staff survey; there is no project instance to adapt it to.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Composite index score, reported as the mean of the collaboration and information-sharing item block on the survey's agreement scale. The mean is the headline because it uses the whole scale: a percentage-favourable figure discards the difference between mild and strong agreement, which is most of what a culture series moves on. A percentage-favourable figure is reported beside the mean, never in place of it.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means staff report stronger collaboration and information sharing.
disaggregationRequired: None. The register records no required disaggregation, and none is added: a required cut on an anonymous staff survey would force the suppression rule to fire in every small unit, and a required disaggregation that is routinely suppressed is worse than an optional one that is published where it can be. The cuts below are optional and subject to the ten-respondent floor.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Organizational unit or program; duty station, country, or region; staff category. These cuts locate where collaboration is experienced as weak, for internal follow-up. Sub-group values are reported only where the number of respondents in a cell is large enough to protect anonymity; cells with fewer than ten respondents are suppressed or merged, matching KPI-OC53. The template's "optional (project-specific)" field does not apply to an Institutional indicator; these are optional institutional cuts the owning function may add.
unitOfObservation: Individual (staff member); the reported value is the institutional composite computed across all responses.
calculationSummary: The score is a summary value computed across respondents. Value: the unweighted mean of the item means across the items in the collaboration and information-sharing block, on the survey's agreement scale. Items are equally weighted, because a weighting scheme applied to a perception block would encode a judgment about which aspect of collaboration matters more that no evidence supports. The item list in force is reported with the value rather than restated on this sheet, so a reader can see what the composite covers and whether it changed between waves, and so that the sheet and the instrument cannot drift into disagreeing about what the block contains. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1 (Censuses & surveys): CIMMYT's culture and engagement survey (fielded roughly every two years), an internal all-staff survey collecting responses directly from staff (internal corporate instrument, no public URL). Fallback DS1 (Censuses & surveys): a shorter internal pulse survey carrying the same collaboration and information-sharing items, used only in an interim year when a full wave is not fielded; any value produced this way is flagged as fallback-sourced with its instrument and coverage stated, because a pulse sample is not comparable to a full all-staff wave without adjustment. Not applicable DS2 (Administrative & registry data): administrative records (for example platform usage logs) measure system activity, not staff-reported experience of collaboration; they cannot produce this score. Not applicable DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation): staff-reported sentiment is not remotely observable. Not applicable DS4 (Secondary & international databases): no third party publishes CIMMYT's internal staff-survey results. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): an anonymous internal staff survey cannot be substituted by crowdsourced data.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: The culture and engagement survey questionnaire (fielded roughly every two years), specifically its collaboration and information-sharing item block. Respondent rule: all CIMMYT staff, one response per person. Mode: self-administered, anonymous, online. Item wording and block composition are set by human resources as the instrument's owner, versioned per wave, and the version in force is reported with the value.
collectionFrequency: Every two years, one survey wave per cycle.
reportingFrequency: Annually; between survey waves the most recently measured score is carried forward with its wave year stated.
referencePeriod: The survey fielding window in the wave year: a point-in-time snapshot of staff experience at that wave, subject to any recall wording in the items themselves.
baselineRequired: Yes. The baseline is the 2022 culture and retention survey wave, the earliest wave of this instrument reported in the 2030 Strategy. Where the item block changed between that wave and the current instrument, the baseline is recomputed on the items common to both and the recomputation is stated; where the response scale changed, or too few items are common for a recomputation to mean anything, the first wave under the current instrument becomes the baseline and change is reported only from it forward. Either way the baseline wave and its basis travel with every change claim.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable; there are no project instances, a single institutional value exists per wave and is carried forward in interim years. A wave measured through the fallback pulse instrument is reported alongside the series with a note, not blended silently into it. If the indicator is ported to other CGIAR centers, report each center separately or pool the underlying responses and recompute; do not average center scores.

B: Combination method. Computed and reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level as the unweighted mean of the block's item means; never rebuilt by averaging sub-group scores, since a mean of unit means misweights units of different size.

C: Levels and operations. The score is computed once, at institutional level, and is never averaged across units, functions or waves: a mean of scores is not a score, because the item sets and response bases beneath them differ. A view for any subgroup is recomputed from that subgroup's own responses, subject to the suppression floor for small groups. A wave measured on the fallback pulse instrument is reported beside the series rather than blended into it. Also report: the scale and range in force, the respondent count and response rate, the item block used, and any wave whose instrument differs from the series.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no (the default; each level measures something different). Within the Continuous improvement & learning group this outcome sits above the output-level count of knowledge-sharing platforms and communities of practice (KPI-O50); they connect as a results narrative (platforms are built, staff then experience better collaboration), never arithmetically.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: prevented by design, one response per staff member per wave enforced by the survey platform; disaggregated figures partition the same respondent pool and are never summed into the headline. Overlap with other register indicators: the staff engagement and inclusion index (KPI-OC53, Workforce & talent) is drawn from the same staff survey but summarizes different item blocks (engagement, belonging, inclusion); one wave's responses feed both composites, which is not double counting because the two indicators are never added; the two sheets draw different cuts of one instrument and are never presented as independent corroboration.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion and exclusion: the survey population is all CIMMYT staff on an employment contract at the fielding date, internationally and nationally recruited alike. Consultants, interns and affiliated staff are outside the population: they are not inside the working relationships the block asks about for long enough to rate them, and including them would move the score with the size of the consultant roster. Where CIMMYT chooses to survey them, their responses are reported separately and never merged into this value.

Missing data: staff who did not respond are excluded from the computation, and their absence is captured in the response rate, which is always reported alongside the score. Within a partial response, an item left blank is excluded from that item's mean rather than imputed; a respondent who completed fewer than half the items in the block is excluded from the composite altogether, because a mean built from two items of six is not the same measure as the block.

Repeated observations: the survey is fielded once per wave with one response per staff member; responses are anonymous, so duplicates cannot be linked afterwards, and the survey platform's one-response-per-invitation control is the de-duplication mechanism.
limitations: Measures perception, not behaviour: the score captures how staff experience collaboration and information sharing, not actual knowledge flows, platform use, or cross-unit outputs. Self-report biases (social desirability, survey fatigue, the organizational mood at fielding time) move the value independently of real practice; read it alongside the platform and learning-review outputs (KPI-O50, KPI-O51) for the fuller picture.

The value is only as informative as the response rate: staff who feel disengaged are often likelier to skip the survey, so a low-response wave can overstate the score. Always report and interpret the score with its response rate, and treat a wave with a materially lower response rate as weak evidence of change in either direction.

Comparability over time requires a frozen instrument: any change to item wording, response scale, survey timing, or the composite rule breaks the series. Version the instrument, keep the fielding window constant across years, and flag any break explicitly rather than reading through it.

Supports a contribution claim only: the score responds to leadership changes, restructuring, workload, and remote-working patterns as much as to knowledge-sharing investments, so a rise does not by itself show that Excellence in Operations interventions worked, and a dip does not show they failed; it signals where to look, not what caused it.
subMetrics: None. The score is one composite; its constituent survey items are internal dimensions of the same block, not separately governed indicators. The staff engagement and inclusion index from the same staff survey is a separate register indicator (KPI-OC53, Workforce & talent) with its own reference sheet, not a sub-metric of this one.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
Strategic mandate: CIMMYT (2023), Science and Innovation for a Food and Nutrition Secure World, CIMMYT's 2030 Strategy, CIMMYT, for the Excellence in Operations objectives and the culture and retention survey passage.

CIMMYT culture and engagement survey, the operative instrument: an internal CIMMYT questionnaire with no public URL, cited by name and wave year. Its collaboration and information-sharing item block, and the item list in force for the wave, are the construct's definition of record.

Definitional anchor: CIMMYT's own convention, set out in this sheet's Definition and Calculation method. No external normative standard governs this composite.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Institutional indicator; roles sit with human resources, the enabling unit the 2030 Strategy names, which owns the culture and engagement survey and its item bank. Data collection: human resources, fielding the wave and holding the anonymous response file. Validation: human resources, checking response coverage, the one-response control and data integrity for the wave. Calculation: human resources, computing the score per the Calculation method and the response rate; the CIMMYT MEAL unit receives both and holds them for the register, and applies the suppression floor to any disaggregated view it publishes. Approval: head of human resources. Reporting: human resources to the CIMMYT MEAL unit. The same function computes Vol. 12 · KPI-OC53 from the other block of the same wave, which is what keeps the two indicators on one instrument.

name: Percentage of improvement actions from learning reviews implemented within the agreed timeline
resultsLevel: Outcome. Within the institutional results chain: conducting reviews and logging actions is the direct output (KPI-O51); the follow-through, units changing their systems and practices by the agreed date, is the behavioural change that output is meant to produce, which is what this indicator measures.
primaryObjective: Excellence in Operations (institutional enabler component). The indicator serves the component's second 2030 objective, that enabling activities across CIMMYT are streamlined to enhance collaboration and effectiveness, and specifically its sub-objective 2.3: incorporate learning and make timely adjustments as needed for continuous improvement and increased agility (CIMMYT, 2023). As an Institutional indicator it maps to one of the five institutional enabler components, not to a mission Primary Objective (PO1 to PO5); the register's Primary Objective column is accordingly blank for this row.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. The timely implementation of internal improvement actions is an organizational enabler; it delivers no direct result in any of the five CGIAR Impact Areas, and no genuine direct link exists.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator corresponds to an organization's internal rate of implementing improvement actions on schedule.
otherFrameworks: None. Implementation-rate measures of after-action review commitments are common internal management practice across development agencies, but no donor or external reporting framework carries this measure as a standard indicator; the definitional anchor is internal (the CIMMYT 2030 Strategy's Excellence in Operations component), and the definition stands on CIMMYT's own authority.
definition: Measures the share of improvement actions arising from CIMMYT's structured learning and after-action reviews that are implemented within their agreed timeline. An improvement action is a specific, recorded change commitment logged in the improvement-action tracker at the close of a review, with a named responsible unit and an implementation deadline. The indicator compares the actions completed on or before their agreed or default deadline against all actions logged from those reviews whose agreed or default deadline falls within the reporting year, so it reads whether CIMMYT follows through on what its own reviews conclude, not merely whether reviews happen.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT acts on its own learning: the outcome half of the continuous-improvement pair, in which KPI-O51 counts the reviews conducted and the actions they log, and this indicator measures the share of those logged actions delivered on schedule. It serves institutional reporting under the 2030 Strategy's Excellence in Operations component, whose objective to streamline enabling activities includes incorporating learning and making timely adjustments for continuous improvement and increased agility; a review practice that logs actions no unit implements would satisfy the output count while failing that objective.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional scope). This indicator measures a property of CIMMYT as an organization, reported once at Center level from corporate records; no project instantiates it, so there is no project-specific layer.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Percentage of improvement actions (implemented on time as a share of all actions due in the reporting year).
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of the improvement actions due in the year were closed as implemented by their deadline. A persistent 100 percent prompts a check that deadlines are ambitious and actions substantive.
disaggregationRequired: Required: None mandated. The indicator is a single institutional percentage reported once at Center level, and no CIMMYT-wide mandatory disaggregation set for Institutional-scope indicators is documented. Recommended for management use: by responsible organizational unit; by review type or trigger (project or phase closure, event, incident or process failure, periodic learning review); by action outcome status (implemented on time, implemented late, still open past deadline, cancelled).
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional scope; no project layer).
unitOfObservation: Organization (CIMMYT at Center-institutional level). The record assessed is the individual improvement action in the central tracker.
calculationSummary: Numerator: improvement actions closed as implemented in the improvement-action tracker on or before their agreed or default deadline, with closure evidence recorded. Denominator: all improvement actions logged from structured learning and after-action reviews (the same action log that feeds KPI-O51) whose agreed or default deadline falls within the reporting year. Value = (numerator / denominator) x 100. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative and registry data): CIMMYT's central improvement-action log or tracker, the same log in which the reviews counted under KPI-O51 register their actions, carrying for each action its source review, responsible unit, agreed deadline, any documented deadline revision or cancellation, status, completion date and closure evidence. Fallback: None applicable. Whether internal actions were completed by internal deadlines can be verified only from CIMMYT's own records; no lower-resolution or third-party substitute exists. Not applicable: DS1 (Censuses and surveys), staff could recall that actions were completed but recall cannot evidence a dated completion against a recorded deadline; DS3 (Geospatial and Earth observation), internal organizational actions are not observable from satellite or GIS data; DS4 (Secondary and international databases), no external database records CIMMYT's internal improvement actions; DS5 (Citizen-generated and other non-traditional data), crowdsourced or informal reports cannot evidence formal closure against an agreed deadline.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, secondary source. The recommended source is DS2 administrative records; verification is by review of each action's tracker record (deadline, status, completion date, closure evidence) against the rules in Eligibility criteria and missing data, not by a survey module or primary-collection tool.
collectionFrequency: Continuous: action status, completion dates and closure evidence are updated in the tracker as actions are implemented. The percentage is compiled once per year over the actions due that year.
reportingFrequency: Annual, reported with the raw numerator and denominator counts and the number of cancelled actions alongside the percentage.
referencePeriod: The reporting year in which the action's agreed or default deadline falls.
baselineRequired: No. Each year's rate is self-standing and interpretable on its own. The first assessed year anchors the trend; no improvement claim should be made until at least two years are on record under the same deadline and closure rules.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: Not applicable in the mission sense; the indicator is reported once at Center level. Unit-level rates are computed from the pooled unit numerators and denominators, never by averaging unit-level percentages, since units log very different numbers of actions. If the indicator is reused across CGIAR centers for portability, report each center's rate separately; do not pool actions across centers whose deadline and closure rules have not been harmonized.

B: Combination method. A ratio of sums, formed once: improvement actions closed as implemented over all improvement actions due in the year. Never an average of per-review or per-unit percentages.

C: Levels and operations. The share is computed once, at institutional level, over all improvement actions due in the reporting year, and is recomputed from its own numerator and denominator wherever a narrower view is wanted, never averaged from the views beneath it: a mean of unit shares weights a unit of three equally with one of three hundred. There is no level beneath the institution here, because an improvement action is one record in the denominator, not a reporting level. The denominator is a portfolio of records rather than a population measured in the field, so the measurement levels do not apply and every breakdown is a reporting view. Also report: the denominator itself, the number of actions due, the number carried over, and the share closed after their deadline, since on-time closure and closure are different claims.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: No. This outcome-level percentage does not combine arithmetically with the output-level KPI-O51 count of reviews conducted and actions logged; the two connect through the results chain as a narrative, reviews log actions and this indicator tracks whether those actions get implemented on time. There is one deliberate data linkage, which is not aggregation: the actions logged by the reviews KPI-O51 counts feed this indicator's denominator, so the two sheets must read the same action log.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: each action is one tracker record counted once, in the year its deadline falls, whatever the number of units or reviews it involves; an identical action logged by two reviews is merged before calculation (deduplicate by action ID). If actions are compiled from unit-level lists rather than a central tracker, the same joint action can appear on several lists, so deduplicate by action description, owner and deadline before calculating; if deduplication is not possible, flag the rate as computed on an inflated denominator.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion and exclusion: includes every logged action whose agreed or default deadline falls in the reporting year, whichever year it was logged in; excludes actions not yet due at year end (they are assessed in the year their deadline falls); excludes an entry logging a KPI-O51 review's finding that nothing needed to improve, which is not a change commitment; excludes actions formally cancelled as no longer applicable before their deadline, with documented justification and approval, and the count of cancellations is reported alongside the percentage.

Missing data: an item with no agreed deadline is not excluded. It takes a default due date of twelve months from the date of the review report that raised it, enters the denominator in the year that default date falls, and cannot enter the numerator unless it is closed with evidence on or before that date. Excluding it would reward never setting a deadline, which is the most common way an action quietly never happens. The number of items carrying a default due date is reported alongside the value, because a default is a symptom rather than a deadline.

Repeated observations: each action is counted once, in the year its agreed or default deadline falls; where a deadline is formally revised before the original date passes, the action is assessed against the revised deadline and counted in that year; an identical action logged by more than one review is merged into one record and counted once (deduplicate by action ID).
limitations: Measures timeliness of follow-through, not the quality or effect of the actions: an action can be closed on schedule without improving anything, and a rise in the rate means a larger share of logged commitments were delivered on time, not that CIMMYT's operations got better. Read it together with KPI-O51 and the substance of what the reviews found.

The rate is manipulable at both ends: lenient or repeatedly revised deadlines, trivially scoped actions, and cancelling actions that are about to fall overdue all inflate it. The figure is only as meaningful as the tracker's discipline, which is why deadline revisions and cancellations require documented justification and approval and are reported alongside the rate.

The denominator inherits the completeness of the review logging practice measured by KPI-O51: actions never logged are invisible here, and in the first years after a central tracker is introduced, movements can reflect changes in recording discipline as much as changes in implementation behaviour.

With a small denominator the percentage is volatile: a handful of actions moving across a year boundary can swing the value by tens of points, so single-year changes should not be over-read and the raw counts must always accompany the percentage.

CGIAR's output/outcome distinction is written for research results, where an outcome is a change among actors external to the research team; for an internal institutional indicator there is no external actor, so the Outcome classification here rests on the institutional results chain (follow-through as the behavioural change the review output is meant to produce), not on the research-facing test.
subMetrics: None. The numerator and denominator counts, the count of cancelled actions, and the recommended breakdowns by unit and action status are context reported alongside the percentage, not separately calculated sub-metrics. The denominator's feed, the count of reviews conducted and actions logged, has its own reference sheet (KPI-O51).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Institutional indicator; there is no project team, so roles sit with corporate functions. Data collection: the unit responsible for each improvement action updates its status, completion date and closure evidence in the central tracker; CIMMYT names its donor relationship management function (DFS) as the unit tracking agreed deadlines overall, and the roles here are stated for the central tracker, whether DFS holds it or a separate internal improvement-action log does. Validation: the tracker owner verifies closure evidence, deadline records and any revisions or cancellations against the rules in Eligibility criteria and missing data. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (annual compilation and deduplication per the Calculation method). Approval: head of the corporate function that owns the tracker. Reporting: CIMMYT MEAL unit into institutional Excellence in Operations reporting.
sourceRef: Volume 11 · Institutional performance & operations — Reference sheet KPI-OC50

name: Annual workforce (staffing) plan produced and updated against anticipated Center needs
resultsLevel: Output
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Talent Management (institutional enabler component: attract and retain top talent and provide an empowering, career-growth environment). As an Institutional indicator it does not map to a mission Primary Objective (PO1 to PO5): Institutional indicators map to institutional enabler components, not to the mission objectives; the register's Primary Objective column is accordingly blank for this row..
institutionalComponent: Talent Management (institutional enabler component: attract and retain top talent and provide an empowering, career-growth environment). As an Institutional indicator it does not map to a mission Primary Objective (PO1 to PO5): Institutional indicators map to institutional enabler components, not to the mission objectives; the register's Primary Objective column is accordingly blank for this row.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. Internal workforce planning is an organizational enabler; it delivers no direct result in any of the five CGIAR Impact Areas, and no direct link exists.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator corresponds to whether an organization produces an internal annual workforce plan. SDG 8 (decent work and economic growth) is thematically adjacent but offers no direct indicator correspondence, so None is recorded rather than a stretched mapping.
otherFrameworks: None. No donor or external reporting framework uses "annual workforce plan produced" as a standard indicator; the indicator is defined on CIMMYT's own authority against the 2030 Strategy's Talent Management component.
definition: Measures whether CIMMYT produces and updates an annual workforce or staffing plan against the Center's anticipated staffing needs, and whether that plan is complete (contains its required elements: projected headcount by staff category, identified critical and hard-to-fill roles, a succession position for every post at or above the grade band Human Resources designates as senior, and a costed budget envelope) and delivered on time. A workforce or staffing plan is the Human Resources document setting out the roles, numbers, grades and timing of the staff the Center expects to need. This is a milestone indicator: it tracks the planning deliverable, not headcount, vacancies or hiring volume. Beside that status it reports the country workforce-plan coverage rate (Sub-metrics).
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT systematically anticipates its staffing needs each year through a current, complete, on-time planning deliverable. Tracked for institutional Talent Management reporting: the workforce plan is the upstream planning step that makes needs-matched, timely recruitment possible, and it feeds the recruitment-agility result measured downstream by KPI-OC51 (median time-to-hire).
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional scope). This indicator measures a property of CIMMYT as an organization, reported once at Center level from corporate systems; no project instantiates it, so there is no project-specific layer.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Binary status (Yes / No) for the reporting year: whether the annual workforce or staffing plan was produced, updated against anticipated needs, complete, and on time. For a multi-year view, an optional roll-up can be reported as the on-time completion rate, the percentage of assessed years in which the plan met all criteria (see Calculation method). The country workforce-plan coverage rate is a percentage of operating countries (Sub-metrics).
directionOfChange: Reference value: Yes, in every reporting year. The plan is an annual corporate deliverable, so the reference is the requirement itself and not a target set here. A No, or a plan delivered late or incomplete, identifies a missed deliverable and triggers follow-up rather than reading as a lower point on a scale. For the country workforce-plan coverage rate the reference value is 100%.
disaggregationRequired: Headline: None. The headline is a single institutional status reported once at Center level; there is no population or sub-group to disaggregate over. No CIMMYT-wide mandatory disaggregation set for Institutional-scope indicators is documented, and a binary annual value has nothing meaningful to disaggregate. Country workforce-plan coverage rate: region, on CIMMYT's own regional structure as Human Resources records it, so that a Center rate is read with the regions that make it up.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional scope; no project layer).
unitOfObservation: Organization (CIMMYT at Center-institutional level); for the country coverage rate, the operating country.
calculationSummary: This is a binary milestone indicator. Value = Yes if, for the planning cycle covering the reporting year, the annual workforce or staffing plan was (a) produced, (b) updated against the Center's anticipated staffing needs, (c) complete, meaning it contains all of its required elements, and (d) delivered on time against the Human Resources planning-calendar deadline for that cycle. Value = No if any of the four conditions fails. The country workforce-plan coverage rate is computed separately: (operating countries with a qualifying country plan / operating countries) x 100, each country assessed on the qualifying-plan rule in Eligibility criteria and missing data. Optional multi-year roll-up, reported once three assessed reporting years exist: on-time completion rate = (number of assessed reporting years in which the plan met all four conditions / number of assessed reporting years) x 100. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): CIMMYT Human Resources records, specifically the annual workforce or staffing plan document itself together with its version history and formal approval or sign-off dates, which establish production, completeness, and timeliness; for the country coverage rate, each country plan or dated country section with its approval date, and Human Resources staff records by country of employment on the planning-calendar deadline date, which fix the denominator and the region. This is the authoritative source because the deliverable exists only inside CIMMYT's own corporate Human Resources system (internal, no external URL). Fallback: None applicable; the plan's existence and dating can be verified only from Human Resources' own records, so no lower-resolution or third-party substitute exists. Not applicable: DS1 (Censuses & surveys), DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation), DS4 (Secondary & international databases), DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): whether an internal corporate planning document was produced, approved, and dated cannot be measured through respondent surveys, Earth observation, external databases, or crowdsourced data.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source. Verification is by document and approval-date review against the four conditions in the Calculation method, not by a survey module or primary-collection tool.
collectionFrequency: Annual (once per planning cycle).
referencePeriod: The reporting year: the annual planning cycle the plan covers, assessed against that cycle's Human Resources planning-calendar deadline.
baselineRequired: No. Each year's binary status is self-standing: the intended state (produced, complete, on time) is fixed and interpretable without a prior-period reference. Where trend reporting is wanted, the first assessed year anchors the optional multi-year on-time completion rate. Targets, baselines, and actuals are out of scope for this reference sheet.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: Not applicable. The indicator is reported once at Center level from corporate Human Resources systems; there are no project instances to pool. If reused across CGIAR centers for portability, do not blend statuses into one figure; report each center's status (or its on-time completion rate or country coverage rate) separately.

B: Combination method: not combined; the country coverage rate is a ratio of sums. A status is a single institutional fact for the reporting year; there is no arithmetic that turns several statuses into one, and a percentage of centers reporting Yes is a different indicator. The country coverage rate is qualifying countries summed over operating countries summed.

C: Levels and operations. The status is reported once, at institutional level, from the corporate system that holds the plan; no project, site or unit holds a share of it. The country coverage rate runs on three levels: each country is Yes or No; a region's rate is its qualifying countries over its operating countries; the Center rate is all qualifying countries over all operating countries, recomputed from the counts and never averaged from regional rates. The status and the rate are reported side by side, and neither is derived from the other. Also report: the date the status was determined and the system it was read from, with the planning-calendar deadline date it was assessed against; for the country coverage rate, the qualifying and operating country counts at each level.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: No. This output-level status does not combine arithmetically with the outcome it enables, KPI-OC51 (median time-to-hire); the two connect through the Theory of Change as a narrative (a current, complete workforce plan enables faster, needs-matched hiring), not through arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: Not applicable to the status. There is a single institutional planning deliverable per reporting year, so the same unit cannot be counted twice; in the country coverage rate each operating country counts once per year, regardless of how many plans it holds. The country coverage rate is computed over every operating country, a census of the domain: it carries no sampling error and no coefficient-of-variation band, and the operating-country count is reported instead.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion and exclusion (headline): only the single Center-level annual workforce or staffing plan owned by Human Resources counts toward the headline; unit-level or project-level staffing lists, and working drafts without formal approval, are excluded. Country plans enter the country coverage rate only, under the rule below. Condition (b), updated against anticipated needs, is met where the approved version states projected headcount for the cycle it covers; a prior cycle's plan re-approved without its projections restated for the new cycle fails it. Missing-data treatment: if no plan and no approval or version record exists for the reporting year, the value is No, not missing; a plan produced but never formally approved and dated cannot demonstrate timeliness and is treated as not on time.

Repeated observations: one status per reporting year; if the plan is revised several times within the year, the indicator records whether at least one approved, on-time version meeting the completeness criteria exists, so multiple revisions never count as multiple positives.

Country coverage rate: an operating country is one in which CIMMYT employs staff on the Human Resources planning-calendar deadline date for that cycle, per Human Resources records; the denominator is fixed on that date, so a country first staffed after the deadline never counts against that year's rate and enters the next cycle's denominator. A country qualifies with a standalone country plan or a dated country section of the Center plan that carries the four required elements for that country's staff (the succession element only where the country holds such a post) and is approved by the Human Resources planning-calendar deadline; a country with no such record counts as not qualifying, not missing, and several plans for one country count once.

Multi-year roll-up: an assessed reporting year is one for which a status was determined under the rules above; years before the first determined status are excluded.
limitations: Measures the existence, completeness, and timeliness of a planning deliverable, not its quality or use: a plan can be produced complete and on time yet be poorly matched to the Center's real needs, or never acted on.

The completeness judgment depends on the required-elements list stated in the Definition; comparability holds while that stated list is applied unchanged, and breaks if Human Resources adopts a different list without restating it here.

Supports no attribution to hiring or workforce outcomes: producing the plan is a necessary enabling step, not a guarantee of faster recruitment or better staffing. Read it together with KPI-OC51 (median time-to-hire) and the retention and engagement indicators (KPI-OC54, KPI-OC53) for the full Talent Management narrative.

A Yes means the planning system worked as intended that year; it does not mean staffing gaps were closed. A No flags that the deliverable was absent, incomplete, or late, not that the Center failed to hire.

The country coverage rate counts plans that exist, are complete and are on time; it is called coverage rather than execution because neither it nor the headline measures whether a plan was carried out. Its denominator moves as CIMMYT opens or closes country operations, so a change in the rate is read with the operating-country count behind it. Regional rates rest on few countries and move in large steps, so each is read with its country count. Where country plans are sections of the Center plan, a late Center plan fails those countries as well: the two figures are computed separately but are not independent. The denominator is fixed on the planning-calendar deadline, which may fall before the cycle it covers and which moves between cycles, so the country set behind a year's rate is not necessarily the set operating during that year.

Comparability across CGIAR centers requires a shared definition of what an annual workforce plan must contain and when it is due; without that shared definition the status is not meaningfully comparable between centers.
subMetrics:
The register definition bundles two attributes (completeness and on-time) that can each be reported as a binary sub-metric, and the Center status is reported with a country coverage rate. All three are drawn from Human Resources records and are not calculated on separate KPI sheets:

— Completeness: Yes if the plan contains all of its required elements, No otherwise. Formula: checklist pass/fail against the required-elements list stated in the Definition. (Human Resources may replace it with its own list, and completeness is then assessed against that list.)

— Timeliness (on-time): Yes if the plan was produced, updated, and approved by the Human Resources planning-calendar deadline for the cycle, No otherwise. Formula: comparison of the plan's approval or version date against the deadline.

— Country workforce-plan coverage rate (%): the share of operating countries holding a qualifying country plan. Formula: (operating countries with a qualifying country plan / operating countries) x 100, reported by region; the reference value is 100%. The operating-country and qualifying-plan rules are in Eligibility criteria and missing data.

The headline value is Yes only when the completeness and timeliness sub-metrics are both Yes and the plan was produced and updated against anticipated needs. Reporting those two separately shows whether a No was caused by an incomplete plan, a late plan, or both. The coverage rate does not enter the headline: a Center plan that is complete and on time while half the operating countries hold none is the gap the rate exists to show.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
Definitional anchor (internal): CIMMYT 2030 Strategy, Talent Management enabler component; institutional page: https://www.cimmyt.org/about/our-strategy/. No external methodological standard (SDG metadata, CGIAR Results Framework, donor reporting frameworks) governs an internal annual-workforce-planning milestone indicator; this absence is stated rather than filled with a non-applicable standard. The required-elements list is this toolbox's and is stated in the Definition.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Institutional indicator; the responsible corporate function is Human Resources. Data collection: CIMMYT Human Resources (custodian of the workforce or staffing plan and its version and approval records). Validation: Human Resources leadership (Director of Human Resources or designate). Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (applies the four conditions, computes the country coverage rate and, if used, the multi-year on-time rate). Approval: the Director of Human Resources with senior management endorsement, as the plan's approving authority (the sheet follows CIMMYT's delegation where it differs). Reporting: CIMMYT MEAL unit into institutional Talent Management reporting.
sourceRef: Volume 12 · Workforce & talent — Reference sheet KPI-O52

name: Number of staff completing structured capacity or career development through the CIMMYT Learning and Training academy
resultsLevel: Output
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Talent Management.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. The indicator measures a property of CIMMYT as an employer (development of its own workforce), an internal enabler rather than a result delivered to an external population. The sex disaggregation supports internal equity monitoring of access to development opportunities, but the CGIAR Gender Equality, Youth & Social Inclusion Impact Area measures outcomes for the populations CGIAR centers serve, not center staff.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator corresponds directly to an employer's count of its own staff completing internal development programmes. The nearest reference, SDG indicator 4.3.1 (participation rate of youth and adults in formal and non-formal education and training), measures population-level participation, not staff completions within one organization, so it is thematically adjacent only, not a correspondence.
otherFrameworks: GRI 404: Training and Education 2016, the sustainability-reporting standard on employee training (disclosure 404-1 counts training hours per employee; 404-2 covers programmes for upgrading employee skills).
definition: Counts CIMMYT staff completing structured capacity or career development through the Learning and Training academy in the reporting year. "Structured" means a defined development programme with stated objectives and explicit completion criteria, as distinct from one-off or informal learning events. The value counts distinct staff completing a defined development programme: each staff member is counted once in the reporting year regardless of how many programmes they complete, so the figure is a headcount of staff developed, not a count of course completions.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT is delivering on its Talent Management commitment to "implement a continuous capacity and career development strategy that ensures equitable opportunities for success" (CIMMYT 2030 Strategy, Talent Management objectives). The Learning and Training academy is the delivery vehicle the Strategy itself names for responding to staff demand for greater learning opportunities. This output feeds the Talent Management results chain: staff who receive structured development are expected to be more engaged and more likely to stay, which the outcome indicator KPI-OC53 (staff engagement and inclusion index) measures. Tracked for institutional human-capital reporting and to make workforce-development effort visible and comparable year on year.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator). Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate systems; there is no project instance to adapt it to.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Number of staff (count of distinct staff who completed at least one structured Learning and Training academy development programme in the reporting year)
directionOfChange: Increase, read with the supply caveat in Limitations. A rising value means more staff completed a structured development programme. The count also reflects how many programmes the academy offered in the year, so it does not measure staff demand on its own.
disaggregationRequired: Sex, female/male at minimum, on CGIAR's sex-disaggregated data standards (Doss & Kieran, 2014); staff category (register-required; the cut is CIMMYT's own staff-category classification as Human Resources maintains it, and the values applied are stated with the figure). Cells are published under CIMMYT's own Human Resources data-protection rules, and this sheet sets no disclosure floor of its own.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Programme type or theme (leadership, technical, digital, supervisory skills); duty station or region; grade band or career stage. These are optional institutional cuts Human Resources may add; the project-specific tier does not apply to an Institutional indicator.
unitOfObservation: Individual (the staff member).
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct CIMMYT staff members who met the stated completion criteria of at least one structured Learning and Training academy development programme during the reporting year. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): the Learning and Training academy's completion records or learning management system, together with the Human Resources training registry, recording the staff member, programme, completion date, and completion status. Fallback DS2 (lower-resolution instance of the same code): departmental or manual training registers, used only where centralized academy records are unavailable for all or part of the year; a value built from these must be flagged as fallback-sourced because de-duplication and completion evidence are weaker. Not applicable DS1 (Censuses & surveys): completion is an administrative record, not a respondent-reported condition, so no survey feeds this indicator. Not applicable DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation): staff development cannot be observed remotely. Not applicable DS4 (Secondary & international databases): CIMMYT's internal staff records are not held by third parties. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): not relevant to an internal personnel record.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source. The indicator is compiled from existing DS2 completion records, not collected with a DS1 or DS5 instrument.
collectionFrequency: Continuous administrative logging: each completion is recorded in the academy or Human Resources learning records as it occurs.
referencePeriod: The CIMMYT reporting year in which the programme was completed.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual institutional count; the previous year's value is the reference for trend. Where a multi-year trend is wanted, the first year with complete academy completion records serves as the reference year.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: Not applicable. This is an Institutional indicator drawn once from corporate systems; there are no project-level instances to pool, so the Recommended-versus-Fallback pooling rule does not arise. If any period had to rely on fallback manual registers, that portion is noted alongside the figure rather than blended silently.

B: Combination method. Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level: distinct-staff completions are summed across programmes, units, and duty stations after de-duplication by staff identifier; never averaged.

C: Levels and operations. Computed once, at institutional level, as the count of unique staff who completed at least one structured development programme in the reporting year, de-duplicated on the corporate person identifier. Where a view by function, grade or duty station is wanted, it is recomputed from that subset's own records. Also report: the number of completions behind the headcount, since the two differ, and the number of records dropped for want of an identifier.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: No. Following the toolbox-wide default, results levels connect through the theory of change narratively, not arithmetically. This output does not combine arithmetically with the outcome it contributes to (KPI-OC53, staff engagement and inclusion index); they connect through the Talent Management theory of change as a narrative, not through addition.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: a staff member who completes several programmes, or transfers between units or duty stations within the year, is counted once, matched on the unique staff or employee ID before the institutional headcount is formed. Where source registers use identifier schemes that cannot be reconciled with each other (a record with no identifier at all is dropped and reported in the dropped-record count, Block C), the reported figure is labelled an upper estimate. CIMMYT staff completing internal capacity development are excluded from Vol. 2 · KPI-O04, so the two counts do not overlap. The count is computed over every completion record in the academy's records for the year, and in the Fallback registers for any period those records do not cover, a census of the domain: it carries no sampling error and no coefficient-of-variation band, and the completion count is reported instead.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion and exclusion: includes staff on CIMMYT employment contracts during the reporting year, the population KPI-OC54 counts, who satisfy the completion criteria of a structured programme delivered through the Learning and Training academy; excludes internal training outside the academy, structured programmes delivered outside it included; partial or abandoned participation; attendance at one-off or informal sessions outside a defined programme; and participants not on a CIMMYT employment contract (consultants, contractors, interns).
limitations: Output-level only: completing a programme evidences participation, not that a capability was gained, retained, or applied, and not that a career advanced. The intended workforce outcomes (engagement, inclusion, retention) are measured separately by KPI-OC53 and KPI-OC54.

The count is supply-sensitive: a rise can reflect the academy offering more programmes in a year as much as more staff seeking development. Interpret movements alongside the size of the programme offering.

Comparability depends on a consistent completion rule: until one institutional definition of "completed" applies across all academy programmes, a shift may partly reflect differences in how programmes certify completion rather than a real change in staff developed.

The distinct-staff headcount understates total learning volume, since a person completing several programmes counts once. It answers "how many staff were developed through the academy", not "how much development took place". Internal training outside the academy is counted by no indicator in the register.

The headline number says nothing about who is reached: only the sex and staff-category disaggregation, read against the workforce's composition by sex and staff category in the same year (the average headcounts KPI-OC54 reports), shows whether access to development is equitable, in line with the Strategy's "equitable opportunities for success" objective. A rising total can still mask uneven access.
subMetrics:
None. The required disaggregations (sex, staff category) are cuts of the same headcount, not separately calculated metrics. The related measure "number of programme completions" (counting every completion) is a distinct volume measure, deliberately out of scope because this indicator is defined as a distinct-staff headcount.

A follow-up measure of whether staff apply what a programme taught, the share of completers demonstrating or applying the acquired competency some months after completion, is not carried here, and the reason is the instrument rather than the idea. It would require a post-programme follow-up of named completers on a clock set by the programme rather than by the reporting year, and the academy runs no such follow-up; attaching it as a sub-metric of a completion headcount would put a number in the toolbox that no records can produce. The pathway consequently has no outcome level for staff development: this sheet counts completions, and the workforce outcomes measured downstream (KPI-OC53, KPI-OC54) are engagement and retention, not capability applied.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
Comparator disclosure: Global Reporting Initiative (2016), GRI 404: Training and education 2016, via the GRI Standards English-language library; SDG indicator 4.3.1 metadata, cited as the adjacency reference for the "None" SDG determination, not as a mapping.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: Human Resources and the Learning and Training academy (completion logging). Validation: Human Resources. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (de-duplication and the distinct-staff headcount per the Calculation method). Approval: Director of Human Resources. Reporting: Human Resources to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
