name: Median time-to-hire (days)
resultsLevel: Outcome
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Talent Management (institutional enabler component). As an Institutional indicator it does not map to the mission Primary Objectives PO1 to PO5; it maps to one of the five enabler components of the 2030 Strategy, and recruitment agility belongs to Talent Management (attracting and retaining top talent)..
institutionalComponent: Talent Management (institutional enabler component). As an Institutional indicator it does not map to the mission Primary Objectives PO1 to PO5; it maps to one of the five enabler components of the 2030 Strategy, and recruitment agility belongs to Talent Management (attracting and retaining top talent).
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. This is an internal workforce-process measure with no direct link to any of the five official Impact Areas (Climate Adaptation & Mitigation; Environmental Health & Biodiversity; Nutrition, Health & Food Security; Poverty Reduction, Livelihoods & Jobs; Gender Equality, Youth & Social Inclusion).
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator corresponds to an organization's time-to-hire. The theme is adjacent to SDG target 8.5 (full and productive employment and decent work for all), but there is no direct indicator correspondence.
otherFrameworks: None. No sustainability-reporting, donor or CGIAR framework carries a recruitment-timing disclosure: GRI 401: Employment 2016 covers hires and turnover but not the interval taken to fill a vacancy. Time-to-hire and time-to-fill are standard measures in general human-resources analytics practice, and this indicator is defined on CIMMYT's own authority.
definition: Measures the median number of days CIMMYT takes to fill a vacant position, counted from the date the job requisition is approved to the date the selected candidate accepts the offer, across all positions filled during the reporting period. Requisition approval, not vacancy posting, is the fixed clock start. The median is used rather than the mean because a few long searches right-skew the duration distribution. It is a recruitment-agility measure: lower values mean CIMMYT converts vacancies into accepted hires faster.
rationale: Answers how quickly CIMMYT can staff itself: the time between deciding a role is needed and a candidate saying yes. Human Resources and senior leadership track it because prolonged vacancies leave research and support functions understaffed, overload existing teams, and delay delivery, while a shorter time-to-hire signals a talent-acquisition function able to compete for candidates and staff the Center against anticipated needs, the core of the 2030 Strategy's Talent Management component.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable. This is an Institutional indicator, measured once at CIMMYT level from corporate Human Resources systems; there is no project instance to adapt it to.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Days (median number of days per completed hire)
directionOfChange: Decrease. A falling value means the median vacancy is filled in fewer days from requisition approval to offer acceptance. It can also fall because hard-to-fill roles were withdrawn rather than filled, so it is read with the number of completed hires behind the median.
disaggregationRequired: Required: job family/grade (per the register), so medians are compared within comparable role types; senior and specialised scientific posts systematically take longer to fill than junior or administrative ones, and an aggregate median mixes the two. Cells are published under CIMMYT's own Human Resources data-protection rules, and this sheet sets no disclosure floor of its own.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: The project-specific tier does not apply to an Institutional indicator. For its own management analysis, Human Resources may additionally cut the median by duty station or region and by internationally versus nationally recruited staff; these are internal analytical views, not required institutional disaggregations. Human Resources may likewise cut the median by the sex of the appointed candidate, read within job family/grade and reported with the number of hires behind each median, to check whether posts filled by women take longer than those filled by men. It is not required because the clock starts at requisition approval, before any candidate exists, so a gap by sex is a signal to investigate rather than a finding about a population.
unitOfObservation: One completed recruitment (one vacancy filled by one accepted offer); reported once at institutional level.
calculationSummary: For each position filled during the reporting period, compute the elapsed days from the requisition-approval date to the date the selected candidate accepted the offer. The reported value is the median of that set of durations. This is a median over completed hires, not a numerator divided by a denominator. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): CIMMYT's Human Resources applicant-tracking or recruitment system plus the Human Resources information system, which timestamp the requisition-approval date and the offer-acceptance date for every recruitment. Internal corporate system, no external URL. Fallback DS2 (Administrative & registry data): manual Human Resources recruitment logs or spreadsheets, used only where the system does not capture both required timestamps; values reconstructed this way are flagged as fallback-sourced. Not applicable DS1 (Censuses & surveys): recruitment duration is a process fact held in administrative records, not information elicited from respondents. Not applicable DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation): a hiring timeline cannot be observed from satellite or GIS data. Not applicable DS4 (Secondary & international databases): no third party publishes CIMMYT's internal per-hire timings. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): crowdsourced or non-traditional data cannot supply internal recruitment timestamps.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source. The value is computed from system timestamps; collection instruments are specified only for DS1 or DS5 sources.
collectionFrequency: Continuous. The underlying timestamps are recorded in the Human Resources recruitment or applicant-tracking system as each requisition progresses; the median is consolidated annually (with quarterly internal snapshots possible for HR management).
reportingFrequency: Annually, in institutional reporting for the Talent Management component.
referencePeriod: The reporting year: all recruitments whose offer acceptance falls within that 12-month window.
baselineRequired: No, not in the project baseline sense (Institutional indicator with no project start point). The previous reporting year's median is the natural reference for judging change in recruitment agility. Targets, baselines, and actuals are otherwise outside what this reference sheet covers.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: Not applicable. The indicator is reported once from corporate systems; there is no project instance to pool. If reused across CGIAR centers for portability, do not average the centers' medians (a median of medians is not the system median); pool the underlying per-hire durations and recompute, or report each center separately.

B: Combination method: recomputed, not averaged. The median is computed from the underlying per-hire durations. There is no formula that combines medians, because a median of medians is not the system median.

C: Levels and operations. Computed once, at institutional level, over every completed hire in the reporting year. Where a view by region, function, grade or sex of the appointee is wanted, it is recomputed from that subset's own per-hire durations, never taken as the median of the sub-medians. Where the indicator is reused across CGIAR centers, pool the underlying durations and recompute, or report each center separately. Also report: the number of completed hires the median rests on, since a median over eleven hires can move with a single search where one over four hundred cannot, the count of hires excluded under Eligibility, and the companion count of failed, cancelled and still-open searches in the same period, alongside the median: only accepted offers enter the median, so this companion count is what shows a search that never closes.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: No. This outcome does not combine arithmetically with the output indicator in the same indicator group (KPI-O52, annual workforce or staffing plan produced and updated); the plan anticipates staffing needs and agile recruitment fills them, a Theory of Change connection told as a narrative, not arithmetic.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: each completed hire enters once, keyed by its requisition identifier together with the appointee, so a recruitment pool contributes one observation per accepted offer while the clock runs from the one requisition; re-advertised vacancies are governed by the repeated-observations rule in Section 3 so one filled role never contributes two durations. The median is computed over every completed hire in the period, a census of the domain: it carries no sampling error and no coefficient-of-variation band, and the hire count is reported instead.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: recruitments that ended in an accepted offer, with the acceptance date inside the reporting period.

Exclusion: requisitions cancelled or withdrawn before an offer was accepted, searches still open at period end (no duration exists for them yet); internal promotions and transfers filled without an open competition, which raise no requisition and so cannot be keyed or timed; and consultants, short-term appointments and internships, whose recruitment runs on different processes and timelines. An offer accepted and withdrawn before the start date is not a completed hire: that search enters the failed-search companion count of the year in which the offer was accepted, and the re-opened vacancy raises a new requisition; a withdrawal recorded after that year's median is reported is a restatement of the year's value and its companion count under the Core's rules for restated values (Section 4.2).

Missing data: a hire missing either the start timestamp (requisition-approval date) or the acceptance date in both the recruitment system and the manual Human Resources logs that Data source names as the Fallback is excluded rather than imputed, because its duration cannot be computed; the number of exclusions is reported alongside the value.

Repeated observations: each accepted hire counts once, keyed by its requisition identifier together with the appointee; if one requisition produces several hires (a recruitment pool), each accepted hire is one observation. A vacancy re-advertised after a failed search raises a new requisition identifier, so the clock runs from the approval of that new requisition rather than from the original requisition; the original failed search is not dropped silently, it enters the failed-search companion count (Aggregation rule, Block C).
limitations: Speed, not quality. Time-to-hire says nothing about whether the right person was hired or whether the hire stays; a fast search that yields a poor fit or early departure is not a success. Read it alongside the pathway’s turnover/retention (KPI-OC54) and engagement (KPI-OC53) indicators.

The clock starts at requisition approval, ruled rather than left open because the alternative (vacancy posting) can differ by weeks and the two are not interchangeable; the register's definition (requisition or posting to offer acceptance) matches what practitioner references call "time-to-fill", while "time-to-hire" conventionally starts when the successful candidate first applies. Applied consistently, requisition approval is comparable across years and job families within CIMMYT; comparison against external benchmarks still depends on the benchmark using the same start point, which is not assured.

The mix of vacancies moves the number. A year with more senior, specialised, or internationally recruited posts will show a longer median even if the recruitment function worked exactly as fast; compare within job family/grade, not only in aggregate.

Only successful searches are visible. Because the median is computed over accepted offers, cancelled, failed, or still-open searches drop out, so a low median can coexist with long-standing unfilled critical posts and can flatter the picture. A companion count of failed, cancelled and still-open searches is reported alongside the median for exactly this reason (Aggregation rule, Block C), so a low median cannot be read alone as evidence that every post was filled.

External drivers matter. Labour-market tightness, salary competitiveness, visa and relocation timelines for international posts, and hiring freezes all shape the value; a movement in the median is not by itself evidence that Human Resources performance changed.

Filling a post is not securing the competency. This indicator measures recruitment agility and nothing about whether the person hired meets the competency profile the role requires. A measure that did, the share of critical scientific and technical positions filled by staff meeting a required competency profile, would need two artefacts held corporately and kept current: a designation of which positions are critical, and a competency profile per role against which a hire can be assessed. Neither is evidenced anywhere in this toolbox, and a sheet cannot supply them by defining them itself, because the definitions would then describe a framework this toolbox has no evidence CIMMYT runs. The gap is real and is recorded here rather than closed.
subMetrics: None. The job family/grade breakdown is a disaggregation of the same median, not a separately calculated metric.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
Definitional anchor: CIMMYT's own convention, set out in this sheet's Definition and Aggregation rule: the clock definition, the population of recruitments and the median convention. No external methodological standard governs this measure; GRI 401: Employment 2016 is the nearest sustainability-reporting disclosure and covers hires and turnover, not recruitment timing, so it is not cited as the authority here.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Institutional indicator owned by the Human Resources corporate function. Data collection: Human Resources talent-acquisition team (applicant-tracking system records). Validation: Human Resources operations or HR information-system analyst. Calculation: Human Resources analytics, following the Calculation method above. Approval: Director of Human Resources. Reporting: Human Resources to the CIMMYT MEAL unit for institutional reporting.

name: Staff engagement and inclusion index (culture and retention survey)
resultsLevel: Outcome
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Talent Management (institutional enabler component). The indicator measures progress against the Talent Management 2030 objective "An enabling, empowering, career growth environment develops and retains top talent" and its sub-objective on protecting and promoting diversity, inclusion, and recognition of staff contributions. As an Institutional indicator it does not map to the mission Primary Objectives PO1 to PO5; institutional indicators map to strategy components rather than mission objectives, and the register's Primary Objective cell is "-" while the Strategy Component column carries the mapping..
institutionalComponent: Talent Management (institutional enabler component). The indicator measures progress against the Talent Management 2030 objective "An enabling, empowering, career growth environment develops and retains top talent" and its sub-objective on protecting and promoting diversity, inclusion, and recognition of staff contributions. As an Institutional indicator it does not map to the mission Primary Objectives PO1 to PO5; institutional indicators map to strategy components rather than mission objectives, and the register's Primary Objective cell is "-" while the Strategy Component column carries the mapping.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. This indicator measures CIMMYT as an employer, not a result delivered to an external population. Its inclusion content is thematically close to Gender Equality, Youth & Social Inclusion, but that Impact Area concerns inclusion outcomes in agrifood systems; no direct link is claimed for internal staff sentiment.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator corresponds directly to an organization's internal staff engagement and inclusion index. SDG 8 (decent work) is thematically related but has no indicator at the level of this composite.
otherFrameworks: None. No external framework is evidenced for the instrument, which Human Resources owns, so no correspondence is claimed.
definition: The staff engagement and inclusion index from CIMMYT's culture and retention survey, fielded roughly every two years: a composite index score summarizing staff-reported engagement, belonging, and inclusion for the wave year. The survey asks all CIMMYT staff to rate their own experience of working at the Center, and the responses to the engagement, belonging, and inclusion items are combined into one index value; a higher score indicates stronger engagement. Because the value rests on a composite built by CIMMYT's Human Resources (People and Culture) function, the exact item set, response scale, and scoring formula are defined by that function's survey methodology, which is internal and not restated here.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT is becoming the organization its 2030 Strategy commits to: one where a sense of belonging is fostered and staff feel energized, supported, and valued. It gives senior management and Human Resources a repeatable measure, taken roughly every two years, of staff sentiment for the Talent Management component of the strategy, and it turns the culture and retention survey the strategy itself cites into a tracked institutional outcome. Read together with turnover and retention (KPI-OC54), it helps explain whether the enabling, career-growth environment the strategy targets is experienced by staff.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable. Institutional scope: the indicator is measured once, at CIMMYT-institutional level, from a corporate survey; there is no project instance to adapt it to.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Composite index score. The reported scale and range (for example a 1 to 5 mean, a 0 to 100 index, or a percentage-favorable figure) are set by the Human Resources survey methodology, and the scale in force is stated with the value.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means staff report stronger engagement, belonging and inclusion. The scale and range are reported with the score, since index values produced by different instruments are not comparable.
disaggregationRequired: Required: staff category (CIMMYT's own staff-category classification as Human Resources maintains it); region (per the register). Sub-group values are reported only where the number of respondents in a cell is large enough to protect anonymity: cells with fewer than ten respondents are suppressed or merged into the next level up, and the suppression is stated rather than left as a silent gap in the table.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional scope has no project layer).
unitOfObservation: Individual (staff member); the reported value is the institutional index computed across all responses.
calculationSummary: The index is a summary score computed across respondents, not a single numerator over a denominator. Value: the composite of scored responses to the engagement, belonging, and inclusion item blocks, computed by Human Resources per its survey methodology (the item set, weighting and headline format belong to that methodology and are recorded with the series). Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS1 (Censuses & surveys): CIMMYT's culture and retention survey (fielded roughly every two years; the register also names it the culture and engagement survey, one instrument under two names), an internal all-staff survey collecting responses directly from staff for the purpose of this indicator (internal corporate instrument, no public URL). Fallback DS2 (Administrative & registry data): Human Resources records and analytics from a prior survey wave, used only where a wave Human Resources has scheduled is not fielded; a value carried past its scheduled wave is flagged as fallback-sourced with its wave year stated. Carrying the latest wave forward in the years between scheduled waves is the rule in Reporting frequency and is not a Fallback. Not applicable DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation): staff-reported sentiment cannot be observed from satellite or GIS data. Not applicable DS4 (Secondary & international databases): no third party publishes CIMMYT's internal staff-survey results. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): an anonymous internal staff survey cannot be substituted by crowdsourced or non-traditional data.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional scope).
collectionInstrument: The culture and retention survey questionnaire (fielded roughly every two years), specifically its engagement, belonging, and inclusion item blocks. Respondent rule: all CIMMYT staff, one response per person. Mode: self-administered, anonymous, online. Item wording and block composition are held by Human Resources.
collectionFrequency: Roughly every two years, one survey wave per cycle, where the register's definition says annual; the wave history is stated with each value.
reportingFrequency: Annually; between survey waves the most recently measured index is carried forward with its wave year stated.
referencePeriod: The survey fielding window in the wave year: a point-in-time snapshot of staff experience at that wave.
baselineRequired: Yes. The baseline is the earliest survey wave whose instrument is comparable to the current one. The 2022 culture and retention survey, which the 2030 Strategy cites, is a candidate baseline rather than an established first wave, and the wave history and instrument comparability travel with the value. If no comparable prior wave exists, the current wave becomes the baseline and change is reported only from it forward; with no baseline at all the index can be monitored but no change claim can be made.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: Not applicable. There are no project instances; a single institutional value exists per wave and is carried forward in interim years. If the indicator is ported to other CGIAR centers, do not average center scores, since a mean of means misweights centers of different size: report each center separately, and pool the underlying responses and recompute only where the centers field the identical item set, scale and scoring rule.

B: Combination method. Computed and reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level by pooling individual responses within the survey wave under the Human Resources scoring rule; never rebuilt by averaging sub-group scores.

C: Levels and operations. The index is computed once, at institutional level, from its component items, and is never averaged across units, functions or years: a mean of index scores is not an index, because the components carry different item counts and response bases beneath it. A view for any subgroup is recomputed from that subgroup's own responses. Also report: the component values with the score where the survey methodology produces them, the scale and range in force, the respondent count and response rate, and any component whose item set was incomplete.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: No. This outcome index does not combine arithmetically with output-level Workforce & talent indicators (staffing plan KPI-O52, Learning & Training academy completions KPI-O53); those connect through the Talent Management results chain, not through arithmetic, following the toolbox-wide default that results levels connect narratively and are never aggregated arithmetically.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: prevented by design; the survey issues one response per staff member per wave, and disaggregated figures (staff category, region) partition the same respondent pool and are never summed into the headline value. Vol. 11 · KPI-OC49 draws on another item block of the same wave; the two are never summed or presented as independent corroboration. The survey is addressed to every member of the in-scope population, so the index is an attempted census, not a sample estimate: no sampling error or coefficient-of-variation band is computed, and its error is non-response, governed by the response-rate floor and the response rate reported with every value.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion and exclusion: the survey population is all CIMMYT staff on an employment contract at the fielding date, internationally and nationally recruited alike, and every member of it is invited; a respondent counts toward the index where their response is scorable under the Human Resources scoring rule; staff who did not respond are excluded from the computation but their absence is captured in the response rate, which is reported alongside the index. A minimum response rate governs publication: the index is not published for a wave, nor for a disaggregation cell, whose response rate falls below the floor in force, and the floor applied is stated with the value. The floor is the one Human Resources declares for the wave before the survey is fielded, recorded with the series; a floor declared after fielding counts as no declared floor, and a wave published without a declared floor is reported as a value whose non-response bias is unbounded.
limitations: Contribution claim only. Engagement and inclusion respond to leadership, workload, compensation, restructuring, and the external labour market as much as to any specific talent-management action, so a movement in the index reflects overall staff experience, not the effect of one initiative.

Self-reported perception. The index measures what staff say about their experience at the moment of the survey. Survey timing, recent organizational events, and response mood shape the value; it is a sentiment measure, not an objective audit of working conditions.

Non-response bias. Participation is voluntary and anonymous, so the score represents respondents only. A low or uneven response rate across regions or staff categories can bias the value; the response rate is reported with the index for every wave, and restated with any carried-forward value.

An internal trend series, with no evidenced external benchmark. No published psychometric validation, comparison value at another CGIAR center or employer, or absolute level at which a score is good is evidenced for the index. It is interpretable only against CIMMYT's own earlier waves on an unchanged instrument, and is never presented as a benchmarked score.

Instrument stability governs comparability. Year-on-year comparison holds only while the item set, scale, and scoring are unchanged; any revision to the questionnaire breaks the series and must be flagged in reporting. Anonymity thresholds also suppress small sub-groups, limiting fine-grained comparison.

What a movement means. A rise means staff on average reported stronger engagement, belonging, and inclusion that year; it does not by itself mean turnover fell or that any programme worked. Pair with turnover and retention (KPI-OC54) and the recruitment and development indicators (KPI-O52, KPI-O53, KPI-OC51) for the Talent Management narrative. The staff collaboration score (Vol. 11 · KPI-OC49) is drawn from the same survey; the two indices are different cuts of one instrument and are never presented as independent corroboration.
subMetrics:
None reported as standalone KPIs. The composite draws on three item blocks measuring distinct dimensions of staff experience:

— Engagement: staff energy for and commitment to their work and the organization.

— Belonging: staff sense of being valued and part of the CIMMYT community.

— Inclusion: staff experience of fair treatment, voice, and recognition regardless of role or background.

These are internal dimensions of one index, not separately governed indicators, and none has its own KPI reference sheet. Dimension-level sub-scores are reported alongside the composite where the survey methodology produces them.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
Definitional anchor: CIMMYT's own convention, set out in this sheet's Definition and Calculation method: the composite draws on Human Resources' own survey methodology. No external methodological standard is evidenced for this measure; the index is built on an instrument Human Resources owns.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Corporate function: Human Resources (People and Culture); no project team exists for this indicator. Data collection: Human Resources, through the survey administration each wave. Validation: Human Resources analytics (response-rate and data-quality checks). Calculation: Human Resources, per its index methodology. Approval: Director of Human Resources. Reporting: Human Resources to senior management and to the CIMMYT MEAL unit for institutional reporting.

name: Annual staff turnover and retention rate
resultsLevel: Outcome
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Talent Management (institutional component). Serves both Talent Management 2030 objectives: "Top talent is retained and attracted for future proofing the achievement of our mission" and "An enabling, empowering, career growth environment develops and retains top talent"..
institutionalComponent: Talent Management (institutional component). Serves both Talent Management 2030 objectives: "Top talent is retained and attracted for future proofing the achievement of our mission" and "An enabling, empowering, career growth environment develops and retains top talent".
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. This indicator measures a property of CIMMYT as an employer, not a result delivered to an external population, so it does not map to any of the five CGIAR Impact Areas.
sdgTarget: None. No SDG indicator corresponds to an individual employer's internal turnover or retention rate (the SDG 8 decent-work indicators measure economy-wide employment, earnings, and labour rights, not organizational separation rates).
otherFrameworks: GRI 401: Employment 2016, disclosure 401-1 (new employee hires and employee turnover), the sustainability-reporting disclosure closest to this indicator.
definition: Measures the movement of staff out of CIMMYT over a reporting year, and the persistence of the staff who were in post at the start of it, as two separately calculated rates with different denominators. The separation rate is separations during the year over the average headcount over the year. Cohort retention is the share of the staff in post on the first day of the reporting year who are still in post on the last day, over the opening headcount. The two are reported together and neither is the other's complement: they run over different populations, because the separation rate's denominator absorbs staff hired during the year while the retention cohort is closed at the opening date. The register's definition describes retention as "the complementary share remaining"; that reading is not carried here, because a rate over an average headcount and a rate over a fixed opening cohort cannot be complements, and the sheet is the authority for the formula.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT is keeping its people, the core question of the Talent Management component of the 2030 Strategy: an organization that people choose to stay in is one where "top talent is retained and attracted for future proofing the achievement of our mission". CIMMYT tracks it because the strategy itself cites significantly declining turnover rates and high staff satisfaction as evidence of its employment environment, and because turnover and retention are standard human-capital measures that HR reports to leadership.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator: reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate HR systems, no project instance to adapt it to).
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Percentage of staff per year, two rates reported together on different bases: the separation rate over average headcount, and cohort retention over the opening headcount.
directionOfChange: Not directional. Falling turnover and rising retention generally signal a more stable and engaging workplace, in line with the strategy's declining-turnover ambition. But very low turnover can also mean stagnation and limited renewal, and some separations are healthy: contract completion, planned succession, performance management. It is interpreted against a band for the role mix, set by Human Resources and stated with the value, rather than pushed toward zero, and the two rates are reported together on their different bases.
disaggregationRequired: Sex (female / male at minimum, on CGIAR's sex-disaggregated data standards (Doss & Kieran, 2014)), because pooled rates cannot show whether women leave, or stay, at different rates than men; staff category (CIMMYT's own staff-category classification as Human Resources maintains it); separation type (voluntary vs involuntary), because a pooled rate cannot distinguish resignations from restructuring. Cells are published under CIMMYT's own Human Resources data-protection rules, and this sheet sets no disclosure floor of its own.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Separation sub-type (resignation vs end of contract; a cross-cut of the required voluntary/involuntary split, since an end of contract can fall on either side of it); contract type (open-ended vs fixed-term / grant-funded); region or duty station; tenure band; age band.
unitOfObservation: Individual (employee record). The reported value is a single organization-level rate computed from individual records.
calculationSummary: Two rates, each with its own numerator and its own denominator. Separation rate = (separation events during the reporting year / average headcount over the year) x 100. Average headcount = the mean of the twelve month-end headcounts. Cohort retention rate = (staff in post on the first day of the reporting year who are still in post on the last day / headcount on the first day of the reporting year) x 100. 100 minus the separation rate is not the cohort retention rate and neither rate may be derived from the other. A staff member hired in March and gone in October raises the separation rate and leaves cohort retention untouched; a staff member in post all year who is internally transferred affects neither. Both rates are published, with the denominator stated against each. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: CIMMYT Human Resources information system (personnel and payroll records) supplying headcount, hires, and separations at employee level. Fallback: None. There is no legitimate lower-resolution substitute: the rate can only be computed from CIMMYT's own administrative records. Not applicable: DS1 (surveys cannot establish who separated; self-report would duplicate what the HR system already records exactly), DS3 (geospatial and Earth observation data are irrelevant to a workforce measure), DS4 (no external database holds CIMMYT's internal staffing records), DS5 (citizen-generated data cannot produce an official staff figure).
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). No survey module or field instrument; the value is derived directly from HR system records.
collectionFrequency: Annual, computed from continuously maintained HR administrative records.
referencePeriod: The reporting year the value describes (the calendar year, register-wide).
baselineRequired: Yes: the strategy's declining-turnover ambition is a change claim, which needs a prior-year reference value. Where no baseline was set prospectively: reconstruct prior-year rates from retained HR records, which normally hold historical headcount and separation data. If no historical records are recoverable: monitoring only, no change claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: Not applicable. The indicator is computed once, at CIMMYT-institutional level, from corporate HR systems; project-level values do not exist, so there is nothing to pool and no Recommended/Fallback split to manage.

B: Combination method: two rates, each a ratio of sums. The separation rate and cohort retention rate are computed separately, each from its own numerator over its own denominator (the separation rate over average headcount, cohort retention over the opening headcount), and are reported together; neither is derived from the other and the two are never added.

C: Levels and operations. Both rates are recomputed at every level from their own numerator and denominator, never averaged from the levels beneath them: a mean of unit turnover rates weights a unit of six equally with one of six hundred. They are computed once, at institutional level, from corporate HR systems. Where a view by function, grade, duty station or sex is wanted, each rate is recomputed on its own terms: the separation rate from that subset's own separation events over that subset's own average headcount, and cohort retention from that subset's own opening-cohort staff still in post at year end over that subset's own opening headcount. Also report: both denominators the rates rest on (the subset's average headcount for the separation rate, the subset's opening headcount for cohort retention), the separation count and the opening-cohort count behind each, and any subset suppressed for small numbers, since one separation moves a rate over eleven staff by about nine points and one over eleven hundred by less than a tenth of a point.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: No. This outcome does not combine arithmetically with the Workforce & talent outputs (for example KPI-O53, staff completing Learning & Training academy development) or with the engagement and inclusion index (KPI-OC53) it contributes to; the levels connect through the Talent Management results narrative, not through addition.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: within the single institutional computation, de-duplicate headcount and separations by employee ID so that rehires and internal transfers are not counted twice; each distinct separation event counts once. Both rates are computed over every employee record in the population, a census of the domain: they carry no sampling error and no coefficient-of-variation band, and the denominators are reported instead.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion and exclusion: includes all staff on CIMMYT employment contracts during the reporting year, fixed-term and grant-funded appointees among them; excludes interns and consultants of any duration, who are not employees and whose contract endings would distort the rate. Contract type is carried as a disaggregation. A fixed-term or grant-funded contract renewed or converted without a break in service is not a separation; what counts as a break in service follows Human Resources' own convention. A contract that ends without renewal is a separation, classed involuntary unless the staff member declined an offered renewal, in which case it is voluntary.

Missing data: HR records are effectively complete for the fact of a separation; a separation with a missing reason still counts in the turnover numerator but is excluded from any voluntary/involuntary split. An ending whose record does not establish that a renewal was offered and declined is classed involuntary; the missing-reason exclusion applies to separations that are not contract endings. Where monthly headcount records do not exist for the full reporting year, average headcount is the mean of start-of-year and end-of-year headcount, and the separation rate is then flagged as computed on the start-and-end average, since a start-and-end average misstates it wherever headcount moved sharply mid-year. Cohort retention is unaffected, its denominator being the opening headcount.

Repeated observations: de-duplicate by employee ID so that a staff member rehired or internally transferred within the year is counted once in the headcount; each distinct separation event counts once. An opening-cohort member who separates and is rehired within the year is a separation and is not retained.
limitations: Attribution boundary: turnover responds to the external labour market, salary competitiveness, family and relocation decisions, and the grant-funding cycle (grant-funded posts end when grants end). CIMMYT's talent-management actions are one influence among several; a movement in the rate cannot be attributed to any single HR intervention.

Measurement error from the population definition: the rate is only as reliable as the rule for who counts as staff and how contract expiries are classified. The rule in Eligibility criteria and missing data classes each renewal and each contract ending, and year-to-year movements can be artefacts of counting if this rule is not applied consistently. Because an unrenewed contract is classed involuntary, that class mixes routine contract expiry with restructuring; it is read with the optional separation sub-type cut.

Comparability limits: comparisons across years, staff categories, or CGIAR centers are only valid under a constant population definition and denominator convention. A largely grant-funded research organization has structurally higher fixed-term turnover than an employer of mostly permanent staff; aligning definitions to GRI 401-1 improves external comparability.

The two rates can diverge, and that is not a contradiction. Because they run over different populations, a year of heavy recruitment followed by early departures raises the separation rate while cohort retention holds; in a year with no hiring the two move almost as complements, so a wide gap between them points to in-year hiring or to early exits of new hires. Read them together and never infer one from the other.

What a movement does and does not mean: a falling separation rate and rising cohort retention suggest a more stable and engaging workplace; they do not say why people stay or leave, and very low separation can signal limited renewal rather than health. Read alongside the staff engagement and inclusion index (KPI-OC53) for the interpretive narrative.
subMetrics:
Two separately calculated rates, each on its own denominator:

— Separation rate = (separation events during the year / average headcount over the year) x 100. Denominator: average headcount over the year.

— Cohort retention rate = (opening-cohort staff still in post at year end / headcount at the start of the year) x 100. Denominator: the opening headcount, a fixed cohort.

The two denominators differ and the two rates are not complements; neither is computed from the other, and both are published. Sex and staff category are disaggregations of both rates, not separate sub-metrics. Neither rate has its own KPI sheet; this sheet covers both.
referenceStandardsAndLinks:
Comparator disclosure: Global Reporting Initiative (2016), GRI 401: Employment 2016, disclosure 401-1 (new employee hires and employee turnover), accessed via the GRI Standards English-language library.

Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: CIMMYT Human Resources (HR information system). Validation: HR analytics / HRIS administrator. Calculation: CIMMYT Human Resources per the Calculation method above. Approval: Director of Human Resources. Reporting: HR to the CIMMYT MEAL unit for institutional Talent Management reporting.

name: Number of competitive proposals/consortia submitted as lead or named partner
resultsLevel: Output. Read from the indicator statement, as the Core's results-level test requires for an Institutional-branch indicator, what this count reports is a delivery by CIMMYT's resource-mobilization function, a proposal lodged with a funder: a delivered result, not a change, which is the Core's definition of an output. The outcome it feeds is the win rate, KPI-OC55. CIMMYT's institutional MEAL Framework places resource mobilization under Processes; the register keeps Output on this reading.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Resource Mobilization.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. The indicator measures a property of CIMMYT as an organization (its fundraising activity), an internal enabler of the mission rather than a result delivered to an external population. The five CGIAR Impact Areas measure results for the people and systems CGIAR centers serve; the resources this pipeline secures enable work across all of them, but that is an enabling link, not a direct mapping.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator corresponds to an individual organization's count of funding proposals submitted. The SDG 17 finance targets measure resource flows to developing countries at the country and system level, not one institution's bidding activity, so they are thematically adjacent only.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Institutional Funding & Resource Mobilization (IF&RM) 2023-24 Strategy, the CGIAR working document widely known by the "Towards $2 Billion" ambition it carries: the CIMMYT 2030 Strategy states this framework guided the development of its Resource Mobilization objectives (CIMMYT 2030 Strategy). It is a working strategy document, not an indicator framework, and defines no corresponding indicator; noted here for institutional alignment only, never as a settled system standard. No donor reporting framework uses this indicator or a close variant.
definition: Counts the competitive proposals or consortium bids that CIMMYT submits in the reporting year, either as the lead applicant or as a partner named in another organization's bid to a donor or investor. "Competitive" means the submission enters a selection process in which a funder chooses among competing applications, whether the call is open or restricted to invited applicants (requests for applications or proposals, competitive calls, tenders, competitive consortium windows). The value is a count of distinct submissions lodged with funders: it measures the volume of CIMMYT's resource-mobilization pipeline.
rationale: Answers how actively CIMMYT is pursuing the funding needed to deliver its strategy. The CIMMYT 2030 Strategy makes achieving its objectives conditional on the Center having the resources to implement them and sets Resource Mobilization objectives to expand the resource base and range of donors (CIMMYT 2030 Strategy, Resource Mobilization chapter). This indicator is the entry point of that results chain: submissions are the pipeline from which wins (KPI-OC55, the share of proposals won, which builds its denominator from this count) and mobilized income (KPI-OC56) follow. Tracked for institutional management and board-level reporting on resourcing effort, and to make pipeline volume visible and comparable year on year.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator). Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate records; there is no project instance to adapt it to.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Number of submissions (count of distinct competitive proposals or consortium bids lodged in the reporting year)
directionOfChange: Increase, as a measure of pipeline volume. A rising value means more competitive proposals or consortium bids were lodged. It is read alongside the win rate (KPI-OC55), since submitting more is not the same as winning more.
disaggregationRequired: CIMMYT role (lead applicant versus named partner), required on this sheet and not by the register, since Block C reports the split. The register requires no disaggregation for this indicator.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Funder type, in the six funder categories used across this pathway; traditional versus non-traditional funder; proposal value band. Under an Institutional indicator these are optional institutional cuts the resource-mobilization function may add.
unitOfObservation: The proposal submission, recorded under the Core's result object value.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct competitive proposals or consortium bids submitted to funders during the reporting year with CIMMYT as lead applicant or named partner. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): CIMMYT's corporate proposal-tracking or grants-management records, logging for each submission the funder, call, CIMMYT role (lead or named partner), consortium members, submission date, and status. The system that holds this record has not been identified by CIMMYT, so the sheet states the record the indicator requires rather than naming an application; where no such record is held, the fallback route below is what the indicator is reported from. Fallback DS2 (lower-resolution instance of the same code): program-, region-, or unit-level opportunity trackers consolidated manually, used where the corporate record is not held or is incomplete for all or part of the year; a value built this way must be flagged as fallback-sourced because de-duplication across units is weaker. Not applicable DS1 (Censuses & surveys): a submission is an administrative fact, not a respondent-reported condition; no survey feeds this indicator. Not applicable DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation): proposal activity cannot be observed remotely. Not applicable DS4 (Secondary & international databases): no third party publishes a comprehensive record of CIMMYT's submissions; individual funder portals see only their own calls. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): not relevant to an internal corporate record.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source. The indicator is compiled from existing DS2 proposal-tracking records, not collected with a DS1 or DS5 instrument.
collectionFrequency: Continuous administrative logging: each submission is recorded in the proposal-tracking records as it is lodged.
referencePeriod: The reporting year, which is the calendar year register-wide, in which the submission was lodged with the funder.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual institutional count; the previous year's value is the reference for trend. Where a multi-year trend is wanted, the first year with a complete corporate submission record serves as the reference year.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable. This is an Institutional indicator drawn once from corporate records; there are no project-level instances to pool. Any portion of the year that had to rely on fallback unit trackers is noted alongside the figure rather than blended silently.

B: Combination method. Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level: distinct submissions are summed across programs, regions, and units after de-duplication by proposal record; never averaged.

C: Levels and operations. Computed once, at institutional level, as the count of distinct competitive proposals or consortia submitted as lead or partner in the reporting year, de-duplicated on the proposal identifier per Block E. There is no level beneath it, because no programme or unit holds a share of an institutional count. Where a view by unit, region or funder type is wanted, it is recomputed from that subset's own records, never taken as a share of the institutional figure. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels. Also report: the split between lead and partner roles, since they are different commitments; the number excluded under Eligibility; the count of first-stage expressions of interest screened out before invitation, which is the sub-metric in Section 5 and is never added to this count; and that the outcome of these submissions is KPI-OC55 and is never combined with this count.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no, the default holds. This output connects to the outcomes it feeds (KPI-OC55 win rate, KPI-OC56 funds mobilized) through the Resource Mobilization results chain as a narrative, not through addition. One arithmetic dependency must be respected: this count is the base of KPI-OC55's denominator, which sets aside withdrawn and undecided proposals, so both indicators must apply identical inclusion, exclusion, and de-duplication rules; that is a ratio construction between two indicators, not aggregation of one.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: one submission is counted once even when several CIMMYT programs, units, or country offices contributed to it, matched on a unique proposal identifier in the system of record; related bids count separately only if the funder processes them as separate entries. If unit-level trackers cannot be de-duplicated against the corporate record, the reported figure is labelled an upper estimate. Overlap with other register indicators: none counts the same event; submissions that are later won reappear in KPI-OC55's numerator and, once their agreements are signed, in KPI-OC56's income, by design, as progression along the chain, not double counting.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion and exclusion: includes every submission into a competitive selection process, whether CIMMYT leads the bid or is named as a partner in another organization's bid, counted in the year the submission is lodged with the funder. Exclusions: non-competitive negotiated agreements and sole-source renewals; pooled-fund allocations made without competing applications (a pooled-funded call in which centres or teams compete counts); internal concepts never lodged with a funder; and appearances in another organization's bid without a defined budget share in that bid, since a named role with no budget line is a letter of support. Staged competitions: a staged process counts once, at the full-proposal stage, and only where CIMMYT was invited to submit the full proposal; a first-stage expression of interest or concept note screened out before invitation does not enter this count and is reported instead as the sub-metric in Section 5. Both rules are KPI-OC55's, applied here unchanged: this count is the base of that indicator's denominator, which removes only proposals withdrawn before a decision or still undecided, and a rate whose numerator and denominator are drawn on different rules is not a rate.

Missing data: a submission discovered outside the system of record is entered into it with its lodging evidence, then counted, and the figure restated with a note; nothing is imputed, because a submission is an administrative fact that must be evidenced.

Repeated observations: each distinct submission counts once. The identifier is one per submission event: proposal × funder × call round. Revisions lodged in the same round before the funder decides, or in negotiation after selection, count once, in the year the first full proposal was lodged. The same or an adapted proposal lodged with another funder or call, or with a later round after being declined, is a new submission in the year it is lodged. A single consortium bid involving several CIMMYT programs or offices counts once.
limitations: Volume is not quality: a rising count can mean broader, well-targeted ambition or untargeted bidding that consumes staff time on weak opportunities. Judge pipeline performance only together with the win rate (KPI-OC55) and income mobilized (KPI-OC56), never from this count alone.

Completeness depends on central capture: the 2030 Strategy describes resource mobilization at CIMMYT as a decentralized process involving staff across programs, regions, and units, so submissions logged only in local trackers, or not logged at all, undercount the pipeline. The reported figure is only as complete as the corporate system of record.
Counting rules drive comparability: any change is noted, the series restated, and the same change carried to KPI-OC55 in the same pass.

Submissions are not equivalent units: a small consortium proposal in which CIMMYT holds a minor budget share and a flagship multi-year bid led by CIMMYT each count as one. The headline count says nothing about the value, effort, or strategic weight of what was submitted; the optional role and value-band cuts carry that reading.

A movement in this value means CIMMYT lodged more or fewer competitive bids, nothing more: submitting is CIMMYT's own act, so the count evidences the organization's own pipeline activity, not funder response, competitiveness, or resourcing achieved, which the downstream outcome indicators measure.
subMetrics:
One sub-metric, derived from the same submission records and needing no reference sheet of its own:

— First-stage submissions screened out before invitation. Formula: count of expressions of interest and concept notes lodged with a funder in the reporting year that were not invited to the full-proposal stage, counted in the lodging year once the screening decision is known; those whose decision is not yet known are reported as pending. The staged-competition rule places these outside the headline count, so without this figure a center that writes many first-stage submissions and is screened out of most of them is indistinguishable from one that writes few, and fundraising effort is omitted from the only indicator that counts it. Reported alongside the headline count and never added to it; it does not enter KPI-OC55's denominator either, which is what keeps a screening-out from reading as a loss.

The optional cuts (CIMMYT role, funder type, value band) are disaggregations of the headline count, not separately calculated metrics. The share of these submissions that is won is a separate indicator with its own reference sheet, KPI-OC55, which builds its denominator from this count.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: the CIMMYT resource-mobilization / business-development function (logging each submission in the corporate record). Validation: the same function's management, checking completeness against program and regional trackers. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (de-duplication and the annual count per the Calculation method). Approval: head of the resource-mobilization function. Reporting: resource-mobilization function to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
