name: Number of structured donor engagement, learning, or networking events convened
resultsLevel: Output. Read from the indicator statement, as the Core's results-level test requires for an Institutional-branch indicator, what this count reports is events CIMMYT convened: a delivered result, not a change, which is the Core's definition of an output. The outcome it feeds is donor retention, KPI-OC58.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Resource Mobilization. The register carries no PO1-PO5 mapping for this indicator, which is correct: Institutional indicators map to one of the five enabler components rather than to the mission objectives. Within the component, the indicator sits under the 2030 objective "Donor relations at all levels are deepened"..
institutionalComponent: Resource Mobilization. The register carries no PO1-PO5 mapping for this indicator, which is correct: Institutional indicators map to one of the five enabler components rather than to the mission objectives. Within the component, the indicator sits under the 2030 objective "Donor relations at all levels are deepened".
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. The indicator measures a property of CIMMYT as an organization (its investment in donor relations), an internal enabler rather than a result delivered to an external population.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator counts an organization's own donor or partner engagement events; the Goal 17 partnership indicators measure country-level cooperation frameworks and financial commitments, not institutional convening activity.
otherFrameworks: The CIMMYT 2030 Strategy states that its Resource Mobilization objectives were developed under the framework of the CGIAR Institutional Funding & Resource Mobilization (IF&RM) 2023-24 Strategy, the working document widely known by the "Towards $2 Billion" ambition it carries. No donor or reporting framework carries a corresponding indicator: the count is defined on CIMMYT's own authority.
definition: Counts the structured donor engagement, learning or networking events CIMMYT convenes in the reporting year. An event counts when it is a distinct, organized occasion, with a stated purpose, an agenda, an invited external audience and a documented record, that brings CIMMYT together with donors, partners or alumni for engagement, shared learning or networking, whether held in person, virtually or in hybrid form. The value is a count of distinct events, not of sessions, participants or organizations reached.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT is actively investing in its donor relationships, rather than only transacting with funders grant by grant. The CIMMYT 2030 Strategy commits, under its Resource Mobilization objective "Donor relations at all levels are deepened", to engage donors and partners in continuous improvement and shared learning and to invest in better networking its donors, partners and alumni to share learnings and successes and build a community around CIMMYT's vision. This indicator makes that convening effort visible and countable year on year. It is an effort measure: the relationship result it works toward, donors choosing to fund CIMMYT again, is measured separately by the donor retention rate (KPI-OC58), to which this output contributes.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator). Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate records; there is no project instance to adapt it to.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Number of events (count of distinct events per reporting year)
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means CIMMYT convened more qualifying events; it measures convening effort, not relationship quality, which is read from donor retention (KPI-OC58).
disaggregationRequired: Partner or institution type of the event's audience, per the register, in the six funder categories used across this pathway: multilateral, bilateral public, foundation or philanthropy, private sector, CGIAR pooled fund, and other, derived from the confirmed 13-category partner and institution list. An event is tagged by its primary intended audience, and one with no single primary audience is tagged mixed, a seventh category beside the six. Event type (donor engagement, learning exchange, networking), required on this sheet and not by the register, since Block C reports the split.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Format (in person, virtual, hybrid); region or duty station convening the event; new versus existing donor audience, which links this count to the strategy's objective of expanding the donor base. Under an Institutional indicator these are optional institutional cuts the responsible function may add.
unitOfObservation: The event. The event is the counting unit, recorded under the Core's result object value, whose definition names a convened event; it is not forced into "organization".
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct structured donor engagement, learning or networking events convened by CIMMYT during the reporting year with donors, partners or alumni among the external participants. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative & registry data): a central event record held by the CIMMYT function responsible for resource mobilization and donor relations, capturing each event's title, date, format, purpose, audience type and evidence (invitation, agenda, participant list). The system that holds this record has not been identified by CIMMYT, so the sheet states the record the indicator requires rather than naming an application; where no such record is held, the fallback route below is what the indicator is reported from. Fallback DS2 (lower-resolution instance of the same code): unit-level calendars, communications records and event documentation held by programs and regional offices, used to reconstruct the count where no central record exists for part of the year; a value assembled this way is flagged as fallback-sourced because de-duplication and evidence are weaker. Not applicable DS1 (Censuses & surveys): convening an event is a documented administrative fact, not a condition reported by survey respondents. Not applicable DS3 (Geospatial & Earth observation): events cannot be observed from satellite or geographic data. Not applicable DS4 (Secondary & international databases): no third party maintains a record of CIMMYT's donor events. Not applicable DS5 (Citizen-generated & other non-traditional data): social media or crowdsourced mentions may evidence that an event happened but cannot serve as the count, since they are incomplete and cannot apply the structured-event boundary.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source. The indicator is compiled from existing DS2 event records, not collected with a DS1 or DS5 instrument. A standard event-record entry (title, date, format, purpose, audience type, convening unit, evidence reference) should nonetheless be defined so records are comparable across units.
collectionFrequency: Continuous administrative logging: each event is recorded as it is held, with its date, purpose, audience type and evidence reference.
referencePeriod: The reporting year, which is the calendar year register-wide, in which the event took place; a multi-day event is assigned to the year of its start date.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual institutional count; the previous year's value is the reference for trend. Where a multi-year trend is wanted, the first year with a complete central event record serves as the reference year, since earlier reconstructed years are not comparable in coverage.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable; this is an Institutional indicator drawn once from corporate records, so there are no project-level instances to pool. Any portion of the count reconstructed from fallback unit-level records is noted alongside the figure rather than blended silently.

B: Combination method. Reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level: events are summed across programs, regional offices and units after de-duplication; never averaged.

C: Levels and operations. Computed once, at institutional level, as the count of distinct structured donor engagement, learning or networking events held in the reporting year, de-duplicated on the event identifier per Block E. There is no level beneath it, because no programme or unit holds a share of an institutional count. Where a view by unit, region or funder type is wanted, it is recomputed from that subset's own records, never taken as a share of the institutional figure. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels. Also report: the split by event type, the number of distinct funders engaged, which is a different count and is not this one, and the number excluded under Eligibility.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count does not combine arithmetically with the donor retention rate (KPI-OC58), which is a percentage at outcome level; the two connect through the Resource Mobilization results chain as a narrative (CIMMYT convenes engagement spaces, donor relations deepen, donors return), not through addition.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: this is the main technical risk, because the strategy describes resource mobilization at CIMMYT as a decentralized process running across programs, regions and units, so one event can plausibly be logged by several units. De-duplicate on the event record (title, date, venue or platform) before forming the institutional count; an event co-convened by two CIMMYT units counts once, and an event co-convened with an external partner or another CGIAR center counts once for CIMMYT with the co-convener noted. Sessions of one series are not counted as separate events. If de-duplication cannot be completed, label the reported count an upper estimate.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData: Inclusion and exclusion: includes events CIMMYT organizes or co-organizes that meet all four tests in the Definition: a stated engagement, learning or networking purpose, an agenda, an invited external audience and a documented record (invitation or participant list); an event lacking any one is not counted. CIMMYT organizes or co-organizes an event when it initiated it or set or co-set its agenda, documented in the invitation or agenda. An event need not include a funder: learning and networking events with partners or alumni alone count. Examples are donor days, funder roundtables, learning exchanges on grant or delivery-partner management, and alumni network gatherings. Excludes routine meetings required under an individual grant (progress reviews, negotiations, audits); meetings between CIMMYT and a single external organization, whatever their agenda; internal CIMMYT events with no external audience; scientific conferences whose purpose is research dissemination rather than donor relations; events whose primary purpose, as stated in the invitation or agenda, is policy dialogue or advisory engagement with decision-makers (Vol. 10 · KPI-O37) or training (the capacity indicators), even where donors attend; and attending, presenting at or sponsoring another organization's event, which is not convening. An event whose stated purpose is engaging, learning with or networking donors, partners or alumni is counted here and not under KPI-O37 or the capacity indicators.
limitations: Effort, not results: the count evidences that CIMMYT created engagement and learning spaces, not that donor relations deepened or that funding followed. The relationship result is measured by the donor retention rate (KPI-OC58) and income indicators elsewhere in this pathway; never present this count as evidence of mobilized resources.

All events weigh the same: a two-hour virtual roundtable and a multi-day global donor conference each count once, so the headline number says nothing about scale, attendance or quality. Read it with the audience-type and event-type disaggregations, and with attendance context where the event record carries it.

The boundary sets the number: the value depends directly on where "structured event" ends and routine grant-cycle meetings begin, and on the series rule. Values are comparable across years only if the same boundary and series conventions are applied; a rule change must be flagged in reporting, since it can move the count more than any real change in convening activity.

Decentralized recording biases the count in both directions: because many units convene donor-facing events, an incomplete central record undercounts, while unreconciled unit records double count. Until a single event record with a standard entry exists, treat year-on-year movements with caution.

A rise means CIMMYT convened more qualifying events; it does not mean donor engagement improved, and a fall may reflect deliberate consolidation into fewer, larger events rather than disinvestment in donor relations.
subMetrics: None. The audience-type, event-type and format breakdowns are cuts of the same count, not separately calculated metrics. Related measures that are deliberately not this indicator: the number of participants or organizations reached per event (a volume measure the event record can carry as context) and the donor retention rate (KPI-OC58, the outcome this output feeds, with its own reference sheet).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: the CIMMYT corporate function responsible for resource mobilization and donor relations (event logging with evidence). Validation: the same function's lead, checking the structured-event boundary and de-duplication. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (de-duplicated annual count per the Calculation method). Approval: head of the resource mobilization function. Reporting: the resource mobilization function to the CIMMYT MEAL unit.
sourceRef: Volume 13 · Resource mobilization & donor relations — Reference sheet KPI-O55

name: Number of joint fundraising initiatives undertaken with partners
resultsLevel: Output. Read from the indicator statement, as the Core's results-level test requires for an Institutional-branch indicator, what this count reports is joint fundraising initiatives CIMMYT undertook with partners: a delivered result, not a change, which is the Core's definition of an output. The outcome it feeds is new grant income, KPI-OC56.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Resource Mobilization (institutional enabler component). Institutional indicators map to one of the five enabler components rather than to PO1 to PO5; the register carries no primary objective for this row, consistent with that status. Within the component, the indicator measures Resource Mobilization objective 3.3, "Engage in joint fundraising with partners to attract more science-oriented funders with longer term impact horizons" (CIMMYT 2030 Strategy)..
institutionalComponent: Resource Mobilization (institutional enabler component). Institutional indicators map to one of the five enabler components rather than to PO1 to PO5; the register carries no primary objective for this row, consistent with that status. Within the component, the indicator measures Resource Mobilization objective 3.3, "Engage in joint fundraising with partners to attract more science-oriented funders with longer term impact horizons" (CIMMYT 2030 Strategy).
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. Measures CIMMYT's own resourcing practice, not a result delivered in any of the five official Impact Areas; funds mobilized ultimately resource mission work across all of them, but that is an enabling link, not a direct one.
sdgTarget: None. No official SDG indicator corresponds to a count of joint fundraising initiatives. The nearest partnership target, SDG 17.17, is monitored by indicator 17.17.1, the amount in United States dollars committed to public-private partnerships for infrastructure (custodian: World Bank): a financial-commitment measure for infrastructure PPPs, not collaborative fundraising by a research organization, so None is recorded rather than an unsupported mapping.
otherFrameworks: Neither the CGIAR Technical Reporting Arrangement 2025-30 nor the 32 CRF standard indicators in Claus, Davel & Belcher (2023) contains a fundraising or resource-mobilization indicator. The CGIAR Institutional Funding & Resource Mobilization (IF&RM) 2023-24 Strategy, the working document widely known by the "Towards $2 Billion" ambition it carries and which the CIMMYT 2030 Strategy says guided its Resource Mobilization objectives, is a strategy document, not an indicator framework.
definition: Counts the distinct joint fundraising initiatives CIMMYT undertakes with one or more partner organizations during the reporting year. A joint fundraising initiative is a discrete, documented resource-mobilization effort that CIMMYT and at least one external partner organization plan and pursue together toward an identified funder or funding opportunity: co-developing a funding concept or consortium bid, jointly approaching a donor or investor, or co-organizing a funding campaign.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT is putting its joint-fundraising commitment into practice: the 2030 Strategy commits the Center to work more closely with its partners in fundraising and mutual learning and, under its Resource Mobilization objectives, to "engage in joint fundraising with partners to attract more science-oriented funders with longer term impact horizons". It serves institutional Resource Mobilization reporting and sits upstream of the headline funds-mobilized result (KPI-OC56): joint initiatives are one route through which new grant income is expected to arrive.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator). No project instantiates this indicator; joint fundraising is a CIMMYT-institutional activity recorded in CIMMYT's own resource-mobilization systems.
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Number of initiatives (count of distinct joint fundraising initiatives active in the reporting year).
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more joint fundraising initiatives were undertaken with partners. It signals more collaborative fundraising practice, not more income.
disaggregationRequired: None is required by the register; two are required on this sheet and not by the register. (1) Partner or institution type, in the six funder categories used across this pathway: multilateral, bilateral public, foundation or philanthropy, private sector, CGIAR pooled fund, and other, derived from the confirmed 13-category partner and institution list, an initiative with partners of several types being classified by its lead partner or, where no partner leads, as mixed, a seventh category beside the six; (2) initiative status in the year (newly launched versus continuing), so growth is distinguishable from carry-over. Sex and age do not apply: the unit is an initiative, not a person.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator; no project layer).
unitOfObservation: The joint fundraising initiative. The initiative is the counting unit, recorded under the Core's result object value, which covers any countable thing that is not a person, a place, a post or a body; it is not forced into "organization".
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct joint fundraising initiatives meeting every inclusion criterion below and active at any point in the reporting year. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2 (Administrative and registry data): a consolidated initiative register kept by the resource-mobilization and business development function from CIMMYT's donor pipeline, proposal development and partnership records, supplying partners, target funder or opportunity, dates, and status (internal systems, no external URL). The system that holds this record has not been identified by CIMMYT, so the sheet states the record the indicator requires rather than naming an application; where no such record is held, the fallback route below is what the indicator is reported from. Fallback DS2 (same code, lower-confidence route): where no consolidated initiative register exists, reconstruct from consortium proposal records (the joint submissions counted under KPI-O54), teaming agreements, and donor correspondence; flag any such value as fallback-sourced, since it captures mainly initiatives that reached a submission and undercounts earlier-stage joint efforts. Not applicable: DS1 (Censuses and surveys), DS3 (Geospatial and Earth observation), DS4 (Secondary and international databases), DS5 (Citizen-generated and other non-traditional data): a joint initiative is a documented fact in CIMMYT's own records; it cannot be surveyed, observed from satellites, or crowdsourced, and no third party publishes CIMMYT's fundraising activity.
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). The recommended source is a DS2 administrative register; the operation is a query with the inclusion and exclusion filters applied, followed by review of records with missing or ambiguous attributes.
collectionFrequency: Continuous. Initiative records are created and updated in CIMMYT's resource-mobilization systems as efforts start, progress, and close; the indicator is extracted once per reporting year, more often if needed without additional collection.
referencePeriod: The reporting year, which is the calendar year register-wide: an initiative counts if it is active, as Eligibility criteria and missing data defines it, at any point in that year, whether launched in the year or continuing from an earlier one. A stock-with-flow measure, not a snapshot on a single date.
baselineRequired: No. This is an annual institutional count, and the previous year's value is the reference for trend, as on KPI-O54 and KPI-O55. Because the indicator is newly proposed, the first year extracted under this definition is the reference year; earlier years may be reconstructed from consortium proposal records and teaming agreements, stating the first year producible under identical criteria and labelling the reconstructed series a likely undercount, since early-stage efforts are poorly archived. Where no comparable earlier year can be produced, the series carries no change claim until a second year exists.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable. Institutional indicator reported once at CIMMYT-institutional level; there are no project instances to pool. For portability across CGIAR centers, do not sum center-level counts without de-duplication: a joint initiative between two centers would otherwise be counted twice.

B: Combination method. Sum: the count of distinct qualifying joint fundraising initiatives in the reporting year, de-duplicated on the initiative identifier. Never averaged.

C: Levels and operations. Computed once, at institutional level, as the count of distinct joint fundraising initiatives undertaken with partners in the reporting year, de-duplicated on the initiative identifier per Block E. There is no level beneath it, because no programme or unit holds a share of an institutional count. Where a view by unit, region or funder type is wanted, it is recomputed from that subset's own records, never taken as a share of the institutional figure. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels. Also report: the partner type on each initiative, the number with at least one submission in the year (the second sub-metric), whose submissions are counted in KPI-O54 and are not netted into this count, and the number excluded under Eligibility.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. Never summed with the funds-mobilized outcome KPI-OC56 it contributes to or any other value in the pathway; the link is narrative, since joint initiatives are one route through which new grant income arrives and only some of that income will trace back to initiatives counted here.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting: de-duplicate by initiative identifier; amendments, phases, and repeated funder approaches within one initiative are one initiative. Overlap named explicitly: a consortium proposal developed under an initiative also appears in KPI-O54 as a submission, and a donor event held under one also appears in KPI-O55 as an event; the three indicators answer different questions and must never be summed into a combined activity figure.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion criteria: at least one external partner organization is jointly involved in planning or executing the effort; the effort targets an identified funder, funding instrument, or opportunity; and there is joint planning or joint pursuit documented before submission, meaning a record of shared design, division of work or a partnering agreement (joint concept note, co-signed funder approach, consortium or teaming agreement, or equivalent record) made as the effort was formed rather than assembled after a proposal went in. An effort that never reaches a submission qualifies on the same evidence, the record being dated before the call closed or the effort was dropped. Exclusion criteria: fundraising efforts CIMMYT pursues alone; routine donor reporting or relationship maintenance carrying no funding ask; arrangements where a partner is merely named in a CIMMYT-written proposal without joint planning; donor engagement or networking events (counted under KPI-O55 even when held for an initiative counted here); proposal submissions as such (counted under KPI-O54; one initiative may generate several); and efforts whose only partner is the targeted funder itself.

Missing data: an initiative record missing a disaggregation attribute is counted in the headline total and excluded from that breakdown, with the number of incomplete records reported alongside; an undocumented effort is not counted; documentation assembled after a proposal was submitted is treated as undocumented for the timing test; no imputation.

Repeated observations: each initiative counts once per reporting year regardless of the meetings, documents, submissions, or partners involved (several partners still one count); a multi-year joint effort is one initiative, counted in each year it is active, so annual values must never be summed across years. An initiative is active in a year in which at least one documented joint fundraising action occurs: a joint-planning record of the kinds Inclusion names (a joint concept note, a co-signed funder approach, a consortium or teaming agreement), a joint proposal drafted or submitted, or a joint meeting with the funder on the ask. It opens on the date of its first joint-planning record, which dates it as newly launched, and closes on the funder's final decision on its last submission or on a documented decision to stop. Implementing an award is not fundraising; a later joint approach for a further phase reopens the same initiative.
limitations: Counts effort, not success. An initiative says nothing about whether funds were raised, how much, or on what terms; read with the proposal win rate (KPI-OC55) and new grant income (KPI-OC56) before any statement about resource-mobilization performance.

No external standard defines a "joint fundraising initiative", so the boundary rules in this sheet are CIMMYT's own. The value is not comparable with other organizations' figures, and cross-center comparison requires a shared granularity rule (what counts as one initiative).

Recording completeness sets the ceiling on accuracy. Early-stage joint efforts are often recorded only in meetings and correspondence, so the count is biased downward, and a jump between years may record better registry discipline rather than more collaborative fundraising.

The count is sensitive to packaging: one broad joint effort can be recorded as one initiative or several. The sheet's rule is Block E's, under which amendments, phases and repeated funder approaches within one effort are one initiative; applied unchanged it keeps the series comparable, and the distinct-partner sub-metric shows whether a rise comes from a broader partner base.

A rise means CIMMYT is doing more of the collaborative fundraising its 2030 Strategy commits it to; it does not mean donor relations improved or income grew, and it supports no claim about partners' own fundraising capacity.
subMetrics:
Two sub-metrics, both derived from the same initiative records and neither requiring its own reference sheet:

— Distinct partner organizations engaged in joint fundraising. Formula: count of unique partner organization identifiers across all initiatives in the headline total. Distinguishes a rise driven by many initiatives with the same partner from a rise driven by a broader partner base.

— Initiatives generating at least one proposal submission in the year. Formula: count of initiatives in the headline total linked to one or more submissions counted under KPI-O54 in the same year. Shows how much joint-fundraising effort converts into the proposal pipeline, without double counting either indicator.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: the resource-mobilization and business development function, as custodian of the donor pipeline, proposal, and partnership records. Validation: that function's leadership, confirming each counted record meets the inclusion criteria. Calculation: CIMMYT MEAL unit (criteria, de-duplication, disaggregations). Approval: the senior manager accountable for the Resource Mobilization component. Reporting: CIMMYT MEAL unit into institutional reporting.

name: Percentage of competitive requests for applications (RFAs) / grants / consortia / proposals won as lead or named co-developer
resultsLevel: Outcome. Read from the indicator statement, as the Core's results-level test requires for an Institutional-branch indicator, what this rate reports is funders' decisions to select CIMMYT's proposals: a change in behaviour among CIMMYT's partners, not a delivery by CIMMYT, which is the Core's definition of an outcome. The output it is formed on is the submission count, KPI-O54.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Resource Mobilization (institutional component). Primarily serves the component objective "CIMMYT's resource base and range of donors is expanded"; the second component objective, "Donor relations at all levels are deepened", is also reflected in this rate when repeat funders choose CIMMYT again. This indicator measures the resourcing of CIMMYT the organization, not the finance CIMMYT leverages into agrifood systems for beneficiaries, which is a separate mission-level indicator (Vol. 10 · KPI-I16)..
institutionalComponent: Resource Mobilization (institutional component). Primarily serves the component objective "CIMMYT's resource base and range of donors is expanded"; the second component objective, "Donor relations at all levels are deepened", is also reflected in this rate when repeat funders choose CIMMYT again. This indicator measures the resourcing of CIMMYT the organization, not the finance CIMMYT leverages into agrifood systems for beneficiaries, which is a separate mission-level indicator (Vol. 10 · KPI-I16).
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. This indicator measures a property of CIMMYT's own fundraising performance, not a result delivered to an external population, so it does not map to any of the five CGIAR Impact Areas.
sdgTarget: None. No SDG indicator measures an individual organization's proposal success rate; the SDG 17 finance indicators track resource flows to developing countries at country level, not any single organization's fundraising pipeline.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Institutional Funding & Resource Mobilization (IF&RM) 2023-24 Strategy, the CGIAR working document widely known by the "Towards $2 Billion" ambition it carries: the framework that, as the CIMMYT 2030 Strategy itself states, guided the development of CIMMYT's Resource Mobilization objectives. It defines no corresponding indicator; the win rate is defined here on CIMMYT's own convention.
definition: Measures the share of competitive funding proposals (requests for applications, grant calls, consortium bids) won by CIMMYT as lead applicant or named co-developer. Numerator: proposals won; denominator: the proposals KPI-O54 counts for the cohort year, less those withdrawn before a decision and those still undecided. This is the proposal win rate. "Competitive" means the submission enters a selection process in which a funder chooses among competing applications, whether the call is open or restricted to invited applicants (requests for applications or proposals, competitive calls, tenders, competitive consortium windows), as opposed to bilaterally negotiated or sole-source funding.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT's proposals convert into funding when CIMMYT competes. The 2030 Strategy's Resource Mobilization component aims for a resource base and range of donors that is expanded, and winning competitive processes is how that expansion happens. The win rate complements submission volume (KPI-O54) and income mobilized (KPI-OC56): together they show whether funding growth comes from bidding more, winning more often, or both, which leadership and the resource mobilization function need in order to steer bidding strategy.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator: computed once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate proposal pipeline records, no project instance to adapt it to).
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Percentage of decided competitive proposals (0 to 100).
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of CIMMYT's competitive bids succeed. The rate can also rise when the organization bids less ambitiously, so it is interpreted jointly with submission volume (KPI-O54).
disaggregationRequired: None required by the register.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Role (lead vs named co-developer); funder type, in the six funder categories used across this pathway; funding instrument (request for applications, grant call, consortium bid); requested budget band; research-for-development domain.
unitOfObservation: The proposal submission and the funder's decision on it, recorded under the Core's result object value.
calculationSummary: Value = (proposals won / proposals decided) x 100, computed on a defined cohort. Numerator: competitive proposals with CIMMYT as lead or named co-developer for which the funder issued written notice that the proposal is selected for funding, including selection subject to negotiation, CIMMYT retaining a defined budget share in the funded proposal; a proposal funded at reduced budget or scope counts as won, since the competitive decision went CIMMYT's way and the amount belongs to KPI-OC56, and a selected proposal rescinded or failed in negotiation before signature stays won and never enters KPI-OC56. Denominator: competitive proposals submitted in the cohort as counted by KPI-O54, on the inclusion, exclusion and de-duplication rules stated here, which that sheet applies unchanged, less proposals withdrawn before a decision and proposals still pending, which this sheet alone removes. Cohort convention: the submission-year cohort once its decisions are known, so that each year's submissions are tracked to their outcomes rather than mixing decisions from different years. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: CIMMYT's proposal pipeline and grants administrative records (submission logs, proposal tracking system, funder award and rejection notifications), maintained by the resource mobilization function. The system that holds this record has not been identified by CIMMYT, so the sheet states the record the indicator requires rather than naming an application. Fallback: None. There is no legitimate lower-resolution substitute: only CIMMYT's own records hold the full universe of its submissions. Not applicable: DS1 (a survey cannot establish award outcomes that the organization's own records document exactly), DS3 (geospatial and Earth observation data are irrelevant to a fundraising measure), DS4 (public donor and award databases record winners but not the universe of submissions, so the denominator cannot be built from them; at most they cross-check individual awards in the numerator), DS5 (citizen-generated data cannot produce an official record of CIMMYT's proposals).
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). No survey module or field instrument; the value is derived directly from pipeline records.
collectionFrequency: Continuous logging of submissions and decisions in the proposal pipeline records; the rate is computed annually per cohort.
reportingFrequency: Annual, into institutional Resource Mobilization reporting, stating the cohort year. Because award decisions lag submissions, the most recent closed cohort is reported as final; later cohorts are reported as provisional, with their pending count.
referencePeriod: The submission cohort year, a reporting year, which is the calendar year register-wide: the value describes the proposals submitted in one reporting year, assessed against the award decisions those proposals received.
baselineRequired: Yes for any change claim: statements that CIMMYT's conversion is improving need a prior-cohort reference value. Where no baseline was set prospectively: reconstruct prior-year rates from retained pipeline and grants records, which normally hold historical submissions and outcomes. If historical records cannot support a reconstructed rate: monitoring only, no change claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One reporting year and one defined proposal cohort, on the submission date. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable. There are no project instances to pool: the value is computed once from corporate pipeline records, and a proposal is not a project instance.

B: Combination method. A ratio of counts, formed once: proposals won over proposals decided in the cohort. Never an average of per-unit win rates.

C: Levels and operations. The share is computed once, at institutional level, over the decided proposals of the defined cohort, and is recomputed from its own numerator and denominator wherever a narrower view is wanted, never averaged from the views beneath it, since the units beneath it differ in size. There is no level beneath the institution here, because a proposal is one record in the denominator, not a reporting level. The denominator is a portfolio of records rather than a population measured in the field, so the measurement levels do not apply and every breakdown is a reporting view. Also report: the denominator itself, the cohort size, the number still pending at the reporting date, which the denominator excludes, the number of calls with more than one CIMMYT bid, and the cohort's definition.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. The denominator comes from KPI-O54 by construction, but the rate is never added to or combined with any output or outcome value; the levels connect through the resource-mobilization chain, not through arithmetic. Awards counted as won here enter KPI-OC56 only when their agreements are signed, in the signature year; a rate and a USD amount are never combined.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: de-duplicate on the proposal identifier so each distinct submission and each distinct award counts once; a multi-stage application counts once, and a bid involving several CIMMYT programmes counts once institutionally. The rate is reported only for a cohort whose submissions the pipeline record holds in full. Where it does not, including any year in which KPI-O54's count relies on fallback unit trackers, the rate is not reported for that cohort and the gap is stated in its place.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Missing data: proposals with no decision by the computation cutoff remain pending and are excluded until decided or until the cohort closes, then counted in their submission cohort. A cohort closes 24 months after the end of its submission year. A proposal with no funder decision when its cohort closes is recorded as decided and not won. A proposal whose call the funder cancels, or closes for all applicants without a decision, counts as withdrawn before a decision.

Repeated observations: each distinct submission counts once. The identifier is one per submission event: proposal × funder × call round. Revisions lodged in the same round before the funder decides, or in negotiation after selection, count once, in the year the first full proposal was lodged. The same or an adapted proposal lodged with another funder or call, or with a later round after being declined, is a new submission in the year it is lodged. A two-stage application counts once, at the full-proposal stage, and only where CIMMYT was invited to submit the full proposal; an expression of interest screened out at stage one is not a loss.
limitations: Attribution boundary: the win rate reflects donor budget cycles, the number and strength of competitors per call, and how well the year's calls happened to fit CIMMYT's portfolio, alongside proposal quality. A falling rate can mean stronger competition or shrinking donor budgets rather than weaker proposals, so no movement is attributable to proposal quality alone.

Selectivity effect: the rate can be raised by bidding only on safe, well-matched calls and lowered by deliberately ambitious bidding into new domains. A high rate on few submissions is not resource-mobilization success; always read jointly with submission volume (KPI-O54) and funds mobilized (KPI-OC56). Where CIMMYT is named in several competing bids to one call, each counts and at most one can win, which lowers the rate by construction.

Small numbers and cohort timing: annual proposal counts are modest, so a handful of decisions moves the rate by several percentage points, and award decisions often cross year boundaries. Computing on mixed cohorts produces artefactual swings; keep the cohort convention constant across years.

Comparability limits: values are comparable across years or across CGIAR centers only under a constant boundary for "competitive" and a constant role definition for lead and co-developer. Win rates also differ structurally by funder type and instrument, so a shift in the aggregate rate can reflect a changed mix of calls rather than changed performance.

What a movement means: a rising rate means a larger share of bids convert to awards. It says nothing about the size or strategic value of what was won (that is KPI-OC56) and nothing about mission delivery, which the mission branch of the register measures.
subMetrics: None. The numerator (proposals won) and denominator (proposals decided) are components of one rate, not sub-metrics; the denominator is built from a register indicator in its own right (KPI-O54, number of competitive proposals submitted as lead or named partner) with its own reference sheet. Win rates by role (lead vs named co-developer) or by funder type are disaggregations of this rate, not separate sub-metrics.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: CIMMYT resource mobilization function (proposal pipeline and grants records). Validation: pipeline data manager within the resource mobilization function. Calculation: resource mobilization function per the Calculation method above. Approval: head of the resource mobilization function. Reporting: resource mobilization function to the CIMMYT MEAL unit for institutional reporting.
