name: Total new grant income / funds mobilized (USD)
resultsLevel: Outcome. Read from the indicator statement, as the Core's results-level test requires for an Institutional-branch indicator, what this total reports is funders' decisions to commit new funds to CIMMYT in the year, valued in USD: a change in behaviour among CIMMYT's partners, not a delivery by CIMMYT, which is the Core's definition of an outcome. CIMMYT's institutional MEAL Framework places resource mobilization under Processes; the register keeps Outcome on this reading.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Resource Mobilization (institutional component). Primarily serves the component objective "CIMMYT's resource base and range of donors is expanded"; growth in this figure is what that expansion looks like in funding terms. This indicator measures the resourcing of CIMMYT the organization, not the finance CIMMYT leverages into agrifood systems for beneficiaries, which is a separate mission-level indicator (Vol. 10 · KPI-I16); the two must never be conflated or summed..
institutionalComponent: Resource Mobilization (institutional component). Primarily serves the component objective "CIMMYT's resource base and range of donors is expanded"; growth in this figure is what that expansion looks like in funding terms. This indicator measures the resourcing of CIMMYT the organization, not the finance CIMMYT leverages into agrifood systems for beneficiaries, which is a separate mission-level indicator (Vol. 10 · KPI-I16); the two must never be conflated or summed.
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. This indicator measures a property of CIMMYT's own resourcing, not a result delivered to an external population, so it does not map to any of the five CGIAR Impact Areas.
sdgTarget: None. No SDG indicator measures an individual organization's fundraising result; the SDG 17 finance indicators track resource flows to developing countries at country level, not any single organization's grant income.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Institutional Funding & Resource Mobilization (IF&RM) 2023-24 Strategy, the CGIAR working document widely known by the "Towards $2 Billion" ambition it carries: the framework that, as the CIMMYT 2030 Strategy itself states, guided the development of CIMMYT's Resource Mobilization objectives, and whose stated ambition is itself a funds-mobilized target. No donor or reporting framework carries a corresponding indicator; the total is defined here on CIMMYT's own convention.
definition: Measures the total value, in US dollars, of new grant income or funds mobilized by CIMMYT in the reporting year: the sum of new funding the organization secures for its research-for-development work and operations. This is the headline resource-mobilization result. It counts every qualifying new agreement, whatever its route; competitively won awards (KPI-OC55) are one part of it, entering in their signature year. Accounting convention: commitment basis, meaning new signed grant agreements counted once, in the year of signature, at their full contracted value, as distinct from grant revenue recognized in the year.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT is securing the resources to implement its strategy: the 2030 Strategy makes achieving its objectives conditional on the Center having the resources to implement them, and this indicator is the single figure that tells leadership, the board, and the resource mobilization function whether the resource base is growing. Read jointly with submissions (KPI-O54), the win rate (KPI-OC55), new-donor onboarding (KPI-OC57) and donor retention (KPI-OC58), it shows whether funding growth comes from more bidding, better conversion, new funders, or deeper existing relationships.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator: computed once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate grants and finance records, no project instance to adapt it to).
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: US dollars (USD); reported in USD millions in institutional reporting.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means more new funding was committed to CIMMYT. It is interpreted with the composition of the total, restricted against unrestricted and few large awards against many small, since a single large award can move the headline without any broadening of the funding base.
disaggregationRequired: None required by the register. Funder type, in the six funder categories used across this pathway, is required on this sheet and not by the register, since Block C reports the split. Where CIMMYT is a sub-grantee, the funder type is that of the donor named in the prime agreement, as on KPI-OC57 and KPI-OC58. The funding boundary under Eligibility criteria also requires the CGIAR pooled-fund share (Windows 1 and 2) to be reported separately alongside the total. A sub-grant from a sister CGIAR centre whose prime agreement is that centre's CGIAR pooled-fund allocation is counted in the pooled-fund share, as it is under the CGIAR pooled fund in the funder-type split.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Funding channel (CGIAR pooled funding vs bilateral or Window 3 grants); restricted vs unrestricted; new vs existing funders (links to KPI-OC57 and KPI-OC58); research-for-development domain; grant duration band.
unitOfObservation: The signed agreement or cost amendment, recorded under the Core's result object value, whose definition names a signed agreement.
calculationSummary: Value = sum of the USD value of all qualifying new grants in the reporting year. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: CIMMYT's grants management and finance records (signed grant agreements, award notifications, the corporate finance system), maintained by the resource mobilization and finance functions and reconciled through the grants roll-forward (opening unexpended balance plus new commitments, less revenue recognised and de-commitments, equals the closing balance). Fallback: None. Only CIMMYT's own records hold the complete universe of its new agreements at contracted value; there is no legitimate lower-resolution substitute. Not applicable: DS1 (a survey cannot establish contracted grant values that the organization's own records document exactly), DS3 (geospatial and Earth observation data are irrelevant to a financial measure), DS4 (public CGIAR and donor financial reporting records funding received or disbursed, not new commitments, so it cannot reproduce this indicator; at most it cross-checks individual awards), DS5 (citizen-generated data cannot produce an official record of CIMMYT's grant agreements).
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). No survey module or field instrument; the value is derived directly from grants and finance records.
collectionFrequency: Continuous logging of signed agreements and amendments in the grants management and finance systems; the total is computed annually.
reportingFrequency: Annual, into institutional Resource Mobilization reporting, stating the commitment basis alongside the figure so it is never misread as annual income.
referencePeriod: The reporting year, which is the calendar year register-wide, in which the grant agreements were signed. Each reported value describes one year's newly contracted funding, not the cash received in that year.
baselineRequired: Yes for any change claim: statements that CIMMYT's resource base is growing need prior-year reference values. Where no baseline was set prospectively: reconstruct prior-year totals from retained grants and finance records, which normally hold historical agreements and values. If historical records cannot support a reconstructed series on a constant accounting basis: monitoring only, no change claims.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One reporting year, one currency basis and one accounting basis, stated. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable. There are no project instances to pool.

B: Combination method. Sum of the qualifying USD amounts as Eligibility criteria and missing data sets them, for the funding actions signed in the year. Never averaged, and never added to a prior year's total without saying the series is cumulative.

C: Levels and operations. A monetary volume adds. Computed once, at institutional level, as the sum of qualifying new grant values, each converted to USD at the stated rate and date basis. There is no level beneath it: a grant belongs to CIMMYT's portfolio, not to the unit that wrote the proposal. Where a view by funder, unit or domain is wanted it is recomputed from that subset's own grants, never taken as a share of the total. Values on different currency or deflation bases are never pooled: the headline is nominal USD, and a real series, where shown, deflates every year with one named USD price index held constant, because a total that moved with the exchange rate did not move with the work. Also report: the conversion basis and rate source, the accounting basis in force, the number of grants behind the total, the split by funder type, since a bare total hides which type of funding moved, the CGIAR pooled-fund share (Windows 1 and 2) that Eligibility requires beside the total, the funds de-committed in the year, the number of agreements recording an in-kind contribution, and the amount contracted onward to sub-grantees, CGIAR and other, so the part retained for CIMMYT's own work is recoverable.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This total is never combined with KPI-OC55's conversion rate or with the submission counts that precede it: a rate, a count and a value are three quantities and no arithmetic joins them.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication: de-duplicate on the grant identifier and amendment number so a multi-year grant counts its full contracted value once, in its signature year, and an amendment only the increase it adds, in its amendment year, and a grant led jointly by two CIMMYT units counts once institutionally. Coverage is established by matching the year's new agreements in the grants record against those booked in the finance system; unmatched agreements either way are reported with the value.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: new grant agreements signed in the reporting year with CIMMYT as recipient. The value counted is the funder's committed cash contribution. CIMMYT's own cost share or match never counts; in-kind contributions are not valued in the total, and the number of agreements that record one is reported beside it. Where CIMMYT is a named sub-grantee under another lead, including a sister CGIAR centre, only CIMMYT's own contracted share counts. Where CIMMYT is the lead grantee of a consortium award, the full contracted value counts, with any share contracted onward to another CGIAR centre reported separately and netted out in cross-centre aggregation, so the lead side and the sub-grantee side of one award never sum to more than the award. Full contracted value means the amount the agreement commits to CIMMYT, including amounts CIMMYT is to sub-grant. Amounts committed directly to co-beneficiaries who are themselves parties to the funder's agreement never count here, even where CIMMYT coordinates the consortium or passes on their payments. Amendments: cost extensions and top-ups count as new funds in the amendment year; no-cost extensions never do. A termination, de-obligation or cost-reducing amendment is never netted from the year's total and never restates the signature year; it is reported beside the total as funds de-committed in the year, in USD at the rate recorded for the funding action it reduces. An agreement that both funds CIMMYT and commits finance into agrifood systems is counted on one side only, by where the funding is directed, which is the rule Vol. 10 · KPI-O38 states from the other side of the same boundary. Funding boundary: all donor income counts, including CGIAR pooled-fund allocations (Windows 1 and 2), with the pooled share reported separately, so the part CIMMYT raised directly stays visible; a CGIAR pooled-fund allocation counts in the year the instrument committing it to CIMMYT is executed, at the amount that instrument commits.

Repeated observations: each funding action counts once, keyed on agreement ID and amendment number; an original agreement counts at its contracted value and a cost extension or top-up counts only the increase it adds, in the amendment year. Currency: non-USD agreements are converted to USD at the exchange rate at the signature date of the funding action counted, an original agreement at its own date and a cost extension or top-up at the date of the amendment, with the rate and its source recorded against the agreement, and the convention is held constant across years.
limitations: Concentration in large awards: annual new-grant totals are dominated by a small number of large awards, so a single multi-year agreement can double one year's figure and its absence can halve the next. Year-on-year movements reflect donor budget cycles and the timing of large calls as much as fundraising performance; read the figure over a multi-year window, not one year at a time.

Accounting basis: on the recommended commitment basis the figure front-loads a grant's full multi-year value into its signature year and says nothing about cash available in that year. It is not comparable to annual revenue in the financial statements, and mixing the two bases across years produces artefactual swings; state the basis with every reported value and keep it constant. Commitments can also be reduced or terminated after signature, and the headline never nets them, so a series of headlines overstates the funding finally secured; read it with the de-committed figure.

Volume is not quality: the total says nothing about the composition of funding, how restricted it is, how well it covers indirect costs, or whether it funds strategic priorities; a growing total can coexist with a narrowing funder base. Pair with the retention, new-funder and (where available) restricted/unrestricted disaggregations for that reading. As lead grantee the headline is gross of every onward sub-grant; only cross-centre aggregation nets the CGIAR share.

Comparability limits: values are comparable across years only under a constant accounting basis, a constant boundary for what counts as "new" funds, and a constant currency-conversion convention; totals are stated in nominal USD, so part of any multi-year trend is exchange-rate movement and inflation rather than real resource growth.

What a movement means: a rising total means funders committed more new funds to CIMMYT the organization. It does not mean more research was delivered or more impact achieved, and it is not the finance CIMMYT mobilizes into agrifood systems for beneficiaries, which Vol. 10 · KPI-I16 measures on the mission side of the register.
subMetrics: None. Splits of the total (by funder type, funding channel, restricted vs unrestricted, new vs existing funders) are disaggregations of one figure, not separately calculated metrics. The related resource-mobilization measures each have their own reference sheet: submissions (KPI-O54), win rate (KPI-OC55), new and non-traditional funders onboarded (KPI-OC57), donor retention (KPI-OC58).
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: CIMMYT resource mobilization function with Finance (signed agreements, amendments, contracted values). Validation: Finance, through reconciliation against the corporate finance system and the grants roll-forward. Calculation: Finance with the resource mobilization function, per the Calculation method above. Approval: head of the resource mobilization function. Reporting: resource mobilization function to the CIMMYT MEAL unit for institutional reporting.
sourceRef: Volume 13 · Resource mobilization & donor relations — Reference sheet KPI-OC56

name: Number of new and non-traditional donors, investors, or PPP partners onboarded
resultsLevel: Outcome. Read from the indicator statement, as the Core's results-level test requires for an Institutional-branch indicator, what this count reports is funders' decisions to enter a funding relationship with CIMMYT for the first time, or on an instrument they have not used with it before: a change in behaviour among CIMMYT's partners, not a delivery by CIMMYT, which is the Core's definition of an outcome. CIMMYT's institutional MEAL Framework places resource mobilization under Processes; the register keeps Outcome on this reading.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Resource Mobilization (institutional component). Primarily serves component objective 1, "CIMMYT's resource base and range of donors is expanded", through its sub-objectives on new and non-traditional donors and investors, PPPs with new kinds of funders in pre-competitive spaces, and engagement pathways to non-traditional donors. This indicator measures the resourcing of CIMMYT the organization; it is distinct from the finance CIMMYT leverages into agrifood systems for beneficiaries, which is a mission-level indicator (Vol. 10 · KPI-I16)..
institutionalComponent: Resource Mobilization (institutional component). Primarily serves component objective 1, "CIMMYT's resource base and range of donors is expanded", through its sub-objectives on new and non-traditional donors and investors, PPPs with new kinds of funders in pre-competitive spaces, and engagement pathways to non-traditional donors. This indicator measures the resourcing of CIMMYT the organization; it is distinct from the finance CIMMYT leverages into agrifood systems for beneficiaries, which is a mission-level indicator (Vol. 10 · KPI-I16).
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. This indicator measures a property of CIMMYT's own funding base, not a result delivered to an external population, so it does not map to any of the five CGIAR Impact Areas.
sdgTarget: None. The nearest SDG indicator, 17.17.1, measures US dollars committed to public-private partnerships for infrastructure at country level; no SDG indicator counts an individual organization's new funding relationships.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Institutional Funding & Resource Mobilization (IF&RM) 2023-24 Strategy, the CGIAR working document widely known by the "Towards $2 Billion" ambition it carries: the CIMMYT 2030 Strategy states this framework guided the development of its Resource Mobilization objectives, and it is the 2030 Strategy that reports the CGIAR document as organised in five action areas and names alignment opportunities especially in action area 2, growing emerging markets, action area 3, tapping climate finance funds, and action area 4, engaging country partners and international finance institutions, all of which describe non-traditional funding avenues for CIMMYT. No donor or reporting framework carries a corresponding indicator; the count is defined here on CIMMYT's own convention.
definition: Counts the new funding relationships CIMMYT concludes in the reporting year, one per funder organization: with funders that have no prior funding relationship with CIMMYT, and with established funders entering an investment or public-private partnership (PPP) arrangement for the first time, the second reported as the existing-funder-new-instrument sub-count. A relationship is concluded when its funding agreement is signed, matching KPI-OC56's commitment basis. Each funder counted is classified once, at onboarding, as traditional or non-traditional; non-traditional means a funder falling under one of the sources listed in this sheet's own versioned taxonomy under Eligibility criteria and missing data, a list defined for CIMMYT's purposes.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT is broadening who funds it, not only how much it raises. The 2030 Strategy's first Resource Mobilization objective is that "CIMMYT's resource base and range of donors is expanded", pursued specifically by establishing strategic partnerships with new and non-traditional donors, investors and partners, creating PPPs with new kinds of funders for research-for-development in pre-competitive spaces, and building engagement pathways to non-traditional donors. This indicator is the direct count of that diversification result, and leadership reads it alongside total funds mobilized (KPI-OC56) and donor retention (KPI-OC58) to see whether growth comes from new relationships, larger grants, or deeper existing ones.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator: computed once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate grants and partnership records, no project instance to adapt it to).
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Number of funder organizations with which a new funding relationship was concluded in the year (first-time funders plus existing-funder-new-instrument cases).
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means CIMMYT concluded more new funding relationships in the year. It is interpreted jointly with funds mobilized (KPI-OC56) and donor retention (KPI-OC58), since many small new relationships are not by themselves resource-mobilization success (see Limitations).
disaggregationRequired: Partner/institution type, per the register, in the six funder categories used across this pathway: multilateral, bilateral public, foundation or philanthropy, private sector, CGIAR pooled fund, and other, derived from the confirmed 13-category partner and institution list. PPP arrangements are recorded against the partner's own category with the instrument noted. Funder route (first-time traditional, first-time non-traditional, existing-funder-new-instrument) is required on this sheet and not by the register, since Block C reports the three-way split.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Funding instrument (grant, investment, PPP agreement); region of the funder; research-for-development domain funded.
unitOfObservation: Organization (the funder, investor, or PPP partner organization); the reported value is a single institutional-level count of these organizations.
calculationSummary: Value = the count of distinct funder organizations with which CIMMYT concluded a new funding relationship during the reporting year: first-time funders, plus established funders entering an investment or PPP arrangement for the first time. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: CIMMYT's corporate grants, agreements, and donor-relationship administrative records (signed funding agreements, finance records of first funds received, donor and partner registry), maintained by the resource mobilization function, with the historical funder register used to verify that a relationship is new. The system that holds the donor and partner registry, and the historical funder register, has not been identified by CIMMYT, so the sheet states the records the indicator requires rather than naming an application. Fallback: None. Only CIMMYT's own records hold both the year's new agreements and the complete funder history that "new" is judged against; where the historical register cannot be produced or reconstructed, the rule under Eligibility criteria and missing data applies. Not applicable: DS1 (a survey cannot establish contractual funding relationships that the organization's own records document exactly), DS3 (geospatial and Earth observation data are irrelevant to a funding-base measure), DS4 (public donor and award databases record some awards but cannot establish whether a funder is new to CIMMYT or non-traditional for CIMMYT; at most they cross-check individual entries), DS5 (citizen-generated data cannot produce an official record of CIMMYT's funding agreements).
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). No survey module or field instrument; the value is derived directly from grants and donor-relationship records.
collectionFrequency: Continuous logging of new agreements and funder records in the grants and donor-relationship systems; the count is compiled annually.
reportingFrequency: Annual, into institutional Resource Mobilization reporting, stating the reporting year and the taxonomy version used for the non-traditional boundary.
referencePeriod: The reporting year, which is the calendar year register-wide: the value describes the new funding relationships whose qualifying onboarding event falls within that year.
baselineRequired: No. The previous reporting year's count is the reference value for any change claim. In the first year there is no reference, so the count is reported as a level and no change is claimed. Establishing that a relationship is new requires CIMMYT's historical funder register (Eligibility criteria and missing data).
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One reporting year, and each organization counted at most once in the year, as a first-time funder or as an existing-funder-new-instrument case. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable. There are no project instances to pool.

B: Combination method. Sum: the count of distinct funder organizations with which a new funding relationship was concluded in the year, de-duplicated on organization identity.

C: Levels and operations. Computed once, at institutional level, as the count of distinct funder organizations with which a new funding relationship was concluded in the reporting year, de-duplicated on the organization identifier per Block E. There is no level beneath it, because no programme or unit holds a share of an institutional count. Where a view by unit, region or funder type is wanted, it is recomputed from that subset's own records, never taken as a share of the institutional figure. An object count is not observed at the farm measurement levels. Also report: the headline split three ways, first-time traditional, first-time non-traditional and existing-funder-new-instrument, which sum to the headline; the taxonomy version in force; the number of funders returning after a lapse longer than three years; and the number of funders that funded CIMMYT in the three preceding years and do not in the reporting year, on KPI-OC58's window and entity boundary, which the count does not net off.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. This count is never added to KPI-OC56's USD total: a funder and a dollar are not commensurable, and the two are reported side by side because a few large funders and many small ones are different portfolios.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication, on the boundary KPI-OC58 applies. De-duplicate on the funding body in whose name the funding agreement is made, which for a sub-award is the prime agreement (Eligibility): a ministry or agency, a multilateral organization or fund, a foundation or a company. An office of that body (a country mission, a delegation, or a regional or country office) that signs for it is the same funder. Two ministries or agencies of one government that each sign in their own name are two funders. Coverage is established by matching the year's newly signed agreements in the relationship record against the funders the finance record holds for the year; unmatched funders either way are reported with the value.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: (a) funders with no prior funding relationship with CIMMYT (first-time funders); (b) established funders entering an investment or public-private partnership arrangement with CIMMYT for the first time (the existing-funder-new-instrument case). Each is counted in the year its funding agreement is signed. An investment arrangement is an instrument under which the funder expects repayment or a financial return, or holds equity or a revenue share (a loan, equity, a recoverable grant, a programme-related or impact investment, a revenue-sharing agreement); a grant a funder calls an investment is a grant. A public-private partnership arrangement is an agreement under which a private-sector party commits its own cash to an activity jointly governed with CIMMYT, with or without a public funder. A fee-for-service contract is neither. Where CIMMYT is funded as a sub-grantee, the funder is the donor named in the prime agreement; the lead is recorded as the channel and never counted as a funder. A CGIAR pooled-fund allocation is not a sub-grant: the pooled fund is the funder. Each counted funder is classified once, at onboarding, as traditional or non-traditional under the non-traditional taxonomy this sheet sets out, whose first version comprises private investors; public donors of countries that are not members of the OECD Development Assistance Committee at onboarding; and philanthropies new to agricultural research, a judgement recorded at onboarding with its evidence. The instrument (grant, investment, PPP) is recorded separately and does not classify the funder. A revision that adds or removes a source opens a new version, which is stated with the value. The relationship must carry monetary funding, in-kind-only contributions being counted under the Vol. 01 partnership indicators where they meet those indicators' criteria (KPI-O03; KPI-O57 for local and Global South partners) instead.

Exclusion: renewals, extensions, or follow-on grants from existing donors on the same footing as before (continuity of funders active in the three preceding years is measured by KPI-OC58; a funder returning after a longer lapse is reported beside this count), which does not exclude the existing-funder-new-instrument case above; memoranda of understanding or partnerships without funding attached, counted under the same partnership indicators where they meet their criteria, and not here; prospects still in negotiation with no concluded agreement.

Missing data: a relationship whose signed funding agreement is not documented by the computation cutoff is not counted, whatever payments have been received; once documented it is counted in its signature year, and a value already reported is restated with a note. Establishing that a relationship is new requires CIMMYT's complete historical funder register; where none was maintained prospectively, funder history is reconstructed from retained grants and finance records, and where it cannot be reconstructed, a relationship is counted only where it is documented individually as a new funding relationship, the value is reported for monitoring with no change claims, and the gap is stated; a relationship is never counted as new on an incomplete record.

Repeated observations: each funder organization counts at most once in a year; a funder onboarded in an earlier year never re-enters the count as a new funder, and several grants or instruments from the same funder in one year count as one relationship. An established funder entering a PPP or investment arrangement counts as a new funding relationship, not as a new funder, recorded as an existing-funder-new-instrument case once, in the year of its first such arrangement, and reported as its own part of the headline split, since the relationship is new even where the organisation is not; records are de-duplicated by funder identity across CIMMYT's programs, regions and units, since resource mobilization at CIMMYT is a decentralized process in which many units build funding relationships in parallel.
limitations: A count is not a value measure: one small pilot grant and one major multi-year facility each add one to the count. The indicator says nothing about the size, duration, or strategic fit of what was secured; read it with KPI-OC56 (USD mobilized).

Definitional sensitivity: the value depends on where the onboarding event is drawn, and its traditional and non-traditional split on where the non-traditional boundary is drawn. A shifting taxonomy or a change from agreement-signed to first-funds-received can manufacture an apparent trend, so comparability over time requires holding both definitions constant and versioning the taxonomy.

Attribution boundary: a new funder's decision reflects donor budget cycles, One CGIAR joint arrangements, and sector-wide funding trends as well as CIMMYT's own outreach; where a relationship arrives through a CGIAR-level agreement, CIMMYT's count supports a contribution claim only.

Incentive risk: maximizing the count rewards many shallow engagements over fewer strategic ones, and can pull effort away from deepening existing relationships (the result KPI-OC58 measures). The pathway is designed to be read as a set precisely to keep this pressure visible.

What a movement means: a rising count means CIMMYT concluded more new funding relationships in that year, with first-time funders or with established funders entering an investment or PPP arrangement for the first time. It does not mean income grew, that the new relationships will persist, or that dependence on the largest funders fell, which would need a concentration or share measure this indicator does not provide.
subMetrics: None. Investors and PPP partners are recorded under their organization's own category with the instrument noted; the three-way split under the aggregation rule is a partition of the headline, not a sub-metric.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: CIMMYT resource mobilization function (grants, agreements, and donor-relationship records). Validation: donor-registry data manager within the resource mobilization function. Calculation: resource mobilization function per the Calculation method above. Approval: head of the resource mobilization function. Reporting: resource mobilization function to the CIMMYT MEAL unit for institutional reporting.

name: Donor retention rate (%) and investment growth from continuing donors
resultsLevel: Outcome. Read from the indicator statement, as the Core's results-level test requires for an Institutional-branch indicator, what this rate reports is funders' decisions to fund CIMMYT again, measured against the donors of the three preceding years: a change in behaviour among CIMMYT's partners, not a delivery by CIMMYT, which is the Core's definition of an outcome. CIMMYT's institutional MEAL Framework places resource mobilization under Processes; the register keeps Outcome on this reading.
primaryObjective: Institutional indicator, no primary objective; sits under the CIMMYT 2030 institutional component Resource Mobilization (institutional component). Primarily serves the component objective "Donor relations at all levels are deepened", whose sub-objectives commit CIMMYT to engaging donors in continuous improvement and shared learning and to better networking of donors, partners and alumni; sustained repeat funding is the evidence that those relationships hold. It also informs the first component objective, "CIMMYT's resource base and range of donors is expanded", as the retained counterpart to new-donor acquisition (KPI-OC57). This indicator measures the resourcing of CIMMYT the organization, not the finance CIMMYT leverages into agrifood systems for beneficiaries, which is a separate mission-level indicator (Vol. 10 · KPI-I16)..
institutionalComponent: Resource Mobilization (institutional component). Primarily serves the component objective "Donor relations at all levels are deepened", whose sub-objectives commit CIMMYT to engaging donors in continuous improvement and shared learning and to better networking of donors, partners and alumni; sustained repeat funding is the evidence that those relationships hold. It also informs the first component objective, "CIMMYT's resource base and range of donors is expanded", as the retained counterpart to new-donor acquisition (KPI-OC57). This indicator measures the resourcing of CIMMYT the organization, not the finance CIMMYT leverages into agrifood systems for beneficiaries, which is a separate mission-level indicator (Vol. 10 · KPI-I16).
cgiarImpactArea: Not applicable. This indicator measures a property of CIMMYT's own funding relationships, not a result delivered to an external population, so it does not map to any of the five CGIAR Impact Areas.
sdgTarget: None. No SDG indicator measures an individual organization's donor retention; the SDG 17 finance indicators track resource flows to developing countries at country level, not any single organization's funding relationships.
otherFrameworks: CGIAR Institutional Funding & Resource Mobilization (IF&RM) 2023-24 Strategy, the CGIAR working document widely known by the "Towards $2 Billion" ambition it carries: the framework that, as the CIMMYT 2030 Strategy itself states, guided the development of CIMMYT's Resource Mobilization objectives. No donor or reporting framework carries a corresponding indicator; the rate is defined here on CIMMYT's own convention.
definition: Measures whether CIMMYT keeps the donors that fund it. Headline: the donor retention rate. Numerator: donors that provided funding in any of the three preceding years and provide funding again in the reporting year (repeat donors); denominator: all donors that provided funding in any of the three preceding years. The rate counts donors, not money, so a retained small funder moves it as much as a retained large one; what the continuing relationships are worth is measured by the sub-metric, investment growth from continuing donors. A donor is a funding entity, and investment is funding recognized in CIMMYT's audited finance records. All other funders in the reporting year are new donors for this measure.
rationale: Answers whether CIMMYT keeps the funders it wins, so that the resource base rests on continuing relationships rather than on constant replacement of lapsed donors. The 2030 Strategy's Resource Mobilization component commits CIMMYT to deepening donor relations at all levels and to continued work on existing relationships with key donors. Whether donors fund CIMMYT again, and whether continuing donors invest more, are the observable results of that relationship work, and the most readily available proxy for whether CIMMYT delivered what it promised the last time it was funded. Leadership and the resource mobilization function read it jointly with new-donor acquisition (KPI-OC57) and total funds mobilized (KPI-OC56) to see whether funding growth comes from keeping existing funders, adding new ones, or both.
projectSpecificApplication: Not applicable (Institutional indicator: computed once at CIMMYT-institutional level from corporate finance and grants records, no project instance to adapt it to).
projectSpecificRationale: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
projectTypesRaw: Not applicable. This indicator has no project instance: it is a property of CIMMYT as an organisation, computed once at institutional level from corporate systems.
unit: Percentage of donors (0 to 100). The sub-metric is a percentage change, which can be negative.
directionOfChange: Increase. A rising value means a larger share of the donor base continues to choose CIMMYT. It is interpreted jointly with new-donor acquisition (KPI-OC57): a very high rate alongside near-zero acquisition signals dependence on a static donor pool rather than resource-mobilization strength (see Limitations).
disaggregationRequired: Partner/institution type, per the register, in the six funder categories used across this pathway: multilateral, bilateral public, foundation or philanthropy, private sector, CGIAR pooled fund, and other, derived from the confirmed 13-category partner and institution list.
disaggregationRequiredForProjectType: None. The register names a project type in none of its rows, and this indicator has no project instance in any case.
disaggregationProjectSpecific: Donor size band (share of total investment); funding instrument or window (pooled, bilateral, project grant); region of donor; traditional versus non-traditional funder, as classified by KPI-OC57's taxonomy at the donor's onboarding, a classification the donor keeps while retained; a donor onboarded before the taxonomy's first version is classified once, under that first version.
unitOfObservation: Organization (the donor entity), observed through its funding records; the reported value is a single organization-level rate for CIMMYT.
calculationSummary: Value = (repeat donors / donors in the lookback window) x 100. Numerator: donors that provided funding in any of the three preceding reporting years and provide funding again in the reporting year. Denominator: donors that provided funding in any of the three preceding reporting years. Investment means funding recognized in the period in CIMMYT's audited finance records, and a donor's presence in any year, in the lookback window or the reporting year, is established from that same ledger; a donor is present in a year when its net recognized funding in that year is greater than zero. Investment is taken in the presentation currency of CIMMYT's audited financial statements, at the rates those statements apply, in nominal terms; the currency is stated with every value. Donor identity: funding entities are de-duplicated at donor-entity level across periods before matching. The sub-metric's formula is under Sub-metrics. The investment-weighted share reported beside the rate is (lookback-window investment of repeat donors / lookback-window investment of all donors in the lookback window) x 100, a donor's lookback-window investment being its funding recognized across the three preceding years; it is formed on the rate's own donors, ledger and entity boundary, so a lapsed donor enters its denominator with its full weight. Every inclusion, exclusion, missing-data and repeated-observation rule is in Eligibility criteria and missing data; none is restated here.
dataSource: Recommended DS2: CIMMYT's finance and grants administrative records (donor ledger, grant agreements, income recognition records), maintained by the finance and resource mobilization functions. Fallback: None. There is no legitimate lower-resolution substitute: only CIMMYT's own records hold the full donor-by-donor funding series needed to match funders across periods. Not applicable: DS1 (a survey cannot establish funding amounts that the organization's own audited records document exactly), DS3 (geospatial and Earth observation data are irrelevant to a funding measure), DS4 (public funder databases such as the CGIAR Trust Fund dashboard record contributions to CGIAR or individual awards, not CIMMYT's complete donor ledger, so neither numerator nor denominator can be built from them; at most they cross-check individual contributions), DS5 (citizen-generated data cannot produce an official record of CIMMYT's donor funding).
dataSourceProjectSpecific: Not applicable (Institutional indicator).
collectionInstrument: Not applicable, administrative source (DS2). No survey module or field instrument; the value is derived directly from finance and grants records.
collectionFrequency: Continuous, as a by-product of finance and grants administration; the rate is computed annually at period close.
reportingFrequency: Annual, into institutional Resource Mobilization reporting, stating the lookback window used and reporting the sub-metric and the investment-weighted share alongside the rate, with the other figures the aggregation rule lists.
referencePeriod: The reporting year, which is the calendar year register-wide, with repeat status assessed against the three-year lookback window; the sub-metric compares the reporting year with the previous year.
baselineRequired: No. The previous reporting year's value is the reference for the rate, and the sub-metric builds the previous year into its own formula, so no separately established baseline is needed. A first year is reported as not computable, never as zero: the rate and the investment-weighted share are reported in their first year only where finance records cover the three preceding years, and the sub-metric is reported in any year whose previous year is held in the finance records, and as not computable otherwise. Zero is a real value, no donor retained or no growth, and entering it for a year that cannot be computed would show a false rise the year after.
aggregationRule:
A: Pooling domain. One reporting year, one funding-recognition rule, one donor-entity boundary and one definition of a repeat donor, stated with the value. (2) Aggregation across projects: not applicable. There are no project instances to pool.

B: Combination method. A ratio of counts, formed once: repeat donors over donors in the lookback window. Never an average of per-category or per-unit percentages. The sub-metric is a change, computed once at institutional level from its two sums. The investment-weighted share is a ratio of sums over the rate's own donor set, repeat donors' lookback-window investment over all lookback-window investment, formed once.

C: Levels and operations. The rate is computed once, at institutional level, over all donors in the lookback window, and is recomputed from its own numerator and denominator wherever a narrower view is wanted, never averaged from the views beneath it, since the units beneath it differ in size. There is no level beneath the institution here, because a donor is one record in the denominator, not a reporting level. The denominator is a portfolio of records rather than a population measured in the field, so the measurement levels do not apply and every breakdown is a reporting view. Also report: the numerator and denominator counts, the repeat definition in force and the window it looks back over, the number of reporting-year donors treated as new because they could not be matched to a lookback record, the number of donors restated on the entity map, the number of lapsed donors leaving the window in the year, the sub-metric with the previous-year investment it rests on, and the investment-weighted share, since a high count-based rate can coexist with the loss of the largest funder.

D: Never pooled. (1) Aggregation across results levels: no. The rate, the sub-metric and the investment-weighted share are never combined with one another, with KPI-OC56's total or with KPI-OC57's count; a share of donors, a share of investment, a growth rate, a value and a count are five quantities.

E: Deduplication and coverage. (3) Double counting and de-duplication, before either term is formed. De-duplicate on the funding body in whose name the funding agreement is made, which for a sub-award is the prime agreement (Eligibility): a ministry or agency, a multilateral organization or fund, a foundation or a company. An office of that body (a country mission, a delegation, or a regional or country office) that signs for it is the same funder. Two ministries or agencies of one government that each sign in their own name are two funders. Before matching, every lookback record is restated on the reporting year's entity map: a successor that took over a predecessor's agreements by merger, renaming or transfer is the same donor, and predecessors merged into one successor count as one donor across the window; where a donor splits, the predecessor counts once and is retained if any successor funds in the reporting year, and no successor of a split is a new donor. The number of donors so restated is reported with the value. KPI-OC57 applies the same entity boundary, so the two identify donors the same way; "new" differs, this indicator's meaning absent from the three-year window and KPI-OC57's meaning the one set out in that sheet's Eligibility criteria and missing data, which is not restated here. Coverage is the share of donor funding the finance record covers.
eligibilityCriteriaMissingData:
Inclusion: all donor funding counts, including CGIAR pooled-fund allocations; the CGIAR pooled fund is one donor, and its investment is reported separately in the sub-metric and the investment-weighted share. Where CIMMYT is funded as a sub-grantee, the funder is the donor named in the prime agreement; the lead is recorded as the channel and never counted as a funder. A CGIAR pooled-fund allocation is not a sub-grant: the pooled fund is the funder.

Exclusion: receipts that are not donor funding (for example sales of goods and services or interest earned).

Missing data: donor records come from audited finance systems and are complete by construction; a reporting-year donor that cannot be matched to a record in the lookback window, including a renaming, merger or restructuring not yet documented, is treated as new, which is the conservative convention because it can only lower the rate; once the match is resolved the value already reported is restated with a note. The convention applies to individual unmatched records, never to a lookback window the records do not cover: a year whose three preceding years are not held in the finance records is reported as not computable, never as zero.

Repeated observations: a donor with several grants or disbursements counts once as a donor, in the denominator and, where it funds again, in the numerator, and all of its investment counts once in the sub-metric; each period's value is computed independently.
limitations: Attribution boundary: repeat funding reflects donor budget cycles, strategy shifts, political changes in funder governments, and the timing of call windows, alongside CIMMYT's relationship management. A lapsed donor may have exited the sector entirely, so a fall in the rate is not attributable to weaker donor relations alone, and a funder that moves from bilateral grants into the CGIAR pooled fund reads as lapsed.

Count and value diverge: the rate counts every donor equally, so losing one major funder moves it as much as losing a small one while removing far more funding. The sub-metric and the investment-weighted share carry the value side, and a high headline rate can coexist with a sharp fall in funding; read the three together.

Multi-year grant cycles: grants are multi-year and a loyal funder can have a gap year between agreements. A one-year lookback would read such a funder as lapsed and then as new, deflating the rate for reasons unrelated to the relationship, which is why the window is fixed at three years and held constant across the series. Recognized funding also follows grant spending, so the sub-metric moves with implementation pace as well as with donor decisions, and the rate moves later and more smoothly than the decisions behind it; a donor mid-way through a multi-year grant counts as retained on the decision it took when that grant was signed.

Comparability limits: the value depends on the donor-entity boundary (for example whether two ministries of one government are one donor) and on the lookback window; a change in either breaks the series. It is not comparable with retention figures other organizations compute on income rather than on donor counts, or over a different window. The sub-metric and the investment-weighted share are nominal: exchange-rate movements on grants in other currencies, and inflation, move them without any change in donor decisions.

What a movement means: a rising rate means a larger share of the donor base continues to fund CIMMYT. A donor that lapses stays in the denominator while its last funding is inside the three-year window, so one lapse lowers three successive values and the rate rises in the fourth year with no change in any relationship; read a movement with the number of donors that left the window that year. It does not mean more new funding was committed (that is KPI-OC56), that the donor base broadened (that is KPI-OC57), or that continuing donors invest more (that is the sub-metric), and a very high rate with little acquisition can indicate a static, concentrated funding base rather than strong resource mobilization.
subMetrics:
One sub-metric, reported alongside the headline rate and never combined with it:

— Investment growth from continuing donors (%): the year-on-year change in what CIMMYT's continuing donors invest. Formula: (reporting-year investment from continuing donors - the same donors' previous-year investment) x 100 / the same donors' previous-year investment. A continuing donor provided funding in both the previous and the reporting year, so the denominator is positive by construction, and a donor returning after a gap year is not read as growth from zero (it counts as retained in the headline). The value can be negative. Investment is funding recognized in the period in CIMMYT's audited finance records, on the headline's donor-entity boundary.

The headline says how many funders CIMMYT keeps; the sub-metric says whether the relationships that continue are growing. Donors that lapsed are absent from the sub-metric by construction, so a positive value can coexist with a shrinking donor base. The investment-weighted share, reported beside both under the aggregation rule, is context and not a second sub-metric.
referenceStandardsAndLinks: Every other source is cited inline at the point of the claim it supports; the reference list is at the end of this volume.
sheetStewardDataRoles: Data collection: CIMMYT finance function jointly with the resource mobilization function (donor ledger and grants records). Validation: finance function (audited finance records; donor-entity matching validated by the resource mobilization function). Calculation: resource mobilization function per the Calculation method above. Approval: head of the resource mobilization function. Reporting: resource mobilization function to the CIMMYT MEAL unit for institutional reporting.
